claims.text: A Hero gains about 50-54 HP per AP put into HP at level up, and about 50-55 per AP moved into HP with an AP Reset.
claims.say: hero gets ~50-55 hp per ap into hp

claims.text: Taking an AP out of MP with an AP Reset removes about 4 MP from a Hero.
claims.say: each reset out of mp costs a hero ~4 mp

claims.text: INT adds extra MP on each level up, about 1 MP per 10 INT, so more INT means more MP available to wash into HP.
claims.say: int gives ~1 mp per 10 int each level, more to wash

claims.text: Normal washing: put the level-up AP into HP, use AP Resets to move AP from MP into HP until you reach minimum MP, then move one AP from HP back to STR.
claims.say: normal wash: lvl ap to hp, reset mp into hp to min mp

claims.text: Double washing: put the level-up AP into MP, reset the extra MP AP into HP, then reset one AP from MP back to STR; it finishes sooner but costs many more AP Resets.
claims.say: double wash finishes faster but eats way more resets

claims.text: By the author's math, reaching 30,000 HP at level 200 takes a Hero about 325 washes.
claims.say: ~325 washes for a 30k hp hero at 200

claims.text: With about 70 INT, mostly from gear, normal washing uses the fewest AP Resets to bring a Hero to 30,000 HP at 200.
claims.say: 70 int + normal washing uses the fewest resets

claims.text: The author's preferred Hero plan is about 80 base INT with double washing, which can finish all washing by level 120 without INT gear.
claims.say: 80 int double washing gets you done by 120

claims.text: Double washing with 120 INT needs the fewest double washes but requires INT gear early, so the author finds it overkill compared with normal washing.
claims.say: 120 int double wash is overkill

claims.text: When washing is done, reset the extra INT back down to 4.
claims.say: reset int back to 4 when washing is done

claims.text: HP washing works because HP and MP share one AP pool: you trade surplus MP for extra HP by moving points with AP Resets.
claims.say: hp washing is trading your spare mp for hp with ap resets

claims.text: To wash, put one level-up AP into HP, use an AP Reset to take a point out of MP, and put it into your main stat (LUK for a thief, STR for a warrior). Do it one AP at a time, not all five into HP.
claims.say: 1 ap into hp, reset 1 out of mp into your main stat, repeat

claims.text: You can only wash MP above your class minimum; for bowmen and thieves past 2nd job it is about 14 x level + 148, so a level 200 thief must keep 2948 MP. Other tables give thieves + 156 instead.
claims.say: bow and thief keep about 14 mp per level plus 148, wash the rest

claims.text: HP and MP each cap at 30,000 for every job, with or without Hyper Body.
claims.say: hp and mp cap at 30k each, hyper body or not

claims.text: MP gained per level rises with total INT, about one extra MP per 10 INT, so leveling with more INT leaves more MP to wash later.
claims.say: 10 int is about 1 more mp per level, more mp to wash

claims.text: Start leveling in INT gear from the mid 30s on, swapping it on just before the level-up (at 99.99% exp) to get the extra MP.
claims.say: put on int gear right before you level for more mp

claims.text: Cheap low-level INT gear to wear when leveling: Wooden Wand (level 8), Yellow Work Gloves (level 10), Bathrobe and Maple Shield (level 20), all worth scrolling for INT.
claims.say: wooden wand, yellow work gloves, bathrobe, maple shield for int

claims.text: Mid-level INT gear for washers: Raccoon Mask (level 35) or White Raccoon Mask (45), Diao Chan Sword (48), Yellow Adventurer Cape and Yellow Snowshoes (level 50).
claims.say: raccoon mask, yellow adventurer cape and snowshoes give int

claims.text: Alcaster's long quest chain starts at level 55 with the Book of Ancient part, and the Dark Crystal part needs level 60. No other quest has to be done first.
claims.say: alcaster's book of ancient chain needs lvl 55, dark crystal part 60

claims.text: The chain is optional, but it is most useful for classes that burn many Summoning Rocks, like Hermits and Night Lords, and for Priests and Bishops who use Magic Rocks for Mystic Door.
claims.say: magic rocks for mystic door, summon rocks for hermit and nl

claims.text: Start by taking the quest from Alcaster in El Nath, then speak to Elma the Housekeeper in Orbis Park about the missing Hella. Pick the second option about Hella's close friends, which sends you to Jade in El Nath.
claims.say: alcaster quest first, then elma in orbis park, pick 2nd option for jade

claims.text: Jade tells you to give up, so go back to Elma, then to Jade again; he names the old lady as Spiruna, who lives in the Old Man's House in Cloud Park IV of Orbis.
claims.say: jade, elma, jade again points you to spiruna in cloud park iv

claims.text: Spiruna wants her Black Crystal. Click the Rock Covered in Snow in Ice Valley I to get a Cracked Black Crystal and bring it back to her.
claims.say: spiruna sends you to ice valley i for a cracked black crystal

claims.text: After she flips out over the cracked crystal, her assistant says it needs fairy dust. Choose the third option, I need fairy dust, with Kriel the Fairy in the Orbis potion shop; she wants 100 Starpieces, 50 Moonpieces and 30 Sunpieces.
claims.say: kriel in orbis wants 100 starpiece, 50 moonpiece, 30 sunpiece

claims.text: Return the fairy dust to Spiruna for a random defense scroll, take her assistant's pendant to Jade for another scroll, then click the Small Tomb in Wolf Territory I for an Old Ring and bring it to Alcaster.
claims.say: pendant to jade, then small tomb in wolf territory i for old ring

claims.text: After the Dark Lord gives the last map piece, go back to Alcaster, who sends you to Corporal Easy in Cloud Park VI; he trades the memory powder for 3 Werewolf Toenails.
claims.say: corporal easy in cloud park vi wants 3 werewolf toenails

claims.text: Alcaster uses the memory powder to read the map, which says the book is in the Orbis Tower. Inspect and keep talking to the statue on the 8th floor so the Old Ring lets you take the Book of Ancient, then return it to Alcaster.
claims.say: statue on orbis tower 8th floor has the book, use the old ring

claims.text: The final part needs one Dark Crystal and one Star Rock handed in to Alcaster.
claims.say: last part of alcaster's chain needs a dark crystal and a star rock

claims.text: Orbis Tower is the most annoying part of the chain, so carry Nearest Town Scrolls: used on floors 20 down to 8 they warp you to Orbis, and used on floors 7 down to 1 they warp you to El Nath.
claims.say: nearest town scroll in orbis tower: floors 20-8 orbis, 7-1 el nath

claims.text: To go from El Nath to Orbis without a scroll, climb the Orbis Tower, or go through Aqua Road, take the Dolphin to Herb Town, then take the crane to Mu Lung and another crane to Orbis.
claims.say: no scroll? climb orbis tower or go aqua, herb town, mu lung cranes

claims.text: For item turn-in quests, gather everything first, then accept and hand in with back-to-back talks to the NPC instead of making repeat trips.
claims.say: grab the turn-in items first then just talk to the npc twice

claims.text: Characters HP/MP-washed with a high base INT are weak in the early levels, so questing is a safer way to level them than grinding.
claims.say: washed chars are weak early so questing is the safe way to level

claims.text: In Orbis, Staff Sergeant Charlie accepts stacks of 100 monster drops for exp and a random prize. It is repeatable, best for levels 11-20 but usable at any level.
claims.say: turn in 100 mob drops to staff sergeant charlie in orbis for exp

claims.text: Help Me Find My Glasses at level 15 needs no fighting: click the bushes on the right side of the outdoor Nautilus map until you find Abel's Glasses.
claims.say: click the bushes outside nautilus for abel's glasses

claims.text: The DANGER! mushroom quests ask for 99 kills each: Green Mushroom at level 15, Horny Mushroom at 20 and Zombie Mushroom at 22. Good exp while you hunt those mobs anyway.
claims.say: do the danger mushroom quests while you grind those mobs

claims.text: Planting Trees at level 20 asks for 54 Seedlings from Ghost Stumps; collect them first and talk to Winston twice for a big exp reward.
claims.say: farm 54 seedlings off ghost stumps for winston at lvl 20

claims.text: Kerning City Party Quest opens at level 21 and is easy to rush if you dual-screen a second character and let your main do the attacking. If you dislike the PQ, quests are the alternative.
claims.say: kpq from 21 is quick if you rush it with a second window

claims.text: Lazy Little Calico (10 Evil Eye Tails) and Strange Dish 1 (40 yellow Evil Eye Tails to Tangyoon in the Nautilus cafeteria) both open at level 25; farm about 50 tails once and do both.
claims.say: farm 50 evil eye tails once and do calico + strange dish 1

claims.text: The Importance of Life Alchemy at level 29: kill 80 Scorpions and turn in 40 Scorpion Stings for strong exp at that level.
claims.say: life alchemy quest at 29 is 80 scorpions and 40 stings

claims.text: Delivering Food to Spiruna at level 30: buy 20 each of Apple, Egg and Orange from shops and bring them to the NPC in Cloud Park IV of Orbis; no fighting needed.
claims.say: buy 20 apples, eggs, oranges for the spiruna quest at 30

claims.text: Information for Dr. Kim at level 30 is only worth it if you have the Warp Cards from Bartol's Request: take the leftmost door on the top level of the Nautilus to Omega Sector, talk to Rolonay, then Dr. Kim.
claims.say: get bartol's warp cards first, then do dr kim's quest at 30

claims.text: A Hole in the Nautilus at level 30 pays the best of the level 30 quests: bring 50 Solid Horns from Jr. Cellion, Jr. Grupin or Jr. Lioner to Bonnie on the Nautilus bottom floor, collecting them before you talk to her.
claims.say: bonnie's solid horn quest at 30 pays a lot, farm 50 horns first

claims.text: Do your second job advancement at level 30 with your job instructor, then start working through the level 31-40 quests.
claims.say: get your 2nd job at 30, then start the 31-40 quests

claims.text: Most Korean Folk Town quests give a book as part of the reward; hand each book to Wiz the Librarian for extra bonus exp.
claims.say: korean folk town quest books go to wiz the librarian for bonus exp

claims.text: The Lantern at Mushroom Shrine at level 35: kill 100 Paper Lantern Ghosts and turn in 50 of their lanterns for good exp.
claims.say: lantern quest at 35, kill 100 paper lantern ghosts for lanterns

claims.text: Strange Dish 2 (level 35, 50 Curse Eye tails) and Strange Dish 3 (level 40, 50 Cold Eye tails) go to Tangyoon in the Nautilus cafeteria and pay much more than most quests at those levels.
claims.say: strange dish 2 and 3 pay more each time, tails to tangyoon

claims.text: Brotherly Love at level 37 is just clicking Rice Stacks back and forth in Korean Folk Town; it gives several small rewards plus a book for Wiz, and it is a prerequisite for Legends of Hometown.
claims.say: brotherly love at 37 is just clicking rice stacks, and needed later

claims.text: Eliminating the Escaped Pot at level 49: kill 400 Jars for one of the biggest exp rewards in the late 40s.
claims.say: kill 400 jars at 49 for a big exp quest

claims.text: Most Mu Lung quests, which start around level 50, are worth doing.
claims.say: most mu lung quests from about 50 are worth doing

claims.text: Keeny's research quests pay big for simple turn-ins: Roid at level 55 wants 80 Wires and Neo Huroid at level 60 wants 160 Plugs. Collect them first and talk to her twice.
claims.say: keeny's roid quest at 55 and neo huroid at 60 give big exp

claims.text: The Brewing Storm (turn in 10 Stormbreaker Badges) and Storming the Castle (kill 75 each of Windraider, Firebrand and Nightshadow, after Stemming the Tide) both start at level 70 and give very large exp.
claims.say: brewing storm and storming the castle at 70 are great exp

claims.text: Urban Jungle at level 80: kill 100 Wolf Spiders for solid exp. The quest can be repeated afterwards for less exp.
claims.say: urban jungle at 80: kill 100 wolf spiders, repeatable

claims.text: Wyvern's Sudden Attack at level 100: kill 18 each of Red, Blue and Dark Wyverns for a large exp reward.
claims.say: wyvern quest at 100: 18 red, blue and dark wyverns

claims.text: Temple of Time quests start around level 95 and need 999 kills per mob, but they are the way to unlock the later hunting grounds.
claims.say: temple of time quests from 95 need 999 kills but unlock maps

claims.text: The Zakum pre-quests need level 50. Start in El Nath by asking your third-job instructor for permission to do the Zakum quests.
claims.say: zakum prequests start at lvl 50, ask your 3rd job npc in el nath

claims.text: To reach the Zakum pre-quest area, take the Danger Zone taxi from El Nath to Ice Valley II and walk through each Dead Mine map until you arrive at The Door to Zakum.
claims.say: taxi to ice valley 2 then walk the dead mine to the door

claims.text: Form a party before talking to Adobis for part one. Up to six can join and a group is much quicker than going solo, but Haste and Teleport do not work inside this part.
claims.say: party up before adobis for part one, haste and teleport don't work

claims.text: Part one of the Zakum pre-quest is gathering seven keys from chests and rocks, dropping them as a bundle on the big chest in area 16-5 to get a piece of ore, then returning to the first map where Aura makes it a complete Fire Ore.
claims.say: part one: 7 keys on the 16-5 chest, then aura makes the ore

claims.text: A handy order for the seven keys is chest 11-1, chest 9-2, chest 14-1, rock 4-2, chests 16-3 and 16-2, then rock 16-5. Area 16 is reached through room 10 or room 7.
Some chests in the key area warp you back to the start, which can save the walk back to Aura or cost you time; if no warp chest is left in 16-5 you face a slow walk.
claims.say: some chests in part one warp you back to start, handy to get to aura

claims.text: Many rocks in the part one rooms hold documents that can be turned into Dead Mine scrolls. They are optional and most runners skip them when rushing.
claims.say: rocks in part one have documents for dead mine scrolls, optional

claims.text: Finishing all three parts gives several Eyes of Fire, which are needed to enter the Zakum fight. When you run out, redo the pre-quests or buy more from other players.
claims.say: finish all 3 parts for eyes of fire, redo it when you run out

claims.text: To reach New Leaf City, go to the Kerning City subway station, buy an NLC ticket from Bell, then hand it in at the ticket gate to board.
claims.say: buy an nlc ticket from bell in kerning subway, then use the gate

claims.text: The New Leaf City subway only accepts tickets during boarding windows; if the gate refuses yours, try again a little later, then wait out the ride in the waiting room.
claims.say: nlc train only boards at set times, just retry the gate

claims.text: Icebyrd Slimm, standing just outside the NLC subway station, gives a twelve-question quiz quest worth doing as soon as you reach level 10.
claims.say: talk to icebyrd slimm outside nlc subway for a quiz quest

claims.text: Ludibrium Party Quest has nine stages plus a bonus stage. It needs level 35 or higher and a party of six, and is mostly run by players around levels 35 to 50.
claims.say: lpq needs lv35+ and a party of 6, mostly for lv35-50

claims.text: Finishing Ludibrium Party Quest 35 times in full earns a pair of Broken Glasses.
claims.say: 35 full lpq clears gets you broken glasses

claims.text: LPQ is at Eos Tower 101st Floor. Ship from Ellinia to Orbis, take the Ludibrium route from the Orbis station NPC, head left past Ludibrium Village and Eos Tower Entrance, then climb the screws on the 100th floor to the brown door.
claims.say: lpq is at eos tower 101st floor, orbis boat to ludibrium then left

claims.text: If nobody is waiting at Eos Tower 101st Floor, switch to channel 1 where LPQ parties tend to gather; if it is still empty, wait a while or do something else.
claims.say: if the lpq room is empty try channel 1

claims.text: For a smooth full LPQ run, bring a thief with Dark Sight, a ranged attacker (assassin, hunter or crossbowman) and a magician with Teleport among the six members.
claims.say: lpq party wants a ds thief, a ranged guy and a tele mage

claims.text: Buy some All Cure Potions before LPQ. Alishar can seal you or put you in darkness for a while, and the potions fix both.
claims.say: bring all cure potions for alishar, he seals and blinds

claims.text: LPQ stage 2 needs 15 passes. The first member in hits the second box from the top, which is a portal to Tower's Trap with four boxes, and types clear in chat; the rest then follow, hit every box and give passes to the leader.
claims.say: stage 2: hit the 2nd box from the top, say c in chat

claims.text: LPQ stage 3 needs 32 passes. Hit the boxes so Bloctopus spawn, kill them, and hand the passes they drop to the leader.
claims.say: stage 3 hit the boxes and kill the bloctopus for passes

claims.text: LPQ stage 4 (Darkness in the Tower): the topmost and bottommost portals do not work, leaving five. The top three hold monsters weak to magic so magicians should take them; the bottom two hold monsters weak to weapon attacks.
claims.say: stage 4: top 3 portals are mage-weak, bottom 2 are weapon-weak

claims.text: LPQ stage 4 needs 6 passes in total from five portals, because the second-to-last portal (the left one) has two monsters inside and so gives two passes.
claims.say: stage 4 second-last portal has 2 mobs, needs 2 passes

claims.text: In LPQ stage 4, drop a 10 meso coin or an etc item inside your portal so others know it is taken. The monsters can only be hurt while their eyes are open.
claims.say: drop a 10 meso coin in your portal and hit them when eyes open

claims.text: LPQ stage 5 (Tower's Maze) needs 24 passes across six rainbow portals. The top portal is for a magician with Teleport and the bottom one for a thief with Dark Sight; each portal has four boxes, so bring back four passes.
claims.say: stage 5: tele mage takes top portal, ds thief takes bottom

claims.text: A thief with Haste should buff the party before they split up in LPQ stage 5; the stage is a chore without the speed.
claims.say: thief with haste should buff everyone before stage 5

claims.text: Do not go down into the lower area of LPQ stage 5 unless you have Dark Sight or a heavily washed HP pool; the monsters there hit very hard.
claims.say: dont drop to the lower area in stage 5 without ds or big hp

claims.text: LPQ stage 6 gives no passes. Press up on the boxes, which act as portals; a wrong box sends you back to the bottom. The order is fixed: 133, 221, 333, 123, 111.
claims.say: stage 6 box order is 133 221 333 123 111

claims.text: LPQ stage 7: the ranged member climbs up and kills the Ratz and Bloctopus one by one so the party is safer when the three Rombots spawn. Each Rombot drops one pass for the leader.
claims.say: stage 7 ranged guy clears the platforms, rombots drop the passes

claims.text: Clerics in LPQ stage 7 should stay alert and heal the party, focusing on keeping everyone alive over dealing damage.
claims.say: cleric heal people in stage 7 more than attacking

claims.text: LPQ stage 8 is a box-combination puzzle like the Kerning barrel stage, with five people. Start on boxes 1-2-3-4-5; the last person cycles through the free boxes, and when he reaches the end the person before him moves up one box.
claims.say: stage 8: last guy walks the boxes, then the next steps up one

claims.text: In LPQ stage 8, someone standing on box 1 alternates between boxes 1 and 2, but only after whoever started on box 2 has moved down to box 3.
claims.say: stage 8: box 1 guy alternates 1 and 2 once box 2 is empty

claims.text: There are two ways to solve LPQ stage 8: the plain box order, which most parties use, and an imagined renumbering of the boxes that is faster but harder to picture. Both follow the same last-person-finishes rule.
claims.say: stage 8 has an easy box order and a faster but trickier one

claims.text: LPQ stage 9: the ranged member kills the Ratz to summon Alishar. Watch for his seal and darkness attacks, and have All Cure Potions ready.
claims.say: stage 9 ranged guy kills the ratz to summon alishar

claims.text: Alishar can summon Chronos, Platoon Chronos and Master Chronos. A cleric can kill them with Heal while keeping the party alive.
claims.say: cleric heal kills the chronos alishar summons

claims.text: Alishar drops the Key of Dimension. The leader picks it up and talks to the Violet Balloon, which moves the party to the bonus stage.
claims.say: leader takes alishars key to the violet balloon

claims.text: The Napoleon items and earrings from the LPQ bonus boxes are worth picking up; use them or sell them to an NPC or in the Free Market for mesos.
claims.say: grab the napoleons and earrings from lpq bonus, they sell

claims.text: With heavy HP washing, a character with roughly 9k or more HP, or a mage with about 1.8k or more, can tank the golems in the maze and take the place of a Dark Sight thief.
claims.say: a very high hp char can tank the golems instead of a ds thief

claims.text: Complete every quest on Maple Island before leaving at level 10, since you cannot come back to the island afterwards.
claims.say: do all the maple island quests before u leave, no coming back

claims.text: The four job training quests from the instructors can no longer be accepted once you pass level 20, so do them soon after your first advancement.
claims.say: do the job instructor quests before lvl 20 or they lock

claims.text: Manji and the Secret Group and To the Desert open at level 18 and cannot be accepted any more after level 29, so start them in time.
claims.say: manji and to the desert quests lock after lvl 29, grab em early

claims.text: To finish To the Desert you ride with Manji to Ariant five times; Karcasa in Ariant sends you back to Victoria Island quickly.
claims.say: to the desert = 5 trips to ariant w manji, karcasa brings u back

claims.text: The second part of the Evil Eye POLLUTED quest cannot be accepted after level 57, and the second part of the Curse Eye one cannot be accepted after level 65, so start those parts before the cutoff.
claims.say: polluted evil eye pt2 locks after 57, curse eye pt2 after 65

claims.text: A quest with a maximum accept level can still be handed in later, as long as you accepted it before passing that level.
claims.say: if u accepted a level locked quest in time u can finish it later

claims.text: After Help Kevin The Soldier's Vacation Plans you can drop both ripped ticket pieces, or just one, to unlock two separate Lost Piece of the VIP Ticket quests, and both can be completed.
claims.say: drop the ripped vip ticket pieces for 2 extra quests

claims.text: Wearing the Alcadno cape starts Russellon's Items for Experiment and wearing the Zenumist cape starts Helping Out Bedin, both around level 35.
claims.say: wear the alcadno or zenumist cape to unlock their lvl 35 quests

claims.text: The faction chains in Magatia at levels 52 and 70 (Destroy the Roid, Getting in the Way of Alcadno, Maed's Experiment, Carson's Experiment) only unlock while you wear a faction cape and have finished that faction's earlier quests.
claims.say: keep ur faction cape on to unlock the next magatia quests

claims.text: Byron's Recommendation Letter only shows up at level 30 and cannot be accepted once you have picked your second job.
claims.say: grab byrons recommendation letter at lvl 30 before 2nd job

claims.text: The Seed that Swallow Lost starts if you forfeit any Nolbu or Hongbu quest in progress and drop the seed Swallow gave you; it is lost for good once you complete Opening the Gourd.
claims.say: forfeit the nolbu hongbu quests then drop swallows seed for a bonus

claims.text: After finishing each storybook quest line (Shim Chung, Brotherly Love, Kong Ji, Sun and Moon, Nolbu, Axes, Goblin), drop the book to start a bonus quest from Wiz the Librarian.
claims.say: drop each storybook after its quest for a bonus quest from wiz

claims.text: Two bonus quests come from dropping the Sap of Nependeath: once after Ericsson's Reward before starting Elma's Nependeath Juice, and again before you accept Alfonse's Smile.
claims.say: drop the sap of nependeath at the right step for bonus quests

claims.text: The level 55 Pirate quests (Outlaw in the Sea, Eliminating the Pirates, Pirate's Map, Captain Lord Pirate) cannot be accepted after level 100, although you can still enter the Pirate Party Quest later.
claims.say: do the lvl 55 pirate quests before 100, they lock after

claims.text: When you obtain the white essence, drop, trade or store it to pick up The Lost White Essence quest; it is gone once you hand in the black essence.
claims.say: drop the white essence when u get it for a bonus quest

claims.text: Visiting Authorized Personnel Only triggers the level 52 quest Parwen the Ghost.
claims.say: go to authorized personnel only to trigger parwen the ghost

claims.text: After finishing the quest to kill Papulatus (Protect Ludibrium), drop the Ludibrium Medal to unlock the bonus quest The Lost Medal.
claims.say: drop the ludibrium medal after the papulatus quest for a bonus

claims.text: Dropping the Saddle after Monster Riding starts Lost Saddle, but it needs roughly 600 drops including 200 Dark Yeti skins from only a few spawns, so it is rarely worth doing.
claims.say: lost saddle needs like 600 drops incl 200 dark yeti skins, skip it

claims.text: Drop the Pheromone Perfume after completing the quest that follows Monster Riding to unlock a bonus quest.
claims.say: drop the pheromone perfume after its quest for a bonus quest

claims.text: After Lost in Translation 2, drop the Translated Communique before you complete Lost in Translation 3 to get a bonus quest.
claims.say: drop the translated communique before lost in translation 3

claims.text: Beginner characters cannot do Cleaning Up the Streets in New Leaf City, which also locks Urban Warrior and Cool as Ice for them.
claims.say: beginners cant do cleaning up the streets so no cool as ice either

claims.text: Cool as Ice is given by Icebyrd Slimm after you have completed all the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest quests and are carrying a Mark of Narician.
claims.say: cool as ice needs the cwkpq quests done plus a mark of narician

claims.text: After your 4th job advancement, drop the Maple Warrior 10 skill book you receive to start a bonus quest; it cannot be accepted once you have used the book.
claims.say: drop the maple warrior book before using it for a bonus quest

claims.text: Tatamo's Suggestion can no longer be accepted after you reach 4th job.
claims.say: get tatamos suggestion done before 4th job

claims.text: Do not drop quest items unless you know the chain gives a replacement quest; some have no replacement, though forfeiting the quest sometimes recovers it.
claims.say: dont drop quest items unless u know theres a replacement quest

claims.text: Hunters at 40-50 can use Arrow Bomb on Lupins and Zombie Lupins at Monkey Forest II, standing on the left side to hit mobs on three platforms at once.
claims.say: hunter 40s: arrow bomb lupins from the left, hits 3 platforms

claims.text: Ludibrium Party Quest is a common option for archers in their 40s; players disagree on how easy it is to find a party for it.
claims.say: lpq is decent in the 40s if you can find a party

claims.text: Other archer spots in the 40s and 50s: Platoon Chronos, Master Chronos and Truckers in Ludibrium, or Mysterious Path 3 and Ghost Ship 1 in the upper 40s.
claims.say: 40s-50s try platoon or master chronos, truckers, mp3 or gs1

claims.text: One levelling path: leech or LPQ to 51, Ludibrium Maze Party Quest to 58, then leech to 70; players without leech money or a Bishop friend often stay in LMPQ until 70.
claims.say: 51-58 lmpq, then leech or keep doing lmpq to 70

claims.text: Voodoos are a suggested training spot from 70 to about 74.
claims.say: voodoos are fine from 70 to about 74

claims.text: Wolf Spiders are suggested from 75 to 85, but an archer at 75-80 can find them deadly, so be sturdy before going.
claims.say: wolf spiders at 75 are rough, be careful

claims.text: The 3rd job advancement at 70 needs a Dark Crystal, so have one ready before starting the quest.
claims.say: 3rd job at 70 needs a dark crystal, bring one

claims.text: Warrior first job needs level 10 and 35 STR. The instructor is Dances with Balrog in the Warriors' Sanctuary in Perion.
claims.say: warrior 1st job: lvl 10, 35 str, dances with balrog in perion

claims.text: Bowman first job needs level 10 and 25 DEX. The instructor is Athena Pierce in the Bowman Instructional School in Henesys.
claims.say: bowman 1st job: lvl 10, 25 dex, athena pierce in henesys

claims.text: Magician first job needs level 8 and 20 INT. The instructor is Grendel the Really Old in the Magic Library in Ellinia.
claims.say: magician 1st job: lvl 8, 20 int, grendel in ellinia library

claims.text: Thief first job needs level 10 and 25 DEX. The instructor is the Dark Lord in the Thieves' Hideout in Kerning City.
claims.say: thief 1st job: lvl 10, 25 dex, dark lord in kerning

claims.text: Pirate first job needs level 10 and 20 DEX. The instructor is Kyrin in the Navigation Room of Nautilus.
claims.say: pirate 1st job: lvl 10, 20 dex, kyrin in nautilus

claims.text: Second job needs level 30. Talk to your first job instructor for a letter to another instructor, collect 30 Dark Marbles from the monsters in that map, take the Proof of a Hero back to your first job instructor to advance.
claims.say: 2nd job: letter, 30 dark marbles, proof of a hero, back to instructor

claims.text: The second job test maps: warriors go to West Rocky Mountain IV in Perion, bowmen to Road to the Dungeon in Henesys, magicians to the Forest North of Ellinia, thieves to the Construction Site North of Kerning City.
claims.say: 2nd job test spots: rocky mtn 4, road to dungeon, ellinia north, kerning site

claims.text: After the Black Charm, your first job instructor gives a Necklace of Strength to bring to the third job instructor, who sends you to the Holy Stone; pass its 5 questions to get the Necklace of Wisdom and return to advance.
claims.say: charm to necklace of strength, holy stone quiz, necklace of wisdom, advance

claims.text: The Holy Stone is in the Holy Ground, behind the wooden door at the top right of Sharp Cliff II. Quick route: take the Danger Zone Taxi in El Nath to Ice Valley II, talk to Jeff to reach Sharp Cliff I, then go up one map.
claims.say: holy stone: danger zone taxi, jeff, then up from sharp cliff 1

claims.text: The Holy Stone area is cold and drains health, so sit in a chair or keep potting while answering its questions, or you can die before you finish.
claims.say: sit on a chair or pot up at the holy stone, the cold hurts

claims.text: Before entering the dark clone fight for the Black Charm, bring All Cure Potions and attack potions, since the clone can inflict status effects and hits hard.
claims.say: bring all cure and attack pots for the dark clone

claims.text: Holy Stone questions of the form which NPC is not in a town: Roel is not in Ellinia, Teo is not in Henesys, Luke is not in Kerning City.
claims.say: holy stone: roel not in ellinia, teo not henesys, luke not kerning

claims.text: More Holy Stone NPC answers: Francois is not in Perion, Sophia is not in Orbis, Sophia or Elma the Housekeeper is not in El Nath depending on the options shown, and Teo is not on Maple Island.
claims.say: holy stone: francois perion, sophia orbis, sophia or elma el nath

claims.text: Holy Stone item and quest answers: give Maya Weird Medicine; Fairy Wing is not needed for Hero's Gladius; Arwen and the Glass Shoes is repeatable; Alcaster and the Dark Crystal needs the highest level to begin.
claims.say: holy stone: weird medicine for maya, arwen glass shoes repeatable

claims.text: Holy Stone general answers: Pizza recovers 400 HP; Sunrise Dew recovering 3000 MP is the false pairing; level 1 to 2 needs 15 exp; Sera is the first NPC; Amherst or Southperry is the town not in Victoria Island. The Sera answer is disputed.
claims.say: holy stone: pizza 400 hp, 15 exp for lvl 2, amherst not victoria

claims.text: Holy Stone NPC trivia: Peter is not in Alpha Platoon's network, Shane has nothing to do with refinement or item creation, Vicious has nothing to do with pets, and Chief Stan is Alex's father.
claims.say: holy stone: peter not alpha platoon, vicious not pets, chief stan

claims.text: Holy Stone job trivia: Mage/Outlaw is not a second job; the false first job requirement is Thief with 20 LUK, while Archer with 25 DEX is correct; Athena's green eyes mean DEX; Dark Lord stays in the Thieves' Hideout.
claims.say: holy stone: archer needs 25 dex, mage/outlaw isnt a 2nd job

claims.text: For fourth job you can kill the two bosses: Manon drops the Heroic Pentagon and Griffey drops the Heroic Star.
claims.say: manon drops the heroic pentagon, griffey drops the heroic star

claims.text: For free Eos Rock Scrolls, take The Lost Guard from the Lost Soldier on the 93rd floor of Eos Tower: bring 15 propellers from Helly and 15 worn-out goggles from Chirppy on floors 92 and 91, for 20 scrolls. Spawns are poor.
claims.say: lost guard quest on eos 93f gives 20 eos rock scrolls

claims.text: LMPQ is a maze of 16 rooms: 15 contain boxes that release monsters carrying passes, and room 16 is the exit where the party hands the passes in.
claims.say: lmpq: break boxes, kill the mobs, loot passes, meet in room 16

claims.text: The exp handed out at the end of LMPQ grows with the number of passes the party turns in, so more kills before the exit means a bigger payout.
claims.say: more passes turned in at the end means more lmpq exp

claims.text: The party needs at least 30 passes at room 16 to finish LMPQ and receive the reward.
claims.say: you need 30 or more passes to clear lmpq

claims.text: A fast LMPQ path: start in room 1, take the middle portal through rooms 8, 15, 7, 14, 6, 13 and 5, then the left portal to 9, and the middle portal from 9 into exit room 16.
claims.say: lmpq path: 1-8-15-7-14-6-13-5 middle, left to 9, middle to 16

claims.text: Room 1 of LMPQ is packed with Coolie Zombies, so clear it before moving on since everyone starts there anyway.
claims.say: kill the coolie zombies in lmpq room 1 before you leave

claims.text: Room 9 of LMPQ has Dark Jr. Yetis and Master Chronos; only stop to clear it if the party is moving very fast.
claims.say: lmpq room 9 is optional, only clear it if your party is quick

claims.text: If you lose your way in the LMPQ maze, keep taking the middle portal and you will reach room 16 eventually.
claims.say: lost in lmpq? keep using the middle portal, it ends at 16

claims.text: Pick up the passes from your own kills right away in LMPQ so the rest of the party is not left waiting for them.
claims.say: loot your own passes in lmpq so nobody has to wait

claims.text: The spells of LMPQ monsters, such as Tauromacis lightning and Coolie Zombie poison, push you back but do practically no damage.
claims.say: lmpq mob spells just knock you back, they dont really hurt

claims.text: Keep two empty Use inventory slots before finishing LMPQ, otherwise the reward is not given.
claims.say: keep 2 free use slots or you miss the lmpq reward

claims.text: If a disconnect throws you out of LMPQ, change channel and reform the party; a member still holding passes from the broken run keeps the party from entering again.
claims.say: if anyone still has old lmpq passes the party cant get back in

claims.text: LMPQ rewards are mostly large potion stacks such as Sorcerer Elixir, Mana Elixir, Ginger Ale, Red Bean Sundae and Power Elixir, which you can drink or sell to an NPC for mesos.
claims.say: lmpq pays in potion stacks, drink them or npc them for mesos

claims.text: LMPQ can also reward big bundles of Diamond Arrow for Bow or Diamond Arrow for Crossbow, which archers can use right away.
claims.say: lmpq can give big stacks of diamond arrows for archers

claims.text: Balanced Fury is a strong throwing star that is crafted rather than bought, usable by star-throwing thieves from level 70.
claims.say: balanced fury is a crafted star thieves can throw from 70

claims.text: The Balanced Fury recipe needs one Tao of Sight, one Tao of Harmony, one Tao of Shadows, 100 Black Crystals and 30 Typhon Feathers.
claims.say: fury needs 3 taos, 100 black crystals and 30 typhon feathers

claims.text: The NPC who crafts Balanced Fury is Fiona, found at Dead Man's Gorge in the Phantom Forest.
claims.say: fiona in dead man's gorge, phantom forest, crafts the fury

claims.text: The three Taos for Balanced Fury come out of Gachapon; the author points to the New Leaf City machine as a good one to use.
claims.say: taos come from gachapon, the nlc one works fine

claims.text: Typhon Feathers, needed for Balanced Fury, are dropped by Typhons.
claims.say: typhon feathers drop off typhons

claims.text: Black Crystals come from Black Crystal Ore, which drops from monsters in many different areas.
claims.say: black crystals come from black crystal ore, lots of mobs drop it

claims.text: The Mushroom Shrine Gachapon gives out almost nothing but scrolls, mostly dark scrolls for every equip slot, and it is the machine that can drop a Chaos Scroll 60%.
claims.say: shrine gach is nearly all scrolls, chaos scrolls come from it

claims.text: The New Leaf City Gachapon is the one to roll when hunting a White Scroll; its other notable prizes are the Stonetooth Sword and a long list of 100% and 60% accessory and armor scrolls.
claims.say: want a white scroll? roll the nlc gach

claims.text: Kerning City Gachapon is mostly thief gear plus claw and dagger scrolls; its big prizes are the Pink Gaia Cape and the Dragon Purple Sleeve, which are worth a lot when they roll high attack.
claims.say: kerning gach jackpot is pink gaia cape or dragon purple sleeve

claims.text: Sessions at the NLC and Kerning City Gachapons are swingy: without a White Scroll or a Pink Gaia Cape, most of what comes out is gear you can only sell to a shop.
claims.say: nlc and kerning gach are all or nothing

claims.text: Mushroom Shrine and Showa Town Gachapons give steadier returns: even without a Chaos Scroll or Sky Ski, Shrine still yields sellable scrolls and Showa yields INT gear.
claims.say: shrine and showa gach are the safer bets

claims.text: Showa Town Gachapon prizes include the Sky Ski, INT pieces such as Yellow Work Gloves and Red Marker, Maple Leaf accessories, and many 100% armor scrolls.
claims.say: showa gach has sky skis, int gloves and 100% scrolls

claims.text: Perion Gachapon is often overlooked: its value is spread across many items, notably the Taru Spirit Cape, the Pink Adventurer Cape and several endgame warrior weapons such as the Dragon Claymore.
claims.say: perion gach is overlooked, capes and dragon weapons

claims.text: Henesys Gachapon is bowman-themed; the prizes people chase there are Brown Work Gloves, the Naricain Jewel and a high-attack Dragon Shiner Bow.
claims.say: henesys gach is for brown work gloves or a good shiner bow

claims.text: Sleepywood Gachapon is a grab bag: Red Emerald Earrings, Maple Leaf, the Naricain Jewel, lots of accessory and pet-equip scrolls, and weapon stimulators such as the Dagger Forging Stimulator.
claims.say: sleepywood gach is random stuff, earrings and lots of scrolls

claims.text: The CBD Gachapon in Singapore offers the Taru Totem, the White Raccoon Mask and Elemental Wand 7, along with the Singapore Flag weapons and many 60% and 100% scrolls.
claims.say: cbd gach has taru totem, white raccoon mask, ele wand 7

claims.text: Ellinia Gachapon is magician-themed: mage gloves, shoes and overalls, the Dragon Staff, Dragon Wand and Phoenix Wand, plus magic attack scrolls for staffs, wands and gloves.
claims.say: ellinia gach is mage gear and wand/staff scrolls

claims.text: Each job town's Gachapon has attack scrolls for its own job's weapons: Perion swords, axes, blunts and spears, Ellinia staffs and wands, Henesys bows and crossbows, Kerning claws and daggers, Nautilus guns and knucklers.
claims.say: each town gach has scrolls for its own class weapons

claims.text: To reach Phantom Forest, ride the subway from Kerning City to New Leaf City, then take the NLC Taxi at the far left of town to Haunted House.
claims.say: subway to nlc, far-left taxi to haunted house

claims.text: Bigfoot can spawn in eight maps: the five Twisted Paths, Forgotten Path, Evil Rising and The Evil Dead.
claims.say: bigfoot: 5 twisted paths, forgotten path, evil rising, evil dead

claims.text: All five Twisted Paths maps share the same layout with five portals and aren't numbered in game, which is why people get lost there.
claims.say: twisted paths all look the same, 5 portals each

claims.text: Changing channel inside a Twisted Paths map always puts you just left of the middle portal.
claims.say: cc in twisted paths puts you left of the middle portal

claims.text: A loop through all five Twisted Paths starts and ends at Dead Man's Gorge: right portal, then rightmost, leftmost, second from right, second from right again, then middle; change channel and repeat.
claims.say: gorge loop: right, rightmost, leftmost, 2nd right x2, middle

claims.text: To reach Forgotten Path, go from Dead Man's Gorge through the right portal, then take the middle portal or the one just right of it.
claims.say: forgotten path: gorge, right portal, then middle

claims.text: From Haunted House to Evil Rising: take the rightmost portal, then the portal in the middle of the next map beside a tree, one portal to the left, the leftmost portal, then press up at the wooden sign on the upper half.
claims.say: evil rising: rightmost, middle by tree, left, leftmost, sign

claims.text: From Dead Man's Gorge to The Evil Dead: take the rightmost portal, then go 3 portals right, 2 left and 1 left, and press up at the wooden sign at the top middle.
claims.say: evil dead from the gorge: rightmost, then 3 right, 2 left, 1 left

claims.text: Bigfoot only respawns once its timer is up and the monsters in its map get killed, so clearing mobs is more reliable but slower.
claims.say: kill the mobs in bigfoot's map once his timer is up

claims.text: Riding through the Bigfoot maps on a mount without killing mobs is quicker and takes less attention, but relies on someone else having cleared them.
claims.say: or just cycle the maps on a mount, less reliable

claims.text: A LUK mage keeps base LUK around 105 to wear the level 103 Elemental Staff, which adds extra magic attack for Ice and Lightning spells. Keep base LUK as low as possible beyond that and use AP resets.
claims.say: luk mage keeps about 105 luk for the elemental staff

claims.text: A LUK mage is cheap to gear and can wear any armor, plus it gets the elemental bonus. It hits weaker than other mages before level 103, needs many AP resets at 130, and is hard to resell items for.
claims.say: luk mage: cheap gear, any armor, but slower early and needs resets

claims.text: At level 130 a LUK mage buys many AP resets to take LUK down to zero, or keeps the LUK until about level 163 if leveling fast.
claims.say: luk mage resets luk at 130, or waits until 163 if leveling fast

claims.text: A LUK mage with good gear can nearly match a lukless mage at level 103, but the lukless mage stays slightly ahead in raw magic; the main appeal is gear that gives both INT and LUK.
claims.say: luk mage can nearly match lukless but lukless is a bit ahead

claims.text: Mages should scroll earrings for magic attack and INT, never LUK, because INT and magic attack both add to total magic; earrings with magic attack and INT are a must-have slot.
claims.say: scroll mage earrings for int or matt, never luk

claims.text: Good mage earrings are Fallen Leaf Earrings, which sometimes come with 1 to 2 extra magic attack and are cheap, and Crystal Leaf Earrings, which give 3 INT clean and 6 slots but cost far more.
claims.say: fallen leaf earrings are cheap, crystal leaf are better but pricey

claims.text: For a mage hat, a Zakum Helmet gives about 15 LUK and 15 INT; if you cannot afford one, use an ordinary helmet with magic attack and INT. LUK on gear stops mattering once you drop LUK at 130.
claims.say: zakum helmet is the best mage hat, cheap one with matt int till then

claims.text: Mages should aim for a level 38 overall with 8 INT and 5 LUK clean, scrolled with one 30% and nine 60% scrolls; a level 88 overall is better if you will not resell. Never scroll LUK onto it.
claims.say: mage overall: lv38 with int and luk clean, scroll int not luk

claims.text: A clean Esther Shield with 2 or more INT is a budget mage shield, since shield magic attack scrolls cost a lot. With more money, use a Maple Shield (10 slots) scrolled with INT scrolls.
claims.say: esther shield on a budget, maple shield with int scrolls later

claims.text: For mage gloves, take a high-level pair with plenty of INT and LUK, scrolled with a 30% and some 60% scrolls. Glitter Gloves resell better since lukless mages like them.
claims.say: high level gloves with int and luk, glitter gloves resell better

claims.text: Mage weapons worth using: Poison Mushroom, Maple Lama Staff, Mystic Cane, Evil Wings, Kage, Pyogo Mushroom, the level 70 Elemental Wand and the level 103 Elemental Staff.
claims.say: good mage weapons: maple lama staff, mystic cane, elemental wand/staff

claims.text: The author sees level 26 as the best point to start buying leech.
claims.say: 26 is a good level to start buying leech

claims.text: Levels 30-36 can be leeched on Jr. Wraiths in Line 1 <Area 2> of the Kerning Subway.
claims.say: 30-36 leech on jr wraiths in line 1 area 2

claims.text: Levels 43-53 can also be leeched on Wraiths in Line 1 <Area 4> of the Kerning Subway.
claims.say: 43-53 wraiths in line 1 area 4 work too

claims.text: In Singapore's Ghost Ship maps, leech at Ghost Ship 1 for 53-55, Ghost Ship 5 for 55-58 and Ghost Ship 2 for 58-65.
claims.say: 53-65 leech in the singapore ghost ship maps

claims.text: Leech exp depends mostly on how fast the seller clears the spawns, not on the seller's level.
claims.say: leech exp is about seller speed, not seller level

claims.text: Zakum parties often sell Zakum Helmets to buyers, and the sale money is divided evenly among the main party of attackers and the bishop.
claims.say: zak helm sales usually get split evenly in the main party

claims.text: If you are paying for a Zakum Helmet, switch off your pet's auto-loot before the run and pick up just one helmet unless you ask first.
claims.say: buying a helm? turn pet loot off and only grab one

claims.text: The bishop in a Zakum run should be ready to go back to the entrance and open a Mystic Door so party members can rejoin quickly.
claims.say: bishop, be ready to door people back to the zak entrance

claims.text: In a Zakum run the leader normally picks up any skill book drops and notes everyone's names so the split can be paid out later.
claims.say: leader loots the books in zak and tracks names for splits

claims.text: Attackers at Zakum are expected to use attack-boosting potions at the very least.
claims.say: bring attack pots for zak, everyone uses them

claims.text: Horntail attackers always drink attack potions such as Onyx Apples or Gelt Chocolate.
claims.say: use attack pots like onyx apples or gelt at horntail

claims.text: Horntail runs share loot evenly like Zakum, except a Horntail Necklace usually goes to a member picked by level or by range.
claims.say: ht necklace priority usually goes by level or range

claims.text: On the two pre-heads a Corsair can keep shooting freely until the head's horn lights up, which signals an attack is starting. Their attacks are slow and easy to dodge, so this is the Corsair's best stretch of the fight.
claims.say: on the pre heads just keep shooting till the horn lights up

claims.text: The big charge-up attack from the first two heads covers the whole map. Dismount from your ship just before the charge-up animation finishes and you avoid it easily.
claims.say: dismount right before the big charge up finishes

claims.text: On the first pre-head the icicle attack shows exactly where it will land. If you stand in the gap between two targeted spots you sometimes do not even need to dismount.
claims.say: icicles show where they land, stand in the gap

claims.text: The lightning attack of the second pre-head (and of Head C) marks random spots you cannot see from the ship, and it fires at uneven timing. Dismount almost at once, use Rapid Fire until the strike lands, then keep attacking.
claims.say: lightning timing varies, dismount fast and rapid fire till it lands

claims.text: If you are getting hit by many attacks while on the ship during the main body fight, dismount and use Rapid Fire for a few seconds to recover your footing. Those few seconds help more than you would expect.
claims.say: getting spammed on the ship? hop off and rapid fire a bit

claims.text: Never stand idle during Horntail: whenever you have to dismount and cannot remount because another attack is coming, fire Rapid Fire so every second adds damage.
claims.say: if you cant get back on the ship just rapid fire

claims.text: After you take a hit, or an attack misses you, you are briefly unable to be hurt again. That window often lets you ignore the next incoming Horntail attack.
claims.say: after a hit youre invincible a sec so you can skip the next one

claims.text: Horntail has eight body parts, but a Corsair only needs to watch the three heads. The hand is also worth watching in some situations.
claims.say: only watch the 3 heads, hands help sometimes

claims.text: Corsairs do poorly on the leg and tail, so only attack those parts when Head A and Head B have used weapon cancel at the same moment.
claims.say: dont hit leg or tail unless both heads weapon cancel together

claims.text: You count as dismounted the moment you press the Battleship button; the ship leaving is only a visual animation afterward. You can therefore time the dismount very late.
claims.say: you are off the ship the second you press it, anim is just visual

claims.text: Take your attack potions while you are off the ship, not while riding it.
claims.say: drink attack pots when youre dismounted

claims.text: Head A is the first main head to kill and the trickiest. Stand where the left rock and right wing cannot hit you, and dismount as soon as it lowers for its icicle attack, since you cannot react once it starts.
claims.say: vs head a dismount as soon as it lowers, stand clear of rock and wing

claims.text: If Head A uses weapon cancel, jump off and put Homing Beacon on Head B instead of wasting time.
claims.say: head a weapon cancel? jump and homing beacon head b

claims.text: Head B usually dies last. For its long-animation attack, dismount, Rapid Fire briefly and dodge once the ground animation shows. Its other attack always hits the whole map but charges slowly, so it is easy to dismount from.
claims.say: head b is easy, watch the ground animation then dodge

claims.text: Head C is next after Head A. Stay left of the red line so the rock misses you. Its full-map charge attack has a delay, so fire a couple of cannon shots before dismounting. A purple hand animation means a 1 damage hit.
claims.say: head c: stay left of the red line, shoot a bit before dismounting

claims.text: On the first pre-head, putting a mule (or a Bishop if running without mules) on the bottom makes its 1/1 icicle attack target the bottom, so it will not hit the platform you attack from.
claims.say: put a mule at the bottom so the icicle skips your platform

claims.text: Corsairs around level 190+ can ignore the fast, hard-hitting version of the lightning attacks and only dismount before the delayed 1/1 one; the ship has enough HP and their avoid is decent.
claims.say: at 190+ you can just tank the quick hit and dodge the delayed one

claims.text: Your ship takes exactly the damage you would take: a 1 damage hit while mounted costs the ship 1. The hand is handy because when you mess up it can hit you instead of something worse.
claims.say: ship takes the same dmg you would, so hand hits are harmless

claims.text: Thief and archer HP can be washed up to about 30k, the most a character can reach.
claims.say: 30k hp is basically the max you can wash to

claims.text: When MP washing, keep the number of MP washes close to your base INT to keep costs low, and only bother once you have at least about 150 INT.
claims.say: keep base int near your mp wash count, 150+ int to be worth it

claims.text: Warriors hardly need to plan HP washing, since they gain plenty of HP naturally.
claims.say: warriors dont really need to plan hp washing

claims.text: The Crown Flyer is a strong Pepe map for a Bishop or Arch Mage, whose wide attacks clear it quickly, but it takes active play rather than AFK.
claims.say: bishops or archmages can clear the crown flyer pepes fast

claims.text: The Crown Flyer also serves as a leech map around levels 55-60, with exp roughly on par with Roids.
claims.say: crown flyer is ok leech for 55-60, about like roids

claims.text: Equips that sell to NPCs drop often at The Crown Flyer and some fetch a good price, so the trip earns mesos on top of the beaks.
claims.say: the equip drops at crown flyer sell well to npcs too

claims.text: Players who only want to AFK farm are better off at Authorized Personnel Only than at The Crown Flyer.
claims.say: for afk farming go to authorized personnel only instead

claims.text: To marry, both partners must be at least level 10, of any job, and in a party together.
claims.say: both need lv 10 and be in a party to get married

claims.text: Wedding preparation starts by talking to Thomas Swift in Henesys, who handles the trip to Amoria.
claims.say: talk to thomas swift in henesys to start the wedding stuff

claims.text: The groom asks Moony for an engagement ring: bring Proof of Love from any four of the six town Nanas (Henesys, Ellinia, Perion, Kerning, Orbis, Ludibrium), then pick one of four rings and supply its materials and mesos.
claims.say: groom gets 4 proof of love from the nanas, then moony makes a ring

claims.text: Double-click the engagement ring box to propose, and the partner must accept. Dropping the ring or empty box breaks the engagement, and you can pick someone else freely until you have proposed.
claims.say: double click the ring box to propose, they have to accept

claims.text: For a Cathedral wedding the groom buys a Cathedral wedding ticket from the Cash Shop and books it with the NPC Victoria, listing wished gifts; the premium ticket adds the party map and gift vault.
claims.say: cathedral needs a wedding ticket, then book it with victoria

claims.text: For the Cathedral the bride also needs the Officiator's Permission: High Priest John sends her to Mom and Dad at Meet the Parents, who want two Proof of Love for the Parent's Blessing to bring back.
claims.say: bride gets the parents blessing, then permission from john

claims.text: For a Chapel wedding the groom buys a Chapel wedding ticket from the Cash Shop and books it with the NPC Wayne.
claims.say: chapel wedding: buy the chapel ticket and book with wayne

claims.text: The bride starts the wedding with Assistant Nicole (Cathedral) or Assistant Bonnie (Chapel). Guests double-click the invitation in their ETC tab and only need to be on the same channel; they may need to relog to receive it.
claims.say: guests double click the invite on the same channel to get in

claims.text: Inside, click the NPC at the bottom to start the ceremony once guests are ready; otherwise it starts by itself halfway through the timer (10 minutes for the Cathedral, 5 for the Chapel).
claims.say: click the npc at the bottom to start or it starts at half time

claims.text: The couple must stay in the cake room until the timer ends to be officially married and get the ring.
claims.say: stay in the cake room till the timer ends or youre not married

claims.text: Becoming a Warrior at level 10 requires 35 STR, and the early maps do not need any DEX, so early AP can go straight into STR.
claims.say: need 35 str to turn warrior at lvl 10

claims.text: If you begin missing Pigs or Ludibrium monsters, add about one DEX per level for a while; warriors normally need only a small DEX investment for accuracy.
claims.say: missing pigs? add a dex point per level for a bit

claims.text: Pages can stay low on DEX because job mastery, Maple weapons and a Zakum Helmet cover accuracy; if you are unsure, take a little extra DEX, since AP can be reset later.
claims.say: page can run low dex, zakum helm and maple weps help acc

claims.text: Swordman SP: 5 into Improving HP Recovery, 10 into Improving Max HP Increase, then max Slash Blast and Power Strike; leftovers can go to Endure, HP Recovery or Iron Body.
claims.say: swordman sp: hp skills first then max power strike + slash blast

claims.text: Leave Final Attack at zero on a Page; it ends up lowering a Paladin's overall damage compared with spending those points elsewhere.
claims.say: dont put any sp in final attack as a page

claims.text: White Knight charges are weapon specific: swords use Fire, Ice and Thunder Charge, blunt weapons use Flame, Blizzard and Lightning Charge, so check your weapon before spending third-job SP.
claims.say: charges differ for sword and bw so check before spending sp

claims.text: Decide between sword and blunt weapon by second job; switching after third job means respending the weapon-specific charges plus a large amount of third and fourth job SP, which is expensive in resets.
claims.say: pick sword or bw early, switching after 3rd job costs a ton

claims.text: White Knight SP: max the Fire and Ice charges for your weapon (either order), then Lightning Charge and Charged Blow, and spend any leftovers as you like.
claims.say: wk sp: max fire and ice charge, then lightning and charged blow

claims.text: Horntail's arms keep draining a seduced warrior's MP to nothing, so strong MP recovery matters because it lets you afford Hero's Will to cure the seduce.
claims.say: ht arms drain your mp, mp recovery keeps hero's will usable

claims.text: Fourth-job Paladin priority is Advanced Charge, then Blast, then Holy Charge, then Power Stance; Heaven's Hammer, Achilles and the rest are personal preference once the core skills are in.
claims.say: paladin 4th: advanced charge, blast, holy charge, then stance

claims.text: Some Paladins put Power Stance ahead of Holy Charge because it helps in bosses and grinding, and they favour fighting elemental-weak monsters over chasing the best neutral damage, leaving Holy Charge unspent.
claims.say: some pallies get stance before holy charge, it helps a lot

claims.text: The Advanced Charge skill book is a Zakum drop that few people want, so Paladins can often tag along on a Zakum run just to collect it.
claims.say: advanced charge book drops off zak, ask for a carry run

claims.text: Use Holy Charge on monsters with no elemental weakness, as long as they do not resist holy; against elemental-weak monsters use the matching charge instead.
claims.say: holy charge for neutral mobs, otherwise match their weakness

claims.text: Crushed Skull, a one-handed blunt weapon wearable from level 120, is among the best weapons a Paladin can use, and only Pages have blunt weapon mastery and booster to go with it.
claims.say: crushed skull is about the best weapon a paladin can use

claims.text: Levels 15-20: Pig Beach is a good place for a warrior to train.
claims.say: 15-20 pig beach is good for warriors

claims.text: Levels 50-70: Mysterious Path 3 or the Forest of Golem.
claims.say: 50-70 mysterious path 3 or forest of golem

claims.text: Levels 70-80: more Forest of Golem or Voodoos; golem spawns may be thin, but Voodoo maps are usually packed and let you build up your charge.
claims.say: 70-80 forest of golem or voodoos, voodoo maps are usually packed

claims.text: Levels 90-100: Spirit Vikings are excellent, and Rextons are another option.
claims.say: 90-100 spirit vikings are great, rextons work too

claims.text: The Qualm area of Temple of Time offers good drops for making mesos.
claims.say: qualm monk area in tot drops good stuff for mesos

claims.text: Bossing-minded Paladins can start Zakum runs around level 135, and Horntail becomes an option at 155.
claims.say: zak from around 135, ht from 155

claims.text: A warrior does not have to HP wash to boss at normal levels and can manage without a Hyper Body, though many still wash.
claims.say: warriors dont need hp washing to boss, hyper body isnt required

claims.text: Warriors get a large HP return from HP washing because each MP point they trade is worth a lot of HP, so raising MP first, for example with INT gear or temporary base INT that is reset later, pays off.
claims.say: warriors wash really well, int gear then reset the int

claims.text: Black Crow and Headless Horseman are weak to lightning, so a Paladin kills them well with Lightning Charge.
claims.say: use lightning charge on black crow and headless horseman

claims.text: Zakum's body is easy for a Paladin but the arms are awkward: Blast single arms because neighbours differ in weakness, or use Advanced Charge from the bottom-right platform to catch three arms.
claims.say: zak arms are messy: blast single arms or adv charge from low right

claims.text: Magicians can take first job at level 8, so leave Maple Island at 8 and head straight to Ellinia to advance.
claims.say: mages can job at 8, go to ellinia right after maple island

claims.text: As a new magician, max Magic Claw first.
claims.say: new mage? max magic claw first

claims.text: Run Kerning City Party Quest from about 21 to 30, then make the Cleric advancement.
claims.say: kpq from 21 to 30, then go cleric

claims.text: Monster Carnival is a quick way to level a Cleric from 30 to about 43.
claims.say: cpq is good for a cleric from 30 to about 43

claims.text: Around 43, scroll a clean Maple Lama Staff with 100% magic attack scrolls and use it until your next weapon.
claims.say: scroll a maple lama staff with 100% matt scrolls for your 40s

claims.text: A Maple Shine Wand is a good weapon for a Cleric or Priest from level 64.
claims.say: maple shine wand is a good pick from 64

claims.text: At 51 switch to Ludibrium Maze Party Quest and run it until about 64.
claims.say: at 51 run lmpq until about 64

claims.text: Party up at Ghost Ship 2 from about 64 to 70, and keep training there after the Priest advancement until 75.
claims.say: party at ghost ship 2 from 64 to 75

claims.text: From 75 to 81, a paid leech at the Wolf Spider maps is the fastest way to get a Priest to max Holy Symbol.
claims.say: 75 to 81 a leech at wolf spiders gets max hs fastest

claims.text: For a Holy Symbol mule, keep LUK at base and put all AP into INT; others argue LUK mages save mesos because they can wear better robes and cheaper wands.
claims.say: for an hs mule go lukless, all int

claims.text: For levels 15 to 21 the standard spot is Line 1 <Area 1> in the Kerning subway. Melee and ranged classes can also use Henesys Hunting Ground I, and Ant Tunnel is a fallback.
claims.say: 15 to 21 go line 1 area 1, hunting ground 1 also works

claims.text: From level 21 to 30 run the Kerning City Party Quest or train at Land of Wild Boar II; Ant Tunnel is the fallback.
claims.say: 21 to 30 do kerning pq or land of wild boar 2

claims.text: Ranged classes can hit Chronos at 35 to 40, then Platoon Chronos or Master Chronos from 40 to 51 as alternatives to the carnival.
claims.say: ranged 35 to 40 chronos, 40 to 51 platoon or master chronos

claims.text: Mages can use Line 1 <Area 2> or Chronos around 35 to 40 and Platoon Chronos from 40 to 51 when they skip the carnival.
claims.say: mage 35 to 40 line 1 area 2 or chronos, then platoon chronos

claims.text: Melee classes at 51 to 75 can train at Ghost Ship 2, Forest of Golem or on Voodoos; Ghost Ship 5 and Mysterious Path 3 are alternatives.
claims.say: melee 51 to 75 ghost ship 2, forest of golem or voodoos

claims.text: Ranged classes at 51 to 75 can use Voodoos, with Water Goblins around 55 to 65, Ghost Ship 2 and Mysterious Path 3 as alternatives.
claims.say: ranged 51 to 75 voodoos or water goblins, or ghost ship 2

claims.text: Voodoos are a strong source of mesos for low-funded characters, from selling their equipment drops and Heartstoppers, and the area is less crowded than other grinding spots.
claims.say: voodoos make good money, heartstoppers and gear sell

claims.text: Want exp: go to Forest of Golem first, and move to Voodoos later when you want money more than raw exp, since Voodoos have a lower mob rate but better drops.
claims.say: forest of golem for exp, voodoos later for money

claims.text: Fire/Poison mages with the Poison Mist build can train at the Nest of a Dead Dragon from 75, an alternative to Wolf Spider Cavern and the Buddha spot.
claims.say: fp with poison mist build can grind nest of a dead dragon

claims.text: Bishops and Priests can party at Wolf Spider Cavern from 75 to 95, and a higher Holy Symbol makes them more welcome. Some players find parties hard to get there and prefer other maps.
claims.say: priests can party at wolf spiders with holy symbol

claims.text: Do not solo Temple of Time: the maps are huge and the quests drag on even for an Arch Mage or Bishop, so duo with a friend.
claims.say: dont solo temple of time, maps are huge, duo it

claims.text: You only get full exp from a partner's kills if your level is no more than 5 below the monster's level; spots marked solo until a level mean you must reach that level before leeching them.
claims.say: you need to be within 5 levels of the mob to get full party exp

claims.text: New Leaf City sells the best healing potions, so stock up there instead of using weaker town potions.
claims.say: nlc sells the best hp pots, stock up there

claims.text: In the Ludibrium Maze Party Quest every room has a left, middle and right portal, each moving you a fixed number of rooms ahead: left 4, middle 7, right 3.
claims.say: lmpq portals: left +4 rooms, middle +7, right +3

claims.text: Room numbers in the Ludibrium Maze wrap around once you count past room 15, so the portal steps loop back to the low rooms.
claims.say: lmpq room numbers wrap after 15, keep counting from the start

claims.text: Taking the middle portal two times in a row in the Ludibrium Maze lands you one room behind where you started.
claims.say: middle portal twice puts you one room back in lmpq

claims.text: If you lose track in the Ludibrium Maze, repeatedly taking the middle portal will eventually bring you to room 16.
claims.say: lost in lmpq? just keep taking the middle portal till room 16

claims.text: Some Phantom Forest portals only work in one direction, so after using one you need a different route to get back.
claims.say: some portals there are one way, plan your way back

claims.text: Headless Horseman can also spawn in The Evil Dead and Forgotten Path, but Bigfoot spawns there too, so be careful hunting in those maps.
claims.say: evil dead and forgotten path can spawn hh or bigfoot, careful

claims.text: To hunt Bigfoot or Headless Horseman, kill one regular mob in a spawn map so the boss has room to appear, check the map, then change channel and repeat.
claims.say: kill one mob to make room, check the map, then cc

claims.text: Staff Sergeant Charlie in Orbis runs a repeatable exchange: turn in 100 of the same etc item for exp, as many times as you want.
claims.say: charlie in orbis trades 100 of one etc item for exp, repeatable

claims.text: Maple Sword, the level 35 one-handed sword, drops from Block Golems.
claims.say: maple sword drops from block golems

claims.text: Maple Bow (level 35) drops from Block Golem, Tick-Tock, Iron Hog, Wild Boar and Wild Kargo.
claims.say: maple bow drops from wild boars and iron hogs

claims.text: Maple Crow, the level 35 crossbow, drops from Star Pixie and Block Golem.
claims.say: maple crow drops from star pixies and block golems

claims.text: Maple Claw (level 35) drops from Zombie Lupin, Wraith, Tauromacis, Zombie Mushroom, Jr. Cellion and Werewolf.
claims.say: maple claw drops from zombie mushrooms and zombie lupins

claims.text: Maple Staff (level 35) drops from Master Death Teddy, Sentinel and Ligator.
claims.say: maple staff drops from ligators and sentinels

claims.text: Maple Knuckle (level 35) drops from Zombie Mushroom, Drumming Bunny, Barnard Gray, Ginseng Jar and Hector.
claims.say: maple knuckle drops from zombie mushrooms and hectors

claims.text: Maple Gun (level 35) drops from Ghost Stump, Fire Sentinel, Jr. Seal, Stone Golem and Mithril Mutae.
claims.say: maple gun drops from ghost stumps and stone golems

claims.text: Spearmen have no level 35 Maple weapon; the level 25 Pumpkin Spear or the level 33 Orange Ski fill that gap.
claims.say: no lv35 maple spear, use a pumpkin spear instead

claims.text: Bandits have no level 35 Maple dagger; the level 35 Korean Fan is the usual stand-in.
claims.say: bandits use a korean fan at 35, no maple dagger

claims.text: The Maple Sword is a slow farm and worth skipping: Red Whip has the same attack and is slightly faster, though it gives speed instead of accuracy.
claims.say: skip the maple sword, red whip is just as good

claims.text: Maple Soul Singer, the level 43 one-handed sword, drops from Brown Teddy.
claims.say: maple soul singer drops from brown teddies

claims.text: Maple Dragon Axe (level 43) drops from Wild Boar and Cerebes.
claims.say: maple dragon axe drops from wild boars and cerebes

claims.text: Maple Doom Singer (level 43) drops from Cold Eye, Tauromacis, Drake, Brown Teddy, Lucida and Cerebes.
claims.say: maple doom singer drops from drakes and cold eyes

claims.text: Maple Impaler (level 43) drops from Toy Trojan, Lazy Buffy, Wild Boar and Yellow Lizard.
claims.say: maple impaler drops from wild boars and toy trojans

claims.text: Maple Scorpio (level 43) drops from Nependeath and Ligator.
claims.say: maple scorpio drops from ligators and nependeaths

claims.text: Maple Soul Searcher, the level 43 bow, drops from Drumming Bunny, Wild Boar, Red Drake, Iron Hog and Drake.
claims.say: maple soul searcher drops from wild boars and drakes

claims.text: Maple Crossbow (level 43) drops from Malady, Block Golem, King Block Golem and Red Lizard.
claims.say: maple crossbow drops from block golems and maladies

claims.text: Maple Wagner, the level 43 dagger, drops from Wild Boar, Bain, Trixter, Zombie Lupin and Red Lizard.
claims.say: maple wagner drops from wild boars and trixters

claims.text: Maple Lama Staff (level 43) drops from Ratz and Horny Mushroom.
claims.say: maple lama staff drops from horny mushrooms and ratz

claims.text: Maple Storm Finger, the level 43 knuckle, drops from Chipmunk, Chief Gray, Dark Rash and Dual Ghost Pirate.
claims.say: maple storm finger drops from chief grays and chipmunks

claims.text: Maple Storm Pistol (level 43) drops from Krip, Lorang, Transformed Yeti, Buffoon and Birk.
claims.say: maple storm pistol drops from krips and lorangs

claims.text: Maple Glory Sword, the level 64 one-handed sword, drops from Sr. Bellflower Root, The Book Ghost, Stone Golem and Hector.
claims.say: maple glory sword drops from stone golems and hectors

claims.text: Maple Steel Axe (level 64) drops from Lioner, Mixed Golem, Malady and Roid.
claims.say: maple steel axe drops from lioners and mixed golems

claims.text: Maple Havoc Hammer (level 64) drops from Dark Stone Golem, Miner Zombie, Red Drake, Panda and Neo Huroid.
claims.say: maple havoc hammer drops from dark stone golems

claims.text: Maple Soul Rohen, the level 64 two-handed sword, drops from Lioner, The Book Ghost, Mixed Golem, Buffy and Yeti.
claims.say: maple soul rohen drops from lioners and yetis

claims.text: Maple Demon Axe (level 64) drops from Jr. Lucida and Dark Drake, and only rarely from The Book Ghost and Sage Cat.
claims.say: maple demon axe drops from dark drakes

claims.text: Maple Belzet (level 64) drops from Dark Jr. Yeti, Coolie Zombie, Sage Cat and Master Soul Teddy.
claims.say: maple belzet drops from coolie zombies and sage cats

claims.text: Maple Soul Spear (level 64) drops from Cellion, MT-09, Hector, Sage Cat and Homun.
claims.say: maple soul spear drops from cellions and sage cats

claims.text: Maple Karstan, the level 64 polearm, drops only from Sr. Bellflower Root and Neo Huroid.
claims.say: maple karstan drops from sr bellflower roots

claims.text: Maple Kandiva Bow (level 64) drops from Miner Zombie, Sage Cat, Wild Kargo, Officer Skeleton and Transformed Yeti.
claims.say: maple kandiva bow drops from sage cats and wild kargos

claims.text: Maple Nishada, the level 64 crossbow, drops from Stone Golem, Dark Stone Golem, White Fang, Sage Cat and Dark Drake.
claims.say: maple nishada drops from stone golems and white fangs

claims.text: Maple Skanda, the level 64 claw, drops from Luster Pixie, Grizzly, Dyle, Soul Teddy and Zeno.
claims.say: maple skanda drops from luster pixies and soul teddies

claims.text: Maple Asura Dagger (level 64, adds STR) drops from Sr. Bellflower Root, Reindeer, Lazy Buffy and Neo Huroid, and only rarely from Hogul.
claims.say: maple asura dagger drops from sr bellflower roots

claims.text: Maple Dark Mate (level 64, adds LUK) drops from Skeleton Soldier, Mr. Alli, Soul Teddy, Ice Drake and Homun.
claims.say: maple dark mate drops from skeleton soldiers and mr alli

claims.text: Maple Shine Wand (level 64) drops from Samiho, Straw Target Dummy, Soul Teddy and Jr. Lucida.
claims.say: maple shine wand drops from samiho and soul teddies

claims.text: Maple Wisdom Staff (level 64) drops from Firebomb, Mr. Alli, Kru, the split-off Dark Pepe and Homun.
claims.say: maple wisdom staff drops from firebombs and homuns

claims.text: Maple Golden Claw, the level 64 knuckle, drops from Firebomb, Grupin, Hector, Jr. Lucida and Dark Drake.
claims.say: maple golden claw drops from grupins and firebombs

claims.text: The level 20 Maple Shield drops from Jr. Yeti and Platoon Chronos.
claims.say: lv20 maple shield drops from jr yetis and platoon chronos

claims.text: A Gunslinger/Corsair puts all AP into DEX until level 90, then adds STR (about 50, up to 60 by level 100) so a Concerto is wearable; Maple weapons need no STR, and later STR gear lets you reset some of it.
claims.say: all dex till 90 then add str so you can wear a concerto at 100

claims.text: To become a Pirate you need level 10 and at least 20 DEX, then speak to Kyrin in the Navigation Room at Nautilus Harbor.
claims.say: need lvl 10 and 20 dex, talk to kyrin in nautilus to be a pirate

claims.text: For second job, talk to Kyrin again; she sends you to a special map to collect 15 Potent Wind Crystals from Octopirates, then talk to her once more to become a Gunslinger.
claims.say: 2nd job: kyrin sends you to kill octopirates for 15 wind crystals

claims.text: For the final advancement, see your third-job instructor, then the fourth-job instructor in Leafre, who wants a Heroic Star from Griffey and a Heroic Pentagon from Manon.
claims.say: 4th job needs heroic star from griffey, heroic pentagon from manon

claims.text: Pirate SP: max Double Shot, Dash and Bullet Time, putting the last 11 points into Somersault Kick; it trains slower, but the extra avoidability and accuracy from Bullet Time pays off when sniping later.
claims.say: pirate sp: max double shot, dash, bullet time, rest in somersault

claims.text: The alternative build maxes Somersault Kick and leaves Bullet Time at 11, which mobs faster but means finishing Bullet Time with second-job SP later, and that is easy to forget.
claims.say: max somersault kick for mobbing, but dont forget bullet time later

claims.text: Gunslinger SP: max Invisible Shot (your mobbing skill) and Gun Mastery (steadies damage) first, then Recoil Shot, Wings, Blank Shot and Gun Booster, with any leftover points going into Grenade.
claims.say: gunslinger sp: invisible shot and gun mastery first, then the rest

claims.text: Outlaw SP: max Burst Fire first as your main attack, then Ice Splitter, Flamethrower, Octopus and Homing Beacon, since Homing Beacon is needed to max Bullseye later; Gaviota can wait.
claims.say: outlaw sp: burst fire first, homing beacon needed for bullseye

claims.text: Corsair SP order: Battleship Cannon to 30 first for the four-shot cannon, then Bullseye to 20, then Battleship, then Rapid Fire to 30, with Maple Warrior after; cannon first speeds up Bigfoot kills.
claims.say: corsair sp: cannon first, bullseye, battleship, rapid fire

claims.text: Bullseye marks one mob for extra damage and locks your targeting onto it, so shots pass through mobs standing in front of the marked one until you mark something else.
claims.say: bullseye locks onto one mob so your shots skip the ones in front

claims.text: Dismounting right before a damaging attack lands and remounting straight after stops the Battleship from taking damage, keeping it off cooldown and your damage steady.
claims.say: dismount just before a hit then remount, ship takes no dmg

claims.text: On Zakum's arms, some Corsairs skip dismounting and let the ship take hits since it survives at higher levels, while others learn each arm's range and dismount to dodge everything.
claims.say: on zak arms some just tank in the ship, others dismount to dodge

claims.text: To pin Bigfoot, aggro him, go to a corner, Recoil Shot away over him, then keep him pinned with Double Shot or Rapid Fire; it takes practice, so carry Safety Charms in case you die.
claims.say: pin bigfoot in a corner with recoil shot then double shot

claims.text: Corsairs can kill Bigfoot very quickly, so farming it and selling the toes it drops is a steady way to make mesos.
claims.say: corsairs kill bigfoot fast, sell the toes for mesos

claims.text: Corsairs have low HP; washing to around 10k HP is enough to fight Horntail comfortably without Hyper Body.
claims.say: wash to about 10k hp and you can do ht without hyper body

claims.text: HP washing is especially expensive for Corsairs because the HP gained per MP given up is poor, so expect big spending and leeching until around level 135 if you wash high.
claims.say: washing a corsair costs a ton, the hp per mp ratio is bad

claims.text: Wear a DEX-scrolled Green Bandana early and get a Zakum Helmet as soon as you can afford one, around level 50; it is the best-value upgrade for a Gunslinger line character.
claims.say: dex scrolled green bandana early, zakum helm asap around 50

claims.text: Get a Maple Gun at level 35 and a Maple Storm Pistol at level 43; both drop from regular monsters and are the cheap early gun upgrades.
claims.say: maple gun at 35, maple storm pistol at 43, both are mob drops

claims.text: Pink Gaia Cape and Pink Adventurer Cape are the standard attack capes; Pink Gaia Capes can be gambled for at the Kerning City Gachapon.
claims.say: pink gaia or pink adventurer cape, gacha kerning for gaia

claims.text: Macro Recoil Shot followed by Wings into one key so the back-hop and boost fire together; putting Recoil first is less annoying when you are Bigfooting a lot.
claims.say: macro recoil shot into wings for one key backhop

claims.text: Macro Ice Splitter then Flamethrower in that order, so enemies are frozen first and you spend fewer HP potions.
claims.say: macro ice splitter then flamethrower, freeze first saves pots

claims.text: Levels 10-21: Henesys Hunting Ground I or the job quests early on, then Bubblings and Horny Mushrooms from level 15.
claims.say: 10-21 hh1 and job quests, then bubblings and horny mushrooms
