claims.text: Levels 21-30: do the Kerning City Party Quest, or grind Wild Boars if you prefer to solo.
claims.say: 21-30 kerning pq, or wild boars if you want to grind

claims.text: Levels 31-51: Chronos or Pink Teddies in Ludibrium at first, then Master and Platoon Chronos, the Ludibrium Party Quest, and the Monster Carnival up to level 51.
claims.say: 31-51 chronos in ludi, ludi pq, and monster carnival

claims.text: Levels 51-70: the Ludibrium Maze, Orbis and Pirate party quests, or grind Voodoos and Mysterious Path 3.
claims.say: 51-70 maze pq, orbis pq, pirate pq, voodoos or mp3

claims.text: Levels 70-120: snipe Jr. Newties at the Destroyed Dragon Nest in Leafre with Burst Fire, which is dull but levels very fast; if you miss a lot try Voodoos, Mysterious Path 3 or Headless Horseman.
claims.say: 70-120 snipe jr newties at the dragon nest with burst fire

claims.text: Horntail becomes an option for a Corsair from about level 155 if you can survive him, which in practice means washing HP first.
claims.say: ht from around 155 if youre washed enough

claims.text: The Battleship skill quest: talk to Kyrin, choose the second option to fight her, and survive for two minutes to receive the skill.
claims.say: battleship quest: fight kyrin and survive 2 minutes

claims.text: For Battleship Cannon, defeat 150 Spirit Vikings and collect 50 of their drops; the Torpedo quest is the same with Gigantic Spirit Vikings.
claims.say: cannon quest is 150 spirit vikings, torpedo uses gigantic ones

claims.text: A Gunslinger line character does weak damage before level 120, so the way there is grindy; the class pays off after fourth job when Bullseye and the Battleship come online.
claims.say: corsair is a slog till 120 but it gets great after 4th job

claims.text: Heartstoppers drop from Voodoo and Hoodoo and also from Psycho Jack, though not from Psycho Jack while it is still in its box form.
claims.say: stoppers drop from voodoo, hoodoo and psycho jack, not the box

claims.text: Bowmasters get a spot in almost every party because Sharp Eyes raises the whole party's critical rate and damage, so max it early in fourth job.
claims.say: bowmasters get invited everywhere because of sharp eyes

claims.text: Bowmen are fragile unless HP washed, cannot use most skills at point-blank range, and have no party skill before fourth job, so they rely on distance and Power Knock-Back.
claims.say: archers are squishy and cant use most skills up close

claims.text: Bowmaster AP is STR-less into low STR: everything into DEX with Maple bows that need no STR, adding only the STR endgame bows demand once gear covers most of it, which leaves more DEX for Maple Warrior.
claims.say: all ap in dex, only add the str you need for endgame bows

claims.text: Bowman SP: 1 in Arrow Blow, 3 in The Blessing of Amazon to unlock the next skills, max The Eye of Amazon for range, then max Critical Shot and Double Shot, and put the rest into Focus.
claims.say: bowman sp: eye of amazon first, then crit shot and double shot

claims.text: Hunter SP: 1 in Arrow Bomb first, then Bow Mastery, 5 in Bow Booster and 3 in Soul Arrow, max Arrow Bomb and Power Knock-Back, finish Booster, Soul Arrow and Mastery, rest in Focus.
claims.say: hunter sp: arrow bomb, bow mastery, booster, then power knock-back

claims.text: Max Power Knock-Back as a Hunter: archers cannot use most skills with a monster right beside them, so knocking monsters away lets you keep using Double Shot and Arrow Bomb.
claims.say: max power knock-back so you can keep shooting instead of whacking

claims.text: Skip Final Attack : Bow; it interferes with Double Shot and Arrow Bomb and does not work with any third or fourth job skill, so leave it at zero.
claims.say: skip final attack bow, it breaks double shot and arrow bomb

claims.text: Ranger SP: 1 in Strafe, 5 in Mortal Blow to unlock Arrow Rain, max Arrow Rain, then Strafe, Puppet and Mortal Blow, 15 in Silver Hawk, max Inferno, and leftovers in Thrust.
claims.say: ranger sp: arrow rain first, then strafe, puppet, mortal blow, inferno

claims.text: Max Arrow Rain right after unlocking it with 5 points in Mortal Blow, since you can train with it whether or not a monster is standing next to you.
claims.say: max arrow rain early, it works even with mobs right next to you

claims.text: Max Puppet for training: monsters may attack it instead of you, which saves potions and lets you train faster.
claims.say: max puppet, mobs hit it instead of you and it saves pots

claims.text: Put only 15 points into Silver Hawk, because the fourth-job Phoenix needs level 15 Silver Hawk and is stronger than the Hawk.
claims.say: only put 15 in silver hawk, phoenix just needs lvl 15 of it

claims.text: Bowmaster SP: 1 in Hurricane, max Sharp Eyes, then max Hurricane and Bow Expert, Maple Warrior, a few points in Hero's Will before Horntail, then Phoenix and Concentrate with Phoenix first.
claims.say: bowmaster sp: sharp eyes first, then hurricane, bow expert, mw

claims.text: Raise Hero's Will before joining Horntail expeditions around level 155, since it cures the seduce.
claims.say: get some hero's will before ht, it cures seduce

claims.text: Maple Warrior 10 is given automatically, Maple Warrior 20 drops from Horntail, and Maple Warrior 30 from Pink Bean.
claims.say: mw 20 book comes off horntail, mw 30 from pink bean

claims.text: Bow Expert 30 and Concentrate 20 are Zakum drops, and Concentrate 30 is a Horntail drop.
claims.say: zak drops bow expert 30 and concentrate 20, ht drops concentrate 30

claims.text: Hurricane 20 drops from Nest Golem or comes from the Guild Party Quest; Hurricane 30 drops from Leviathan, Papulatus or Lyka.
claims.say: hurricane 20 from nest golems, hurricane 30 from leviathan/papu/lyka

claims.text: Sharp Eyes 20 drops from Cold Shark and the left Pianus, and Sharp Eyes 30 from the right Pianus.
claims.say: sharp eyes 20 off cold shark/left pianus, 30 off right pianus

claims.text: Phoenix quest: talk to Kumo in Leafre, take the giant egg from the hidden map in Cave of Trials III in El Nath, drop it on the nest at the top of Sky Nest I, kill whatever hatches, then report back to Kumo.
claims.say: phoenix: get the egg in cave of trials 3, drop it at the sky nest

claims.text: Concentrate finale: The Insignificant Being in Sleepywood wants 50 Dark Soul Rocks (Wild Kargo, Tauromacis, Taurospear, Jr. Balrog drops), then a special map where you kill 300 Jr. Balrogs with another fourth-job archer.
claims.say: concentrate: 50 dark soul rocks then 300 jr balrogs with a partner

claims.text: The first bow to use is the War Bow, which needs no STR and is sold by Karl at the Henesys weapon store.
claims.say: war bow from karl in henesys is your first bow, no str needed

claims.text: Maple Bow (level 35), Maple Soul Searcher (43) and Maple Kandiva Bow (64) need no STR and attack faster than normal bows, so a Bowman can use them until the endgame bows are wearable.
claims.say: maple bow at 35, soul searcher 43, kandiva 64, none need str

claims.text: White, Golden and Dark Nisrock bows need level 100 and 105 STR and give avoidability, jump and speed respectively; they drop from bosses and are fallback endgame bows if you cannot find a good Dragon Shiner Bow.
claims.say: nisrock bows are the backup endgame bow if no good dragon shiner

claims.text: Dragon Shiner Bow is the endgame bow from level 110, needing 115 STR; it drops from Horntail, comes out of the Henesys Gachapon, and can be crafted by Mos in Leafre.
claims.say: dragon shiner bow at 110, craftable by mos in leafre

claims.text: Use a Green Bandana early and scroll it for DEX; it has 10 upgrade slots against 7 on other hats, and it covers you until you can equip a Zakum Helmet.
claims.say: green bandana scrolled for dex until you get a zakum helm

claims.text: The level 50 Zakum Helmet drops from Zakum and has 10 upgrade slots, with bonuses to all four stats plus accuracy and avoidability.
claims.say: zakum helm drops off zak, gives all stats and acc/avoid

claims.text: Capes: the level 50 Pink Adventurer Cape comes from the Perion Gachapon, the level 65 Pink Gaia Cape from the Kerning City Gachapon, and the level 100 Blackfist Cloak from the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest bonus stage.
claims.say: pink adv cape from perion gacha, pink gaia from kerning gacha

claims.text: Bathrobes for Men or Women, sold by Momoyo in Zipangu, are the level 20 overall to scroll for DEX early on, boosting damage and accuracy.
claims.say: bathrobe from momoyo in zipangu, scroll it for dex early

claims.text: Staff Sergeant Charlie gives exp for each 100 Zombie's Lost Tooth handed in, open from level 7; it is the usual way to power-level from about 10 to 30.
claims.say: hand 100 zombie teeth to sgt charlie for exp, from lvl 7

claims.text: One exp reward can raise you at most one level; anything beyond leaves you just short of the following level, so hold big turn-ins until one reward no longer overflows.
claims.say: a quest reward cant give 2 levels, extra exp gets cut off

claims.text: A Corsair's main stat is DEX with STR as the secondary one. Put level-up AP into DEX until your equipment supplies enough STR for the stronger guns.
claims.say: all ap into dex, get the str from your gear for the gun

claims.text: A Zakum Helmet adds a good amount of STR, which helps a DEX-heavy gunslinger meet the strength requirement of better guns in the nineties and low hundreds.
claims.say: zakum helm gives str so you can wear better guns

claims.text: Advancing from Beginner to Pirate needs 20 DEX, so put early ability points into DEX before level 10.
claims.say: you need 20 dex to become a pirate

claims.text: Somersault Kick is the only area attack in the first Pirate job, so max it first to speed up training before second job.
claims.say: max somersault kick first, its your only aoe at 1st job

claims.text: Max Dash after Somersault Kick: double tapping a direction triggers a run speed and jump boost that makes moving between mobs faster.
claims.say: max dash next, double tap a direction for speed and jump

claims.text: Put the first second-job point into Invisible Shot; it is the main gunslinger attack at that stage and hits up to three targets.
claims.say: invisible shot is your main attack in 2nd job, hits 3 mobs

claims.text: Max Gun Mastery early in second job; it steadies and raises your damage range, which matters even more than the attack skill itself.
claims.say: max gun mastery early, it stabilizes your damage

claims.text: Five points in Wings unlock Recoil Shot, a short-cooldown hop that works like a flash jump for reaching higher platforms and repositioning; max both for mobility.
claims.say: 5 points in wings unlocks recoil shot, its your flash jump

claims.text: Blank Shot stuns up to three monsters, so stun a group with it and finish them with Invisible Shot to grind more safely.
claims.say: stun with blank shot then finish them with invisible shot

claims.text: Burst Fire is the main third-job attack, so max it right after advancing; the other third-job skills mostly support it or unlock fourth-job skills.
claims.say: max burst fire right when you hit 3rd job

claims.text: Flamethrower deals better area damage than Ice Splitter, so max it once Ice Splitter has its freeze points.
claims.say: max flamethrower after ice splitter for the better aoe

claims.text: At fourth job put the first three points into Battleship, Battleship Cannon and Rapid Fire. A point in Rapid Fire is a better early pick than one in Battleship Torpedo.
claims.say: first 3 sp go to battleship, cannon and rapid fire

claims.text: For a bossing Corsair, max Battleship first for more ship HP, then Battleship Cannon, Bullseye, Rapid Fire and Wrath of the Octopi, in that order.
claims.say: bossing order: battleship, cannon, bullseye, rapid fire, octopi

claims.text: Bullseye locks your attacks onto one target until it leaves the map and adds a damage bonus, making it a core skill for single-target boss damage.
claims.say: bullseye locks onto one target and boosts damage, max it

claims.text: Spawn Wrath of the Octopi while spamming Cannon and again whenever you dismount to dodge, so the octopi keep damaging the boss while you are off the ship.
claims.say: drop octopi while you shoot and when you dismount

claims.text: To get Battleship, talk to Kyrin, choose the option to fight her and survive two minutes; the skill is given at its maximum level, so there is no skill book to find.
claims.say: talk to kyrin, choose to fight her and survive 2 min for battleship

claims.text: Battleship Cannon needs 150 Spirit Vikings defeated and 50 of their drops collected; the Battleship Torpedo quest is the same but with Gigantic Spirit Vikings.
claims.say: cannon quest is 150 spirit vikings, torpedo uses the gigantic ones

claims.text: Hypnotize comes from a jump quest where touching the pink or blue Mu Lung snakes sends you back to the start; after it you protect an NPC from monster waves.
claims.say: hypnotize is a jump quest, dont touch the mu lung snakes

claims.text: The level 20 Rapid Fire mastery book can drop from Dark Wyvern and from Manon.
claims.say: rapid fire 20 book drops from dark wyverns and manon

claims.text: The level 20 Bullseye mastery book can drop from Nest Golem and from Pianus.
claims.say: bullseye 20 book comes from nest golem and pianus

claims.text: The Hypnotize level 20 mastery book drops from Papulatus.
claims.say: hypnotize 20 book drops from papulatus

claims.text: While you ride Battleship the ship takes the same damage you would; potions cannot repair it, and when its HP runs out the ship breaks and the skill goes on cooldown.
claims.say: the ship takes your damage and potions dont heal it

claims.text: The core Corsair habit is to dismount just before a boss attack lands, so you take the hit and the ship takes none, then remount afterwards; learn each boss's attack signals to time it.
claims.say: dismount right before big hits so your ship takes nothing

claims.text: Washing HP is worth it for Corsairs: strong boss hits one-shot an unwashed character, and Horntail runs often turn away low-HP attackers when no Hyper Body is available.
claims.say: wash your hp before horntail, low hp attackers get rejected

claims.text: Summoning Papulatus takes a quest chain that rewards a Piece of Cracked Dimension; drop it in the slot right of the map's centre, lined up exactly with the crack in the wall, or the boss will not appear.
claims.say: align the cracked dimension piece with the crack to spawn pap

claims.text: Papulatus signals its attacks: a yellow magic circle on its body means a 1/1 attack and a blue circle means lightning, so dismount on those cues; its small bombs also hurt a lot.
claims.say: watch pap's circles, yellow means 1/1 so dismount

claims.text: Pianus is mainly farmed for skill books: the left side drops only level 20 mastery books and the right side only level 30 books.
claims.say: pianus left side drops lvl 20 books, right side lvl 30

claims.text: In The Cave of Pianus both sides can attack at once and cast weapon and magic cancel; the left is weaker but seals, dispels and uses 1/1, while the right has more HP but neither seals nor dispels.
claims.say: left pianus seals and dispels, right one has more hp but no dispel

claims.text: For Bigfoot, pull it into a corner, Dash and Recoil Shot over it, then pin it with Burst Fire and finish it from the ship; its invincibility frames make solo easier than a party.
claims.say: pin bigfoot in a corner, recoil shot over it then burst fire it

claims.text: At Zakum's arms stage, a Corsair does best starting from the bottom left and shooting arms 7 and 5, because arms from the top right keep knocking a low-mobility class off the platform.
claims.say: start zakum arms from bottom left, hit arms 7 and 5 first

claims.text: Solo Zakum arm order for a Corsair is 1, 4, 2, 3, 6, 8, 7, then 5.
claims.say: solo zakum arm order is 1, 4, 2, 3, 6, 8, 7, 5

claims.text: On Zakum's top platform watch the arm attack circles: a blue circle does only token damage, so stay mounted, but dismount for a purple circle; Recoil Shot back if you are near the edge.
claims.say: dismount for zakum's purple circles, blue ones only do 1 dmg

claims.text: Triple Throw damage ignores DEX completely, so extra DEX raises a Night Lord's shown range but adds no real damage.
claims.say: dex does nothing for triple throw, its all luk

claims.text: Secondary stat is worth only a fraction of main stat for damage range, and the ratio depends on the weapon; for a Buccaneer, about 3.7 DEX gives the same range as 1 STR.
claims.say: bucc: about 3.7 dex is worth 1 str for range

claims.text: Weapon damage multipliers: one-handed sword 4.0, two-handed sword 4.6, one-handed axe or blunt weapon 4.4 swinging and 3.2 stabbing, two-handed axe or blunt 4.8 swinging and 3.4 stabbing.
claims.say: 1h sword x4.0, 2h sword x4.6, axes and bw lower when stabbing

claims.text: Spears hit harder stabbing (multiplier 5.0) than swinging (3.0); polearms are the reverse, 5.0 swinging and 3.0 stabbing.
claims.say: spears hit hardest stabbing, polearms hardest swinging

claims.text: Other weapon multipliers: bow 3.4, crossbow 3.6, thief daggers and claws 3.6, daggers for non-thieves 4.0, knuckle 4.8 and gun 3.6.
claims.say: bow 3.4, xbow 3.6, claw 3.6, knuckle 4.8, gun 3.6 multipliers

claims.text: Brandish averages a multiplier of about 3.8 with one-handed axes or blunts and 4.1 with two-handed ones; Blast averages about 3.92 and 4.24.
claims.say: brandish and blast average between swing and stab multipliers

claims.text: The more weapon attack you have, the more each stat point is worth, so the stat-to-attack ratio shrinks as attack rises.
claims.say: more weapon attack makes every stat point worth more

claims.text: Once you meet your gear's secondary stat requirements, use the secondary-to-main stat ratio to compare items that mix both stats against items with only main stat.
claims.say: use the dex to str ratio to compare mixed stat gear

claims.text: A player seduced by Horntail can use neither potions nor skills except Hero's Will and is forced left, right or into a jump, so a Bishop must keep that player healed.
claims.say: seduced ht players cant pot, bishop has to heal them

claims.text: The Horntail seduce target is usually a high-HP melee with defensive skills: Hero, Dark Knight, Paladin, Buccaneer or Shadower. A Night Lord with enough washed HP can do it too.
claims.say: ht seduce target is usually hero dk pally bucc or shadower

claims.text: The seduce target needs enough HP to survive the wings. About 20k is the comfortable number, and experienced players manage with 15k or a bit less.
claims.say: aim for about 20k hp as seduce target, 15k is the floor

claims.text: In Horntail's first prehead the Bishop should enter first and be the seduce target there, because a Bishop can hang from the second rope on the right side.
claims.say: bishop goes in first on prehead 1 and hangs on the right rope

claims.text: For the second prehead and the main body, whoever enters first is the main seduce target, then the rest enter in HP order. The Bowmaster or Marksman goes fifth and the Bishop last.
claims.say: enter by hp order, bowman fifth and bishop last

claims.text: When the seduce lands, the target should call it out in chat and hang on a rope, which makes the Bishop's healing much easier.
claims.say: call out s when seduced and hang on a rope

claims.text: Horntail's two arms run separate seduce timers. If the whole party stays on one side only one arm triggers, but anyone crossing the midline sets off the other arm and causes a double seduce.
claims.say: dont cross the middle of ht or both arms seduce at once

claims.text: Horntail's heads spawn wyverns in waves of red, then blue, then dark, around six of each. A good seduce target kills the wyverns to keep them off the Bishop.
claims.say: heads spawn red then blue then dark wyverns, clear them

claims.text: Dark wyverns dispel, which strips Magic Guard. The Bishop needs enough HP to live without Magic Guard and should hold or tap the skill whenever dark wyverns appear.
claims.say: dark wyverns dispel so recast magic guard and have the hp

claims.text: A Horntail Bishop should bring maxed Resurrection, Hero's Will and Holy Shield, about 3000 Ginger Ales, around 100 All Cure Potions, at least 2k HP, and HP gear if under about 2.6k HP.
claims.say: bishops bring 3000 ginger ales and 100 all cures to ht

claims.text: The Horntail Bishop's job: watch the seduce and dispel timers, learn the boss animations, cast Holy Symbol, Holy Shield and Dispel when needed, and heal and follow the seduce target.
claims.say: bishop watches timers and heals and follows the seduce target

claims.text: In prehead 1 the Bishop stays on the second rope to the right and does not go AFK, because wyverns can knock a player off it. If seduced toward the head, use Hero's Will at once.
claims.say: prehead 1: stay on right rope, hero's will if seduced to head

claims.text: In the main body the Bishop keeps the seduce target alive and casts Holy Symbol when parts are about to die. Dispel and Holy Shield are needed more on the right side because the right arm curses.
claims.say: main body: hs when parts die, more dispel and shield on right

claims.text: Do not Teleport to heal a seduced player pushed to the right while the tail or legs are alive. The tail hit would kill the Bishop, except a Hero with Achilles or a Shadower with Meso Guard.
claims.say: dont teleport to heal a seduced target near the tail

claims.text: A dispel from Head B or the left arm while Head A is still alive can kill the Bishop, because Head A's ice strike hits very hard. A Bishop can shield with wyverns or stand under the left wall rocks.
claims.say: if head a is alive a dispel can leave you dead to ice strike

claims.text: Once the other parts are dead, kill the right arm first because the left arm can dispel and kill the Bishop. If a mass seduce or dispel happens toward the left arm, the Bishop uses Hero's Will.
claims.say: kill the right arm first, left arm dispels can kill the bishop

claims.text: After the right arm is dead, sitting on a chair or hanging on a rope on the right side avoids being seduced.
claims.say: after the right arm dies sit on a chair on the right

claims.text: Learn the tells: a purple pointing finger from an arm means seduce is coming, a yellow-orange circle on a head means wyverns are spawning.
claims.say: purple finger from the arm = seduce, orange circle = wyverns

claims.text: Washing a Horntail Bishop to about 5.5k HP and 20k+ MP lets it survive a hit while dispelled and even tank the tail with Invincible, and cuts potion use. Some players think washing a Bishop is wasteful.
claims.say: a washed bishop at ~5.5k hp survives dispel hits at ht

claims.text: A Bishop who can take a hit can use Genesis on wyverns during dispels, so attackers are not dispelled or swarmed, and can also add Genesis damage on the main body.
claims.say: gene the wyverns so attackers dont get dispelled

claims.text: If the Bishop dies, the seduce target should ask the attackers to kill the wings first, because the wings hit a seduced player very hard.
claims.say: if the bishop dies kill the wings first, they hit hard

claims.text: Sap of Ancient Tree is the slow one to collect for the series; East Rocky Mountain V is a good place to farm it.
claims.say: farm sap of ancient tree at east rocky mountain v

claims.text: Nependeath's Honey has the lowest drop rate of the items the series needs; farm it in Orbis or buy it from other players if you have mesos.
claims.say: nependeath honey drops rarely, farm it in orbis or buy it

claims.text: Ginger Ale is a well-liked recovery potion, and Miki on the middle right side of New Leaf City sells it.
claims.say: miki in nlc sells ginger ale, middle right side of town

claims.text: Mages are at their best on bosses where they can hit several parts at once, such as Zakum's arms and Horntail.
claims.say: mages shine at zakum arms and horntail

claims.text: Sharp Eyes is close to required for bossing because it helps every class, while Speed Infusion only helps some of them.
claims.say: se is a must at bosses, it helps everyone

claims.text: Buccaneers use Demolition while Super Transformation is active and switch to Barrage plus Dragon Strike while it is down.
claims.say: bucc: demolition while transformed, barrage and dragon strike else

claims.text: Bowmasters keep Phoenix and Marksmen keep Frostprey summoned during boss fights for extra damage.
claims.say: keep phoenix or frostprey out at bosses

claims.text: In Ludibrium Party Quest stage 8, five players must stand on the right 5 of 9 boxes, which gives 126 possible combinations; work through them in order (1-2-3-4-5, then 1-2-3-4-6 and so on) instead of guessing.
claims.say: lpq stage 8: 126 combos, go through them in order, dont guess

claims.text: A faster stage 8 method renumbers the boxes so stepping to the next box takes one motion: from 5 slide down to 6, jump diagonally up to 7, then slide down to 8 and again to 9.
claims.say: renumber the lpq 8 boxes so each move to the next is one motion

claims.text: With that renumbering only two steps need two motions: from 3 jump up to 5 then down-jump to 4, and from 4 jump up to 7 then down-jump to 5.
claims.say: only 3 to 4 and 4 to 5 take two moves in the reordered layout

claims.text: Once box 3 is free, the first player keeps cycling boxes 1, 2 and 3 in stage 8: down-jump from 1 to 2, down-jump from 2 to 3, then jump back up to 1.
claims.say: front guy cycles boxes 1-2-3: down jump twice, jump back up

claims.text: Telecasting means casting your mage ultimate while teleporting, so you reposition during the cast instead of waiting for it to end.
claims.say: telecast = cast your ultimate and teleport at the same time

claims.text: To practice telecasting, hold a direction key for a moment, then press the ultimate and Teleport keys at the same time.
claims.say: practice holding an arrow then press ult and teleport together

claims.text: Bind Teleport and the ultimate to two plain letter keys such as C and S; putting them on Ctrl or Shift can add a delay that breaks the telecast.
claims.say: put teleport and your ult on plain keys like c and s

claims.text: A Bishop puts every ability point into INT. The wands and staves you use along the way need no LUK, so a luckless build is fine.
claims.say: bishops go all int, no luk needed for wands and staves

claims.text: Magician job advancement is at level 8: go to the Magic Library at the top of Ellinia and talk to Grendel the Really Old.
claims.say: at lvl 8 grendel in the ellinia magic library makes you a mage

claims.text: As a Magician, unlock Improved MaxMP Increase through Improving MP Recovery and max it first, then Magic Claw for damage and Magic Guard last, with leftover points back in MP Recovery.
claims.say: max mp increase first, then magic claw, then magic guard

claims.text: Cleric advancement at level 30: take a letter from Grendel the Really Old to the instructor north of Ellinia, bring back 30 Dark Marbles for a Proof of a Hero, then return it to Grendel.
claims.say: cleric job: grendel's letter, 30 dark marbles, then the proof

claims.text: As a new Cleric put the first point into Teleport for mobility, then pour the following levels into Heal, your signature skill.
claims.say: 1 sp in teleport, then max heal

claims.text: After Heal, take MP Eater, which saves a lot of potions on long grinds, then Bless, Invincible and more Teleport, and leave Holy Arrow for spare points.
claims.say: mp eater saves a ton of potions, then bless, invincible, teleport

claims.text: Priest quest part one: see Robeira in El Nath, then Grendel in Ellinia, clear the Path of the Glittering Crystal via the Door of Dimension in Forest of Evil II for the Black Charm, and trade it to Grendel.
claims.say: priest quest starts with robeira in el nath then grendel

claims.text: Priest quest part two: bring the Necklace of Strength to Robeira, then go to the Holy Ground at the Snowfield, answer the Dark Crystal's five questions for the Necklace of Wisdom, and return it to Robeira.
claims.say: bring robeira the necklace of wisdom from the snowfield holy ground

claims.text: As a new Priest, put one point in Shining Ray for mobbing, a few in Dispel to unlock Holy Symbol, then max Holy Symbol first; it is the class's most valuable party buff.
claims.say: max holy symbol first as a priest

claims.text: After Holy Symbol take Mystic Door (casting it needs a Magic Rock), then max Shining Ray, Dispel and finally Elemental Resistance.
claims.say: mystic door is next after holy symbol, it eats a magic rock

claims.text: Fourth job: get a recommendation letter from your third-job instructor in El Nath, bring it to Gritto in Leafre, and hunt Manon and Griffey for the Heroic Star and Heroic Pentagon he asks for.
claims.say: for 4th job hunt manon and griffey for heroic star and pentagon

claims.text: Genesis is the Bishop's core attack and income source, so it gets the first points; get the level 20 book as soon as you can afford it, then level 30, before spreading points elsewhere.
claims.say: genesis first, grab the lvl 20 book then lvl 30 asap

claims.text: With Genesis settled, spend remaining points roughly in this order: Bahamut, Infinity, Holy Shield, Doom, Angel Ray.
claims.say: after genesis: bahamut, infinity, holy shield, doom, angel ray

claims.text: The Genesis skill quest starts with your third-job instructor, goes through Wiz the Librarian in Korean Folk Town and Grendel in Ellinia, and finally has Shammos in El Nath start the Genesis quest itself.
claims.say: genesis quest runs through wiz in korean folk town and shammos

claims.text: Shammos asks for Life's Root, found in the Cave of Life; getting into the cave requires running the Horntail party quest with at least three players.
claims.say: life's root for genesis needs a horntail run with 3+ players

claims.text: Inside the cave Moira wants an ice cube from a Green Cornian, a skull mask from a Dark Cornian, a Manon kill, 10 Dragon Skins and a broken dagger; Mos then forges a new dagger using a Mithril Plate and a Steel Plate.
claims.say: moira wants cornian drops, a manon kill and 10 dragon skins

claims.text: Bahamut levels come from Raul the Knight in Leafre: turn in 20, 25, 30, 35 and then 40 Dragon Hearts to raise its max level to 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30, and farm Red, Blue and Dark Wyverns for the hearts.
claims.say: farm wyverns for dragon hearts, raul the knight raises bahamut

claims.text: At level 130 a Bishop can equip an Elemental Wand and start two-hitting Skelegons easily, a big jump in leveling speed.
claims.say: at lvl 130 an elemental wand lets you 2hit skelegons

claims.text: Selling party leech with Genesis is the quickest early meso source for a Bishop: it needs little gear, you earn from the moment Genesis is unlocked, and you still get decent exp.
claims.say: bishops make good mesos selling leech right after genesis

claims.text: The Amoria Party Quest opens at level 40 and needs a married couple, so many players marry two of their own characters to run it.
claims.say: apq starts at lvl 40 and needs a married couple

claims.text: In the Amoria Party Quest boss fight, Geist Balrog dispels, so mages lose Magic Guard easily; most mages cannot hit it anyway, so just hold Magic Guard through its third form.
claims.say: in apq the balrog dispels magic guard, keep recasting it

claims.text: A Wooden Wand is enough to reach level 30; after that get a Maple Staff around 35 and a Maple Lama Staff around 43, since pure-INT mages are strong enough on these.
claims.say: wooden wand till 30, maple staff at 35, maple lama staff at 43

claims.text: Staff Sergeant Charlie, on the left side of Orbis, swaps sets of 100 identical etc items for exp and the trade repeats without limit, so buying etc sets lets a new character level from about 7-10 to 30 with mesos.
claims.say: buy etc sets and hand them to charlie in orbis for fast lvls to 30

claims.text: Staying a Beginner until 30 and advancing then only costs warriors and magicians, who miss the extra HP or MP per level from their first-job skills; other classes can skip the level 10 advance freely.
claims.say: only warriors and mages lose hp/mp by staying beginner till 30

claims.text: On a warrior or magician mule made only for a utility skill or for farming, the bonus HP/MP from advancing early is small enough to ignore.
claims.say: on a mule the early hp/mp bonus barely matters

claims.text: The etc items most often bought in bulk for Charlie's exchange are Zombie's Lost Tooth, Yeti Horn, Pepe's Beak and Nependeath's Seed.
claims.say: zombie teeth, yeti horns, pepe beaks or nepen seeds for charlie

claims.text: Before HP washing, place a single AP into HP early so there is a point there for AP Reset to work with later.
claims.say: put 1 ap in hp early so you can use ap resets on it later

claims.text: When washing, equip your INT gear before each level up, since higher INT raises the MP gained per level, and that MP is what you later convert into HP.
claims.say: wear int gear before you level, more int means more mp to wash

claims.text: A washing Hero should reach exactly 35 STR by level 10 for the warrior job advance and not go over it; every other point goes into INT.
claims.say: lv 1-10 get exactly 35 str for warrior, rest goes to int

claims.text: After 35 STR, a washing Hero puts level-up AP into INT until total INT including gear is about 90-100; with strong INT gear little or no base INT is needed.
claims.say: after 35 str pump int to about 90-100 counting your int gear

claims.text: Once base INT plus INT gear sits between about 80 and 120, a washing Hero sends all further level-up AP into STR; more INT helps but 120 is a sensible cap.
claims.say: once you have 80-120 int with gear, put all new ap into str

claims.text: From level 120 on, a Hero washes by using AP Resets to take points out of MP and add them to HP, repeating until the HP goal is reached.
claims.say: at 120+ use ap resets, minus mp plus hp, repeat for more hp

claims.text: When the HP target is reached, use AP Resets to move the base INT you added back into STR.
claims.say: hit your hp goal then reset your base int back into str

claims.text: Bigfoot in Phantom Forest is somewhat harder than Headless Horseman but gives very good exp; its toe is a rare drop.
claims.say: bigfoot gives great exp, the toe drop is rare tho

claims.text: Leprechauns at Creeping Evil die quickly and drop lots of equipment you can sell to NPC shops. Two spawn close together, so standing between them with a summon or an area attack farms both.
claims.say: farm leprechauns in creeping evil, sell the equips to npc

claims.text: Creeping Evil is a good training map for about levels 40 to 50: the Leprechauns die fast to skill spam and give good exp.
claims.say: leprechauns in creeping evil are nice exp around 40-50

claims.text: A purple Elderwraith roams Creeping Evil and hits very hard, so low-level characters farming Leprechauns should avoid it; Dark Sight or Magic Guard can help survive a hit.
claims.say: watch out for the elderwraith in creeping evil at low lvl

claims.text: In Crimsonwood Keep you can be leeched on Windraiders from about level 65.
claims.say: you can get leeched on windraiders in cwk from about 65

claims.text: Stormbreakers in Crimsonwood Keep are a leech spot from about level 75.
claims.say: stormbreakers in cwk are leechable from around 75

claims.text: Doing the Crimsonwood Keep prequests lets you skip many Phantom Forest maps and the jump quest on the way to the Keep.
claims.say: do the cwk prequests, they skip a ton of maps and the jq

claims.text: When waiting for Headless Horseman or Bigfoot, kill the regular mobs in the map, since the boss sometimes does not spawn otherwise.
claims.say: kill some mobs in the map or the boss might not show

claims.text: To receive leech exp from a party kill you must be no more than 5 levels below the monster.
claims.say: to leech you cant be more than 5 levels under the mob

claims.text: Bring a Bishop with Holy Symbol when hunting Bigfoot or Headless Horseman for the extra exp; they can also help clear the regular mobs.
claims.say: bring a bishop for holy symbol when hunting bigfoot

claims.text: Priests around level 105 to 120 often look for someone who can kill Bigfoot, since the party exp is very good for them.
claims.say: priests 105-120 love bigfoot runs, invite one

claims.text: Boss drops become lootable by anyone after a short time and later vanish, so watch the clock when a buyer is waiting to pick one up.
claims.say: drops go public after a few minutes, keep an eye on it

claims.text: A quest in Dead Man's Gorge asking for 50 Phantom Seeds unlocks a hidden shop there that sells All Cure Potions, arrows and Cider, a weapon attack drink.
claims.say: turn in 50 phantom seeds in the gorge to unlock a shop

claims.text: The wraiths in Twisted Paths drop random mage robes and gloves; ones that roll high INT can sell for a lot.
claims.say: twisted paths wraiths drop mage robes, high int ones sell

claims.text: Hollowed Ground is a hidden map reached from Haunted House through a secret portal just before the real portal at the right edge; Headless Horseman spawns there and it is often uncontested.
claims.say: hollowed ground is the hidden portal right of haunted house

claims.text: Hidden Evil is reached from Bent Tree: go to the upper-right platform with the portal and press up at the arrow sign there. Headless Horseman spawns in it.
claims.say: hidden evil is the arrow sign up right in bent tree

claims.text: To reach Creeping Evil, take the lowest rightmost portal in Bent Tree, climb the hill and press up at the arrow sign.
claims.say: creeping evil: bent tree bottom right portal, up the hill

claims.text: Forgotten Path is the forest's main map and spawns both Headless Horseman and Bigfoot; reach it from Bent Tree through the upper-left portal to Dead Man's Gorge, then the right portal twice.
claims.say: forgotten path has both hh and bigfoot spawns

claims.text: From Bent Tree, the central portal leads to one Crossroads and the upper-rightmost portal to another; a third Crossroads is right then left from Dead Man's Gorge. Headless Horseman spawns in all three.
claims.say: crossroads 1 and 2 are off bent tree, both get hh

claims.text: The Evil Dead, a hidden map behind an arrow sign on Forgotten Path, spawns both Headless Horseman and Bigfoot. It is the hardest to reach, so its bosses are often still up.
claims.say: the evil dead is a pain to reach so bosses sit there

claims.text: Bigfoot spawns in Twisted Paths 1 to 5, Forgotten Path, The Evil Dead and Evil Rising.
claims.say: bigfoot: twisted paths, forgotten path, evil dead, evil rising

claims.text: Headless Horseman spawns in Hollowed Ground, Hidden Evil, Creeping Evil, Forgotten Path, the three Crossroads maps and The Evil Dead.
claims.say: hh: hollowed ground, hidden evil, creeping evil, crossroads

claims.text: From Dead Man's Gorge the left portal leads into Twisted Paths 1, with Twisted Paths 2 further left; the right portal leads to Twisted Paths 4, with Twisted Paths 5 further right.
claims.say: from the gorge go left for twisted paths 1, right for 4

claims.text: Evil Rising is a hidden map full of flying ghosts: from Bent Tree take the central portal, then the leftmost, then the rightmost, climb the hill and press up at the arrow sign.
claims.say: evil rising is a hidden sign map full of flying ghosts

claims.text: The way to Crimsonwood Keep is through the leftmost upper portal on the upper part of Forgotten Path, past a spinning hazard that can kill you in one hit.
claims.say: cwk is past the spinning thing at top left of forgotten path

claims.text: Dark scrolls (the 30% and 70% kinds) give the same stats as the 10% and 60% scrolls of the same type, but with a better chance of success. The price is that a failed dark scroll has a 50% chance of destroying the item.
claims.say: 30% and 70% dark scrolls give same stats but can boom on a fail

claims.text: Because a failed dark scroll destroys half the time, each 30% scroll carries a 35% destruction risk and each 70% scroll a 15% risk, while the 10% and 60% scrolls never destroy the item.
claims.say: a 30% scroll booms 35% of the time and a 70% scroll 15%

claims.text: On a weapon, a 10% or 30% attack scroll adds +5 attack while a 60% or 70% scroll adds only +2, so one first-tier scroll is worth about two and a half second-tier scrolls.
claims.say: 10/30% weapon att scrolls give +5, 60/70% only +2

claims.text: Without White Scrolls, filling all slots of a 7-slot weapon with 70% scrolls succeeds roughly 1 time in 12 and with 60% scrolls about 1 in 36, but with 30% scrolls about 1 in 4,500 and with 10% scrolls virtually never.
claims.say: 7 slots of 70% scrolls works about 1 in 12, 30% almost never

claims.text: The risk of at least one destruction piles up quickly: over seven 70% scrolls it is about 68%, over five about 56%, and with 30% scrolls it is already 72% after three and over 90% after six.
claims.say: boom risk adds up: seven 70% scrolls is about 68%, 30% is way worse

claims.text: Success streaks get unlikely fast: three 70% scrolls in a row work about a third of the time and five in a row about 17%, while three in a row with 60% scrolls is only about 22% and with 30% scrolls under 3%.
claims.say: three 70% scrolls in a row hit about a third, five in a row 17%

claims.text: Choosing a scroll tier is a trade-off between the safer lower-reward scrolls and the risky bigger-reward ones, and the odds change a lot with each extra slot, so decide how much risk you can afford before you start scrolling.
claims.say: decide how much boom risk you can take before you start scrolling

claims.text: For a mage, a non-fresh AP placed into HP adds roughly 10 to 20 HP, while taking a point back out of HP removes only 10 HP.
claims.say: mage hp ap gives 10-20 hp but pulling one out only costs 10

claims.text: Mages can cycle AP Resets, moving a point from INT to HP and then from HP back to INT, gaining about 5 HP per cycle on average without spending MP.
claims.say: loop ap resets int to hp and back, about 5 hp gained per loop

claims.text: Because the reset cycle needs no level-ups, a mage could in theory reach 30k HP while still around level 20.
claims.say: with enough resets a mage can have 30k hp even at lv 20

claims.text: HP built up this way can later be moved into MP as well, so a mage could end up with very high HP and MP together.
claims.say: you can shift that washed hp into mp afterwards too

claims.text: The reset cycle is mainly worth it at level 200, where there are no more level-ups and it is the only remaining way to add HP or MP.
claims.say: at 200 the reset loop is the only way left to add hp or mp

claims.text: Three of the six erasers come from town Gachapons: Wraith Eraser from Kerning City's, Mushmom Eraser from Henesys's and Stump Eraser from Perion's.
claims.say: wraith eraser kerning gach, mushmom henesys, stump perion

claims.text: The other three erasers: Slime Eraser from the Sleepywood Gachapon, Lupin Eraser from Ellinia's and Octopus Eraser from Nautilus's.
claims.say: slime eraser sleepywood gach, lupin ellinia, octopus nautilus

claims.text: Hectagon Crystal Necklace and the Seal Cushion takes the six erasers plus a Hectagon Necklace and is turned in to Arwen the Fairy in Ellinia for one random reward.
claims.say: 6 erasers plus hectagon necklace go to arwen in ellinia

claims.text: An Immovable Sword takes the six erasers plus Undine's Cloth and is completed with Burnt Sword at East Rocky Mountain III near Perion.
claims.say: 6 erasers plus undine's cloth, turn in to burnt sword in perion

claims.text: A Revenge on Gray the Alien needs the six erasers and two earlier Omega Sector quests; it shows no pop-up and simply appears among available quests, and is finished with Alien Gray at Kulan Field II.
claims.say: gray quest needs 6 erasers and 2 omega quests done first

claims.text: Its prerequisites are Trading with Alien Gray (break storage units in Omega Sector's Silo for 3 Secret Documents) and The Effort to Make-Up (defeat 120 Ultra Gray).
claims.say: do trading with alien gray and the effort to make-up first

claims.text: All the eraser quests can be repeated whenever you collect a fresh set of the required items.
claims.say: you can redo the eraser quests if you get more erasers

claims.text: Prefer gear with your main stat over your secondary stat: the secondary stat only has to reach your weapon's requirement, and anything past that is wasted.
claims.say: take main stat gear, secondary only needs to hit weapon reqs

claims.text: Archers only need STR to meet their bow's requirement, roughly 105 to 110 STR for end-game bows.
claims.say: archers only need ~105-110 str for end game bows

claims.text: A well-funded archer gets most of the needed STR from items like Zakum Helmet and Horntail Necklace plus rings, so a high-DEX top or bottom beats a high-STR one.
claims.say: funded archers get str from zhelm and ht, take dex overalls

claims.text: Buccaneers only need about 100 to 110 DEX and DEX is easy to get from scrolled gear, so they should favor STR on their overall.
claims.say: buccs need little dex, get str on the overall

claims.text: Night Lords need a lot of DEX, around 140 to 150, for their claws, so some DEX on their top and bottom is fine.
claims.say: nls need lots of dex for claws, dex on overalls is fine

claims.text: Corsairs should take DEX over STR on gear, for the same reason as archers.
claims.say: sairs want dex gear, not str

claims.text: Heroes only need some extra DEX to reach about 120, so whether gear has STR or DEX matters little to them.
claims.say: heroes just need ~120 dex, doesn't matter much

claims.text: Shadowers need 150 DEX to use the Dragon Kanzir, so they rarely go over what they need in DEX.
claims.say: shads need 150 dex for dragon kanzir

claims.text: For thieves, STR and DEX both count as the secondary damage stat, but their effect is tiny next to LUK.
claims.say: for thieves str and dex barely matter next to luk

claims.text: Lucky Seven and Triple Throw use their own damage formula that counts only LUK.
claims.say: lucky seven and triple throw only scale off luk

claims.text: Soloing Bigfoot as a Dark Knight is mostly about keeping it pinned in place and picking a weapon attack speed that works around its short invincibility after each hit.
claims.say: solo bigfoot on drk: keep it pinned, mind its iframes

claims.text: Crusher has a slight delay when it hits several mobs, which can lose the pin on Bigfoot; the slower swing of a speed 6 or 7 weapon tends to cover that gap, so use speed 6 when soloing without a mage.
claims.say: use a speed 6 weapon solo on bigfoot so crusher keeps the pin

claims.text: Mana Bull is a handy MP potion for bossing because it stacks 150 to a slot, so you carry more MP recovery in less inventory space.
claims.say: mana bull stacks 150 a slot, saves a lot of inventory room

claims.text: From around level 75, being leeched by a Bishop or Arch Mage is one of the best ways to level a third-job class, since monsters give much more exp and have far more HP than is comfortable to solo.
claims.say: from lvl 75 a bishop or archmage leech is a great way to level

claims.text: Wolf Spiders are the busiest leech and training target for levels 75 to 84, a big step up in exp and HP from earlier mobs that turns kills into several hits.
claims.say: wolf spiders are the classic spot for lvl 75-84

claims.text: Wolf Spiders are the main source of Ilbi Throwing-Stars, and they also drop Steel Ore and Wisdom Crystal Ore, which are worth stockpiling and selling in bulk as crystals.
claims.say: wolf spiders are where ilbi stars come from, stash their ores too

claims.text: Skelegons rarely drop Dragon Scales and Dragon Spirits, the materials for crafting the level 110 weapons of every class, so they are always in demand.
claims.say: skelegons drop dragon scales and spirits for the lvl 110 weapons

claims.text: Skelegons are where end-game knuckles like King Cent and White Fangz come from, along with Spartas, so one-shotting them is among the best money in the game.
claims.say: skelegons drop king cent and white fangz knuckles and spartas

claims.text: Jr. Balrog is found in the dungeon map The Cursed Sanctuary. No pre-quest is needed and it respawns every few hours.
claims.say: jr balrog is in the cursed sanctuary, no prequest

claims.text: Crimson Balrog turns up on the ship between Ellinia and Orbis. No pre-quest is needed.
claims.say: crimson balrog shows up on the ellinia to orbis ship

claims.text: Bigfoot spawns in Forgotten Path, Evil Rising, The Evil Dead and the Twisted Path maps, with no pre-quest. Its touch damage is among the heaviest of the area bosses.
claims.say: bigfoot is in forgotten path, evil rising, evil dead, twisted path

claims.text: Pianus lives in The Cave of Pianus, with a left and a right version on different respawn timers. Its bombs hit far harder than its other attacks, and no pre-quest is needed.
claims.say: pianus is in the cave of pianus, its bombs hurt a lot

claims.text: Black Crow is in the map Encounter with the Buddha and needs no pre-quest. Its magic attack is the main threat.
claims.say: black crow is at encounter with the buddha, no prequest

claims.text: Female Boss is found in the Parlor map in Zipangu. It needs no pre-quest and has touch, slap and gun attacks.
claims.say: female boss is in the parlor in zipangu

claims.text: Papulatus is fought in Origin of Clocktower in Ludibrium and needs a pre-quest. Its two bodies touch hard, and ground and platform bombs hit even harder.
claims.say: papulatus is at origin of clocktower and needs a prequest

claims.text: Zakum is fought at Zakum's Altar in El Nath and requires the Zakum pre-quest series first.
claims.say: zakum is at the altar in el nath, you need the prequests first

claims.text: Horntail is fought in Horntail's Cave and requires its pre-quest. Its legs, wings, tail and heads all hit hard, and the middle head hits hardest.
claims.say: horntail is in horntail's cave and needs a prequest first

claims.text: Furious Scarlion Boss and Furious Targa are in Spooky World in Malaysia. The entry needs the quest line that starts with Lam in Kampung Village.
claims.say: scarlion and targa are in spooky world, quest from lam first

claims.text: Bosses that can dispel your buffs: the pirate boss in Crimsonwood Keep PQ, Horntail's left hand and heads, Pianus, Papulatus, Manon and Griffey. Plan to rebuff against them.
claims.say: horntail left hand and heads, pianus, papulatus, manon dispel you

claims.text: Wraiths are the pick from about 35 to 42-43; characters who are not mages should pop Heartstoppers while training there.
claims.say: 35-43 hit wraiths, use stoppers if you're not a mage

claims.text: Mysterious Path 3 covers 43 to 65; keep using Heartstoppers there until your miss rate drops to roughly 20%.
claims.say: 43-65 at mp3, use stoppers until you rarely miss

claims.text: With mesos to spend, buying leech at Windraiders is the fast option from 65 to 75.
claims.say: 65-75 buy leech at windraiders

claims.text: From 75 to 78 the paid leech spot is Wolf Spiders.
claims.say: 75-78 leech at wolf spiders

claims.text: Harps are the leech spot from 78 to 85.
claims.say: 78-85 leech at harps

claims.text: Mages past 130 can make mesos by selling leech at the strongest mob they can kill in one hit.
claims.say: mages 130+ sell leech on the biggest mob they one shot

claims.text: On a tight budget, train from 10 to 25 on Bubblings.
claims.say: no mesos? do bubblings 10-25

claims.text: Unfunded characters can grind the teddies, Brown Teddy and Pink Teddy, from 25 to 40.
claims.say: 25-40 grind teddies if you're broke

claims.text: On the unfunded route, Wraiths carry you from 40 to 50.
claims.say: 40-50 grind wraiths

claims.text: Without paying for leech, grind Mysterious Path 3 from 50 to 75.
claims.say: 50-75 grind mp3

claims.text: Unfunded players grind Wolf Spiders from 75 to 90.
claims.say: 75-90 grind wolf spiders

claims.text: Fire/Poison wizards can use Fire Arrow on fire-weak mobs in Singapore from around 40 to 58.
claims.say: f/p 40-58: fire arrow fire-weak mobs in singapore

claims.text: Poison Mist never misses and covers an area, but the poison will not finish mobs off, so land the final hit with Magic Claw or Explosion.
claims.say: mist never misses, finish them with magic claw or explosion

claims.text: Unless you are MP washing, grinding is far better value than buying leech before level 65.
claims.say: not mp washing? grind instead of leech before 65

claims.text: Boss quests pay big exp for their level, can add up to a lot of fame in total, and can beat dead party quests or grinding. Most need prerequisite quests first, which can involve grinding a mob or its drop.
claims.say: boss quests give great exp and fame for the level but need prereqs

claims.text: Eliminating King Sage Cat from Do Gong needs level 77 and has no prerequisite. It gives great exp for the level and 17 fame and is worth doing.
claims.say: king sage cat quest from do gong at 77 is great exp and fame

claims.text: The Bounty Hunt from Sirin (Deo) rewards good exp but first needs the whole Sand Bandits quest chain and two Lidium, which can take hours of grinding. Skip it unless you already have the Lidium.
claims.say: deo bounty hunt needs the sand bandit chain and lidium, usually skip

claims.text: Defeat Faust (level 50, Arwen the Fairy) and Eliminating Blue Mushmom (level 85, Hikari) give no fame and little exp for their level, so they are not worth the effort.
claims.say: faust and blue mushmom quests give little exp and no fame, skip

claims.text: Jane's Second Challenge, Carta's Demand and Secret Medicine for Transformation mostly make you fetch a boss drop for a basic quest. They are usually skipped, except Secret Medicine if you want the Dragon Elixir.
claims.say: drop fetch quests arent worth it, except manon for dragon elixir

claims.text: Berserk makes a Dark Knight hit much harder, but only while HP is below half of max HP, so the class is played by hovering under 50% HP without dying.
claims.say: dk only hits hard under half hp, thats what berserk is for

claims.text: Percent-based HP potions heal too much to keep a Dark Knight under half HP, so Berserk users stick to flat-amount HP potions.
claims.say: use flat hp pots not percent ones or u lose zerk

claims.text: Set the pet auto-potion HP alert fairly low so the pet only drinks when you are in danger, and avoid manual potions while HP sits in the safe zone, otherwise you will pop out of Berserk.
claims.say: set pet autopot low and dont manual pot while ur zerking

claims.text: Small flat potions keep a Berserking Dark Knight closer to the half-HP line but need more manual drinking; big flat potions take less effort but leave less spare HP in reserve while zerking.
claims.say: small pots mean more babysitting, big pots are easy but less buffer

claims.text: A warrior can HP wash without raising base INT, because the spare MP above the minimum is already enough; INT on gear adds a bit more washable MP as you level.
claims.say: warriors dont need base int to wash, int gear just helps a bit

claims.text: INT pieces such as a robe, cape, earring, glove and wand, plus a Zakum Helmet with clean INT, give a Dark Knight extra MP to wash into HP.
claims.say: zakum helm and some int gear give extra mp to wash into hp

claims.text: In Horntail the seduced player cannot drink potions for a while and Horntail drains MP, so the seducer needs Hero's Will and enough spare MP left to cast it; extra MP from washing and INT gear helps.
claims.say: seduced in ht means no pots, keep spare mp for hero's will

claims.text: A Dark Knight's damage rides mostly on STR and no gear needs DEX, so put nearly all AP into STR and keep DEX at the bare minimum.
claims.say: dk ap is all str, dex only what u need

claims.text: Before 4th job, fix Dark Knight accuracy with a Zakum Helmet, a Maple Impaler or Maple Soul Spear, accuracy-scrolled gear, or Sniper Pills from Ludibrium instead of spending AP on DEX.
claims.say: fix acc with gear and sniper pills from ludi, not dex ap

claims.text: Early Dark Knight SP: max Improved MaxHP Increase first since it makes HP washing easier, and max Slash Blast as the main attack of 1st and 2nd job.
claims.say: max improved maxhp increase and slash blast early

claims.text: At Spearman, max Spear Mastery, Spear Booster and Hyper Body; Hyper Body is the reason Dark Knights are wanted in boss runs.
claims.say: spearman sp: max mastery, booster and hyper body

claims.text: At Dragon Knight, max Spear Crusher as the main attack, then Elemental Resistance, Power Crash and Dragon Roar.
claims.say: dragon knight sp: crusher, elemental res, power crash, roar

claims.text: At Dark Knight, max Berserk, Power Stance and Achilles, take Beholder to 10, put one point in Rush for movement and all five in Hero's Will.
claims.say: 4th job dk: max berserk, power stance, achilles, hero's will

claims.text: Power Crash removes the defense buff a boss puts on itself, which would otherwise cut your damage a lot; use it when the small shield icon shows over the boss.
claims.say: use power crash when a boss gets the shield icon

claims.text: Dragon Roar costs HP, so it helps a Dark Knight drop under half HP for Berserk, but it stuns you briefly after the cast.
claims.say: dragon roar lowers ur hp for zerk but stuns u a sec

claims.text: Achilles and Elemental Resistance cut incoming damage, which makes living at low HP under Berserk far easier.
claims.say: achilles and elemental res make zerking way safer

claims.text: One point in Rush is enough; it is only a movement helper for a Dark Knight.
claims.say: 1 point in rush is plenty, its just for moving

claims.text: Beholder's Hex gives a random buff (attack, defenses, accuracy or avoidability) and its Aura heals over time; spend spare SP on them as you like, though Aura healing can knock you out of Berserk.
claims.say: hex of beholder buffs u randomly, aura heal can break zerk

claims.text: For 4th job bossing a Dark Knight should use a spear, because Spear Crusher hits a target several times per swing and a spear gets the better swing action for it.
claims.say: use a spear for bossing, crusher hits multiple times

claims.text: In 3rd job a polearm can be better for mobbing, since Dragon Fury with a polearm has long reach and a short delay; switch back to a spear for bosses.
claims.say: polearm is ok for mobbing in 3rd job, spear for bosses

claims.text: If you use Heartstopper or Onyx Apple in boss runs, the fast Sky Ski beats slow spears like Pinaka as an endgame Dark Knight weapon.
claims.say: sky ski is the end spear if you use heartstopper or onyx apple

claims.text: Around level 20 a Fish Spear, farmed from Bubblings, is a good spear that gives accuracy and a speed boost at normal attack speed.
claims.say: fish spear from bubblings is a nice spear around lvl 20

claims.text: A Maple Impaler around level 43 is a fast weapon you will keep for a long time, so look for a well-rolled one.
claims.say: get a good maple impaler at 43, youll use it a while

claims.text: From level 95 a Purple Surfboard, only from the New Leaf City gachapon, is the endgame polearm for a Dragon Knight mobbing in 3rd job.
claims.say: purple surfboard at 95 is the end polearm, nlc gacha only

claims.text: In Zakum a Dark Knight can keep Berserk going without manual potions, as long as he is not the one tanking the body.
claims.say: in zakum dk can zerk with no manual pots if not tanking body

claims.text: In Papulatus body 1 stand on the left platform by the NPC to avoid being dispelled; in body 2 the touch damage can kill a zerking Dark Knight, so manual potions are required.
claims.say: pap body 1 stand left plat by the npc, body 2 needs manual pots

claims.text: Horntail needs manual potions to keep Berserk safe; be careful using Rush on the edge platform next to the heads, since a fall means touch damage, so keep HP high before rushing near a head.
claims.say: ht needs manual pots, careful rushing near the heads or u fall

claims.text: Berserk cannot be kept up in the Bodyguard A fight, so do not plan on zerking there.
claims.say: cant zerk vs bodyguard a, dont bother

claims.text: Between about 95 and 120, party training on Dreamy Ghosts is a solid way to level.
claims.say: party train dreamy ghosts from 95 to 120

claims.text: Late leveling comes from boss runs: Papulatus from around 120, Zakum from around 135 and Horntail from around 155.
claims.say: boss runs for late exp, pap at 120, zakum at 135, ht at 155

claims.text: Most players just grind through Maple Island, but Pio and the Recycling is the one quest worth doing because its chair lets you sit and heal.
claims.say: pio and the recycling gives a chair, nice for sit healing

claims.text: At level 10 pick up Olaf's A Lesson on Job Advancement in Lith Harbor, then advance and do the four instructor quests, which pay potions, town scrolls and a good bit of exp.
claims.say: grab olafs job advancement quest at 10, then instructor quests

claims.text: The Sleepywood kill-99 quests pay in potions: the Horny Mushroom one gives 100 White Potions, the Evil Eye one 100 Mana Elixirs, the Zombie Mushroom one 50 Mana Elixirs, and Curse Eye a random scroll and potion.
claims.say: sleepywood kill 99 quests pay white pots and mana elixirs

claims.text: Manji and the Secret Group is a Perion kill quest for levels 18 to 29 with decent exp for the level.
claims.say: manji and the secret group in perion is ok exp for 18-29

claims.text: Request of Mrs. Reade starts the Cleaning the Nautilus chain, but only its first part is available until level 25, so come back for the rest later.
claims.say: cleaning the nautilus chain only has part 1 until lvl 25

claims.text: For Help Me Find My Glasses, go to the right part of the Nautilus map under the tower and click the bushes; the reward is a stack of Return to Nautilus scrolls.
claims.say: glasses quest: click the bushes right side below the tower

claims.text: Protect the Nautilus' Emergency Food Supply together with the follow-up Find Fresh Milk gives a large exp reward for very little effort at level 15.
claims.say: nautilus emergency food + fresh milk quests are easy exp

claims.text: Pia and the Blue Mushroom is a level 20 Henesys drop quest that pays a random DEF scroll.
claims.say: pia and the blue mushroom in henesys gives a random def scroll

claims.text: Shumi's Lost Coin is a level 20 jump quest in Kerning City that pays exp, a point of fame and 30 random town scrolls.
claims.say: shumis lost coin jq in kerning gives town scrolls and fame

claims.text: Camila's Gem is a level 23 puzzle quest in Henesys with good exp for the level and a stack of cakes.
claims.say: camilas gem puzzle in henesys is decent exp plus cakes

claims.text: Stranger's Request in Kerning City is worth the drop grind at level 25 because it pays good exp and an Old Raggedy Cape.
claims.say: strangers request in kerning is worth the grind, gives a cape

claims.text: Around El Nath and Aquaroad, Delivering Food to Spiruna (30) pays mesos and fame, Master Sergeant Fox's Secret (33) pays strong exp, and Tae Gong's Love For His Wife (35) is a plain drop quest.
claims.say: el nath: spiruna gives fame, master sergeant fox good exp

claims.text: At level 52 in Magatia, Parwen the Ghost is a talk-only quest, Getting in the Way of Alcadno needs Helping Out Bedin and leads to An Incident and the Missing Alchemist, and Destroy the Roid needs Russellon's Items for Experiment.
claims.say: lvl 52 magatia: parwen is just talking, the rest need prereqs

claims.text: An Old Code at level 69 in the World Tour area only needs walking and talking and pays moderate exp.
claims.say: an old code at 69 is just walk and talk for some exp

claims.text: Questing is not the most efficient way to level; it is a change of pace from grinding and a way to pick up useful rewards, and these quests can be done solo without funding.
claims.say: questing isnt the fastest exp, its a nice break from grinding

claims.text: Ludibrium Maze PQ is for levels 51 to 71 and is one of the fastest ways to level in that range. A party needs at least three players and five or six is best; start it by talking to Rolly in Ludibrium.
claims.say: maze pq is lvl 51-71, bring 3 to 6, talk to rolly in ludi

claims.text: To reach Ludibrium for the maze PQ, take the ship from Ellinia to Orbis and continue on to Ludibrium.
claims.say: ellinia ship to orbis then on to ludibrium

claims.text: The maze needs at least 30 passes collected to clear it, and the more passes and the less time used, the more exp. The whole maze must be done within 15 minutes.
claims.say: maze needs 30 passes min within 15 min, more and faster is more exp

claims.text: If anyone dies or disconnects and the party drops below three, everyone is kicked out of the maze, so keep the party alive.
claims.say: don't let the maze party drop below 3 or everyone is kicked

claims.text: The maze has 16 rooms. Rooms 1 to 12 have monster boxes that drop passes, rooms 13 to 15 spawn nothing, and room 16 is the meeting room where everyone drops passes for the leader.
claims.say: maze rooms 1-12 have boxes, 13-15 are empty, 16 is the meet room

claims.text: Maze portals change your room number: left goes forward 4, middle forward 7 and right back 3. From room 1 take left, left, middle to reach room 16, and left twice lands on room 9.
claims.say: maze: left +4, middle +7, right -3; 1 to 16 is left left middle

claims.text: Each maze player clears one or two rooms, skips any leftover rooms and heads for room 16. Everyone drops their passes there for the leader, who gives them to Pietri, so make sure no one forgets to drop.
claims.say: clear your rooms, skip leftovers, drop passes in room 16

claims.text: Maze rewards include a random consumable such as elixirs, dews, arrows or monster sacks, plus a random scroll, mostly for armor defense and some 10% cape and overall scrolls for INT or DEX.
claims.say: maze gives a random pot or arrows plus a random scroll

claims.text: Because the maze starts you in room 1, pop the zombie boxes there first, since that room is a solid source of passes.
claims.say: you start the maze in room 1, so smash the zombie boxes there

claims.text: Corsairs cannot give Speed Infusion, which is a Buccaneer skill; their only party buff is Maple Warrior. They are known for self-sufficiency in a Zakum run, not for buffing the team.
claims.say: corsairs cant give speed infusion, only maple warrior

claims.text: Damage a Corsair takes while on the Battleship lowers both the boat's HP and the Corsair's own HP by the same amount, and no potion can heal the boat.
claims.say: hits on the boat cost boat hp and your hp, pots dont heal the boat

claims.text: At Zakum, a Corsair dismounts only just before the 1/1 attack, the biggest hit. Dismounting for weaker attacks costs more damage than it saves.
claims.say: corsairs dismount only for zakum's 1/1, not smaller hits

claims.text: Bullseye makes a Corsair's shots hit only the marked target even with monsters in between, and Battleship Cannon still fires with monsters on top of you, so Zakum's summons do not block a Corsair's damage.
claims.say: with bullseye up, summons dont block a corsair's cannon

claims.text: A Corsair at Zakum likes to stand among the summons: constant weak hits and the short invulnerability after each shield the boat from the big 1/1. Leave the summons around a Corsair alive instead of clearing them.
claims.say: dont kill the summons hugging the corsair, theyre protecting him

claims.text: A Corsair usually stands on the right side of Zakum's body to hide in the summons, so top platforms, especially top right, are poor spots for one in a Zakum run.
claims.say: corsairs want the right side of zakum, not the top platforms

claims.text: While the boat is broken a Corsair falls back on Burst Fire and Wrath of the Octopi, which still hit hard. Burst Fire works badly with monsters very close, so the Corsair may step back left.
claims.say: boat broke? burst fire and octopi, still decent damage

claims.text: A Corsair has to watch Zakum's attack animations to dismount in time, so he chats little during the fight; talking costs boat HP and damage, especially when HP washed and using % potions.
claims.say: corsairs dont chat much at zakum, they watch for the 1/1

claims.text: Corsairs sometimes keep their HP below max with flat-heal food such as Melting Cheese or Reindeer Milk so Zakum's 1/1 hurts less. % potions on a big HP pool make that hit worse, which is why they dislike extra healing.
claims.say: corsairs keep hp below max so 1/1 hurts less, dont over heal

claims.text: If the Sharp Eyes user disconnects during Zakum, Corsairs lose much less damage than Night Lords do, because their damage is calculated differently.
claims.say: losing sharp eyes hurts night lords more than corsairs

claims.text: To start washing a Night Lord, gather about 60-80 INT worth of gear, add some INT, and wash whenever you can on the way to 135.
claims.say: get 60-80 int of gear and wash on the way to 135

claims.text: Adding INT only from level 85 on gives too few levels of extra MP before you reset it, so some players advise making a new character with INT and washing from early on.
claims.say: adding int at 85+ is too late, better remake and wash early

claims.text: Thieves gain more HP from putting fresh level-up AP into HP than from washing it later, so start adding HP from around level 30.
claims.say: thieves get more hp adding fresh ap to hp, start around 30

claims.text: Before entering Orbis Party Quest, the party leader can feed Wonky the Fairy food to raise the odds of a secret mission, which adds extra exp at the bonus stage.
claims.say: leader should feed wonky before opq for a secret mission

claims.text: Wonky's first replies about enjoying the food don't mean success yet; keep feeding him, same or mixed food, until he turns happy and hands over some items, often after three or four feeds.
claims.say: keep feeding wonky until hes happy and gives you items

claims.text: The food you feed Wonky the Fairy can be bought from the shops in Orbis.
claims.say: you can buy wonky food in orbis

claims.text: Once inside the PQ, talk to Wonky the Fairy right away; you get only one chance to take the mission, and if he just offers to let you leave, no mission was granted.
claims.say: talk to wonky inside, if he only offers exit theres no mission

claims.text: Secret missions are picked at random: clear the PQ within 25 minutes, gather all pieces from the Lobby, gather all seeds from the Garden, kill the Cellions, or kill the Lucidas.
claims.say: opq missions are random: 25 min clear, items, cellions or lucidas

claims.text: For the Lobby piece and Garden seed missions, collect all of them (6 pieces, 7 seeds), and the leader must keep every one in inventory until the bonus stage.
claims.say: for item missions the leader holds every piece till bonus

claims.text: For the Cellion mission, the leader has to be the first one into the Room of Darkness, then the party kills every Jr. Cellion inside.
claims.say: cellion mission: leader enters room of darkness first

claims.text: The Lucida mission has three rooms that only one player each can enter; Lucidas hit hard, so send a warrior or a mage with Magic Guard, and Dark Sight gives no protection there.
claims.say: lucida rooms: send a warrior or magic guard mage, dark sight fails

claims.text: Normal attacks don't hurt the Lucidas; you kill each one by hitting the levers in its room.
claims.say: hit the levers to kill lucidas, normal attacks dont work

claims.text: The leader shouldn't do the Lucida rooms: one person per room means a dead leader can't hand over leadership. Whoever goes in should give their stone pieces to a teammate first.
claims.say: leader skips lucida rooms, give your stone pieces away first

claims.text: A good split is one player soloing the Lucida mission while everyone else runs the normal Orbis PQ stages.
claims.say: one person solos lucidas while the rest do normal opq

claims.text: After killing the Lucidas, climb to the top and break the boxes in the next room; they drop crystal ores and refined crystals.
claims.say: after lucidas, break the boxes up top for crystal ores

claims.text: Secret missions aren't guaranteed, but proper feeding gets one in most runs; the author restarts the PQ when none appears, since missions take a minute or two and add good exp.
claims.say: no secret mission? some leaders just restart opq

claims.text: A thief needs 25 DEX at level 10 to advance, so add DEX first; LUK does little until you start throwing stars.
claims.say: thief needs 25 dex at 10, luk can wait

claims.text: If you put too much into LUK and reach level 10 short of 25 DEX, either keep leveling until DEX hits 25 or remake the character.
claims.say: short on dex at 10? keep leveling or just remake

claims.text: Beginners can use Three Snails, which throws snail shells, to add damage while working toward level 10.
claims.say: use three snails with snail shells for extra damage

claims.text: Finish all the Maple Island quests before leaving; their exp makes reaching level 10 much quicker.
claims.say: do all the maple island quests, easy exp toward 10

claims.text: Start Kenta's Advice by talking to Kenta, the Zoo Assistant, on Aqua Road.
claims.say: kenta the zoo assistant on aqua road gives the pet speed quest

claims.text: Kenta's Advice needs five pieces of paper found in boxes on the monster maps of Aqua Road. Your pet needs closeness of at least 15; its level does not matter.
claims.say: 5 papers from aqua road boxes, pet needs 15 closeness not level

claims.text: The speed bonus only goes to the lead (boss) pet. For several pets, finish the quest once, then re-accept it and turn it in again for each other pet with that pet as the lead; you do not need to collect the papers again.
claims.say: multi pets: turn in again with each pet in front, no papers

claims.text: Test the new pet speed on a flat map, since uneven maps make it hard to see whether the speed bonus worked.
claims.say: test pet speed on a flat map

claims.text: Corsair damage comes from DEX, and STR is only there to meet gun equip requirements, so keep STR as low as you can while still being able to hold your gun.
claims.say: dex is the main stat for corsair, str just for gun reqs

claims.text: Put every AP into DEX until about level 90, then add STR a little at a time so you can hold a strong endgame gun; this keeps early damage high and still lets you transition.
claims.say: all dex till around 90 then add str for your endgame gun

claims.text: A permanently STR-less Corsair is very strong early but falls behind a low-STR one later, because weapon attack becomes worth more than DEX at higher levels.
claims.say: dexless corsair is great early but falls off later

claims.text: Pirates can level through first job with Somersault Kick, which hits several mobs and does not need a gun, so wield the highest weapon attack weapon you have while doing it.
claims.say: somersault kick trains pirate fast, no gun needed

claims.text: The first job core is Double Shot and Dash maxed; leftover points go to Bullet Time and Somersault Kick, and the order of those last two barely matters.
claims.say: max double shot and dash first, the rest barely matters

claims.text: Take one point in Invisible Shot to unlock a multi-target attack, max Gun Mastery next, then max Invisible Shot, which becomes your main attack, especially in Monster Carnival.
claims.say: 1 point invisible shot, max gun mastery, then max invisible

claims.text: After your main attack, a handful of points in Gun Booster is plenty; maxing it early only buys a longer buff duration.
claims.say: dont max gun booster early, just a few points

claims.text: Wings needs about five points to unlock Recoil Shot, which works like a slower flash jump; max Recoil Shot right after that, then finish Wings for mobility.
claims.say: 5 points in wings unlocks recoil shot, max that next

claims.text: Bind Wings then Recoil Shot to one macro key and spam it while running and turning in mid-air; it makes gunslingers noticeably faster across flat maps.
claims.say: macro wings + recoil shot to cross maps way faster

claims.text: Blank Shot stuns monsters; you will rarely rely on it, but it is worth maxing after Recoil Shot and Wings for the occasional stun.
claims.say: blank shot stuns, rarely used but nice to have

claims.text: Spare second job points can go into Bullet Time or Grenade; neither matters much, so spend on them last.
claims.say: extra sp goes to bullet time or grenade, low priority

claims.text: Ice Splitter and Flamethrower are the Outlaw mobbing skills. Ice Splitter is more about freezing than damage, so stop adding points once it hits its full target count and freeze time.
claims.say: ice splitter is for freezing, dont overinvest in it

claims.text: Put Ice Splitter and then Flamethrower on one macro key so mobs get frozen and burned in a single press when mobbing.
claims.say: macro ice splitter into flamethrower for mobbing

claims.text: Max Homing Beacon during third job, because Bullseye in fourth job requires it.
claims.say: max homing beacon in 3rd job, bullseye needs it

claims.text: One early point in Homing Beacon helps if you want to hunt the Headless Horseman before fourth job.
claims.say: a homing beacon point helps vs the headless horseman

claims.text: Battleship health goes up with every character level above 120, so a fresh Corsair has a fragile ship that becomes sturdier with each level.
claims.say: battleship gets more hp every level past 120

claims.text: To get Battleship, talk to Kyrin, choose the second option to fight her, and survive for two minutes.
claims.say: talk to kyrin, pick option 2 and survive 2 min for battleship

claims.text: Battleship Cannon needs 150 Spirit Viking kills plus 50 of their drops, and Battleship Torpedo needs the same from Gigantic Spirit Vikings.
claims.say: cannon wants spirit vikings, torpedo wants gigantic ones

claims.text: Hypnotize starts with the girl in the training room: choose the second option, clear three small jump sections where touching the pink or blue snakes sends you back to the start, then talk to the NPC at the end.
claims.say: hypnotize has a jump quest, dodge the snakes or restart

claims.text: At 120 put one point each into Battleship, Battleship Cannon and Battleship Torpedo, then max Cannon, Bullseye and Rapid Fire in that order before spending on anything else.
claims.say: 1 pt each ship skill then max cannon, bullseye, rapid fire

claims.text: Bullseye marks a single target so it takes extra damage from you, which makes it excellent for bosses.
claims.say: bullseye is great on bosses, max it after cannon

claims.text: After 120 most Corsair exp comes from bossing, so run bosses whenever they are up instead of grinding.
claims.say: as a corsair bossing beats grinding for exp after 120

claims.text: Rapid Fire keeps your damage up while the Battleship is broken, which matters in long boss fights like Zakum where the ship will go down a few times.
claims.say: rapid fire covers you when the ship breaks at zakum

claims.text: Guns attack fast but not at the fastest speed with Gun Booster alone, so a Buccaneer's Speed Infusion gives Corsairs extra attack speed, while claw users already hit the cap with just their booster.
