claims.say: speed infusion actually helps gun users, unlike claws

claims.text: Corsairs bring no party buffs but add top-tier single-target damage, which is why bossing parties want them; they benefit from nearly every buff they are given.
claims.say: corsair has no buffs but huge boss dps, parties want one

claims.text: Corsair damage depends on riding the Battleship, so the class needs more attention during boss fights than most others.
claims.say: corsair dps depends on your ship so watch it in boss fights

claims.text: With Sharp Eyes and Speed Infusion a Corsair out-damages a Night Lord, with only Sharp Eyes the Night Lord does more, and solo the Corsair does more.
claims.say: corsair beats nl solo, nl wins with only sharp eyes

claims.text: Corsair leveling from third job to 120 is slow with weak damage and mobbing, so expect a long grind until fourth job, where the class finally becomes strong.
claims.say: corsair is slow until 4th job, then it gets strong

claims.text: Instead of only killing snails to level 7, run the Maple Island quest chain plus the first job quests; a new character ends up around level 11.
claims.say: do the maple island quests, you hit about 11 after 1st job

claims.text: For Pio's Collecting Recycled Goods, break the 10 boxes found along the way from Maria to Lucas.
claims.say: pio's quest: smash the 10 boxes between maria and lucas

claims.text: Kill 7 Red Snails during Mai's training so Lucas' Cute Daughter finishes at the same time.
claims.say: kill 7 red snails, counts for mai and lucas' daughter

claims.text: Accept Helping Out Yoona early; it is finished by killing 10 Shrooms.
claims.say: yoona's quest is just 10 shrooms

claims.text: Once on Victoria Island, find Olaf for A Lesson on Job Advancement, then follow the Path quest for the job you want.
claims.say: on victoria talk to olaf for the job advancement quest

claims.text: First job advancement happens in Henesys for bowmen, Perion for warriors, Nautilus for pirates and Kerning City for thieves.
claims.say: 1st job: bow henesys, war perion, pirate nautilus, thief kerning

claims.text: Future magicians should skip Lucas' Cute Daughter so they don't overlevel before advancing at level 8.
claims.say: mages skip lucas' cute daughter, don't overlevel before 8

claims.text: Advance to Magician at level 8 before turning in The Path of a Magician so its exp lands on your new job instead of overleveling a beginner.
claims.say: mages: job advance at 8 first, then the path of a magician

claims.text: You need to be at least level 7 to leave Maple Island.
claims.say: you can leave maple island at lv 7

claims.text: In the Mu Lung Dojo at roughly levels 120 to 159, most of your damage comes from the energy bar's Bamboo Rain, so spend the bar on that. Power Explosion only pays off if your damage is already huge.
claims.say: in dojo at that level just spend your bar on bamboo rain

claims.text: Night Lords, Corsairs, Marksmen and Bowmasters fill the dojo energy bar quickest, so they make the best bar builders and are the best ones to nuke early and refill.
claims.say: nl corsair mm and bm fill the dojo bar fastest

claims.text: A Bishop who is not needed for healing at the moment can cast Magic Claw or Energy Bolt to build the energy bar and add a nuke for the party instead of only healing.
claims.say: bishop, magic claw between heals fills the bar for nukes

claims.text: Bishops, Night Lords, Shadowers and Buccaneers cope on their own with avoid, i-frames or healing, so they should support the team: loot potions for low members, heal, or draw the boss's attention.
claims.say: tanky classes should loot pots for the weaker ones and pull aggro

claims.text: If you are low on HP with no way to heal, step to a safe spot and let teammates finish the boss instead of playing hero. A living player can still add another nuke later, which is worth more than a few hits.
claims.say: low hp? hide and let others kill it, alive beats a few hits

claims.text: Spamming your top damage skill drains MP, so on long dojo fights like Papulatus ration it once potions run out and pick the skills that deal the most damage per MP rather than per second.
claims.say: watch your mp on long bosses, dont just spam the top skill

claims.text: Dojo bosses only summon their minions after losing roughly a third of their health, and potions dropped on the floor vanish after 3 minutes, so plan your potion supply around those drops.
claims.say: minions only spawn once the boss is hurt, and pots vanish in 3 min

claims.text: Manon, Griffey and Papulatus cast a debuff that strips your buffs. It also removes Magic Guard, which is deadly for Arch Mages and Bishops, so keep checking your buffs during these fights.
claims.say: dojo debuff strips magic guard so recheck your buffs as a mage

claims.text: Manon's one-HP attack comes when it looks up and takes a big breath before blowing fire downward. The windup is long, so you have time to react.
claims.say: manon looking up and inhaling means the 1hp breath is coming

claims.text: Dodging Manon's one-HP breath: back away if you have range, walk into its body for contact damage if you fight up close, or use an i-frame or mobility skill. Leave its body afterwards to avoid stun and debuff.
claims.say: back off from manon's breath or eat the contact hit instead

claims.text: Manon and Griffey have short reach, so teams usually corner them against the right edge, and a hurt player with no heal can wait on the far edge out of range.
claims.say: corner manon or griffey to the right, weak ones wait on the far edge

claims.text: At this level Manon and Griffey normally go down without any Bamboo Rain, and most party members have their energy bars built up by the time Manon dies.
claims.say: no need to nuke manon or griffey, just fill your bar

claims.text: Griffey's pendant glows blue before its debuff and yellow before its one-HP attack, so watch the pendant and be ready to react.
claims.say: griffey pendant glows blue for debuff, yellow for the 1hp hit

claims.text: Griffey's one-HP attack has a short windup and is hard to predict. If you have five-digit HP, standing in its body and taking contact damage is better than being cut to 1 HP.
claims.say: with 5 digit hp just eat griffey's contact hit rather than the 1hp

claims.text: Griffey's one-HP attack seems to hit only whoever stands in front of it, so sturdier teammates should keep it near the centre to draw its attention off weaker players.
claims.say: let the tanky ones keep griffey centered so it faces them

claims.text: If you are down to 1 HP as Griffey dies, wait on that floor until teammates collect potion drops before entering Leviathan's floor, since Leviathan's attacks cover a large area.
claims.say: at 1hp before leviathan? wait on the floor for pots first

claims.text: Leviathan has no one-HP attack but a huge hit box and plenty of health, and this is the floor where players with low survivability tend to die.
claims.say: no 1hp move on leviathan but squishy players still die there

claims.text: Leviathan's confusion flips your direction keys, but you can still jump by pressing down first. Its weaken, which looks the same, is worse: jumping is the only way to dodge its fire without i-frames.
claims.say: confused on leviathan? press down before jumping, still works

claims.text: Leviathan glows yellow, then spits knockback fire over the whole side of the map it faces. Jump just before the breath or stand inside its body to avoid it. Its closer frost breath can weaken you.
claims.say: jump right before leviathan's fire breath or stand in its body

claims.text: Instead of cornering Leviathan, keep it away from the edges and let tanky teammates pull its aggro so it faces away from weaker players. Swap sides if needed, accepting some contact damage.
claims.say: keep leviathan off the edges and let tanks pull it away from squishies

claims.text: Papulatus' lightning hits a huge area all around it but not the whole map. Standing on the opposite edge from it is safe, so pin it to one edge and keep to the other.
claims.say: stand on the opposite edge from papulatus to dodge its lightning

claims.text: If the team has Dark Knights or Buccaneers, have them shove Papulatus to an edge right away so everyone else gets a safe edge from its lightning.
claims.say: dk or bucc should knock papulatus to one edge right away

claims.text: Papulatus' one-HP attack comes when it opens its mouth and a yellow plate forms over its face. It reaches medium range all around it, and afterwards it curls into a shell that blocks attacks.
claims.say: papulatus mouth open with yellow plate = 1hp attack incoming

claims.text: To dodge Papulatus' one-HP attack: retreat if you have range, run into its body for contact damage if you fight up close, or use an i-frame skill. Slow, drawn-out attack animations leave no time to react.
claims.say: retreat, eat the contact hit, or use an i-frame vs papulatus 1hp

claims.text: Papulatus' bombs explode if you get close and then drop no potions. Kill them from range, and close-range attackers should back off as soon as the pink swirl and blue stars show where they spawn.
claims.say: kill papulatus bombs from range, if they blow up they drop no pots

claims.text: HP washing raises max HP by shifting AP out of MP and into HP with AP Resets; it is most common on Night Lords, Bowmasters and Corsairs.
claims.say: nls, bms and sairs hp wash with ap resets for bossing

claims.text: Dark Knights also HP wash so they can keep Berserk going at Horntail, which needs a large HP pool and plenty of Ginger Ales.
claims.say: dks wash hp so they can berserk at horntail

claims.text: Level up wearing as much INT as possible, from gear or base stats, because higher INT means more MP per level and so more to wash later.
claims.say: level in int gear, more int means more mp to wash

claims.text: If you leveled in INT gear for a while without washing, you can still convert that stored MP later by AP Resetting from MP into HP until you can no longer wash.
claims.say: skipped washing? you can still reset mp into hp later

claims.text: Double washing puts every level-up AP into MP and then resets those points from MP into HP; it can reach very high HP but costs a lot of AP Resets.
claims.say: double wash: all level ap into mp, then reset mp into hp

claims.text: Many Night Lords wash to around 12k HP so they can survive Black Crow without needing Hyper Body.
claims.say: nls usually wash to ~12k hp to tank black crow without hb

claims.text: AP placed into MP is not wasted; you can keep leveling with it there, even while leeching, and wash it out whenever you like, even at level 200.
claims.say: ap parked in mp can be washed out later, even at 200

claims.text: Light washing while relying on a Dark Knight's Hyper Body for bosses is the cheapest approach, though it leaves you with less HP than heavy washing.
claims.say: cheap route: wash lightly and lean on a dk's hyper body

claims.text: A Husky pet can wear Snowboard Gear, Husky Yellow Tights, the Bunny Suit, Bare Bones, the Oinker Suit or the Red Fur Coat.
claims.say: husky pets can wear snowboard gear or the red fur coat

claims.text: A Panda pet can wear the Chestnut Cap, Clown Dress or Pet-o-Lantern.
claims.say: panda pets can wear the chestnut cap or clown dress

claims.text: A Penguin pet's equip is the Penguin Earmuff Set.
claims.say: penguin pets wear the penguin earmuff set

claims.text: A Skunk pet's equip is the Gas Mask.
claims.say: skunk pets wear the gas mask

claims.text: A Black Pig pet's equip is the Mushroom Suit.
claims.say: black pig pets wear the mushroom suit

claims.text: The baby dino pets, boy and girl, can wear Dino King & Queen or Ghosty.
claims.say: dino pets can wear dino king and queen or ghosty

claims.text: A Kargo pet can wear Cowboy Kargo or Mini Kargo Wings.
claims.say: kargo pets wear cowboy kargo or mini kargo wings

claims.text: A Jr. Balrog pet's equip is the Crimson Mask.
claims.say: jr balrog pets wear the crimson mask

claims.text: A Snowman pet's equip is the Snowman Gear.
claims.say: snowman pets wear snowman gear

claims.text: A Yeti pet can wear Prince Pepe or White Angel.
claims.say: yeti pets can wear prince pepe or white angel

claims.text: A Turkey pet's equip is the Baby Turkey Carriage.
claims.say: turkey pets wear the baby turkey carriage

claims.text: A Porcupine pet's equip is the Porcupine Sunglasses.
claims.say: porcupine pets wear porcupine sunglasses

claims.text: A Sun Wu Kong pet's equip is the Mini Celestial Wand.
claims.say: sun wu kong pets wear the mini celestial wand

claims.text: A White Duck pet's equip is the Scuba Mask.
claims.say: white duck pets wear the scuba mask

claims.text: A Pink Bean pet's equip is the Starry Stereo Headset.
claims.say: pink bean pets wear the starry stereo headset

claims.text: A Kino pet's equip is Kino's Green Mushroom Hat.
claims.say: kino pets wear kinos green mushroom hat

claims.text: A Golden Pig pet's equip is the Golden Pig Fortune Pouch.
claims.say: golden pig pets wear the golden pig fortune pouch

claims.text: A Rudolph pet's equip is Rudolph's Sleigh.
claims.say: rudolph pets wear rudolphs sleigh

claims.text: A Baby Tiger pet's equip is the Baby Tiger Wings.
claims.say: baby tiger pets wear baby tiger wings

claims.text: Moonstone and Star Gem wedding rings give 30 magic defense and 3 slots, while Golden Heart and Silver Swan give 10 and 2 slots; the first two are better but need pricier ingredients.
claims.say: moonstone or star gem are the best wedding rings

claims.text: Wedding rings are untradeable and one-of-a-kind, so each character can only ever hold one.
claims.say: you only get one wedding ring and its untradeable

claims.text: Spouses standing near each other with their wedding rings equipped show a special effect.
claims.say: wear your wedding rings near each other for an effect

claims.text: Chaos Scroll 60% works on rings too, and Zakum is one place to get Chaos Scrolls.
claims.say: you can chaos scroll rings, zakum drops chaos scrolls

claims.text: A washing Night Lord may need MP washing as well: add AP to MP, then reset that point back into LUK, so there is enough MP to keep washing HP.
claims.say: mp wash too: ap into mp, then reset it back into luk

claims.text: The usual mage wash: each level put the 5 new AP into MP, then use AP Resets to move those points from MP to INT, and further resets to move MP into HP.
claims.say: mage wash: level ap into mp, reset mp to int, then mp to hp

claims.text: Applying the same skill-reset idea to MP washing is not worth it: the extra MP is small and you would sit on hundreds of unspent AP for a long time.
claims.say: dont bother with the skill reset trick for mp washing

claims.text: Chief Bandits are among the fastest levelers from 70 to 120 using only Meso Explosion; one strong method is farming Dreamy Ghosts while a Priest herds them.
claims.say: cb levels fast 70-120 with meso explosion at himes

claims.text: The Priest teleports from right to left hitting every Dreamy Ghost with Heal (Shining Ray casts too slowly), waits on the left until they bunch up, then teleports back to the Chief Bandit.
claims.say: priest tags every hime with heal and drags them over

claims.text: The Chief Bandit waits in Dark Sight on the right side dropping mesos; when the Priest shows up on the minimap, leave Dark Sight, jump right so you face left, and tap Meso Explosion as the ghosts arrive.
claims.say: drop mesos in dark sight, then pop meso explosion on the pack

claims.text: Meso Explosion damage comes from the dropped mesos, not your weapon or stats, so a clean low-level dagger is enough and HP washing does not hurt it.
claims.say: meso explosion ignores your weapon, a clean dagger is fine

claims.text: Dreamy Ghosts deal both touch and magic damage, so with Meso Guard on set your auto-HP high enough that a potion always keeps you safe, around 30-35% with 3000 HP and 2000 HP potions.
claims.say: set auto hp around 30-35% when bombing himes

claims.text: Bubblings at Kerning Subway Line 1 Area 1 are a standard pick for levels 10 to 20.
claims.say: bubblings at subway line 1 area 1 are good for 10 to 20

claims.text: Wild Boars in The Land of Wild Boar I are the pick for levels 20 to 25.
claims.say: wild boars at perion are the spot for 20 to 25

claims.text: Pink Teddies and Brown Teddies in the Ludibrium Terrace Hall suit levels 25 to 30.
claims.say: teddies in ludibrium terrace hall are good for 25 to 30

claims.text: Jr. Wraiths at Kerning Subway Line 1 Area 2 suit levels 30 to 36.
claims.say: jr wraiths at subway line 1 area 2 for 30 to 36

claims.text: Wraiths at Kerning Subway Line 1 Area 4 suit levels 43 to 51.
claims.say: wraiths at subway line 1 area 4 for 43 to 51

claims.text: Oly Oly and Dark Fission at Malaysia's Muddy Banks 1 suit levels 51 to 53.
claims.say: oly oly and dark fission at muddy banks 1 for 51 to 53

claims.text: Rodeos at Malaysia's Muddy Banks 2 suit levels 56 to 65, and it is also a preferred leech trading map.
claims.say: rodeos at muddy banks 2 are good for 56 to 65

claims.text: Froscolas and Jester Scarlions at Malaysia's Fantasy Theme Park 1 suit levels 67 to 75.
claims.say: froscola and jester scarlion at fantasy theme park 1, 67 to 75

claims.text: Harps and Blood Harps at Leafre's Sky Nest II suit levels 78 to 85, and you need to be level 78 to get exp from them.
claims.say: harps at sky nest 2 in leafre for 78 to 85

claims.text: Skelegons and Skelosauruses at Leafre's The Dragon Nest Left Behind are a pick from level 108 up.
claims.say: skelegon and skelosaurus at the dragon nest from 108

claims.text: To get exp from a party member's kills, the low-level partner must be at most five levels below the character doing the killing; being far above the killer's level is fine.
claims.say: to leech exp you need to be within 5 levels of the killer

claims.text: Gobies hit hard and other Aqua Road monsters can one-shot a weak character, so a partner sharing the kills has to stay at the keyboard, keep Magic Guard up and feed the pet.
claims.say: gobies hit hard so keep magic guard up and dont afk

claims.text: Bigfoot, the area boss in the Phantom Forest, is a target for characters from about level 105.
claims.say: bigfoot in the phantom forest is a boss for 105 and up

claims.text: Bigfoot only hurts with its lower body, so you can jump straight over it.
claims.say: you can jump over bigfoot, only its lower body hits

claims.text: A Marksman can pin Bigfoot by luring it near a wall, jumping over it and using Power Knock-Back until about half its body is pushed off-screen.
claims.say: jump over bigfoot and power knockback it into the corner

claims.text: Find the pin depth where all Strafe hits land on Bigfoot: pushed too far, some hits miss during its invincibility frames; too shallow, it slips out of the pin.
claims.say: pin bigfoot at the right depth or strafes start missing

claims.text: On the Bigfoot map crowded with Jr. Wraiths, bring Frostprey or another summon to keep them cleared.
claims.say: bring frostprey to clear the jr wraiths around bigfoot

claims.text: Your hits must be strong enough to knock Bigfoot back; a lightly funded Marksman in the 120s or 130s may not manage it.
claims.say: low funded mms might not hit hard enough to knock bigfoot back

claims.text: Max speed and jump make Bigfoot easier to handle; extra pets with speed and jump pet equipment help reach the cap.
claims.say: get max speed and jump for bigfoot, pet equips help

claims.text: A Marksman with plenty of HP can fight Bigfoot fairly safely; the pinning method is for those who cannot take its hits.
claims.say: with enough hp mm can tank bigfoot, pin it if you can't

claims.text: With similar gear and a perfect pin a Marksman may out-damage a Bowmaster on Bigfoot, but a Bowmaster simply holds Hurricane and has a much easier time.
claims.say: bm on bigfoot is easier, mm only wins with a perfect pin

claims.text: The 10% Scroll for Pet Equip. for Speed (+3 speed) drops from Jr. Wraith, Lorang and Dyle.
claims.say: 10% pet speed scrolls drop from jr wraith, lorang and dyle

claims.text: The 100% Scroll for Pet Equip. for Speed (+1 speed) drops from Bubbling, Green Mushroom and Horny Mushroom.
claims.say: 100% pet speed scrolls: bubbling, green mushroom, horny mushroom

claims.text: The 10% Scroll for Pet Equip. for Jump (+3 jump) drops from Lorang and Tae Roon.
claims.say: 10% pet jump scrolls drop from lorang and tae roon

claims.text: The 100% Scroll for Pet Equip. for Jump (+1 jump) drops from Green Mushroom and Jr. Necki.
claims.say: 100% pet jump scrolls drop from green mushroom and jr. necki

claims.text: HP washing raises base HP without Hyper Body or HP gear: use AP Resets to move points out of MP and into HP.
claims.say: hp washing = using ap resets to turn mp points into hp

claims.text: Washing with fresh level-up AP: put a point in HP, then use an AP Reset to take one point out of MP and place it in your main stat. That gives about 20 to 24 HP per reset and costs 12 MP.
claims.say: fresh ap into hp then reset mp into a stat nets 20 to 24 hp

claims.text: Straight MP-to-HP washing: use an AP Reset to remove a point from MP and add it to HP. That gives about 16 to 20 HP per reset and costs 12 MP each.
claims.say: mp straight into hp with resets gets 16 to 20 hp each

claims.text: MP washing builds base MP so you can wash more HP later. Every 10 base INT adds one extra MP per AP put into MP on level-up, so put fresh AP into MP and reset it into your main stat.
claims.say: mp wash fresh ap then reset it, more int means more mp per point

claims.text: Leveling up with Maple Warrior active gives more MP from AP put into MP, since the extra INT counts at the moment you level.
claims.say: level up with maple warrior on to get more mp per point

claims.text: The lowest MP you can wash down to is level x 14 + 148. Your extra MP is your base MP minus that minimum, and each HP wash uses 12 MP of it.
claims.say: min mp is level times 14 plus 148, the rest is washable

claims.text: Early build for a washing thief: use the starting 9 AP on INT, bring INT to 20 and DEX to 25, then put everything into INT up to level 10 and advance to Rogue.
claims.say: wash thief lvl 1 to 10: int to 20, dex to 25, then all int

claims.text: From level 11 to 30, put all AP into INT while leveling a washing thief, and wear low-level INT gear at the right levels.
claims.say: wash thief 11 to 30: all ap into int

claims.text: From level 31 to 70, plan on 5 AP Resets per level. HP wash that level's 5 points if you have 60 or more extra MP, otherwise MP wash them, and keep building INT to your goal.
claims.say: 31 to 70: hp wash if you have 60+ extra mp, else mp wash

claims.text: HP washing early lets a thief do Zakum at about level 50 without Hyper Body, because the base HP is high enough.
claims.say: hp washed thieves can zak at 50 without hyper body

claims.text: Decide your base INT goal by level 70: at least about 240, and around 400 base INT if you want to reach 30k HP.
claims.say: pick your base int goal by 70: 240 min, ~400 for 30k hp

claims.text: From level 71 to 135, MP wash on every level up. After reaching the base INT goal, MP wash into LUK instead, or save the fresh AP and wash it all at once.
claims.say: 71 to 135: mp wash every level, then into luk once int goal is hit

claims.text: From level 136 on, HP wash every level up. If you run out of levels before your goal, finish by doing straight MP-to-HP resets.
claims.say: 136+: hp wash each level, finish with straight mp to hp

claims.text: With about 400 base INT and Maple Warrior at each level up, 30k HP is possible from around level 125 to 130, and MP washing until level 135 makes it a sure thing.
claims.say: 30k hp is possible around lvl 125 to 130 with 400 base int

claims.text: HP washing between level 30 and 70 is optional. Fresh AP gives more HP than MP-to-HP, so it is efficient early, but you can still reach 30k HP either way.
claims.say: hp washing at 30 to 70 is optional, you can still reach 30k

claims.text: This heavy washing route assumes you have mesos or a Bishop or Archmage mule with Holy Symbol to carry you to level 135. A lone assassin with no support should not follow it.
claims.say: this wash route needs a bishop mule or mesos, not for a lone assassin

claims.text: A Robo pet can evolve once it reaches pet level 15 by using the Rock of Evolution; the evolved color varies, and gold is one possible result.
claims.say: robo pets evolve at pet lvl 15 with a rock of evolution

claims.text: If no evolution quest appears for a pet that qualifies, put the pet away and summon it again; that makes the quest show up.
claims.say: no evolve quest? put your pet away and take it out again

claims.text: A warrior planning to HP wash can put only the STR needed for the first job advance into STR and every other AP into INT from level 1, building a large MP pool.
claims.say: wash warrior: min str for job, rest int from lvl 1

claims.text: After advancing to warrior at 10, put SP into Improved MaxHP Increase first.
claims.say: after 1st job put sp in improved maxhp increase first

claims.text: A mostly-INT warrior does almost no damage, so this plan relies on buying leech through the low levels, ideally up to somewhere between 30 and 50.
claims.say: an int warrior can't kill much, get leeched to 30-50

claims.text: Once leeched, use AP Resets to move the INT into STR, then HP wash as usual and max out STR.
claims.say: then ap reset the int into str and hp wash

claims.text: Skin care in Ludibrium, Mu Lung, Ariant, Henesys, New Leaf City, Singapore and Orbis Park offers the Light, Tanned, Dark, Pale, Ashen, Green and Ghostly complexions.
claims.say: skin care in most towns has the 7 basic skin tones

claims.text: The Pale Pink and Clay complexions are only offered at the skin care in Ariant and Orbis Park.
claims.say: pale pink and clay skin are only in ariant and orbis park

claims.text: To bank MP for HP washing, a warrior can add only the 35 STR the job needs and the rest into INT, then after advancing at 10 reset that STR into INT and leave STR and DEX at 4.
claims.say: int warrior: 35 str to advance, then reset it all into int

claims.text: While early levels need little exp, put every AP into INT and put on whatever INT gear you own before each level up to collect as much MP as possible.
claims.say: put all ap in int and wear int gear before you level

claims.text: An INT warrior still levels skills like a normal warrior, maxing Improved MaxHP Increase first.
claims.say: max improved maxhp increase first, rest like a normal warrior

claims.text: An INT warrior gets damage from cheap STR-scrolled low-level armor and a blunt weapon scrolled with 30% attack scrolls; seven passes can make a starter club match a level 35 Maple weapon with no stat requirement.
claims.say: scroll a cheap club with 30% att scrolls, no str needed

claims.text: Cheap accuracy scrolls (30%, 60% or 70%) on gloves and a hat let an INT warrior keep hitting mobs while STR and DEX stay at 4.
claims.say: acc scroll gloves and hat so the int warrior can hit stuff

claims.text: Attack and accuracy boosting potions from NPC shops are cheap enough to use the whole way while leveling an INT warrior.
claims.say: use att and acc pots the whole time on an int warrior

claims.text: An INT warrior doing Kerning City Party Quest should plan on being the party leader rather than counting on joining other groups.
claims.say: as an int warrior, lead your own kpq runs

claims.text: Leeching from a low-level Dragon Knight using Dragon Roar costs less than a Bishop leech, gives a similar share of exp, and lets you wear full INT gear for more MP per level.
claims.say: leech off a low dk with dragon roar, cheaper than a bishop

claims.text: Around level 50 you HP wash the stored MP and reset INT back into STR, or STR with some DEX, for a normal build.
claims.say: around 50, wash the mp into hp and reset int to str

claims.text: From level 1 to 20 you can simply explore the world and take every available quest that NPCs offer; there is no need to rush to a fixed training map.
claims.say: early on just explore and take every quest npcs offer

claims.text: Land of Wild Boar II suits an archer from about level 20 to 45. Its drops are good for mesos: Leather (craftable into work gloves), Power Crystal Ore, Steel Ore and the occasional Maple weapon.
claims.say: land of wild boar ii is good for archers lvl 20-45, leather and ores

claims.text: Sahel 3 on Sunset Road is a decent archer spot for roughly levels 35 to 55, with DEX Crystal Ore, Steel Ore and Mithril Ore among the drops worth selling.
claims.say: sahel 3 works for archers around lvl 35-55, drops ores

claims.text: Monkey Swamp II is an archer option for about levels 40 to 70. Damage feels low if you stacked INT, but it drops Emerald Ore, Leather and equipment like Maple claws and Red Whip.
claims.say: monkey swamp ii for archers lvl 40-70, emerald ore and leather drops

claims.text: Cold Field II is a long-term archer spot from about level 55 up to 135. It drops Steel Ore, LUK Crystal Ore, Leather, Scrolls for Cape for DEX 60% and Maple weapons that sell well.
claims.say: cold field ii is a long term archer spot from lvl 55 to 135

claims.text: Spiegelmann's Necklace is an early accessory you earn by collecting coins from Monster Carnival, a good low-cost upgrade for a character around level 30.
claims.say: get spiegelmann's necklace with monster carnival coins around lvl 30

claims.text: A solo archer can add INT with AP every level and MP wash it back with AP Resets, topping out at around 200 base INT, to get the MP pool for later; the author did this up to level 135 and says to start early.
claims.say: solo archer can mp wash with base int and ap resets, start early

claims.text: Movement speed matters a lot for farming; scrolled shoes, a bathrobe and a scrolled pet equip all add speed, so assemble speed gear before long grinding sessions.
claims.say: get speed gear like shoes and bathrobe before long farming

claims.text: To price items, look at what similar ones actually sold for rather than what is currently listed, and watch the Free Market regularly: a bargain item bought below market is an easy early profit.
claims.say: check what stuff actually sold for, not listing prices

claims.text: If your build depends on gear before you level, keep a few completed quests in reserve and turn them in for exp when you are ready to level, instead of levelling before the gear is in place.
claims.say: keep finished quests handy so you only level when your gear is ready

claims.text: Only extra MP can be washed into HP: that is your current max MP minus the minimum max MP your job has at your level. Anything above that floor can be turned into HP with AP resets.
claims.say: only mp above your minimum for the level can be washed

claims.text: For a thief or archer the minimum max MP is 14 x level + 148; anything above that is washable extra MP.
claims.say: thief and archer min mp is 14 x level + 148

claims.text: For a pirate the minimum max MP is 18 x level + 111; anything above that is washable extra MP.
claims.say: pirate min mp is 18 x level + 111

claims.text: For a Spearman the minimum max MP is 4 x level + 156; anything above that is washable extra MP.
claims.say: spearman min mp is 4 x level + 156

claims.text: For a Fighter or Page the minimum max MP is 4 x level + 56; anything above that is washable extra MP.
claims.say: fighter and page min mp is 4 x level + 56

claims.text: With more than 12 extra MP, one AP reset moving a point from MP to HP costs a thief or archer 12 MP and gives 16 HP. A pirate gains 18 HP for each reset but loses 16 MP.
claims.say: reset mp into hp: thief/archer -12 mp +16 hp, pirate -16 +18

claims.text: Before AP resets will touch HP and MP, you need one AP point sitting in HP or MP. After you finish washing, use a reset to move that point back into your main stat.
claims.say: put one ap in hp or mp first, then reset it to main stat at the end

claims.text: A second way to wash: put your level-up AP straight into HP, then at the end use resets to take MP down into your main stat so your attack stat does not suffer. This is not limited by reset count the same way.
claims.say: you can also put level up ap in hp then reset mp into main stat

claims.text: Warriors gain 50 to 58 HP per AP put directly into HP because of Improved MaxHP Increase, and resetting MP into STR only costs 4 MP, so warriors need much less extra MP than other jobs.
claims.say: warriors get 50-58 hp per ap into hp, so they wash easiest

claims.text: Each level you normally gain 3 to 5 extra MP plus your INT divided by 10, which is why base INT matters for washing.
claims.say: each level gives 3-5 mp plus int/10

claims.text: MP washing: add fresh AP into MP, then reset it out to your main stat. You net the MP gained (4 to 8 plus INT/10) minus the MP the reset removes (12 for thief and archer, 4 for warrior, 16 for pirate).
claims.say: mp wash: ap into mp then reset out, net mp depends on int

claims.text: MP washing nets other jobs roughly base INT/10 (rounded down) minus 1 MP per wash, but pirates only net base INT/10 minus 5. With 100 base INT that is 9 versus 5.
claims.say: pirates net way less per mp wash, 5 vs 9 at 100 int

claims.text: MP washing eats many AP resets, so work out how much MP your target HP needs, do only that much MP washing, then switch to HP washing. Gear price, INT gear and reset price all change the cheapest plan.
claims.say: figure out your goal hp first so you dont waste resets

claims.text: You can mix both wash methods when you have plenty of extra MP. Level-up AP into HP gives a larger random gain, but it uses AP that MP washing would need, so mixing can also save resets.
claims.say: if you have lots of extra mp you can mix both wash methods

claims.text: Which method is best differs by job: resetting MP into HP suits thieves, level-up AP into HP suits warriors, magicians and pirates, and archers get the same range either way. One poster says the first author had this partly backward.
claims.say: reset method for thieves, level up ap in hp for war/mage/pirate

claims.text: Weapon speed runs from 2 (fastest) to 9 (slowest) and sets how often you attack; it often decides whether a weapon is truly endgame or just for show.
claims.say: weapon speed matters, lower number means faster attacks

claims.text: The Sky Ski is a level 85, speed 6 spear that only comes from the Showa Gachapon, which keeps clean ones expensive.
claims.say: sky ski only comes from showa gach, pricey clean

claims.text: Poorly scrolled Sky Skis sell cheap, so pick one up as your long-term spear and improve it later when you can afford to.
claims.say: grab a cheap badly scrolled ski and upgrade later

claims.text: The Fishing Pole, a level 45 speed 5 spear from the Showa Gachapon, beats every other spear for single-target damage whenever you play without Speed Infusion.
claims.say: no speed infusion? fishing pole beats other spears 1v1

claims.text: Dragon Carabella is the best one-handed sword (level 110, speed 5); get it from Horntail, the Perion Gachapon or Leafre crafting.
claims.say: dragon carabella is the best 1h sword, horntail or leafre

claims.text: A perfect Stonetooth Sword only out-damages a Dragon Carabella when paired with an attack potion stronger than a Heartstopper; otherwise the Carabella's one-handed damage range wins and you save on potions.
claims.say: carabella beats stonetooth unless you pop big att pots

claims.text: The Stonetooth Sword is a level 100 two-handed sword with speed 5, rare for its type; it drops from Black Crow and comes from the New Leaf City Gachapon.
claims.say: stonetooth is a fast 2h sword, black crow or nlc gach

claims.text: The Stonetooth Sword needs 120 DEX, which is hard to reach, but it still beats many swords with modest base DEX; DEX scrolls on helmet and bottom plus DEX gear cover the gap.
claims.say: stonetooth needs 120 dex, use dex scrolls on helm and pants

claims.text: The New Leaf City Gachapon is a popular place to spend tickets because it can give both Stonetooth Swords and White Scrolls.
claims.say: nlc gach is popular for stonetooths and white scrolls

claims.text: A well scrolled White Nisrock works either as a final bow or as a stepping stone before a perfect Dragon Shiner Bow.
claims.say: a good nisrock is fine as an endgame bow

claims.text: Dragon Shiner Bow (level 110) is the best bow; few people spend tickets at the Henesys Gachapon, so most players craft it in Leafre, and Horntail drops it too.
claims.say: dragon shiner bow is the best bow, most craft it in leafre

claims.text: The author thinks moving from a good Nisrock to a Dragon Shiner Bow is rarely worth it: crafting costs Power Crystals and the few extra attack points cost about as much as extra white scrolled slots.
claims.say: upgrading a nisrock to a shiner bow is rarely worth it

claims.text: Dragon Kanzir (level 110, speed 4) is the usual endgame dagger thanks to higher base attack than the Dragon Khanjar; get it from Horntail, the Kerning Gachapon or Leafre.
claims.say: dragon kanzir is the endgame dagger

claims.text: Dragonfire Revolver (level 110, speed 5) is the endgame gun, from Horntail, the Nautilus Harbor Gachapon or Leafre; most people craft it rather than gamble tickets.
claims.say: dragonfire revolver is the endgame gun, craft it in leafre

claims.text: The Nautilus Harbor Gachapon can also give Black Versal Materia.
claims.say: nautilus gach can give black versal materia

claims.text: King Cent (level 100 knuckle, speed 5) is easy to find because Skelosaurus drops it; Griffey, Manon, Leviathan, Zakum, Dark Wyvern and Horntail drop it as well.
claims.say: king cents drop from skelosaurus

claims.text: Dragon Slash Claw (level 110, speed 5) is the best knuckle; it comes from Horntail, the Nautilus Gachapon or Leafre, and is easy to craft since King Cents are plentiful.
claims.say: dragon slash claw is the best knuckle, easy to craft

claims.text: Endgame mages use Elemental Wand 5 (New Leaf City Gachapon) or Elemental Wand 7 (CBD Gachapon), level 130 and speed 7; Bishops prefer Wand 5 since its INT adds magic attack, while Wand 7 gives LUK.
claims.say: bishops want ele wand 5, the int helps magic att

claims.text: Pole arms like the Purple Surfboard are mobbing weapons; since Dark Knights mostly boss or hunt Bigfoot against one or two targets, a spear is the better endgame investment.
claims.say: dks should perfect a spear, pole arms are for mobbing

claims.text: The Crushed Skull is left off endgame lists because its speed is only normal and well scrolled ones are rare.
claims.say: crushed skull is too slow for endgame

claims.text: Around level 8 to 10 (8 for mages), run your job instructor's quest line to the end; it should bring you to about level 13.
claims.say: after 1st job finish your job quest line, gets you to ~13

claims.text: From 21 to 25, run the Kerning City Party Quest.
claims.say: kpq from 21 to 25

claims.text: Monster Carnival is the main way to level from about 30 (if experienced friends carry you) or 35 up to 50.
claims.say: cpq from 30-35 all the way to 50

claims.text: In Monster Carnival the usual summon to spend your points on is Rombots.
claims.say: in cpq just summon rombots

claims.text: Turn off pet auto-loot in Monster Carnival; grabbing the wrong items can stun your side and annoys your team.
claims.say: turn off pet loot in cpq, the stun items hurt everyone

claims.text: From 50 to 70, keep leveling in the second Monster Carnival.
claims.say: 50-70 just do cpq2

claims.text: From 70 to 75, grind at Mysterious Path 3.
claims.say: 70-75 grind mysterious path 3

claims.text: By around level 90, look into HP washing; the extra HP makes bossing much easier.
claims.say: look into hp washing, it makes bossing a lot easier

claims.text: Telecasting means starting Genesis and then teleporting during the cast, which lets a Bishop hit mobs across a wide map; it only pays off if timed to the spawn waves, not spammed everywhere.
claims.say: telecast genesis but time it to the spawns, dont just spam

claims.text: End each cycle with a stationary Genesis, not a telecast, because a new wave is about to spawn where you are and you do not want to teleport away from it.
claims.say: finish each cycle with a standing genesis, new mobs spawn there

claims.text: Telecasting matters most for the longest cycle; the shorter cycles can still be finished in time even if a telecast fails, so imperfect teleporting still works there.
claims.say: the long cycle needs good telecast, short ones are forgiving

claims.text: Both washing methods cost one AP Reset per point, so it is better to put fresh AP into HP (banking unspent AP if needed) and later move MP into LUK than to swap MP straight into HP.
claims.say: save fresh ap for hp, then apr mp into luk

claims.text: Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest needs at least five players with one explorer from each branch (warrior, magician, archer, thief, pirate), all level 90 or above, each holding a Crimsonwood Keystone.
claims.say: cwkpq needs 5 ppl one of each class, lvl 90+ and the keystone

claims.text: Each player should bring All Cure Potions and attack potions, and have roughly 3,500 max HP if ranged or 7,000 if melee before going in.
claims.say: bring all cures and atk pots, around 3.5k hp ranged or 7k melee

claims.text: Bring someone with a rush-type skill (Rush, Corkscrew Blow or Backspin Blow) to herd the bottom-floor bosses together toward the left side.
claims.say: bring someone with rush or corkscrew or backspin to herd bosses

claims.text: Someone, normally a thief, needs max Haste for the party; it speeds up the jump stages and the bonus stage a lot.
claims.say: need a thief with max haste for the jump stages and bonus

claims.text: Every entry into Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest costs 12 Crimson Hearts, dropped by Crimson Guardians at the gate to Crimsonwood Keep and inside it.
claims.say: each cwkpq run costs 12 crimson hearts from crimson guardians

claims.text: Crimson Guardians spam Seal and resist fire, poison, lightning and ice, and they are immune to Holy so Genesis does nothing to them; carry All Cure Potions when farming them.
claims.say: guardians seal u and resist most elements, bring all cure pots

claims.text: A Bishop can cast Doom on Crimson Guardians to turn them into Blue Snails, which strips their resistances while their HP stays high; each Doom costs one Magic Rock.
claims.say: bishops can doom crimson guardians, costs a magic rock each

claims.text: Subani's Legacy - Transgression and Deliverance: take the rightmost portal twice from New Leaf City, use the teleportals up, kill Electrophants (immune to ice) for 50 Hyper Glyphs and I.AM.ROBOTs for 50 MesoGear Map Pieces.
claims.say: electrophants give hyper glyphs, i.am.robots give mesogear pieces

claims.text: Finding Jack: to reach Jack at Crimsonwood Mountain, walk from Phantom Forest, get a Mystic Door, or use a Teleport Rock to someone at the Windraider or Stormbreaker training spots.
claims.say: to reach jack use a door or tele rock to someone near windraiders

claims.text: Stemming the Tide only has to be started with Jack to unlock Storming the Castle; once Lukan hands over the Crimsonwood Keystone you never need to turn Stemming the Tide in.
claims.say: just start stemming the tide, no need to finish it for the keystone

claims.text: Storming the Castle: in the Hall of Mastery next to the party quest, kill 75 each of Nightshadows (top left room), Firebrands (middle left) and Windraiders (bottom left), then return to Lukan for the Keystone.
claims.say: storming the castle: 75 each of nightshadow, firebrand, windraider

claims.text: You can reach the party quest by walking, a Mystic Door, or a Teleport Rock to someone at the nearby Windraider or Stormbreaker training spots; the lobby entrance is the electrified door at the top right.
claims.say: get to cwkpq with a door or tele rock to someone near windraiders

claims.text: In Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest each class sigil only lights from a matching class skill; warriors can use Charged Blow, Shout or the Dragon Knight's Dragon Fury.
claims.say: warrior sigil needs charged blow, shout or dragon fury

claims.text: Magician sigils in Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest respond to Magic Claw, Fire/Poison's Explosion, Ice/Lightning's Ice Strike or the Bishop's Bahamut.
claims.say: mage sigil: magic claw, explosion, ice strike or bahamut

claims.text: Archer sigils in Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest respond to Strafe, Piercing Arrow, or the summoned bird of a Ranger or Sniper.
claims.say: archer sigil: strafe, piercing arrow or your summon bird

claims.text: Thief sigils in Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest respond to Avenger, Shadow Partner, Chakra, Meso Explosion or Band of Thieves.
claims.say: thief sigil: avenger, shadow partner, chakra, meso explosion, bot

claims.text: Pirate sigils in Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest respond to Flash Fist, Transformation, Dragon Strike, Gaviota or Rapid Fire.
claims.say: pirate sigil: flash fist, transformation, dragon strike, gaviota, rf

claims.text: Stage 1 (Inner Sanctum Hallway) has a hidden portal at the next dark pillar after the hanging bags; the leader must talk to Jack first or the portal will not work.
claims.say: stage 1 hidden portal is at the dark pillar after the hanging bags

claims.text: Stage 2 (Forgotten Storage Chamber): light the five sigils with matching class skills, then take the portal that opens between the Thief and Pirate sigils.
claims.say: stage 2: light 5 sigils, portal opens between thief and pirate ones

claims.text: Stage 3, The Test of Agility, spreads the sigils over an easy jump quest; pillars start moving when you light the nearest sigil and hit for just under max HP, so keep full HP. Five players must pass the top portal.
claims.say: stage 3 pillars hit near max hp so stay full, 5 must reach the top

claims.text: In stage 3 thieves should Haste the party; if you die, do not press OK, you respawn once the fifth player clears the top portal; Night Lords can Flash Jump through the wall near the thief sigil.
claims.say: if u die in stage 3 dont click ok, u respawn when 5th goes up

claims.text: Stage 4, The Test of Wit, hides nine sigils on a jump quest, with fakes for every class except pirate; keep searching until chat says your class sigil is activated, and split up with your class partner.
claims.say: stage 4 has fake sigils, keep looking til chat says yours is on

claims.text: In stage 4 the fires switch on and off depending on who stands on the platforms along the bottom, and the Stirges are turned off by hitting two special sigils; Buccaneers can Corkscrew Blow Stirges to move.
claims.say: stage 4 fires follow the bottom platforms, 2 sigils stop stirges

claims.text: Stage 5 gives each class its own room for a relic weapon (an Etc item, so keep slots free); drop it on the main room statue: staff top left, bow bottom right, sword middle hand, gun at the belt, claw top right.
claims.say: stage 5 each class gets a relic weapon, keep etc slots free

claims.text: Stage 5 rooms: the magician teleports left through map one and right through map two to the statue for the Staff of First Magic; the archer talks to the statue to spawn 7 Master Guardians, kills them, then gets the Ancestral Bow.
claims.say: mage teles left then right for staff, archer kills 7 guardians

claims.text: Stage 5 rooms: the warrior fights to the top for the Master Sword, the pirate opens chests with basic attacks until the Forbidden Gun drops, and the thief taps purple eyeballs up the room (some need Flash Jump) for the Primal Claw.
claims.say: warrior climbs for sword, pirate opens chests, thief taps eyes

claims.text: Stage 6, Grandmaster Council Hall: talk to the Battle Statue to summon mobs, then again for the five bosses; the simple plan is rushing the bottom bosses left and pinning the top ones, melee on the bottom, ranged on top.
claims.say: stage 6 melee takes the bottom bosses, ranged take the top ones

claims.text: Margana (top platform) zombifies, poisons and heals, and her pillar blocks projectiles; she is weak to Holy so a strong Paladin kills her fast, and Bishops must not heal while she lives or zombified allies die.
claims.say: margana is weak to holy, bishops dont heal while shes alive

claims.text: Council Hall weaknesses: Hsalf (bottom floor) is weak to ice, immune to Holy and hard to hit without accuracy; Rellik is weak to fire; Red Nirg is weak to lightning.
claims.say: hsalf weak to ice, rellik to fire, red nirg to lightning

claims.text: Rellik can 1/1, stun, poison and seal and knocks back, so stand on top of the pinned bosses to dodge the stun; Red Nirg buffs to hit very hard, knocks back and summons Crimsonwood mobs partway.
claims.say: rellik stuns and seals, red nirg buffs up and hits hard

claims.text: Before the Crimsonwood Armory bonus stage, agree which chests each person takes, give the closest ones to the least mobile classes, have a thief Haste everyone, and call the countdown so all enter the portal together.
claims.say: in the bonus stage split the chests, give slow classes the close ones

claims.text: The bonus stage pays well, especially when it gives a strong pair of Spectrum Goggles or a Blackfist Cloak.
claims.say: cwkpq bonus can drop spectrum goggles and blackfist cloak

claims.text: Phantom Forest mixes two-way portals with one-way portals that send you somewhere new if you go back through them, so taking portals at random can leave you going in circles.
claims.say: phantom forest has one way portals, random ones will loop you

claims.text: Dead Man's Gorge is the hub of Phantom Forest: its left and right portals lead into two separate groups of Twisted Paths maps, and only a few portals cross between the two halves.
claims.say: dead mans gorge is the middle, twisted paths split left and right

claims.text: The Crimsonwood Keep jump quest starts at the top of Forgotten Path: from Dead Man's Gorge go right to the far-right Twisted Paths, head left past one portal and take the next, then climb to the top-left portal.
claims.say: cwk jq starts at the top left of forgotten path

claims.text: After channel-hopping for Bigfoot, keep moving through the forest portals rather than using a town scroll; walking back from Haunted House up the Bent Tree to Dead Man's Gorge costs a lot of time.
claims.say: dont town scroll after bf hunting, just walk through the portals

claims.text: Around levels 10 to 15, Slimes in the forest south of Ellinia are a steady early training choice.
claims.say: 10-15 slimes in the forest south of ellinia are solid

claims.text: From levels 15 to 30, Wild Boars in the Land of the Wild Boar maps are a reliable place to train.
claims.say: 15-30 wild boars at land of the wild boar are decent

claims.text: Green Mushrooms and Horny Mushrooms in the forest south of Ellinia (the fourth dungeon map) work for levels 15 to 30.
claims.say: green and horny mushrooms south of ellinia work for 15-30

claims.text: Evil Eyes in The Cave of Evil Eye I give decent exp for levels 15 to 30.
claims.say: evil eyes in the cave of evil eye i are fine for 15-30

claims.text: Axe Stumps and Dark Axe Stumps in East Rocky Mountain V are a decent grinding spot for levels 15 to 30.
claims.say: axe stumps at east rocky mountain v are ok for 15-30

claims.text: The Kerning City Party Quest opens at level 21 and is worth running while levelling through the 20s.
claims.say: kpq opens at lvl 21, worth running while leveling 21-30

claims.text: The first Monster Carnival suits levels 30 to 51 and the second suits levels 51 to 71; it can be entered from Orbis, Kerning City or Ludibrium and usually beats grinding for most classes in this range.
claims.say: monster carnival is good exp for 30-70 over plain grinding

claims.text: The Ludibrium Party Quest opens at level 35 and stays worth doing at any level above that.
claims.say: lpq opens at 35 and stays worth doing

claims.text: The Orbis Party Quest opens at level 51 and stays worthwhile at higher levels; remember to feed Wonky during it for easy bonus exp.
claims.say: opq from 51, dont forget to feed wonky for bonus exp

claims.text: Zombie Lupins in Monkey Swamp III give solid exp for levels 30 to 51, and one reply says they are especially good for Hunters in their early 30s.
claims.say: zombie lupins in monkey swamp iii are great, esp for hunters

claims.text: Paper Lantern Ghosts in A Night in the Forest are a good grinding choice for levels 30 to 51.
claims.say: paper lantern ghosts at a night in the forest are good for 30-51

claims.text: Coolie Zombies in the Forest of Dead Trees maps give some of the best exp in the 30 to 51 range.
claims.say: coolie zombies in forest of dead trees are top exp for 30-51

claims.text: Windraiders at Tornado Corridor give far more exp than other spots in the 51 to 71 range, making them a standout choice for the level 58 and up crowd.
claims.say: windraiders at tornado corridor give crazy exp for the level

claims.text: Mysterious Path 3 (Slimy and Selkie Jr.) is a strong spot for levels 51 to 80, and Ice and Lightning wizards with good INT gear, or warriors with enough accuracy and attack, can start there as early as levels 30 to 35.
claims.say: mysterious path 3 is great, il mages and warriors can start ~35

claims.text: Captains and Krus at Red Nose Pirate Den 2 are usable from levels 51 to 80, though exp there is only average.
claims.say: captains and krus at red nose pirate den 2, only average exp

claims.text: Levels 71 to 80 are a slow stretch, so lean on party quests: the Pirate Party Quest (levels 70 to 101), the Romeo and Juliet Party Quest (71 and up) and the Orbis Party Quest.
claims.say: 71-80 is slow, run ppq, rjpq and opq

claims.text: Homunculi in Lab - Unit 202 give good exp for levels 71 to 80.
claims.say: homunculus in lab unit 202 is good for 71-80

claims.text: Black Kentauruses in The Area of Black Kentaurus pay well for levels 71 to 80.
claims.say: black kentaurus area pays well for 71-80

claims.text: Wolf Spiders in Wolf Spider Cavern are a high-exp option for levels 71 to 80, but a party is recommended there.
claims.say: wolf spider cavern is good exp but bring a party

claims.text: Jr. Newties in the Destroyed Dragon Nest give very high exp for levels 80 to 100.
claims.say: jr newties at destroyed dragon nest give huge exp for 80-100

claims.text: The three Kentaurus battlefields (Fire and Darkness, Water and Darkness, Fire and Water) are strong party grinding spots for levels 80 to 100.
claims.say: kentaurus battlefields are good party exp for 80-100

claims.text: Risell Squids in Dangerous Sea Gorge II give strong exp for levels 80 to 100.
claims.say: risell squids in dangerous sea gorge ii are solid for 80-100

claims.text: Temple of Time quests unlock from level 90 and the Temple of Time maps are good for grinding, giving steady exp from level 90 upward; more of its quests open again at 100 and 120.
claims.say: temple of time quests and maps are great exp from 90 on

claims.text: The Ellin Forest Party Quest opens at level 110, with its pre-quests available from level 100.
claims.say: epq opens at 110, do the pre-quests from 100

claims.text: As a rough order for bossing, Pianus and Papulatus fit around levels 120 to 135, Zakum comes around 135 to 155, and Horntail is a 155 and up target; do each boss's pre-quests first.
claims.say: boss order: pianus and papulatus, then zakum, then horntail

claims.text: Warriors should keep their DEX at 40 base and use accuracy potions while leveling, then reset the DEX points once gear such as DEX equipment, a Zakum Helmet and Maple weapons covers the accuracy.
claims.say: warriors keep 40 base dex + acc pots, reset dex once gear covers it

claims.text: Training in a party gives bonus exp for each active member who is killing, so a full party earns noticeably more per kill, and grinding with friends matters even more at higher levels.
claims.say: grind in a full party, bonus exp for every active member

claims.text: HP washing raises max HP: put AP or gear into Intelligence so each level up gives extra MP, then use an AP reset to move that spare MP into HP. It is expensive and nearly always has to be started from the very beginning of a character.
claims.say: hp washing = stack int for mp then ap reset the mp into hp

claims.text: Bosses like Zakum and Horntail can hit for more than the unwashed base HP of some classes, even a level 200 bowman, which is why people who boss wash their HP.
claims.say: boss hits can top a bowman's base hp so hp wash for bossing

claims.text: Mason the Collector is a one-time quest from level 60 with a chance at an Omok game item that sells for a high price.
claims.say: mason the collector at 60 can give a valuable omok item

claims.text: Protect Ludibrium is repeatable from level 80; the clown NPC at the end gives a Piece of Cracked Dimension, which summons Papulatus but can also simply be sold to bossers instead of being used.
claims.say: protect ludibrium at 80 gives a cracked dimension piece to sell

claims.text: Amoria Party Quest from level 40 needs you to be married; the bonus round can drop Onyx Apples, one of the best attack buffs for bossing, so repeated runs can make good mesos.
claims.say: apq bonus can drop onyx apples, a great boss buff to sell

claims.text: Leeching is the most lucrative meso earner: a mage with a fourth-job area spell clears maps faster than any other class while the party shares exp, which beats hunting by hand, especially from around level 80 upward.
claims.say: mages can sell leech, they clear maps fastest and party shares exp

claims.text: The author suggests a mage as a first character, since you can sell leech to build up funds while still working out your long-term goals.
claims.say: a mage is a good first char since you can sell leech for mesos

claims.text: For raw Paladin damage the ranking is two-handed sword first, then one-handed sword, then one-handed blunt weapon, with the two-handed blunt weapon last.
claims.say: pally dps order: 2h sword, 1h sword, 1h bw, 2h bw

claims.text: A one-handed Paladin with a shield gets Guardian, which blocks a share of incoming hits, so it takes less damage and spends fewer potions.
claims.say: 1h pally with a shield has guardian to block hits and save pots

claims.text: Each knockback at Zakum or Horntail costs attack time. Power Stance lowers the chance of being knocked back and Guardian's blocks lower it further for a one-hander, which is the case for a 1H plus shield Paladin.
claims.say: fewer knockbacks at zak and ht means more hits, 1h shield pally helps

claims.text: At Zakum a two-handed sword is the best Paladin weapon for damage.
claims.say: 2h sword is the best pally weapon at zakum

claims.text: At Horntail a one-handed weapon works best for a Paladin, partly because it is steadier when knocked around.
claims.say: 1h weapon is best for a pally at horntail

claims.text: As the only warrior on Zakum, a Paladin stands on the lowest left platform near the arms (there is a small drop to get closer) and hits 5 to 8 arms with Heaven's Hammer. Ice charge reaches the ice-weak middle and bottom arms.
claims.say: as lone warrior stand on the low left platform near the arms

claims.text: A low-DEX Paladin (around 23 DEX) is the suggested build: with a little DEX gear it still hits most monsters in Monster Carnival and levels far more smoothly than a dexless one.
claims.say: low dex around 23 is a good paladin build, dexless sucks

claims.text: A first-time Paladin can add roughly one DEX per two levels and reach about 22 DEX by level 20; extra DEX can be taken back out later with AP resets.
claims.say: put 1 dex per 2 levels early, you can reset it later

claims.text: As a Swordsman, max Improving Max HP Increase first, then take Power Strike and Slash Blast, and park spare points in Endure or Improving HP Recovery.
claims.say: swordsman: max hp increase first, then power strike + slash blast

claims.text: As a Page, get your weapon's Mastery, Booster and Power Guard; that is all you need for third job. Threaten does not work on most endgame content, so leave it at a low level.
claims.say: page needs mastery, booster and power guard, threaten is meh

claims.text: White Knights should have Fire Charge, Ice Charge and Lightning Charge all maxed for their weapon by about level 99, maxing first the element that fits where you currently grind.
claims.say: get all three charges maxed by 99, start with your mob's weakness

claims.text: Lightning Charge first is a good start because Goby gives some of the best exp around level 75; a Paladin who prefers grinding in Ludibrium should max Fire Charge first instead.
claims.say: lightning charge first for gobies, fire first if you do ludi

claims.text: Elemental Charge skills still add extra damage on monsters with no weakness, as long as the monster does not resist that element.
claims.say: charges still add dmg on neutral mobs unless they resist

claims.text: Keep MP Recovery up for Horntail: enough MP regen lets you cast Hero's Will after a mana burn while seduced, which can save the Paladin.
claims.say: mp recovery helps you hero's will after hts mana burn

claims.text: At level 120 every Paladin should first put one point each into Advanced Charge, Heaven's Hammer and Rush before spending anything else.
claims.say: first 3 sp at 120: advanced charge, heaven's hammer, rush

claims.text: A Paladin who plans to solo grind for a while can take Maple Warrior to level 10 before Blast.
claims.say: if soloing a lot, get maple warrior before blast

claims.text: Blast locks onto whichever monster or boss you hit first and keeps priority on it even when others bunch up; Advanced Charge and Heaven's Hammer do not break that lock.
claims.say: blast locks onto the first thing you hit, hammer/acb keep it

claims.text: Warriors should save up for a Zakum Helmet by around level 50.
claims.say: save up for a zakum helmet by level 50

claims.text: Paladins do not need HP washing, and it is cheap if wanted later: a Zakum Helmet plus a few INT sources lets a warrior wash fairly high HP at low cost.
claims.say: paladins dont need hp washing but its cheap with a zhelm

claims.text: If you keep missing while leveling, scroll your gear for accuracy and carry accuracy potions; it makes grinding much smoother.
claims.say: if you keep missing, scroll accuracy on your gear and pot up

claims.text: Around levels 75 to 94, grind Goby; the author considers it the best mob for that range.
claims.say: gobies are great exp at 75 to 90

claims.text: Papulatus is a good exp boss for Paladins from level 120.
claims.say: papulatus is decent exp from 120 up

claims.text: Once you have Blast, Bigfoot is the best solo exp for a Paladin, if you can find one up.
claims.say: once you have blast bigfoot is great solo exp

claims.text: In the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest boss stage, the Mage boss is the best spot for a Paladin: Holy Charge plus Blast can handle it solo while the ranged attackers focus the Pirate boss.
claims.say: in cwkpq take the mage boss with holy charge blast

claims.text: The three melee bosses in the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest are weak to different elements (Fire for the Archer, Lightning for the Warrior, Ice for the Thief), so Blast them down in that order using its lock-on.
claims.say: cwkpq melee bosses: archer fire, warrior lightning, thief ice

claims.text: Paladins are weaker than Heroes and Dark Knights on Zakum's arms because Advanced Charge may only hit one arm, but they pull ahead on the body with single-target damage and spawn clearing.
claims.say: pally is meh on zak arms but great on the body

claims.text: Zakum's arms are weak to different elements: use Ice Advanced Charge to hit several arms at once, then Holy Blast the top-left arm and Lightning Blast the curse arm.
claims.say: zakum arms: ice acb first, then holy blast, then lightning blast

claims.text: Scarlion and Targa have opposite element weaknesses (one Fire, one Ice), so fighting both at once ruins Paladin damage; kill them one at a time if the party can.
claims.say: scarlion and targa have opposite weaknesses, kill one at a time

claims.text: In Horntail, use Advanced Charge when a wing rises to hit Head A, Head B and the wing together, since Blast would lock onto the wing and lose damage; use Heaven's Hammer when Head A ducks.
claims.say: ht: acb when the wing goes up, hammer when head a ducks

claims.text: When a Hero or Dark Knight joins the Horntail run, they take priority on AoE damage, so the Paladin should use Blast only.
claims.say: if a hero or dk is in the ht run, just use blast

claims.text: A Paladin does not need huge HP to take the seduce role in Horntail: the Bishop keeps you alive, and your job is to warn the Bishop when seduce is about to come and stand in the right spot.
claims.say: as the sed paladin, warn the bishop and stand in the right spot

claims.text: Papulatus's fat body is weak to Lightning and its skinny body is weak to Holy.
claims.say: papulatus fat body is weak to lightning, skinny to holy

claims.text: A one-hand blunt weapon plus shield is the cheapest Paladin weapon route because Crushed Skull from Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest is cheap and BW scrolls are cheap; two-handed blunt weapons are badly underpowered.
claims.say: bw + shield is the cheapest paladin setup, 2h bw is bad

claims.text: If you also plan to make a Hero, go with a sword for your Paladin, since one weapon can then serve both characters.
claims.say: planning a hero too? use a sword so one weapon fits both

claims.text: The next quest, Making the Path to the Sea, asks for 120 Slimy and 120 Selkie Jr. kills.
claims.say: next: 120 slimy and 120 selkie jr

claims.text: Then The Great Secret Reveals asks for 300 Mr. Anchor kills and rewards a White Essence, so keep an etc slot free.
claims.say: 300 mr anchors gets you the white essence, keep etc space

claims.text: Horntail's hand skills fire as long as even one party member stands on that hand's side, so keep everyone on their assigned side; one player or mule crossing over doubles the seduce timers.
claims.say: stay on your side at ht arms, one stray guy doubles the seduces

claims.text: Horntail's Right Hand curses the party with Seal, Darkness and Weakness and raises its own magic defense; these are the debuffs a Bishop clears with Dispel.
claims.say: right arm seals, darkens and weakens you, bish has to dispel

claims.text: Horntail's Tail casts a Poison Mist that hurts anyone standing in it over time.
claims.say: dont stand in the tail's poison mist

claims.text: A 4th job skill book opens the first levels of a skill, and mastery books lift the cap to 20 or 30. Skill books can't be traded, mastery books can.
claims.say: skill book unlocks it, mastery books raise the cap

claims.text: Everyone gets a Maple Warrior skill book on reaching 4th job, and the level 20 mastery book for it drops from Horntail.
claims.say: maple warrior 20 book drops off horntail

claims.text: Hero's Will needs a quest: Chief Tatama sends you to Carta the Sea Witch in a hidden Deep Sea Gorge map, and you give her a Miniature Pianus to enter a special map and gather spirit rocks.
claims.say: hero's will: tatama sends you to carta in deep sea gorge

claims.text: Big Bang is a default 4th job mage skill. Level 20 books drop from Pianus and Dark Wyvern, and Dark Wyverns have a map to themselves, so farming one is easy.
claims.say: big bang 20 book drops from pianus and dark wyverns

claims.text: Papulatus drops the Infinity level 20 mastery book and Zakum drops the level 30 one.
claims.say: infinity 20 is a papulatus drop, 30 is zakum

claims.text: Mana Reflection is a default 4th job mage skill with easy books: Pianus, Dark Cornian and Elderwraith drop level 20, Pianus and Dodo drop level 30.
claims.say: mana reflection books drop all over, pianus and dodo for 30

claims.text: Genesis starts with an errand loop: your 3rd job instructor sends you to an NPC in the Ludibrium library, then to Grendel in Ellinia, then Shammos in El Nath, and you shuttle between them before the real task.
claims.say: genesis starts with grendel in ellinia then shammos in el nath

claims.text: Shammos asks for a Life's Root, which Skelegons drop in Life's Cavern. You can only get there by clearing the Horntail prequests, and you can leave as soon as the root drops.
claims.say: shammos wants a life's root, skelegons drop it in life's cavern

claims.text: Moira's Horntail prequest wants a Cornian's Marrow from a Green Cornian, a Skull Shoulder Pad from a Dark Cornian, 10 Red Dragon Skins from Red Wyverns, a repaired Cornian's Dagger, and Manon killed.
claims.say: moira wants cornian parts, wyvern skins and manon dead

claims.text: Mos repairs the busted dagger that Dark Cornians drop if you bring him a Steel Plate and a Mithril Plate.
claims.say: mos fixes the busted cornian dagger for steel and mithril plate

claims.text: Genesis mastery books are among the priciest items in the game: Zakum drops level 20 and Horntail drops level 30.
claims.say: genesis books are zakum 20, horntail 30, super expensive

claims.text: Angel Ray's skill book drops from Zakum. Level 20 mastery books are common from Skelegons and several monk monsters, and level 30 comes from Papulatus.
claims.say: angel ray book is from zakum, level 30 mastery from papulatus

claims.text: Bahamut has no mastery books. Raul the Knight in Leafre repeats a quest for Dragon Hearts from Red, Blue or Dark Wyverns, and each turn-in raises the skill cap by 5 levels up to 30.
claims.say: bahamut levels come from raul's dragon heart quests in leafre

claims.text: Holy Shield is a default Bishop skill. Scarlion, Targa, Skelosaurus and Tree Rod drop the level 20 book and Manon drops the level 30 one.
claims.say: holy shield 30 book drops from manon

claims.text: For the Resurrection quest, Carta the Sea Witch wants 100 Ice Pieces from Grim Phantom Watches, 50 Firebomb Flames from Firebombs and 5 Undead Charms from Zombie Mushrooms, and rewards a Cold Flame.
claims.say: carta wants ice pieces, firebomb flames and undead charms

claims.text: Meteor Shower uses the same Robeira, Wiz, 1st job instructor and Shammos errand chain as Blizzard, but Shammos finally asks for an Eye of Fire, the item used to summon Zakum.
claims.say: meteor shower needs an eye of fire at the end

claims.text: Blizzard and Meteor Shower level 20 books drop from Zakum and level 30 books from Horntail; the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest also drops Blizzard 30.
claims.say: blizzard and meteor books: zakum for 20, horntail for 30

claims.text: Fire Demon follows a similar trail, starting with a Burning Fire Storybook from Red Kentaurus. Vogen wants a Star Rock, 2 Diamonds and 30 Firebomb Flames for a bottle, then Adobis by Zakum's entrance runs a lava jump quest.
claims.say: fire demon needs a burning fire storybook from red kentaurus

claims.text: Papulatus drops the level 30 books for both Ice Demon and Fire Demon.
claims.say: papulatus drops the ice demon and fire demon 30 books

claims.text: Elquines needs the Fire Demon skill first and follows the same trail as Ifrit, but Alcaster first wants 30 Ice Drake items, 30 Cold Shark items and 40 Grim Phantom Watch items.
claims.say: elquines needs fire demon first, same trail as ifrit

claims.text: Paralyze is a default Fire/Poison skill. Manon and Jr. Newtie drop level 20 books; level 30 comes from the Guild Party Quest, which needs a full group, so it is harder to get.
claims.say: paralyze 30 book comes from the guild party quest

claims.text: Dragon Strike is a default Buccaneer skill with easy books: Pianus and Spirit Vikings drop level 20, Manon, Scarlion, Targa and Squids drop level 30, and all have plenty of spawns.
claims.say: dragon strike books drop from pianus, manon and squids

claims.text: Barrage level 20 books drop from Dodo, Pianus and Blue Dragon Turtles, and the level 30 book comes from Papulatus.
claims.say: barrage 30 book is a papulatus drop

claims.text: After Super Transformation, Kyrin gives the Demolition quest: kill 150 Blue Dragon Turtles and bring back 50 Sturdy Leather. It is a core Buccaneer skill, so unlock it early.
claims.say: demolition: kyrin wants 150 blue dragon turtles

claims.text: Cold Sharks cast slow and Sharks can dispel, which can be deadly for a mage farming books like Demolition or Rapid Fire in those maps.
claims.say: careful, sharks dispel and cold sharks slow you

claims.text: Time Leap needs Rolonay on the Nautilus mid floor hallway: kill Papulatus for a silver key, return, enter the Papulatus portal again to a Papulatus NPC, pick the bottom option, then talk to Rolonay.
claims.say: time leap: rolonay wants a papulatus silver key first

claims.text: Rapid Fire is one of the core Corsair skills and should be maxed early. Manon and Dark Cornian drop the level 20 book, and Dark Cornians have a hidden map with hanging platforms.
claims.say: rapid fire is a core corsair skill, max it early

claims.text: Between about level 40 and 50, Monster Carnival is the fastest way for most classes to level up.
claims.say: cpq is the fastest exp from 40 to 50 for most classes

claims.text: At that range Ludibrium Party Quest is more of a fun option: parties are harder to put together and the exp is less steady than Monster Carnival.
claims.say: lpq is fun but parties are hard to find and exp is less steady

claims.text: Alishar, the monster at the end of Ludibrium Party Quest, drops the Key of Dimension.
claims.say: alishar drops the key of dimension in lpq

claims.text: In Ludibrium Party Quest the Pass of Dimension comes from the Another Dimension monsters, such as Black Ratz from Another Dimension and Bloctopus from Another Dimension.
claims.say: lpq passes drop from the another dimension ratz and bloctopus

claims.text: Black Crow can drop the Stonetooth Sword, a high-level two-handed sword.
claims.say: black crow drops the stonetooth sword

claims.text: Blue Dragon Turtle drops the level 20 mastery book for Barrage.
claims.say: barrage 20 book drops from blue dragon turtles

claims.text: Blue Wyvern drops the level 20 mastery book for Super Transformation.
claims.say: super transformation 20 book drops from blue wyverns

claims.text: Blood Harp drops Steely Throwing-Knives.
claims.say: blood harps drop steelies

claims.text: Blue King Goblin drops Hwabi Throwing-Stars.
claims.say: blue king goblins drop hwabis

claims.text: Black Porky drops Mokbi Throwing-Stars.
claims.say: black porkies drop mokbi stars

claims.text: Tobi Throwing-Stars drop from Bain and Big Cloud Fox.
claims.say: tobis drop from bains and big cloud foxes

claims.text: The Dark Knight skill Berserk is unlocked through a quest chain that opens with Wiz the Librarian, who sends you on to Chief Tatama.
claims.say: berserk quest starts at wiz the librarian, then chief tatama

claims.text: In the Berserk chain, Chief Tatama asks for Sayram's Necklace, which you obtain by hunting a Griffey.
claims.say: tatama wants sayram's necklace, hunt griffeys for it

claims.text: After the necklace, the Berserk chain sends you to The Insignificant Being in Sleepywood, who wants a key that Jr. Balrog drops.
claims.say: next the insignificant being in sleepywood wants a jr balrog key

claims.text: Once you hand over the key, head to Sanctuary Entrance IV and use the portal in the middle of the map to search for a special shield.
claims.say: use the middle portal in sanctuary entrance iv and find the shield

claims.text: Returning the shield to Wiz the Librarian completes the chain and unlocks Berserk.
claims.say: bring the shield to wiz the librarian and berserk unlocks

claims.text: When perfecting an item, scroll in this order: 30% scrolls first, then 30% scrolls with a White Scroll, and 10% scrolls with a White Scroll for the remaining slots.
claims.say: scroll 30% first, then 30% + ws, then 10% + ws for the rest

claims.text: A 10% scroll never destroys the equipment: it either lands or fails and costs the slot. That is why 10% scrolls are the safe choice on valuable gear when paired with a White Scroll.
claims.say: 10% scrolls never boom your gear, they just fail

claims.text: A 30% scroll lands 30% of the time, destroys the item about 35% of the time, and merely fails the remaining 35%, so the real cost includes the clean items you lose.
claims.say: 30% scrolls: 30 pass, 35 fail, 35 boom the item

claims.text: A 10% scroll needs about 10 tries on average to land, though half the time it lands within 7 tries. With White Scrolls that is about 10 scrolls and 10 White Scrolls per slot; budget by the average, not the median.
claims.say: a 10% scroll takes ~10 tries on average, median is 7

claims.text: Landing a 30% scroll costs about 3.3 scrolls and 3.3 clean items on average; with a White Scroll it is still about 3.3 scrolls and 3.3 White Scrolls but only about 2.2 items in total, since the White Scroll saves failed attempts.
claims.say: 30% + ws needs ~3.3 scrolls and ws and ~2.2 items per slot

claims.text: Value a partly scrolled item at the cheapest average way to make it, then reuse that figure when deciding the next slot's method; the cheapest method changes as the item gets worth more.
claims.say: price a +1 item at what it costs to make, then pick the next scroll

claims.text: From the third slot onward, always use 10% plus White Scroll. A lucky 30% can work, but over many tries the gambles lose money.
claims.say: third slot onward, just use 10% + ws

claims.text: A Beginner headed for magician can rely on Three Snails on Maple Island. Each skill level throws a different shell (Snail Shell, then Blue, then Red), so hold off raising it while you still carry the earlier shells.
claims.say: use three snails, but dont level it up while you have old shells

claims.text: Settle on your future class before spending any ability points, so your stats meet that job's advancement requirement.
claims.say: pick your class before spending ap so you meet the job reqs

claims.text: On Maple Island, Mai's training quests and Biggs's story quest are worth doing before you leave.
claims.say: do mai's training and biggs's quest before leaving maple island

claims.text: Leveling past the advancement level before taking your first job does not cost you any skill points.
claims.say: leveling past 10 before job adv doesnt lose you sp

claims.text: Around level 15, take on every quest available at Nautilus Harbor; together they are an easy source of early exp.
claims.say: at 15 grab all the nautilus quests, easy exp

claims.text: The quiz quest in New Leaf City rewards good exp for almost no effort and is worth a detour while leveling in the teens or twenties.
claims.say: the nlc quiz is free exp, worth the trip

claims.text: While training in Sleepywood, keep 100 Zombie Mushroom etc drops for the level 25 cape quest and 50 Evil Eye Tails for other quests instead of selling them.
claims.say: save 100 zombie mush etcs and 50 evil eye tails for quests

claims.text: Choose the class you will enjoy most and judge its 1st to 3rd job play too, since that is where most of your time goes, not just its 4th job.
claims.say: pick what you enjoy, you spend most time in 2nd and 3rd job

claims.text: Before committing to a class, check where its skill books come from; some drop only from hard bosses like Papulatus and can take a long time to obtain.
claims.say: check where your class's skill books drop before you pick it

claims.text: Ice/Lightning mages are among the steadiest grinders, with good area attacks from the middle of 2nd job all the way through 4th job.
