claims.say: i/l is a steady grinder, good aoe from mid 2nd job on

claims.text: Ice/Lightning 4th job play is mostly casting Blizzard over and over, which some players find less fun than the climb there.
claims.say: 4th job i/l is mostly spamming blizzard

claims.text: Buccaneers are all-rounders: fairly tanky, with area attacks in every job, a rushing skill from 2nd job, and very strong single-target damage in 4th job.
claims.say: bucc does it all, aoe every job and big 1v1 at 4th

claims.text: The climb to Buccaneer is slow: early area attacks are short on damage and range, and 4th job has many skills to max before it peaks.
claims.say: bucc early aoe is weak and 4th job has lots to max

claims.text: Marksmen are the best ranged grinders, helped by freezing attacks, but they are weak at bossing.
claims.say: marksman grinds great with freezes, bossing is meh

claims.text: A Marksman's biggest hurdle is maxing Snipe, because the level 30 mastery book comes from Horntail.
claims.say: snipe 30 book comes from horntail, hard to get

claims.text: Most players never HP wash; it only pays off for a concrete goal such as surviving a certain boss's hits, and it makes leveling much harder.
claims.say: no need to hp wash unless you have a set goal, it's a grind

claims.text: In an HP wash, base INT supplies most of the extra MP; INT gear mainly lowers the number of resets you need rather than carrying the build.
claims.say: base int does the heavy lifting for washing, int gear helps

claims.text: When washing, putting all your INT in early makes 2nd job a slog, while adding it slowly is easier but gives less MP from the same total INT.
claims.say: int early = slow 2nd job, int slowly = less mp overall

claims.text: MP gained on a level-up uses your INT at that moment, so a washer puts on INT gear, even weapon or shield pieces, at the end of a level and finishes it on a weak mob or a quest turn-in.
claims.say: swap to int gear at 99% and level on a weak mob for more mp

claims.text: For a cheap INT cape at 25, farm several 100% INT cape scrolls from Bubblings early, then do the level 25 cape quest (Zombie Mushroom etcs plus a Wild Boar drop) and scroll the cape.
claims.say: farm bubbling cape int 100%s early, then do the lvl 25 cape quest

claims.text: Green Bandanas drop from Leprechauns and have 10 upgrade slots, which makes them a strong helmet to scroll.
claims.say: green bandana from leprechauns has 10 slots

claims.text: Maple Shields drop from Platoon Chronos and are a good shield to scroll.
claims.say: maple shield drops from platoon chronos

claims.text: The Bathrobe from the Showa hot spring is an overall any class can wear; class overalls also have 10 slots, so either makes a good scrolling base.
claims.say: showa bathrobe is an overall anyone can wear

claims.text: The White Belt gives +1 to all stats and costs 200 Mu Lung Dojo points; even an early 2nd job can beat the first four Dojo bosses, so about 50 short runs earn it.
claims.say: white belt is 200 dojo pts, just farm the first 4 bosses

claims.text: Sentinels and Ice Sentinels drop 60% INT cape scrolls; stock a few ahead of time to scroll a level 50 cape.
claims.say: sentinels and ice sentinels drop cape int 60%

claims.text: Around level 80, the Booper Scarlion map is solid training; clearing the mobs on its ground floor also turns up 60% INT overall scrolls, and Booper Scarlions drop 10% INT cape scrolls.
claims.say: booper scarlion map is good at 80, drops int ova and cape scrolls

claims.text: Sage Cats and Mr. Alli are both good targets for farming 60% INT earring scrolls.
claims.say: sage cats and mr. alli drop earring int 60%

claims.text: Opening an AP Reset's window shows your base HP and MP without equipment bonuses, and looking does not use up the reset.
claims.say: open an apr to see base hp/mp, it wont get used

claims.text: Thieves wash differently: to be efficient each fresh AP must go into HP, so leveling pace is set by how many AP Resets you can use per level.
claims.say: thieves wash by putting fresh ap into hp each level

claims.text: Mages build up plenty of MP just by playing normally, so they can move some into HP with AP Resets whenever they like without planning.
claims.say: mages get lots of mp anyway, just wash some to hp when you want

claims.text: First job needs level 10 (level 8 for Magicians) plus a minimum stat: 35 Strength for Warriors, 25 Dexterity for Bowmen and Thieves, 20 Intelligence for Magicians, and 20 Dexterity for Pirates.
claims.say: need 35 str warrior, 25 dex bow/thief, 20 int mage, 20 dex pirate

claims.text: Spend all your skill points before advancing to the next job, otherwise the advancement will not go through.
claims.say: spend all your sp before you job advance or it wont work

claims.text: Pirates do second job through Kyrin: she sends you to a map with Octopirates that drop Potent Wind Crystals for Gunslingers or Potent Power Crystals for Brawlers. Collect 15, leave through Kyrin, and talk to her again to advance.
claims.say: pirate 2nd job: 15 potent crystals from octopirates, then kyrin

claims.text: Second-job instructors: the Warrior one is in Perion at West Rocky Mountain IV, the Bowman one is near Henesys, the Magician one is in The Forest North of Ellinia, and the Thief one is at the Construction Site North of Kerning City.
claims.say: 2nd job npcs are in perion, henesys, ellinia and kerning

claims.text: Third job is at level 70: talk to your third-job instructor in El Nath's Chief's Residence, who sends you back to your first-job instructor, who sends you to fight your dark copy in a Door of Dimension.
claims.say: 3rd job at 70: el nath chief's residence, then fight your dark copy

claims.text: Any Door of Dimension works for any class, and the easiest to reach is in Ant Tunnel Park: take the taxi from Lith Harbor or Ellinia, walk to the far right of the map and go up at the egg.
claims.say: any door of dimension works, ant tunnel park is the easiest

claims.text: Your dark copy sometimes casts Lock on you, so bring Holy Water from Ludibrium's Path of Time or All Cure Potions. After it dies, hold the pick-up key on the Black Charm until the lock wears off to take it.
claims.say: bring holy water or all cures for the dark copy fight

claims.text: At the Holy Stone you hand over the Dark Crystal and answer its questions to receive a Necklace of Wisdom, which you give to your third-job instructor to advance.
claims.say: holy stone trades your dark crystal for a necklace of wisdom

claims.text: Fourth job is at level 120: your third-job instructor sends you to the fourth-job instructor in a hidden map off the Leafre Forest of the Priest, who asks for a Heroic Star dropped by Griffey and a Heroic Pentagon dropped by Manon.
claims.say: 4th job at 120: heroic star from griffey and heroic pentagon from manon

claims.text: After buying the scroll on Eos Tower's 44th floor, climb above the 55th floor before using a Nearest Town Scroll; anything lower warps you to Omega Sector instead.
claims.say: climb past 55f in eos tower before using a town scroll

claims.text: To save travel time, set Teleport Rocks to your first-job instructor and El Nath for third job, and to your third-job instructor and Leafre for fourth job.
claims.say: set tele rocks to el nath for 3rd job and leafre for 4th

claims.text: The advancement rewards listed are 1 SP each for first and second job, 1 SP plus 5 AP for third job, and 3 SP plus 5 AP for fourth job.
claims.say: 3rd job gives 5 ap, 4th gives 3 sp and 5 ap

claims.text: Battleship Cannon has no minimum range, so you can hit monsters standing right on top of you, and it can be fired while jumping, which lets you reposition without stopping.
claims.say: ship cannon has no min range and works mid jump

claims.text: The Battleship moves slowly and has limited HP, which balances its damage; Corsairs have weak avoid, so the ship mostly protects them by absorbing hits.
claims.say: ship is slow with limited hp, thats its tradeoff

claims.text: Dismounting the Battleship to dodge an attack and then remounting costs roughly a second of cannon fire, because you cannot shoot during the switch.
claims.say: dismount + remount loses about a second of cannon dps

claims.text: On most bosses, especially ones that hit often like Horntail, dismounting to dodge loses more damage than the ship saves; it only pays off against bosses with infrequent heavy hits.
claims.say: skip dismounting on frequent hitters like horntail

claims.text: Rapid Fire has a short effective reach: a monster too close makes you melee and one too far is missed, so positioning is tricky against bosses that lunge forward or in platform fights like Horntail.
claims.say: rapid fire reach is short, monsters cant be too close or far

claims.text: Homing Beacon (Bullseye) boosts Corsair damage and locks shots onto a chosen target, which helps against bosses like Horntail and Zakum by avoiding stray hits on other monsters.
claims.say: homing beacon locks onto the boss, great at ht and zak

claims.text: Ice Splitter can freeze and Blank Shot can stun, which gives a Corsair crowd control against some bosses' clones and awkward monsters.
claims.say: ice splitter freezes and blank shot stuns, nice utility

claims.text: To wash with AP Resets, first put one AP into HP; each AP Reset then moves a point from MP into HP, recycling it while you have spare MP. Once MP hits the minimum you must take from HP to get that first point back.
claims.say: put 1 ap in hp, then each reset moves a point from mp to hp

claims.text: Washing with AP Resets lets every level-up AP go straight into your main stat, which makes washing a pirate much simpler.
claims.say: wash with resets and your level ap can all go to main stat

claims.text: The game won't let you take MP below your class's minimum for your level.
claims.say: you cant take mp below your minimum

claims.text: HP per AP put into HP differs by class: beginners and magicians get the least, bowmen, thieves and most pirates a moderate amount, while warriors and Brawlers gain far more per point.
claims.say: warriors and brawlers get way more hp per ap than others

claims.text: Washing a magician costs a lot of MP per point removed and returns little HP; players disagree on the loss, with figures from about 30 to 90 MP per point.
claims.say: mages lose a lot of mp per wash and get little hp back

claims.text: Players disagree whether HP gained per AP Reset is fixed: one Bowman got +16 on every one of 68 resets, while a Gunslinger's preview showed +18.
claims.say: hp per reset seems fixed, about 16 on a bowman

claims.text: One table puts pirate minimum MP at 18 x level + 111, though other players say several of its rows are mixed up.
claims.say: pirate min mp is around 18 x level + 111, double check it

claims.text: For a pirate heading to Buccaneer, max Somersault Kick and Bullet Time in first job. Double Shot and Flash Fist add very little, so a single point or the leftover points are all they need.
claims.say: max somersault kick and bullet time first, skip the rest

claims.text: Pirates argue over whether Dash deserves skill points. This author leaves it alone and rides a mount for getting around instead.
claims.say: i skip dash and just use a mount

claims.text: As a Brawler, put 10 points into Improve MaxHP first, then one point each in Corkscrew Blow and Backspin Blow, then about 5 in Knuckle Mastery and 6 in Knuckle Booster, and fill out the rest afterwards.
claims.say: improve maxhp first, then a point in each attack, then mastery

claims.text: The finished Brawler build has Knuckle Mastery, Knuckle Booster, Backspin Blow, Double Uppercut and Corkscrew Blow all at 20, Oak Barrel at 10, and only a single point in MP Recovery.
claims.say: max brawler attacks, mastery, booster; oak barrel 10; 1 mp recovery

claims.text: At Marauder, fill Stun Mastery, Transformation, Shockwave, Energy Charge and Energy Blast, and put whatever points remain into Energy Drain.
claims.say: marauder: stun mastery, transformation, shockwave, charge, blast

claims.text: When Energy Blast works properly it should be the main Marauder attack, maxed together with Energy Charge before Transformation and Shockwave; that route beats leaning on Shockwave.
claims.say: energy blast with energy charge is the main marauder attack

claims.text: Once Dragon Strike and Barrage are maxed, add one point to Super Transformation, max Demolition, then finish Super Transformation. Maple Warrior (about 9 points) and one Time Leap point can go in whenever.
claims.say: after dragon strike and barrage, super transformation and demolition

claims.text: Dragon Slash Claw is a knuckle that is relatively cheap to craft compared with other late weapons, needing only mithril and wisdom crystals, which skeleton monsters drop.
claims.say: dragon slash claw is an easy knuckle to craft

claims.text: Keep DEX as low as possible on a Brawler line pirate and add only what the knuckle needs to be equipped; the rest of your points go to the main stat.
claims.say: keep dex low, just enough to wield the knuckle

claims.text: Pirates wash HP differently: put one level-up AP into HP, use AP resets to move points from MP straight into HP, and use the last reset to move MP into your main stat. That gives a guaranteed 40 HP per wash instead of a random 36 to 40.
claims.say: for pirate hp wash, put ap in hp then reset mp into hp

claims.text: HP washing is not required for Buccaneers, but it is easy and worth doing. To tank Bigfoot around level 130 you want about 170 base INT as early as possible, since INT adds to MP gained per level.
claims.say: to tank bigfoot at 130 get about 170 int early for washing

claims.text: Buccaneer damage is low compared to other jobs; the class is valued for its party buff, Speed Infusion, rather than for bossing quickly on its own.
claims.say: bucc damage is low, its worth is speed infusion for the party

claims.text: Grinding a Buccaneer is slow and many quit before fourth job, so making a bishop first is a good way to fund gear and make the climb easier.
claims.say: bucc is a slow grind, a bishop first helps fund the gear

claims.text: A Shadower's boss damage with Meso Explosion is limited by how quickly they can drop mesos on the floor.
claims.say: shad bombing dps is all about how fast you drop mesos

claims.text: For fast meso dropping, place the drop window so its OK button sits over the inventory meso button, enter the amount padded with leading zeros to the field limit, copy it, then hold Ctrl+V while clicking repeatedly.
claims.say: pad the drop amount with zeros, copy it, hold ctrl+v and click

claims.text: Bind an attack skill macro, such as Boomerang Step with Band of Thieves, to V so you keep attacking while holding Ctrl+V to drop mesos.
claims.say: put an attack macro on v so you hit while dropping mesos

claims.text: The Amoria Party Quest needs married characters of level 40 or higher, and the party must include at least one bride and one groom or stage 1 cannot be cleared.
claims.say: apq needs married ppl lvl 40+ and at least 1 bride and 1 groom

claims.text: The groom is whoever proposed and made the engagement ring; character gender does not matter. Leaders should check for a bride and groom before entering the lobby.
claims.say: groom is whoever proposed, gender doesnt matter

claims.text: Farm Lip Lock Keys in the Purplewood Forest maps near Amoria: each run uses 10 keys and a normal set is four runs, so gather 40 keys.
claims.say: farm lip lock keys at purplewood forest, 10 per run

claims.text: A run is spent as soon as you take the entrance ticket from Amos, so entering the lobby and leaving wastes it; parties usually do four runs in a row and expect you to say if you have fewer.
claims.say: a run is spent once u take the ticket, so dont leave the lobby

claims.text: In stage 1 three green portals appear after the leader talks to Amos and only one leads on; do not talk to Amos again because that changes the correct portal, and call the choice in party chat.
claims.say: dont talk to amos again after portals spawn, it reshuffles em

claims.text: The leader can stand beside Glimmer Man and keep the NPC dialog open so the fairy spawns the moment the last mob dies; with pet loot on, step off the platform so your pet does not grab the mirror shard.
claims.say: leader hold npc chat at glimmer man, pet looters step off the mirror

claims.text: When two people have to swap ropes in stage 2, the first mover waits on the small platform and tells the other where to go; the attempt counts if the leader clicks while you fall through the rope area, even if you did not hang on.
claims.say: swapping ropes? first mover waits and calls where 2nd goes

claims.text: In stage 3 everyone but the leader stands on a platform; a wrong combination spawns slimes and the slime count equals how many of the five chosen platforms are correct.
claims.say: stage 3: number of slimes = number of right platforms

claims.text: For stage 3, strong mob clearers like mages and Dark Knights should stand on middle platforms and kill the slimes at once so nobody is knocked off; anyone who cannot jump up in one try needs Haste.
claims.say: mages clear the slimes fast in stage 3, hasters dont idle

claims.text: Stage 4 needs 50 Cupid Code Pieces from the whole party dropped to the leader; stay in one spot and kill and loot instead of roaming, and it takes roughly five or six spawn waves.
claims.say: stage 4 need 50 cupid code pieces total, just stay in one spot

claims.text: In the Amoria bonus stage you get one minute to break boxes for Onyx Apples, so equip your fastest weapon and use Haste and Speed Infusion if you have them.
claims.say: equip ur fastest weapon in apq bonus, haste + speed infusion

claims.text: In the bonus stage you only keep apples from your own boxes, so avoid breaking boxes on a platform someone else is working, spread out with mobility skills, and watch that a pet does not loot another player's apple.
claims.say: bonus stage: spread out, only break ur own boxes, watch pet loot

claims.text: Good party makeup: a bride or groom mage with Genesis, Blizzard or Meteor Shower, a Dark Knight with Dragon Roar or Corsair with Aerial Strike for stage 1 mobs, plus two strong attackers or one plus a Crash user.
claims.say: apq wants a mage w genesis/blizzard/meteor, 2 strong attackers, haste

claims.text: Haste is a must for Amoria party quest to move between stages and run the bonus stage, and Speed Infusion is coveted too. Low-level haste mules are useful there from very low levels.
claims.say: a haster is must in apq, even a lowbie haste mule helps

claims.text: The minimum level for the Amoria Party Quest is 40, but it runs best when most of the party is level 120 or higher.
claims.say: apq is lvl 40 min but best with a mostly 120+ party

claims.text: Earrings picked up during the bonus stage can be sold to an NPC and cover your potion costs for the run.
claims.say: loot earrings in apq bonus and npc them for pot money

claims.text: Axes are a budget route for Heroes: axe gear and scrolls are cheap and axes need no DEX, which frees mesos for HP washing and end-game equipment.
claims.say: axe hero is cheap, axe scrolls cost less and no dex needed

claims.text: Downsides of an axe Hero are a thin market for axes and low accuracy, which makes leveling harder.
claims.say: axes are hard to find and you'll lack accuracy early

claims.text: Build an axe Hero pure STR; skipping DEX leaves roughly 40-60 more STR than a typical Hero before max level, which scales well with weapon attack.
claims.say: axe hero goes pure str, way more str than a normal hero

claims.text: If you need accuracy on an axe Hero, use DEX gear when funded; otherwise don't raise base DEX above 23.
claims.say: need acc? use dex gear, keep base dex at 23 or less

claims.text: Redner is the only fast-speed high-level axe, and a fast weapon matters a lot for grinding.
claims.say: redner is the fast high level axe to aim for

claims.text: Attack speed matters: Brandish comes out faster with a fast weapon than a normal-speed one, even under Speed Infusion.
claims.say: fast weapon speed matters, brandish is quicker even with si

claims.text: At level 50, pick up a Zakum Helmet.
claims.say: grab a zhelm at 50

claims.text: Aim for a top and bottom with as much STR as possible, 10+ STR clean being great, and wear 6+ STR shoes until you get Facestompers.
claims.say: 10+ str overalls, 6+ str shoes til facestompers

claims.text: At 3rd job you have spare SP for 2nd job skills, enough to max both the axe and sword masteries and boosters, so you aren't locked into one weapon.
claims.say: 3rd job leaves sp to max both axe and sword mastery/booster

claims.text: From 1 to 10, do the Maple Island quests and max Nimble Feet.
claims.say: do maple island quests, max nimble feet

claims.text: As a Swordman, put 5 SP into Improved HP Recovery and then max Improved MaxHP Increase.
claims.say: swordman: 5 in hp recovery, then max the max hp skill

claims.text: After that, put 1 SP into Power Strike, max Slash Blast, then max Power Strike.
claims.say: then 1 power strike, max slash blast, max power strike

claims.text: Unfunded new warriors lack accuracy, so after the job quests farm lower monsters like Orange Mushrooms for a while.
claims.say: low acc? farm orange mushrooms for a while

claims.text: Red Snails drop 10% DEX overall scrolls, which you can put on a low-level warrior overall for extra accuracy.
claims.say: red snails drop dex overall scrolls, good for early acc

claims.text: From 21, get carried in the Kerning City Party Quest, or farm Horny Mushrooms and Zombie Mushrooms in the Ant Tunnel if your accuracy gear allows.
claims.say: 21+: kpq carries, or horny/zombie shrooms in ant tunnel

claims.text: At level 30, go to Perion to become a Fighter.
claims.say: lv 30 go to perion for fighter

claims.text: Fighter order: max Rage, put 5 in Axe Mastery and 6 in Axe Booster, then max Axe Mastery, max Axe Booster, and finally max Power Guard.
claims.say: fighter: max rage, then axe mastery/booster, then power guard

claims.text: Rage goes first because Warrior Elixirs are awkward to use in Monster Carnival; if you have Warrior Elixirs to use, maxing mastery first is fine.
claims.say: rage first, unless you've got warrior elixirs to use

claims.text: From 51 to 58, train on Coolie Zombies.
claims.say: 51-58 coolie zombies

claims.text: From 58 to 70, train at Mysterious Path 3.
claims.say: 58-70 mysterious path 3

claims.text: Crusader order: max Combo Attack, max Coma: Axe, then use spare SP to max Sword Mastery and Sword Booster.
claims.say: crusader: max combo, max coma axe, then sword mastery/booster

claims.text: From 70 to 80, level in the Pirate Party Quest.
claims.say: 70-80 do ppq

claims.text: From 110, train on Skelegons and Skelesaurus together with another attacker and a priest.
claims.say: 110+ skelegons/skelesaurus with a partner and a priest

claims.text: Once you are a Hero at 120, Bigfoot and Papulatus become good targets.
claims.say: 120+ do bigfoot and pap

claims.text: Sword Heroes usually keep some DEX until late game because the Stonetooth Sword needs it.
claims.say: sword heroes need dex for stonetooth until late

claims.text: Pet equips come from the Cash Shop and are scrolled like any other equip; nearly all have 7 slots, and since up to 3 pets can be out at once, three scrolled pet equips stack.
claims.say: most pet equips have 7 slots and you can run 3 pets

claims.text: Rudolph's Hat and Christmas Tree Hat are pet equips with only 5 slots instead of the usual 7.
claims.say: rudolph's hat and xmas tree hat only have 5 slots

claims.text: The recommended boss HP figures do not account for damage-reducing skills such as a warrior's Achilles and Power Guard, a magician's Magic Guard or a shadower's Meso Guard.
claims.say: hp targets for bosses dont count guard skills like achilles

claims.text: Aim for about 3,200 HP without Hyper Body before fighting Zakum, and around level 135 is when it becomes worthwhile as an exp boss.
claims.say: zakum wants about 3.2k hp without hyper body

claims.text: Horntail wants about 10,000 HP without Hyper Body. Players can start around level 155, but are more comfortable from the mid 160s up to the 180s depending on how well funded they are.
claims.say: horntail wants about 10k hp without hyper body, lv155+

claims.text: Scarlion and Targa want about 8,000 HP without Hyper Body and are best attempted from the mid 150s.
claims.say: scarlion and targa want about 8k hp, mid 150s levels

claims.text: Melee characters want about 7,000 HP without Hyper Body for the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest.
claims.say: melee want about 7k hp for crimsonwood keep pq

claims.text: Blackfist Cloak is a random reward from the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest bonus stage and the strongest cape for non-magicians, with up to 10 weapon attack and 5 slots. Buying one skips the questline and the PQ.
claims.say: blackfist cloak from cwk pq bonus is the best cape for non-mages

claims.text: Mark of Naricain is an untradable necklace dropped by the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest bosses (about five per run) and the best necklace for most classes. It needs the long Crimsonwood Keep questline first, roughly five hours.
claims.say: mark of naricain from cwk pq is the best necklace for most

claims.text: Mu Lung Dojo belts need training points: Yellow Belt 1,800, Blue Belt 4,000, Red Belt 9,200 and Black Belt 17,000, and each gives bonus HP.
claims.say: dojo belts: yellow 1800, blue 4000, red 9200, black 17000 points

claims.text: The Black Belt from Mu Lung Dojo is the best non-event belt, but it takes a long stretch of dojo training, so many players spread it out over weeks or months.
claims.say: black belt from dojo is the best non-event belt

claims.text: Guild Party Quest needs at least six players from the same guild, and only the guild leader or a jr. leader can organise it. An experienced party takes about 25 minutes per run.
claims.say: gpq needs 6 from one guild, leader or jr leader starts it

claims.text: Broken Glasses from 35 full Ludibrium Party Quest clears are not a pick for endgame players, since better tradable eye accessories exist.
claims.say: broken glasses are meh for endgame, better eye accessories exist

claims.text: Archers can craft the Crimson Arclancer bow or the Dusk Raven's Eye crossbow once they finish the related Crimsonwood Keep quests, and both give bonus HP.
claims.say: archers can craft crimson arclancer or dusk raven's eye after cwk

claims.text: The Romeo and Juliet Party Quest needs a party of exactly four, all level 71 or higher, with at least one mage who can Teleport and at least one member with Haste (or high speed and jump).
claims.say: romeo and juliet pq: exactly 4, lvl 71+, one tele mage, one haste

claims.text: You can start the Romeo and Juliet Party Quest from either Romeo or Juliet in Magatia; the run is nearly identical on both sides, and you later turn in and collect rewards with whichever NPC you started with.
claims.say: start the pq from romeo or juliet in magatia, same run either way

claims.text: Stage 1 is a lab where the party must find a hidden switch by clicking things on the map such as boxes and books; pressing it opens the door to the portal for stage 2.
claims.say: stage 1 lab: click boxes and books to find the hidden door switch

claims.text: A secret letter (Romeo's or Juliet's) can be found in the stage 1 lab; hand it to Romeo or Juliet in stage 4 if you want the Angry Frankenroid at the end instead of the normal one.
claims.say: grab the secret letter in stage 1 and give it to romeo in stage 4

claims.text: Stage 2 is a plain run-and-gun map in the dark: it is flat, so kill the monsters while heading right and leave through the right-hand portal.
claims.say: stage 2 is a dark run and gun, just kill and head right

claims.text: In stage 3 three beakers must be filled by dropping the monsters' ETC drops on top of them. They leak until full, so the party should concentrate on filling one or two at a time.
claims.say: stage 3 fill all 3 beakers with etc drops before they leak out

claims.text: Stage 4 has a middle map where monsters drop card keys; you need two per side. The side doors open only from the middle map, so keep two members outside and send one member into each side.
claims.say: stage 4: get 2 card keys per side, doors open only from middle map

claims.text: To set up the Angry Frankenroid, the party leader clicks Yulete in stage 5 so he mumbles, and the party should not wander too far to the right in that map.
claims.say: for angry frankenroid click yulete in stage 5, dont go far right

claims.text: After the monsters in stage 5 are dead, click the book to open the door that leads to stage 6.
claims.say: stage 5: kill the mobs then click the book to open the door

claims.text: Stage 6 has four doors, one per member. Each leads to a private room of 10 rows with 4 platforms, where exactly one platform per row warps you up. The correct combination changes every run.
claims.say: stage 6: everyone takes a door, 10 rows of 4 platforms, 1 is right

claims.text: For any given row, the platform that works in your room never works in the other three rooms, so use teammates' finished rows to eliminate options: if three others solved a row with 1, 2 and 4, yours is 3.
claims.say: in stage 6 the right platform for a row differs in all four rooms

claims.text: In stage 6 type each solved platform into party chat in short groups (for example four digits, four digits, then two) so everyone can see which rows are done and which platforms to skip.
claims.say: post solved platforms in party chat so mates skip them

claims.text: Talking to Yulete in stage 7 summons Frankenroid and some monsters around Romeo or Juliet. One player should kill the add monsters to keep the NPC alive while the rest kill Frankenroid; the run only succeeds if he dies first.
claims.say: stage 7: kill the mobs on romeo while the rest kill frankenroid

claims.text: For the best clear, hand in the letter in stage 4, make Yulete mumble in stage 5, save Romeo or Juliet in stage 7, and pick the second option when talking to Yulete so the Angry Frankenroid is summoned.
claims.say: letter, yulete mumble, then pick the 2nd option for angry frankenroid

claims.text: To collect rewards after the final boss, talk to Yulete in the next map and then to Romeo or Juliet (whichever one you began the party quest with) in the map after that.
claims.say: after the pq talk to yulete, then romeo or juliet for rewards

claims.text: Orbis Party Quest needs a full party of 6 between levels 51 and 200, a thief with maxed Haste or anyone with at least 112% jump, and a mage with Teleport or a Hermit or Night Lord with maxed Flash Jump.
claims.say: opq needs 6 players, a hasted thief/112% jump, and a teleport mage

claims.text: Orbis PQ takes about 20-25 minutes and gives good experience. Most stages need little hitting, so weak or HP-washing characters can do it, but recruiting a party is hard and the item rewards are poor.
claims.say: opq is good exp and washing friendly but hard to find a party

claims.text: Enter the right portal at the Orbis Tower entrance and talk to Wonky to start the party quest.
claims.say: talk to wonky at the right portal in orbis tower to start opq

claims.text: Stage 1: hit the clouds and collect pieces, going clockwise, then drop 20 pieces on the glowing light in the middle. That spawns Eak, and talking to it moves you on.
claims.say: opq stage 1 collect 20 pieces from clouds and drop them in the middle

claims.text: The Center Tower map links the stages and the leader enters the portals from bottom to top. Each cleared stage gives a piece for the broken statue, and the four roaming Boogies are harmless and can be ignored.
claims.say: opq center tower: do portals bottom to top, each gives a statue piece

claims.text: Stage 2 is a small jump quest where you break boxes to find a disc, and the disc color depends on the weekday: Monday orange, Tuesday yellow, Wednesday purple, Thursday dark blue, Friday light blue, Saturday green, Sunday red.
claims.say: opq disc color depends on weekday, monday is orange

claims.text: In the disc stage the two right platforms need Teleport and Haste. Without a Teleport user, maxed Flash Jump can reach the disc.
claims.say: opq disc stage right platforms need teleport + haste or max flash jump

claims.text: Tell the party when the right disc is found so nobody wastes time, drop it on the jukebox, then the leader clicks the NPC. Never drop a second disc after the right one: the music gets replaced and the stage can never be cleared.
claims.say: opq: drop the right disc once only, a 2nd disc ruins the stage

claims.text: After the Sealed Room is solved, one member goes up to break the box with the piece while the leader waits at the exit portal. The leader must not leave before the pieces are gained, or they are lost and the run fails.
claims.say: opq sealed room: dont leave till the piece is collected or you fail

claims.text: Do not kill a Cellion near a platform corner: the invisible item that triggers the next spawn falls away and the next Cellion never appears, which ruins the run.
claims.say: opq storage: dont kill cellions near the corner or the next wont spawn

claims.text: In the storage stage the member holding the rock piece can climb the ladder and drop it from high above, while the leader waits at the bottom to pick it up and clear the stage at once.
claims.say: opq storage: drop the piece from the ladder to leader to finish fast

claims.text: Stage 5, Lounge, has four portals each holding 10 rock pieces. The top three need 112% jump and 10 Cellions each, so strong attackers should take them; the bottom dark room has invisible platforms with 5 boxes per side and suits two people.
claims.say: opq lounge: hitters take top rooms, 2 people do the dark room

claims.text: For the Lounge, each person takes one room and marks a coin before entering so nobody repeats a room; the 40 rock pieces then go to the leader.
claims.say: opq lounge: mark a coin when you take a room so no one repeats it

claims.text: Stage 7 is a platform guessing climb with a combination the party types or marks with coins. At the top the leader spams the bottom NPC while others hit the lever slowly enough for the leader's clicks to follow.
claims.say: opq last stage: guess the platform combo, hit the lever slowly

claims.text: Return to the broken statue in the Center Tower and drop every piece on its right spot. When the statue is whole, the leader talks to Eak to enter the boss stage.
claims.say: opq: put all pieces on the statue then leader talks to eak

claims.text: Boss stage Garden: kill Nependeaths and drop their seeds into the pots, one seed per pot. A seed can spawn another Nependeath, a Dark Nependeath, or nothing; mark pots with a regular coin or a gold coin for empty ones so nobody replants.
claims.say: opq garden: one seed per pot, mark coins so nobody replants

claims.text: Killing the Dark Nependeath summons Papa Pixie, so tell the party. Papa Pixie resists every element, casts slow, seal and darkness, and summons Pixies, so bring physical damage and cures.
claims.say: papa pixie resists all elements and casts seal/slow/darkness

claims.text: After Papa Pixie dies, drop the Even Stranger Seed on an empty pot, hit the grass that grows to get Grass of Life, leave the map and drop it on the middle of the statue to summon the goddess and clear the quest.
claims.say: after papa pixie plant the even stranger seed, get grass of life for statue

claims.text: The optional Room of Darkness, the diary room, is entered from the statue map above the Disc stage portal; Jr. Cellions there can drop diary pieces for a quest, and it takes about a minute after the boss.
claims.say: opq diary room has jr cellions dropping diary pieces, quick after boss

claims.text: A regular bandit keeps about 50 to 80 DEX, which is fine while you are learning or cannot afford gear; resetting DEX later is expensive.
claims.say: regular bandit keeps 50-80 dex, fine if broke but a reset costs lots

claims.text: A dexless bandit puts every point into LUK, the stat that gives bandits most of their damage; high level Maple weapons need no stats, so it works even without being rich.
claims.say: dexless bandit = all luk, maple weapons dont need stats

claims.text: Strength bandits can use high level shields with extra attack such as the Dragon Khanjar; with a Horntail Necklace and Zakum Helmet it is possible to be both strength and dexless.
claims.say: str bandits wear dragon khanjar, ht necklace and zakum helm

claims.text: Thieves pick one of two first-job styles: a sindit throws stars with Lucky Seven until at least level 40 (some stay until 70), while a pure dit uses the dagger throughout; the choice does not change the later build.
claims.say: sindit = stars w lucky seven till 40+, pure dit = dagger all the way

claims.text: Sindit first-job SP: Keen Eyes to 5 early, Lucky Seven to 20 by level 18, then Disorder 3, Dark Sight 10, Nimble Body 20 and Double Stab 3 by level 30.
claims.say: sindit sp: keen eyes 5, max lucky seven, dark sight, nimble body

claims.text: Pure dit first-job SP: Double Stab to 20 by level 17, then Disorder 3, Dark Sight 10, Nimble Body 20, Keen Eyes 5 and a few points in Lucky Seven so you can advance.
claims.say: pure dit sp: max double stab, dark sight, nimble body, keen eyes

claims.text: Steal can serve as an early mobbing attack so you may take it sooner, but do not max it because all the other second job skills are needed later and Steal is not.
claims.say: steal is ok for early mobbing but dont max it

claims.text: Third job SP: Band of Thieves to 20 by level 79, Shadow Partner to 20 by 85, Assaulter to 20 by 92, and Flash Jump to 20 by 98, with a few early points in Chakra.
claims.say: 3rd job: band of thieves, shadow partner, assaulter, then flash jump

claims.text: Boomerang Step is one of the most important Shadower attacks: it hits twice with a stun chance and permanently strengthens Savage Blow, Steal and Assaulter.
claims.say: boomerang step is a key 4th job move, also buffs savage blow

claims.text: Haste boosts speed and jump for the whole team, which makes a bandit welcome in parties; it reaches max level in the second job build.
claims.say: haste buffs the whole party speed and jump, bandits are wanted for it

claims.text: You cannot attack or be attacked while Dark Sight is up, and Assassinate is used from Dark Sight: the longer you stay hidden before it, the more damage it deals and the last hit is a fatal blow.
claims.say: hide in dark sight longer before assassinate for bigger damage

claims.text: Meso Explosion detonates mesos lying on the ground to hit many monsters, but it cannot explode mesos that belong to other players; Pickpocket makes mesos fall as you attack without costing you any.
claims.say: meso explosion only blows up ur own mesos, pickpocket makes more

claims.text: Meso Guard soaks part of the damage you take by paying with mesos from a pool set aside when you cast it.
claims.say: meso guard absorbs dmg by spending mesos

claims.text: Shadow Partner mimics your attacks for a limited time and uses up one Summoning Rock each time you cast it, so keep a stock of them.
claims.say: shadow partner burns a summoning rock per cast, keep a stack

claims.text: Chakra converts MP into HP but only works while your HP is under half.
claims.say: chakra only heals when ur under 50% hp

claims.text: Venomous Stab gives your dagger attacks a chance to poison; poison does not stack and cannot take a monster below 1 HP.
claims.say: venomous stab = chance to poison, cant kill and doesnt stack

claims.text: Assaulter strikes a single monster three times with a chance to stun it, and Savage Blow lands six very quick hits on one target.
claims.say: assaulter is 3 hits + stun chance, savage blow is 6 quick hits

claims.text: Disorder lowers a monster's weapon attack and defence and cannot be reused on the same monster, while Nimble Body permanently raises your accuracy and avoidability.
claims.say: disorder lowers mob atk/def, nimble body gives acc and avoid

claims.text: Steal hits several monsters and has a chance to take an item from a monster, but it only works once per monster, so keep trying on others until it succeeds.
claims.say: steal only works once per mob so keep trying other mobs

claims.text: Flash Jump is a double jump, and the higher you level it the further it takes you, which helps both traveling and dodging.
claims.say: flash jump = double jump, further as it levels

claims.text: Jumping into the pit at the bottom right of Dragon Forest I drops you into a hidden cornian tomb full of Dark and Green Cornians; Hidden Dragon Tomb II there has particularly good spawns.
claims.say: cornian tomb is the pit at bottom right of dragon forest i

claims.text: Leafre is reached through the portal in The Field Up North of Ellinia, and coming from Ariant the NPC Karcasa gets you to Ellinia quickly.
claims.say: leafre portal is in the field up north of ellinia

claims.text: In tall maps like Valley of the Antelope, changing channels drops you back at the top, which is quicker than climbing up after you work your way down.
claims.say: channel swap puts you back up top in valley of the antelope

claims.text: The Gigantic Spirit Viking map opens from the top left corner of Warped Path of Time 4, and the Grim Phantom Watch map from a platform near the bottom middle of Forgotten Path of Time 4.
claims.say: gigantic spirit vikings are via top left of warped path of time 4

claims.text: You must have completed the Papulatus prequest before you can enter Ellin Forest, so skipping it locks you out of the Ellin Forest content.
claims.say: do the papulatus prequest or ellin forest stays locked

claims.text: Both Dangerous Sea Gorge I and II have Squids; the Flyeye map sits just before the Pianus boss map and is reached from The Grave of a Wrecked Ship, the Shark map.
claims.say: flyeyes are in the map right before pianus

claims.text: Cold Sharks and Gobies spawn on the same Deep Sea Gorge map; when the sharks are done, take the top left portal to Deep Sea Gorge II for more Gobies.
claims.say: cold sharks and gobies share a map, then top left portal for more gobies

claims.text: Crimson Guardians in Crimsonwood can seal your skills, so carry cure potions. There is a room for them inside the Keep, but the keep entrance map works just as well.
claims.say: bring cure potions for crimson guardians, they lock your skills

claims.text: The VIP cab in Ellinia is the quick way to the Wild Kargo area in Sharenian, and Commander and Officer Skeletons spawn together in both of their maps.
claims.say: take the vip cab from ellinia to get to the kargos fast

claims.text: The Saitie map is hidden: enter the Magatia lab on the right and head down to find the secret entrance. The Saitie-looking NPC on the right can't be targeted.
claims.say: saitie map: right-side magatia lab, go down to the secret entrance

claims.text: For Nest Golems, Peak of the Big Nest is easier than Dangerous Dragon Nest: simpler terrain, and Jr. Newties won't keep knocking you off ladders.
claims.say: peak of the big nest is easier than dangerous dragon nest for golems

claims.text: Skelegons and Skelosauruses share The Dragon Nest Left Behind; once you want only Skelegons, Nest of a Dead Dragon one map to the left has more of them.
claims.say: nest of a dead dragon has more skelegons

claims.text: Shadower is a middle-of-the-road damage dealer that needs no party buffs, dodges a lot thanks to LUK, and takes reduced damage through Meso Guard and Shadow Shifter, so it survives bosses well.
claims.say: shadower is self sufficient and tanky, dont need party buffs

claims.text: Speed Infusion adds nothing to a Shadower's damage rate because a dagger with Dagger Booster is already at maximum attack speed.
claims.say: dagger + booster is already max speed so skip speed infusion

claims.text: As a first-job Thief, max Dark Sight (Assassinate needs it later) and Nimble Body, put 1 point in Lucky Seven, and spend the rest on Double Stab or Disorder. Sin-dits put the rest into Lucky Seven instead.
claims.say: max dark sight and nimble body, rest in double stab

claims.text: Double Stab is better to max than Lucky Seven: Lucky Seven is awkward inside mob packs and you will use a dagger later anyway. Some max Lucky Seven and play a sin-dit until mid second job.
claims.say: double stab over lucky seven, you use a dagger later anyway

claims.text: Disorder stops a monster from casting spells, so spare first-job points can go there, even ahead of Double Stab if you are being leeched early.
claims.say: disorder stops mobs casting spells, good spare point sink

claims.text: Max Dagger Mastery, Dagger Booster and Haste in second job; nearly every Shadower agrees on these three.
claims.say: max dagger mastery, dagger booster and haste in 2nd job

claims.text: Meso Explosion is the Chief Bandit's bread and butter: it lets you train on your own from third job without buying leech.
claims.say: meso explosion lets you self train from 3rd job, no leech needed

claims.text: Max Band of Thieves as your first mobbing skill; it pairs well with Boomerang Step in fourth job.
claims.say: max band of thieves, pairs well with boomerang step

claims.text: Assaulter gives great vertical mobility in tall platform maps. In the Horntail fight you can use his arms and wings to jump back up onto a platform to attack from.
claims.say: assaulter gets you up platforms fast, even off horntail's arms

claims.text: Assassinate is the main single-target attack and only works from Dark Sight. Bind it and your normal attack to easy keys so you can leave Dark Sight quickly, since you cannot use potions while in it.
claims.say: assassinate needs dark sight and you cant pot inside it

claims.text: Assassinate is not hit by damage reflect, so against damage-reflecting monsters use Dark Sight then Assassinate instead of other attacks.
claims.say: vs damage reflect use dark sight + assassinate, it isnt reflected

claims.text: Taunt makes monsters you hit give more exp and drops at the cost of higher defense; with Boomerang Step it makes Shadower an excellent farming class, second only to mages.
claims.say: taunt boosts exp and drops from mobs, great for farming

claims.text: Take Hero's Will because Shadowers are often the Horntail seduce target, and it is a lifeline if something goes wrong.
claims.say: hero's will is a good lifeline when youre the seduce target

claims.text: Ninja Ambush does less damage than a normal attack (though it works through weapon cancel) and Venomous Stab is weak for bossing and so-so for grinding, so leave both for last.
claims.say: ninja ambush and venomous stab are low priority

claims.text: Plan AP around wearing end-game gear: Dragon Kanzir and Dragon Khanjar need 75 STR and 150 DEX. Equips can cover that while you keep base STR 4 and DEX 25 (the thief minimum) and put the rest into LUK.
claims.say: keep base str 4 and dex 25, equips cover the rest, rest in luk

claims.text: A Shadower needs roughly half the usual recommended boss HP thanks to Meso Guard; around 12k HP covers nearly every boss, and Hyper Body helps further. Washing to 30k is possible but costly.
claims.say: 12k hp is plenty for a shadower, meso guard halves the hits

claims.text: At levels 14-20 as a Thief, follow the worthwhile quest list and use the Orbis exchange quest if you have the drops or mesos; otherwise train on Bubblings.
claims.say: lvl 14-20 do quests or train on bubblings

claims.text: Party training at the Forest of Golems is good for income and exp around levels 51-70, and Mysterious Path 3 is another great party training spot.
claims.say: party at mysterious path 3 or the forest of golems for 51-70

claims.text: You can drop mesos while attacking: bind an attack or macro to V, paste the meso amount with Ctrl+V and spam, and the skill fires between drops.
claims.say: bind your attack to v and hold ctrl+v to drop mesos while attacking

claims.text: The author argues the Horntail Necklace beats Mark of Naricain for end-game Shadowers: it makes the STR/DEX requirements easy so more base AP goes into LUK, and Maple Warrior scales with base stats. Other players disagree.
claims.say: horntail necklace vs mark of naricain is debated for shadowers

claims.text: For more damage range, upgrade the dagger first, then the shield, then attack gear (shoes, cape, gloves); gear that lowers the stats you must keep is about as valuable as attack gear.
claims.say: upgrade dagger first, then shield, then attack gear

claims.text: Stacking several Shadowers in a party allows unusual boss runs, for example an all-Shadower Horntail clear.
claims.say: all shadower horntail runs are a thing, they stack well

claims.text: A party of Shadowers can clear Horntail without ranged attackers: kill the tail first from inside Smokescreen cover, then the legs so mules can cross to the right side, then push on to the arms.
claims.say: shadower ht run: tail first under smokescreen, then legs

claims.text: Layer your Smokescreens so a new one lands a few seconds before the old one ends. That leaves no gap where the tail or a seduce target can get hit between them.
claims.say: overlap smokescreens a few secs so theres no gap

claims.text: Teams unsure of their damage can have Shadowers drop meso bags at the tail's hit-spot before the rock is broken, then blow them with Meso Explosion once Horntail appears. Stronger teams skip the bags and just hit the tail.
claims.say: unsure about tail dps? drop meso bags then meso explosion

claims.text: Shadowers are the best class for Horntail's right side because Boomerang Step hits up to four targets at once, so they should stay on the right side while several parts are alive.
claims.say: shadowers should hit ht's right side, boomerang step hits 4

claims.text: On Horntail use Boomerang Step as the main attack while three or four parts are alive; once only two targets remain, alternate Assassinate with Boomerang Step instead.
claims.say: 2 targets left on ht? switch to assassinate plus boomerang step

claims.text: Aim to kill the right arm and Head C around the same time so Shadowers keep hitting several targets. Single-target attackers should take Head C and multi-target attackers the arm and wings.
claims.say: kill ht right arm and head c together so multi hitters stay useful

claims.text: Before rushing a Horntail arm, have every Hero's Will off cooldown. Non-Shadowers must use it at the first mass seduce, because the heads can drop seduced players to 1 HP and cause many deaths.
claims.say: use hero's will out of mass seduce on ht or the heads 1/1 you

claims.text: If one attacker lacks Hero's Will, an active Bishop can use Hero's Will at the first mass seduce and heal the attackers to keep them alive through it.
claims.say: a bishop with hero's will can cover attackers at ht mass sed

claims.text: A Buccaneer with Time Leap ready can reset cooldowns once the Hero's Wills and Smokescreens are spent, letting the party repeat the will-then-smoke cycle through a long arm rush.
claims.say: buccs time leap resets wills and smokes for a long arm rush

claims.text: As a last resort when a mass seduce comes and cover is gone, jump into a mob at the bottom of the map to get invincibility frames from the touch hit and dodge the 1 HP attacks. It is risky and you can still die.
claims.say: last resort at ht mass sed, touch a mob for iframes

claims.text: Once the left arm is dead, seduces and armor ups stop, so no more dispelling or armor cancelling is needed; finish heads A and B as in a normal run, with Shadowers hitting Head A.
claims.say: left arm dead means no more seduce, just finish heads a and b

claims.text: Have one person own the timers for mass seduces and Smokescreens during a Horntail run, since the whole arm-rush plan depends on knowing when the next seduce and cover are due.
claims.say: get someone to keep timers for mass sed and smokescreens

claims.text: Shadowers should bring a solid HP pool for a Horntail run, at least about 8000 HP and ideally more.
claims.say: shadowers want 8k hp minimum for ht, more is better

claims.text: The author thinks an Ice/Lightning Mage should put no points into Luk: high-tier weapons mostly cost their magic attack back in Luk requirements, and Zakum Helmets and Horntail Necklaces already supply Luk for low-Luk gear.
claims.say: i/l should skip luk, zakum helm and ht necklace cover low luk gear

claims.text: First-job mage build: 1 point in Energy Bolt, a few into Improving MP Recovery, 10 into Improving MaxMP Increase, then max Magic Claw (your main training skill) and put 20 into Magic Guard.
claims.say: mage 1st job: maxmp increase 10, max magic claw, then magic guard

claims.text: Skip Cold Beam early since no good ice-weak spot gives great exp or mesos, and Slow is rarely used because late bosses are stationary or already slow; maxing first-job Magic Armor is probably better.
claims.say: skip cold beam and slow, magic armor is better to max

claims.text: Do not put early points into Meditation: the elixirs sold in New Leaf City give the same effect and last longer.
claims.say: dont spend early sp on meditation, nlc elixirs do the same longer

claims.text: The core third-job skills are Element Amplification, Ice Strike and Spell Booster; Thunder Spear is very slow, Seal and Partial Resistance rarely matter, and Element Composition is weak on single targets.
claims.say: il core skills are amp, ice strike and spell booster, rest is meh

claims.text: After level 20 with Magic Claw maxed, you can one- or two-shot Wild Boars and Dark Axe Stumps in The Land of Wild Boar; it stays fast with Teleport and is decent until around 40, mostly for money later on.
claims.say: wild boars and dark axe stumps at the land of wild boar are quick 20-30

claims.text: From level 30, Monster Carnival free wins (a solo party against a crowd you join) are an extremely fast way through the early levels, but such parties are hard to find; if you cannot get one, keep training on Wild Boars.
claims.say: carnival free wins are super fast at 30 but hard to find

claims.text: Platoon Chronos in the Path of Time is a good money spot for 40 to 55: it often drops Maple Shields that sell well, plus Scroll for Gloves for ATT 60% and Power Crystal Ore.
claims.say: platoon chronos at 40-55 is good money, drops maple shields

claims.text: In the late 50s to 70 the Forest of Golem gives good exp and mesos: the Golems are thick, and you can sell dropped equips to an NPC and sell the glove scrolls.
claims.say: forest of golem at 55-70 for exp and mesos, npc the equips

claims.text: Since a Luk-less mage cannot wear high-Luk weapons, use Maple weapons and the Elemental Wands; the end-game goal is an Elemental Wand 5 to 8 with around 190 total magic attack.
claims.say: luk-less il uses maple weapons and elemental wands, end goal wand 5-8

claims.text: A Zakum Helmet is the second most important item for an Ice/Lightning Mage: roughly 15 INT plus a big weapon and magic defense boost, which matters because you wear lower-level gear.
claims.say: zakum helm is worth it for about 15 int and the defense

claims.text: Earrings scrolled with INT or magic attack give the best boost per scroll; start with a lightly scrolled pair and later scroll your own with the 10% and 30% scrolls, finishing with a few 60%.
claims.say: scrolled earrings are the best int/matk boost per scroll

claims.text: An overall scrolled with INT is also useful for HP washing; aim for around 15 INT, since going far above that gets extremely expensive.
claims.say: overall with about 15 int is the sweet spot, more gets expensive

claims.text: A Purple Gaia Cape scrolled with INT is a good cape slot; they usually come with 5 to 7 magic attack, and INT cape scrolls are cheap enough to scroll one yourself.
claims.say: purple gaia cape with int scrolls is a good cape for il

claims.text: A Maple Shield scrolled for magic attack is a big-ticket item: the 60% scroll is extremely costly, and rushing its 10 slots with 30% and 70% scrolls risks blowing it up.
claims.say: maple shield with matk scrolls is pricey, dont rush the slots

claims.text: The Silver Deputy Star is the best pendant for an Ice/Lightning Mage, giving INT and the Luk needed for low-Luk gear, and it can be chaosed for a bit more INT.
claims.say: silver deputy star is the best pendant for il

claims.text: Gloves scrolled for magic attack rank low for an Ice/Lightning Mage because the scrolls add little magic attack for the cost; buy the other equips first.
claims.say: magic attack gloves are low priority, scrolls give too little

claims.text: One player rates Master Chronos as the best spot for 40 to 50 for a Teleport user: a great map layout, wonderful drops, and at later levels you can hunt Timer there for scrolls.
claims.say: master chronos is a great 40-50 spot for mages with teleport

claims.text: Ludibrium Maze Party Quest is fast exp for an Ice/Lightning Mage around 50 to 60 without the potion burn of Ghost Ship 2, but it slows down in the 60s.
claims.say: lmpq is fast exp at 50-60 with no pot burn, slows in the 60s

claims.text: Ice Strike reaches about three quarters of the map when fighting Voodoos, a nice change in the early 70s if you tire of Ghost Ship 2 and a decent place to farm for mesos.
claims.say: ice strike covers most of the map at voodoos, decent for mesos

claims.text: HP washing works because HP and MP share one AP pool: once you have MP above your class minimum, you add AP to HP and then use AP Resets to take points back out of MP.
claims.say: hp wash: ap into hp, then ap reset points out of mp

claims.text: The spare MP used for washing comes from INT: every 10 total INT, from base stats or equipment alike, gives about 1 extra MP on each level up.
claims.say: every 10 int gives about 1 extra mp per level up

claims.text: A fresh level-up AP put into MP gives the class's usual MP gain plus base INT divided by 10, rounded down. INT from equipment does not raise this bonus; only base INT does.
claims.say: fresh ap into mp gets base int/10 bonus, gear int doesnt count

claims.text: An AP Reset that removes a point from MP only takes away the class's fixed amount, so the base INT bonus from a fresh point stays as spare MP. Doing this deliberately is called MP washing.
claims.say: resetting out of mp only takes the base amount, bonus stays

claims.text: MP washing steps: level up with base INT in a multiple of 10, put the new AP into MP, then use AP Resets to move those points into the stat you really want.
claims.say: mp wash: level with base int, ap into mp, then reset it away

claims.text: Without base INT, thieves and bowmen gain about 10-12 MP per point in MP but lose 12 when resetting it, and warriors gain about 2-4 but lose 4, so an MP wash with no base INT is a small loss.
claims.say: no base int means mp washing just loses a bit of mp

claims.text: Only fresh level-up AP earns the INT bonus. Resetting a point into MP and back out gives no bonus and loses about 1 MP on average each time.
claims.say: only fresh ap gets the int bonus, reset ap doesnt

claims.text: Mages can MP wash by itself to push toward max MP, which lets Magic Guard absorb more damage.
claims.say: mages can mp wash so magic guard tanks better

claims.text: Double washing means MP washing first and then spending the extra MP it creates on more HP washes.
claims.say: double wash = mp wash first, then hp wash with the extra mp

claims.text: Double washing is not needed for common HP goals like 8k to 13k or for bossing at reasonable levels; it only pays off for 15k+ HP and costs many AP Resets plus resetting the base INT later.
claims.say: no need to double wash unless you want 15k+ hp

claims.text: Base INT is a far more efficient washing source than INT gear, since only base INT adds MP to each fresh point placed in MP; one level of MP washing with modest base INT beats several levels of costly INT gear.
claims.say: base int beats int gear for washing by a lot

claims.text: If you have no base INT and will not add any, MP washing does nothing for you; keep HP washing the normal way.
claims.say: no base int? skip mp washing and just hp wash normally

claims.text: Warriors are the cheapest class to wash: a wash costs them about 4 MP and returns much more HP, while thieves and bowmen pay about 12 MP for roughly 18 HP per wash.
claims.say: warriors wash cheapest, about 4 mp per wash vs 12 for thieves

claims.text: From level 1 to 10, finish every quest on Maple Island before leaving.
claims.say: do all the maple island quests till lv10

claims.text: For a new warrior from 10 to 21, Henesys Hunting Ground I to III and Line 1 <Area 1> in the Kerning subway have large spawns.
claims.say: lv10-21: henesys hunting grounds or subway line 1 area 1

claims.text: From 21 to 30, run the Kerning City Party Quest; it works well for roughly levels 21 to 35.
claims.say: 21-30 just do kpq

claims.text: As a Page from 30 to 51, Monster Carnival is a good choice: winning is what counts, the mobs give high exp and the reward for a win is strong.
claims.say: 30-51 do carnival pq, win for the big exp

claims.text: From 51 to 70, the Orbis Party Quest gives more exp than the later Monster Carnival, so it is the recommended choice.
claims.say: 51-70 opq beats carnival for exp

claims.text: As a White Knight from 70 to 100, run the Pirate Party Quest, killing every monster and leaving the box unopened.
claims.say: 70-100 ppq, kill everything and leave the box alone

claims.text: Beginner skill points: put them into Three Snails and Nimble Feet and skip Recovery, which is not needed early or later. Three Snails uses snail shells as ammo.
claims.say: beginner sp: three snails and nimble feet, skip recovery

claims.text: Paladins never get Haste or Flash Jump, so taking Nimble Feet early as a beginner is worth it for the extra speed.
claims.say: paladins have no haste, grab nimble feet as a beginner

claims.text: Early warrior SP: 1 point in Power Strike at 10 and 1 in Slash Blast at 11, then 5 points in Improved HP Recovery and 10 in Improved MaxHP Increase by level 16.
claims.say: lv10-16: 1 power strike, 1 slash blast, then hp skills

claims.text: Then max Power Strike by about level 22, max Slash Blast by about 28, and spend the last 1st job points in Endure.
claims.say: max power strike, then slash blast, rest in endure

claims.text: For a future Paladin, Power Strike and Slash Blast stay the main attacks all the way from 10 to 120, so max both.
claims.say: power strike and slash blast carry you to 120, max them

claims.text: As a Page, max the mastery for your weapon type (Sword Mastery or BW Mastery) by about 37, then its booster by about 44.
claims.say: page: max weapon mastery first, then booster

claims.text: After the booster, put the next points into Power Guard and max it by about level 54.
claims.say: after booster, max power guard by about 54

claims.text: From 55 to 70, max the other weapon type's mastery and booster as well and put the remaining points into Threaten.
claims.say: 55-70: max the other mastery and booster, rest in threaten

claims.text: Skip Final Attack on a Page; the author found it lowered damage output and regretted adding it.
claims.say: skip final attack, it drags your dps down

claims.text: Threaten seldom works on bosses, so there is no reason to max it.
claims.say: threaten barely works on bosses, don't max it

claims.text: Maxing both Sword and BW masteries keeps a Page flexible early, since good one-handed blunt weapons are hard to come by.
claims.say: max both masteries, good 1h bws are hard to find

claims.text: A warrior needs 35 STR at level 10 to make the job advancement.
claims.say: need 35 str at lv10 for warrior

claims.text: Get about 40 base DEX by level 21 so you can hit the Ligators in the Kerning City Party Quest, then put the rest of your AP into STR.
claims.say: get 40 dex by 21 so you hit the ligators in kpq, rest str

claims.text: Gear with DEX can stand in for base DEX; once your equipment gives enough accuracy, use an AP Reset to move the extra DEX into STR.
claims.say: enough dex from gear? ap reset the extra dex into str

claims.text: Gear priorities for a Paladin: helmet and overall with high DEX, shoes with DEX and STR, gloves and cape with weapon attack or STR, and a shield with weapon attack.
claims.say: dex on helm and overall, attack on gloves cape and shield

claims.text: Maple weapons are a good pick for a Paladin because they add accuracy.
claims.say: maple weapons are nice for the extra accuracy

claims.text: A Zakum Helmet scrolled for DEX is a must-have piece for a Paladin.
claims.say: get a zakum helmet and scroll it for dex

claims.text: The level 30 Squishy Shoes from King Slime are a recommended pair of shoes.
claims.say: squishy shoes from king slime are great at 30

claims.text: Spiegelmann's Necklace or Spiegelmann's Necklace of Chaos is a must-have necklace for a Paladin.
claims.say: a spiegelmann's necklace is a must have

claims.text: Spiegelmann trades level 30 to 50 weapons for Monster Carnival coins.
claims.say: spiegelmann trades lv30-50 weapons for carnival coins

claims.text: The Ellin Forest questline opens after the Papulatus pre-quests, up to the point just before fighting him. Finishing every quest needs level 110, and completing the line unlocks the Ellin Forest Party Quest.
claims.say: ellin forest quests open after the papu pre-quests, need lv110

claims.text: Papulatus pre-quest part 1: Mr. Bouffon in Ludibrium Path of Time asks for 10 Tachion, dropped by Soul Teddy, Buffy, Lazy Buffy and Master Soul Teddy.
claims.say: papu prequest 1: 10 tachion from soul teddies or buffys

claims.text: Papulatus pre-quest part 2: Mr. Bouffon wants 300 Tachion from the same teddies plus 100 Mysterious Powder from Master Death Teddy.
claims.say: papu prequest 2: 300 tachion and 100 mysterious powder

claims.text: Papulatus pre-quest part 3: Flo, on the left of Ludibrium Path of Time, wants cracked dimension pieces A, B and C from Gigantic Spirit Vikings or Grim Phantom Watches. The Ellin Forest entry quest only shows after you hand these in.
claims.say: papu prequest 3: crack pieces a/b/c from spirit vikings

claims.text: Once the Papulatus pre-quests are done you get a text welcoming you to Ellin Forest, which you enter from a spot in Ludibrium.
claims.say: ellin forest is entered from ludibrium after the papu prequests

claims.text: Rius, one map left of the Tree Rod map, asks for 200 Rubble from Stone Bugs; after that you go deeper into the forest to find Lohd for the 999 Mossy Mushrooms.
claims.say: ellin: rius wants 200 rubble from stone bugs

claims.text: Time check for the Ellin Forest questline: the Moss Snail grind is 20 to 30 minutes, Tree Trunks about an hour, the Rius, Lohd and Kanderune section 2 to 3 hours, and the fairy hunt 1 to 2 hours.
claims.say: ellin quests: mushroom/boar part is 2-3h, fairies 1-2h

claims.text: The Ellin Forest Party Quest takes a party of 4 to 6 and needs the Ellin Forest prequest done first; gather at Deep Fairy Forest and talk to Ellin to start its 7 stages.
claims.say: epq needs 4-6 ppl and the prequest, start at ellin

claims.text: In stage 2 (Deteriorated Forest), pull the Poison Golems to the middle of the map over the water before killing them; done right, the tree there drops Diluted Poison, and the golems' own drops can't be looted.
claims.say: stage 2: kill the golems over the water in the middle

claims.text: Collect 4 Diluted Poison in stage 2, then drop them one at a time next to the portal at the far right to clear the vines.
claims.say: drop 4 diluted poison by the right portal one by one

claims.text: Stage 3 (Forest of Haze) is a big portal maze; split up, and once anyone reaches Ellin at the bottom right and talks to her, the whole party moves on.
claims.say: stage 3 maze: split up, first one to ellin bottom right

claims.text: In stage 4 (Poisoned Forest) every member talks to Ellin and picks the first option to get 10 Purification Marble; they go in the use tab, so put them on a hotkey.
claims.say: stage 4: get 10 purification marbles from ellin, hotkey them

claims.text: The party needs 20 Monster Marbles in total; give them to Ellin, who summons the Sprite, then click the Sprite to reach the next stage.
claims.say: turn in 20 monster marbles to ellin, then click the sprite

claims.text: The Primitive Boars in stage 5 are very tanky; don't try to kill them, just keep pushing them away from the Sprite.
claims.say: don't kill the boars, just push them off the sprite

claims.text: Warriors with Rush make stage 5 much easier because they can shove the boars away from the Sprite.
claims.say: bring a warrior with rush for the sprite stage

claims.text: Night Lords can pin the stage 5 boars in place with Ninja Storm and Shadow Web.
claims.say: nl can hold the boars with ninja storm and shadow web

claims.text: Stage 6 (Forest's Empty Lot) splits the party into 3 groups for a jump quest; whoever reaches the top breaks all the wooden boxes to find the Purple Stone of Magic.
claims.say: stage 6: jq to the top, break boxes for the purple stone

claims.text: The player holding the Purple Stone of Magic talks to the Sprite to send the party into the boss stage.
claims.say: whoever has the purple stone talks to the sprite

claims.text: In the last stage (Forest of Poison), drop the Purple Stone of Magic in front of the shrine to summon the Poison Golem boss, which comes in three forms.
claims.say: last stage: drop the purple stone at the shrine for the golem

claims.text: The Poison Golem boss is easy: push it over to the right side and burst it down.
claims.say: golem boss is easy, push it right and nuke it

claims.text: Each clear of the Ellin Forest Party Quest rewards 1 Altaire Fragment.
claims.say: you get an altaire fragment every clear

claims.text: Altaire Fragments from the party quest are crafting material for the Glittering Altaire Earrings.
claims.say: save altaire fragments to craft the altaire earrings

claims.text: HP gear eases washing: Blackfist Cloak and Blue Belt each add about 100 HP, and scrolling pet equips with HP adds about 100 per pet.
claims.say: blackfist cloak and blue belt give hp, hp scroll your pet equips

claims.text: A Night Lord can stay unwashed until 135, then wash every level to 165: put all 5 AP into HP and use AP Resets to move MP back into LUK.
claims.say: nl can stay unwashed till 135, then wash every level

claims.text: Even with no base INT, wear INT gear while levelling; about 100 INT from gear up to 165 lets a Night Lord wash to around 8.65k HP with roughly 138 AP Resets.
claims.say: wear int gear while leveling even with no base int

claims.text: If mesos are tight, aim to hit the HP goal at 175 instead of 165, which lowers how much INT gear and how many resets you need.
claims.say: short on mesos? aim for the hp goal at 175 instead

claims.text: For hand-in quests, collect the items first, then talk to the NPC twice to start and finish in one go instead of making extra trips.
claims.say: grab the items first then talk to the npc twice, saves a trip

claims.text: Warriors and Magicians should not skip Improving MaxHP Increase or Improved MaxMP Increase when leaving the starter levels, since missing it makes later HP or MP washing cost more.
claims.say: dont skip the maxhp/maxmp skill, it makes washing cheaper later

claims.text: The DANGER! mushroom quests are kill-99 tasks for Green Mushrooms at 15, Horny Mushrooms at 20 and Zombie Mushrooms at 22; Forest Up North VI is the usual spot for the Green Mushrooms.
claims.say: the danger mushroom quests are kill 99 of each, green horny zombie

claims.text: Wait until level 22 to do the Horny Mushroom and Zombie Mushroom DANGER! quests together in Sleepywood, since the two spawn side by side. Keep the Zombie Mushroom charms for a later quest.
claims.say: wait till 22 and do the horny and zombie mushroom quests together

claims.text: Planting Trees (level 20) wants 54 Seedlings from Ghost Stumps and Shawn the Excavator's Request (level 25) wants 5 Wooden Boards and 5 Slates; both go to Winston, so waiting until about 25 lets you finish both together.
claims.say: planting trees and shawn's request both go to winston, do at 25

claims.text: Shumi's Lost Coin, Shumi's Lost Bundle of Money and Shumi's Lost Sack of Money are jump quests at levels 20, 30 and 40 that pay decent exp without any grinding.
claims.say: shumi's jump quests at 20, 30 and 40 give free exp

claims.text: Camila's Gem (level 23) just needs you to walk the gem through Utah's maze to Utah's farm, and it pays a lot of exp for such a quick errand.
claims.say: camila's gem is a quick walk through utah's maze for big exp

claims.text: Strange Dish 1, 2 and 3 are turn-ins to Tangyoon in the Nautilus cafeteria at levels 25, 35 and 40: 40 Evil Eye Tails, 50 Curse Eye Tails and 50 Cold Eye Tails. Each pays far more exp than the one before.
claims.say: strange dish 1, 2 and 3 are eye tail turn-ins, each pays more

claims.text: The Importance of Life Alchemy (level 29) asks you to kill 80 Scorpions and turn in 40 Scorpion Stings for good exp.
claims.say: life alchemy quest is 80 scorpions and 40 stings

claims.text: The Bounty Hunt (level 38) asks you to give 1 Lidium to Muhamad and kill Deo. It pays extremely well for the level and needs The True Identity of Sand Bandits done first.
claims.say: the bounty hunt at 38 is a lidium for muhamad and killing deo

claims.text: Delivering Food to Spiruna (level 30) wants 20 each of Apples, Eggs and Oranges bought from shops and delivered to the NPC in Orbis: Cloud Park IV.
claims.say: spiruna quest is 20 apples, eggs, oranges to cloud park iv

claims.text: To reach Omega Sector from the Nautilus, finish Bartol's Request for the warp cards and start the next quest before using the portal: you only get 3 warps. The portal is behind the left-most door on the top level.
claims.say: get bartol's warp cards and start the quest before warping to omega

claims.text: Assembling the Alarm Clock needs 10 Table Clocks from Tick-Tocks, 10 Cogs from Chronos and a Special Battery from Master Robo for Pink Mesoranger; the battery only drops once the quest is active, so start it first.
claims.say: special battery only drops once the alarm clock quest is started

claims.text: Omega Sector quests run from the late 30s to about 47, so do them in one batch (using the warp capsules) rather than going back and forth.
claims.say: save up omega sector quests and do them in one trip

claims.text: A Hole in the Nautilus (level 30): give Bonnie on the bottom floor of the Nautilus 50 Solid Horns from Jr. Cellions, Jr. Grupins and Jr. Lioners. Buy Sniper Pills in Ludibrium for accuracy since they are tough to hit.
claims.say: a hole in the nautilus: 50 solid horns, use sniper pills

claims.text: Many Korean Folk Town quests end with a storybook, and each one is worth extra exp when handed to Wiz the Librarian.
claims.say: turn the folk town storybooks in to wiz the librarian for more exp

claims.text: Turn in a Swallow's Lost Seed for The Lost Seed (level 37), then drop the Magic Seed on Nolbu's or Hongbu's roof for Opening Nolbu's Gourd and Opening Hongbu's Gourd and loot what pops out.
claims.say: the lost seed's magic seed goes on nolbu's or hongbu's roof

claims.text: Fool's Gold (level 40) asks for 30 Lucky Charms from Leprechauns and can be repeated afterwards; Creeping Evil is a good map for it. It is part of the line toward a Silver Deputy Star.
claims.say: fool's gold: 30 lucky charms from leprechauns, repeatable

claims.text: Ranged classes around levels 40-50 can grind Leprechauns and repeat Fool's Gold; they drop Japanese Map, Green Bandana and Dark Noel, and the other equips vendor for decent mesos.
claims.say: ranged classes can grind leprechauns around 40-50 and repeat fool's gold

claims.text: A Bishop can earn money by selling leech, killing monsters so low-level party members collect the exp; leech for low levels is the most in demand.
claims.say: bishops make good money selling leech, low level leech sells best

claims.text: A Fire/Poison mage paired with a Holy Symbol mule can also sell leech, starting at a lower level and needing less funding than a Bishop.
claims.say: f/p mage with a holy symbol mule can sell leech too

claims.text: Bowmasters are sought after in boss parties because Sharp Eyes is one of the strongest party damage buffs and their own damage is above average.
claims.say: bowmasters always get boss invites thanks to sharp eyes

claims.text: For a bossing Bowmaster, spend on HP washing toward 20k HP before top-end gear, since a Bowmaster you tire of still works as a Sharp Eyes mule.
claims.say: wash hp on your bowmaster before buying godly gear

claims.text: A Night Lord keeps getting stronger with every bit of extra attack on gear, and a high-range Night Lord is welcome in boss parties even without a Sharp Eyes mule.
claims.say: nl scales great with gear, high range nls get boss spots

claims.text: As a Pirate, max Somersault Kick first since it is the main attack until 3rd job, then Bullet Time for accuracy and avoid later, then Flash Fist, which is needed to advance. Dash and Double Shot are mostly filler.
claims.say: max somersault kick first, then bullet time and flash fist

claims.text: On becoming a Brawler, put the first ten skill points into Improve MaxHP before any new skill, so you build up as much HP as early as possible.
claims.say: brawlers max improve maxhp first before anything else

claims.text: After Improve MaxHP, take Knuckle Mastery and a few Knuckle Booster points, then max Corkscrew Blow, finish Knuckle Booster, then Backspin Blow, then Oak Barrel and MP Recovery. Double Uppercut goes last.
claims.say: mastery, corkscrew, booster, backspin; double uppercut last

claims.text: Corkscrew Blow works like a Rush that can also carry you up platforms and has an invincible frame while casting. Backspin Blow is a backwards rush that also stuns.
claims.say: corkscrew blow rushes up platforms, backspin goes back and stuns

claims.text: MP Recovery turns HP into MP and Energy Drain steals HP from a monster once your energy is fully charged; both are handy for the Mu Lung Dojo.
claims.say: mp recovery and energy drain are handy for dojo runs

claims.text: Marauders have two usual SP paths: max Shockwave first with one point in Transformation to start grinding sooner, or max Energy Charge and then Energy Blast, which is the stronger 3rd job skill.
claims.say: shockwave first to grind sooner, or charge into energy blast

claims.text: Energy Blast is useless until Energy Charge is maxed, because the charge bubble fills far too slowly before that.
claims.say: energy blast is pointless until energy charge is maxed

claims.text: If you plan to run Balrog, take the Energy Charge then Energy Blast build instead of Shockwave first; the author rates it clearly the better one for that boss.
claims.say: running balrog? max energy charge then energy blast

claims.text: Energy Blast can only be used while the Energy Charge bubble is active; when it is down you must attack with Somersault Kick to charge it again.
claims.say: energy blast needs the bubble up, kick to recharge it

claims.text: Transformation makes you faster and unlocks Shockwave, a slower but harder-hitting multi-target attack that hits more mobs than Energy Blast. Every Transformation cast uses up one Magic Rock.
claims.say: transformation eats a magic rock each cast, shockwave needs it
