claims.text: Demolition is a ranged single-target attack that hits eight times and needs Super Transformation; Barrage is a six-hit melee single-target attack with knockback. Both give invincible frames, so they can dodge hits.
claims.say: demolition is your best single target, barrage knocks back

claims.text: Dragon Strike is the strong multi-target attack, hitting up to six enemies at max level. Snatch also hits up to six and needs Super Transformation, but is weaker and pulls mobs and moving bosses toward you.
claims.say: snatch pulls mobs in, dragon strike hits harder on groups

claims.text: Time Leap resets the cooldowns of skills for everyone in the party, though not Time Leap itself. It does work on Echo of Hero, so you can keep refreshing Echo of Hero.
claims.say: time leap resets party cooldowns, even echo of hero

claims.text: Balanced 4th job SP: Super Transformation, Demolition and Speed Infusion first, then max Demolition and Barrage, then Dragon Strike, Maple Warrior and Time Leap, then Snatch and Hero's Will. Max Maple Warrior when you can afford it.
claims.say: 4th job: demo and si first, then barrage, dragon strike, mw

claims.text: Choose the combo by target count: Barrage plus Demolition for one target, Barrage plus Dragon Strike for exactly two targets that are not weapon cancelled, and Dragon Strike plus Snatch for three or more.
claims.say: 1 target barrage+demo, 2 barrage+ds, 3 or more ds+snatch

claims.text: Buccaneers put almost all AP in STR and only enough DEX for their knuckle: a Pirate needs at least 20 DEX to advance, King Cent wants 100 DEX and Dragon Slash Claw 110, so about 23 base DEX is a sensible start.
claims.say: str main, dex only for the knuckle, 100 dex for king cent

claims.text: Start with at least a 98 attack knuckle, then upgrade to one around 103 to 106 attack before saving for a perfect one.
claims.say: start with a 98 att knuckle, upgrade to 103-106 later

claims.text: King Cent or White Fangz are better knuckle picks than Dragon Slash Claw because they need less DEX and are more common.
claims.say: king cent or white fangz over dragon slash claw, less dex

claims.text: Prioritise the knuckle, the overall and attack gear (shoes, cape, glove) over multi-stat equips, and scroll untradeable pieces like helmet, rings, belt, earrings and eye or face accessories for DEX.
claims.say: knuckle and overall first, scroll untradeables for dex

claims.text: A good Mark of Naricain helps a Buccaneer much more than a Horntail Necklace, so start running Crimsonwood Keep early. Still keep a Horntail Necklace around for avoid or to wear your knuckle without proper DEX gear.
claims.say: mark of naricain beats horntail necklace for bucc

claims.text: A Buccaneer washes at a flat rate: each AP reset used as minus MP, plus HP removes 16 MP and adds 40 HP.
claims.say: bucc washes at -16 mp +40 hp per ap reset

claims.text: Do not wash with fresh level-up AP; wash with AP resets whenever you like, because fresh AP gives a random and lower average HP per point than the flat 40 from used AP.
claims.say: wash with ap resets, not fresh ap, for flat 40 hp

claims.text: Without funds to wash, put about 50 AP into INT early, wear cheap INT gear, and wash the INT and MP out much later; leveling on that base INT until 135 barely hurts damage.
claims.say: no wash funds? dump ~50 ap into int early, fix it later

claims.text: In the Crimsonwood Keep boss stage a Buccaneer can attack the mage boss with the single-target combo, or hit all three bottom bosses together with Snatch plus Dragon Strike.
claims.say: in cwk boss stage, snatch + dragon strike hits the 3 bottom bosses

claims.text: Against Horntail, hold Barrage plus Demolition through the pre-heads, and on the tail use Demolition from a distance, since you do not need to stand close.
claims.say: horntail pre-heads hold barrage+demo, tail use demolition from far

claims.text: On Horntail Head A and B, hop between the two heads: use Barrage plus Demolition to fill the charge, then Barrage plus Dragon Strike to hit both while neither head is weapon cancelled. Use wings or mobs to climb back up fast.
claims.say: horntail heads: charge with barrage+demo then ds both heads

claims.text: If another party holds Zakum in your channel, enter the first prequest stage through Adobis, relog into a new channel to land in that stage's exit room, then talk to Adobis there to go straight to the Zakum entrance.
claims.say: zak ch taken? enter stage 1, relog new ch, talk to adobis

claims.text: From Ariant town, head through the portals on the right and ride the camel taxi to reach Magatia right away.
claims.say: take the camel from ariant to get to magatia

claims.text: A rock at Eos Tower 56th Floor reaches two towns: a town scroll used there returns you to Ludibrium, while dropping one floor and using it sends you to Omega Sector.
claims.say: eos 56 returns to ludi, one floor down returns to omega

claims.text: In Leafre, Corba turns you into a dragon to fly to Temple of Time; holding jump speeds up the flight and holding down at the end takes the portal in.
claims.say: corba in leafre flies you to tot, hold jump to go faster

claims.text: Saving Top of Black Mountain, the far-right Korean Folk Town map, also covers Aqua Road, because the well in Korean Folk Town takes you there quickly.
claims.say: kft well is a fast way into aqua road

claims.text: Stairway to the Sky II, where Eliza spawns, is a convenient VIP rock spot for getting to Orbis.
claims.say: rock stairway to the sky 2 for quick orbis access

claims.text: A regular rock saved at the Crimsonwood Keep courtyard, where Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest starts, can be used from New Leaf City.
claims.say: save the cwk courtyard on a normal rock, use it from nlc

claims.text: Warped Path of Time <1> in the deep Ludibrium Clocktower has Buffy and Lazy Buffy.
claims.say: warped path of time 1 has buffys and lazy buffys

claims.text: Warped Path of Time <2> has Buffoon and Deep Buffoon.
claims.say: buffoons and deep buffoons are in warped path of time 2

claims.text: Warped Path of Time <3> has Ghost Pirates; a hidden portal at its top middle leads to Unbalanced Time, home of Dual Ghost Pirates.
claims.say: warped path 3: ghost pirates, top middle portal for dual ones

claims.text: Warped Path of Time <4> has Spirit Vikings; a hidden portal at its top left leads to Twisted Time with Gigantic Spirit Vikings.
claims.say: warped path 4: spirit vikings, top left portal for gigantic ones

claims.text: Forgotten Path of Time <1> has Soul Teddy and Master Soul Teddy.
claims.say: forgotten path of time 1 has soul teddys and master soul teddys

claims.text: Forgotten Path of Time <2> has Klock and Dark Klock.
claims.say: klocks and dark klocks are in forgotten path of time 2

claims.text: Forgotten Path of Time <3> has Death Teddies; the portal on its middle-right red platform leads to Lost Time with Master Death Teddies.
claims.say: forgotten path 3: death teddys, red platform portal to master ones

claims.text: Forgotten Path of Time <4> has Phantom Watches; the portal on its bottom red platform leads to Forbidden Time with Grim Phantom Watches.
claims.say: forgotten path 4: phantom watches, bottom portal to grim ones

claims.text: Steal works on any monster that is not boss-flagged. Each use takes either mesos or one item from its drop list; mesos can keep being taken, but after an item is taken that monster cannot be stolen from again.
claims.say: steal grabs mesos or one item off a non boss mob

claims.text: Steal forces one extra item out of a monster on top of its kill loot, but the item taken will not drop from that same monster again when it dies. It never takes duplicates of an item.
claims.say: steal adds a free drop, but that item wont drop again on death

claims.text: Steal still procs when the hit misses, so low accuracy or Darkness from blinding mobs does not stop it. You only lose the damage on that swing.
claims.say: steal still works on a miss, blind mobs dont stop it

claims.text: Anything on a monster's drop list can be stolen: equips, potions, scrolls, skillbooks, etc items, quest items and even its Monster Book card.
claims.say: steal can pull scrolls, quest items and cards off a live mob

claims.text: Stolen mesos are boosted by Meso Up and Taunt and can be blown up with Meso Explosion just like dropped or pickpocketed mesos.
claims.say: stolen mesos get meso up and can be exploded too

claims.text: Steal can take quest-only items from a living mob, giving one extra item per monster during collect quests. It helps most early on, before you can mob, and late game together with Taunt.
claims.say: use steal on collect quests, quest items can be stolen

claims.text: Steal works inside party quests and can take drops without killing the mob, such as door keys in the Pirate Party Quest and party potions in the Monster Carnival.
claims.say: you can steal pq keys and carnival pots without killing

claims.text: King Slime in the Kerning City Party Quest is not boss-flagged and has a tiny drop list, so a steal is guaranteed to give one of its few items on top of the kill drops.
claims.say: you can steal from king slime in kpq, tiny loot table

claims.text: For the best item odds, steal first and then Taunt: the steal forces one drop, then Taunt raises the rates for the rest of the loot. A strong pairing for rare card and quest hunts.
claims.say: steal first then taunt for best drop odds

claims.text: When item hunting with Steal and Taunt, put no points in Venomous Stab, because the poison damage drops weak mobs to 1 HP and leaves no room for extra steals.
claims.say: skip venomous stab if you farm drops with steal and taunt

claims.text: Voodoo has a small loot table, so Steal is a good way to chase Heartstopper and other sellable drops from them while also getting their normal kill loot.
claims.say: steal on voodoos for heartstoppers, small loot table

claims.text: Against fast-spawning mobs you can one-hit that have a large loot table, using Steal first costs extra swings and killing outright is often faster, so steal is not always worth using.
claims.say: steal isnt worth it on big loot mobs you one shot

claims.text: Crimson Guardian in Crimsonwood Keep has a small loot table, and stunned ones are easy to steal hearts from, which speeds up the party.
claims.say: steal hearts off stunned crimson guardians in cwk

claims.text: Shadower stuns from Boomerang Step and Assaulter give a safe window to land steals on the stunned mob.
claims.say: steal on mobs you just stunned with boomerang step

claims.text: A Steal plus Disorder macro lets you steal almost danger-free, since Disorder can de-aggro many mobs such as Imperial Guards and keep them off your back.
claims.say: macro steal with disorder to drop aggro while stealing

claims.text: Bandit second job order: max Dagger Mastery, Savage Blow and Haste, put a few points in Dagger Booster, then start Steal and raise Booster later. Maxing both Steal and Booster means skipping Endure.
claims.say: bandit sp: mastery, savage blow, haste, low booster, then steal

claims.text: If Steal was not maxed in second job, finish it in third job, where Pickpocket and Chakra often get skipped anyway.
claims.say: finish maxing steal in 3rd job if you skipped it before

claims.text: One build maxes Endure and Steal in second job by keeping Dagger Booster low until the end of third job, then maxes Chakra. Endure and Chakra both help you survive and recover in the Mu Lung Dojo.
claims.say: max endure and steal early, chakra later, good for dojo

claims.text: In the Ellin Forest chain Athena Pierce sends you to Shadrion, who wants 999 Tree Rods killed before you report back to her.
claims.say: shadrion wants 999 tree rods dead, then go back to athena

claims.text: Perzen asks for 200 Black Mushroom Spores during the Ellin Forest chain, while Lohd's side task of killing 999 Mossy Mushrooms is optional.
claims.say: perzen wants 200 black mushroom spores, lohd's kills are optional

claims.text: Sion passes you on to Rius, who needs 200 Rubble for the Ellin Forest chain.
claims.say: rius needs 200 rubble for the ellin chain

claims.text: The Ellin Forest chain opens with Yuris, Loha, Tess (snail shells), Loha again, Athena Pierce and Perzen, then continues with Yuris, Ellin (more shells) and Yuris once more.
claims.say: start at yuris, then loha, tess, loha, athena pierce and perzen

claims.text: A Bowmaster makes a good second attacker for any boss run, because Sharp Eyes helps the whole party.
claims.say: bm is a great alt attacker, sharp eyes helps any run

claims.text: A Bowmaster has a short buff routine, mostly Sharp Eyes and Soul Arrow, while Night Lords and warriors need a long chain of buffs.
claims.say: bm only needs sharp eyes and soul arrow, super easy to buff

claims.text: For raw damage Night Lord is the strongest second attacker; at bosses that need repositioning like Horntail, Hero or Paladin are easiest, then Shadower and Night Lord, and elsewhere Bowmaster is the least demanding.
claims.say: nl has the top dps, hero/pally are easiest at ht, bm elsewhere

claims.text: Before starting the Genesis quests, have a Mithril Plate and a Steel Plate ready for repairing the Cornian's Dagger.
claims.say: bring a mithril and steel plate before starting genesis

claims.text: A Dragon Elixir is what lets you into the Cave of Life, where the Life Root is found.
claims.say: need a dragon elixir to get into the cave of life

claims.text: Chief Tatamo's Moira's Whereabouts leads to Moira at Peak of the Big Nest, just outside the Horntail entrance, who gives Making the Secret Medicine for Transformation.
claims.say: tatamo sends you to moira near ht for the medicine quest

claims.text: For the Manon kill count you only need to be on the same map when Manon dies.
claims.say: just be on the map when manon dies to get credit

claims.text: Dark Cornians in The Burning Forest drop the Cornian's Marrow, Skull Shoulder Pad and Busted Dagger the medicine quest needs.
claims.say: dark cornians drop the marrow, skull pad and busted dagger

claims.text: Collect the 10 Tough Dragon Skin from the wyverns in the Leafre canyon maps.
claims.say: get your 10 tough dragon skins from wyverns

claims.text: Completing the medicine quest with Moira gives 2 Dragon Elixirs.
claims.say: moira gives 2 dragon elixirs when you finish

claims.text: The Horntail Party Quest needs at least 3 members, each with a Dragon Elixir; drink it to enter the Cave of Life, then talk to the NPC at the bottom to reach the second cave.
claims.say: htpq needs 3+, everyone drinks an elixir to get in

claims.text: Repeat until the Skelegon room gives a Red Key; the runners then come back and the leader talks to the NPC at the bottom right to move the whole party on.
claims.say: once the skelegons give the red key, leader talks bottom right

claims.text: In the next cave, hit the light flower bulb in the middle of the map once to open the entrance into a map full of Skelegons.
claims.say: hit the flower bulb in the middle once to open the way

claims.text: Skelegons in that last map drop the Life Root; bring one back to Shammos to learn Genesis.
claims.say: life root drops from the skelegons, give it to shammos

claims.text: Capt. Latanica is weak to Holy. He can inflict Weakness, heals himself, and summons Selkie Jr. and Mr. Anchor helpers.
claims.say: latanica is weak to holy, watch for weakness curse

claims.text: Capt. Latanica needs level 63 and Ralph the Wanderer's quests in Boat Quay Town: kill Pac Pinky and Slimy, then Slimy and Selkie Jr., then 300 Mr. Anchor, for a White Essence to drop at the Engine Room middle door.
claims.say: latanica: do ralphs quests at boat quay for a white essence

claims.text: The Papulatus clock is weak to Lightning and hides with invincible frames; it summons bombs, can dispel and uses 1/1. The real Papulatus is weak to Holy and has no special skills.
claims.say: papulatus clock hates lightning, real papulatus hates holy

claims.text: Margana, the mage boss in Crimsonwood Keep, is weak to Holy, zombifies and poisons, can raise Weapon Defense and casts pillars that block projectiles. Pin her top left and let a Bishop dispel the defense buff.
claims.say: pin margana top left, bishop dispels her wdef up

claims.text: Hsalf, the thief boss, is weak to Ice and has no special skills. Pin him bottom right, where his normal knockback already sends him.
claims.say: hsalf is weak to ice, pin him bottom right

claims.text: Red Nirg, the warrior boss, is weak to Lightning, stuns, uses super knockback and summons Stormbreakers, Windraiders, Firebrand and Nightshadow. Pin him bottom right, let a tank touch him, and use Holy Shield against debuffs.
claims.say: red nirg weak to lightning, tank touch and holy shield

claims.text: Each Crimsonwood Keep boss drops one untradeable Mark of Naricain. The bonus room adds Naricain's Demon Elixir, Ssiws Cheese, Gelt Chocolate and Banana Graham Pie.
claims.say: cwk bosses drop mark of naricain, one per boss

claims.text: Scarlion is weak to Fire and Targa to Ice. Both knock you far, cancel weapon and magic damage, and summon helpers (Scaredy Scarlions and Ratatulas); Targa also stuns and is invincible while dashing.
claims.say: scarlion weak to fire, targa weak to ice

claims.text: Scarlion and Targa need level 90 and Lam's quests in Kampung Village: Busticket from Yabber Doo, 200 Viking Helmets from Vikerola, 200 Toy Planes from Booper Scarlion, 200 Wooden Pony Tails from Galloperas, and items from Rodeoos.
claims.say: scarlion/targa quest: lam at kampung village, lv 90

claims.text: Zakum's eight arms come in pairs by weakness: two are weak to Holy, two to Ice, two to Fire and two to Lightning.
claims.say: zakum arms: 2 each weak to holy, ice, fire and lightning

claims.text: Zakum's body forms differ by weakness: the first is weak to Lightning, the second to Ice and the third to Fire. All of them use 1/1, stun, seal, weapon cancel and magic cancel.
claims.say: zakum body weak to lightning, then ice, then fire

claims.text: Among Zakum's arms, one buffs attack and defense and heals the others in an area, one seals, blinds, weakens and curses you, and one lays poison mist, and two drain HP and MP.
claims.say: zakum arms: one heals and buffs, one seals and curses

claims.text: Zakum's quest starts with Adobis at the Door to Zakum at level 50: collect 7 keys from rooms 4-2, 9-2, 11-1, 14-1, 16-2, 16-3 and 16-5, drop them in the big chest in 16-5, then take the Piece of Fire Ore to Aura for a Fire Ore.
claims.say: zakum quest part 1: 7 keys to the 16-5 chest, fire ore from aura

claims.text: Start Zakum by talking to Adobis at the Entrance to Zakum Altar and dropping an Eye of Fire on the altar in the middle of the map. Zakum drops Zakum Helmets.
claims.say: drop an eye of fire on the altar to start zakum

claims.text: In Horntail's head map, the first player in is the Seduce target, which will be the expedition leader. Do not move until everyone is in, since moving can start the battle and lock the map. Dark Wyverns can dispel.
claims.say: horntail: leader gets seduced, wait till all are in the map

claims.text: Horntail weak points: legs and tail are weak to Holy, wings to Ice; left head and left hand to Lightning, right head and right hand to Fire; Head A to Lightning and Head B to Ice.
claims.say: horntail: legs and tail holy, wings ice, head a lightning

claims.text: While fighting Horntail's tail, never touch it, and avoid crossing to the right side of the map, which triggers the right hand's seduce timer.
claims.say: dont touch horntails tail or cross right, it triggers seduce

claims.text: Horntail's hand skills (besides seduce) only affect you on their own side of the map: the left hand on the left, the right hand on the right. Each hand gives a warning message at low HP before its mass seduce.
claims.say: horntail hand debuffs only hit you on their own side

claims.text: Horntail's wings buff attack, heal an area, and summon Green then Dark Cornians as their HP drops. They are weak to Ice.
claims.say: horntail wings heal and summon cornians, hit with ice

claims.text: Seduce locks potion use and movement and forces you to walk left or right or jump; Confusion reverses your movement; Stun briefly disables movement and skills.
claims.say: seduce locks potions and forces you to walk, confusion flips keys

claims.text: Zombify halves the effect of HP and MP potions and makes a Bishop's Heal damage you; Curse lowers exp gain; Poison and Bleed damage you every second.
claims.say: zombify halves potions and bishop heals hurt you

claims.text: Seal locks your skills, Weakness locks jumping, Darkness lowers your accuracy and Slow cuts your movement speed.
claims.say: seal stops skills, weakness stops jumping, darkness lowers acc

claims.text: A boss with Weapon Cancel takes only 1 damage from weapon attacks and one with Magic Cancel takes 1 from magic, so wait or use the other damage type until it ends.
claims.say: weapon cancel makes physical hits do 1, use magic until it drops

claims.text: On bosses where you keep dismounting, summon a maxed Octopus right after each dismount and then remount. Octopus out-damages the few Rapid Fire shots you could fit in that gap; use Rapid Fire only while Octopus is on cooldown.
claims.say: summon octopus after dismounting, then remount. rapid fire if on cd

claims.text: On bosses that drain MP or use 1/1 attacks, use potions that restore both HP and MP, like Elixir or Power Elixir. Pets burn HP potions first, so with an HP-only potion you may lack the mana to remount Battleship right away.
claims.say: bring elixirs or power elixirs so u always have mp to remount

claims.text: When a boss 1/1s you while mounted, Battleship soaks damage equal to the HP you had. Keep your HP only a little above the biggest unavoidable hit, using low-HP potions, so a late dismount cannot cost the ship a full health bar.
claims.say: keep hp just over the boss's max hit so 1/1 cant wreck ur ship

claims.text: At Horntail's legs a Corsair should not keep remounting. Tank the falling rock on the ship instead: it does little damage and avoids most stuns, and the ship usually lasts about as long as the legs.
claims.say: ht legs: tank the falling rock on ur ship, dont keep remounting

claims.text: If Battleship still has HP when Horntail's legs die, let the tail break it. You want the ship's cooldown back, and you should not be mounted during the tail anyway.
claims.say: let the ship break after ht legs so the cd comes back

claims.text: Horntail's arms hit a Corsair and the ship for only 1 damage, and just one arm can reach you at a time. You can usually skip remounting for an arm hit unless you need to reposition after the next attack.
claims.say: ht arms only do 1 dmg so u dont need to dismount for them

claims.text: Attack Horntail's right head (Head C) from the top platform. Octopus can reach it there, Head A's and Head B's 1/1 attacks cannot reach that height, buffs are easier to receive, and wyverns rarely fly up.
claims.say: hit ht's right head from the top platform, a and b 1/1s cant reach

claims.text: Head C's Thunderbolt has no delay, so remount the moment you see it; its Lightning Breath is slow, so fire two more shots first. Its 1/1 lightning falls vertically and can reach the top platform.
claims.say: head c thunderbolt = remount asap, its breath is slow

claims.text: Against Head A, watch your own character's head: dismount only when an icicle lands on it. Icy Breath only hits the ground and the look-alike 1/1 ice strike cannot reach the top platform, so ignore those.
claims.say: vs head a only dismount if an icicle shows on ur own head

claims.text: Horntail's Head B raises its head slowly to cast Fire Breath, which leaves time for about three more attacks before you remount.
claims.say: head b fire breath is slow, get 3 more hits in before remounting

claims.text: Head B's Fire Splash hits the whole map and looks like its ground-only 1/1 Fire Tomb. Remount unless fire tombs show up on the ground platform on your mule's screen; if they do, it is the harmless one.
claims.say: no fire tombs on mule's ground = fire splash, remount

claims.text: Skip Octopus on Head B: you would have to stand close for it to attack, and if you get knocked out of range it stops hitting.
claims.say: skip octopus on head b, u cant stay in range

claims.text: Bring a second character as a mule on the bottom platform and watch its screen at Horntail. It shows where 1/1 tombstones and fire tombs land, so you only dismount when one lands on your own spot.
claims.say: put a mule on the bottom platform to see where 1/1s land

claims.text: On Horntail's left prehead, Icy Breath has a long cast delay, so fire two more cannons before remounting. It knocks you far left, so use Recoil Shot to reposition instead of walking back.
claims.say: left prehead icy breath is slow, 2 more cannons then remount

claims.text: On the right prehead, Lightning Strike and 1/1 Thunder look the same. If your mule's screen shows no tombstone at your spot, it is Lightning Strike with a one-second delay, so remount at once.
claims.say: right prehead: no tombstone at ur spot = lightning strike, remount

claims.text: When seduced or stunned you cannot press skills, so the only way off Battleship is right-clicking its buff icon. Keep your mouse near the icon and dismount immediately, or the ship soaks the damage.
claims.say: when seduced right click the battleship icon to dismount

claims.text: When an arm attack lands together with a head attack at Horntail, remount if you see Head A's icicle, a 1/1 icicle at your spot, or Head C casting anything but Breath of Lightning. Ignore it if Head B is the one casting.
claims.say: arm + head together: remount for a's icicle or c, not for b

claims.text: Bodyguard A's cast does only 1 damage to a Corsair, so you need not remount if your party pins it well; stay far enough away and its attack will not reach you at all.
claims.say: bodyguard a only does 1 dmg to ur ship if pinned, no remount

claims.text: Bodyguard B has an annoying invincibility frame and very high touch damage. Its only skill is an MP suck that does 1 damage to the ship, so no remount is needed.
claims.say: bodyguard b only mp sucks for 1 dmg, no remount needed

claims.text: The author recommends a pure INT magician: every AP goes into INT, which raises magic attack and max MP, so damage and mana beat a LUK mage.
claims.say: go pure int on a mage, more damage and more mp than luk

claims.text: Pure INT is also cheaper to gear: boosting a Bathrobe with INT scrolls costs far less than the LUK gear a LUK mage wants.
claims.say: pure int is cheap, just scroll a bathrobe with int

claims.text: A Wooden Wand is the first weapon to use at level 8.
claims.say: grab a wooden wand at level 8

claims.text: An optional level 25 cape, the Old Raggedy Cape, is a reward from the quest Stranger's Request.
claims.say: stranger's request in kerning gives a cape at 25

claims.text: To meet the brush's STR need, add a few STR (removed later with an AP Reset) or wear STR items such as Squishy Shoes from King Slime in Kerning City Party Quest or Spiegelmann's Necklace from Monster Carnival.
claims.say: for the str use squishy shoes from kpq or spiegelmann necklace

claims.text: Later weapons: Maple Staff at 35, Maple Lama Staff at 43, then Maple Wisdom Staff or Maple Shine Wand at 64.
claims.say: maple staff 35, lama staff 43, wisdom staff or shine wand 64

claims.text: From level 70 elemental mages use Elemental Wand 1-4 and from 130 Elemental Wand 5-8, picking the color of their element: purple for poison, blue for ice, red for fire, yellow for lightning.
claims.say: use the elemental wand of your element, red fire blue ice etc

claims.text: At the level 8 job advancement, put the first skill point into Energy Bolt.
claims.say: first sp at 8 goes into energy bolt

claims.text: Over levels 9 and 10 put five points into Improved MP Recovery and one into Improved Max MP Increase, then max Improved Max MP Increase by about level 13.
claims.say: then mp recovery and max out improved max mp increase by 13

claims.text: From level 14 to 20 max Magic Claw, the main attack.
claims.say: max magic claw from 14 to 20

claims.text: From level 21 to 30 spend points on Magic Guard and the rest of Improved MP Recovery.
claims.say: 21 to 30 magic guard and the rest into mp recovery

claims.text: Stay on Maple Island until level 8 with all AP in INT, which gives about 48 INT when you advance.
claims.say: stay on maple island till 8, all ap in int

claims.text: The Magician job advancement is done with Grendel the Really Old at the top of Ellinia.
claims.say: grendel at the top of ellinia gives the mage job

claims.text: After leaving Maple Island you arrive at Lith Harbor, where the taxi driver Phil can take you to Ellinia.
claims.say: phil the taxi in lith harbor takes you to ellinia

claims.text: Olaf's quiz quests in Lith Harbor are well worth doing between levels 8 and 14.
claims.say: do olaf's quiz quests in lith harbor early

claims.text: Henesys Hunting Ground suits a new magician at levels 15-17.
claims.say: henesys hunting ground is good at 15 to 17

claims.text: In Nautilus, The Prince's Request (bring one Mana Elixir) and Shining Stone (touch the stone in the Generator Room) are easy optional quests for levels 14-20.
claims.say: in nautilus do the prince's request and shining stone

claims.text: Train at the Ant Tunnel from about level 17 to 24.
claims.say: ant tunnel is the spot from 17 to 24

claims.text: At level 25 do Stranger's Request and then Stranger's Identity at Niora Hospital in Kerning City.
claims.say: at 25 do stranger's request then stranger's identity in kerning

claims.text: From 25 to 30 train on Wild Boars for the best mesos, at the Ant Tunnel with a party, or in Kerning City Party Quest.
claims.say: 25 to 30 hit wild boars for mesos or do kpq

claims.text: Jane and the Wild Boar, taken in Lith Harbor, adds exp while you train on boars in the mid 20s.
claims.say: do jane and the wild boar quest from lith harbor

claims.text: POLLUTED <1-Evil Eye>, done at The Cave of Evil Eye I, is another exp quest for levels 25-30.
claims.say: the polluted evil eye quest is good exp in the late 20s

claims.text: Bored of Genin around 35-40, a Cleric can switch to Jr. Wraiths, attacking with Heal once it reaches level 15.
claims.say: clerics can heal jr wraiths from 35 once heal is 15

claims.text: Ice/Lightning mages around 35-40 can move to Lorang with Thunder Bolt at level 15, or any map with good mob density.
claims.say: il can thunder bolt lorangs from 35 at level 15

claims.text: From 40 to 50 Clerics do well on Wraiths or Master Chronos.
claims.say: clerics do wraiths or master chronos from 40 to 50

claims.text: Truckers are another option for Ice/Lightning mages at 40-50, though the author finds them slower.
claims.say: truckers work for il too but kinda slow

claims.text: From 50 to 70 Clerics can train on Coolie Zombies for more mesos or at Mysterious Path 3 for more exp.
claims.say: clerics 50 to 70 coolies for mesos, mysterious path 3 for exp

claims.text: Nightghosts are weak to both lightning and Heal, so Clerics and Ice/Lightning mages can farm them for Cape INT 60% scrolls.
claims.say: nightghosts are weak to lightning and heal, drop cape int scrolls

claims.text: For an Islander, DEX matters most because it lifts the minimum damage per hit, bringing you closer to one-shotting Maple Island monsters.
claims.say: islanders want dex, it raises your minimum damage

claims.text: Outland permabeginners usually pump STR, sometimes with DEX for accuracy, and use polearms, swords or daggers. Their max HP is very low, and basic attacks eventually cannot keep up with monsters of their own level.
claims.say: perma beginners go str, a bit of dex for accuracy

claims.text: A permawarrior stays a first job Warrior, relying on Power Strike and Slash Blast for offence and Improved MaxHP Increase and Iron Body for defence. It can use polearms, swords, axes, blunt weapons and even daggers.
claims.say: permawarriors use power strike and slash blast, any weapon type

claims.text: An HP warrior adds only enough STR to advance, waits until Improved MaxHP Increase is maxed, then puts every AP into MaxHP, which can reach the 30k HP cap around levels 90 to 100.
claims.say: hp warrior: just enough str to advance, all ap to maxhp

claims.text: HP warriors kill by touching enemies with Power Guard, so they go Fighter or Page rather than Spearman, and keep their WDEF as low as they can; Rage's debuff helps. They can fight most enemies by level 41 or so.
claims.say: hp warriors use power guard, go fighter or page not spearman

claims.text: Warriors can wear thief daggers that only need STR and DEX, so a dagger warrior is possible. It keeps Power Strike and Slash Blast, but later jobs add Rage, Threaten, Hyper Body, Berserk, Shout and especially Combo Attack.
claims.say: warriors can use str/dex daggers, fighter line gets combo attack

claims.text: Dagger warriors normally go Fighter, Crusader, Hero for Combo Attack, and cannot use Dragon Roar. With just enough DEX to wield the dagger and the rest in STR they are among the strongest odd jobs for raw DPS.
claims.say: dagger warrior: fighter-crusader-hero, str with min dex

claims.text: A DEX warrior keeps 35 STR to advance and puts every other AP into DEX, trading a lot of damage for superb accuracy, stable damage and extra avoidability, and can wield the Stonetooth Sword.
claims.say: dex warriors give up damage for accuracy and avoidability

claims.text: A permamagician relies on Magic Claw and Energy Bolt, with Magic Guard, Magic Armor and Improved MaxMP Increase for defence. It is fairly durable but has no multi-target attacks and no Teleport, and is elementally neutral.
claims.say: permamagicians use magic claw and magic guard, no teleport

claims.text: A STR mage fights by basic attacking in melee, with Magic Guard and Magic Armor for durability, Teleport for hit-and-run, and weapons like the Fusion Mace. Common paths are cleric, priest, bishop or fire/poison.
claims.say: str mage melees, teleports in, usual paths bishop or f/p

claims.text: A STR fire/poison mage still gets Poison Mist, whose lingering cloud ignores magic accuracy, so it can poison any non-boss monster even without INT or LUK. Slow and Seal are available too.
claims.say: poison mist ignores macc so str f/p can still poison mobs

claims.text: A STR Bishop is very durable and still brings Bless, Holy Symbol, Doom, Dispel and Resurrection, using Heal only defensively.
claims.say: str bishop is tanky and still gives bless, holy symbol, doom

claims.text: A magelet is a pure LUK mage. It keeps normal magic accuracy so all its skills work, and excels at avoidability, claw damage and weapon accuracy. Poison skills ignore its magic attack, and Heal damage scales with LUK.
claims.say: magelet: pure luk mage, uses claws, poison skills fine

claims.text: A gish splits AP across STR, DEX, INT and LUK to use both physical and magic attacks without swapping gear, favouring items with both bonuses like Crimson Arcglaive, Flamekeeper Cordon and Kebob. It is a very hard build.
claims.say: gish mixes str/dex and int/luk, hard to build right

claims.text: A permarcher relies on Critical Shot with Double Shot or Arrow Blow. With only Focus for avoidability and no second job max HP bonus it is fragile and single-target, but hits hard for an odd job. Crossbows edge out bows.
claims.say: permarchers hit hard on one target but are very fragile

claims.text: A woodsman is a pure STR archer who basic-attacks in melee and still shoots, using Silver Hawk, Frostprey, Sharp Eyes, Focus and The Blessing of Amazon. Gear is hard without DEX; Maple weapons and the Bow of Magical Destruction help.
claims.say: str archers melee and shoot, maple bows help the dex gap

claims.text: Some say crossbow users make better woodsmen thanks to Snipe, but both bow and crossbow users make strong ones.
claims.say: crossbow woodsmen get snipe, but bows work fine too

claims.text: A bow-whacker never shoots arrows and uses Power Knock-Back, which scales on DEX then STR like a normal archer's AP build. It hits up to six monsters but gets no Bow Mastery or Critical Shot crits; Sharp Eyes still works.
claims.say: bow-whackers use power knock-back, dex main, hits six mobs

claims.text: A permarogue mixes ranged claw Lucky Seven with dagger Double Stab; thanks to Lucky Seven's built-in mastery it is the strongest perma-first for single-target damage. It can attack in mid-air but is fragile with no max HP bonus.
claims.say: permarogue lucky seven is the best single target perma-first

claims.text: A brigand is a LUKless bandit that avoids daggers and plays like a STR beginner with polearms or swords, but gains Disorder, Steal, Meso Explosion, Dark Sight, Haste and Meso Guard, making it far sturdier than a permabeginner.
claims.say: brigand = luckless non-dagger bandit, meso guard keeps it tanky

claims.text: A LUKless assassin puts AP into STR and DEX and uses claws like Maple claws or Shinobi Bracers. Shadow Meso ignores stats and Claw Mastery, making LUKless hermits top single-target odd jobs; Avenger handles mobbing.
claims.say: luckless hermit: shadow meso ignores stats, strong single target

claims.text: A LUKless bandit adds just enough STR to wield a dagger and puts the rest in DEX, since STR and DEX add equally to damage and DEX also gives accuracy and avoidability. With high Dagger Mastery, Savage Blow damage is nearly constant.
claims.say: luckless dit: min str for dagger, rest dex, steady savage blow

claims.text: A blood bandit adds only enough DEX to advance and puts every AP into MaxHP; with Meso Guard it is nearly unkillable. Meso Explosion ignores stats but costs a lot of mesos, and it can fight almost anything by level 70 to 80.
claims.say: blood bandit: all ap to maxhp, meso guard, meso explosion

claims.text: A permapirate uses Somersault Kick and Flash Fist for melee and Double Shot at range; STR suits the melee skills and DEX suits Double Shot, so most specialise. It is mobile with Dash but fragile, with only Bullet Time for avoidability.
claims.say: permapirates pick str for kicks and fists or dex for double shot

claims.text: A DEX brawler dumps all AP into DEX. Brawlers gain extra avoidability per DEX, so they can hit the avoidability cap, and they have the highest accuracy of any odd job, though they deal far less damage than a normal one.
claims.say: dex brawlers hit the avoid cap but deal far less damage

claims.text: Guild PQ starts in Perion at the Excavation Site camp. The guild's Jr. Master talks to Shuang to begin it, then everyone talks to Shuang again to enter the waiting area before the portal opens.
claims.say: gpq starts in perion, jr master talks to shuang first

claims.text: Guild PQ needs at least 6 players, all from the same guild but not necessarily in one party. If fewer than 6 are in the run it fails and everyone is warped out. The waiting area gives 3 minutes.
claims.say: need 6 guildmates minimum or the run fails and warps you out

claims.text: Bring a Jr. Master, a low-level attacker, a mage with at least Teleport level 1, a thief with Dark Sight and max Haste, and an area or ranged attacker. One character can fill several of these roles.
claims.say: gpq needs a jr master, low lvl attacker, a mage and a thief

claims.text: The low-level attacker (level 10-30) must kill 20 mobs and do a jump quest. A level 25-30 magician is the best pick since it never has accuracy problems and can Teleport, so it can also be the Teleport mage.
claims.say: use a lvl 25-30 mage as the low level attacker, teleport helps

claims.text: Dying in Guild PQ does not fail the run, but you lose exp (and a Safety Charm if you carry one) and have to walk back from the first map.
claims.say: dying in gpq just walks you back from map 1 but costs exp

claims.text: The statue stage is a memory game: statues light up in a sequence of 4, then 5, then 6. The Jr. Master starts each round through the NPC, and one player on each side calls their statues in party chat so both hit them in order.
claims.say: statues is a memory game, 4 then 5 then 6 in order

claims.text: One mistake in the statue stage sends you back to the 4-statue round, but there is no limit on attempts. Everyone else should wait quietly in the middle so the two callers can focus.
claims.say: one miss resets statues to round 1, stay quiet in the middle

claims.text: Avoid long weapons such as spears or two-handed swords when hitting the statues, because the extra reach can hit the wrong statue.
claims.say: dont use spear or 2h sword on statues, they hit the wrong one

claims.text: The spear stage needs 4 Longinus Spears, each locked behind jump quests or a mage and thief puzzle, which are then placed in the Room of Justice. A player can only hold one spear at a time.
claims.say: grab 4 longinus spears, only carry one at a time

claims.text: In the spear jump quest rooms, climb to the top, auto-attack the spear to break its chains, then press jump while looting it to get it into your inventory.
claims.say: attack the spear to unchain it then jump while looting

claims.text: In the first mage/thief room, kill the Muscle Stones to get a key and drop it in front of the sealed door. A mage is best at this because it can mob them.
claims.say: kill muscle stones for the key, mage does it best

claims.text: The thief should recast Dark Sight before walking back out of the room with the spear.
claims.say: recast dark sight before you leave with the spear

claims.text: Placing the spears means four more jump quests in a row, one needing Haste or Teleport and one needing Teleport. Use a short o/x code in party chat to show which of the four are already done.
claims.say: tell your party which spear jqs are done with an o/x code

claims.text: The Fountain of the Wiseman stage is a Mastermind code puzzle: four statues each get one offering from Medal, Scroll, Wine and Food, repeats allowed. The Jr. Master can check the combination 7 times.
claims.say: fountain stage is mastermind with medal, scroll, wine, food

claims.text: Each check reports offerings that are right and in place (Pleased), right type in the wrong place (Incorrect Offering), or not in the code (Unknown Offering). After 7 failed checks mobs spawn and you restart with a new code.
claims.say: pleased = right spot, incorrect = wrong spot, unknown = not in code

claims.text: Loot the Scroll and Medal drops before you enter a Wine or Food room, or they despawn and the PQ fails. Only the player who looted an offering can pick it up again after dropping it.
claims.say: loot scroll and medal drops before the wine and food rooms

claims.text: If the statues keep saying only one offering per statue, an invisible event drop that fell for whoever made the kill is in the way. Loot all medals and scrolls, enter a Wine or Food room, and come back to clear it.
claims.say: got a one offering error? enter a wine or food room and come back

claims.text: The Waterway Maze has four ETCs (shoes, pants, top, hat), each behind its own jump quest, reached through teleporting platforms. With max Haste or Jump you can hop straight onto the right platforms.
claims.say: waterway maze has 4 etcs, grab each before the exit

claims.text: Get each maze ETC before taking its exit, because you cannot go back to a jump quest afterwards, except by taking off your earrings, dying and walking back.
claims.say: cant go back to a maze jq, so get the etc before leaving

claims.text: The shoes jump quest can be done by anyone and movement skills are allowed. Go left to right, up the ladder, right to left, then left to right to hit the box for the shoes. Jump down the second part to leave.
claims.say: shoes jq is easy and skills are allowed

claims.text: Players too weak for the boss fight can stay on the left or slip through the crack in the middle pillar to a safe observation spot.
claims.say: weak chars can hide in the crack of the middle pillar

claims.text: Hit the Rubian on the throne to spawn Ergoth. He uses Weapon Cancel and Magic Cancel, though an all-ranged party avoids it. His four statues use 1/1, Curse and Dispel, and you don't have to kill them to move on.
claims.say: hit the rubian on the throne to spawn ergoth

claims.text: Ergoth drops the Rubian ETC. The Jr. Master must loot it and finish the dialogue with the NPC on the left to be teleported to the bonus stage.
claims.say: jr master loots the rubian and talks to the left npc for bonus

claims.text: Do not use Meso Explosion on Ergoth, since it can blow up or bug the ETC he drops, which you need to reach the bonus room and could ruin the run.
claims.say: dont use meso explosion on ergoth, it bugs the drop

claims.text: The bonus room has boxes far apart and little time. Haste is essential, Teleport or Flash Jump is recommended, and pet loot should be on. A mage with Teleport reliably opens 6-7 boxes, and 5 or more players open the most.
claims.say: bonus room needs haste, teleport or flash jump and pet loot

claims.text: Where a Priest or Bishop's Mystic Door shows up in town depends on their party slot, which is set by the order they joined; the party leader or a caster with no party gets the first spot.
claims.say: door spot in town depends on when the priest joined the party

claims.text: The town end of the door stays on the slot the caster got when joining, so it does not shift to a new spot if another member leaves the party later.
claims.say: door wont move if someone leaves, it keeps the join slot

claims.text: For Horntail runs, have the Bishop create the party so the door lands in the middle of Leafre rather than off to one side.
claims.say: have the bishop make the ht party so door is mid leafre

claims.text: Before Power Knock-Back is leveled, from the 20s to the mid 30s, an archer can train at Ant Tunnel I, Ant Tunnel IV and Deep Ant Tunnel II.
claims.say: 20s to mid 30s archers can grind ant tunnel i, iv or deep ii

claims.text: From the mid 30s into the 40s, The Cave of Evil Eye II is a strong grinding map for a Hunter.
claims.say: mid 30s to 40s hunters do great in evil eye cave ii

claims.text: The Cave of Evil Eye II has two Jr. Boogie spawn points, and both have sniping spots where the Jr. Boogie cannot reach you in melee.
claims.say: evil eye ii has safe spots to snipe jr boogie

claims.text: Hunter order for dense spawns: 1 point in Arrow Bomb : Bow at 30, Bow Mastery to 9 by 33, then max Power Knock-Back by 40 before putting more into Arrow Bomb : Bow.
claims.say: 30-40: arrow bomb 1, mastery 9, then max power knock-back

claims.text: Power Knock-Back comes first because the Evil Eye cave spawns are dense, and without it you end up hitting mobs with your bow in melee all the time.
claims.say: power knock-back keeps evil eyes off you, level it first

claims.text: Bowmen's long range and high accuracy make them good at fighting hard-to-hit monsters like Jr. Boogie.
claims.say: archers have the accuracy to hit jr boogies

claims.text: A normal STR and DEX build is recommended so you can wear more equipment; pure DEX is possible but leaves you on weak bows for longer.
claims.say: go normal str/dex so you can wear better bows

claims.text: A monster's card set is complete at five cards. The monster book counts a monster once you own a single card, so its basic-card total overstates finished sets; boss cards are listed separately as special cards.
claims.say: a card set needs 5 cards, one card only counts as basic

claims.text: Finish an area's quests before card hunting there, since many quests need kills while the quest is active and you collect cards along the way.
claims.say: do an area's kill quests first, cards drop while you do them

claims.text: Around 60 card sets come from party content you can't solo, and Lycanthrope and the area bosses are among the slowest sets to finish.
claims.say: lycanthrope and area boss cards take forever

claims.text: Ranged classes can collect Firebomb cards in the Zakum jump quest.
claims.say: ranged can farm firebomb cards in the zakum jump quest

claims.text: Doing the Maple Island quests in a fixed efficient order lets you finish all of them by level 10 and reach level 11 right at the first job advancement without wasting skill points.
claims.say: do maple island quests in a good order and you hit 11 at job adv

claims.text: For Todd's How-To-Hunt kill a Tutorial Drumming Rabbit for a Toy Drum and a Tutorial Leatty for Leatty's Hairball, then turn it in to Peter. That gets you to level 2.
claims.say: todd's quest needs a toy drum and a leatty hairball, hand in to peter

claims.text: Your first three skill points on Maple Island, from levels 2 to 4, all go into Nimble Feet, which helps with running around the quest maps.
claims.say: put your first 3 sp into nimble feet

claims.text: Robin the Walking Encyclopedia starts as soon as you enter Snail Hunting Ground I; picking dialogue options 2, 2 and 4 completes it and takes you to level 3.
claims.say: robin's quiz answers are 2, 2, 4

claims.text: Sam gives Love Counseling and Help Hunt the Snails. Kill 10 Snails on the way right, then report to Maria at the split road, who then opens Letter for Lucas, Maria's Nutritious Juice and Maria's Map Reading.
claims.say: sam gives two quests, kill 10 snails then see maria

claims.text: Finish Love Counseling on the way to Southperry by killing Stumps until you have 3 Tree Branches, then hand them to Bari.
claims.say: get 3 tree branches off stumps and give them to bari

claims.text: Break the wooden boxes you pass on Maple Island: each gives Old Wooden Boards and Rusty Screws, and Pio's recycling quests in Amherst want 10 of each.
claims.say: smash the wooden boxes for pio's boards and screws

claims.text: Rain's Maple Quiz in Amherst is passed by choosing options 1, 1, 1, 4, 2, 3 and 1 in order.
claims.say: rain's maple quiz answers: 1,1,1,4,2,3,1

claims.text: On Maple Island, changing channels usually drops you at the far left of a map, which is a quick way to backtrack between quest NPCs.
claims.say: change channel to get put back at the left of the map

claims.text: In the field east of Amherst, Mai's trainings ask in turn for Stumps and Tree Branches, 10 Red Snail Shells, Slimes plus Squishy Liquid, and finally Pigs. Doing them in one go takes you to level 8.
claims.say: mai's four trainings take you from 6 to 8 on the east field

claims.text: Bari's Test, taken after the juice delivery starts, needs 2 Orange Mushroom Caps from the mushrooms near Southperry.
claims.say: bari's test just needs 2 orange mushroom caps

claims.text: Back in the field west of Amherst, finish Helping out Yoona with 15 Mushroom Spores plus the leftover Snail Shells and kills of Snails and 10 Blue Snails; this gets you to level 9.
claims.say: yoona's quest wants 15 mushroom spores and snail kills, gets you 9

claims.text: Biggs, up the first ladder in Southperry, gives Here Little Piggy and Biggs Collection of Items; hand them in later on your way out and he starts Biggs Story on Victoria Island.
claims.say: biggs in southperry gives two quests, hand both in later

claims.text: Archers can restock arrows quickly from almost any town: ask Spinel for Mushroom Shrine, drink Fruit Milk to reach Showa, take the portal into the marketplace and buy from the grocer at the far left.
claims.say: spinel to mushroom shrine, fruit milk, then the showa grocer

claims.text: After shopping, drink Strawberry Milk to return to Mushroom Shrine, then talk to Spinel to go back to where you started.
claims.say: drink strawberry milk to go back, then spinel home

claims.text: Get the teleport milks once from the vendor inside the Showa bathhouse, entered through Hikari, or buy them from other players.
claims.say: buy the teleport milks in the showa bathhouse once

claims.text: Bowmasters and Marksmen should boss with real arrows rather than Soul Arrow, since Soul Arrow throws away the weapon attack the arrows add.
claims.say: use real arrows not soul arrow when bossing

claims.text: For a beginner who stays on Maple Island, DEX raises minimum damage fastest because beginners have almost no weapon mastery. STR mostly lifts the top end of the damage range.
claims.say: on a beginner dex lifts your min dmg, str mostly your max

claims.text: Max damage is about (STR times the weapon multiplier plus DEX) times weapon attack divided by 100. Min damage uses only 90 percent of the STR part scaled by mastery, so DEX and weapon attack dominate it.
claims.say: max dmg = (str*mult + dex)*watk/100, min leans on dex and watk

claims.text: Weapon multipliers: one-handed sword and dagger 4, two-handed sword 4.6, spear 5 on a stab but 3 on a swing, polearm the reverse. Use the lowest multiplier when working out min damage and the highest for max damage.
claims.say: spears hit harder on stab, polearms on swing, 1h swords are a flat 4

claims.text: Avoidability is roughly half your LUK plus a quarter of your DEX, so LUK is the stat to stack if you want monsters to miss you.
claims.say: avoid is luk/2 + dex/4, so luk is what makes mobs miss

claims.text: Your chance to dodge a monster is about your avoid divided by 4.5 times that monster's accuracy, and the beginner job tops out at an 80 percent dodge chance.
claims.say: dodge chance is avoid / (4.5 x mob accuracy), beginners cap at 80%

claims.text: Around 30 weapon defense is enough to cut hits from the toughest Maple Island mobs, like Orange Mushrooms and Pigs, down to 1 damage. Ordinary starter-island clothing and hats can reach that.
claims.say: about 30 wdef makes orange mushrooms and pigs hit you for 1

claims.text: Movement is capped at 140 percent speed and 123 percent jump, so gear that adds speed or jump stops helping once you hit those caps.
claims.say: speed caps at 140 and jump at 123, extra past that is wasted

claims.text: Maximum jump is not always best: on maps with platforms close together, time spent in the air is wasted, so a bit less jump can train faster.
claims.say: max jump can actually slow you down on maps with tight platforms

claims.text: A sensible island-only build puts DEX first until your minimum hit kills an Orange Mushroom outright, then LUK to dodge hits in places like Dangerous Forest where you can be knocked off a ledge, and STR last for bigger numbers.
claims.say: dex first till you one-shot orange mushrooms, then luk, str last

claims.text: Three Snails is the only damaging spell a beginner has. It costs very little MP, so it works for sniping mobs you cannot reach, and natural MP regeneration keeps up with it.
claims.say: three snails is cheap on mp, good for sniping stuff out of reach

claims.text: On Maple Island, magic attack, magic defense and extra HP do nothing useful: the only spell is fixed damage, the mobs hit physically, and potions are plentiful.
claims.say: magic atk, mdef and hp dont matter on the island

claims.text: INT only matters on the island for extra MP per level or to meet a wand's INT requirement, such as the Metal Wand, so most island builds ignore it.
claims.say: int is only for mp or wearing a metal wand on the island

claims.text: The Gold Surfboard, a polearm usable from level 15 that drops from Slimes, is the classic first big weapon upgrade on Maple Island: more damage, long reach and a bonus to jump.
claims.say: slimes drop the gold surfboard, great first weapon upgrade

claims.text: The three starting weapons also drop in the field: the Sword from Snails, the Wooden Club from Stumps and the Hand Axe from Shrooms. Variable or godly rolls of them are worth farming for a better early weapon.
claims.say: sword drops from snails, club from stumps, hand axe from shrooms

claims.text: The Fruit Knife, a dagger usable from level 8, is a reward from the quest Biggs' Collection of Items. It has the fastest attack speed on the island, but daggers have shorter reach than other weapons.
claims.say: fruit knife from biggs quest, super fast swings but short reach

claims.text: Reach differs by weapon class: spears and polearms reach about a snail's width farther than one-handed swords, axes and maces, while daggers match them at the minimum but fall about half a snail short at the maximum.
claims.say: polearms and spears reach about a snail further than 1h weapons

claims.text: The author reckons a character should be level 175 or higher before taking on Pink Bean.
claims.say: you want around lvl 175 for pink bean

claims.text: Ranged attackers (Bowmasters, Marksmen, Night Lords, Corsairs) should have about 11,500 max HP before Hyper Body, roughly 18,400 with it, to survive Pink Bean.
claims.say: ranged need about 11.5k hp, 18k with hyper body, for pink bean

claims.text: Melee warriors should preferably have about 18,750 max HP before Hyper Body, which becomes 30,000 with it, for Pink Bean.
claims.say: warriors want 18.7k hp, 30k with hyper body, for pink bean

claims.text: Shadowers need less HP for Pink Bean: about 6,000 before Hyper Body, around 9,600 with it.
claims.say: shadowers can get by with about 6k hp, 9.6k with hyper body

claims.text: A good Pink Bean squad is four parties: two melee and two ranged, each built around a Dark Knight and a Bishop, with Bowmasters or Marksmen and Night Lords filling out the ranged parties.
claims.say: bring 4 parties, 2 melee 2 ranged, each with a dk and a bishop

claims.text: Zombify turns everyone on the map undead, so while it lasts a Bishop's Heal damages players instead of healing them.
claims.say: when zombified a bishop heal hurts people, dont heal

claims.text: Confusion reverses your left-right and up-down controls, so expect to move the wrong way until it wears off.
claims.say: confusion flips your movement keys, careful until it wears off

claims.text: Damage Reflect is the deadliest Pink Bean mechanic: if you attack while it is active the damage bounces back and can kill you, even at 30,000 HP, so attackers must stop when it goes up.
claims.say: stop attacking while reflect is up, it can kill you even at 30k hp

claims.text: There are three Damage Reflect symbols: weapon, magic, and both. Hugin and Munin use one type at a time, while Pink Bean's both-type reflect affects everybody, mage or not.
claims.say: check the reflect icon, pink beans hits mages and non mages alike

claims.text: Pink Bean cannot start a Damage Reflect while it is in the middle of another attack animation, so experienced squads keep hitting through the last seconds of the timer, but this is risky if you do not understand it.
claims.say: bean cant reflect mid animation, but only push the timer if youre sure

claims.text: Pin Pink Bean toward the left so it faces right: facing right it uses 1/1, while facing left it is likely to cast Seduce and Stun on the squad.
claims.say: keep pink bean facing right so he doesnt seduce, pin him left

claims.text: Hugin and Munin cast reflect and Seduce on anyone who strays past certain distance lines, so attackers stay inside the safe stretch beside them. Crossing over is safe only while the statue has not been attacked yet.
claims.say: dont step past hugin or munin's range lines, they reflect and seduce

claims.text: Pink Bean summons Mini-Beans that usually cast Cancel Weapon and Magic Attack soon after they appear, which cripples attackers, so kill them quickly.
claims.say: kill the mini beans fast, they cancel your attacks

claims.text: Ranged attackers who have not HP-washed lose most of their damage on Pink Bean because they keep dying, so wash before going.
claims.say: ranged guys should wash hp before pink bean or theyll just die

claims.text: A Paladin and Bishop pair can farm Crimson Hearts: the Bishop casts Genesis on each side to tag the mobs and pull them together, then the Paladin finishes them with Heaven's Hammer.
claims.say: pally plus bish: gen to clump them, heavens hammer to finish

claims.text: Another split: two Ice/Lightning mages spam Blizzard from the safe platform on the right while a Bishop and Paladin stand on the left under the mobs, cycling Blizzard, Heaven's Hammer and Genesis.
claims.say: or put 2 il mages on the right spamming blizzard

claims.text: Stage 8 of Ludibrium Party Quest is a box puzzle where five members stand on boxes in different combinations until the leader finds the right one.
claims.say: lpq stage 8: five people on boxes, leader tests combos

claims.text: To cut walking in LPQ stage 8, start members on boxes 1-3-6-7-4 instead of 1-2-3-4-5, counting the boxes row by row from the top.
claims.say: lpq 8 tip: start on 1-3-6-7-4, not 1-2-3-4-5

claims.text: With this relabeling, standard box 2 sits on physical box 3, 3 on 6, 4 on 7, 5 on 4, 6 on 8, 7 on 2 and 8 on 5, while boxes 1 and 9 keep their places.
Because of lag, the LPQ leader can confirm a combination as soon as a member is seen starting to move onto a box, since that member is already there on their own screen.
claims.say: leader, confirm as soon as they start moving, lag hides it

claims.text: For a Goby leech the author uses Brawlers rather than warriors because Brawler skills add far more accuracy; the lower the Brawler's level the more accuracy it needs to always hit, so bring accuracy and attack potions.
claims.say: brawlers make good goby leechers, their skills give accuracy

claims.text: A Bishop of about level 136 or higher with Genesis and Maple Warrior can sell leech at The Dragon Nest Left Behind once its magic attack is high enough to one-hit the skeleton dragons there.
claims.say: a genesis bishop can leech at dragon nest left behind

claims.text: Stoppers can be farmed at Sophilila's Bedroom in the Haunted House by running several summon characters at once (Bishop, Fire/Poison, Ice/Lightning, Bowmaster, Marksman) whose summons one-hit the mobs.
claims.say: summoners farm stoppers in sophilila's bedroom, haunted house

claims.text: Players disagree whether selling drops to an NPC pays while farming Stoppers: on many summon characters the trip costs map time, but keeping attackers on the map and sending a separate collector to sell does pay off.
claims.say: npc trips may not pay off when you farm on many chars

claims.text: A Night Lord makes the best looter for these mage farms thanks to Meso Up and high avoid, which saves potions.
claims.say: night lord makes the best looter, meso up and avoid

claims.text: Six mages at Ice Valley II in El Nath, two per channel over three channels, plus a looter (a thief is best) farm well; a looter changing channel lands at the top next to the shop NPC, so no Mystic Door is needed.
claims.say: 6 mages at ice valley 2, looter cc's and npcs at the top

claims.text: For the Ice Valley II farm the author prefers Fire/Poison mages, and Meteor Shower need not be maxed; it only has to one-hit the mobs, which also saves potions.
claims.say: fp works for pepe farm, meteor just needs to one hit

claims.text: A Dark Knight's Berserk only pays off while HP sits inside its narrow low-HP window, so on bosses you steer your HP with potions yourself instead of letting automatic heals push you back above it.
claims.say: for berserk keep hp inside the range, dont let autopot overheal

claims.text: The pet's autopot percentage sets your lowest HP, because the pet drinks once you fall under that line. Pick a percentage whose floor, plus a manual potion, still survives the boss's strongest hit.
claims.say: autopot % sets your hp floor, pick it so the big hit cant kill you

claims.text: Against Bodyguard A, manually drink a strong potion just before his touch hit lands so you can tank the touch and his kick, then fall back into Berserk range. Attack in the gap while your invincibility frames run out.
claims.say: vs bodyguard a pot right before his touch hit, attack during iframes

claims.text: For Anego (the Showa Female Boss), react to sound: when you hear her slap, drink a strong manual potion like Reindeer Milk at once. Autopot covers her small gunshots. Avoid her touch hit, it ruins your potion rhythm.
claims.say: anego: hear the slap sound, pot right away, autopot covers gunshots

claims.text: Anego's slap sound is easier to pick out when soloing, because in a party the noise from other players hides the sound cue.
claims.say: anego is easier solo, party noise hides the slap sound

claims.text: When a boss's Seduce hits you during a Berserk fight, clear it right away with Hero's Will. Being forced to walk while sitting at low HP is how Dark Knights die.
claims.say: got seduced? hero's will it asap, walking at low hp is deadly

claims.text: While Zombified, potions only heal about half as much, so expect to need extra potions to climb back to your target HP.
claims.say: zombified halves potion healing, pot extra to get hp back

claims.text: Dragon Roar costs HP, so use it to drop into Berserk range only from a safe position when no big attack is about to land, rather than casting it carelessly mid-fight.
claims.say: only dragon roar when its safe, not while a big hit is coming

claims.text: If a heal overshoots and lifts you out of Berserk range, Sacrifice brings you back down. Do not cast it while the boss has a reflect effect active.
claims.say: overhealed? sacrifice drops you back, but not while reflect is up

claims.text: Rush can dodge many boss attacks through its invincibility frames. A higher skill level makes them last longer, and you must trigger it just before the attack connects.
claims.say: rush gives iframes, time it right before the hit lands

claims.text: The Beholder's healing aura can fire while you are manual potting and lift you above Berserk range by accident, so some Berserk players leave it unlearned. It happens rarely, so it is a minor concern.
claims.say: beholder aura can overheal you out of berserk range sometimes

claims.text: Mages make the easiest early mesos: a Bishop or Fire/Poison Arch Mage that leeches parties in leech maps, especially end-game Bishop leech, earns well by selling leech services.
claims.say: bishop or fp arch mage leech is good early mesos

claims.text: Sell drops that fall inside the normal stat range to an NPC, but keep gear whose stats are 1-5 above the normal maximum (godly), since clean perfect gear sells to players for a lot.
claims.say: npc the normal drops but keep the godly stat gear to sell

claims.text: Use an Owl of Minerva to check current market prices before selling an expensive item, instead of guessing the price.
claims.say: use an owl of minerva to price expensive stuff before selling

claims.text: Clean near-perfect gear can be scrolled with a 10% scroll then 30% scrolls, since each success raises its sale value; stopping around +3 is a good start. 60%, 70% and 100% event scrolls are rarely worth it for profit.
claims.say: scroll clean gear with 10% then 30%, stop around +3 to profit

claims.text: Items commonly chaos scrolled for a profit gamble are Stormcaster Gloves, Facestompers, Dragon Khanjar and clean perfect high-level gear with double stats. Not every item pays off for the scroll.
claims.say: people chaos scroll stormcaster gloves, facestompers, dragon khanjar

claims.text: The Mushroom Shrine Gachapon is considered a great place to spend Gachapon Tickets, since it can give Chaos Scrolls, 30% and 70% scrolls and Elemental Wands that sell well.
claims.say: mushroom shrine gachapon can give chaos scrolls and good scrolls

claims.text: Clean godly Spectrum Goggles from the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest sell for good money, so they are worth keeping and selling.
claims.say: clean godly spectrum goggles from cwkpq sell well

claims.text: Onyx Apples from the Amoria PQ bonus stage are profitable, but you need to be married to enter.
claims.say: onyx apples from amoria pq sell well but you have to be married

claims.text: When reselling in a player shop, anything you bought roughly 10% or more under the market price is already a profit. Check a price list or owl before pricing, and stock enough items for several shops before opening one.
claims.say: buy 10% under market and resell, thats already profit

claims.text: Crossbow Mastery must be maxed at level 20 to unlock Marksman Boost in fourth job. Level 19 gives nearly the same accuracy, so you can delay the last point briefly.
claims.say: max crossbow mastery, its needed to unlock marksman boost later

claims.text: After Mastery and Booster, max Iron Arrow. It is a crossbowman's mobbing skill, hits several monsters at once and makes solo training much easier.
claims.say: max iron arrow, it hits multiple mobs and makes grinding easier

claims.text: Soul Arrow: Crossbow is a low priority since arrows are cheap. It is mainly a backup if you run out of arrows mid-boss, and while it is active you lose the attack bonus of your arrows.
claims.say: soul arrow is just a backup, arrows are cheap and it drops arrow atk

claims.text: Power Knock-Back is worth maxing as a crossbowman: it pushes monsters off you and is still useful later in bossing.
claims.say: max power knock-back, great for pushing mobs off you

claims.text: As a Sniper, max Strafe first. It replaces Double Shot as your main single-target skill.
claims.say: sniper: max strafe first, it replaces double shot

claims.text: After Strafe, a Sniper maxes Blizzard and Arrow Eruption one after the other. Arrow Eruption is the stronger mobbing skill, while Blizzard's freeze saves potions and makes grinding easier, so the order is a matter of taste.
claims.say: blizzard saves pots with freeze, arrow eruption mobs harder

claims.text: Blizzard cannot land critical hits, so critical bonuses like Sharp Eyes do nothing for it.
claims.say: blizzard cant crit, so sharp eyes wont help it

claims.text: Max Puppet as a Sniper: it draws the aggro of monsters you are attacking, which can trivialize some bosses, but it does not work if another player is also hitting that target.
claims.say: puppet pulls aggro off your party, but not if someone else hits the target

claims.text: Put Golden Eagle to level 15 to unlock Frostprey in fourth job. The eagle itself is weak, so no need to go further.
claims.say: golden eagle to 15 unlocks frostprey, no need for more

claims.text: As a Marksman, max Sharp Eyes first, then Snipe, then Marksman Boost. After that, choose by the content you plan to run, and max Maple Warrior and Hero's Will when you can afford them.
claims.say: marksman sp: sharp eyes, snipe, marksman boost, then what you need

claims.text: Sharp Eyes is what gets Marksmen into every boss run: it boosts critical output for the whole party, which helps Night Lords especially.
claims.say: sharp eyes is why mms get invited, nls love it

claims.text: Piercing Arrow and Strafe are close on three targets, but Piercing Arrow becomes much better with four or more targets lined up.
claims.say: pierce beats strafe once there are 4+ mobs in a line

claims.text: Dragon's Breath is not worth heavy investment: it does very little damage and its knockback does not work on bosses or boss monsters. Keep those points for Hero's Will and Maple Warrior.
claims.say: dont max dragon's breath, save the sp for hero's will and mw

claims.text: Archers are inefficient HP washers: each wash costs about 12 MP for roughly 16 to 20 HP, and you do not need fresh level-up AP for it.
claims.say: archers lose 12 mp per wash for 16-20 hp, not very efficient

claims.text: The lowest MP an archer can wash down to is 14 times level plus 148.
claims.say: archer min mp for washing is 14 x level + 148

claims.text: For HP washing, put AP into base INT early and wear INT gear while leveling to bank extra MP, then use AP resets to move MP into HP. Pull the INT back out when you are ready to attack, commonly around levels 135 to 155.
claims.say: wash plan: stack int while leveling, then reset mp into hp later

claims.text: A Marksman's main stat is DEX. Keep base STR only as high as needed to equip your crossbow, since the weapon's STR requirement equals its level, and Maple Warrior can cover the last bit for you.
claims.say: mm is all dex, only enough str to wear the crossbow

claims.text: A Zakum Helmet scrolled for DEX is a staple helmet for a Marksman. Look for one with high STR so you meet the weapon requirement more easily.
claims.say: zakum helmet scrolled for dex is a solid mm helm

claims.text: Players disagree on pendants: an enhanced Horntail Pendant usually beats a Mark of Naricain until the Mark has about 5 weapon attack or more, but the Mark gives HP and MP and drops from Crimsonwood Keep runs.
claims.say: htp beats mark of naricain until the mark has ~5 att

claims.text: In the Crimsonwood Keep council hall, Marksmen and Bowmasters should take the Pirate boss with Puppet: drop it as he winds up an attack, then run back to the portal and teleport up. His jumping attack can spoil it.
claims.say: in cwk drop puppet on the pirate boss as he winds up, then portal up

claims.text: Party mules standing on the right-hand platforms in the Crimsonwood Keep council hall draw the Pirate boss's aggro away from the Puppet, so ask them to wait on the floor instead.
claims.say: in cwk tell mules to stand on the floor or the pirate ignores puppet

claims.text: A Marksman can hit two heads, an arm and the wings of Horntail at once with Piercing Arrow, from either side. On the right with smoke you can stand and spam it, and you can charge it while stepping back into position.
claims.say: pierce can hit 2 heads + arm + wings on horntail from the right

claims.text: If your Bishop dies in a Horntail run, Piercing Arrow can clear the waves of wyverns, especially the ones that dispel your party. Arrow Eruption helps against the wyverns flying below you.
claims.say: pierce clears horntail wyvern waves, eruption hits ones below

claims.text: Skip Frostprey in Horntail: it drags summoned wyverns toward you, which is a liability, so ask the party before using it at bosses and follow their lead.
claims.say: dont use frostprey on horntail, pulls the wyverns onto you

claims.text: Frostprey is fine at Zakum: drawing the summoned monsters toward you does not matter because Piercing Arrow shreds them.
claims.say: frostprey is fine at zakum, pierce kills whatever it pulls

claims.text: A Marksman is useful in the Ellin Forest Party Quest: help push things in the second stage, and the stage where you protect an NPC can almost be soloed by spamming Blizzard with Frostprey out.
claims.say: mm is great at epq, blizzard + frostprey solos the protect stage

claims.text: Bind Snipe and Strafe so you can buffer Snipe straight into Strafe with no delay while weaving attacks.
claims.say: bind snipe into strafe so you chain them with no gap

claims.text: A Marksman always wants Speed Infusion for maximum damage output, so bring a Buccaneer or a dedicated mule to supply it in content that allows it.
claims.say: always get speed infusion, bring a bucc or mule for it

claims.text: Snipe ignores defenses, including weapon cancel. Against a boss that cancels your weapon, keep sniping: it shows as a critical 1 but the full damage still goes through.
claims.say: snipe ignores weapon cancel, keep sniping, full dmg goes through

claims.text: Archers can jump-attack by pressing jump and attack at the same moment, which helps you advance while attacking. Piercing Arrow can also be charged or cancelled on ropes, and you can jump or crouch while charging it.
claims.say: press jump and attack together to jump-attack, pierce charges on ropes

claims.text: To lure monsters that cannot be pushed, hit them all first, then drop a Puppet somewhere. They slowly walk toward it as long as nobody else attacks them, bunching up for Piercing Arrow.
claims.say: hit mobs then drop puppet to slowly lure ones that wont push

claims.text: A new Bishop gets Genesis through the Horntail Party Quest, which needs a Dragon Elixir from the Manon prequest and 3 players; many buy it as a service.
claims.say: genesis comes from htpq, needs an elixir and 3 people

claims.text: When selling low-level leech, don't wander the map looting; apart from Maple weapons and shields most drops sell poorly, and the walking costs kills.
claims.say: don't loot while leeching, most drops sell for nothing

claims.text: For better leech exp, learn the map's respawn timing and recast Genesis as the mobs reappear, keeping on the move rather than idling in one spot.
claims.say: time genesis to respawns, never just stand and wait

claims.text: Around 140 speed mixed with Teleport makes leech rotations much faster than teleport-casting alone; Squishy Shoes from Kerning City Party Quest plus a scrolled bathrobe, a mask and a Sirius cloak get you there.
claims.say: get 140 speed and mix walking with teleport

claims.text: To find leech buyers cheaply, stand in the Henesys Free Market with a Chalkboard showing your price instead of paying for Super Megaphones.
claims.say: sell leech with a chalkboard in fm, skip smegas

claims.text: A Bishop with too little HP for Skelegons can still sell leech there if a Spearman leecher keeps Hyper Body on; with Magic Guard the extra HP and MP let the Bishop survive.
claims.say: low hp bishop at skeles? get a spearman's hb + magic guard

claims.text: For the Bigfoot last-hit leech, a helper who can pin the monster in place, such as a Corsair or Buccaneer, makes it easier but is not required.
claims.say: a sair or bucc pinning bigfoot helps but isnt needed

claims.text: During a last-hit leech the low-level character must stay out of a party with the helpers, because partying breaks the kill bonus; that also rules out party buffs like Holy Symbol for the leecher.
claims.say: dont party the leecher or the kill bonus breaks

claims.text: One kill or one quest reward can raise you at most a single level; any exp past that is cut off just short of the following level, so huge exp chunks are partly wasted at low levels.
claims.say: one kill or quest cant give you more than one level

claims.text: A low-level leecher misses high-level monsters often, so stack accuracy; the chance to hit the same monster climbs noticeably as the leecher gains levels.
claims.say: stack accuracy as a lowbie leecher, you miss a lot

claims.text: Ranged characters suit last-hit leeching because fast multi-hit attacks like Double Shot give more chances at the final blow; warriors with a Final Attack skill also do well.
claims.say: archers with double shot are best at stealing the last hit

claims.text: A low-level mage leeching by last hit should wear accuracy gear and use plain basic attacks, since magic attacks almost never connect on monsters far above the mage's level.
claims.say: lowbie mage? basic attack with acc gear, spells will miss

claims.text: A Paladin's Heaven's Hammer leaves ordinary monsters at 1 HP instead of killing them, which makes it a tool for setting up last hits for low-level characters.
claims.say: heavens hammer leaves normal mobs at 1 hp

claims.text: With the same accuracy, a level 50 leecher lands hits on these monsters far more often than a level 35 one, so the leech speeds up as the leecher levels.
claims.say: a lvl 50 leecher hits way more often than a lvl 35

claims.text: In a basic HP wash, level-up AP goes into your main stat as normal, and each level you use 5 AP Resets to move points from MP into HP.
claims.say: basic wash: ap into main stat, then 5 resets mp to hp per level

claims.text: MP washing means putting the 5 level-up AP into MP, then using 10 AP Resets per level: five move MP to HP and five move MP to your main stat. It costs double but builds a bigger MP pool to wash from.
claims.say: mp wash: ap into mp, then 10 resets, 5 to hp and 5 to main stat
