claims.text: The Smokescreen skill quest begins with a storybook dropped by Lucida; the hidden room in the Mushroom Shrine area is the best place to farm it.
claims.say: smokescreen book drops from lucida around mushroom shrine

claims.text: Hughes in Orbis Tower then asks for a fan, a battery, 100 Squid drops, 20 Steel Plates, 50 propellers from Dual Ghost Pirates, 50 Screws and 50 gears from Chronos.
claims.say: hughes in orbis tower wants a fan, a battery and lots of parts

claims.text: The fan comes from Kay the engineer in Omega Sector, who wants 100 yellow propellers from Helly and 1 Steel Plate.
claims.say: kay in omega sector gives the fan for helly propellers

claims.text: For the battery, talk to Porter in the Omega Sector tower, defeat Papulatus in Ludibrium for the Papulatus Certificate and trade it to him.
claims.say: kill pap for the certificate, porter swaps it for the battery

claims.text: Bring everything back to Hughes, who gives you a computer; using it adds Smokescreen to your skills.
claims.say: hughes gives a computer, use it to learn smokescreen

claims.text: The Assassinate quest starts from your third job instructor, who sends you to Shawn at the Perion Excavation Site.
claims.say: assassinate starts at your 3rd job guy, then shawn in perion

claims.text: Shawn sends you into an arena alone where you break boxes to move up each level within 20 minutes; hand him the item you find, then report to your third job instructor to learn Assassinate.
claims.say: solo box arena, 20 min limit, then back to your instructor

claims.text: HP washing is a way to get extra max HP without losing damage: add AP to Int to build MP, turn that MP into HP with AP resets, then move the spent Int back into your main stat.
claims.say: washing = int builds mp, ap resets turn mp into hp

claims.text: HP and MP share one AP pool: a point put into HP can later be taken out of MP. That is what makes washing possible, since the same point can be moved from MP into HP again and again.
claims.say: hp and mp share an ap pool so you can move a point from mp to hp

claims.text: A common mistake is converting each fresh AP into HP only once. The minus-MP plus-HP reset can be repeated with the same point as long as your MP stays above its minimum, so keep going until you cannot.
claims.say: keep repeating -mp +hp with the same point until you hit min mp

claims.text: If an AP reset lets you remove from HP but not from MP, you have hit your minimum MP. You need more MP, from levelling with high Int or an MP wash, before you can take more out of MP.
claims.say: cant -mp on an ap reset? youre at min mp and need more mp first

claims.text: Total Int from base, Maple Warrior and gear counts when you level up: every 10 Int (rounded down) gives one extra MP per level. So level with Maple Warrior and Int gear on to build the MP you will wash.
claims.say: every 10 total int is +1 mp per level, so level with mw on

claims.text: A big part of washing cost is adding a lot of base Int (some add 300 or more) and then, for non-mages, spending one AP reset per point to move it back into the main stat to restore damage.
claims.say: a lot of wash cost is resetting that base int back out later

claims.text: Washing costs differ by class: warriors get a very favourable MP-to-HP exchange and high natural HP, ranged classes get a worse rate, and mages get the worst, so the same HP goal costs different amounts.
claims.say: warriors wash cheapest, ranged worse, mages worst

claims.text: MP washing is optional: add a fresh AP to MP, then use an AP reset to move it into another stat. It only cuts cost on big HP goals, because it nets more MP than adding another Int once your base Int is high.
claims.say: mp washing is optional, only worth it with big hp goals

claims.text: One MP wash gains about base Int divided by 10 minus 1 MP, rounded down, or minus 5 for pirates. Only base Int counts, not gear or Maple Warrior, so the more base Int you have, the better it pays.
claims.say: mp wash gives about base int/10 mp, pirates get less

claims.text: Thieves gain more HP from a fresh AP added to HP than from a reset, so they add fresh AP to HP and take it out of MP into Luk. Every other class gets equal or more from resets, so do not add fresh AP straight to HP.
claims.say: only thieves put fresh ap into hp, everyone else uses resets

claims.text: The HP and MP changes the AP reset window predicts are often badly wrong, so ignore them and go by how your real stats change after each reset.
claims.say: ignore the ap reset preview numbers, check your actual stats

claims.text: Washing is not strictly required. Only Bishops and other mages really need it to survive bosses, while other classes may wash just to skip the HP grind, and many mix washing with HP quests and gear.
claims.say: you dont have to wash unless youre a bishop, quests and gear help

claims.text: A reasonable HP goal for running Horntail is about 10,000 max HP by level 155, from natural HP plus washing plus gear and quests.
claims.say: aim for around 10k hp by lvl 155 to run horntail

claims.text: Mages need less HP thanks to Magic Guard: about 5,000 to 10,000 max HP is enough for a Bishop to run Horntail, with as much MP as you like on top.
claims.say: mages can get by on 5-10k hp for horntail thanks to magic guard

claims.text: Shadowers need less HP because of Meso Guard, but extra HP still helps since they are often picked as the seduce target on Horntail and may take extra damage.
claims.say: shadowers need less hp but are often the seduce target on ht

claims.text: Paladins and Heroes can aim a bit lower for HP because Power Guard and Achilles cut damage taken and their natural HP is already high.
claims.say: heroes and paladins can aim a bit lower on hp, power guard helps

claims.text: By level 145 natural max HP sits around 5,000 for ranged classes and 10,000 to 12,000 for melee. Your washing goal is your target HP minus natural HP minus what you expect from gear and quests.
claims.say: natural hp by 145 is about 5k ranged, 10-12k melee

claims.text: On your first character, skip washing: it is expensive and the mesos are better spent elsewhere. HP quests give 3,000 to 4,000 HP fairly quickly, which covers many needs without it.
claims.say: first char? skip washing, do the hp quests instead

claims.text: Washing late is still possible but costs more, because MP comes from the Int you hold at each level up, so later Int has to be higher for the same result. Add Int early if you plan to wash.
claims.say: you can wash late but it costs more, add int early

claims.text: You can wash in stages instead of once: some HP around level 50 for Zakum, more around 120 for Horntail, and again whenever you reset your base Int, as minimum MP rises with level.
claims.say: wash in stages, some for zakum at 50 and more for ht at 120

claims.text: Bloodwashing means putting all your AP into HP and leaving it there. It is cheap and needs no resets, but you lose damage, so it only suits mule characters, not a class you want to play.
claims.say: bloodwashing is all ap in hp, fine for mules but no damage

claims.text: The ring arrives as a box in your Use tab; open it and enter your partner's name to propose, then wait for them to accept.
claims.say: open the ring box and type your partners name to propose

claims.text: For the wedding permit, talk to High Priest John, then both partners visit Mom and Dad by climbing the heart rope in Henesys Hunting Ground II.
claims.say: mom and dad are up the heart rope in henesys hunting ground 2

claims.text: Mom and Dad ask for 2 more Proof of Love from the Nanas in Orbis and Ludibrium; bring them back and you both get Parent's Blessing.
claims.say: mom and dad want 2 more proof of love from orbis and ludi nanas

claims.text: Hand Parent's Blessing to High Priest John for Officiator's Permission; then both partners talk to him to start the wedding.
claims.say: bring parents blessing to high priest john for the permit

claims.text: Being married unlocks the Amoria Party Quest.
claims.say: being married lets you do apq

claims.text: HP washing means gaining extra MP from base INT and INT gear as you level, then using AP Resets to pull MP out and put it into HP.
claims.say: hp wash: get extra mp from int, then ap reset it into hp

claims.text: MP washing means adding level-up AP straight into MP while you have base INT, since gear INT does not count; it is an extra on top of HP washing for even more HP.
claims.say: mp wash: put level ap into mp with base int, then wash it

claims.text: Washing works best started at low level with base INT; a character starting around level 70 runs out of MP before gaining much HP.
claims.say: washing at 70 is late, start it at low level

claims.text: If you start late, skip washing and just level and do HP-raising quests; you can still wash the small extra MP that INT gear like a Zakum Helmet gives.
claims.say: late? skip washing, just wash a bit from int gear like zhelm

claims.text: Night Lords put almost every ability point into LUK as their damage stat. DEX is only support: keep the 25 base DEX needed to advance to Thief at level 10 and add more only when gear demands it.
claims.say: nl is all luk, just keep the 25 dex you need for thief

claims.text: For a claw user, every 5 points of LUK add roughly as much damage as 1 point of weapon attack, so LUK and attack on gear matter a great deal.
claims.say: about 5 luk is worth 1 weapon attack for a nl

claims.text: Maple weapons ask for nothing but level, so a thief can leave DEX at its base from first job until mid third job and pour points into LUK, getting more damage than the old high-DEX style.
claims.say: skip dex until about 3rd job, a maple claw doesnt need it

claims.text: Around level 100 raise base DEX to about 50 so DEX from gear can reach the 140 needed for the Red Craven claw, then let base DEX fall back toward 25 near level 200 once you own better gear.
claims.say: get dex to about 50 near lv100 to wear a red craven

claims.text: Rogue skills: one point in Lucky Seven first, then max Keen Eyes for range, then max Lucky Seven, then Dark Sight for grinding and party quests. Nimble Body can wait until second job.
claims.say: rogue: keen eyes, max lucky seven, then dark sight

claims.text: Assassin SP: max Critical Throw first (a few Claw Mastery points unlock it). A Maple Claw already throws fast, so delay Claw Booster, then max Haste, Claw Mastery and Claw Booster, then finish Nimble Body and Endure.
claims.say: assassin: max critical throw first, then haste and claw skills

claims.text: Hermit SP: one point in Avenger, then max Shadow Partner for early third job damage, then Flash Jump for mobility, then Avenger, Alchemist, Shadow Web and Meso Up. Keep Shadow Meso at 1 and put leftovers in Drain.
claims.say: hermit: shadow partner first, then flash jump and avenger

claims.text: Night Lord SP: one point in Shadow Stars, then max Triple Throw, then Maple Warrior 10, Shadow Shifter, the rest of Shadow Stars, Hero's Will and Ninja Storm. Venomous Star and Taunt take the spare points.
claims.say: 4th job nl: triple throw first, then mw, shifter, shadow stars

claims.text: Take Maple Warrior early so you hit hard solo or when nobody else buffs it. If a Bishop mule with Maple Warrior 20 always comes along, you can delay it until after Hero's Will or Ninja Storm.
claims.say: get maple warrior early unless a bishop buffs you with mw20

claims.text: Shadow Shifter steadies Night Lord damage by cutting how often knockback interrupts your attacks, which makes it the first big defensive max after Triple Throw and Maple Warrior.
claims.say: shadow shifter keeps knockback from breaking your damage

claims.text: Shadow Web immobilises mobs, which helps in some fourth job fights and in the Ellin Forest Party Quest, so Hermits max it after Alchemist.
claims.say: shadow web is handy for ellin pq and some 4th job fights

claims.text: A Night Lord relies on Sharp Eyes from a Bowmaster or Marksman to be worth bringing to most fourth job bosses, so line up a Sharp Eyes buffer before boss runs.
claims.say: nls need sharp eyes from a bowmaster for bossing

claims.text: Night Lords need a washed HP pool for the later bosses such as Horntail and Scarlion, using HP quests or AP resets, and the class is costly to wash and gear.
claims.say: nls need a washed hp pool for horntail and scarlion

claims.text: The first Triple Throw book drops from Zakum, as does its level 20 mastery book, while the level 30 mastery book comes from Horntail.
claims.say: triple throw books drop off zakum, the top one off horntail

claims.text: The Maple Warrior level 20 book only comes from Horntail; before that you use the level 10 version from your fourth job instructor.
claims.say: maple warrior 20 only comes from horntail

claims.text: Ninja Ambush quest: speak to Hellin, the fourth job Thief instructor, who sends you to the Dark Lord in Kerning City. He sends you to a special map to beat six enemies, then talk to him again to unlock it.
claims.say: ninja ambush: hellin then dark lord in kerning, beat six mobs

claims.text: At levels 10 to 15, finish the first job instructor quests and train at Henesys Hunting Ground I.
claims.say: lv10-15 train at henesys hunting ground 1

claims.text: Creeping Evil in Phantom Forest: sneak in with Dark Sight, stand between the two left-side Leprechauns and kill them with Lucky Seven. Loot only while they are in money-bag form, since the devil form hits very hard.
claims.say: kill leprechauns in creeping evil, loot only in bag form

claims.text: For levels 51 to 85, train on Windraiders at Lower Ascent on Crimsonwood Mountain or at Tornado Corridor in Crimsonwood Keep.
claims.say: lv51-85 windraiders at crimsonwood

claims.text: Between 110 and 135, join a party hunting Skelegons and Skelosaurus, but only one that has a Bishop or Priest to provide Holy Symbol.
claims.say: skelegon party needs a priest with holy symbol

claims.text: Farming Leprechauns in Creeping Evil is a strong early meso source: sell the junk equips to a vendor and keep Lucky Charms and any good mage gear to sell on the market.
claims.say: leprechauns are good money, sell equips and keep lucky charms

claims.text: The Amoria Party Quest can earn mesos by selling the Onyx Apples it gives, but your character has to be married to enter.
claims.say: amoria pq needs a married char, onyx apples sell well

claims.text: Early thief weapons: Garnier or Steel Titans claws at low levels, a Maple Claw by about level 35, and a Maple Kandayo later, which matters more than any other piece of gear in that range.
claims.say: garnier or steel titans early, maple claw by lv35

claims.text: HP washing means putting fresh AP into HP and then removing AP from MP with an AP reset, which converts MP above your class minimum into HP.
claims.say: hp washing: ap into hp, then ap reset out of extra mp

claims.text: Every 10 points of base INT add 1 extra MP per level up, so washers with very high base INT put fresh AP into MP to build lots of extra MP to wash into HP.
claims.say: high base int gives bonus mp per level, that mp gets washed into hp

claims.text: You can skip HP washing by keeping base INT low and getting extra HP from party quest gear and other items instead, at the cost of not always wearing the best damage gear.
claims.say: unwashed is possible if you stack hp gear from pqs

claims.text: The Goddess Wristband from Orbis Party Quest, once scrolled, is a good HP piece for characters that do not wash their HP.
claims.say: orbis pq goddess wristband is a good hp piece

claims.text: Broken Glasses from Ludibrium Party Quest give solid HP once fully scrolled, so they are worth getting for unwashed characters.
claims.say: ludi pq broken glasses give nice hp when fully scrolled

claims.text: Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest rewards the Mark of Naricain and Blackfist Cloak, both strong HP items for fourth-job attackers; mages gain little from the Mark.
claims.say: cwkpq drops mark of naricain and blackfist cloak for hp

claims.text: Around 10,000 HP is a comfortable target before fighting Horntail; learning his attack patterns lets you manage with less.
claims.say: aim for around 10k hp before horntail

claims.text: If you only need to beat a boss once for a quest and lack the HP goal, Hyper Body in the party can cover the gap.
claims.say: hyper body can cover missing hp for a one time boss clear

claims.text: In a Goby session the Bishop casts Genesis to kill the Goby houses and pull the Gobies toward a buffed low-level Brawler, who sits in the top-right corner and keeps attacking to kill the Goby fish.
claims.say: bishop gens the goby houses, brawler kills the fish in the corner

claims.text: The Goby Bishop needs about 1,100 total magic attack with Genesis at level 20 to one-hit the Goby houses. High speed and jump, about 140 and 123, make the house clearing much quicker.
claims.say: bishop needs ~1100 magic att and genesis 20 to one hit goby houses

claims.text: A Goby Bishop does well to take Resurrection to revive a dead attacker and Angel Ray to snipe Bone Fish in two hits before they kill the client or make the Brawler hit the wrong target.
claims.say: bishops snipe bone fish with angel ray and res dead attackers

claims.text: Brawlers beat warriors as Goby attackers: Bullet Time adds accuracy, Somersault Kick has a taller hitbox that hits more fish than Slash Blast, and they only need Knuckles instead of sword and shield sets.
claims.say: brawlers beat warriors at gobies, somersault kick hits more

claims.text: Goby Brawlers should max Bullet Time and Somersault Kick at first job, then Knuckle Mastery and as much Knuckle Booster as possible. Skip Improve MaxHP on the level 35 and 43 attackers but take it from about level 50.
claims.say: goby brawler sp: bullet time, somersault kick, then mastery+booster

claims.text: For accuracy, each point of DEX is worth about 0.8 accuracy and each point of LUK about 0.5, so DEX gear on the overall, eye and face slots helps a leech attacker hit Gobies reliably.
claims.say: each dex is about 0.8 acc and each luk 0.5 acc

claims.text: For low-level Goby Brawlers put STR on hat, cape, earrings, belt and rings, attack on gloves, attack or accuracy on shoes, and accuracy on the overall, eye and face accessory. All AP goes into STR.
claims.say: goby brawler: str on hat cape earrings, acc on overall eye face

claims.text: Mu Lung Dojo belts and wedding rings can be scrolled for STR or DEX, which is a cheap way for low-level characters to get extra STR.
claims.say: dojo belts and wedding rings can be scrolled for str

claims.text: A Goby Brawler should wear the highest STR hat it can get until level 50, then switch to a Zakum Helmet and favor as much DEX on it as possible.
claims.say: at lvl 50 swap to a zakum helmet and favor dex on it

claims.text: A Goby run needs Hyper Body so thief, pirate and bowman clients, who have low HP at level 30, survive. A level 40 Spearman can be the Hyper Body buff mule.
claims.say: gobies need hyper body for thieves, pirates and bowmen clients

claims.text: Maple Warrior is worth keeping up through a whole Goby session: its stat boost helps damage and accuracy thresholds and gives clients extra INT for HP washing.
claims.say: keep maple warrior on during goby, helps dmg acc and washing

claims.text: A Goby client needs a pet with auto HP, HP set to 100 percent, and about 1500 potions per hour from the Aqua Road shop. Mages also need auto MP and both Unagi and Red Bean Sundae.
claims.say: for gobies bring a pet with auto hp and lots of pots, mages need mp too

claims.text: Non-warrior clients should be second job and carry HP gear for roughly 1200 HP, because when they level up their HP can briefly fall back to the value without Hyper Body and a lag spike can kill them. Warriors only need auto HP.
claims.say: non warrior clients need 2nd job and ~1200 hp gear for gobies

claims.text: Beginners can wear INT gear to HP wash while being leeched at the Monster Carnival, whereas at the Gobies they need HP gear just to stay alive.
claims.say: beginners can wear int gear and wash in cpq, gobies need hp gear

claims.text: Level 35 and 43 Goby Brawlers are best HP washed with roughly 15 to 20 AP Resets each so they survive the Gobies without Hyper Body.
claims.say: hp wash lvl 35 and 43 goby brawlers so they live without hb

claims.text: Two-spot rotation: hit the first cluster, wait for the respawn, hit it again while telecasting toward the second cluster, repeat there and head back; flat maps with two clusters are the easiest place to learn it.
claims.say: hit each spot twice per respawn, tc over on the second cast

claims.text: Recast party buffs like Holy Symbol and Maple Warrior while hanging on a rope, which skips the cast's recovery time, and fit them into the slack you build up by running cycles quickly.
claims.say: rebuff hs and mw on a rope so you dont lose a cycle

claims.text: On maps with three clusters, visit each in turn and hit it twice, before and after respawn; when one cluster is small or too far, as on the Master Chronos and Platoon Chronos maps, skip it on some cycles.
claims.say: on 3 spot maps you can skip the weak spot some cycles

claims.text: On tight maps a missed telecast can cost a whole hit, so move to a spot you can still reach and cast there; landing two hits every respawn cycle matters more than perfect positioning.
claims.say: missed a tc? just make sure you still get 2 hits per cycle

claims.text: Every three minutes or so, break the rotation and sweep the platforms where drops pile up so your pets can loot them, then pick the cycle back up.
claims.say: every few minutes pause the rotation so pets can loot

claims.text: A Dark Knight has no use for base DEX, so all ability points can go into STR. Accuracy is the only limit on that, so aim for about 200 accuracy over time, mostly from gear.
claims.say: dk puts everything in str, just check you have enough accuracy

claims.text: As a Warrior, max Improved MaxHP Increase first (Improved HP Recovery is its prerequisite), then Slash Blast as the main attack, and Power Strike. Spare points do not matter.
claims.say: warrior: max hp increase first, then slash blast

claims.text: Spearman SP: take Spear Mastery and Spear Booster first, then max Hyper Body, leave Iron Will at a few points, and spend what is left on the Pole Arm skills.
claims.say: spearman: spear mastery and booster, then max hyper body

claims.text: Hyper Body raises max HP and MP for the whole party, which helps players with unwashed HP survive at bosses.
claims.say: hyper body boosts party hp and mp, great for unwashed bossing

claims.text: Dragon Knight SP: max Spear Crusher first, then Dragon Roar, Dragon Fury: Spear and Elemental Resistance, a mid-level Sacrifice, and Power Crash. Spear Crusher stays your main attack all the way to level 200.
claims.say: dragon knight: spear crusher first, then roar, fury, crash

claims.text: Avoid Dragon Blood: it bleeds your HP every few seconds, does not stack with attack potions, and can push you out of Berserk range or even kill you.
claims.say: skip dragon blood, it drains hp and clashes with attack pots

claims.text: Use Sacrifice for small HP trims and Dragon Roar for big drops when you need to get back under half HP for Berserk. Roar locks you in place and costs a large chunk of HP.
claims.say: sacrifice for small hp trims, dragon roar for big drops

claims.text: Power Crash strips Defense Up and Attack Up from mobs and bosses around you, which is handy when several bosses are up at once.
claims.say: power crash strips defense up and attack up off mobs and bosses

claims.text: An unfunded Dragon Knight can level faster by maxing Dragon Fury: Pole Arm and grinding with a pole arm through third job, then resetting to the spear version for endgame.
claims.say: unfunded dk can grind with pole arm dragon fury in 3rd job

claims.text: A spear with Crusher is the usual Dark Knight weapon for bossing because stab attacks hit harder with Crusher; a pole arm with Crusher is weak. Use a pole arm only for grinding with Dragon Fury.
claims.say: use a spear with crusher for bossing, pole arm only for grinding

claims.text: Dark Knight fourth job order: Berserk first, then Power Stance, Monster Magnet and Achilles, then Beholder, Maple Warrior, Rush, and Hero's Will last. With Magnet and Rush started you can begin mobbing hunts around level 150.
claims.say: dk 4th job: berserk first, then stance, magnet, achilles

claims.text: Berserk only adds damage while your HP is below half, so a Dark Knight keeps HP low on purpose using Sacrifice, Dragon Roar or an auto-pot setting.
claims.say: berserk only boosts damage under half hp, so stay low on purpose

claims.text: Monster Magnet pulls mobs in from far away and is the key skill for mobbing content.
claims.say: monster magnet pulls mobs in from afar, key for mobbing

claims.text: Power Stance gives a high chance to resist knockback when hit while buffed, helping you hold position.
claims.say: power stance makes you resist knockback while buffed

claims.text: Achilles cuts all damage you take, which is essential for keeping your HP inside the Berserk range.
claims.say: achilles cuts damage taken, needed to hold berserk hp range

claims.text: Do not spend skill points on Aura of the Beholder; it is the least useful fourth job skill for a Dark Knight.
claims.say: skip aura of the beholder, its the weakest 4th job skill

claims.text: Maxed Hex of the Beholder gives accuracy and avoidability, but it does not stack with accuracy or avoid potions; only the better of the two applies.
claims.say: hex of the beholder gives acc and avoid but wont stack with pots

claims.text: Hero's Will cures the Seduce status, which makes it the answer to being seduced at Horntail and similar bosses.
claims.say: hero's will cures seduce

claims.text: To wash a Dark Knight's HP, wear 40 to 50 INT gear while leveling or hold about 40 base INT until fourth job. The end goal is about 18,750 clean HP, which is 30,000 with Hyper Body.
claims.say: wash a dk with 40-50 int gear or 40 base int until 4th job

claims.text: Dark Knights gain a lot of damage from both Sharp Eyes and Speed Infusion, so bring those buffs along whenever you can.
claims.say: dk loves sharp eyes and speed infusion, bring them along

claims.text: On the pet auto-pot HP setting, each notch is 5 percent of max HP, so you count notches from the left to set the HP threshold at which the pet drinks.
claims.say: each notch on the pet autopot bar is 5 percent of max hp

claims.text: Even with just level 1 Rush, a Dark Knight is already a good Bigfoot killer around level 120, so try Bigfoot early.
claims.say: dk with rush is a good bigfoot killer around lv120

claims.text: In the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest bosses, use Power Crash every so often, because the bosses' attack buff stacks and can kill you.
claims.say: in cwkpq keep using power crash, the boss attack buff stacks

claims.text: As a Dark Knight at Horntail, stand where one attack reaches a wing, the left arm and a leg for three targets, and once the tail is dead move alone to the right side to hit three targets there.
claims.say: ht: hit wing, left arm and leg together for three targets

claims.text: At Horntail, use Power Crash whenever the left arm casts Defense Up, since the buff goes onto every body part, including ones without a visible icon.
claims.say: ht: power crash when the left arm casts defense up

claims.text: A simple Horntail order for mixed melee and ranged groups: kill legs and tail, then head C, then wings, then head A, head B, and arms last.
claims.say: mixed ht party: legs and tail, head c, wings, head a, b, arms

claims.text: Top and bottom suit the average Dark Knight better than an overall, because the DEX on them helps cover accuracy, especially when wearing high attack or STR helmets.
claims.say: top and bottom beat an overall for dk accuracy

claims.text: The Zakum Helmet is the easy default Dark Knight helmet: loot a few and scroll them with DEX or accuracy scrolls, DEX for a little more damage and accuracy scrolls for more accuracy.
claims.say: zakum helmet is the easy dk helm, scroll it for dex or acc

claims.text: A Marksman can solo Mu Lung Dojo by relying on Puppet, because the dojo bosses go after the Puppet instead of you.
claims.say: marksman can solo dojo, the bosses chase your puppet

claims.text: A Bowmaster trying the Puppet dojo method should attack with Strafe, since Hurricane burns too much MP over a long run.
claims.say: bm in dojo should strafe, hurricane eats too much mp

claims.text: Blind helps a Marksman in the dojo by making boss attacks miss more often, one reason the solo run is easier than on a Bowmaster.
claims.say: blind makes dojo bosses miss you more, big help for mm

claims.text: In the dojo, pull Manon or Griffey, drop a Puppet to your left and keep attacking; while they target the Puppet they skip their HP and MP to 1 attack and do not dispel you.
claims.say: manon and griffey hit the puppet, no 1/1 and no dispel

claims.text: For Leviathan, place the Puppet as far left as you can, keep your distance so he cannot curse you, and jump his attacks so you are not blown into the wall; by the right wall he only summons and walks at the Puppet.
claims.say: leviathan: puppet far left, stay back, jump over his attacks

claims.text: Dojo Papulatus still dispels, stuns and slows while chasing your Puppet, but will not use his HP and MP to 1 attack while it is up; push him into the right wall and keep your distance.
claims.say: dojo pap won't 1/1 while puppet is up, but still dispels

claims.text: A Night Lord's damage comes from total LUK times total weapon attack; STR and DEX add nothing, so judge gear and AP by what they do to those two numbers.
claims.say: nl dmg is basically total luk x total watt, dex adds nothing

claims.text: Keep a Night Lord's DEX only as high as the gear needs, for example a Red Craven or Dragon Purple Sleeve, and put the rest of the AP into LUK.
claims.say: nl dex only as high as ur gear needs, rest in luk

claims.text: Monster weapon defense is subtracted from base damage before skill percentage multipliers apply, which makes defense the only non-linear part of the damage calculation.
claims.say: mob wdef comes off before the skill multiplier

claims.text: Sharp Eyes adds its bonus to Critical Throw's damage instead of multiplying it, which is part of why a Night Lord gains so much from it.
claims.say: sharp eyes adds on top of critical throw, nl loves it

claims.text: A claw has low weapon attack, so an attack potion adds proportionally more for a Night Lord; judge gear by the damage you actually do with the potion you use, such as Heartstopper or Onyx Apple.
claims.say: claws have low watt so atk pots help nl a lot

claims.text: For a Night Lord a plain Horntail Necklace does about as well as a top-rolled Mark of Naricain, and it lets you keep DEX lower, so a non-perfect Horntail Necklace is fine for a long time.
claims.say: for nl a normal horntail necklace is close to a perfect mon

claims.text: Do not pay for boss runs just to reloot a pendant: the slot adds very little damage for a Night Lord compared to the time and mesos spent; one early run for your first Horntail Necklace around level 120 is enough.
claims.say: dont waste mesos relooting pendants, one ht run is enough

claims.text: Pirate Party Quest takes a party of three to six players at level 70 or higher; the leader starts it by talking to Guon in the waiting area.
claims.say: ppq is 3-6 players lvl 70+, leader talks to guon to start

claims.text: To reach the Pirate Party Quest waiting area, go from Herb Town to Isolated Swamp, press up on the top cage to find a secret portal to Red-Nose Pirate Den, then take the top portal in Red-Nose Pirate Den 1.
claims.say: from herb town go to isolated swamp, up on top cage, then the den

claims.text: Stepping into a stage portal starts the next room's timer for the whole party, so wait until everyone is ready unless the group is fast and active.
claims.say: dont enter the ppq portal until everyone is ready, timer starts

claims.text: In stage 2 the leader must collect 20 each of Mark of the Rookie Pirate, Mark of the Rising Pirate and Mark of the Veteran Pirate, and each wave of pirates that drops them is summoned by talking to Guon.
claims.say: ppq stage 2: leader gets 20 of each mark, guon spawns the waves

claims.text: A weaker or low-level group can clear one pirate wave in stage 2, heal up, and only then talk to Guon for the next wave.
claims.say: in ppq stage 2 clear a wave and heal before calling the next one

claims.text: Stages 3 and 4 are deck rooms where you only defeat every monster and move on; the optional bonus doors inside them are the only extras.
claims.say: ppq decks 1 and 2 are just kill everything and move on

claims.text: The final Pirate Party Quest boss, Lord Pirate, only buffs his defense and summons creatures, so a prepared party defeats him easily.
claims.say: lord pirate is easy, he just buffs defense and summons stuff

claims.text: The party leader must still be alive and in the quest to complete Pirate Party Quest and collect the reward exp, so protect the leader; if the leader is lost and leadership does not pass on, abandon the run.
claims.say: ppq cant finish if the leader dies so keep the leader alive

claims.text: Players from level 55 to 99 can take five Pirate Party Quest side quests, two from Guon, two in Herb Town and one in Lith Harbor, so grab them before level 100 when they stop being offered.
claims.say: grab the ppq side quests before lvl 100, they stop after that

claims.text: Finding the Ingredients for Tae Sang in Herb Town needs 100 Ginseng Concentrate and 50 Bellflower Concentrate, and Bellflower Concentrate only drops in the bellflower bonus room, a few per room.
claims.say: bellflower concentrate only drops in the ppq bellflower room

claims.text: The Pirate's Map quest from Lith Harbor, available from level 55, has you collect 6 Pieces of the Pirate Map from Lord Pirate while running Pirate Party Quest.
claims.say: pirate's map quest in lith harbor needs 6 map pieces from lord pirate

claims.text: Both deck stages have two bonus doors: Deck 1 has the Bellflower room on the left and the Captain/Kru room on the right, and Deck 2 is mirrored, so one run can do two of each room.
claims.say: ppq deck 1 bellflower left kru right, deck 2 is the mirror

claims.text: Each player can hold only one chest key, so two different party members must each open a chest in both Bellflower rooms for the party to face Enraged Lord Pirate.
claims.say: you need 2 people with chest keys to get to enraged lord pirate

claims.text: A party of at least three must enter Pirate Party Quest, but only the leader has to survive to the end, so the other members can leave once the quest is underway.
claims.say: ppq needs 3 to enter but only the leader has to finish

claims.text: Stages 1 to 5 of Pirate Party Quest each have a six minute limit and the Lord Pirate fight has ten, so keep a steady pace.
claims.say: ppq has 6 min per room and 10 for the boss, stay quick

claims.text: A Night Lord keeps base DEX at the 25 needed to equip gear and puts every other point into LUK, adding DEX later only when better armor demands it.
claims.say: keep dex at 25 and dump the rest into luk

claims.text: With weak DEX-free gear start adding DEX around levels 80-100; with good DEX-free gear you can wait until about 120-130 before adding DEX to wear better armor.
claims.say: ok gear: add dex around 80-100, good gear: 120+

claims.text: A base DEX of about 70-80 is a sensible target once geared, since scrolls and pieces like the Zakum Helmet and Horntail Necklace add DEX, and AP resets let you shift points later.
claims.say: 70-80 base dex is a fine target once you gear up

claims.text: As a Rogue take 1 point in Lucky Seven, then 5 in Nimble Body to unlock Keen Eyes, max Keen Eyes for much longer throwing range, and then max Lucky Seven.
claims.say: rogue: 1 seven, 5 nimble body, max keen eyes, then max seven

claims.text: Claw Mastery can wait for Assassins because Lucky Seven's damage formula ignores mastery, so the damage range stays steady without it.
claims.say: lucky seven ignores mastery so claw mastery can wait

claims.text: After the main Assassin skills, put 3 points in Endure to unlock Drain; Drain can top off HP between Lucky Seven throws and save a potion.
claims.say: endure 3 unlocks drain, tops off hp between throws

claims.text: Hermits max Shadow Partner first, then Flash Jump, Avenger, Alchemist, Meso Up and Shadow Web; Shadow Meso is nearly useless and can be skipped.
claims.say: hermit: shadow partner first, then flash jump, avenger, alchemist

claims.text: Shadow Partner consumes Summoning Rocks, so a Hermit should do the Alcaster questline to get a supply.
claims.say: shadow partner eats summoning rocks, do the alcaster quests

claims.text: Night Lords max Triple Throw first, then Maple Warrior and Shadow Shifter, then Shadow Stars, Venomous Star, Ninja Storm and Taunt; Ninja Ambush gets nothing.
claims.say: night lord: triple throw first, then maple warrior, shifter

claims.text: Put one point into Shadow Stars right away; even level 1 saves stars while grinding or bossing.
claims.say: one point in shadow stars already saves a ton of stars

claims.text: Shadow Shifter adds an extra chance to avoid hits on top of a Night Lord's high avoidability, saving potions and sometimes your life against hits like the Horntail tail or Zakum's body.
claims.say: shadow shifter dodges extra hits, saves you at bosses

claims.text: Venomous Star poison does not work on bosses, so it only helps with skeleton grinding at low levels; one point is plenty.
claims.say: venomous star doesnt work on bosses, 1 point is plenty

claims.text: Taunt is a mob-gathering skill: it raises exp and drops from mobs but not bosses, costs no stars and needs no minimum distance, unlike Avenger.
claims.say: taunt boosts exp and drops on mobs and gathers them well

claims.text: Ninja Storm pushes mobs away like Rush, but its success rate is low until maxed, so it is best near full level; it also keeps Jr. Wraiths off you at Bigfoot.
claims.say: ninja storm pushes mobs away but only works well when maxed

claims.text: Right after the 4th job advancement the job NPC gives Maple Warrior, and Shadow Shifter, Shadow Stars and Venomous Star are available at once.
claims.say: maple warrior comes from the 4th job npc right after advancing

claims.text: To unlock Ninja Ambush, talk to Hellin, then to the Dark Lord in Kerning City who sends you to defeat his six disciples, and finish by talking to Arec in El Nath.
claims.say: ninja ambush: hellin, then dark lord, beat 6 disciples, then arec

claims.text: Aim to have Hero's Will by about level 155; even one point cures Seduce and can save you during the Horntail fight.
claims.say: get hero's will by 155, it can save you at horntail

claims.text: At levels 21-29 options are Kerning City Party Quest, Land of Wild Boar II in Perion, Cave of Evil Eye II, Terrace Hall in Ludibrium, and Perion Excavation Site III for Rocky and Wooden Masks.
claims.say: 21-29: kerning pq, wild boar land, evil eye cave or terrace hall

claims.text: Between 51 and 74: Ludibrium Maze Party Quest, Sophilia's Bedroom in the haunted house, Forest of Dead Trees IV (and III from 72) in El Nath, Ghost Ship 2 in Singapore, and Windraiders from level 60.
claims.say: 51-74: maze pq, dead trees, ghost ship 2, windraiders

claims.text: From 75: Wolf Spider Cavern in MesoGears, Windraiders and Stormbreakers at the Cavern of Pain, Leafre's Destroyed Dragon Nest from 85, and the squids in Aquarium's Deep Sea Gorge I for 85-94.
claims.say: 75-94: wolf spider cavern, cavern of pain, dragon nest, deep sea gorge

claims.text: The Headless Horseman is good training from about level 80 as long as you can keep knocking him back; stun-lock him with Lucky Seven or pin him with Triple Throw because his magic hits hard.
claims.say: hh is good exp from ~80 if you can keep him knocked back

claims.text: To knock back the first Papulatus body you need very high damage per hit, so bring Sharp Eyes and attack potions; stand out of his attack range and you can spam Triple Throw without getting dispelled.
claims.say: pap needs big hits to knock back, bring sharp eyes and atk pots

claims.text: For Zakum finish the prequests, hold an Eye of Fire, and drop it on the middle altar to summon him; kill the arms first (Night Lords just spam Triple Throw), then the main body in its phases.
claims.say: zakum: drop the eye of fire, kill the arms, then the body

claims.text: Monster Carnival is a leveling route up to about level 51, when you outgrow its entry range.
claims.say: cpq is good till about 51

claims.text: A Zakum leech crew can be a high magic attack Bishop, a Paladin as main damage, a Shadower whose Smokescreen covers reviving a dead buyer, and a Dark Knight for Hyper Body if the buyer's HP is low.
claims.say: zak leech crew: bishop, paladin, shadower, dk for hyper body

claims.text: Kill Zakum's sixth arm first, because it heals the other arms.
claims.say: kill zak's 6th arm first, it heals the other arms

claims.text: On Zakum's sixth arm, the Paladin attacks with Blast while Lightning Charge is active.
claims.say: paladin blasts the 6th arm with lightning charge on

claims.text: In a Zakum leech the buyer stays out of the party and lands the last hit on each part to get the exp.
claims.say: buyer stays out of party and takes the last hits

claims.text: Zakum's arms recover a bit of HP, so the buyer should hit an arm right after a Heaven's Hammer lands.
claims.say: arms heal a bit, buyer hits right after heaven's hammer

claims.text: Kill Zakum's arms from the bottom up; the top arms give the most exp.
claims.say: kill zak arms bottom to top, top arms give the most exp

claims.text: On Zakum's body, the buyer takes the final hit after a Heaven's Hammer; attack-boosting items help at this stage.
claims.say: on the body, buyer last hits after hh, pop att items

claims.text: After the sixth arm dies, a Shadower can use Boomerang Step on arms 5, 7 and 8 to even out their HP and shorten the Heaven's Hammer stage; a Corsair or Hero dealing similar damage also works.
claims.say: shadower boomerang steps arms 5, 7, 8 to speed up the hh part

claims.text: A Fruit Knife bought at the Lith Harbor weapon store is a cheap, quick-swinging tool for the APQ bonus boxes; any other fast weapon also works.
claims.say: grab a fruit knife at the lith weapon shop for apq bonus boxes

claims.text: Spears and polearms are a poor fit for the APQ bonus boxes because their attack reach does not line up well with how the boxes are placed.
claims.say: skip spears and polearms in apq bonus, the reach is awkward

claims.text: Have Haste on before the APQ bonus starts; several box positions need the extra speed and jump, and some high platforms cannot be reached without it.
claims.say: get haste before apq bonus, some ledges need the extra jump

claims.text: A pet that loots items saves precious seconds in the APQ bonus; apples often roll into neighbouring spots, so pick up what lands near you and hand back any that belong to others.
claims.say: bring a looting pet to apq bonus, give back apples that arent yours

claims.text: Where each player lands in the APQ bonus room follows the order the party was formed, so the leader usually assigns positions beforehand; some positions hold one more box than others.
claims.say: apq bonus spots go by party order, ask the leader where you stand

claims.text: The hardest APQ bonus position has broken platforms and normally goes to a mage, since Teleport lets them reach every box in time; other classes there may have to give up a box.
claims.say: the broken-platform spot in apq bonus is for a mage with teleport

claims.text: Gun ammo climbs two attack per tier: Bullet 10, Split Bullet 12, Mighty Bullet 14, Vital Bullet 16, Shiny Bullet 18 and Eternal Bullet 20.
claims.say: bullets: bullet, split, mighty, vital, shiny, eternal is best

claims.text: Blaze Capsule and Glaze Capsule are not shooting ammo; they are only used up by the Outlaw skills Flamethrower and Ice Splitter.
claims.say: capsules are only for flamethrower and ice splitter

claims.text: Starter stars rise two attack per step: Subi 15, Wolbi 17, Mokbi 19, Kumbi 21, Tobi 23, then Steely Throwing-Knives at 25.
claims.say: subi, wolbi, mokbi, kumbi, tobi, then steelys at the top

claims.text: Ilbi Throwing-Stars and Hwabi Throwing-Stars are the next step up from Steely Throwing-Knives, and Crystal Ilbi Throwing-Stars hits harder still.
claims.say: after steelys go ilbis or hwabis, crystal ilbis are even better

claims.text: Novelty stars like Snowball, Wooden Top, Icicle, Orange, Paper Fighter Plane and Maple Throwing-Stars sit between Wolbi and Kumbi in attack, so none of them beat Steely Throwing-Knives.
claims.say: fun stars like icicles or oranges are weaker than steelys

claims.text: Bow arrows go from Arrow for Bow up through Bronze Arrow for Bow and Steel Arrow for Bow, with Red Arrow for Bow and Diamond Arrow for Bow the strongest regular ones.
claims.say: arrows: plain, bronze, steel, then red or diamond are best

claims.text: Crossbow bolts follow the same ladder: Arrow for Crossbow, then Bronze and Steel, with Blue Arrow for Crossbow and Diamond Arrow for Crossbow at the top.
claims.say: xbow bolts: plain, bronze, steel, then blue or diamond

claims.text: Max Improved MaxHP Increase as early as you can as a Swordman; it only adds HP on future level-ups, so points put in late lose that HP for good.
claims.say: max improved maxhp increase asap, late points lose hp

claims.text: Power Strike for single targets and Slash Blast for groups are a Spearman's main attacks until 3rd job.
claims.say: power strike and slash blast carry you till 3rd job

claims.text: A Spearman is already useful at 2nd job because Hyper Body raises the whole party's max HP and MP, which parties value in Ludibrium Party Quest and Monster Carnival.
claims.say: spearman hb makes you welcome in lpq and cpq

claims.text: At 3rd job, max Spear Crusher first; it stays the line's main attacking skill from then on.
claims.say: max spear crusher first at 3rd job, it's your main attack

claims.text: Power Crash strips a monster's weapon defense buff, which helps against bosses that raise their defense.
claims.say: power crash cancels a boss's defense buff

claims.text: Dragon Blood boosts attack but keeps draining your HP while it runs, which can leave you open to one-shots at hard hitters like Zakum.
claims.say: dragon blood drains hp, watch out at zakum

claims.text: Elemental Resistance lowers the damage you take from monsters' magic attacks.
claims.say: elemental resistance cuts magic damage taken

claims.text: The author considers Sacrifice a waste of skill points.
claims.say: sacrifice isn't worth the sp imo

claims.text: Use Dragon Roar to bring your own HP down into Berserk range, and set your pet's HP potion threshold low enough that it doesn't heal you back out of it.
claims.say: dragon roar to drop hp, set pet pots low for berserk

claims.text: Achilles is a passive that reduces the damage monsters deal to you.
claims.say: achilles = less damage taken

claims.text: Max Beholder; the summon gives small heals plus defense, magic defense, accuracy and avoid buffs.
claims.say: max beholder for heals and def/acc/avoid buffs

claims.text: Maple Warrior 20 is a luxury: get the mastery book only if you can afford it, since most high-level parties already bring someone who has it.
claims.say: mw20 only if you can afford the book

claims.text: Monster Magnet pulls monsters over to you.
claims.say: monster magnet drags mobs to you

claims.text: Put 1 point into Rush early, then raise it to 30 later for more range when pushing mobs left or right.
claims.say: rush 1 early, max it later for more range

claims.text: Hero's Will isn't essential; aim for at least level 5 of it, and level 10 if you have the mesos.
claims.say: hero's will 5 is fine, 10 if you're rich

claims.text: Dark Knights are a strong pick for Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest because their attacks hit several of the lower bosses at once.
claims.say: dk is great in cwkpq, hits several bosses at once

claims.text: Dark Knights are nearly always wanted in Zakum runs, both for Hyper Body and because their attacks hit three arms at once.
claims.say: dks get zakum spots for hb and hitting 3 arms

claims.text: The Spearman line suits a first main because Hyper Body covers HP, so it needs much less HP washing than other classes.
claims.say: spearman is a good first main, hb means less hp washing

claims.text: High-level bishops make mesos selling leech: they clear a map with Genesis while paying buyers in the party share the exp, so the bishop needs enough magic attack to one-hit every mob there.
claims.say: bishops sell leech, you need genesis to one-hit the whole map

claims.text: Mages should scroll their belt for INT rather than LUK; a Yellow Belt or a better belt is a fine base to scroll.
claims.say: scroll your belt for int, yellow belt or better

claims.text: An earring with unused upgrade slots is wasted magic attack: either scroll the slots or sell it and buy an already finished magic attack earring.
claims.say: dont leave earring slots empty, scroll it or buy a finished one

claims.text: Finishing the Ellin Forest questline rewards a medal that adds 3 to all stats, a cheap stat boost for any character.
claims.say: do the ellin forest quests, the medal gives +3 all stats

claims.text: A Wizard Elixir from New Leaf City gives a temporary magic attack boost that can push a mage over a one-hit threshold before the gear catches up.
claims.say: nlc wizard elixir can push you over a one-hit line

claims.text: Party exp from a leech is split by each member's level compared with the party's average level, so a lower-level seller leaves more exp for the buyers; a higher seller can still sell but should charge less.
claims.say: lower lvl seller = more exp for buyers, charge less if higher

claims.text: Sap of Ancient Tree is a rare Wild Boar drop that players want for an HP quest.
claims.say: sap of ancient tree from boars is wanted for an hp quest

claims.text: The Land of Wild Boar II is a quieter but far boar map reached by going east from Perion through Perion Street Corner, East Rocky Mountain I and the Rocky Roads to East Domain of Perion, then a hidden entrance.
claims.say: land of wild boar ii is far east of perion, hidden way in

claims.text: Crimson Hearts are always in demand because Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest needs them, but Crimson Guardians drop little else and curse you, so farm them with a fast killer such as a Shadower and carry All Cure Potions.
claims.say: crimson hearts sell well but guardians curse, bring a fast killer

claims.text: An Outlaw can farm Crimson Hearts by dropping Aerial Strike at the bottom of the map every few seconds, ideally with mages on the safe platform on the right and a Corsair covering the left.
claims.say: outlaws can farm crimson hearts spamming aerial strike at the bottom

claims.text: Amoria Party Quest rewards Onyx Apples that are always in demand and sell fast, but it needs a full reliable party and a small ticket investment, and the apple count is luck-based.
claims.say: apq gives onyx apples that sell fast but you need a full party

claims.text: Mix several farming methods instead of repeating one forever; changing routine keeps farming fun and spreads the luck-based drops out.
claims.say: mix up ur farming spots so it doesnt get boring

claims.text: If you have no Mystic Door, carry Teleport Rocks so you can return to your farming map right after selling loot to an NPC.
claims.say: keep tele rocks to get back to ur farm map after selling

claims.text: INT from equipment counts the same as base INT for the extra MP gained on level-up, but only if the gear is worn at the moment you level.
claims.say: int on gear counts for mp if you wear it when you level

claims.text: Each level-up adds extra MP equal to your INT divided by 10, rounded down, on top of the normal gain, so more INT means more MP you can later wash into HP.
claims.say: every 10 int gives about 1 extra mp per level

claims.text: The HP you can still wash at a level is the MP you hold above that level's minimum MP, divided by the MP each reset removes, times the HP each reset adds.
claims.say: spare mp over the minimum is what you can wash into hp

claims.text: A White Scroll keeps the upgrade slot when a scroll fails, but it is used up whether the scroll passes or fails.
claims.say: white scroll saves the slot on a fail, but is used up either way

claims.text: While a ship, plane or elevator is between departure and arrival nobody can board it; boarding reopens once it has landed.
claims.say: cant board while the ride is in transit, wait till it lands

claims.text: Scrolling patterns or rituals do not change your odds; every scroll is an independent roll, so do not pay for or rely on a dummy-scrolling routine.
claims.say: dummy scrolling doesn't work, every scroll is its own roll

claims.text: A 70% scroll succeeds 70% of the time, fails 15% of the time and destroys the item the other 15%.
claims.say: 70% scrolls: 70 pass, 15 fail, 15 boom the item

claims.text: For scrolls like shield attack, bottom DEX and top LUK, the 70% version gives +2 and the 30% version +3. The 70% is usually the cheaper way to stat gear, except in rare cases like finishing perfect equipment.
claims.say: 70% scrolls are usually better value than 30% ones

claims.text: A White Scroll only protects the slot on a plain failure; it is used up on a success too, and it does not stop a destroying scroll from exploding the item.
claims.say: white scroll only saves the slot on a fail, not from a boom

claims.text: Whether to use a White Scroll depends only on what losing a slot would cost: use it if the slot is worth more than the White Scroll price divided by the chance of a plain failure.
claims.say: use a ws when losing the slot costs more than ws / fail chance

claims.text: The failure chance to divide by is 40% for chaos scrolls, 35% for 30% scrolls and 15% for 70% scrolls. The chance of destroying the item does not enter the White Scroll decision.
claims.say: fail chance to use: chaos 40%, 30% scroll 35%, 70% scroll 15%

claims.text: Using a White Scroll with a 30% scroll and retrying after each plain failure, a slot ends in success about 46% of the time and in a destroyed item about 54% of the time.
claims.say: 30% + ws: roughly 46% it lands, 54% it booms

claims.text: Bishops can telecast Genesis: put Teleport and Genesis on two neighbouring keys, walk the way you want to move, then hit both keys at once while still holding the arrow key.
claims.say: bind teleport and genesis side by side, hold arrow, hit both

claims.text: Placing Teleport right beside your attack skill key lets a mage telecast with one hand, which is less tiring over long training sessions than a two-handed setup.
claims.say: keep teleport next to your attack key, telecast one handed

claims.text: Zakum Helmet can be worn from level 50, so pick one up early; a well-scrolled one stays a core piece all the way into the endgame.
claims.say: get a zakum helmet at 50, you keep using it forever

claims.text: Horntail Necklace, wearable at 120, is the pendant for Night Lords and Shadowers; other classes can use it until they land a good Mark of Naricain.
claims.say: htp is the pendant for nl and shad

claims.text: For every class other than Night Lords and Shadowers, Mark of Naricain from Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest is the best pendant.
claims.say: mark of naricain from cwkpq is the best pendant for most

claims.text: Mu Lung Dojo rewards White, Yellow, Blue, Red and Black belts; by around 135 aim to have a scrolled Red or Black belt.
claims.say: get a red or black dojo belt and scroll it by 135

claims.text: After the weapon, the cape, gloves and shoes are your main source of weapon attack, so most of your damage budget goes into attack versions of those three.
claims.say: cape gloves shoes with attack are where your mesos go

claims.text: Good attack cape bases are Pink Adventurer Cape, Pink Gaia Cape and Blackfist Cloak; warriors can also use Taru Spirit Cape.
claims.say: pac, pink gaia cape or blackfist cloak for attack capes

claims.text: Brown Work Gloves and Stormcaster Gloves are the usual bases for weapon attack gloves.
claims.say: bwg or stormcaster gloves for attack gloves

claims.text: Facestompers are a top pick when buying weapon attack shoes.
claims.say: facestompers are the attack shoes to get

claims.text: Up to about level 120 you need almost no gear spending; a few 60% scrolls on a Maple weapon and your gloves are plenty.
claims.say: dont spend on gear before 120, just scroll a maple weapon

claims.text: From about 120 to 135, focus on reaching the secondary stat your end-game weapon needs: buy a top, bottom, earrings and face accessory that give it, and start on your untradeables.
claims.say: 120-135, get enough secondary stat to equip your big weapon

claims.text: Do not count on your cape, gloves or shoes to meet weapon stat requirements, because you will swap them for attack versions later.
claims.say: dont use cape glove shoes for stats, you swap them later

claims.text: Jobs that use a shield should pick up a good one around level 135.
claims.say: if your job uses a shield, get one around 135

claims.text: At 200, buy a perfect weapon and keep upgrading attack cape, gloves and shoes; once those upgrades get very costly, buy tops, bottoms and earrings with secondary stats so you can move AP out of it.
claims.say: at 200 get a perfect weapon then keep upgrading cgs

claims.text: Late in the game, fill empty equipment slots such as the eye accessory.
claims.say: dont leave your eye accessory slot empty

claims.text: When your job can choose, wear a separate top and bottom rather than an overall, since two pieces give more of the secondary stats you need; overalls only make sense much later.
claims.say: top and bottom beat an overall for secondary stats

claims.text: As your gear adds more of your secondary stat, take AP out of that stat and move it into your main stat.
claims.say: as gear gives dex, reset that ap into your main stat

claims.text: As a rough rule, 4 to 5 points of main stat are worth about 1 weapon attack, depending on your job.
claims.say: 4-5 main stat is worth about 1 attack

claims.text: Scroll your pet equipment for extra speed and jump, or for HP.
claims.say: scroll your pet equips for speed jump or hp

claims.text: Warriors should check the DEX and accuracy on the tops and bottoms they buy, since accuracy can become a problem later on.
claims.say: warriors check dex and acc on tops and bottoms

claims.text: Warriors can scroll their own high-STR warrior gloves before buying a top attack glove; they are cheap and need no secondary stat to wear.
claims.say: warriors can scroll their own str gloves first, cheap

claims.text: When choosing the next upgrade, weigh rarity: a rare item with a smaller damage gain can be a better buy than a common one with a bigger gain.
claims.say: rare items hold value, think about that when upgrading

claims.text: If you reach 200 without a good Mark of Naricain or Horntail Necklace, make the pendant your top priority.
claims.say: no good pendant at 200? get one first

claims.text: A Smokescreen-focused Horntail party runs three or four Shadowers with a Paladin, a Bishop and a Buccaneer.
claims.say: shad ht run: 3-4 shads plus a pally, bishop and bucc

claims.text: Assign one player as the seduce target; that player goes through the portal first after each pre-head stage is cleared.
claims.say: your seduce target enters each portal first

claims.text: In the pre-head stages the Bishop should keep Holy Shield running and be ready to Dispel anyone hit by head skills.
claims.say: bishop keeps holy shield up and dispels after head skills

claims.text: Announce every Smokescreen in party chat during Horntail so casts never overlap.
claims.say: call out your smokes in chat so they don't overlap

claims.text: A Horntail leader should settle who is the seduce target and what the Bishop covers before the run starts.
claims.say: set who's sed target and bishop duties before going in

claims.text: New warriors start with little accuracy and miss a lot against higher-level monsters such as Ligators and Jr. Neckis, and a monster above your own level needs even more accuracy to hit reliably.
claims.say: warriors miss a lot early, ligators and jr neckis are the worst

claims.text: DEX adds accuracy, a bit under one point per DEX. Staying at minimum DEX for maximum damage needs accuracy gear and scrolls, which a fresh warrior does not have.
claims.say: dex gives accuracy, pure str needs accuracy gear first

claims.text: A newbie warrior can start with 20 to 23 base DEX, which is enough to hit early monsters like Green Mushrooms and Wild Boars.
claims.say: start a new warrior with about 20-23 dex to hit early mobs

claims.text: If a warrior still misses too much, raise base DEX to around 40 to 60 and rely on gear for the rest; going much past 60 base DEX cuts damage noticeably. Extra DEX can be reset to STR later with AP resets.
claims.say: if you still miss, 40-60 dex is the cap, more kills your damage

claims.text: The Fish Spear is a cheap early spear with built-in accuracy that is easy to equip, bought in Showa Town.
claims.say: fish spear from showa town is a cheap early accuracy spear

claims.text: Sniper Potions from potion shops add a little accuracy early on, and the stronger Sniper Pill is sold only in Ludibrium shops. Better ones in New Leaf City and Ludibrium cost more and need travel; none is a long-term fix.
claims.say: sniper potions help early accuracy, pills are only in ludibrium

claims.text: Wild Boars are a good spot for a warrior in the 20s up to about level 30: decent exp and lots of drops to sell to NPCs, which funds early scrolls and gear.
claims.say: wild boars at lvl 20-30 give decent exp and lots to sell

claims.text: The Balrog prequest starts with Manji's Request from Manji in Perion; he moves you on to Mu Young, then the Suspicious Man at the Stairway to the Underground Temple, then back to Mu Young and Manji.
claims.say: balrog prequest starts with manji in perion

claims.text: Next, pick up the note in the lower left of The Tunnel That Lost Light II and bring it to Mu Young, who sends you into a room to defeat a Jr. Balrog.
claims.say: grab the note bottom left of tunnel that lost light 2

claims.text: Leave Balrog's head alone at the start; once it is hit, it keeps attacking and casting dispel for the rest of the run.
claims.say: dont hit balrog's head early or it dispels all run

claims.text: Kill Balrog's right arm first, then the left arm, and finish with the head.
claims.say: balrog order: right arm, left arm, then the head

claims.text: Hit Balrog's left arm from against the left wall so you don't have to keep repositioning.
claims.say: hit balrog's left arm from the left wall

claims.text: On Balrog's head, melee should stand right next to it and ranged attackers should use the upper left platform so neither falls off.
claims.say: melee stand by the head, ranged use the upper left platform

claims.text: Amoria Party Quest groups usually do several runs back to back at about ten minutes each, so only join if you can stay until the last run.
claims.say: apq runs are ~10 min each, stay for all the runs

claims.text: In the Amoria Party Quest bonus, the apples from your own assigned boxes are yours; if your pet grabs one from someone else's box, give it back afterwards.
claims.say: apq bonus: loot only your own box, return stray apples

claims.text: Before entering Papulatus, players drop a coin at the door outside to show the room is in use; if you see one there, do not go in.
claims.say: drop a coin at pap's door to claim it, dont enter if one's there

claims.text: Turn pet auto-loot off during boss runs so you never pick up drops that belong to other players.
claims.say: turn pet loot off in bosses

claims.text: Agree on who gets which drops before a boss run starts; valuables are usually sold by the leader and split evenly, or one member buys the item out and pays everyone else their share.
claims.say: settle loot before the boss, sales get split evenly

claims.text: Zakum is summoned by dropping an Eye of Fire, so decide before the run who will drop it.
claims.say: someone drops an eye of fire to summon zak, decide who first

claims.text: In Zakum, parties usually use Heartstoppers on the arms, then one or two Onyx Apples for the main body, going back to Heartstoppers once the apples run out.
claims.say: zak: stoppers for the arms, onyx apples for the body

claims.text: A typical Zakum run takes roughly 20 to 30 minutes.
claims.say: a zak run takes about 20-30 min

claims.text: Horntail runs take one to one and a half hours; Heartstoppers are used on the preheads and Onyx Apples on the main body, though using apples on the preheads is becoming more common.
claims.say: ht: stoppers on the preheads, onyx apples for the body

claims.text: A Bishop in a boss party is expected to help with Dispel and Holy Shield, and with Genesis when the boss has several parts to hit.
claims.say: bishops in bosses: keep up dispel and holy shield

claims.text: A Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest run takes about 40 minutes; parties usually burn two Onyx Apples and finish on Heartstoppers, and the archer carries the heaviest load.
claims.say: cwkpq: ~40 min a run, 2 onyx apples then stoppers

claims.text: In Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest, whoever loots the Mark of Naricain drops sits out the bonus stage; pet loot is fine inside the bonus but should be off again for the next run.
claims.say: cwkpq: mon looter skips bonus, pet loot only in bonus

claims.text: Romeo and Juliet Party Quest needs a party of four at level 71 or higher, including one magician for the teleport maze and at least one member who can reach 120 jump through Haste, gear or a jump potion.
claims.say: r&j pq needs 4 people, one mage, and someone with 120 jump

claims.text: Romeo and Juliet Party Quest is very good exp for levels 71 to 90, and a team that knows the stages can finish a run in roughly 15 to 17 minutes.
claims.say: r&j pq is great exp for 71-90, about 15 min a run

claims.text: You can enter the Romeo and Juliet Party Quest from either Romeo's side or Juliet's side in Magatia; it makes no difference to the run, except that entering from Juliet's side ends you at Romeo's.
claims.say: romeo or juliet side, doesnt matter for the pq

claims.text: Stage 1 of Romeo and Juliet: click the books, quills and ink to find a switch, which opens the gate to stage 2, and a letter from Romeo or Juliet that you must keep until stage 4.
claims.say: r&j stage 1: find the switch and the letter, keep the letter

claims.text: Stage 3 of Romeo and Juliet: kill mobs and drop their drops onto the three leaking jars. One person handles the mobs while others drop, filling at most two jars at a time, one drop about every 4 seconds; dropping faster wastes items.
claims.say: r&j stage 3: drop items on jars, one every 4 sec or it wastes

claims.text: Stage 4 of Romeo and Juliet: give the stage 1 letter to the opposite NPC, then kill the mobs for a keycard that opens the doors on the left and right sides.
claims.say: r&j stage 4: hand in the letter, kill mobs for the keycard

claims.text: Behind the keycard doors: the right door leads to a teleport maze only a magician can use (one player), the left to a conveyor belt maze needing 120 jump (one or two players). Never send all four in or the run fails.
claims.say: right door mage maze, left door jump maze, never send all four

claims.text: In each Romeo and Juliet maze, break the boxes to find the single Document item (the other boxes give Unagi). One member stays outside to open the door; give both Documents to the NPC and the leader moves to stage 5.
claims.say: break boxes in the maze for the document, one stays outside

claims.text: Stage 5 of Romeo and Juliet: only the leader moves and talks to Yulete first, then the others may enter. Kill the monsters that spawn on the right, then press the switch hidden in the open book on Yulete's lectern.
claims.say: r&j stage 5: leader talks to yulete first, then hit the book switch

claims.text: For the Romeo and Juliet boss, the leader talks to Yulete and selects the second option to summon the angry version, kills it, then talks to whoever started the party quest to collect the reward.
claims.say: leader picks the 2nd option with yulete for the angry boss

claims.text: To get Yulete's Report in Romeo and Juliet, protect the NPC in the boss room; the Neo Huroids that attack him drop the report.
claims.say: guard the npc in the r&j boss room, neo huroids drop the report

claims.text: After Keeny's quest, his lab opens from the only sewer without water. Doing Yulete's Request, three quests done on the far left of labs 1 to 3, unlocks trading the marbles for Horus's Eye.
claims.say: yulete's request quests in labs 1-3 unlock the horus's eye trade

claims.text: A thief can only remove MP with an AP Reset while base MP stays above a minimum of about level x 14 + 148; MP from equipment does not count toward it.
claims.say: thief min mp is about level x14 + 148, gear mp doesnt count

claims.text: Each AP Reset taken out of MP removes about 12 MP, so you need at least 12 spare MP above your minimum for every reset you plan to use.
claims.say: each mp reset eats 12 mp, need 12 spare per reset

claims.text: For thieves, a fresh AP put into HP adds roughly 20 to 24 HP, while moving a point from MP to HP with an AP Reset adds roughly 16 to 20.
claims.say: thief: fresh ap to hp ~22, mp to hp reset ~18

claims.text: INT only matters in steps of 10 for MP gains, both on level-up and when adding AP to MP, so a washer stops at a round number such as 330 base INT.
claims.say: int only counts in steps of 10 for mp, stop at round numbers

claims.text: MP gained by leveling uses your total INT, including gear and Maple Warrior, but MP gained by putting AP into MP uses base INT only.
claims.say: int gear and mw help level-up mp, not ap-into-mp

claims.text: Double-clicking an AP Reset is a quick way to read your base MP without equipment, and it does not consume the item.
claims.say: double click an apr to check base mp, it doesnt use it

claims.text: To set up a thief for HP washing, add only the 25 DEX needed for the level 10 advancement and put every other point into INT.
claims.say: wash thief: 25 dex for job adv, rest into int

claims.text: Up to about level 69, put each fresh AP into HP and reset 12 MP into INT whenever you have MP to spare, building toward 330 base INT; the first chance is near level 22 and by the 60s all 5 AP can be washed.
claims.say: till 69 put fresh ap in hp, reset spare mp into int toward 330

claims.text: Once at 330 base INT, put every fresh AP into MP and reset 12 MP into LUK (or DEX for gear needs); each point nets about 32 MP, far more than leveling alone gives.
claims.say: at 330 int put fresh ap in mp, reset it into luk

claims.text: After banking enough MP, reset INT back down to 4 and into LUK, then put fresh AP into HP every level and spend the banked MP on MP-to-HP resets.
claims.say: after banking mp, reset int into luk, then fresh ap into hp

claims.text: Raising INT to 330 by level 70 and then only washing HP does not bank enough MP for 30k HP; you also need to MP wash with fresh AP from the 70s into the 130s.
claims.say: int to 330 then just hp washing wont reach 30k hp

claims.text: Maximum HP is capped at 30,000, so there is no point washing past that.
claims.say: hp caps at 30k

claims.text: Cheap early INT gear for a washer: a Wooden Wand at level 8, then a Green Bandana and Yellow Work Gloves at level 10.
claims.say: int gear: wooden wand at 8, green bandana and work gloves at 10

claims.text: Mid-level INT pieces for washing: Bathrobe for Men and Maple Shield at level 20, an INT cape at 25, and Spiegelmann's Necklace at 30.
claims.say: bathrobe and maple shield at 20, spiegelmann's necklace at 30

claims.text: Squishy Shoes, level 30 shoes that can carry a little INT, are a rare drop from King Slime at the end of Kerning City Party Quest.
claims.say: squishy shoes are a rare king slime drop in kpq

claims.text: Broken Glasses, an eye accessory with a small INT bonus, are earned by completing Ludibrium Party Quest 20 times.
claims.say: broken glasses come from doing lpq 20 times

claims.text: A washed character with weak attack can bring Onyx Apples for a large weapon attack boost during the 2nd and 3rd job advancement tests.
claims.say: weak from washing? bring onyx apples for the job adv tests

claims.text: Dalair, the medal NPC found in several towns, gives adventurer medals such as Veteran Adventurer at 70 and Master Adventurer at 120, each worth a point or two of INT for washers.
claims.say: dalair gives adventurer medals with a bit of int

claims.text: The White Belt is unlocked with 200 Mu Lung Dojo training points, and the Dojo itself requires level 25.
claims.say: white belt needs 200 dojo points, dojo opens at 25

claims.text: To enter Horntail's cave you need the Horntail prequest done and a Dragon Elixir; meet the party at Cave of Life - Entrance, use the elixir and drop down.
claims.say: use a dragon elixir at cave of life entrance and drop down

claims.text: Each entry uses up a Dragon Elixir, so frequent Horntail runs mean repeating the prequest.
claims.say: elixirs get used up, redo the prequest for more

claims.text: The party leader starts the Horntail sign-up at the Mark of the Squad, waits for everyone to sign, then uses it to enter, just like Zakum.
claims.say: leader signs up at mark of the squad like zakum

claims.text: An NPC on the left side of the sign-up room sends you back to the slate room, which helps when bringing more than 6 characters through.
claims.say: left npc in signup sends you back, helps get 7+ in

claims.text: Paladins get Holy Charge from the stump at the far right of Horntail's sign-up room; they can be badged past the Horntail Party Quest instead of running it.
claims.say: paladin: holy charge stump is far right of ht signup

claims.text: The Horntail Party Quest is required for the Bishop Genesis quest (check that the quest is asking for the life root first) and for the badge.
claims.say: htpq is needed for genesis and for the badge

claims.text: The Horntail Party Quest needs at least 3 characters, and you must reach its last stage to get the drops for the badge and Genesis quests.
claims.say: htpq needs 3+ and the last stage for the quest drops

claims.text: Dragon Elixirs stack as high as you like, so stock up ahead of time in case no Manon is around before a run.
claims.say: stock elixirs early, manon isn't always up

claims.text: When someone asks if you have an elixir for Horntail they mean a Dragon Elixir, not the ordinary Elixir potion.
claims.say: elixir for ht means dragon elixir, not the potion

claims.text: Movement speed is capped at 140; open the Detail view of the character stat window to see your current speed.
claims.say: speed caps at 140, check it under detail in your stats

claims.text: Mages who train by teleporting and casting should push speed to the cap so they reach the monsters at the edges of the map instead of leaving them alive.
claims.say: max your speed for telecasting so you dont miss edge mobs

claims.text: More speed can come from a Cash Shop pet equip, which has 7 upgrade slots, scrolled with pet equip speed scrolls.
claims.say: scroll your pet equip for speed, it has 7 slots

claims.text: The multi-pet quest only starts if a pet is summoned when you speak to Trainer Bartos, and it needs a Pet Snack bought from the Cash Shop.
claims.say: have your pet out when you talk to bartos, bring a pet snack

claims.text: Pet-Walking Road is entered from Henesys Park by pressing up at the cat statues.
claims.say: pet-walking road: henesys park, press up at the cat statues

claims.text: When you take out a second or third pet the game asks whether to swap your lead pet; pick cancel to keep the current one in front.
claims.say: summoning a 2nd pet? hit cancel to keep your lead pet

claims.text: The Owl of Minerva searches the Free Market and shows every shop currently selling the item you look up.
claims.say: use an owl of minerva to find who sells an item in fm

claims.text: Players write HTP for the Horntail Necklace, the pendant that comes from Horntail.
claims.say: htp means horntail necklace

claims.text: ZH or zhelm is chat shorthand for the Zakum Helmet, and ZK or zak means Zakum.
claims.say: zh or zhelm is the zakum helmet

claims.text: Cape shorthand: PAC is Pink Adventurer Cape, PGC is Pink Gaia Cape, and PuAC or PuGC are the purple versions.
claims.say: pac is pink adventurer cape, pgc is pink gaia cape

claims.text: Glove shorthand: BWG is Brown Work Gloves, YWG is Yellow Work Gloves, WG is Work Gloves and SCG is Stormcaster Gloves.
claims.say: bwg is brown work gloves, scg is stormcaster gloves

claims.text: Shoe shorthand: FS means Facestompers and YSS means Yellow Snowshoes.
claims.say: fs is facestompers, yss is yellow snowshoes

claims.text: Weapon shorthand: ST is the Stonetooth Sword and RK is the Red Katana.
claims.say: st is stonetooth sword, rk is red katana

claims.text: WS means White Scroll, while CS can mean Chaos Scroll or the Cash Shop depending on context.
claims.say: ws is white scroll, cs is chaos scroll or cash shop

claims.text: HS can mean the Heartstopper potion or the Holy Symbol buff; context tells which.
claims.say: hs is heartstopper or holy symbol

claims.text: EoF stands for Eye of Fire, the item used to summon Zakum.
claims.say: eof is eye of fire, you need it to summon zakum

claims.text: ACA is the Hero skill Advanced Combo Attack.
claims.say: aca is advanced combo attack, hero skill

claims.text: Advanced Charge is a passive Paladin skill whose job is to strengthen Charged Blow from White Knight, which is why players often call it ACB.
claims.say: advanced charge just buffs charged blow, people say acb

claims.text: HB means Hyper Body and MW means Maple Warrior.
claims.say: hb is hyper body, mw is maple warrior

claims.text: Party buff shorthand: SE is Sharp Eyes, SI is Speed Infusion and TL is Time Leap.
claims.say: se is sharp eyes, si is speed infusion, tl is time leap

claims.text: ME means Meso Explosion; MM can mean Monster Magnet or the Marksman job.
claims.say: me is meso explosion, mm is monster magnet or marksman

claims.text: Warrior skill shorthand: DR is Dragon Roar and BR is Brandish (BR can also mean a bathrobe).
claims.say: dr is dragon roar, br is brandish

claims.text: Thief skill shorthand: TT is Triple Throw, SHST is Shadow Stars, SHSH is Shadow Shifter and SS is often Smokescreen.
claims.say: tt is triple throw, shst shadow stars, shsh shadow shifter

claims.text: HH can mean the skill Heaven's Hammer or the Headless Horseman monster.
claims.say: hh is heaven's hammer or headless horseman

claims.text: MS can mean the skill Meteor Shower or a Maple Shield.
claims.say: ms is meteor shower or maple shield

claims.text: PQ shorthand: KPQ is Kerning City, LPQ Ludibrium, OPQ Orbis, HPQ Henesys and LMPQ the Ludibrium Maze party quest.
claims.say: kpq kerning, lpq ludi, opq orbis, hpq henesys, lmpq maze

claims.text: More PQ shorthand: APQ is Amoria, CPQ is Monster Carnival, GPQ is Guild Party Quest and CWKPQ is Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest.
