claims.say: apq amoria, cpq carnival, gpq guild, cwkpq crimsonwood

claims.text: Place shorthand: MP3 is Mysterious Path 3, NLC is New Leaf City and FM is the Free Market.
claims.say: mp3 is mysterious path 3, nlc new leaf city, fm free market

claims.text: Boss shorthand: HT means Horntail and PB means Pink Bean.
claims.say: ht is horntail, pb is pink bean

claims.text: Monster shorthand: BF is Bigfoot, and BGA and BGB are Bodyguard A and Bodyguard B.
claims.say: bf is bigfoot, bga and bgb are bodyguard a and b

claims.text: Job shorthand: AM Arch Mage, F/P and I/L the fire-poison and ice-lightning mages, BM Bowmaster, MM Marksman, NL Night Lord, CB Chief Bandit, DK Dragon Knight, DrK Dark Knight.
claims.say: nl night lord, bm bowmaster, drk dark knight, am arch mage

claims.text: Trade chat shorthand: B> buying, S> selling, LF> looking for, PC price check, C/O current offer, S/B starting bid, A/W auto win price.
claims.say: b> is buying, s> selling, c/o current offer, a/w auto win

claims.text: General chat shorthand: CC means change channel, CH is channel, KS is kill stealing, DC is a disconnect and JQ is a jump quest.
claims.say: cc means change channel, ks is kill stealing

claims.text: A tiny group struggles to finish Henesys PQ without heavy wave clear such as a warrior's Slash Blast or a pirate's Somersault Kick, and the exp is poor for the effort.
claims.say: hpq needs wave clear like slash blast, and the exp is meh

claims.text: In a very small Kerning PQ run the first stage is the slowest part; the later stages are straightforward.
claims.say: kpq stage 1 is the slow bit with a small group, rest is easy

claims.text: Ludibrium PQ needs one Mage for Teleport and one ranged character with real damage. The thief-portal part can be handled by any character with enough HP to survive the hits.
claims.say: lpq needs a mage for teleport and one solid ranged attacker

claims.text: A Corsair's Recoil Shot makes the stage 5 rope climb in Ludibrium PQ very fast, but Corsairs are rare, so do not count on having one.
claims.say: recoil shot makes lpq stage 5 ropes super quick

claims.text: Orbis PQ does not strictly need a Mage if someone has a maxed Flash Jump or Corsair Wings, but Haste or very high jump is required. Only the Sealed Room and On the Way Up parts need several characters moved.
claims.say: opq doesn't need a mage if you have flash jump, but need haste

claims.text: In the Ludibrium Maze the portals shift your room number: left adds 4, middle adds 7, right subtracts 3. Keep going through the middle portal and you will eventually reach the end room.
claims.say: maze portals: left +4, middle +7, right -3

claims.text: Romeo and Juliet PQ is worth running for the quest medal, which unlocks more quests for quest completion. Have the relevant quests in progress before you run it.
claims.say: do rnj pq for the medal, start the quests first

claims.text: Stages 5 and 6 of Romeo and Juliet PQ go much faster with Flash Jump and Haste, which Night Lords bring; a character with maxed movement stats can manage without.
claims.say: rnj stage 5 and 6 are easier with night lord haste and flash jump

claims.text: Keep a notepad handy for stage 6 of Romeo and Juliet PQ, which has to be memorised.
claims.say: keep a notepad for rnj stage 6

claims.text: For the stage 5 Wild Boars in Ellin Forest PQ, keep pet HP healing on and use Magic Guard.
claims.say: epq stage 5 boars hurt, keep magic guard and pet hp on

claims.text: A Shadower Rogue maxes Nimble Body and Dark Sight (with 3 in Disorder to unlock it) and takes Double Stab to about 9 as the early dagger attack; Lucky Seven only needs one point.
claims.say: shadower rogue: nimble body and dark sight max, double stab ~9

claims.text: Dark Sight keeps touch damage off you and is required to use Assassinate later, but bosses can still kill you inside it.
claims.say: dark sight stops touch damage and is needed for assassinate

claims.text: Disorder is used at level 1 mainly to pull a boss's attention off you, since a Shadower does not need it for damage.
claims.say: disorder is mostly for de-aggroing bosses

claims.text: Bandit order: a few points in Dagger Mastery and Dagger Booster first, max Savage Blow around 36-45, then max Haste, then finish Mastery and Booster, and put the remaining points into Steal.
claims.say: bandit: booster, savage blow max, haste, mastery, then steal

claims.text: Steal can lift any item from a monster's drop table, including monster cards and quest items, so a Shadower can help friends farm rare drops; it is not an area attack, so do not max it early for mobbing.
claims.say: steal can grab cards and quest items, great for helping friends

claims.text: Chief Bandit order: max Meso Explosion first for fast leveling, put 3 in Chakra to unlock Meso Guard, then max Band of Thieves, Assaulter, Meso Guard and Chakra; skip Shield Mastery and Pickpocket.
claims.say: chief bandit: meso explosion first, then bot, assaulter, meso guard

claims.text: Band of Thieves is the Chief Bandit's multi-target attack, hitting six targets when maxed; it stays useful in 4th job paired with Boomerang Step for mobbing.
claims.say: band of thieves is your 6 target mobbing skill

claims.text: Assaulter dashes through a monster and stuns it; use it to reposition at bosses or cross maps fast, including jump-casting during the Horntail wings and arms phase.
claims.say: assaulter is great for repositioning at bosses

claims.text: Shield Mastery is useless because a Dragon Khanjar has so little defense, and Pickpocket drops too little meso to matter, so leftover points can go into Endure.
claims.say: skip shield mastery and pickpocket, theyre dead skills

claims.text: At levels 72-81 a Shadower can use Meso Explosion on the Headless Horseman for fast exp.
claims.say: 72-81 bomb the headless horseman with meso explosion

claims.text: Bigfoot kills in one touch and has invincibility frames: aggro it safely, hide in Dark Sight, drop meso in open space, lure it past the stack and bomb once as it walks toward you, then repeat.
claims.say: bigfoot: aggro, dark sight, drop meso, bomb once as it walks over

claims.text: A faster but riskier Bigfoot method: drop meso near the left corner, wait until it walks fully into the wall, bomb twice, pause until it turns around, then bomb twice again and repeat.
claims.say: pin bigfoot at the left wall and bomb twice per turn, risky

claims.text: Shadower order: max Assassinate and Boomerang Step first, then Smokescreen by about level 150, Shadow Shifter, Maple Warrior 10, Hero's Will 5 and finally Taunt.
claims.say: shadower 4th job: assassinate, boomerang step, smokescreen first

claims.text: Assassinate is the single-target attack and needs Dark Sight active; interrupting it makes you dash and land an extra critical hit, and it ignores damage reflect.
claims.say: assassinate needs dark sight and goes through reflect

claims.text: Boomerang Step is the Shadower's main mobbing skill, hitting up to four targets twice, and its invincibility frame starts the moment you press it so it doubles as a dodge.
claims.say: boomerang step mobs 4 targets and has an i-frame to dodge

claims.text: Smokescreen makes everyone standing in it immune to nearly all damage, environmental included, but not to status effects like seal or darkness, and reflect damage still hurts.
claims.say: smokescreen blocks damage but not seal or darkness

claims.text: Hero's Will cures Seduce, which makes it valuable for Shadowers in seduce-heavy boss fights like Horntail.
claims.say: hero's will cures seduce, worth having for horntail

claims.text: Taunt hits six mobs and raises their drop rate but also cuts the damage they take, so it can cost an extra hit; it fails if it kills the mob, so do not use it as a finisher, and it needs Shadow Shifter 10.
claims.say: taunt boosts drops but dont use it as the killing blow

claims.text: Venomous Stab does not work on bosses and Ninja Ambush deals tiny damage and needs a prequest, so neither is worth skill points for a Shadower.
claims.say: skip venomous stab and ninja ambush

claims.text: A Shadower keeps base DEX at 25 and STR at 4 and puts the rest into LUK, adding a little DEX or STR only if a piece of LUK gear cannot be equipped.
claims.say: shadower: 25 dex, 4 str, rest in luk

claims.text: Shadowers reach max attack speed with just Dagger Booster, so Speed Infusion from a party only saves you from casting booster yourself.
claims.say: shadowers dont need speed infusion, booster is enough

claims.text: For a single target, macro Assassinate together with Boomerang Step; you must already be in Dark Sight to start Assassinate.
claims.say: single target: assassinate into boomerang step from dark sight

claims.text: For three or more targets use a Boomerang Step plus Band of Thieves macro, and hold a direction key while spamming it to creep forward between hits.
claims.say: 3+ mobs: boomerang step plus band of thieves

claims.text: The only shield worth using is the Dragon Khanjar, needing 150 DEX and 75 STR, which matches or exceeds any dagger's needs, so any dagger will do and only its attack matters.
claims.say: dragon khanjar is the shield, any dagger works so pick by attack

claims.text: A Horntail Necklace is the comfier pendant for most Shadowers, as its stats help reach DEX and STR and add avoidability; Mark of Naricain needs 150 DEX plus 75 STR for the shield, so chase it only when rich and well geared.
claims.say: horntail necklace is easier for shadowers, mark of naricain is endgame

claims.text: Spectrum Goggles are an easy eye accessory because high-DEX ones are cheap and help you equip other items; mixed STR, DEX and LUK pairs exist but cost more.
claims.say: spectrum goggles with good dex help you wear your gear

claims.text: The well portal in Korean Folk Town sits a little left of its graphic; step slightly left if it won't take you.
claims.say: kft well portal is a bit left of where it looks

claims.text: The elevator between Ludibrium and Korean Folk Town means waiting for it to arrive, so allow extra time.
claims.say: the ludi to kft elevator has a wait, plan for it

claims.text: Keeping return scrolls for Ellinia or Kerning City on you is handy, and they also get you out of Sleepywood quickly.
claims.say: keep an ellinia or kerning return scroll on you

claims.text: Monster Carnival is started by talking to Spiegelmann in Kerning City, Orbis or Ludibrium; the first carnival is for levels 30-50 and the second for levels 51-70.
claims.say: talk to spiegelmann for carnival pq, 30-50 first and 51-70 second

claims.text: Two parties compete for 10 minutes: killing monsters earns Carnival Points, which you spend to summon monsters on the other team, and the party with more CP at the end wins. Both sides still kill as fast as they can for exp.
claims.say: carnival: kill mobs for cp, spend cp to summon mobs on the other team

claims.text: Play 2v2 in Room 3 or 4, with Room 4 preferred because it has more monsters, and 3v3 in Room 5 or 6; Rooms 1 and 2 are oversized and rarely used.
claims.say: 2v2 use room 4, 3v3 use room 5 or 6, skip rooms 1 and 2

claims.text: Parties often agree before entering to swap wins, taking turns winning so both sides keep getting the larger winner exp.
claims.say: agree to swap wins in carnival before you go in

claims.text: In Monster Carnival you summon monsters, cast skills or place protectors with the F1 to F10 hotkeys, and the Tab key switches between the Mobs, Skills and Protectors lists.
claims.say: carnival: f1-f10 summon, tab switches mobs/skills/protectors

claims.text: Carnival monsters drop CP pickups, party potions that heal or cure the whole team, Cube of Darkness items that afflict the enemy, Stunners, and Maple Coins that can be exchanged for rewards.
claims.say: carnival drops party potions for the team and cubes for the enemy

claims.text: Maple Coins buy Spiegelmann's Necklace for 50 coins, and Spiegelmann's Marble for 40 coins. The marble can only be used on that necklace.
claims.say: spiegelmann sells necklace for 50 maple coins, marble for 40

claims.text: For farming CP in Room 4, a Fighter is the recommended class: he can mostly spam Slash Blast to clear Rombots without needing very expensive gear or complicated skill rotations.
claims.say: fighter is a good cp farmer in room 4, just spam slash blast

claims.text: Brawlers have the highest CP potential because they move well and can reposition Rombots with Corkscrew Blow, but reaching it takes very expensive gear, so the extra investment is rarely worth it for CP farming.
claims.say: brawler can farm the most cp with corkscrew blow but gear is pricey

claims.text: For a CPQ Fighter a good two-handed sword is the practical choice: it is cheaper, easier to get and has longer reach, while a one-handed sword with a weapon attack shield can reach a higher attack range but costs much more.
claims.say: a 2h sword is cheaper and has more reach for fighter cpq

claims.text: Put Stunner, Mini Cube of Darkness and Cube of Darkness on your pet's excluded items list so you do not pick up the harmful ones. Optionally also exclude the party potions, since teammates may need them.
claims.say: set pet to ignore stunner and cubes of darkness in carnival

claims.text: In the Ludibrium dollhouse quest from the guards on the tower's first floor, ten dollhouses look nearly identical and you must find and attack the one real one.
claims.say: only one of the ten dollhouses is real, find it and break it

claims.text: The real dollhouse has a thick white shine, a few pixels tall, running across the whole top of its handle; the fakes show only a thin line over most of the handle.
claims.say: real dollhouse: thick shine across the whole handle top

claims.text: The Crimsonwood Keep prequests are for level 120 and up. Bring lots of HP and MP potions, a pet with auto-potion, return scrolls for New Leaf City and elsewhere, about 200 All Cure Potions, and patience.
claims.say: cwkpq prequests need lvl 120, bring pots, return scrolls and all cures

claims.text: The prequest chain has three parts: the first five quests are monster kills and drops, the next six are walking and talking between NPCs, and the final quests are more monster kills before you can enter the party quest.
claims.say: cwkpq preq is 5 kill quests, lots of errands, then more kills

claims.text: Subani's Legacy - Transgression: gather 50 Hyper Glyphs dropped by Electrophants in the MesoGears Ice Chamber, about four maps from John Barricade, then turn them in.
claims.say: transgression wants 50 hyper glyphs from electrophants in ice chamber

claims.text: Subani's Legacy - Deliverance: collect 50 MesoGear Map Pieces from I.AM Robots on the Masteria Mountain Slopes, about three maps to the right of New Leaf City, and return them to John Barricade.
claims.say: deliverance wants 50 mesogear map pieces from i.am robots

claims.text: Stemming the Tide sends you from Jack to Lukan on the Phantom Forest road; the climb there is much easier with Flash Jump or Teleport.
claims.say: lukan in phantom forest is a rough climb without flash jump/teleport

claims.text: Storming the Castle sends you into the Hall of Mastery to kill 75 each of Windraiders (bottom left), Firebrands (middle left) and Nightshadows (top left), then back to Lukan.
claims.say: 75 windraider bottom, 75 firebrand mid, 75 nightshadow top

claims.text: Finishing Storming the Castle completes the prequests and lets you enter the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest with a party.
claims.say: finish storming the castle and you can enter cwkpq with a party

claims.text: Making the Path to the Sea from Ralph: kill 120 Slimy in Ghost Ship 2 and 120 Selkie Jr. in Mysterious Path 3, then return to Ralph.
claims.say: path to the sea: 120 slimy then 120 selkie jr

claims.text: The Great Secret Reveals: kill 300 Mr. Anchor in Ghost Ship 6, and keep free ETC space before turning in to Ralph, since the reward goes into your ETC tab.
claims.say: great secret reveals: 300 mr anchor, leave etc space

claims.text: The Mu Lung Dojo is reached by taking the ride from Orbis to Mu Lung, then going to the bulletin board on the right and taking the portal beside it to the lobby.
claims.say: dojo is in mu lung, ride there from orbis then go right to the lobby

claims.text: Before real Dojo runs you must complete a short practice run first, which takes only a few minutes.
claims.say: do the quick dojo practice run first before real runs

claims.text: A mount or Haste is practically mandatory for Dojo runs, because getting between floors quickly saves a lot of time over an hour of runs.
claims.say: use a mount or haste in dojo, it saves tons of time

claims.text: The ideal Dojo party has a Bishop with Resurrection, an Archer with Sharp Eyes and a mix of strong single-target attackers such as Night Lords, Corsairs and Shadowers. A Buccaneer with Speed Infusion is also very welcome.
claims.say: best dojo party: bishop, sharp eyes archer, night lords and shadowers

claims.text: Parties with no Bishop or with several Archmages do poorly in the Dojo; Archmages are the weakest choice because the Dojo is one big single-target fight, so bring one Bishop and add single-target attackers instead.
claims.say: dont stack archmages in dojo, bring one bishop and single target dps

claims.text: Sharp Eyes from an Archer is the most valuable damage buff for the party, with a Buccaneer's Speed Infusion second; Speed Infusion boosts Warriors and Corsairs but does not help Night Lords.
claims.say: sharp eyes is the best buff, speed infusion doesnt help night lords

claims.text: For survival in Dojo, a Bishop's Heal and Resurrection come first; a Buccaneer's Time Leap gives the Bishop another Resurrection, Dark Knights add HP with Hyper Body and Shadowers reduce damage with Smokescreen.
claims.say: bishop heal and resurrection keep dojo parties alive, time leap helps

claims.text: Against Manon and Griffey, have one player alone push the boss to the right while nobody else attacks, so the push is not cancelled; the Bishop stays left re-casting Heal and Maple Warrior and heals anyone hit by a 1/1.
claims.say: manon and griffey: one person pins right, bishop heals from the left

claims.text: If a Dojo boss lands a 1/1 on you, either pick up a healing potion from the ground or walk left so the Bishop can heal you.
claims.say: hit by a 1/1 in dojo? grab a potion or go left for the bishop heal

claims.text: Leviathan in the Dojo has no dispel and no 1/1, so the Bishop can safely spend that fight filling the last of the energy bar.
claims.say: dojo leviathan is safe, bishop can fill the bar there

claims.text: Dojo parties work best when people agree before starting who pins bosses, the order of Smokescreens and the order of bamboo rains, and when they do not multitask or leave early, which slows everyone's run.
claims.say: agree on pinner and bamboo order before a dojo run, dont leave early

claims.text: The Ellin Forest Party Quest prequests can only be started after you have fully completed the Papulatus prequests.
claims.say: finish the papulatus prequests before the epq ones

claims.text: Eastern Region of Mossy Tree Forest is an alternative for farming Mossy Snails: it has fewer monsters but is easier to move around in.
claims.say: eastern region of mossy tree forest has fewer mobs but easier to move

claims.text: You could buy most of the ETC items for these prequests ahead of time, but it is pointless because you have to go back and kill the monsters for the quests anyway. Take it one stage at a time.
claims.say: dont bother buying the etc early, youll kill the mobs anyway

claims.text: Once this prequest chain is finished you can enter the Ellin Forest Party Quest with a party of four to six.
claims.say: after the prequests you can run epq with 4 to 6 people

claims.text: The prequest for Scarlion and Targa is a chain of quests from Lam in Kampung Village, Malaysia.
claims.say: scarga prequest is lam's quest chain in kampung village

claims.text: Pick up every Toy Plane you see while farming Fantasy Theme Park 2, because a later Lam quest asks for them.
claims.say: keep any toy planes you loot, you'll need them later

claims.text: Off to the City has you kill 250 Vikerolas and bring back 200 Viking Helmets from Fantasy Theme Park 3.
claims.say: off to the city: 250 vikerolas, 200 viking helmets in ftp3

claims.text: Gift for Brother needs 200 Toy Planes from Booper Scarlions in Fantasy Theme Park 2.
claims.say: gift for brother: 200 toy planes from booper scarlions

claims.text: Every etc item in Lam's quest chain can also be bought from other players instead of farmed.
claims.say: you can buy the scarga etcs instead of farming

claims.text: Scarlion drops STR and DEX helmets while Targa drops INT and LUK helmets, so you could fight only the one whose helm suits your class.
claims.say: scarlion: str/dex helms, targa: int/luk helms

claims.text: Parties usually summon both bosses together, nicknamed Scarga, since members want helms from different bosses.
claims.say: most parties summon both, that's what scarga means

claims.text: The groom proposes by double-clicking the engagement ring box in the Etc tab, and the bride accepts.
claims.say: double-click the ring box to propose

claims.text: The bride enters through Assistant Bonnie, and talking to High Priest John starts the ceremony; guests can't join once it begins.
claims.say: enter via assistant bonnie, high priest john starts it

claims.text: The cake room after the ceremony can't be skipped; wait out its timer and you are married.
claims.say: cake room can't be skipped, just wait it out

claims.text: Amoria Party Quest needs a full party of 6; it won't let 5 or fewer enter.
claims.say: apq needs a full party of 6

claims.text: The main reason to run Amoria Party Quest is Onyx Apples from the bonus stage: they restore most HP and MP and give a big weapon and magic attack boost for 10 minutes, strong for bosses and PQs.
claims.say: apq is for onyx apples, huge att boost for bosses

claims.text: Onyx Apples sell for a good price to other players.
claims.say: onyx apples sell well

claims.text: Before joining Scarlion or Targa runs you must finish the quest chain from Lam in Kampung Village, Malaysia; it opens at level 85 and the last quest needs level 90.
claims.say: do lam's quests in kampung village, starts at 85, last one at 90

claims.text: The first quest, Lam Wants To See The World, needs a Lucky Bus Ticket dropped by Yabber Doo, the bus-shaped mob in Fantasy Theme Park 2; its random reward is worth having.
claims.say: lucky bus ticket drops from yabber doo in fantasy theme park 2

claims.text: After the first quest, Lam's chain continues with Off to the City, Gift For Brother and Merry-Go-Round in Kampung, all available at level 85.
claims.say: after that: off to the city, gift for brother, merry-go-round

claims.text: The final quest, Off to the Fantasy Theme Park, needs level 90 and can be repeated; each clear gives 2 Spirit of Fantasy Theme Park, the item used to summon Scarlion and Targa.
claims.say: off to the fantasy theme park is repeatable, gives summon spirits

claims.text: Off to the Fantasy Theme Park asks for Rodeo's Master, an etc drop from Rodeo, the hippo-like mob found in Muddy Banks 2 and Hibiscus Road 1.
claims.say: rodeo's master drops from rodeo in muddy banks 2 or hibiscus road 1

claims.text: Corsairs mob poorly until about level 150 and the early fourth-job grind is rough, but they pay it back with very high single-target damage later.
claims.say: corsair is a slow start but hits crazy hard later

claims.text: Battleship is a fourth-job mount: it slows you and blocks bullet skills like Rapid Fire, but unlocks Battleship Cannon for one target and Battleship Torpedo for groups.
claims.say: battleship slows you and blocks rapid fire but unlocks cannon

claims.text: Ship damage never heals except by breaking the ship or logging out; map changes, channel changes, the Cash Shop and even dying keep it, so go into a boss with a healthy ship.
claims.say: ship damage stays until it breaks or you relog

claims.text: Dismounting means hopping off Battleship just before a hit lands so only you take the damage; it takes effect the instant you press the key, so watch boss animations and react.
claims.say: hop off the ship right before a hit so only you take damage

claims.text: Attacks that cut HP to 1 (1/1s) are the main thing that wipes chunks of ship HP, so learn those animations and dismount for them.
claims.say: watch for 1/1 attacks, they wipe your ship hp

claims.text: Hopping off the ship in the middle of a laggy skill can cancel its animation delay, a useful speed trick for experienced Corsairs.
claims.say: hopping off ship mid skill can cancel animation lag

claims.text: Corsair's main stat is DEX with STR secondary; about 23 base STR by level 100 lets you equip most gear, as little as 4 works if you only use Maple guns, and going past roughly 50 base STR is wasteful.
claims.say: dex main, around 23 base str is comfy for gear

claims.text: Scroll gear with DEX early on, but late game scroll STR and keep base DEX as high as you can, because Maple Warrior scales with base stats and ignores equipment stats.
claims.say: late game keep base dex high, maple warrior uses base stats

claims.text: The strongest guns past level 100 need around 100 to 110 STR, which you reach by scrolling STR onto gear, so a low base STR is fine and beats a pure-DEX build with a Maple gun at 4th job.
claims.say: best guns need 100+ str, scroll str on gear instead of base

claims.text: As a Pirate headed for Corsair, max Double Shot, Dash and Bullet Time; Somersault Kick and Flash Fist are not worth points for a Gunslinger.
claims.say: pirate: max double shot, dash and bullet time

claims.text: Double Shot is your main attack until third job; its animation is very short so it is easy to jump-fire, and it gains range as you level it, so max it early.
claims.say: max double shot early, its fast and gains range per level

claims.text: Dash is a short self speed buff that ends when you attack or turn; on small platforms jump, turn in midair and double-tap a direction to start it without sliding off.
claims.say: dash cancels on attack or turning, start it after a midair turn

claims.text: Bullet Time gives accuracy and avoidability; the accuracy mostly matters for Brawlers since a Gunslinger's DEX already hits fine, while the avoidability is the useful part for you.
claims.say: bullet time is mainly for the avoid on a gunslinger

claims.text: Corsairs are good at quests and monster card hunting in low to mid level areas thanks to long area attacks and summons, even though the job is mostly about bossing.
claims.say: corsair is solid for cards and quests in low areas

claims.text: Battleship Cannon is the strongest single-target projectile and hits well even with average gear and no party buffs apart from Maple Warrior, so Corsairs are self-sufficient bosses.
claims.say: battleship cannon hits hard with no buffs needed, only maple warrior

claims.text: A corsair's Battleship mount has its own HP bar, shown as a buff. Hits taken while mounted damage the ship instead of the character, and potions or heals cannot restore it.
claims.say: battleship has its own hp bar and pots wont heal it

claims.text: Corsairs protect the ship by dismounting just before a big boss hit lands. That means learning each boss's attack animations, especially the 1/1 attacks that drop HP and MP to 1, and dodging them in time.
claims.say: dismount right before a big boss hit so the ship takes none

claims.text: A 1/1 boss attack deals roughly your current HP, and the ship soaks it. Keeping current HP lower, for example with smaller potions, makes a mistimed dismount cost less ship HP.
claims.say: 1/1 hits for about your current hp, lower hp = less ship damage

claims.text: Pro corsairs do not chase the 30k max HP other attackers want. Around 17k to 19k is the usual aim: enough to survive most single hits, yet low enough that 1/1 attacks do not wreck the ship.
claims.say: corsairs want like 17-19k hp not 30k, 1/1s hurt the ship less

claims.text: Every 10 INT you have at the moment you level up gives 1 extra MP. AP Resets can then move that MP into max HP, which is HP washing, so washers keep a lot of base INT while leveling.
claims.say: every 10 int when you level gives 1 mp, you wash that into hp

claims.text: After any base INT needed for washing is done, a corsair puts all remaining AP into DEX. STR is only the secondary stat, kept just high enough to equip gear.
claims.say: corsair ap: all dex, only enough str to wear your gear

claims.text: Maple Warrior only boosts base stats, not stats from gear. So keep the main stat as base DEX and let scrolls and gear supply the STR needed to equip things.
claims.say: maple warrior only buffs base stats so keep dex base, gear gives str

claims.text: Corsair damage and abilities are poor until 4th job, and a washer's high base INT hurts it further, so it is best to get leeched to around level 120 or higher before relying on your own damage.
claims.say: corsair is weak before 4th job, get leeched to 120ish first

claims.text: Weapon attack is usually the most efficient damage per meso, so upgrade the gun before other slots. Guns resell slowly, so buy a decent one once or save for a good one instead of upgrading constantly.
claims.say: upgrade your gun first, best dmg per meso and dont swap often

claims.text: Get a Zakum Helmet early and scroll it toward 35 to 40 DEX. It is cheap and painless if you join runs, and it is one of the first near end-game pieces a corsair completes.
claims.say: zakum helm scrolled for dex is a great early corsair upgrade

claims.text: For the eye slot, Broken Glasses from the Ludibrium Party Quest are the best pick, with Spectrum Goggles a fine alternative. Eye slot stats are very pricey, so do not overspend on it.
claims.say: broken glasses from ludi pq are the best cheap eye item

claims.text: Corsairs have low avoid and no Stance, so on bosses like Horntail where hits knock you off platforms they struggle, especially when playing beside mules or several other attackers.
claims.say: corsair has no stance so horntail knocks you off platforms easy

claims.text: The Battleship's HP grows with every level, so a ship that breaks often at first becomes sturdier as the corsair levels up.
claims.say: your ship gets tankier every level, dont sweat early breaks

claims.text: Coolie Zombies are undead, so Heal hits them hard and lets Clerics and Priests clear their maps quickly.
claims.say: coolies are undead, heal wrecks them as a cleric

claims.text: Coolie Zombies live in four maps, Forest of Dead Trees I to IV; the first and third are the author's favourites.
claims.say: forest of dead trees 1 and 3 are the nicest coolie maps

claims.text: To reach the Coolies from El Nath, walk through Ice Valley II, Sharp Cliff I and II, Wolf Territory I and II, Dangerous Cliff, Wolf Territory III to V, and on into Forest of Dead Trees I.
claims.say: walk el nath, ice valley 2, sharp cliffs, wolf territory to coolies

claims.text: To use a Teleport Rock, double-click it and choose Add Map while standing in the map you want saved; later double-click, pick the saved map and Move. You can also type a character name to go to that player.
claims.say: double click the rock, add map, later pick it and hit move

claims.text: With a Priest in the party, a Mystic Door cast at the Coolie maps is the quickest way to shuttle between El Nath and the training spot.
claims.say: a priest's mystic door is the fastest way back to coolies

claims.text: Coolie Zombies drop Zombie's Lost Tooth, an ETC that players want for the Orbis ETC exchange quests, so stacks of it can be sold.
claims.say: coolies drop zombie's lost tooth, people buy it for orbis quests

claims.text: Classes other than Clerics can train on Coolie Zombies too, but how efficient it is varies and some jobs have better spots at that level.
claims.say: non clerics can do coolies too, just not as well

claims.text: A Corsair's base HP is too low to survive hits from several bosses, so without HP washing it either cannot join them or can only manage them at much higher levels.
claims.say: sair hp is too low for some bosses so u need to hp wash

claims.text: HP washing means piling up max MP through INT stat points and INT gear, then using AP resets to turn MP points into HP; each wash costs some MP and gives some HP.
claims.say: stack int for mp then ap reset mp into hp, thats a wash

claims.text: How much INT to carry before washing depends on the HP goal: modest boss goals need roughly 150 to 180 INT, while chasing the highest HP needs around 300 base INT plus decent INT gear. The author needed more than first expected.
claims.say: plan way more int than u think, like 300 base for big hp goals

claims.text: Put all of the INT AP in at once instead of adding it gradually; adding it piecemeal cost the author a few hundred HP in the final total.
claims.say: put all your int in at once, adding it slowly costs hp

claims.text: Put your INT gear on right before a level up so the MP gained on that level is larger, since that MP is what you later wash into HP.
claims.say: wear ur int gear right before lvl up for more mp to wash

claims.text: A Zakum Helmet scrolled for INT makes a strong hat for a wash set, alongside scrolled INT capes, overalls, shields and earrings.
claims.say: scroll a zhelm for int, great hat for washing

claims.text: Putting AP into INT is usually cheaper than buying INT equipment that has only a few more INT points, because the price premium for those last points is huge.
claims.say: dumping ap into int beats paying a lot for slightly better int gear

claims.text: Most people take their extra INT back out around levels 135 to 145 for bossing, but washing a Corsair is slow, so the author kept INT much longer and removed most of it around levels 153 to 161.
claims.say: most take int off around 135-145 but sairs can keep it longer

claims.text: While riding the Battleship, one-hit-to-1HP boss attacks hurt the ship in proportion to your HP, so washing far beyond what a boss needs just makes the ship take bigger hits. Keep HP moderate until tougher bosses require more.
claims.say: dont wash past what the boss needs or ur ship eats bigger hits

claims.text: At the start of 4th job, put one point each into Rapid Fire, Battleship and Battleship Cannon, then decide whether to build for mobbing or bossing before spending the rest.
claims.say: 4th job: 1 pt each in rapid fire, battleship, cannon first

claims.text: For a bossing Corsair, spend 4th job SP in this order: Battleship, Battleship Cannon, Bullseye, Rapid Fire, Battleship Torpedo, Elemental Boost, then Maple Warrior.
claims.say: bossing sair sp: battleship, cannon, bullseye, rapid fire first

claims.text: For a mob-farming Corsair, spend 4th job SP in this order: Battleship, Battleship Cannon, Battleship Torpedo, Bullseye, Elemental Boost, Rapid Fire, then Maple Warrior.
claims.say: mobbing sair sp: battleship, cannon, torpedo, bullseye first

claims.text: The Battleship's HP grows with your level and it never heals on its own; it only comes back by breaking and waiting out the cooldown or by relogging.
claims.say: ship hp doesnt heal itself, only a break or relog resets it

claims.text: Hop off the Battleship and back on to dodge heavy or one-hit-kill boss attacks; remounting is quick enough that you lose very little damage time.
claims.say: hop off the ship for 1/1 attacks, remounting is quick

claims.text: Against bosses that have a one-hit-to-1HP attack, cancel Hyper Body if your own HP can survive the hit, and memorize each boss's 1/1 animations ahead of time.
claims.say: cancel hyper body vs 1/1 bosses if ur hp can take it

claims.text: The opening of Horntail's main body is the hardest part for a Corsair because many attack animations come at once; keep your eyes on the belly area rather than darting around so you catch each one.
claims.say: watch ht's belly to catch all the attack animations as a sair

claims.text: Horntail gets much easier once its right head is dead, since most attacks are easy to avoid after that; when only the hands remain it stops attacking and you can stay on the ship.
claims.say: ht gets way easier once the right head is dead

claims.text: A Corsair does best in a Horntail run with two Shadowers, a Buccaneer and a Hero; one Shadower with two Buccaneers also works, but a single Shadower and no Buccaneer is the worst setup. More Smokescreen means a safer run.
claims.say: best ht party for a sair: 2 shads, a bucc and a hero

claims.text: A Corsair is a poor first character for someone planning to wash: it is weak and slow to level once party quests are done. Build a sturdier main first and leech the Corsair up through boss runs.
claims.say: dont make a sair ur first char, lvl a sturdier one first

claims.text: Of the beginner skills only Nimble Feet really matters, so put its 3 points there. The other beginner skills are mostly party tricks.
claims.say: nimble feet is the only beginner skill worth points

claims.text: First-job magician order: Improving MP Recovery to 5, Improved MaxMP Increase to 10, then Magic Claw to 20, leftover into more MP recovery, and Magic Guard to 20 once you can afford to use it.
claims.say: magician 1st job: mp skills first, then magic claw 20

claims.text: I/L wizard order: Thunder Bolt to 30 first, then Teleport 20, Cold Beam 30, MP Eater 20 and Meditation 20, with a single point in Slow.
claims.say: il wizard: max thunder bolt first, then teleport and cold beam

claims.text: Put one point in Cold Beam early so an I/L wizard can fight a Jr. Boogie one on one without getting sealed, since the freeze stops it from casting.
claims.say: 1 point in cold beam early so jr boogie cant seal you

claims.text: I/L mage order: Ice Strike to 30 first, then Element Amplification and Spell Booster, Seal, Thunder Spear to 30 and Partial Resistance to 20. Seal needs only 1 point early because ice mages freeze enemies instead.
claims.say: il mage: ice strike 30 first, then amplification and booster

claims.text: Element Composition is a weak skill for both I/L and F/P mages, so one point is plenty. Cold Beam for ice mages and Fire Arrow for fire mages are stronger single-target options.
claims.say: element composition is bad, 1 point at most

claims.text: Thunder Spear is a niche I/L single-target skill, best against Papulatus, the Headless Horseman and Poison Golem before Chain Lightning, and nearly useless afterward. Magic Armor is a fine alternative dump.
claims.say: thunder spear only matters before you get chain lightning

claims.text: I/L arch mage: 1 point each in Blizzard and Chain Lightning, early Maple Warrior, then both to 30, then Ice Demon, Ifrit, Infinity, Big Bang, Hero's Will, Mana Reflection. Stop Blizzard once it 2-hits skeletons to save MP.
claims.say: il arch mage: blizzard + chain lightning, then ice demon, ifrit, infinity

claims.text: An I/L arch mage with Chain Lightning is perfectly capable of soloing Papulatus at around level 130.
claims.say: il arch mage can solo papu around lv130 with chain lightning

claims.text: F/P wizard order: Fire Arrow to 30 first (great for Monster Carnival), then Teleport 20, Poison Breath 30, then MP Eater and Meditation 20, with one point in Slow. MP Eater waits because F/P has no AoE to refund MP from.
claims.say: fp wizard: fire arrow 30 first, then teleport, poison breath

claims.text: F/P wizards max Teleport before Poison Breath: Poison Breath is not used until about level 56, and its poor accuracy makes training on monsters far above your level painful.
claims.say: max teleport before poison breath, its accuracy is awful early

claims.text: F/P mage order: Poison Mist to 30 first, one point in Explosion for AoE until Mist is strong enough to leave mobs at 1 HP, then Element Amplification, Spell Booster, Seal to 20 and Partial Resistance to 20.
claims.say: fp mage: poison mist 30 first, 1 explosion, then amp and booster

claims.text: F/P arch mage: 1 point each in Paralyze and Meteor Shower, early Maple Warrior, then both to 30, then Fire Demon, Elquines, Infinity, Big Bang, Hero's Will, Mana Reflection. Stop Meteor Shower at your kill cutoff to save MP.
claims.say: fp arch mage: meteor + paralyze, then elquines and infinity

claims.text: Fire Demon's burn does not stack with poison, but one point in it is worth taking because it makes non-boss monsters neutral to every element except ice.
claims.say: fire demon dot doesnt stack with poison but 1 point is useful

claims.text: Cleric order: Heal to 30 first, one early MP Eater point since it refunds MP when healing groups, then Teleport 20, MP Eater 20, Invincible 20 and Bless 20. Holy Arrow is the useless dump.
claims.say: cleric: max heal first, 1 mp eater early, then teleport and bless

claims.text: Priest order: Holy Symbol to 30, Shining Ray, Doom to 30, then Mystic Door, Dispel, Elemental Resistance and Summon Dragon. Doom beats Elemental Resistance since it is needed against holy-resistant and immune monsters.
claims.say: priest: holy symbol 30, then doom 30 before elemental resistance

claims.text: Doom can hit more than six enemies if cast from a rope some distance above them: they shrink, their hitboxes drop, and monsters further away get included.
claims.say: cast doom from a rope above them to hit more than 6 mobs

claims.text: Max Holy Shield before Bahamut if your Bishop focuses on party bosses like Zakum. Bahamut suits semi-AFK farming and adds DPS, but Bishop damage stays low either way.
claims.say: bishop doing zakum runs should max holy shield before bahamut

claims.text: Hunter and Crossbowman: Mastery to 19 and Booster 6 first, then the main attack (Arrow Bomb or Iron Arrow) to 30, Booster 20, Power Knock-Back 20, Soul Arrow, Focus 20. One Power Knock-Back point helps in Monster Carnival.
claims.say: hunter/xbow: mastery and booster first, then arrow bomb or iron arrow

claims.text: Ranger and Sniper should max Strafe before Mortal Blow or the 3rd-job attack (Arrow Rain or Arrow Eruption) so they can fight Balrog earlier.
claims.say: ranger/sniper: max strafe first so you can do balrog sooner

claims.text: Bowmaster order: Sharp Eyes and Hurricane to 30 first, then Phoenix, Bow Expert and Hamstring to 30, then Concentrate, with Dragon's Breath last at about 20. Add Thrust until about 140 percent speed if you are short.
claims.say: bowmaster: sharp eyes and hurricane 30 first, then phoenix, expert

claims.text: Marksman: Sharp Eyes 30, Snipe and Marksman Boost, Piercing Arrow, Blind and Frostprey to 30. For bossing swap Piercing Arrow and Blind; for grinding swap Snipe and Piercing Arrow.
claims.say: marksman: sharp eyes 30 first, swap piercing arrow/blind for bossing

claims.text: Rogues can leave Dark Sight unmaxed and dodge its speed drop in 2nd job by macroing Dark Sight with Haste or Nimble Feet, since the speed buff overrides the drop. Shadowers cannot skip it because they use it constantly.
claims.say: macro dark sight with haste to skip its speed drop

claims.text: Assassin order: Claw Mastery and Critical Throw to 30, Claw Booster and Haste to 6 then raised together to 20 so durations match, Endure 3, Drain 28. For party content max Haste before Claw Booster.
claims.say: assassin: critical throw 30, raise booster and haste together

claims.text: Hermit order: 1 Avenger, then Shadow Partner to 30, Avenger to 5, Flash Jump 20, Avenger to 30, then Shadow Web, Alchemist and Meso Up to 20. If you leech yourself, max Meso Up first.
claims.say: hermit: shadow partner 30 first, then avenger, flash jump, web

claims.text: Night Lord: Triple Throw first, then Shadow Stars, Taunt, Ninja Storm and Venom to 30, with Maple Warrior and Hero's Will along the way. Taunt at level 1 works as a melee-range gathering skill.
claims.say: night lord: triple throw first, taunt lv1 gathers mobs in melee range

claims.text: Bandit: Dagger Mastery 19 and Booster 6 first, then Savage Blow 30, Haste 6, Booster and Haste to 20 together, Endure 20, Steal. Savage Blow starts weaker than level 10 Double Stab, so mastery comes first.
claims.say: bandit: mastery and booster first, then savage blow, haste

claims.text: Shadower order: Assassinate to 30 first, Boomerang Step and Smokescreen, then Hero's Will and Maple Warrior, Taunt and Venom to 30. Hero's Will gets priority because Shadower is the preferred seduce target.
claims.say: shadower: assassinate 30 first, hero's will early for seduce

claims.text: Swordsman order: Improving HP Recovery 5, Improving Max HP Increase 10, Slash Blast 20, Power Strike 20, then 3 each in Endure and Iron Body. Unlike magicians, warriors can attack fine before maxing the HP skill.
claims.say: swordsman: hp skills first, then slash blast and power strike

claims.text: Page: Sword Mastery and Booster first, then Power Guard 30, Final Attack: Sword 30, Threaten 20. Final Attack plus Power Strike is your single-target mode; turn it off when mobbing with Slash Blast.
claims.say: page: mastery/booster, power guard, final attack for single target

claims.text: One point in Charged Blow is worth taking just as a quick way to drop your charge when fighting monsters that resist all three charge elements, such as Lord Pirate.
claims.say: 1 point in charged blow lets you cancel charge vs mobs resisting all

claims.text: Paladin: Advanced Charge 10, Blast 30, Power Stance, Monster Magnet and Holy Charge to 30, then Heaven's Hammer, Rush and Achilles. Blast and Advanced Charge are weak at low levels, so keep Power Strike and Slash Blast for now.
claims.say: paladin: advanced charge 10, blast, power stance, magnet, holy charge

claims.text: Fighter: Sword Mastery and Booster first, then Rage 20, Power Guard 30, Final Attack: Sword 30. Macro Rage with Iron Body to cancel Rage's weapon defense penalty, and note Power Guard reduces knockback from touch damage.
claims.say: fighter: mastery/booster, rage 20, power guard, final attack

claims.text: Hero: Brandish, Advanced Combo, Power Stance, Monster Magnet, Enrage and Achilles to 30. Macro Panic with Combo Attack and fire it when Combo is about to expire; Panic does more damage per cast than Brandish.
claims.say: hero: brandish, adv combo, stance, magnet, enrage, achilles

claims.text: Spearman: Spear Mastery to 19 and Booster 6, Iron Will 3, Hyper Body 30, finish Spear Booster, then Pole Arm Mastery and Booster so you can switch weapons later. Skip Final Attack since Dragon Knight does not use it.
claims.say: spearman: spear mastery/booster, hyper body 30, then pole arm skills

claims.text: Dark Knight is a decent pick: very high HP, a default attack that hits three mobs, which is wanted for Crimsonwood Keep, and the easiest warrior third job. You do have to manage Berserk, and single-target boss damage is a bit low.
claims.say: dark knight is a decent pick, just manage berserk with autopots

claims.text: The author advises against making a Hero first, since Dark Knight and Shadower outclass it in almost every way, though people will still take one to some bosses.
claims.say: hero is outclassed by dark knight and shadower these days

claims.text: Paladin is a solid pick: high HP, decent damage even with little funding, and a highly wanted party buff. Damage flattens at very high investment because of the damage cap.
claims.say: paladin is solid, high hp and a wanted party buff

claims.text: Mages are not bossing classes; their main use is farming and selling leech, which can fund other characters. Do not make one if you do not want to sell leech.
claims.say: mages are for leeching and funding, not really bossing

claims.text: Bishop is a good first character if you are undecided: a Holy Symbol mule is always welcome at bosses and it is the most common class for selling leech. Everyone already has one, which lowers its value a little.
claims.say: bishop is a safe first pick, holy symbol mules go to every boss

claims.text: Fire/Poison and Ice/Lightning both need a Bishop mule at level 81 to be useful, so the author says just make a Bishop. Ice/Lightning is also worse than Fire/Poison.
claims.say: f/p and i/l need a bishop mule to be useful, i/l is the weaker

claims.text: Archers bring Sharp Eyes, which Night Lords and Dark Knights want, so even an unfunded archer easily joins boss parties. Archer damage is mediocre and they lack movement skills.
claims.say: archers get into boss parties for sharp eyes

claims.text: Ranged classes like archers, Night Lords and Corsairs have low natural HP, so they must HP wash or do HP quests to run higher-level bosses, and archers with low avoid get knocked back a lot.
claims.say: ranged classes have low hp, wash or do hp quests for bosses

claims.text: An archer is essential for Crimsonwood Keep PQ and cannot be easily muled there because of a damage check.
claims.say: you need a real archer for crimsonwood keep, a mule can't do it

claims.text: Bowmaster is a simple single-target class that is weak against multiple mobs. Hamstring keeps bosses from moving around, which helps a lot in Crimsonwood Keep.
claims.say: bowmaster is a single target class, hamstring helps in cwk

claims.text: Marksman out-damages Bowmaster at low funding but falls behind at high funding, and handles multiple targets. It requires weaving Snipe in, so it is more complex than Bowmaster.
claims.say: marksman beats bowmaster at low funding, snipe makes it trickier

claims.text: The author does not recommend Night Lord as a first character: expensive, no party buffs, dependent on Sharp Eyes and low in HP. Mobility is good and it has the best single-target damage when highly funded.
claims.say: night lord is pricey and needs sharp eyes, not a great first class

claims.text: Shadower is a good pick: Meso Guard makes it very survivable without much washing, Smokescreen helps the party, it needs no outside buffs, and its high weapon attack keeps it fine even with little funding. Endgame gear is expensive.
claims.say: shadower is a good pick, meso guard keeps it alive, smoke helps

claims.text: Buccaneer is a good pick: high natural HP, very useful Speed Infusion support, relatively cheap, strong scaling into endgame and a great partner for Shadower. The slow attack speed can feel clunky.
claims.say: bucc is a good pick, high hp and speed infusion for the party

claims.text: Corsair is like a Night Lord that depends on skill instead of Sharp Eyes: cheap gear, high damage, no party buffs, miserable until the 160s and the most expensive class to wash. Not recommended for newcomers.
claims.say: corsair is skill based and rough early, not for new players

claims.text: Play the class you actually enjoy rather than chasing the meta, because meta-chasing leads to burnout. Know what a class like Ice/Lightning or Night Lord involves before committing, not just its looks.
claims.say: play what you enjoy, meta chasing burns you out

claims.text: Staff Sergeant Charlie in Orbis runs a repeatable swap: hand over 100 of one kind of monster ETC drop and he returns a reward set, which can be different on each turn-in.
claims.say: orbis staff sergeant charlie trades 100 of one etc for rewards

claims.text: Zombie's Lost Tooth is the ETC most often turned in to Staff Sergeant Charlie, mainly because so many players train on Coolie Zombies and pile them up.
claims.say: coolie zombies drop zombie's lost tooth, save them for charlie

claims.text: 100 Bain's Spiky Collars can be swapped with Staff Sergeant Charlie for a Scroll for Cape for HP 10% along with Mana Elixirs, Topaz Ore, Black Crystal Ore and Diamond Ore.
claims.say: 100 bain's spiky collars at charlie can get a cape hp 10% scroll

claims.text: A stack of 100 Cerebes' Teeth turned in to Staff Sergeant Charlie can give a Scroll for Cape for LUK 10%, plus Mana Elixirs, All Cure Potions, Red Bean Porridge and several ores.
claims.say: cerebes' tooth x100 at charlie can give a cape luk 10% scroll

claims.text: 100 Zombie's Lost Teeth can be exchanged with Staff Sergeant Charlie for a Scroll for Cape for Magic Def 10%, alongside Mana Elixirs, Hot Dogs, Hot Dog Supremes, All Cure Potions and a Fairy Wing.
claims.say: zombie teeth x100 at charlie can give a cape magic def 10% scroll

claims.text: Cellion Tails, Lioner Tails and Grupin Tails each trade 100 at a time with Staff Sergeant Charlie for the same kind of set, including a Scroll for Cape for Weapon Def 10%, White Potions, Salad and Mana Elixirs.
claims.say: cellion, lioner, grupin tails x100 can give a cape wdef scroll

claims.text: Lycanthrope's Toenails traded to Staff Sergeant Charlie in a stack of 100 can return a Scroll for Cape for DEX 10%, with Mana Elixirs, Topaz Ore, Black Crystal Ore and Diamond Ore.
claims.say: lycanthrope toenails x100 at charlie can give a cape dex 10% scroll

claims.text: A stack of 100 Werewolf Toenails can be swapped with Staff Sergeant Charlie for a Scroll for Gloves for ATT 10%, Icicles, Mana Elixirs and some rare ores.
claims.say: werewolf toenails x100 at charlie can give a gloves att 10% scroll

claims.text: Pepe Beaks swapped 100 at a time with Staff Sergeant Charlie can give a Scroll for Shoes for DEX 10%, Mana Elixirs, Screws and Mithril, Steel, Bronze and Gold Ore.
claims.say: pepe beaks x100 at charlie can give a shoes dex 10% scroll

claims.text: Both Dark Pepe Beaks and Firebomb Flames, 100 each at Staff Sergeant Charlie, can pay out a Scroll for Shoes for Jump 10% among the ores and Mana Elixirs.
claims.say: dark pepe beak or firebomb flame x100 gives a shoes jump 10% scroll

claims.text: 100 Hector Tails exchanged with Staff Sergeant Charlie can return a Scroll for Overall Armor for DEX 10%, an Ancient Scroll and a stack each of Warrior, Sniper and Wizard Potions.
claims.say: hector tails x100 at charlie can give an overall dex 10% scroll

claims.text: Jr. Yeti Skins and Dark Nependeath's Seeds both exchange (100 each) with Staff Sergeant Charlie for a Scroll for Topwear for DEF 10% with White Potions, Salad, Mana Elixirs and Screws.
claims.say: jr yeti skin or dark nependeath seed x100 gives a topwear def scroll

claims.text: A stack of 100 Luster Pixie's Sunpieces can be swapped with Staff Sergeant Charlie for a Scroll for Cape for INT 60%, which suits mages, together with White Potions, Mana Elixirs, Salad and Screws.
claims.say: luster pixie sunpieces x100 can give a cape int 60% scroll

claims.text: Both Nependeath's Seeds and Jr. Cerebes Teeth exchange 100 at a time with Staff Sergeant Charlie for a Scroll for Earring for INT 10%, useful for mages, plus potions and Processed Wood.
claims.say: nependeath seeds or jr cerebes teeth x100 give an earring int scroll

claims.text: Star Pixie's Starpieces and Fly-Eye Wings give a Scroll for Helmet for DEF 10% when 100 are turned in; Lunar Pixie's Moonpieces give a Scroll for Shield for DEF 10% instead.
claims.say: starpieces and fly-eye wings x100 can give a helmet def scroll

claims.text: Solid Horn is the lowest-tier turn-in for Staff Sergeant Charlie, paying out potions, Lemons, Fried Chicken, Processed Wood and Return Scroll - Nearest Town, with no equipment scroll.
claims.say: solid horn at charlie only gives potions and return scrolls

claims.text: The Papulatus prequests can be started and finished from level 70, though some required mobs such as Master Death Teddy are tough, so a strong friend helps.
claims.say: pap prequests work from lv70, bring help for death teddies

claims.text: Protect Ludibrium: accept it from Mr. Bouffon at Path of Time and bring back 10 Tachion from Buffy or Lazy Buffy in Warped Path of Time <1>.
claims.say: protect ludibrium: 10 tachion from buffies

claims.text: The Replacement Time Energy, also from Mr. Bouffon, needs 300 Tachion and 100 Mysterious Powder from Master Death Teddy.
claims.say: replacement time energy: 300 tachion, 100 mysterious powder

claims.text: Master Death Teddies are behind a hidden portal on the right side, about halfway down Forgotten Path of Time <3>.
claims.say: death teddies are through a hidden portal in forgotten path 3

claims.text: A Piece of Crack from Flo at Path of Time needs Piece of Cracked Dimension A, B and C from Grim Phantom Watches, behind a hidden portal near the bottom middle of Forgotten Path of Time <4>. Flo rewards a Ludibrium Medal.
claims.say: grim phantom watches drop the cracked dimension pieces

claims.text: For The Lost Medal from Mr. Bouffon, kill Thanatos in Forgotten Passage until a Ludibrium Medal drops; Gatekeepers in Warped Passage also drop it but are worse to fight.
claims.say: kill thanatos in forgotten passage for the ludibrium medal

claims.text: The Ludibrium Medal is untradeable and needed to fight Papulatus. If you lose it, Mr. Bouffon offers The Lost Medal again and Flo hands you a new one on the spot.
claims.say: you need the ludibrium medal to fight pap, don't drop it

claims.text: To farm the gold teeth yourself, hunt Miner Zombies; Dead Mine II has the best spawn. Change channels for a fresh map or hunt Dead Mine III while II respawns. Drops are not guaranteed and it can take hours, so bring plenty of supplies.
claims.say: farm gold teeth from miner zombies in dead mine ii, can take hours

claims.text: Buying the 30 Zombie's Lost Gold Teeth from other players is by far the quickest route to the Eye of Fire, but costs far more mesos than farming them.
claims.say: buying the 30 gold teeth is fastest but costs a lot of mesos

claims.text: Only the Gold Tooth counts for the Zakum quest; the ordinary Zombie's Lost Tooth also drops from Miner Zombies but is useless there. Plain teeth trade to an Orbis NPC for exp, which only matters for levels 10 to 32.
claims.say: only gold teeth count, plain lost teeth are just an exp trade

claims.text: To MP wash a mage, put level-up AP into MP, then use AP Resets to move those points from MP into INT; repeat until you hit your MP target.
claims.say: mp wash: put level ap into mp, then ap reset it over to int

claims.text: Once the MP goal is reached, HP washing is the follow-up loop: AP Reset one point out of MP and into HP, once per reset you own.
claims.say: hp wash: ap reset out of mp into hp, one per reset

claims.text: An AP Reset can only pull a point out of MP if at least one AP is already in MP, so plan a couple of spare resets when budgeting a wash.
claims.say: keep at least 1 ap in mp or you cant reset out of it

claims.text: Monster Carnival is entered by talking to Spiegelmann; from level 51 you are sent to the second carnival and can no longer join the first one.
claims.say: at 51 spiegelmann sends you to cpq2, cant go back to cpq1

claims.text: In the second Monster Carnival both teams share one large map; some monsters can be hit by either team, while the other team's own summons look see-through and can't be hit by you.
claims.say: cpq2 map is shared, you cant hit the other teams see-through mobs

claims.text: The two teams in the second Monster Carnival share one combined summon cap, so one side spamming summons leaves less room for the other.
claims.say: both teams share the summon cap in cpq2

claims.text: The second Monster Carnival takes 3 to 6 players; with an odd number, one member leaves the party in the waiting room and joins the other leader's party to balance the teams.
claims.say: odd number? one member swaps teams in the waiting room

claims.text: When two groups trade wins, the agreed winners take every early kill while the losers kill nothing, and the winners summon exactly 5 monsters for the losers, calling out each count.
claims.say: trading wins: winners take kills and summon exactly 5 for losers

claims.text: The losing team then summons the maximum 10 monsters for the winners; both teams reach 500 points, the winners farm the full 10 minutes, and the roles swap the next round.
claims.say: losers summon the max 10 for winners, then swap next round

claims.text: In a traded round the losing team usually stops after hitting 500 points, since the few spawns left aren't worth the effort.
claims.say: losing team can afk after hitting 500 points

claims.text: The best summon placement is everything on the top row: clerics stand above it spamming Heal, while assassins and bowmen attack from the side platforms.
claims.say: want spawns on the top row, clerics heal from above

claims.text: Summoned monsters keep reappearing where they first spawned, so a bad spawn spot stays bad for the whole round.
claims.say: summons always respawn in the same spot all round

claims.text: When trading wins, avoid picking up the orbs that stun the other team.
claims.say: dont grab the stun orbs when trading wins

claims.text: For summons, clerics want Death Teddy, many groups pick Ghost Pirate, and some take Viking if they can hit it.
claims.say: clerics want death teddy summons, others like ghost pirate

claims.text: The Horntail prequest isn't one-time: you redo it whenever you run out of Dragon Elixir, and each completion gets you 2 Dragon Elixirs from Moira.
claims.say: redo the ht prequest when out of elixirs, you get 2 each time

claims.text: Only on your first time, accept Moira's Whereabouts from Chief Tatamo in Leafre; he warps you to Cave of Life - Entrance, where you hand it in to Moira.
claims.say: first time only: chief tatamo's moira's whereabouts quest

claims.text: Farm the 10 Tough Dragon Skin from Dark Wyverns at Entrance to Dragon Nest, four maps back from Moira.
claims.say: dragon skins: dark wyverns at entrance to dragon nest

claims.text: You can only hold 10 Tough Dragon Skin at once, so there is no point farming extra.
claims.say: you can only carry 10 tough dragon skins

claims.text: Get Cornian's Marrow from Green Cornians in The Hidden Dragon Tomb II, which you reach by jumping into the pit at the bottom right of the Dragon Forest map.
claims.say: marrow: green cornians in hidden dragon tomb ii

claims.text: Only one Cornian's Marrow can be held at a time; while you have one, no more will drop for you.
claims.say: only one marrow at a time

claims.text: Skull Shoulder Pads drop from Dark Cornians in the same tomb map and have no holding limit, so farm extras to save time on later runs.
claims.say: skull pads drop from dark cornians, farm extras

claims.text: Busted Daggers drop from Dark Cornians one at a time; take one with a Steel Plate and a Mithril Plate to Mos in Leafre to have it fixed.
claims.say: busted dagger + steel + mithril plate to mos in leafre

claims.text: Steel Plates and Mithril Plates don't drop from monsters, so plan to buy them from other players.
claims.say: plates don't drop from mobs, buy them

claims.text: Manon lives in Manon's Forest; you may have to change channels and kill the other mobs before he spawns.
claims.say: manon is in manon's forest, cc and kill mobs til he spawns

claims.text: You only need to hit Manon once or twice to get credit for the kill, so a friend can do almost all of the damage.
claims.say: hit manon once or twice and you get the kill credit

claims.text: To go in toward Horntail, use a Dragon Elixir inside Cave of Life - Entrance and walk to the bottom of the map, where an NPC sends you in.
claims.say: use a dragon elixir at the entrance, then talk to the bottom npc

claims.text: In stage 1, inspect the bookshelves: one hides the switch that opens the portal, and one holds Romeo's or Juliet's letter, the first story check. Tell the party who has the letter.
claims.say: stage 1 check the books for the switch and the letter

claims.text: Stage 2 opens once every monster in the dark room is dead, so check for small ones you missed before moving right.
claims.say: stage 2 kill every mob, its dark so look for small ones

claims.text: In the beaker stage, loot the jugs and drop them one at a time in front of a beaker; dropping a stack uses up all of it but only raises the beaker one line.
claims.say: drop jugs one at a time at the beakers, a stack counts once

claims.text: The beakers are cracked and drain if you are slow. A thief in Dark Sight with pet auto-loot can drop and re-loot jugs back to back without being hit, while someone watches the monster that spawns on top.
claims.say: beakers leak, a thief in dark sight with pet loot is fastest

claims.text: Stage 4 holds the second story check: hand the letter to Romeo or Juliet; blue text showing their shock confirms it counted.
claims.say: give the letter to romeo or juliet in stage 4, blue text = ok

claims.text: Monsters in stage 4 drop card keys for two side doors: the right room is a teleport puzzle meant for a magician, the left a conveyor-belt jump room meant for a thief that needs 120% jump.
claims.say: stage 4 right door is a mage teleport room, left needs 120% jump

claims.text: The side doors only open from outside. Break boxes inside until you find the Alcadno or Zenumist report, stand right at the door when you ask to be let out since it shuts almost at once, then hand the report in.
claims.say: find the report in the boxes and wait at the door, it shuts fast

claims.text: Stage 5 is the key story check: only one player sneaks up to Yulete and talks to him until a message says you overheard him. If the party rushes in he spots you, summons monsters and the check is lost.
claims.say: only one person sneaks up to yulete, rest wait till he talks

claims.text: Stage 6 is a climbing code puzzle like Orbis Party Quest: 10 rows of four spots numbered 1 to 4 from the left, and no two members may share a number on a row. Post your numbers as you climb so others can work out theirs.
claims.say: stage 6 post your numbers per row, nobody shares a spot

claims.text: At the boss stage the party leader talks to Yulete and picks the second, skeptic option, which only appears if every earlier check passed; it brings out Angry Frankenroid.
claims.say: leader picks the second option with yulete for angry frankenroid

claims.text: During the boss, send one member to the upper left by the ladder to guard Romeo or Juliet; the monsters there drop quest items, so it suits whoever needs them.
claims.say: one person guards romeo or juliet up by the ladder top left

claims.text: With a party that knows the steps, Romeo and Juliet Party Quest gives better exp than Pirate Party Quest, especially with Holy Symbol.
claims.say: rnj beats ppq if everyone knows it, even better with hs

claims.text: For Alcaster and the Dark Crystal, have one Dark Crystal refined by Vogen in El Nath or Spiruna in Orbis and bring it back to Alcaster.
claims.say: dark crystal quest: get vogen or spiruna to refine one for alcaster

claims.text: Skills such as Mystic Door and Shadow Partner use up rocks when cast, so it pays to unlock Alcaster's shop on the way to 3rd job.
claims.say: door and shadow partner eat rocks, unlock alcaster early

claims.text: Zakum runs call for All Cure Potions, another reason to get Alcaster's quests done well before you start bossing.
claims.say: bring all cures to zakum, alcaster sells them

claims.text: The Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest needs at least ten players with two of each branch: magicians, warriors, thieves, archers and pirates, because stages 2 to 5 require every class to do its own task.
claims.say: cwkpq needs 10+ players, two each of the five classes

claims.text: Two hosts are needed for a Crimsonwood Keep run: the main host needs the keystone from the Crimsonwood quests, and both hosts need 12 Crimson Hearts dropped by the Crimson Guardians at the entrance.
claims.say: cwkpq hosts need 12 crimson hearts, main host a keystone

claims.text: Turn pet loot off during the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest and never take another member's drops, especially in the bonus stage.
claims.say: turn off pet loot in cwkpq and dont steal others loot

claims.text: Stage 1 is only a hidden portal: it is always behind the pillar right under the lion head, so stand beside it and press Up.
claims.say: cwkpq stage 1: portal is behind the pillar under the lion head

claims.text: In stage 2 each class goes to the pillar marked with its own sigil and attacks it with a third-job skill.
claims.say: cwkpq stage 2: each class attacks its own sigil with a 3rd job skill

claims.text: In stage 4 each class has one real sigil and there are fake extras; a sigil that does not spin, or spins too fast, is a fake. Real ones appear at random, but thief sigils are usually on the left and warrior sigils on the right.
claims.say: cwkpq stage 4: sigils that dont spin or spin too fast are fakes

claims.text: In stage 5 every class has its own room next to a statue and must find its missing weapon, then return it to the statue; for example the mage room is at the top left and the thief room at the bottom right.
claims.say: cwkpq stage 5: each class returns its weapon to the statue

claims.text: In the boss stage the leader talks to the far-right NPC to spawn Master Guardians; once they are dead the leader summons the four bosses, which all spawn at the same time.
claims.say: cwkpq boss: leader talks to far right npc, kill guardians first

claims.text: Bishops and priests must not use Heal until Margana is dead: her Zombify turns healing into damage and one Heal can kill the whole party. Take Heal off the hotkeys if needed.
claims.say: bishops dont heal in cwkpq until margana is dead

claims.text: Red Nirg is dangerous mostly for his heavy touch damage; he also casts stun and has a super knockback attack, so the melee party pins him against the left wall.
claims.say: red nirg: big touch damage, stun, super knockback

claims.text: Hsalf, the thief boss, is among the easiest of the four and is weak to ice attacks.
claims.say: hsalf is weak to ice and is one of the easier bosses

claims.text: Before the bonus stage nobody enters until the leader says so: everyone lines up at the right door, then goes in together and breaks the boxes with basic attacks only, so teleport and flash jump give no unfair head start.
claims.say: cwkpq bonus: wait for the leader, then break boxes with basic attacks

claims.text: Put one thief in the melee group so that everyone there gets Haste during the boss fight.
claims.say: put a thief in the melee group so everyone gets haste

claims.text: Put every ability point into INT on a Fire/Poison mage, because INT is the main stat that raises mage damage.
claims.say: all ap into int for fp mage

claims.text: Put one point into Energy Bolt at level 8 so you can stop meleeing monsters with basic attacks.
claims.say: 1 energy bolt at lvl 8 so u stop meleeing

claims.text: Rush five points into Improved MP Recovery to unlock Improved MaxMP Increase, then max Improved MaxMP Increase first because it adds more MP on every level-up.
claims.say: 5 into mp recovery then max maxmp increase early

claims.text: Max Magic Claw between levels 14 and 20, since it is your training attack before second job.
claims.say: max magic claw by 20 for training

claims.text: Max Magic Guard right after Magic Claw (levels 20 to 27); it is essential for the whole mage career. Then finish Improved MP Recovery and leave Magic Armor at zero.
claims.say: max magic guard asap, its huge for mages

claims.text: Take one Teleport point at level 30 for mobility, then max Fire Arrow first since it is your main attack through the 30s and 40s.
claims.say: 1 teleport at 30 then max fire arrow first

claims.text: After Poison Breath, finish Teleport for circling maps during poison training, then MP Eater to save MP potions, and put Meditation last.
claims.say: teleport, then mp eater, then meditation last

claims.text: Meditation is the lowest second-job priority because Wizard Potions from New Leaf City give the same damage boost, though some players would max it right after Fire Arrow.
claims.say: meditation last, wizard pots from nlc do the same buff

claims.text: Do not invest in Slow beyond the single point it forces on you; slowed monsters take longer to walk into your Poison Mist, which defeats its purpose.
claims.say: dont max slow, mobs need to walk into your mist

claims.text: At third job pour every point into Poison Mist until it is maxed, because it makes training much faster.
claims.say: 3rd job: all points in poison mist first

claims.text: After Poison Mist, put three points into Element Amplification to unlock Seal and Spell Booster.
claims.say: then 3 in element amp to unlock seal and booster

claims.text: Put one point into Explosion to kill several poisoned monsters at once, max Seal next, and then max Explosion to make it a proper mobbing skill.
claims.say: 1 explosion to finish poisoned mobs, max seal, then explosion

claims.text: Then max Spell Booster for fewer recasts, Element Amplification for more damage later in fourth job, and finally Partial Resistance.
claims.say: after that booster, element amp, then partial resistance

claims.text: Leave Element Composition at one point; the author found it useless and only keeps the single forced point.
claims.say: leave element composition at 1, its useless

claims.text: At fourth job take Meteor Shower first, two points at level 120 plus one in Paralyze, and max it by level 130; it is your main mobbing skill.
claims.say: 4th job meteor shower first, its your mobbing skill

claims.text: Max Maple Warrior at levels 130 to 136, then max Paralyze (levels 137 to 146).
claims.say: max maple warrior then paralyze after meteor

claims.text: Max Elquines by about level 158 and keep Fire Demon low; Fire Demon is rarely used for training because Meteor Shower hits more monsters for more damage.
claims.say: elquines max, fire demon barely gets used

claims.text: Level 8 to 15 mages can train in the Henesys Hunting Ground maps.
claims.say: lvl 8-15 train at henesys hunting ground

claims.text: Wild Boars in Land of Wild Boar II suit roughly levels 25 to 35 and also earn well in mesos, best if you can one-shot them.
claims.say: wild boars at land of wild boar 2 around 25-35

claims.text: Brown Teddies at Terrace Hall are good exp from the late 20s up to about level 40 if you cannot one-shot Jr. Wraiths yet.
claims.say: brown teddies at terrace hall until about 40

claims.text: From level 50 to 70, train on Selkie Jr. near the Ghost Ship or run Ludibrium Maze Party Quest; Selkie Jr. works best if you can kill it in two hits.
claims.say: 50-70 selkie jr near ghost ship or ludi maze pq

claims.text: From level 76 to 85, use Poison Mist on Risell Squids in Dangerous Sea Gorge II on Aqua Road.
claims.say: 76-85 poison mist the risell squids at sea gorge 2

claims.text: Poison Breath poisons on a chance and poison drains a monster to 1 HP without killing it, so you need one more hit; Magic Claw is the best finisher because it gives two chances to connect.
claims.say: poison breath drops mobs to 1 hp, finish with magic claw

claims.text: For Poison Mist training, teleport around the map placing mists so monsters walking in get poisoned down to 1 HP, then return and finish them with one hit; Explosion can finish many at once.
claims.say: mist the whole map with tele then go back and finish them

claims.text: In the early levels train on whatever you can one-shot that spawns well; in the 50s and 60s the choice mostly depends on whether you can two-shot Selkie Jr. efficiently.
claims.say: pick whatever you can one shot with good spawn early on

claims.text: Fire/Poison gear goals are INT on the Zakum Helmet, robe and Horntail Necklace, and magic attack on gloves, cape, earrings and shield, with a strong Elemental Wand 5 as the weapon.
claims.say: aim for int on zakum helm and robe, magic atk elsewhere

claims.text: The Guild Party Quest needs at least six members of the same guild; if the headcount drops below six at any point, the quest fails and everyone is warped out.
claims.say: gpq needs 6+ from the same guild or it fails

claims.text: A Guild Party Quest group also needs a Thief with Dark Sight and maxed Haste, a Magician with Teleport 17+, a ranged attacker or 4th job mage with Blizzard, Meteor Shower or Genesis, a level 10-30 character and a boss killer.
claims.say: bring a dark sight thief, teleport mage, ranged, and a lowbie

claims.text: Reach the guild quest camp by taking the Perion portal east into the Excavation Site, heading right to Rocky Road III and taking its top portal; the camp is three maps in. Mystic Door also works if a Priest or Bishop comes along.
claims.say: gpq camp is in the excavation site east of perion

claims.text: The Guild Master or a Jr. Master starts the quest by talking to Shuang. Whoever starts it becomes the leader who alone can handle the stage NPCs, and everyone else enters through Shuang's second option.
claims.say: only whoever started gpq can talk to the stage npcs

claims.text: At the start of the Guild Party Quest, hit the purple rocks to get the Protector Rock earrings and keep them on the whole run; entering the castle without them kills you, and dying costs exp (or a charm) and sends you back before Stage 1.
claims.say: grab the protector rock earrings and wear them the whole gpq

claims.text: For the statue stage, two players stand on the left and right sides of the map and type each statue as it lights up (top, middle or bottom layer plus a number) while everyone else waits quietly by the gate so chat stays readable.
claims.say: two ppl watch left and right and call the statues in chat

claims.text: Guild Party Quest Stage 2 is about collecting four Longinus Spears and placing them in the Room of Justice. A player can carry only one spear, and picking one up means jumping and looting at the same moment.
claims.say: gpq stage 2: 4 spears to the room of justice, 1 spear per person

claims.text: The other three Longinus Spears each sit at the top of a jump quest in the Room of Glory, called blue, yellow and red from left to right.
claims.say: the other 3 spears are at the top of the room of glory jqs

claims.text: The Room of Justice has four small jump quests where spears are planted: jump 1 is open to anyone, jump 2 needs maxed Haste, jump 3 is a combination jump, and jump 4 needs Teleport or a Hermit or Night Lord with maxed Flash Jump.
claims.say: room of justice: haste for jump 2, teleport or flash jump for jump 4

claims.text: The combination jump in the Room of Justice, similar to the Ludibrium combination stage, uses the sequence 2-1-5-2-2-1-2 with the platform you start on counted as 1. Check the spear changes to its winged form before going back down.
claims.say: jump 3 combo is 2152212, starting platform is 1

claims.text: Plan Stage 2 in advance: assign who does each colored jump quest and the mage and thief part, and with a bigger group have one member finish the four mini jumps and wait at the top while the others trade the spears over.
claims.say: plan stage 2 roles first and trade the spears to the top person

claims.text: The shoes jump quest in Stage 4 needs maxed Haste and skills work inside it, so Flash Jump helps a lot. Do not enter the middle door until you have climbed to the top box and taken the shoes.
claims.say: stage 4 shoes jq needs max haste, flash jump helps

claims.text: Hit the Rubian to spawn Ergoth and its four statues. Ergoth alternates weapon and magic cancel attacks and the statues curse, dispel and use 1/1, so bring around 4000 HP. You only need to kill Ergoth and the Rubian, not the statues.
claims.say: ergoth needs about 4k hp, no need to kill the statues

claims.text: The Guild Party Quest bonus stage lasts 40 seconds and can give potions, 4th job skill books for mastery 30, and 60% scrolls such as INT overalls, INT earrings or attack gloves.
claims.say: gpq bonus can give 60 percent scrolls and 4th job skillbooks

claims.text: Unlike most party quests, the Guild Party Quest is mostly run as a fun challenge and for Guild Points, which push a guild up the ranking board, rather than for experience.
