claims.say: gpq is more for guild points and fun than exp

claims.text: Dragon Roar is a full-map attack that is ideal for leeching low-level players at places like Wild Boars and Brown Teddies. Only Dragon Knights have a full-map 3rd job skill, and the lower the leechee's level, the more exp they get.
claims.say: dk can leech lowbies with dragon roar, lower lvl gets more exp

claims.text: Berserk is a huge 4th-job damage boost that works while your HP stays below a threshold, putting a fresh Dark Knight on par with the best low-level 4th job classes. Dragon Roar's HP cost is used to drop into Berserk range.
claims.say: berserk is a big dps boost, use dragon roar to drop your hp into range

claims.text: Because Berserk wants low HP, tanking bosses like Horntail and Zakum that can kill you in one or two hits is difficult for a Dark Knight.
claims.say: berserk makes tanking horntail and zakum risky for drk

claims.text: A Dark Knight's main stat is STR. Add DEX only when accuracy is a problem, since each point gives about 0.8 accuracy but adds little damage range. Gear, scrolls and potions can cover accuracy by end game.
claims.say: drk is all str, dex only if you miss, each dex is 0.8 acc

claims.text: A low-DEX build of about 40 base DEX until late 3rd job suits new, unfunded players, since around 120 accuracy hits almost everything. Reset the extra DEX into STR near the end of 3rd job.
claims.say: unfunded drk: about 40 dex until late 3rd job, then reset into str

claims.text: Funded Dark Knights can run about 4 base DEX with all AP in STR, covering accuracy with gear or by getting leeched through the early levels. This gives the best end-game damage.
claims.say: funded drk can go all str with ~4 dex, accuracy from gear

claims.text: A classic high-DEX build of about 80 base DEX is not recommended today: it hurts damage as you level and you end up with far more accuracy than you ever need.
claims.say: dont go 80 dex on a drk, way more acc than you need

claims.text: Swordsman: max Improving Max HP Increase first since you always want more HP, then Slash Blast (better than Power Strike when hitting more than two monsters), then Power Strike. Spend every SP point or you cannot advance.
claims.say: swordsman: max hp increase, then slash blast, then power strike

claims.text: Spearman: Spear Mastery to 19 (level 20 only adds accuracy), Spear Booster to 6, 3 in Iron Will, Hyper Body to 30, then finish the booster, then Pole Arm Mastery and Booster so you can swap to a better polearm later.
claims.say: spearman: mastery 19, booster 6, hyper body, then polearm skills

claims.text: Do not put SP into Final Attack as a Spearman in this version. Slash Blast is your main attack, and Final Attack's damage gets spread across every monster hit, so it hinders more than it helps.
claims.say: skip final attack on spearman, it just spreads damage thin

claims.text: The author prefers a Spear Crusher first build: Crusher reaches its full output on only three monsters while Dragon Fury needs up to six. Leave Crusher at 15, save SP until 21, then add a Fury point for a reliable swing attack.
claims.say: spear crusher first is better, it only needs 3 mobs to hit full dmg

claims.text: Dragon Blood is not worth it because Warrior Elixirs do the same with no drawbacks and last longer. Power Crash is never needed, and Sacrifice does less than a full-power Spear Crusher.
claims.say: skip dragon blood, power crash and sacrifice on dk

claims.text: Dark Knight 4th job opens with 3 SP: 1 in Rush and 2 in Beholder (Rush needs a prequest, Beholder needs no quest or book). Then add Berserk, then Power Stance, then Achilles, with Maple Warrior 9 if nobody else can buff you.
claims.say: drk 4th: rush 1, beholder 2, then berserk, stance, achilles

claims.text: Hero's Will protects against seduce, which Horntail uses, but Horntail parties do not require it, so it is an optional skill for a Dark Knight.
claims.say: hero's will is optional on drk, parties dont require it for horntail

claims.text: A Dark Knight aims for about 18,750 base HP, since Hyper Body then reaches the 30k cap. Unwashed at level 150 you have roughly 9,700, and each wash adds about 52 HP on average, so you need roughly 748 MP from INT gear.
claims.say: drk hp target is about 18750 base, hyper body gets it to 30k

claims.text: Wear INT gear as early as possible, since MP gained at level up comes from INT. To wash, put one AP into HP first, then use AP Resets to turn MP into HP, then put the held point back into STR.
claims.say: wear int gear early to bank mp, then wash it into hp

claims.text: Watch for a Gold Surfboard early, since the spear will be your main weapon for a good while. The Maple Impaler, which Wild Boars can drop, is a key spear for later.
claims.say: grab a gold surfboard early, maple impaler from boars later

claims.text: Slime Tree (Forest Up North I) is the best place for early swordsmen to start: slimes have a great HP to exp ratio, which matters because your damage range is unstable at this stage.
claims.say: slime tree is the best start for swordsmen, good hp to exp

claims.text: Land of Wild Boar is the most recommended swordsman map: it is flooded with spawn, gives great exp, and Wild Boars drop Power Crystal Ores and Maple weapons including the Maple Impaler.
claims.say: land of wild boar is great for swordsmen, tons of spawn and drops

claims.text: Jr. Boogies often pop up when you enter Land of Wild Boar. Attacking the stone pillars at the top of the map kills all of them and keeps them away for a long time.
claims.say: hit the stone pillars up top to wipe the jr boogies

claims.text: Terrace Hall is the standard map for second-job training: great spawn, a small map, and nothing worth noting in drops, so you just push through the levels.
claims.say: terrace hall is where most 2nd jobbers grind, good spawn

claims.text: Forest of Golem gives the best solo exp a warrior can get, with spawn so thick you never gather mobs. Golems are hard to hit right at level 50, so stay on Wraiths until accuracy allows. Mixed Golems drop glove ATT 60% scrolls.
claims.say: forest of golem is the best solo exp at 50+, if you can hit them

claims.text: A handy trick at Forest of Golem: teleport to the Free Market and leave, and you land back at the top of the map, ready to restart your downward sweep. It can be used into early 3rd job too.
claims.say: fm out and back in at forest of golem puts you at the top again

claims.text: Ludibrium Maze Party Quest needs 3 or more: break boxes in the portal rooms, kill what pops out, collect tickets and turn them in at Room 16 for exp based on tickets. Rewards include summoning bags and Overall INT 10% scrolls.
claims.say: maze pq is easy exp with 3+ people, collect tickets and turn in at room 16

claims.text: Wolf Spiders give a huge chunk of exp per kill and are really good training for a Dark Knight, but they hit hard on touch so watch your HP. Sweep the top-left caverns, then the top-right, then drop down the pit spamming Slash Blast.
claims.say: wolf spiders are great exp for drk but they hit hard, watch hp

claims.text: Underwater on Aqua Road, jumping does nothing, and the only way to move or swim faster is to have more speed.
claims.say: underwater jump does nothing, only speed makes you swim faster

claims.text: The author runs the bishop completely lukless, with no AP into LUK, saying the damage difference is significant and the Maple gear to cover it is cheap or turns up while training.
claims.say: go lukless on a bishop, it does noticeably more damage

claims.text: At levels 8 to 15 a cleric can train on Slimes in Southern Forest I.
claims.say: lv8-15 train on slimes in southern forest i

claims.text: At levels 20 to 25 train on Green and Horny Mushrooms in Southern Forest IV, Bubblings in Kerning Subway Line 1 <Area 1>, or Stirges in the Transfer Area.
claims.say: lv20-25 southern forest iv or kerning subway area 1 or transfer

claims.text: Kerning City Party Quest is a good option for levels 21 to 30.
claims.say: kpq is good exp for lv21-30

claims.text: At levels 25 to 30 train on Wild Boars and Dark Axe Stumps in The Land of Wild Boar I.
claims.say: lv25-30 wild boars and dark axe stumps in the land of wild boar i

claims.text: At levels 30 to 35 train on Brown Teddies in Ludibrium Terrace Hall, or on Jr. Cellions, Grupins and Lioners in the Orbis Garden of Red, Green or Yellow I.
claims.say: lv30-35 terrace hall teddies or the orbis gardens

claims.text: Master Chronos give better exp and mesos than Platoon Chronos at levels 40 to 50, and they drop Helmet DEX 60% scrolls that sell well, which helps a cleric just starting out.
claims.say: master chronos beat platoon chronos for exp and mesos at lv40-50

claims.text: At levels 50 to 70 the Singapore Ghost Ship maps 1, 2, 5 and 6 are a good place to train on Pac Pinkys, Slimys, Selkie Jrs and Mr. Anchors.
claims.say: lv50-70 singapore ghost ship 1/2/5/6 is solid

claims.text: Coolie Zombies are a good alternative to Selkie Jrs at levels 50 to 58, with great exp and money, but be careful on the walk up or save a teleport rock location.
claims.say: coolie zombies are great at lv50-58, careful on the walk up

claims.text: Skeleton Soldiers and Officer Skeletons at Camp 1 drop glove and claw attack 60% scrolls, and Soul Teddies in Forgotten Path of Time <1> drop glove attack 60% scrolls.
claims.say: skeleton soldiers and soul teddies drop glove att 60% scrolls

claims.text: At levels 70 to 90 train on Slimys and Selkie Jrs at Mysterious Path 3 or the Ghost Ships, Death Teddies in Forgotten Path of Time <3>, Black Kentaurus in Leafre, or Master Death Teddies in Lost Time.
claims.say: lv70-90 mysterious path 3, death teddies, lost time

claims.text: In Aqua Road, Gobies at Deep Sea Gorge II can be leeched from 80 but are nerfed and not recommended, while Squids and Risell Squids at Dangerous Sea Gorge II can be leeched from 92.
claims.say: aqua road: skip gobies, squids at dangerous sea gorge ii from 92

claims.text: In Leafre, Destroyed Dragon Nest has Jr. Newties to leech from level 100 and Nest Golems from 105.
claims.say: destroyed dragon nest: jr newties from 100, nest golems from 105

claims.text: Skelegons and Skelosaurs in Leafre are a recommended solo area for funded priests with about 100 INT from equips and a z-helm; add a few levels (about 108) if you plan to Holy Symbol and leech.
claims.say: funded priests can solo skelegons with ~100 int from gear

claims.text: At the Skelegon and Skelosaurus maps maxed Shining Ray is really useful for a priest because it does better damage than Heal there; the maps are also safe to go AFK in.
claims.say: shining ray beats heal on skelegons, and the map is safe to afk

claims.text: From level 120 on, keep training at the earlier high-level spots (Himes, Grim Phantom Watches, Squids, Petrifighters, Jr. Newties), and take Skelegons and Skelosaurs once you have Genesis to flatten them.
claims.say: lv120+ go back to skelegons once you have genesis

claims.text: Magician SP: 1 Energy Bolt, 5 Improving MP Recovery, max Improved MaxMP Increase, max Improving MP Recovery, max Magic Claw, max Magic Guard. Maxing Magic Claw before MP Recovery trains faster if you can afford potions.
claims.say: mage sp: 1 energy bolt, 5 mp recovery, max maxmp inc, claw, guard

claims.text: Bless is maxed early to make the cleric attractive to parties, while a solo cleric can max Invincible before Bless for survivability. MP Eater and Teleport can be swapped for someone who teleports a lot.
claims.say: max bless early for parties, invincible first if soloing

claims.text: Shining Ray can be maxed before Holy Symbol for solo damage, but the author advises against it because the usual undead spots can be healed; another player argues Holy Symbol should go first, party or not.
claims.say: max holy symbol first, heal handles the undead anyway

claims.text: Most priest training spots between 50 and 90 are undead such as Slimys, so Heal damages them; Heal plus MP Eater keeps potion use minimal and Holy Symbol mostly speeds things up.
claims.say: heal hurts undead, heal plus mp eater means barely any pots

claims.text: Elemental Resistance, Summon Dragon and Dispel can be reordered depending on whether you boss; max Dispel earlier if you plan to boss.
claims.say: max dispel earlier if you plan to boss

claims.text: Bless helps when you train on mobs above your level and miss a lot, for example early at Ghost Ship 2; others argue it is nearly useless unless a warrior needs the accuracy.
claims.say: bless is worth it vs mobs above your level when you keep missing

claims.text: Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest needs at least ten players with two of every class, one player with maxed Haste and Flash Jump, preferably 4th-job archers with good range, and ideally two rushers for the boss stage.
claims.say: cwkpq needs 10+, two per class, haste + flash jump person

claims.text: Players should be level 90 or higher, with roughly 3,500 HP for ranged characters and 7,000 HP for melee, before joining Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest.
claims.say: need lvl 90 and 3.5k hp ranged or 7k hp melee for cwkpq

claims.text: Bring lots of All Cure Potions, around 300, and attack potions, because the bosses and later stages inflict many status ailments.
claims.say: bring loads of all cure potions for cwkpq, like 300

claims.text: The leader must have finished the pre-quests for the Keystone and carry 12 Crimson Hearts, dropped by Crimson Guardians, for every new round, then starts the run by talking to Jack.
claims.say: cwkpq leader needs the keystone prequests and 12 crimson hearts

claims.text: In stages 2, 3 and 4 each class has its own sigil; one member of that class stands at it and uses a class skill, and the stage clears when all five are lit, so decide beforehand who covers each class.
claims.say: cwkpq sigils: one per class, stage clears when all 5 are lit

claims.text: Warriors light their sigil with Charged Blow (White Knight), Shout (Crusader) or Dragon Fury (Dragon Knight).
claims.say: warrior sigil: charged blow, shout or dragon fury

claims.text: Archers light their sigil with Strafe, Silver Hawk, Golden Eagle or Piercing Arrow.
claims.say: archer sigil: strafe, silver hawk, golden eagle or piercing arrow

claims.text: Thieves light their sigil with Avenger or Shadow Partner (Hermit), or Chakra, Meso Explosion or Band of Thieves (Chief Bandit).
claims.say: thief sigil: avenger, shadow partner, chakra, meso explosion or bot

claims.text: Pirates light their sigil with Transformation (Marauder), Flash Fist, Rapid Fire (Corsair), Dragon Strike (Buccaneer) or Gaviota (Outlaw).
claims.say: pirates light the sigil with flash fist, rapid fire or gaviota

claims.text: Stage 1, Inner Sanctum Hallway, only asks you to find the hidden portal on the right side of the map; staying too long summons Guardians.
claims.say: cwkpq stage 1 just find the hidden portal on the right side

claims.text: In stage 2, Forgotten Storage Chamber, each class finds and activates its own sigil, and the portal to stage 3 opens once all five are lit.
claims.say: cwkpq stage 2: find your class sigil and activate it

claims.text: Stage 3, The Test of Agility, scatters the sigils across a fairly easy jump quest with a 10 minute limit; only the five sigil holders, one per class, should jump while everyone else waits at the bottom.
claims.say: cwkpq stage 3: only the 5 sigil people jump, rest wait below

claims.text: Thieves should cast Haste on the party members who have to jump through The Test of Agility.
claims.say: thieves haste the jumpers before the cwkpq jump quest

claims.text: Moving pillars in The Test of Agility hit for roughly 99 percent of your HP, so keep HP full at all times, with Power Elixirs recommended, or a single touch kills you.
claims.say: keep hp full in the cwkpq jump quest, the pillars nearly one shot

claims.text: After lighting its sigil, each jumper keeps climbing to the top portal rather than going back down; once all five are lit, the jumpers use the top portal, return to the bottom and join the rest into stage 4.
claims.say: after lighting your sigil keep going up, dont jump back down

claims.text: Stage 4, The Test of Wit, is a jump quest with Stirges and flames that knock you down; the sigils sit in random places, so jump to the top first, then go down either side testing them. It has a 10 minute limit.
claims.say: cwkpq stage 4: climb to the top then check sigils down each side

claims.text: In stage 5, The Test of Unity (15 minute limit), each class clears its own room to get a weapon, and everyone should help so the weapons can be placed on the Main Statue in time.
claims.say: cwkpq stage 5: each class clears its room, drop weapons on statue

claims.text: Keep free ETC slots in The Test of Unity so you can pick up the class weapons, especially the ones from the statue NPC; a full inventory can lose the weapon and fail the run.
claims.say: keep etc slots free in cwkpq stage 5 or you lose the weapon

claims.text: In the warrior room, ignore the guards, climb to the top and talk to the statue for the Sword, then drop it on the Main Statue outside.
claims.say: warrior room: ignore guards, climb up, get the sword from the statue

claims.text: In the magician room, Teleport to the right side of the map and talk to the statue for the Staff, then go back to the door; the room can glitch, so returning may need a workaround.
claims.say: mage room: teleport right, grab the staff, head back to the door

claims.text: In the thief room, kill every enemy with regular attacks, then talk to the statue at the bottom to get the Claw and drop it on the Main Statue.
claims.say: thief room: kill everything, the claw is at the bottom

claims.text: The pirate room is flooded and filled with Gobies, Sharks and Squids; find the Gun inside one of the gold treasure chests, then drop it on the Main Statue.
claims.say: pirate room is underwater, the gun is in a gold chest

claims.text: Drop each class weapon on its spot on the Main Statue; if the reactor does not respond, move slightly and try again. Once all are placed, the portal to the boss stage opens.
claims.say: if the statue doesnt react move a bit and drop the weapon again

claims.text: In the boss stage, Grandmaster Council Hall, the leader talks to the statue NPC on the right to call the Guardians; once they are dead, the four bosses Red Nirg, Margana, Rellik and Hsalf spawn together.
claims.say: cwkpq boss: leader calls the statue, kill guardians, 4 bosses spawn

claims.text: Get into position before the Guardians are down: rushers stay at the bottom and others stand on the right of the middle platform, since Margana spawns in the center of it and can be pinned to the left.
claims.say: rushers wait at the bottom, rest on the right of the middle platform

claims.text: Safest plan: while others kill Margana, rushers split the rest, Rellik and Red Nirg to one corner and Hsalf to the opposite one, then attackers kill Hsalf, then Red Nirg, and finally Rellik.
claims.say: kill margana, then hsalf, red nirg, then rellik last

claims.text: A confident party can rush Hsalf, Red Nirg and Rellik into the same corner and kill them together once Margana is dead; stock extra All Cure Potions, because they curse often.
claims.say: strong parties can kill the last 3 bosses together, bring cures

claims.text: Rellik is the hardest boss, with Seal, Stun and Poison plus 1/1 attacks; use All Cure Potions quickly instead of relying on a Priest or Bishop's Dispel.
claims.say: rellik is the toughest, use cure pots fast, dont wait for dispel

claims.text: Rellik is weak to Fire and Hsalf is weak to Ice, while Margana resists Ice, Lightning and Fire.
claims.say: rellik is weak to fire and hsalf to ice

claims.text: A buffed Red Nirg hits for up to roughly 7,000 in melee and knocks players back hard, so melee fighters need healthy HP before engaging.
claims.say: buffed red nirg hits up to ~7k, keep your hp high

claims.text: Each CWKPQ boss drops a Mark of Naricain pendant, and a player can only hold one.
claims.say: each cwkpq boss drops a mark of naricain, you can hold only one

claims.text: After all four bosses are dead, everyone waits at the door on the right, enters together and walks right to the portal for the bonus room full of treasure chests.
claims.say: after the bosses wait at the right door, then go to the bonus room

claims.text: The CWKPQ bonus chests can give level 30 mastery books for Big Bang, Blizzard, Boomerang Step, Demolition, Hurricane, Piercing Arrow, Sharp Eyes and Time Leap.
claims.say: cwkpq bonus chests drop lvl 30 mastery books like hurricane

claims.text: The CWKPQ bonus chests also drop equipment such as Berzerker, Stormshear, White Nisrock, Khanjar, Crossheider, cloaks and capes, plus Taos, chairs, food and storybooks.
claims.say: cwkpq bonus drops berzerker, stormshear, white nisrock, khanjar

claims.text: Bishops unlock Genesis through a quest chain that bounces between Shammos and Grendel the Really Old; near the end Shammos asks for a Life Root, which is the hard part.
claims.say: genesis = shammos/grendel quest chain, ends with a life root

claims.text: The Life Root for the Genesis quest only comes from the Horntail Party Quest, so the Horntail prequest has to be done first.
claims.say: life root only comes from htpq, do the ht prequest first

claims.text: Any class can start the Horntail prequest at level 80 by talking to Chief Tatamo in Leafre, the Magic Seed seller, who sends you on to Moira.
claims.say: ht prequest is lv 80+, start at chief tatamo in leafre

claims.text: Moira's quest Making the Secret Medicine for Transformation needs 10 Tough Dragon Skin plus one each of Skull Shoulder Pad, Cornian's Marrow, Manon's Cry and Cornian's Dagger.
claims.say: moira wants 10 dragon skins, skull pad, marrow, cry, dagger

claims.text: Cornian's Marrow drops from Dark and Green Cornians, while the Skull Shoulder Pad comes from Green Cornians.
claims.say: marrow and skull pad both drop from the cornians

claims.text: Tough Dragon Skin for the Horntail prequest drops from Red, Blue and Dark Wyverns.
claims.say: tough dragon skins drop from red, blue and dark wyverns

claims.text: Manon's Cry for the Horntail prequest comes from killing Manon.
claims.say: manon's cry drops from manon himself

claims.text: First-time and repeat versions of this quest use different item IDs, so pieces looted by someone who already turned it in may not count for you; farm your own or use a first-timer who has the quest active.
claims.say: items a repeat-doer loots may not count, farm your own

claims.text: Turning the items in to Moira transforms you into a Cornian; then talk to the Dark Cornian NPC just below her to enter the Horntail Party Quest.
claims.say: turn in to moira, become a cornian, click the npc below her

claims.text: Do not hand the prequest in unless at least two other party members level 120+ who also finished it are with you, otherwise you must redo the whole prequest.
claims.say: don't turn in til you have 3 people at 120+ ready

claims.text: Bring the Life Root back to Shammos to finish the quest and learn Genesis.
claims.say: take the life root to shammos to learn genesis

claims.text: The Amoria Party Quest is aimed at married couples, so the author's first advice is to get married before trying it.
claims.say: get married before you try the amoria party quest

claims.text: To reach the Amoria Party Quest, talk to Thomas Swift in Henesys to get to Amoria, take the south-east portal and keep walking east to Amos, fighting Snails, Shrooms, Crystal Boars and Indigo Eyes on the way.
claims.say: thomas swift in henesys sends you to amoria, walk east to amos

claims.text: Amos gives an entry ticket (one at a time) in exchange for 10 keys, which drop only from the Crystal Boars and Indigo Eyes on the way; with a ticket you can enter the Amoria Party Quest waiting room.
claims.say: amos gives a pq ticket for 10 keys from crystal boars and eyes

claims.text: An Amoria Party Quest party needs at least six members, with at least one male and one female character, because stage 1 splits the party by gender.
claims.say: apq needs 6 players, at least one guy and one girl

claims.text: Do not stack the Amoria Party Quest party with priests and bishops: against the Balrog's white form holy damage is nearly nullified and you can only hit for 1.
claims.say: dont stack priests vs balrog in apq, holy only does 1 dmg

claims.text: In stage 1 girls go to the left side and boys to the right through the portals Amos opens after the leader talks to him; everyone must kill all the monsters on their side before advancing.
claims.say: apq stage 1: girls go left, boys right, clear every monster

claims.text: Stage 2 is a rope puzzle like the Kerning and Ludibrium party quests: everyone but the leader hangs on three ropes starting 5-0-0, and the leader, who gets the hint, calls out splits such as 3-1-1 until the combination is right.
claims.say: apq stage 2 ropes: leader calls rope splits like 3-1-1

claims.text: When counting slimes in stage 3, kill them with single-target attacks so that slimes jumping together are not hit all at once and miscounted; if every bottom podium gives the same count, they are all correct.
claims.say: kill podium slimes with single target hits so you count right

claims.text: Stage 4 only requires the leader to gather 50 of the quest drops from the monsters on the map to advance.
claims.say: apq stage 4: collect 50 drops from the mobs for the leader

claims.text: Stage 5 is a run to the right breaking gates. Everyone may run ahead, but only one person should attack a gate at a time or the party gets kicked out.
claims.say: apq stage 5: only one person hits a gate at a time

claims.text: Stage 6 is a Balrog fight; kill it and give the fang it drops to the party leader so the party can progress to the bonus room.
claims.say: apq balrog drops a fang, hand it to the leader

claims.text: Orange Mushrooms around the Henesys Hunting Ground, from about level 10, drop Omok pieces that other players pay well for, which makes them a cheap early meso source.
claims.say: orange mushrooms near henesys drop omok pieces that sell well

claims.text: Wild Boars in the Land of Wild Boar near Perion, from about level 21, drop Power Crystal Ore and Leather that sell well, and most of the rest of their loot can be sold to an NPC.
claims.say: wild boars at perion drop power crystal ore and leather to sell

claims.text: Rocky Masks around the Perion Excavation Site, from about level 21, drop 60% scrolls for Earring INT, Spear ATT and Staff Magic ATT, which are worth farming for resale.
claims.say: rocky masks at the excavation site drop good 60% scrolls

claims.text: Crows in the Mushroom Shrine crow forest (about level 21) can drop 30% Shoes for Jump scrolls, and Cloud Foxes in the forest of animals (about 25) drop 10% and 30% two-handed sword scrolls.
claims.say: crows and cloud foxes at mushroom shrine drop sellable scrolls

claims.text: Jr. Wraiths in the Kerning City Subway, from about level 30, drop Power Crystal Ore and Helmet for DEX scrolls, which makes them a decent spot for money.
claims.say: jr wraiths in kerning subway drop dex helmet scrolls and ore

claims.text: Leprechauns in the Phantom Forest near New Leaf City, from about level 40, drop a lot of items, so selling the loot to an NPC adds up to good money.
claims.say: leprechauns in nlc drop tons of loot to npc for mesos

claims.text: Coolie Zombies in El Nath's Forest of Dead Trees, from about level 50, are easy exp, and their Zombie's Lost Tooth drops sell in stacks from a Free Market shop.
claims.say: coolie zombies in el nath are easy exp and the teeth sell in stacks

claims.text: Grizzlies in the Wild Bear Area of Mu Lung, from about level 50, can drop Maple Skanda, a level 64 claw.
claims.say: grizzlies in mu lung can drop a maple skanda claw

claims.text: Before pricing anything, walk through the Free Market shops and watch megaphone sales to learn current prices; scroll and item prices drift up and down.
claims.say: check fm shops and smegas before you price anything

claims.text: INT equipment and INT scrolls usually sell for more than average gear, so mage players should not undersell them.
claims.say: int gear and scrolls go for more, dont sell them cheap

claims.text: A STR-less archer sends every AP into DEX and wears Maple-series bows until around level 90, then begins adding STR so ordinary class bows become wearable.
claims.say: pure dex works for archers, wear maple bows till about lv90

claims.text: Maple bows attack faster than ordinary class bows and add some HP and speed, so a plain bow with a higher listed damage range can still lose damage per minute.
claims.say: maple bows swing faster so they can out dps normal bows

claims.text: A cheap bow progression for a STR-less archer is a War Bow to start, a Maple Bow from level 10, a Maple Soul Searcher from 35, and a Maple Kandiva Bow from 43 until the mid 60s.
claims.say: war bow, maple bow at 10, soul searcher at 35, kandiva at 43

claims.text: A regular class bow needs STR equal to its level plus 5, so a level 100 bow wants 105 STR. Maple weapons are exempt from this rule.
claims.say: class bows need str equal to bow level plus 5

claims.text: Low-STR build: put 4 DEX and 1 STR into each level up until about level 50 so base STR lands near 50, then all DEX. Gear covers the rest; keeping base STR around 50-60 is a good target.
claims.say: 1 str 4 dex a level till 50, then all dex

claims.text: To become a Bowman at level 10 you need 25 DEX, so plan your early AP around reaching that.
claims.say: you need 25 dex to become a bowman at 10

claims.text: Take one Arrow Bomb at 30 so you can finally hit several monsters, then put points into Bow Mastery and a few into Bow Booster, then max Arrow Bomb for more mobbing damage.
claims.say: arrow bomb first at 30, then bow mastery and some booster

claims.text: Max Power Knock-Back around level 55 so you can train on Forest of Golem and Coolie Zombies without having to whack with the bow.
claims.say: max power knock back by 55 to train golems and coolie zombies

claims.text: Make sure Bow Mastery reaches max before second job ends, because it is required for fourth job. The last point only adds a little accuracy, so it can wait until the end.
claims.say: dont forget to max bow mastery, you need it for 4th job

claims.text: Skip Final Attack: it interferes with Arrow Bomb and does not trigger with the third and fourth job attack skills.
claims.say: hunters can skip final attack, it clashes with arrow bomb

claims.text: Put one point into Strafe at level 70: even level 1 Strafe hits harder than a maxed Double Shot, so Double Shot is retired.
claims.say: 1 pt strafe at 70 already beats maxed double shot

claims.text: Arrow Rain-first third job: unlock Arrow Rain through Mortal Blow, max it, then max Strafe for Goby and Squid spots, then raise Puppet to around 6 and Silver Hawk to 29.
claims.say: arrow rain first, then strafe, puppet and silver hawk

claims.text: Strafe-first third job: max Strafe, put five into Puppet to unlock Silver Hawk, and raise Hawk early. That lets you snipe Jr. Newties at Destroyed Dragon Nest and solo the Headless Horseman in your 80s.
claims.say: strafe first plus a good hawk lets you snipe jr newties

claims.text: Puppet pulls aggro from monsters that are already chasing you and does nothing to calm ones. If you place it where monsters cannot reach it, they keep trying while you shoot them safely.
claims.say: drop puppet where mobs cant reach it and shoot from safety

claims.text: At Gobies, if you accidentally hit a Bone Fish, cast Puppet twice: the first cast sends it after the Puppet and the second drops its aggro, so it stops chasing you.
claims.say: cast puppet twice at gobies to drop a bone fish off you

claims.text: Inferno is optional: it lures mobs from a distance without stunning and spreads them better than Arrow Bomb, which helps on big mobs like Temple of Time. If you do not need it, leave it at level 1.
claims.say: inferno is optional, good for long range luring on big mobs

claims.text: Mortal Blow only needs 5 points to unlock Arrow Rain; extra points rarely pay off because an archer should not be in bow-whacking range anyway.
claims.say: only 5 pts in mortal blow, just enough to unlock arrow rain

claims.text: Fourth job core for every Bowmaster: 1 Hurricane and about 9 Sharp Eyes as soon as possible, then max Hurricane, Sharp Eyes and Bow Expert in whatever order suits you.
claims.say: 1 hurricane and 9 sharp eyes first, then max those and bow expert

claims.text: Hurricane out-damages Strafe even at level 1 and overkills less. You cannot walk or use potions while it is firing, but tapping the attack key while moving gives some mobility.
claims.say: hurricane beats strafe even at lvl 1, but no moving or pots mid cast

claims.text: Sharp Eyes raises critical rate and critical damage for the whole party, making it a sought-after party buff and a top priority for fourth job Bowmasters.
claims.say: sharp eyes buffs the whole party's crit, bring it to parties

claims.text: Bow Expert raises your minimum damage and adds weapon attack, so it is one of the skills to max early in fourth job.
claims.say: bow expert raises min damage and attack, max it early

claims.text: Archers can delay Maple Warrior until after about level 140 since other classes need it more. Once the core skills are done, put at least 9 points into it and then work on Concentrate.
claims.say: archers can wait on maple warrior till past 140

claims.text: One point each in Phoenix and Dragon's Breath is plenty until about level 160. Phoenix hits several enemies but does not stun like the third job bird.
claims.say: 1 pt each in phoenix and dragons breath is enough till 160

claims.text: Dragon's Breath replaces Power Knock-Back as your reliable knockback. One point in your 120s or 130s helps when hunting at Temple of Time.
claims.say: dragons breath is the new knockback, 1 pt helps at temple of time

claims.text: Hero's Will cures seduce, which Horntail uses, so a single point is worth it if you run Horntail regularly; it works like a second chance if something goes wrong.
claims.say: hero's will cures seduce, 1 pt is worth it for horntail runs

claims.text: Hamstring is a low priority and is likely the last skill you max; Concentrate gives a big attack and mana saving boost but has a long cooldown, so it comes after the core skills.
claims.say: hamstring is low prio, concentrate comes after the core skills

claims.text: Henesys Hunting Ground II is a solid place to train from level 10 to 15 for a new archer.
claims.say: lv10-15 archers can train at henesys hunting ground 2

claims.text: Archers are weak and slow in first job and early second job, and a monster that touches you gets a bow whack instead of an arrow, so keep your distance and use sniping spots.
claims.say: keep your distance early or you whack with the bow, not shoot

claims.text: Once transformed, click the Cornian NPC to enter; the party leader then talks to the NPC at the top right to start stage 1.
claims.say: click the cornian npc, leader talks to the top right npc

claims.text: In stage 1, kill Cornians for keys; one member who holds no key and isn't the leader stays behind outside while the rest take the top-left portal.
claims.say: stage 1: one keyless non-leader stays out, rest go top left

claims.text: In stages 2 to 4, one member does the jump quest across while the others drop down, kill the wyverns for a key, and then do the jump quest too.
claims.say: stages 2-4: kill the wyverns below for a key, then jq across

claims.text: Drop each key on the shining spot beside the portal; it is sent back to the first map, where the member outside picks it up at the middle tree and talks to the NPC below.
claims.say: drop keys on the glowing spot, outside guy grabs it at the tree

claims.text: Stage 5: kill the Skelegons for 2 keys, finish the jump quest and give both keys to the leader, who takes the portal; if the outside member is leader, pass leadership to the key holder first.
claims.say: stage 5: 2 skelegon keys to the leader, pass lead if needed

claims.text: After stage 5 the leader talks to Horntail's schedule NPC at the far right of the map, which moves everyone to the Cave of Choice.
claims.say: leader talks to the schedule npc on the right after stage 5

claims.text: In the Cave of Choice the leader hits the globe just once from the left or right and enters the portal; the side picks Cave of Light or Cave of Darkness, and extra hits can block entry.
claims.say: hit the globe only once, left or right, then take the portal

claims.text: In the Cave of Light or Darkness, kill Skelegons for 6 keys and give them all to the leader, who climbs the high wall and talks to the NPC.
claims.say: stage 7: 6 skelegon keys to the leader, he climbs to the npc

claims.text: Then clear the remaining monsters; the leader talks to the NPC again and the party is sent to the Horntail entrance, where you wait for the other parties.
claims.say: kill the rest, leader talks again, then wait at ht entrance

claims.text: Life Roots drop from the stage 7 Skelegons; a Bishop who needs one should kill those monsters alone, since they may not drop when someone else gets the kill.
claims.say: bishop needing a life root should solo the skelegons

claims.text: Finishing the party quest takes you to the Cave of Life, where you form a squad to fight Horntail.
claims.say: after htpq form the ht squad in the cave of life

claims.text: A warrior can stay a first-job Swordsman forever: normal STR AP and the usual SP, with spears and polearms preferred because their damage multipliers are higher.
claims.say: perma swordie works, all str and use a spear or polearm

claims.text: An all-DEX warrior works on any warrior line. Damage drops to roughly a third of a normal build, but it is very steady and accuracy is never a worry.
claims.say: all-dex warrior hits for about a third but never misses

claims.text: An HP warrior puts every AP into HP. Fighter or Page can kill by reflecting damage with Power Guard, which burns a lot of HP potions; otherwise normal skills work but deal very weak damage.
claims.say: hp warrior with power guard works but eats a ton of pots

claims.text: A dagger warrior can go pure STR for the most damage, but stat-less daggers are hard to find, or add some DEX to wear common STR daggers. It attacks with Power Strike and Slash Blast; Fighter to Hero has the best skills.
claims.say: dagger warrior: str if you find daggers, else some dex

claims.text: A wand warrior adds just enough INT and LUK to wield common wands and puts the rest into STR. Fighter to Hero is the favoured path, attacking mostly with Power Strike and Slash Blast.
claims.say: wand warrior needs a bit of int and luk, rest str

claims.text: A permanent first-job Magician uses the standard build: all AP in INT, the recommended skills maxed, and any weapon you like.
claims.say: perma mage is just all int and max your first job skills

claims.text: A LUK mage puts everything in LUK, or caps INT at what gear needs and dumps the rest in LUK. LUK adds nothing to magic damage, so it mainly opens many cheap gear and weapon choices and the damage stays poor.
claims.say: luk mage opens cheap gear but the damage is bad

claims.text: A STR mage melees with weapons like a Beginner, so it needs accuracy gear. Fire/Poison is the best fit because Poison Mist does not need magic accuracy.
claims.say: str mage needs accuracy gear, f/p fits it best

claims.text: A melee mage wields weapons such as umbrellas that give both weapon and magic attack. Spells scale with magic, melee with weapon attack, so go pure STR and use spells for luring, or split STR and INT. Fire/Poison is favoured.
claims.say: melee mage uses umbrellas, all str or a str/int split

claims.text: A permanent first-job Archer puts AP in DEX and some STR. Bows attack faster while crossbows hit harder, and crossbow scrolls are far cheaper than bow scrolls.
claims.say: crossbow scrolls are way cheaper than bow scrolls

claims.text: A STR archer fights with melee weapons and has accuracy trouble; second job adds little, but third-job summons help. Sniper then Marksman is the favoured route for Golden Eagle and Frostprey.
claims.say: str archer is rough till 3rd job summons, sniper line suits it

claims.text: A DEX Bandit puts most AP in DEX plus enough STR to wear STR daggers. Damage is weak but very steady until Meso Explosion arrives.
claims.say: dex bandit is weak till meso explosion, then it's fine

claims.text: An HP Bandit puts all AP into HP and struggles until Meso Explosion; with enough time and mesos it can solo nearly anything and rarely dies.
claims.say: hp bandit needs meso explosion and lots of mesos to shine

claims.text: A Brigand is a STR thief: common weapons and Disorder in first job, then Bandit second job for Steal. The Hermit route offers nothing comparable.
claims.say: str thief uses disorder early, bandit gets you steal

claims.text: A permanent first-job Pirate uses the standard skills, with AP depending on weapon: STR for knuckles, DEX for guns.
claims.say: perma pirate: str for knuckles, dex for guns

claims.text: A pure-DEX Brawler gets a huge avoidability boost so it is rarely hit, but its damage is low, though very steady.
claims.say: dex brawler dodges a lot but hits weakly

claims.text: Each Victoria town's Gachapon leans toward one class for equips and weapon scrolls: Perion for warriors, Kerning for thieves, Henesys for bowmen, Ellinia for magicians and Nautilus for pirates.
claims.say: use the gach for your class, perion warrior, kerning thief

claims.text: Mushroom Shrine's Gachapon is packed with 30% and 70% dark scrolls for weapon attack, stats, HP and accuracy, alongside Chaos Scrolls.
claims.say: shrine gach is full of dark scrolls plus chaos scrolls

claims.text: New Leaf City's Gachapon gives forging manuals, among them the Black Phoenix Shield, Infinity Circlet, Dark Shard Earrings, Neva, Glitter Gloves, Zeta Cape, Winkel and Facestompers manuals.
claims.say: nlc gach drops forging manuals like facestompers and zeta cape

claims.text: The New Leaf City Gachapon also gives crafting etc items like Crystal Shard, Typhon Crest, LeFay Jewel and Stone Tiger Head; Crystal Shard and Typhon Crest also show up at Showa, CBD and Sleepywood.
claims.say: crystal shards and typhon crests come from the nlc gach

claims.text: Tao of Harmony, Tao of Shadows and Tao of Sight are spread across the New Leaf City, Mushroom Shrine, Nautilus, CBD and Sleepywood Gachapons.
claims.say: tao items come from nlc, shrine, nautilus, cbd, sleepy gach

claims.text: Black Versal Materia can be won from the CBD and Sleepywood Gachapons.
claims.say: black versal materia comes from cbd or sleepy gach

claims.text: Sleepywood's Gachapon gives the Dagger Forging Stimulator and the Claw Production Stimulator.
claims.say: dagger and claw stimulators come from the sleepy gach

claims.text: Pet equipment scrolls for speed and jump, at several success rates up to 100%, are in Sleepywood's Gachapon.
claims.say: speed and jump pet scrolls come from the sleepy gach

claims.text: Sleepywood's Gachapon has overall scrolls for every stat at most success rates, including 100% LUK, STR and DEX overall scrolls and their 30% and 70% dark versions.
claims.say: sleepy gach has overall scrolls for all stats

claims.text: Sleepywood's Gachapon also gives a 100% glove attack scroll and a 100% one-handed sword magic attack scroll.
claims.say: sleepy gach can give 100% glove att scrolls

claims.text: CBD's Gachapon gives many 100% scrolls, such as shield for magic attack, helmet, earring and eye accessory for INT, and face accessory for avoidability.
claims.say: cbd gach has lots of 100% scrolls, int ones too

claims.text: Ellinia's Gachapon mage equips include Arc Staff (level 45), Dark Penance (50), Magicodar (88) and Dark Pachone (90).
claims.say: ellinia gach gives arc staff and magicodar

claims.text: The CBD Gachapon's set-up items are the Red Round Chair, Blue Seal Cushion and Gold Seal Cushion.
claims.say: cbd gach has the red round chair and seal cushions

claims.text: Most dragon weapons need 20 Dragon Spirits and 25 Dragon Scales on top of crystals and mesos. Pirate dragon weapons need 20 of each.
claims.say: most dragon weapons need 20 dragon spirits and 25 scales

claims.text: Wild Boars are a great source of Power Crystal Ore, and they also drop leather for Work Gloves and Maple weapons to sell or use, so it is a good meso spot overall.
claims.say: wild boars drop lots of power crystal ore and sellable stuff

claims.text: Jr. Wraiths are the best monsters to farm for Power Crystal Ore.
claims.say: jr wraiths are the best for power crystal ore

claims.text: Dragon Wand averages 118-128 magic attack (godly 129-133) and Dragon Staff 120-130 (godly 131-135), so the staff is slightly higher.
claims.say: dragon staff has a bit more magic att than the dragon wand

claims.text: A Marksman's single-target boss rotation is Strafe plus Snipe plus Frostprey.
claims.say: mm boss combo is strafe, snipe and frostprey

claims.text: A Marksman's mobbing rotation is Piercing Arrow plus Snipe plus Frostprey.
claims.say: mm mobbing is piercing arrow, snipe, frostprey

claims.text: A Bowmaster's boss rotation is Hurricane plus Phoenix, with Concentrate up for extra weapon attack.
claims.say: bowmaster boss combo is hurricane, phoenix with concentrate up

claims.text: A Bowmaster mobs with Hurricane and Phoenix, adding the occasional Arrow Bomb.
claims.say: bowmaster mobbing is hurricane and phoenix, bit of arrow bomb

claims.text: Crossbows normally carry about 3 more weapon attack than bows, are easier to scroll, and are cheaper to buy, sometimes nearly free, which is a point in the Marksman's favour.
claims.say: crossbows have about 3 more attack than bows and are cheaper

claims.text: Ranged damage scales with DEX times a weapon constant (3.6 for crossbows, 3.4 for bows) plus STR, times weapon attack. Minimum damage depends on mastery, so Bow Expert or Crossbow Expert raises your damage floor.
claims.say: crossbow dex multiplier is 3.6 vs 3.4 for bows

claims.text: Hurricane fires at a fixed rate whatever your weapon's attack speed, so a Bowmaster gains nothing from a faster bow for that skill.
claims.say: hurricane fire rate ignores weapon speed

claims.text: A Marksman does not need Concentrate's attack buff: attack potions give similar weapon attack and save the skill points a Bowmaster has to spend on it.
claims.say: marksman can use attack pots instead of spending sp on concentrate

claims.text: The critical bonus is added once per hit, so skills that hit several times gain more from Critical Shot and Sharp Eyes. For example, Double Shot out-damages Arrow Blow with crits even though both do similar base damage.
claims.say: crits count per hit so multi hit skills like double shot gain more

claims.text: Phoenix and Frostprey damage comes only from the summon's skill level and does not scale with your own damage range or weapon.
claims.say: phoenix and frostprey dmg only depends on skill level not your weapon

claims.text: With one or two mobs a Marksman should use Snipe, waiting out cooldown for respawns. Against 3 to 6 mobs, use Frostprey to freeze them and then Piercing Arrow through the pack.
claims.say: 1-2 mobs use snipe, 3-6 freeze with frostprey then piercing arrow

claims.text: A Bowmaster can stay far from a group of mobs and keep killing them with Hurricane, so he takes fewer hits than a Marksman who needs to be closer.
claims.say: bowmaster can hurricane from far so he takes less hits

claims.text: Archers can do jump shots by pressing jump and attack quickly, especially with Strafe, and Hurricane can be used while you walk; just tap it now and then while moving.
claims.say: jump shot with strafe, and hurricane works while walking

claims.text: When pricing a Maple Skanda, weapon attack is what counts; accuracy and avoid barely change an assassin's damage, and LUK rolls are so close together that they matter little.
claims.say: skanda price is all about att, ignore acc and avoid

claims.text: Mano, the earliest area boss, spawns in Thicket Around the Beach III.
claims.say: mano spawns at thicket around the beach iii

claims.text: Stumpy spawns in East Rocky Mountain V.
claims.say: stumpy is in east rocky mountain v

claims.text: Seruf spawns in The Seaweed Tower on Aqua Road.
claims.say: seruf is in the seaweed tower on aqua road

claims.text: Faust can be found in Forest of Evil I and Forest of Evil II.
claims.say: faust is in forest of evil 1 and 2

claims.text: Timer spawns around Ludibrium in Lost Time <1>, Lost Time <2> and Whirlpool of Time.
claims.say: timer spawns in lost time 1, 2 or whirlpool of time

claims.text: Mushmom spawns in Someone Else's House.
claims.say: mushmom spawns in someone else's house

claims.text: Dyle spawns in Dangerous Croko I and Dangerous Croko II.
claims.say: dyle is in dangerous croko 1 and 2

claims.text: Zombie Mushmom spawns in The Grave of Mushmom.
claims.say: zombie mushmom is at the grave of mushmom

claims.text: Zeno spawns in Gray's Prairie.
claims.say: zeno spawns in gray's prairie

claims.text: The Nine-Tailed Fox spawns at Moon Ridge in Korean Folk Town.
claims.say: nine-tailed fox is at moon ridge, korean folk town

claims.text: Tae Roon spawns in the Territory of Wandering Bear in Mu Lung.
claims.say: tae roon is in territory of wandering bear, mu lung

claims.text: Jr. Balrog spawns in The Cursed Sanctuary dungeon.
claims.say: jr balrog spawns in the cursed sanctuary

claims.text: Eliza spawns in Stairway to the Sky II.
claims.say: eliza is at stairway to the sky 2

claims.text: Snack Bar spawns in the Drake Area dungeon on Victoria Road.
claims.say: snack bar is in the drake area dungeon

claims.text: Chimera spawns in the Secret Basement Path of the lab.
claims.say: chimera is at secret basement path in the lab

claims.text: Blue Mushmom spawns in the Hall of Mushroom in Zipangu.
claims.say: blue mushmom is in hall of mushroom, zipangu

claims.text: Snowman spawns in the Valley of Snowman near El Nath.
claims.say: snowman is in the valley of snowman by el nath

claims.text: Headless Horseman can appear in several dungeon maps, including Hollowed Ground, Forgotten Path, Hidden Evil, Creeping Evil and The Evil Dead.
claims.say: headless horseman spawns in hollowed ground and the evil dead

claims.text: Manon spawns in Manon's Forest.
claims.say: manon is in manon's forest

claims.text: Griffey spawns in Griffey Forest.
claims.say: griffey is in griffey forest

claims.text: Pianus is fought in The Cave of Pianus.
claims.say: pianus is in the cave of pianus

claims.text: Bigfoot can spawn in several deep dungeon maps: Forgotten Path, Evil Rising, The Evil Dead and the Twisted Path maps.
claims.say: bigfoot spawns in forgotten path, evil dead, twisted path

claims.text: Black Crow spawns in the Encounter with the Buddha map.
claims.say: black crow is in encounter with the buddha

claims.text: Leviathan spawns in Leviathan's Canyon near Leafre.
claims.say: leviathan is in leviathan's canyon by leafre

claims.text: A Marksman needs Strength only to wear gear, so Dexterity is the main stat and Strength stays low. A build with no extra Strength is close to impossible by level 110, but a very low-Strength one works with good gear.
claims.say: mm only needs str for gear so keep it low and go dex

claims.text: The Strength goal for an archer is wearing the level 110 Dragon Shiner Cross, which needs 110 Strength. Most of it should come from equipment like the Zakum Helmet and Horntail Necklace, with only a modest share from AP.
claims.say: 110 str for dragon shiner cross, get most from zhelm and htp

claims.text: When HP washing an archer, roughly 160 or more Intelligence including gear gives 7-8k HP around level 155, while 10k HP at that level needs about 180-200 Intelligence. The rest of each level's AP goes to Dexterity.
claims.say: for 10k hp at 155 you want around 180-200 int with gear

claims.text: The author thinks a Marksman should plan on HP washing from the start; more max HP makes bossing easier, and they sat near 10k HP late in the game.
claims.say: mm should hp wash, more hp makes bossing way easier

claims.text: As a first-job bowman use a bow even if you plan to become a Marksman; the bow attacks faster than a crossbow, which helps a lot when monsters get right next to you at low level.
claims.say: use a bow in 1st job, its faster than xbow for close mobs

claims.text: If you have the funds, Zombie's Lost Teeth are a quick way to gain levels between 10 and 20.
claims.say: if you have mesos zombie's lost teeth level you fast at 10-20

claims.text: In first job max Critical Shot, Double Shot and The Eye of Amazon. Double Shot is much better than Arrow Blow for leveling, and the Eye adds the range a bowman depends on.
claims.say: 1st job max crit shot, double shot and eye of amazon

claims.text: The Blessing of Amazon only needs 3 points because it is a prerequisite for the Eye of Amazon. Focus is optional but worth maxing for the extra avoidability.
claims.say: only 3 in blessing of amazon, its just the req for the eye

claims.text: The author maxes Critical Shot before Double Shot because low-level hits often do 1 damage and cannot break defense, so a lucky critical matters; maxing Double Shot first for more damage is also fine.
claims.say: crit shot first helps low lvl, double shot first is fine too

claims.text: In second job max Crossbow Booster, Soul Arrow, Iron Arrow and Crossbow Mastery. Faster shooting means more damage, Soul Arrow saves arrows, and Iron Arrow is the main mobbing skill for experience.
claims.say: 2nd job max xbow booster, soul arrow, iron arrow and mastery

claims.text: The author skips Final Attack because it adds delay when you spam Iron Arrow while mobbing, though some players like it. Power Knock-Back is taken instead to shove monsters away from you.
claims.say: skip final attack, it delays iron arrow. knock-back is handier

claims.text: By the end of second job aim for Iron Arrow 30 and Crossbow Mastery, Crossbow Booster, Soul Arrow and Power Knock-Back at 20 each; spare SP goes into Focus to max it for more avoidability.
claims.say: put spare 2nd job sp into focus for the extra avoid

claims.text: Arrow Eruption is the Marksman's main mobbing skill in third job because it hits monsters around you in a circle, so max it.
claims.say: arrow eruption is the main mob skill at 3rd job, max it

claims.text: Strafe is the Marksman's only real bossing skill in third job. Its damage is low but you still need it maxed.
claims.say: strafe is your boss skill at 3rd job, max it

claims.text: Blizzard and Arrow Eruption are very strong defensive tools: freeze monsters with Blizzard, then kill them with Iron Arrow or Strafe, which keeps you safe at many hunting spots. Max Blizzard.
claims.say: blizzard freezes mobs then kill them, keeps you safe a lot

claims.text: Mortal Blow is worth maxing in third job because it helps when a monster gets too close to you.
claims.say: mortal blow is handy when mobs get close, max it

claims.text: Golden Eagle is only a prerequisite for the fourth-job Frostprey, so raise it to 15 and stop; you stop using it after fourth job.
claims.say: golden eagle only needs 15, its just the req for frostprey

claims.text: Thrust and Puppet are optional. The author put 20 in Puppet for solo bossing and only 6 in Thrust because a fast crossbow and pet gear already cover speed; spare points can come out of Blizzard since it cannot crit.
claims.say: thrust 6 is enough with speed gear, puppet helps solo bossing

claims.text: In fourth job max Sharp Eyes, Maple Warrior, Snipe and Marksman Boost first; they are the Marksman's core skills, with Snipe and Marksman Boost the most important.
claims.say: 4th job priority is sharp eyes, mw, snipe and marksman boost

claims.text: After the core skills, max Piercing Arrow and Frostprey. Blind and Dragon's Breath are just for fun and not urgent.
claims.say: piercing arrow and frostprey next, blind and dragon's breath later

claims.text: Snipe keeps working when a boss uses weapon cancel, although the hit shows as 1 damage.
claims.say: snipe still works if the boss cancels weapon attacks, shows 1

claims.text: Dragon's Breath only pushes a little at level 1 and cannot be used when a monster is next to you, so the author prefers Blizzard to freeze monsters and then kills them with Iron Arrow or Strafe.
claims.say: dragon's breath cant be used with mobs near, blizzard works better

claims.text: As a Dark Knight, the simple rule is to wield the highest weapon attack spear you can find, and switch to a Sky Ski once you are decently geared and drinking strong attack potions.
claims.say: grab the highest attack spear, sky ski once youre geared and potting

claims.text: For Dark Knight weapon choice the speed gap matters more the higher your total weapon attack from gear, potions and buffs is. A faster spear only pays off once you stack a lot of extra attack.
claims.say: a faster spear only pays off when you have lots of bonus attack

claims.text: A newer Dark Knight is better off with a high-attack Dragon Faltizan for grinding; a 120+ attack one is far easier to find than a good Sky Ski. Buy a Sky Ski later, when you plan to use attack potions at bosses.
claims.say: use a good faltizan for grinding, sky ski later for boss runs

claims.text: A Sky Ski does not out-damage a Dragon Faltizan unless you have a lot of extra weapon attack from potions or gear. Jumping to the Sky Ski too early costs you DPS.
claims.say: dont swap to sky ski too early, you lose dps without bonus attack

claims.text: The Fishing Pole's fast speed looks attractive, but delays round up so its edge is smaller than the raw math suggests. Only a godly, heavily scrolled pole with very high total attack becomes competitive.
claims.say: fishing pole only works if its godly and you have huge attack

claims.text: When comparing two spears, only total weapon attack and attack speed matter: your STR and DEX apply to both equally and cancel out of the comparison.
claims.say: comparing spears only attack and speed matter, str dex cancel

claims.text: Spear Booster makes your weapon two speed stages faster, so a normal (6) spear attacks like a (4) and a slow (7) spear like a (5). Compare spears using their boosted speeds.
claims.say: spear booster drops your weapon speed by 2 stages

claims.text: If a Buccaneer is giving you Speed Infusion, the Sky Ski wins clearly over a slower spear because the extra speed multiplies your attack.
claims.say: with speed infusion sky ski is way better

claims.text: As a warrior going Spearman, finish Improved MaxHP Increase (10 points) before maxing Power Strike; maxing the attack skill first costs a couple hundred HP later on.
claims.say: max improved maxhp increase before power strike

claims.text: Take Slash Blast to 20 before Power Strike in first job, because training with Slash Blast is probably faster than with Power Strike.
claims.say: slash blast first, it trains faster than power strike

claims.text: The warrior first job ends with Slash Blast 20, Power Strike 20, Improved MaxHP Increase 10, Improved HP Recovery 10 and one point in Endure, with Iron Body left alone.
claims.say: 1st job: slash blast, power strike 20, hp skills 10, endure 1

claims.text: A hybrid Spearman raises Pole Arm Mastery to 20 first, then Hyper Body to 30, then Pole Arm Booster, then Spear Mastery and Spear Booster, all maxed at 20 by level 70.
claims.say: pole arm mastery, hyper body 30, then boosters and spear mastery

claims.text: In second job this Spearman build puts about 11 points in Iron Will, finishing it after third job, and takes no points in either Final Attack skill.
claims.say: iron will to 11 for now, no final attack points

claims.text: Near level 120, put leftover third job points back into earlier skills: Iron Will up to 20 and Improved HP Recovery up to 16.
claims.say: leftover sp near 120 goes to iron will and hp recovery

claims.text: HP washing has three phases: build extra MaxMP early through INT, convert that surplus MP into MaxHP with AP Resets, then reset the INT back into your main stat.
claims.say: hp wash = stack int for mp, ap reset it into hp, reset int back

claims.text: INT adds extra MaxMP at each level up, but only in blocks of 10, so 19 INT counts the same as 10. The 4 INT you start with counts too, and it can come from equips or raw AP.
claims.say: int counts in blocks of 10 when you level, so 19 is same as 10

claims.text: INT equips only matter at the moment you level up. Put them on at 99.99 percent exp, level, then take them off again.
claims.say: wear int gear just for the level up itself then swap back

claims.text: Assassins, bowmen, crossbowmen, gunslingers and spearmen are the classes that really need an HP wash; fighters, pages and brawlers benefit from one but can skip it.
claims.say: sins, archers, gunslingers and spearmen should hp wash

claims.text: Bandits do not need an HP wash because Meso Guard absorbs a share of the damage they take.
claims.say: bandits dont need to wash, meso guard covers it

claims.text: Mages do not need an HP wash: Magic Guard protects them and they already have large MaxMP. Fighters, pages and brawlers also have plenty of natural HP.
claims.say: mages dont need washing, magic guard and big mp cover it

claims.text: Washed assassins, archers and gunslingers aim for about 9000 HP by level 155 so they can survive Horntail hits; without a wash they may be unable to take on late bosses.
claims.say: aim for about 9000 hp by lv155 to take horntail hits

claims.text: Warrior, archer and pirate wash needs no level up: seed one AP into HP, then repeatedly reset out MP and add it to HP, and finally pull the seed AP back out of HP into your main stat.
claims.say: archers and warriors wash by resetting mp into hp, no lvl needed

claims.text: MP washing: with enough raw INT, a fresh level-up AP put into MP gains more MP than the reset later removes, so every reset nets MP. It lowers the INT you need and the AP Resets spent. Only raw INT counts, not equips.
claims.say: mp wash needs raw int, equip int doesnt count for it

claims.text: Optimal raw INT for MP washing: assassins 140, archers 160, gunslingers 200. Going above these wastes AP, and you can do five MP washes per level once you reach the number.
claims.say: mp wash int caps: sins 140, archers 160, gunslingers 200

claims.text: You can only pull MP while MaxMP is above a class minimum: thieves and archers about 14 per level plus 148, pirates 18 per level plus 111, spearmen 4 per level plus 156, fighters and pages 4 per level plus 56.
claims.say: you cant reset mp below the class minimum maxmp

claims.text: Assassins use level-up AP for both MP and HP washing, so start early: reach 140 raw INT before about level 50, MP wash around 80-90, and begin HP washing before 100 because it needs about 50 levels. Total is roughly 390 AP Resets.
claims.say: sins: 140 raw int before 50, start washing hp before lv100

claims.text: Archers aim for 160 raw INT before about level 50, MP wash, then convert to HP once around level 155 and move the INT back into DEX. The whole process costs roughly 470 AP Resets.
claims.say: archers: 160 raw int early, wash mp, then reset int back to dex

claims.text: Gunslingers aim for 200 raw INT before about level 60, MP wash for around 65 rounds, then convert to HP near level 155 and send the INT back to DEX. Expect roughly 465 AP Resets in total.
claims.say: gunslingers: 200 raw int by 60, wash, then int back to dex

claims.text: Battleship takes damage equal to what you would take, and a boss attack that drops you to 1 HP hits it for nearly your whole HP pool. A Gunslinger with more HP than needed makes the ship die sooner, so wash only to the goal.
claims.say: dont over wash gunslingers, more hp kills the battleship faster

claims.text: Spearmen keep HP under 40 percent for Berserk, so they wash up to around 15600 base HP to reach about 25k with Hyper Body. It costs only about 99 AP Resets since each reset spends just 4 MP.
claims.say: spearmen wash hp to about 15.6k so hyper body hits 25k

claims.text: Spearmen need only 20 INT if worn from the start; the later you begin, the more you need: 30 INT from level 48, 40 from 84, 60 from 112, 100 from 132. You can do the resets as late as level 155.
claims.say: spearmen need 20 int early, the later you start the more you need

claims.text: Cheap sources of INT for washing: a Zakum Helmet at level 50, a low level wand scrolled for Magic Att, a Green Bandana or cape scrolled for INT, or an INT bathrobe. Sell them when done.
claims.say: zakum helm or scrolled low lvl gear is cheap int for washing

claims.text: AP into HP per point: warriors about 50 or more, brawlers 36-40, thieves 20-24 from a level up but 16-20 from a reset, bowmen 16-20, beginners 8-12, magicians 6-10 from a level up but 10-20 from a reset.
claims.say: warriors get about 50 hp per ap, thieves and archers about 20

claims.text: Average HP and MP per level up: warriors 64-68 HP and 4-6 MP, archers and thieves 20-24 and 14-16, gunslingers 22-28 and 18-23, brawlers 52-58 HP, magicians 10-14 HP and 22-24 MP, beginners 12-16 and 10-12.
claims.say: warriors gain about 66 hp a level, archers and thieves about 22

claims.text: A Night Lord's star damage comes from LUK multiplied by total weapon attack, so LUK and attack are the numbers that matter for Lucky Seven and Triple Throw, while DEX only supports accuracy and equip requirements.
claims.say: nl star damage is luk times total weapon attack, dex is secondary

claims.text: When comparing two claws, weigh two things: the LUK you give up (extra DEX needed to wield the better claw minus the LUK it grants) against the weapon attack you gain on top of your non-claw attack.
claims.say: compare claws by luk you lose to dex vs att you gain

claims.text: A newer Night Lord without funds is better off staying DEXless with a clean Maple Skanda than pushing AP into DEX for a 140-DEX claw like the Red Craven; that swap only pays off after a very large pool of AP, around level 143.
claims.say: no money? stay dexless on maple skanda, dex claw swap pays much later

claims.text: Big attack from outside the weapon, such as Onyx Apples while bossing, makes a higher-attack DEX claw less valuable, so the DEXless Maple Skanda stays competitive for longer on apple runs than on normal training.
claims.say: on apples dexless skanda stays good way longer

claims.text: A mid-geared Night Lord training on Ciders comes out ahead with the 150-DEX Dragon Purple Sleeve, but when bossing on Onyx Apples the DEXless Maple Skanda wins until roughly level 177.
claims.say: mid gear: purple sleeve for training, skanda for apple boss runs

claims.text: A fully geared Night Lord with strong gloves, cape and Crystal Ilbi stars should use the DEX-requiring Dragon Purple Sleeve over the Maple Skanda; the AP spent on DEX pays back around level 133.
claims.say: well geared nl should swap to a dex claw like dragon purple sleeve

claims.text: The Red Craven claw needs 140 DEX, while the Dragon Green Sleeve and Dragon Purple Sleeve need 150 DEX; a perfect Dragon Purple Sleeve has about 60 weapon attack and up to 13 LUK.
claims.say: red craven needs 140 dex, dragon sleeves need 150

claims.text: Ilbi Throwing-Stars give 27 weapon attack and Crystal Ilbi Throwing-Stars 29, which is a large share of a Night Lord's total attack on top of the claw.
claims.say: ilbis give 27 att and crystal ilbis 29, big part of nl damage

claims.text: Attack consumables add to a Night Lord's weapon attack on top of gear: a Cider gives 20 and an Onyx Apple gives 100, which is why apples change which claw is best.
claims.say: cider gives 20 att and onyx apple 100 att

claims.text: From level 1 to 10, train on Snails and Orange Mushrooms on Maple Island.
claims.say: lvl 1 to 10 snails and orange mushrooms on maple island

claims.text: At levels 10 to 15 Slimes give good exp for a Bowman. Arrows are no problem if you have money; otherwise use a melee weapon.
claims.say: 10 to 15 slimes are good exp, use melee if arrows are too pricey

claims.text: The most recommended spot for a Bowman at level 15 to 20 is Orange Mushrooms at the Kerning City Construction Site, since you can make money there.
claims.say: 15 to 20 bowmen: orange mushrooms at kerning construction site

claims.text: At level 20 to 25 Horny Mushrooms and Green Mushrooms are the top picks for a Bowman: good exp plus good money and drops.
claims.say: 20 to 25 horny and green mushrooms are the best for archers

claims.text: Top picks for a Bowman at level 25 to 30: Bubblings (nice spawn, you can earn), Wild Boars, and Rocky and Wooden Masks (average platforms, very good drops).
claims.say: 25 to 30 bubblings, wild boars and masks are best for archers

claims.text: Stirges are easy to kill and drop potions often. A Hunter-line Bowman can use Arrow Bomb on them from level 30 to 40.
claims.say: stirges drop pots a lot, use arrow bomb on them at 30 to 40

claims.text: At level 30 to 35 Wild Boars and Stirges are the most recommended for a Bowman. Boars are crowded with ksers and eat potions but you can still earn.
claims.say: 30 to 35 wild boars and stirges are the best for bowmen

claims.text: Jr. Wraiths have a good spawn and exp for a Bowman at level 35 to 48 and are best with a Cleric along.
claims.say: jr wraiths are good exp at 35 to 48, better with a cleric

claims.text: At level 40 to 48 the most recommended spots for a Bowman are Platoon Chronos and the Star and Lunar Pixies, which have good drops and exp though the pixies hit hard.
claims.say: 40 to 48 platoon chronos and star and lunar pixies are best

claims.text: At level 48 to 55 Stone Golems are the pick for a Bowman: easy to kill with good exp, drops and money. Mateons, Barnard Grays, Lunar Pixies and Skeledogs and Mummydogs are other good picks.
claims.say: 48 to 55 stone golems are the best, easy kills and good drops

claims.text: Jr. Yetis give good drops and exp for a Bowman from level 48 to 60 but burn a lot of potions.
claims.say: jr yetis are good exp and drops but waste a lot of pots

claims.text: Luster Pixies are the standout spot for a Bowman at level 55 to 70, with great exp, spawn, money and drops.
claims.say: luster pixies are great for 55 to 70, exp spawn and money

claims.text: Coolie Zombies at level 60 to 70 are not for soloing. Bring a higher-level partner, ideally a priest, to keep ksers and raiders away, and note the newer platforms are poor.
claims.say: dont solo coolie zombies at 60 to 70, bring a priest

claims.text: From level 89 up, soloing Gobies at Deep Sea Gorge is the recommended pick for a Bowman, especially a sniper: decent exp with little potion loss.
claims.say: 89 and up gobies at deep sea gorge are the best solo spot

claims.text: To drop meso bags quickly, copy the amount to your clipboard, place the drop window so its OK button sits over the meso icon in your inventory, then hold paste while clicking.
claims.say: copy the amount, put ok over the meso icon, paste and click

claims.text: Nobody can drop more than about 6 meso bags per second, and even very fast droppers rarely get past 5.
claims.say: max is about 6 meso bags a second

claims.text: In the Ludibrium Maze Party Quest, learn the maze layout itself instead of memorising one fixed path, since several different routes lead to the same room.
claims.say: learn the lmpq maze layout, lots of routes reach the same room

claims.text: To become a Pirate you need 20 base Dexterity, then talk to Kyrin in Nautilus Harbor at level 10.
claims.say: need 20 dex and lvl 10, then talk to kyrin in nautilus

claims.text: A popular pirate first-job build puts 11 SP in Somersault Kick at levels 10-14 for fast early training, then maxes Double Shot, then Dash, then Bullet Time by level 30.
claims.say: 11 in somersault kick first, then max double shot, dash, bullet time

claims.text: Even at level 1, Somersault Kick out-damages a maxed Double Shot and hits several monsters, so it is the better early grinding skill. It is not maxed because Invisible Shot replaces it in second job.
claims.say: somersault kick beats double shot early, no need to max it

claims.text: Double Shot is maxed first for its range, which helps in the Kerning City Party Quest, then Dash for mobility, and Bullet Time last because a gun user with proper Dexterity should not have accuracy problems.
claims.say: max double shot for range, dash for speed, bullet time last

claims.text: Another build puts 11 SP in Flash Fist instead of Somersault Kick. Flash Fist works while holding a gun but is only a normal hit with no knockback, so the main author still prefers Somersault Kick.
claims.say: flash fist works with a gun but somersault kick is still better early

claims.text: A Gunslinger line pirate can skip Somersault Kick and Flash Fist and use Recoil Shot to push a close monster away; in third job Ice Splitter's freeze also creates breathing room.
claims.say: recoil shot pushes close mobs away, ice splitter freezes later

claims.text: Blank Shot fakes a gun shot and fires a flag instead of bullets, temporarily stunning up to 3 monsters.
claims.say: blank shot stuns up to 3 mobs for a bit

claims.text: A pirate can train on Bubblings and Green Mushrooms from level 14 to 17, then Stirges and Horny Mushrooms from 17 to 19.
claims.say: 14-17 bubblings/green mushrooms, 17-19 stirges and horny mushrooms

claims.text: Alternatives to party quests: the Forest of Golems works until about level 65, and the Ghost Ship is good for levels 51-60 before moving on to Ghost Ship 2.
claims.say: forest of golems works til 65, ghost ship is good for 51-60

claims.text: Henesys Party Quest needs a party of at least 3, every member level 10 or higher, and has to be cleared within 10 minutes.
claims.say: hpq: 3+ people, all lv 10+, 10 min limit

claims.text: Start Henesys Party Quest by talking to Tory with your party.
claims.say: talk to tory to start hpq

claims.text: In Henesys Party Quest, hit the flowers on the map; each flower gives one seed color and the party needs one seed of every color.
claims.say: hit the flowers, get one seed of each color

claims.text: The Moon Bunny makes rice cakes faster the longer it goes unhit, so guard it from the Stirges, Flyeyes and Blins that keep flying in from the map corners.
claims.say: keep mobs off the moon bunny so it makes cakes faster

claims.text: Blins are the toughest of the three; players too weak to kill fast should lure monsters away from the Moon Bunny while the leader picks up cakes.
claims.say: too weak to kill blins? lure them away from the bunny

claims.text: The party leader clears Henesys Party Quest by handing 10 Moon Bunny's Rice Cakes to Growlie.
claims.say: leader gives growlie 10 rice cakes to clear

claims.text: Collect 20 extra rice cakes and give them to Tory at the exit to get the Henesys Party Quest hat.
claims.say: 20 extra cakes to tory at the exit gets you the hat

claims.text: After clearing, Tommy at the exit can send you to a 5-minute bonus map of Pigs, Ribbon Pigs and a few Iron Hogs; it pays only if the party kills fast, so high-level parties should skip it.
claims.say: tommy's bonus map has pigs, skip it if your party is high level

claims.text: Take the elevator down Ludibrium's right-side tower to the library, start A Magician's Story with the librarian, and bring the book to Grendel the Really Old.
claims.say: get the book from the ludi library and take it to grendel

claims.text: In the big map, kill mobs until the leader gets a key. At least one member must stay outside or the run fails, and the fastest killer should be the leader.
claims.say: leave one person outside or the run fails

claims.text: The leader kills mobs inside and drops their keys into the top-left hole of the hollow tree; the member outside picks the key up at the outer tree and talks to the NPC under it to open the next portal. Expect about five rounds.
claims.say: leader drops keys in the tree, outside guy picks them up

claims.text: After regrouping, talk to the NPC at the bottom left, hit the flower bulb once in the next map and let the leader take the bottom-right portal. Have Magic Guard on before entering.
claims.say: magic guard on before the last portal

claims.text: Bishops gain Resurrection through the Method of Contradiction quest, which begins by gathering the items it asks for.
claims.say: rez comes from the method of contradiction quest

claims.text: Give the gathered quest items to Carta and she hands you the Cold Flame.
claims.say: give carta the items and she hands you the cold flame

claims.text: Carry the Cold Flame through Aqua Road to the cave in Dangerous Sea Gorge II.
claims.say: take the cold flame to the cave in dangerous sea gorge ii

claims.text: Inside that cave, stand facing the large pot, drop the Cold Flame on the ground and wait until it vanishes.
claims.say: stand at the big pot, drop cold flame, wait till it's gone

claims.text: Deathly Fear is not dropped by the bats in The Forgotten Darkness; you earn it by finishing the jump quest there.
claims.say: deathly fear is from finishing the jq, not the bats

claims.text: The Forgotten Darkness jump quest opens with lots of falling and hopping over fences; push as far right as you can without dropping too low.
claims.say: start of the jq: keep going right over the fences

claims.text: The second section is in the bottom right where the ground forms stairs; look for floating platforms one jump to the right of a step.
claims.say: at the stairs bottom right, look for platforms a jump to the right

claims.text: Drop mesos as markers on platforms you have found in The Forgotten Darkness, since you will fall many times.
claims.say: drop some mesos to mark spots, you'll fall a lot

claims.text: The final stretch of the jump quest climbs up and over the exit door, and you reach it by dropping onto it from above.
claims.say: the exit door is reached by climbing over it and dropping on it

claims.text: Make sure you have a free Etc slot before going through the exit door of the jump quest.
claims.say: free up an etc slot before you take the exit door

claims.text: The jump quest for the Bishop skill Resurrection has invisible platforms; drop mesos onto them to reveal where each platform begins and ends.
claims.say: drop mesos in the resurrection jq to see the hidden platforms

claims.text: A LUKless Ice/Lightning puts every AP into INT: each INT is one magic attack and also adds MP, so pure INT beats spending points on LUK.
claims.say: i/l just stacks int every level, luk wastes magic

claims.text: If you want base LUK to wear higher-level gear, keep it around 20-30 and let equips supply the rest. Extra LUK for defense is not worth the lost damage, since Magic Guard covers end-game bosses.
claims.say: keep luk around 20-30 if you want gear, magic guard covers def

claims.text: First job: one Energy Bolt to unlock Magic Claw, max Improved MP Recovery and Improved Max MP Increase, max Magic Claw (your main attack until second job) and max Magic Guard. Skip Magic Armor.
claims.say: mage 1st job: 1 energy bolt, max claw, mp skills and magic guard

claims.text: Magic Guard is the most important early mage skill; without it you die easily, so max it before most other first job skills.
claims.say: max magic guard early or you will die a lot
