claims.text: At second job take one Teleport for mobility, then put everything into Thunder Bolt; its area damage makes it the training skill until third job.
claims.say: 2nd job: 1 teleport then max thunder bolt, thats your grinder

claims.text: After Thunder Bolt, either max Teleport, MP Eater, Meditation then Cold Beam, or Cold Beam first then MP Eater, Teleport and Meditation. Some prefer MP Eater first because it nearly removes the need for MP pots.
claims.say: after thunder bolt: mp eater, teleport, meditation, cold beam

claims.text: Cold Beam is a single-target attack that is strong against fire-based monsters, while Slow is nearly useless, so a single point there is plenty.
claims.say: cold beam is good on fire mobs, slow is basically useless

claims.text: At third job max Ice Strike first: it freezes mobs and is the main skill for training.
claims.say: 3rd job: max ice strike first, it freezes mobs for training

claims.text: Third job mage gear to have: a Zakum Helmet with INT, Broken Glasses from Ludibrium PQ, an INT overall such as a bathrobe, magic attack earrings, cape, gloves and a Maple Shield, plus Squishy Shoes from Kerning PQ.
claims.say: zakum helm, broken glasses, bathrobe and ma gloves for 3rd job

claims.text: Elemental Wand 3 boosts ice skills like Ice Strike and Blizzard, and Wand 4 boosts lightning like Thunder Spear and Chain Lightning, until you can use Wand 7 or 8. For big area grinding many players pick Wand 3 and Wand 7.
claims.say: ele wand 3 for ice, wand 4 for lightning, then 7 or 8 later

claims.text: Fourth job: put points into Blizzard first for more damage and one-hit kills at a lower level, then Maple Warrior, which also lifts your magic. Maple Warrior 20 is nice but not required.
claims.say: 4th job: max blizzard first, then maple warrior

claims.text: If you do not plan on using Ifrit or Chain Lightning, max Infinity first: it holds your MP steady for its duration so you can keep casting, which saves potions.
claims.say: if you skip ifrit, max infinity to save on mp pots

claims.text: Defeat Grendel's clone for the Black Charm, trade it to Grendel for the Necklace of Strength, then at Sharp Cliff II bring a Dark Crystal and answer five questions at the secret door for the Necklace of Wisdom. Give both to Robeira.
claims.say: beat grendel's clone, then dark crystal and a quiz at sharp cliff

claims.text: Spend all your remaining skill points before a third or fourth job advancement or it will not let you advance. Leftover AP is fine.
claims.say: spend all your sp before the job advance or it wont work

claims.text: From 50 to 70 the Forest of Golem has an excellent spawn rate and is the author's top pick; Zipangu Secret Spa, the Singapore Ghost Ship (Selkie Jr. and Slimy) and Neo Huroid in Magatia also work.
claims.say: lv50-70 forest of golem has great spawns, ghost ship too

claims.text: Kerning City Party Quest can be started at level 21 and is a good source of exp for the 20s.
claims.say: kerning pq opens at lv21, nice exp for the 20s

claims.text: Ludibrium Party Quest requires level 35 and Monster Carnival level 30, and both are good for levels 30-50.
claims.say: ludi pq needs 35 and carnival needs 30, good for lv30-50

claims.text: Ludibrium Maze Party Quest requires level 51 and is a useful training option through the 50s and 60s.
claims.say: maze pq opens at lv51, good for 50-70

claims.text: Romeo and Juliet Party Quest is good exp for levels 70-75, and the Ellin Forest prequest and party quest suit levels 120-130.
claims.say: r&j pq around 70-75, ellin forest pq at 120-130

claims.text: Arch Mages cannot cast Holy Symbol, so spots like Dreamy Ghost are better with a priest, and many players keep a low-level Cleric alt to supply it.
claims.say: i/l has no holy symbol, party with a priest for more exp

claims.text: Ice/Lightning mages farm items by casting Ifrit and letting it kill mobs while standing by, since a summon needs little attention, and loot what it kills yourself.
claims.say: cast ifrit and let it farm for you, then pick up the loot

claims.text: White Scrolls are in the prize pool of the New Leaf City Gachapon, so that machine is the usual place to spend tickets hoping for one.
claims.say: white scrolls come out of the nlc gach

claims.text: The Gachapon at Mushroom Shrine can give Chaos Scroll 60%.
claims.say: chaos scrolls drop from the mushroom shrine gach

claims.text: Sky Ski (level 85) and Fishing Pole (level 45) both come from the Showa Town Gachapon.
claims.say: sky ski and fishing pole are from the showa gach

claims.text: Equips in the New Leaf City Gachapon include Stonetooth Sword, Elemental Wand 5, Purple Surfboard and Horus's Eye.
claims.say: nlc gach has stonetooth, ele wand 5 and purple surfboard

claims.text: The CBD Gachapon in Singapore holds Elemental Wand 7, Elemental Staff 4, Doomsday Staff and the Eviscerator.
claims.say: cbd gach has ele wand 7, ele staff 4 and doomsday staff

claims.text: Sleepywood's Gachapon can give Elemental Staff 5, Elemental Wand 3 and Shield Earrings.
claims.say: sleepy gach has ele staff 5, ele wand 3, shield earrings

claims.text: Showa's Gachapon also carries Elemental Staff 7, Elemental Wand 2, the Crossheider and the level 120 Dragon Khanjar.
claims.say: showa gach also has ele staff 7, crossheider, dragon khanjar

claims.text: Mushroom Shrine's Gachapon gives the level 130 Elemental Wand 6 and the Purple Gaia Cape.
claims.say: shrine gach gives ele wand 6 and purple gaia cape

claims.text: Perion's Gachapon is the warrior machine: it gives Dragon Carabella, Dragon Claymore, Blue Dragon Helmet, Dark Valhalla Helmet and Mikhail among other warrior gear.
claims.say: perion gach is the warrior one, dragon claymore and carabella

claims.text: Weapon attack scrolls for every warrior weapon (swords, axes, blunt weapons, spears, pole arms), including 30% and 70% dark versions, come from the Perion Gachapon.
claims.say: perion gach is where warrior weapon att scrolls come from

claims.text: Henesys' Gachapon is the bowman machine, with Dragon Shiner Bow, Red Hunter Gloves, Yellow Crow, Fire Raven and bow attack scrolls.
claims.say: henesys gach has dragon shiner bow and bow att scrolls

claims.text: Nautilus Harbor's Gachapon is the pirate one, giving Concerto, Red Belly Duke, Burning Hell, Fury Claw and gun and knuckler attack scrolls.
claims.say: nautilus gach is the pirate one, concerto and gun scrolls

claims.text: New Leaf City's Gachapon has a wide spread of armor scrolls, including 100% cape scrolls for INT, DEX and LUK and a 100% glove magic attack scroll.
claims.say: nlc gach has lots of armor scrolls, 100% cape ones too

claims.text: Showa's Gachapon is heavy on 100% armor scrolls, such as overall for STR, overall armor for INT, topwear for LUK and shoes for speed.
claims.say: showa gach drops a lot of 100% armor scrolls

claims.text: Elixirs come from the New Leaf City, Showa, Mushroom Shrine, CBD and Sleepywood Gachapons, and Power Elixirs from nearly every Gachapon.
claims.say: most gachs can give power elixirs

claims.text: Hwabi Throwing-Stars and Eternal Bullets turn up in the New Leaf City, Showa and CBD Gachapons; Vital Bullets come from Sleepywood's.
claims.say: hwabi stars and eternal bullets from nlc, showa, cbd gach

claims.text: Chairs by Gachapon: Beach Chair from Showa, Fishing Chair from Nautilus, White Seal Cushion from Kerning, and Green Chair plus Grey Seal Cushion from New Leaf City.
claims.say: fishing chair from nautilus gach, beach chair from showa

claims.text: More Gachapon chairs: Red Round Chair and Blue Seal Cushion from CBD, The Red Relaxer and Kadomatsu from Mushroom Shrine, and Amorian Relaxer, Moon Star Chair and Warrior Throne from Sleepywood.
claims.say: warrior throne and moon star chair come from sleepy gach

claims.text: Protect Ludibrium, from Mr. Bouffon, rewards 30 fame, the most of any quest on the fame list.
claims.say: protect ludibrium gives 30 fame

claims.text: A Brave Warrior to Defeat King Clang Appears! rewards 10 to 15 fame.
claims.say: the king clang quest gives 10-15 fame

claims.text: A Puppet gives 7 fame along the way but also takes 5 away, so it only nets 2.
claims.say: a puppet nets you just 2 fame

claims.text: Movie Star needs its prequest done before level 40, so plan it early.
claims.say: do the movie star prequest before lv40

claims.text: Building a New House for Blackbull gives 2 fame but needs 10 fame to start.
claims.say: blackbull's house quest needs 10 fame to start

claims.text: Quests that give 1 fame: Shumi's Lost Coin, Shumi's Lost Bundle of Money, Shumi's Lost Sack of Money, Sabitrama and the Diet Medicine, Jay's Curiosity and Food-Hunting for Moppie III.
claims.say: shumi's lost money quests give 1 fame each

claims.text: More 1-fame quests: Dress for Kyrin, The Soul Collector, Returning to Master Sergeant Fox, Gwin's Thanks, Ericsson Loves Cats and Alfonse's Smile.
claims.say: the soul collector and dress for kyrin give 1 fame

claims.text: The Cursed Dolls collecting series pays more as it goes: 1 fame each for 100 and 200 dolls, 2 for 400 and 600, and 3 for 1000.
claims.say: cursed doll quests give up to 3 fame at 1000 dolls

claims.text: Bigger fame quests worth 15 to 20 fame: Restoring the Spirit of the Snow Sculpture, Tae Soo's Reward, Eliminating King Sage Cat and Eliza's Eternal Sleep.
claims.say: eliza's eternal sleep pays 15-20 fame

claims.text: The level 35 Maple Gun is dropped by Ghost Stump, Fire Sentinel, Jr. Seal, Stone Golem and Mithril Mutae.
claims.say: farm ghost stumps or stone golems for a maple gun

claims.text: The level 35 Maple Knuckle is dropped by Zombie Mushroom, Drumming Bunny, Barnard Gray, Ginseng Jar and Hector.
claims.say: zombie mushrooms drop the maple knuckle

claims.text: The level 35 Maple Bow is dropped by Block Golem, Tick-Tock, Iron Hog, Wild Boar and Wild Kargo.
claims.say: wild boars drop the maple bow

claims.text: The level 35 Maple Claw is dropped by Zombie Lupin, Wraith, Tauromacis, Zombie Mushroom, Jr. Cellion and Werewolf.
claims.say: zombie lupins and wraiths drop the maple claw

claims.text: The level 35 Maple Crow is dropped by Star Pixie and Block Golem.
claims.say: star pixies drop the maple crow

claims.text: The level 35 Maple Sword only comes from Block Golems in Ludibrium.
claims.say: only block golems in ludi drop the maple sword

claims.text: The level 35 Maple Staff is dropped by Master Death Teddy, Sentinel and Ligator, not by Fire Boars.
claims.say: ligators drop the maple staff, fire boars dont

claims.text: The level 43 Maple Storm Pistol is dropped by Krip, Lorang, Transformed Yeti, Buffoon and Birk.
claims.say: krips and lorangs drop the maple storm pistol

claims.text: The level 43 Maple Storm Finger is dropped by Chipmunk, Chief Gray, Kru, Dark Rash and Dual Ghost Pirate.
claims.say: chief grays drop the maple storm finger

claims.text: The level 43 Maple Soul Searcher is dropped by Drumming Bunny, Wild Boar, Red Drake, Iron Hog and Drake.
claims.say: wild boars drop the maple soul searcher

claims.text: The level 43 Maple Crossbow is dropped by Malady, Block Golem and King Block Golem.
claims.say: block golems drop the maple crossbow

claims.text: The level 43 Maple Wagner is dropped by Wild Boar, Bain, Trixter and Zombie Lupin.
claims.say: wild boars drop the maple wagner

claims.text: The level 43 Maple Soul Singer drops from Brown Teddy, not from Green Mushrooms as some lists claim.
claims.say: brown teddies drop the maple soul singer

claims.text: The level 43 Maple Scorpio is dropped by Nependeath and Ligator.
claims.say: ligators drop the maple scorpio

claims.text: The level 43 Maple Impaler is dropped by Toy Trojan, Lazy Buffy and Wild Boar.
claims.say: toy trojans drop the maple impaler

claims.text: The level 43 Maple Lama Staff is dropped by Ratz and Horny Mushroom.
claims.say: horny mushrooms drop the maple lama staff

claims.text: The level 43 Maple Dragon Axe is dropped by Wild Boar and Cerebes.
claims.say: wild boars drop the maple dragon axe

claims.text: The level 43 Maple Doom Singer is dropped by Cold Eye, Tauromacis, Drake, Brown Teddy, Lucida and Cerebes.
claims.say: cold eyes and drakes drop the maple doom singer

claims.text: The level 64 Maple Golden Claw is dropped by Firebomb, Grupin, Hector, Jr. Lucida and Dark Drake.
claims.say: grupins and firebombs drop the maple golden claw

claims.text: The level 64 Maple Kandiva Bow is dropped by Miner Zombie, Sage Cat, Wild Kargo, Officer Skeleton, Transformed Yeti and Soul Teddy.
claims.say: sage cats and soul teddies drop the maple kandiva bow

claims.text: The level 64 Maple Skanda is dropped by Luster Pixie, Grizzly, Dyle, Soul Teddy and Zeno.
claims.say: luster pixies drop the maple skanda

claims.text: The level 64 Maple Nishada is dropped by Stone Golem, Dark Stone Golem, White Fang, Sage Cat and Dark Drake.
claims.say: stone golems drop the maple nishada

claims.text: The level 64 Maple Asura Dagger is dropped by Hogul, Sr. Bellflower Root, Reindeer, Lazy Buffy and Neo Huroid.
claims.say: sr bellflower roots drop the maple asura dagger

claims.text: The level 64 Maple Dark Mate is dropped by Skeleton Soldier, Mr. Alli, Soul Teddy, Ice Drake and Homun.
claims.say: skeleton soldiers drop the maple dark mate

claims.text: The level 64 Maple Glory Sword is dropped by Sr. Bellflower Root, The Book Ghost, Stone Golem and Hector.
claims.say: stone golems drop the maple glory sword

claims.text: The level 64 Maple Steel Axe is dropped by Lioner, Mixed Golem, Malady and Roid.
claims.say: lioners drop the maple steel axe

claims.text: The level 64 Maple Havoc Hammer is dropped by Dark Stone Golem, Miner Zombie, Red Drake, Panda and Neo Huroid.
claims.say: dark stone golems drop the maple havoc hammer

claims.text: The level 64 Maple Karstan is dropped by Sr. Bellflower Root and Neo Huroid.
claims.say: sr bellflower roots drop the maple karstan

claims.text: The level 64 Maple Soul Spear is dropped by Cellion, MT-09, Hector, Sage Cat and Homun.
claims.say: cellions drop the maple soul spear

claims.text: The level 64 Maple Wisdom Staff is dropped by Firebomb, Mr. Alli, Kru, the split-off Dark Pepe and Homun.
claims.say: firebombs drop the maple wisdom staff

claims.text: The level 64 Maple Soul Rohen is dropped by Lioner, The Book Ghost, Mixed Golem, Buffy and Yeti.
claims.say: lioners drop the maple soul rohen

claims.text: The level 64 Maple Demon Axe is dropped by The Book Ghost, Sage Cat, Jr. Lucida and Dark Drake.
claims.say: dark drakes drop the maple demon axe

claims.text: The level 64 Maple Belzet is dropped by Dark Jr. Yeti, Coolie Zombie, Sage Cat and Master Soul Teddy.
claims.say: coolie zombies drop the maple belzet

claims.text: The level 64 Maple Shine Wand is dropped by Samiho, Straw Target Dummy, Soul Teddy and Jr. Lucida.
claims.say: samiho and soul teddies drop the maple shine wand

claims.text: The level 20 Maple Shield is dropped by Jr. Yeti and Platoon Chronos.
claims.say: jr yetis drop the lv20 maple shield

claims.text: Mia in Henesys makes the level 64 Maple shields from a level 20 Maple Shield, 20 Screws, 20 Processed Wood and 3 crystals: Wisdom for the Magician one, Power for the Warrior one, LUK for the Thief one.
claims.say: mia in henesys makes the lv64 maple shields

claims.text: Amoria PQ needs 6 players: all married (engaged is not enough), level 40+, at least one of each gender, and an Entrance Ticket each. They need not be married to each other. The time limit is 1 hour 15 minutes.
claims.say: amoria pq: 6 married players lvl 40+, both genders, with a ticket

claims.text: Don't enter until the whole party is ready: the ticket is taken at entry so you cannot leave and come back. Everyone talks to Amos for the waiting area and the leader goes in last. If the channel is busy, change channel.
claims.say: cant leave amoria pq once in, ticket is taken, be ready first

claims.text: Entry is level 40, but Geist Balrog can wipe weak parties. The author never invites anyone under level 70, finds even the 70s iffy, and feels much safer with level 85 or higher.
claims.say: geist balrog in amoria pq is rough under lvl 70, 85+ is safer

claims.text: Bring mostly strong attackers, especially ranged ones like Hermits and Rangers/Snipers since Geist Balrog flies around the platforms. A Priest's Bless helps a lot, but a weaker party under about level 80 may prefer another attacker.
claims.say: bring ranged attackers for the amoria boss, priest bless helps

claims.text: Stage 1: Amos opens three glowing portals and only one leads to the middle area. There women take the left portal and men the right, and each side kills every monster on its half.
claims.say: amoria stage 1: girls go left, guys go right, kill everything

claims.text: Stage 2: five players hang on three ropes while the leader stays on the ground and talks to Amos. A layout like 041 means 0 on the left rope, 4 in the middle, 1 on the right. You get 6 tries; start with 500.
claims.say: amoria ropes stage: start with all 5 on the left rope (500)

claims.text: Amos only answers each rope layout with whether the ropes weigh the same or all differently. A decision chart that branches on those Same/Different answers solves the rope stage within the 6 tries.
claims.say: ropes stage: amos only says same or different, use a chart

claims.text: Stage 3 has 9 platforms (4 top, 5 bottom) and five players must stand on the right ones. Start on the four top platforms plus the first bottom one. A wrong layout spawns slimes: one slime per correct platform.
claims.say: amoria stage 3: slime count = how many platforms are right

claims.text: Move only the bottom player one platform at a time. More slimes than the last check means the new platform is correct, fewer means it is wrong. Don't kill the slimes before counting them, and marking correct platforms with mesos helps.
claims.say: move one player at a time, more slimes = that platform is right

claims.text: Stage 4: collect 50 Cupid Code Pieces from the Evil Eyes and Toy Trojans. With six players, one sits out (usually the leader) and the other five collect 10 each and hand them over.
claims.say: amoria stage 4: 50 cupid code pieces, 10 each from 5 people

claims.text: Before clearing stage 4, make sure everyone is present and ready, because the next run-right stage starts at once and anyone who wandered off will die and waste the party's effort.
claims.say: dont clear stage 4 until everyone is with the party

claims.text: Stage 5: right after stage 4 you must run right while monsters chase you. Most hit weakly, but the slow Rombards at the back hit extremely hard, so keep moving and don't stop. Haste and other speed buffs don't work here.
claims.say: amoria run stage: keep running right, haste doesnt work

claims.text: In stage 5 you open the gateways with a normal weapon attack, since skills don't work. Only one person should hit a gate at a time, because several attackers at once are known to disconnect players.
claims.say: open the gates with a normal attack, only one person at a time

claims.text: Geist Balrog has three forms and the last flies around the warp platforms. Send one ranged player (Hermit or Ranger works best) to pull it down to where the party waits, so repeated knockback on the ground makes big damage.
claims.say: lure geist balrog down with one ranged guy, party waits below

claims.text: The thorns on the platforms hurt only a little compared to a Geist Balrog hit, so stand in them for cover and to avoid being knocked off. Just watch your HP if you stay on thorns for long.
claims.say: stand on the thorns vs geist balrog, they hurt less than his hits

claims.text: Geist Balrog casts Super Defense, Super Magic Defense and Dispel. Watch your buffs, mages should keep an eye on Magic Guard, and recast party buffs like Haste or Hyper Body once everyone gathers.
claims.say: geist balrog dispels, recheck magic guard, haste and hyper body

claims.text: The bonus stage lasts about a minute. Bring a fast weapon rather than a slow spear or staff, and hit two boxes that are close together in alternation during the attack delay to open twice as many.
claims.say: use a fast weapon in the amoria bonus and hit two boxes at once

claims.text: The Power Stance quest means lasting 10 minutes alongside Tylus; monsters you kill come back near him, so the aim is to hold them away rather than kill them.
claims.say: stance quest: dont kill the mobs, they respawn on tylus

claims.text: A Dragon Knight can solo the Power Stance quest: strip accuracy gear and hold a weak low-level polearm so every hit misses, use Dragon Roar to grab aggro, drag the mobs to one end of the map and roar again now and then.
claims.say: solo stance as drk: no acc gear, roar and drag mobs to a corner

claims.text: Other warriors may hold aggro in the Power Stance quest the same way with Shout or Rush, or by equipping a spear or polearm and using Slash Blast while geared to miss.
claims.say: other warriors can try shout, rush or slash blast to hold aggro

claims.text: Warriors usually bring a mage along for the Power Stance quest, but it can be finished alone when no mage is free.
claims.say: no mage around? you can still do stance alone

claims.text: On a warrior's first job, put SP into Improving Max HP Increase first, then Slash Blast, then Power Strike. Leftover points can go anywhere since they hardly matter.
claims.say: max hp increase first, then slash blast, then power strike

claims.text: Spend every first-job skill point before trying the second job advancement; leftover first-job SP blocks the advance to Fighter.
claims.say: spend all your first job sp or you cant advance

claims.text: Slash Blast beats Power Strike whenever it hits more than two monsters, which is nearly always during early training, so use Power Strike only for single targets.
claims.say: slash blast beats power strike once theres 3+ mobs

claims.text: For a sword Fighter's second job, max Sword Mastery, Sword Booster and Power Guard. Extra SP can go into Axe Booster and Axe Mastery for fun, but axes do less damage overall.
claims.say: fighter: max sword mastery, booster and power guard

claims.text: Rage's attack bonus does not stack with attack potions and replaces the potion buff on party members, so this author skips it and relies on long-lasting potions like Warrior's Elixirs.
claims.say: rage overrides atk pots so i skip it

claims.text: Do not spend SP on Final Attack: when it procs while you hit a pack, its damage is split across every target, so it adds less than just using your area skill.
claims.say: dont bother with final attack, it spreads dmg thin

claims.text: A Crusader's third job is simple: max Combo Attack. Keeping the orbs full is better than burning them on Panic or Coma and rebuilding them afterwards.
claims.say: crusader just maxes combo attack and keeps the orbs up

claims.text: Improving MP Recovery, Shield Mastery and Armor Crash are poor picks for a Crusader. Armor Crash cannot remove the melee-cancel buff late bosses use, and Shield Mastery only adds weapon defense.
claims.say: skip armor crash and shield mastery as crusader

claims.text: Shout is not worth much: it has short range, deals little damage and is slow to use, so only invest if you want to.
claims.say: shout is slow and weak, not worth the sp

claims.text: On reaching fourth job, put one point in Rush for its mobility, then raise Brandish to level 11 and switch to it as your main attack in place of Slash Blast.
claims.say: 4th job: 1 in rush, brandish to 11 then use it over slash blast

claims.text: After maxing Brandish, take Advanced Combo (its skill book drops from Zakum), then Power Stance, then Maple Warrior. Maple Warrior can come before Stance if knockback does not bother you.
claims.say: after brandish go adv combo, then stance, then maple warrior

claims.text: Keep one SP for Hero's Will before fighting Horntail; it cures seduce, which otherwise shoves you to the right and stops you from drinking potions.
claims.say: save 1 sp for hero's will before horntail, it cures seduce

claims.text: Once the core skills are done, max Rush because each level lets it carry you farther, then Achilles for tankiness, then a point in Hero's Will for Horntail.
claims.say: after core skills max rush then achilles

claims.text: Guardian only suits a one-handed weapon with a shield; most Heroes choose a two-handed Stonetooth Sword since only one item needs scrolling and two-handers gain more from strong attack potions like Heartstopper and Onyx Apple.
claims.say: guardian only if you use 1h + shield, most go 2h

claims.text: A Hero is built around STR; DEX is only for accuracy and the Stonetooth Sword requirement. Get DEX from gear, since Maple Warrior scales off base stats so extra base STR pays off more.
claims.say: hero = str, get dex from gear not ap

claims.text: If you are short on funds by level 120, a base DEX of about 30 to 50 is a fine compromise; AP Resets can shift points later and scrolls cover the rest of the accuracy.
claims.say: 30-50 base dex is a safe middle if youre not funded

claims.text: A four-base-DEX Hero only works if funded: either get leeched through the first levels or wear gear with plenty of accuracy from the start.
claims.say: 4 base dex hero needs good accuracy gear

claims.text: Putting 80 base DEX on a Hero is the old classic but wasteful now; DEX scrolls and gear provide it, so you can save that AP for STR instead of paying for resets later.
claims.say: 80 base dex is outdated, scroll dex gear instead

claims.text: Swords beat axes for a Brandish Hero because the skill alternates stab and slash hits, and axes get a lower multiplier on stabs, while swords have one steady multiplier. Good axes are also scarce.
claims.say: swords over axes for brandish, steadier dmg

claims.text: A Gold Surfboard, dropped by Slimes, is a good first-job weapon thanks to its reach and early attack speed; hunt Slimes to train and to get one.
claims.say: gold surfboard from slimes is great for first job

claims.text: Lionheart is the weapon for levels 35 to 50: it is fast, with a booster it is the fastest weapon around, and it drops from Wild Boars, a mob you train on at that stage anyway.
claims.say: use a lionheart around 35, wild boars drop it

claims.text: If you have funds, a Flaming Katana from the Sleepywood Gachapon is much stronger than other one-handed swords around level 38 and is fast; it stays useful with a weapon-attack shield until about 70.
claims.say: flaming katana from sleepywood gacha is strong at 38+

claims.text: Diao Chan Sword drops from Cloud Fox, a low-level mob that is also good for mesos, and matches the Flaming Katana's speed, so hunt it if gachapon luck fails.
claims.say: cloud foxes drop diao chan sword, decent fast sword

claims.text: Midway through second job move to a Japanese Map, another fast sword; check shops or spam attacks on Leprechauns until one drops.
claims.say: japanese map from leprechauns is a solid fast sword

claims.text: Maple Soul Rohen gives a big accuracy boost though it is the slowest option; unfunded Fighters can use it to train on tougher mobs like Wolf Spiders earlier. Mixed Golems in Forest of Golem drop it.
claims.say: maple soul rohen = lots of acc, mixed golems drop it

claims.text: Red Katana (dropped by Pepe, Nightghost and Beetle) is a fast sword good for training and bossing from level 70. Use Maple Soul Rohen instead only if accuracy is the problem.
claims.say: red katana is fast and good for 70-100

claims.text: Stonetooth Sword is the recommended endgame Hero weapon for its speed and how easy a near-perfect one is to get, but it needs 120 DEX, so plan gear and scrolls for DEX early or you must wash base DEX later.
claims.say: stonetooth needs 120 dex, plan your dex gear early

claims.text: Dragon Claymore, craftable in Leafre, is the best two-handed sword; with a booster it can hit Bigfoot without wasting swings on its invincibility frames.
claims.say: dragon claymore with booster is best for bigfoot

claims.text: A Bathrobe bought in the Showa spa is a fine overall for levels 20 to 100 because of its speed bonus, which helps the close-range grinding warriors do; scroll it with STR or DEX.
claims.say: bathrobe from showa spa gives speed, good until 100

claims.text: Early on use a Green Bandana (Leprechaun drop), scrolled for accuracy, as your helmet if you want to run low on DEX.
claims.say: green bandana scrolled for acc is a fine early hat

claims.text: The Zakum Helmet is the best warrior helmet and gives lots of accuracy, so get it early. Scroll it for DEX if using a Stonetooth Sword, or hunt a clean high-STR one for other weapons.
claims.say: zakum helmet is the best hat, tons of acc

claims.text: Start with attack-scrolled Work Gloves (crafted in Kerning City) and swap to Stormcaster Gloves (crafted in New Leaf City) around level 50; a good pair is a big damage jump worth splurging on.
claims.say: work gloves early, stormcaster gloves from 50

claims.text: For shoes early, Black Gomushin from the Kerning City weapon shop already has speed and is cheap; later Red Snowshoes from El Nath have an extra slot. Scroll for speed or DEX depending on accuracy needs.
claims.say: black gomushin is cheap speed shoes early on

claims.text: Endgame shoes are Facestompers, crafted in New Leaf City, but they get very expensive. Blue Crescent Boots from Skelegon are a cheaper option, especially for Stonetooth users since they carry dual stats.
claims.say: facestompers are best shoes, blue crescent boots cheaper

claims.text: If you need accuracy at lower levels, a Sad Mask from the Singapore Gachapon is a good face accessory because it comes with a large clean accuracy bonus.
claims.say: sad mask from singapore gacha gives good acc

claims.text: Accuracy is the main weakness of an unfunded Hero in the mid levels; offset it with accuracy potions and equips carrying DEX, LUK or accuracy.
claims.say: mid level heroes miss a lot, use acc gear or pots

claims.text: Power Guard and Achilles together let a Hero shrug off touch damage from mobs, and with a few HP washes it can tank most bosses.
claims.say: power guard + achilles lets heroes tank touch dmg

claims.text: For fast exp, rush only stages 1 to 3 of Ludibrium PQ: a good party finishes them in about four and a half minutes, while the full run takes three to four times as long and the later stages add little exp for the time.
claims.say: rush stages 1 to 3 in lpq, the full run wastes time

claims.text: AOE classes are much better than single-target ones for the stage 1-3 rush, because in stage 3 the Bloctopus jump away when their box breaks, and an AOE attack right after the break pins them until they die.
claims.say: bring aoe classes for lpq, bloctopus run off from single target

claims.text: A strong LPQ rush party is two Spearmen, one Fighter, one Hunter, one Assassin and one Ice/Lightning mage, all level 40 or higher. If a class is missing, just replace it with another AOE class.
claims.say: lpq rush party: 2 spears, fighter, hunter, sin, i/l. aoe if missing

claims.text: In LPQ stage 3 send one Spearman and one Hunter, both level 45 or higher, to the top half. The Spearman breaks boxes and fights at close range while the Hunter stuns and picks off escaping Bloctopus.
claims.say: lpq stage 3: spear and hunter take the top half

claims.text: On the bottom half of LPQ stage 3, one Spearman breaks the first two boxes while the rest run past. The Ice/Lightning mage takes the lone right-side box; Fighter and Assassin drop to the very bottom for its two boxes.
claims.say: lpq stage 3 bottom: spear takes first 2 boxes, i/l the right one

claims.text: A Hunter is a poor choice for the lone right-side box in LPQ stage 3, since it has to retreat to shoot after breaking it and most of the Bloctopus escape. A mage or any warrior suits that box better.
claims.say: don't give hunters the lone box in lpq stage 3, they get away

claims.text: A Fighter is the warrior of choice for an LPQ rush party because Rage boosts the whole party's attack.
claims.say: fighter is the best warrior for lpq, rage helps everyone

claims.text: An Assassin is useful in LPQ for Haste, for killing the hard-to-reach Ratz in stage 1, and for ranged single-target damage on Bloctopus that slip away in stage 3.
claims.say: sin in lpq is for haste and hitting the ratz others can't reach

claims.text: An Ice/Lightning mage fits an LPQ rush party because its AOE needs no knockback and Teleport speeds up stage 1; a mage is also needed if you ever play the full run.
claims.say: i/l is good in lpq, no knockback needed and teleport for stage 1

claims.text: As party leader, hand out stage 3 jobs at the end of stage 2, before turning in the passes. Give a rough split on the first run and the detailed instructions on the second, so nobody is overloaded.
claims.say: assign lpq stage 3 jobs right before handing in passes

claims.text: It pays to wait a few minutes in channel 1 for level 40+ members with the right classes, and to keep good partners on your buddy list, since a strong party saves far more time over a long session.
claims.say: wait for a good lpq party, good members save time all session

claims.text: A warrior's hit range grows with total weapon attack times the weapon's multiplier on STR plus DEX; DEX is minor, so ignoring it when comparing weapons gives under 1% error.
claims.say: warrior dmg scales with weapon att and weapon mult x str, dex minor

claims.text: Which warrior weapon is best depends on how much attack you get from outside the weapon (gloves, cape, face accessory, shoes, necklace, medal and attack potions like Onyx Apple), so count that before choosing.
claims.say: the best warrior weapon depends on how much outside att you have

claims.text: When comparing a one-handed weapon with a two-hander, add the shield's attack to the one-hander's attack; do not count it as outside attack or the comparison comes out wrong.
claims.say: add your shield's att to the 1h weapon when comparing with a 2h

claims.text: HP washing means building up spare max MP and then spending AP Resets to convert that MP into max HP. It is the standard way some classes reach high HP.
claims.say: hp washing is turning spare max mp into max hp with ap resets

claims.text: Assassins, bowmen (hunters and crossbowmen), gunslingers and spearmen are the classes that genuinely need to HP wash. Other classes can get by without it.
claims.say: assassins, bowmen, gunslingers and spearmen should hp wash

claims.text: Fighters and pages are cheap to wash, so washing them is a reasonable extra, but they do not need it to function.
claims.say: fighters and pages are cheap to wash but it's optional

claims.text: Brawlers and bandits can be washed too, but it is expensive for them and not necessary.
claims.say: brawlers and bandits can wash but it's pricey and optional

claims.text: Mages can wash, but extra HP or MP does little for them, so nearly all mages skip washing.
claims.say: mages skip washing, extra hp and mp barely helps them

claims.text: Warriors are the cheapest class to wash: each AP reset into HP gives them roughly 50 max HP while costing only about 4 max MP.
claims.say: warriors wash cheapest, ~50 hp per reset for only ~4 mp

claims.text: Thieves and bowmen gain about 16 to 20 max HP per AP reset into HP and lose about 12 max MP each time, so they need much more MP set aside than warriors.
claims.say: thieves and bowmen get ~16-20 hp per reset, lose ~12 mp

claims.text: Magicians lose about 90 max MP per washing reset while gaining only 10 to 20 max HP, which is why washing a mage is poor value.
claims.say: mages lose ~90 mp per reset for tiny hp, bad value

claims.text: Gunslingers gain about 20 max HP per washing reset and lose 16 MP, while brawlers gain about 40 HP for the same 16 MP, so brawlers get twice the HP for their MP.
claims.say: brawlers get ~40 hp per reset, gunslingers only ~20

claims.text: Average max HP per level up differs a lot by class: warriors about 66, brawlers about 55, gunslingers about 25, thieves and archers about 22, magicians about 12. Natural HP formulas only apply after second job.
claims.say: hp/level: warriors ~66, brawlers ~55, thief/bowman ~22, mage ~12

claims.text: HP from fresh level-up AP and from AP-reset points is not the same. A thief putting a level-up point into HP gets about 20 to 24 max HP, while a reset point gives only about 16 to 20.
claims.say: fresh level up ap gives thieves more hp than reset ap does

claims.text: Archers can wash either by putting fresh level-up AP into HP or by using AP reset points, since both give about the same HP for them.
claims.say: archers can wash with level up ap or with reset ap

claims.text: Thieves wash with their own method that only allows 5 washes per level, so divide the washes you need by five to see how many levels it will take and start early enough.
claims.say: thieves can only wash 5 times a level, so plan the levels early

claims.text: The spare MP you wash comes from raw INT or INT gear worn while you level up, because INT raises the MP gained per level. Classes that need lots of MP can also MP wash with AP resets.
claims.say: int points or int gear while leveling build the mp you wash

claims.text: As a rule of thumb, MP wash when your washing plan needs more than about 100 raw INT; below that, plain INT and INT gear are enough.
claims.say: if you'd need over 100 raw int, mp wash as well

claims.text: Pirates lose more MP per level when washing than other classes, so plan about 50 extra INT for them when working out an MP washing build.
claims.say: pirates need around 50 extra int to mp wash

claims.text: Each level up leaves a small MP shortfall when washing, so add about 10 INT beyond your calculated optimal INT, whatever number of levels you spread the INT build over.
claims.say: add ~10 extra int to your washing plan to cover the mp shortfall

claims.text: Once you hit your HP goal, use AP resets to take the raw INT back out and put it into your main stat, since the INT was only there to be converted.
claims.say: after the hp goal, reset the raw int back into your main stat

claims.text: Washing a spearman costs far less than washing an assassin, bowman or gunslinger, which cost several times more in AP resets for a high HP goal.
claims.say: spearmen wash way cheaper than assassins, bowmen, gunslingers

claims.text: During Horntail's mass seduce, stay in the middle on the arms with Haste off: you walk slowly to the rocks and take fewer rock hits than when running there.
claims.say: turn haste off for horntail's mass seduce, fewer rock hits

claims.text: Head B and the left arm dispel buffs on Horntail, so the Dark Knight should refresh Hyper Body before it runs out and have it up before mass seduce. Stay next to him so you are re-buffed at once.
claims.say: dk: refresh hyper body early on horntail, head b dispels it

claims.text: Skip the Horntail Party Quest: bring Moira a certificate each from Zakum, Papulatus and Pianus plus three party quest badges for the Certificate of the Dragon Squad, then use the Encrypted Slate of the Squad while not in a party.
claims.say: ht pq can be skipped with the dragon squad certificate from moira

claims.text: The Horntail party quest needs a transformation potion first. Talk to Moira at the Cave of Life entrance and bring 10 Tough Dragon Skin, a Cornian's Dagger, a Cornian's Marrow, a Skull Shoulder Pad and one Manon kill.
claims.say: moira at cave of life entrance gives the ht pq transformation quest

claims.text: A Busted Dagger has to be repaired before it counts: bring it with a Steel Plate and a Mithril Plate to Mos, the weapon forger in Leafre.
claims.say: fix the busted dagger with a steel plate and mithril plate at mos

claims.text: The Dragon Elixir turns you into a Green Cornian for the Cave of Life; you cannot attack or use skills, and leaving the cave undoes it so you must redo the quest, which is repeatable about once an hour.
claims.say: the cornian transform cant attack and wears off if u leave

claims.text: Horntail Party Quest needs at least three players, all level 120 or higher, gathered on the map before the Cave of Life with the transformation quest turned in. Then jump down and talk to Keroben to enter.
claims.say: ht pq needs 3+ players lvl 120+, transformed, talk to keroben

claims.text: Horntail PQ stages 2-4: one member does the jump quest, the rest kill monsters for the key and follow. Drop the key at the shining spot by the portal; the member left behind takes it from the tree and talks to the NPC below it.
claims.say: ht pq stages 2-4: key goes to the shining spot, waiter grabs it

claims.text: Horntail PQ stage 5: one member does the jump quest, the others drop down to kill monsters for a key, then do the jump quest. The key goes to the party leader, who walks through the portal.
claims.say: ht pq stage 5: pass the key to the leader

claims.text: Horntail PQ stage 6: talk to the Horntail's Schedule NPC to be sent to the Cave of Choice. The leader hits the globe from the left or the right, and the side chosen sends everyone to the Cave of Light or the Cave of Darkness.
claims.say: ht pq stage 6: leader hits the globe, left or right picks the cave

claims.text: Horntail PQ stage 7: kill monsters for six keys and hand them to the leader. He climbs the high wall and talks to the NPC, everyone kills the remaining monsters, and the leader talks to the NPC again to warp to the Horntail entrance.
claims.say: ht pq stage 7: collect six keys for the leader, clear the rest

claims.text: Monsters in every stage of the Horntail party quest can drop Life's Root, and every Bishop in the party needs one before the group moves on to the Horntail fight.
claims.say: bishops need a life's root from the pq drops before leaving

claims.text: Kill Horntail's body in this order: tail, legs, wings, the seducing hand, the right head, the left head, the middle head, and the other hand last.
claims.say: ht order: tail, legs, wings, a hand, heads, middle, last hand

claims.text: Before entering the Horntail cave, line the party up as: seduce mule, backup seduce mules (shadowers or warriors), warriors, mages other than Bishops, attacker classes, then Bishops. Only stage three cares about this order.
claims.say: ht entry: sed mule, warriors, mages, attackers, bishops last

claims.text: The two preliminary heads are easy: everyone keeps hitting while a seduce mule hangs on a rope (to the right at the first head, near the top of the rope closest to entry at the second). Watch for Dark Wyverns, which dispel.
claims.say: ht preheads are easy, mule hangs on a rope, watch dark wyverns

claims.text: Both preliminary Horntail heads want at least about 5500 HP for everyone.
claims.say: need around 5.5k hp for the horntail preheads

claims.text: In the real Horntail cave, do not hit the purple crystal on the right until everyone is ready, since it summons Horntail. Parties rest a few minutes here and split up: ranged on the right, melee on the left.
claims.say: dont break the purple crystal until everyone is ready

claims.text: On legs and tail, melee stand left with the seduce party and hit the legs, while ranged stay under the falling rocks on the right and kill the tail without touching it. Bishops follow the seduce in only after the tail dies.
claims.say: ht: ranged right under rocks on tail, melee left on legs

claims.text: For Horntail's legs and tail stage, melee need roughly 9800 HP and ranged roughly 7900 HP.
claims.say: legs and tail need about 9.8k hp melee, 7.9k hp ranged

claims.text: The seduce mule should hang on a rope: a character on a rope does not move when seduced. Call out when you are seduced so the Bishops know to follow.
claims.say: seduce mule hangs on a rope so seduce cant move him

claims.text: For Horntail's wings, the seduce mule moves to the rope on the right and everyone else stands on the platform and attacks. With legs and tail dead you can swap HP gear for stronger gear.
claims.say: after ht legs and tail die, swap hp gear for stronger gear

claims.text: On the side heads the seduce mule returns to the left rope, and extra seducers clear the wyverns the head summons. Red wyverns appear around 75 percent HP, blue around 50 and dark around 25 to 30; the dark ones dispel.
claims.say: ht heads summon red, blue, dark wyverns, dark ones dispel

claims.text: The middle Horntail head has more HP than the others and casts a full-map dispel at about half HP, which is rare, but otherwise plays like the side heads.
claims.say: middle ht head has more hp and a full map dispel at half

claims.text: Horntail's hands mostly mana-burn for 1 damage (about 2000 MP) and cast status effects, so the real threats are the falling rocks and seduce. At 30 percent HP they cast mass seduce on the first ten people in.
claims.say: ht hands just mana burn, watch rocks and the mass seduce

claims.text: Ranged classes (Night Lords, Bowmasters, Marksmen, Corsairs) need roughly 4850 base HP before Hyper Body, about 7700 after, wearing a Zakum Helmet; HP gear or HP washing is recommended.
claims.say: ranged need ~4.8k base hp before hyper body for horntail

claims.text: Mages (I/L, F/P and Bishops) need at least about 2k base HP and 8k MP with maxed Magic Guard on, and must be able to one-hit kill Dark Wyverns. Bishops chosen to be seduce targets need more.
claims.say: mages need 2k hp, 8k mp w/ magic guard, one-shot dark wyverns

claims.text: Bishops need Resurrection maxed for Horntail, and maxed Holy Shield is optional but valuable for the attacking parties.
claims.say: bishops need max resurrection for ht, holy shield is a bonus

claims.text: Melee classes need about 157 accuracy after Bless if they are above level 160, or about 210 below that, so DEX gear is recommended.
claims.say: melee need ~157 acc after bless at 160+, ~210 below, wear dex

claims.text: To hit a monster 100 percent of the time as a warrior, you need accuracy of (55 + 2 x levels you are below the monster) x monster avoid / 15. Training efficiently means hitting with no misses.
claims.say: warrior acc for 100% = (55 + 2 x level gap) x mob avoid / 15

claims.text: Dragon Knights are an exception: level 90 with maximum Hyper Body is enough for Horntail as long as you reliably keep Hyper Body up.
claims.say: dk only needs lv 90 hyper body for ht but must keep it up

claims.text: Shadowers need Shadow Shifter at level 20 or higher for Horntail; higher is better.
claims.say: shadowers need shadow shifter 20+ for ht

claims.text: Buccaneers should have at least level 1 Time Leap for Horntail and keep track of when they last used it.
claims.say: buccaneers need time leap and track when they used it

claims.text: Horntail drops a Nine Spirit's Egg that starts a one-time quest for a Dragon Stone, which you scroll onto the Horntail Necklace once.
claims.say: ht drops nine spirit's eggs for the one-time dragon stone quest

claims.text: A pet only picks up mesos while wearing a Meso Magnet and only picks up items while wearing an Item Pouch; both are Cash Shop pet equips.
claims.say: pet needs meso magnet and item pouch to loot

claims.text: Wing Boots make the pet walk over to drops on its own, and a Binocular widens how far it will go for them.
claims.say: wing boots let your pet run to loot, binocular adds range

claims.text: Magic Scales make the pet grab the drops that will vanish soonest first, and the Item Ignore Pendant lets you pick items for it to skip.
claims.say: item ignore pendant stops your pet grabbing junk

claims.text: The Auto HP Potion Pouch and Auto MP Potion Pouch let your pet drink HP or MP potions from your inventory for you.
claims.say: get the auto hp pouch so your pet pots for you

claims.text: Autopot setup: summon the pet, equip the pouch on it, open the pet section of the equipment window and drag a potion into the empty box beside the pouch, not onto the pouch itself.
claims.say: drag the pot into the box next to the pouch, not onto it

claims.text: Once a potion is placed, the HP/MP Alert slider in System Options sets the percentage your HP or MP must fall below before the pet drinks.
claims.say: set the hp alert slider, pet pots below that percent

claims.text: Pet autopot fires once per trigger, such as taking a hit or using a skill, so a weak potion may not heal enough before the next hit; give the pet potions strong enough that one drink matters.
claims.say: pet pots once per hit, give it stronger pots

claims.text: The author found the pet potion slots clear on logout, so check and set the potions again after each login.
claims.say: redo your pet pot slots after you log in

claims.text: Any potion can go in either pouch slot, for example an HP potion in the MP slot, but each pouch holds only one kind of potion at a time.
claims.say: one pot type per pouch, any pot works in either slot

claims.text: Water of Life resets a pet's expiration date so it can keep being used.
claims.say: water of life resets your pet's expiry

claims.text: A Pet Name Tag renames the pet; the author says putting its name before a command, name then comma then command, makes it obey more often.
claims.say: name your pet and say its name before commands

claims.text: Pets learn extra commands as they level, usually around level 10 or 11 and again at 20 or 21 depending on the pet; a Husky, for example, learns bark at level 10.
claims.say: pets learn new commands around lv10 and lv20

claims.text: Once a pet reaches level 15 you can make it speak by typing /pet followed by your text.
claims.say: at pet lv15 type /pet and text to make it talk

claims.text: The Rock of Evolution from the Cash Shop is what evolves Dragon and Robo pets into their final forms.
claims.say: rock of evolution evolves dragon and robo pets

claims.text: Pets never pick up items or mesos that you dropped yourself.
claims.say: pets wont loot stuff you dropped yourself

claims.text: A pet skips loot when your inventory is full, when you did not deal most of the damage to the monster, or when it is a unique or quest item you cannot hold more of.
claims.say: pet wont loot if your inv is full or you didnt do most dmg

claims.text: Scroll for Pet Equip. for Speed adds 3 speed at 10%, 2 at 60% and 1 at 100%; the bonus reaches your character through the pet's clothing and does not change how fast the pet moves.
claims.say: pet speed scrolls boost your speed through pet clothes

claims.text: Sleepywood's Gachapon can also give 10% and 60% pet equipment scrolls.
claims.say: the sleepy gach can give pet scrolls

claims.text: To make a pet move faster, do the Kenta's Advice quest; the pet needs only 15 closeness, not level 15, and afterwards it keeps pace with your own speed, mounts included.
claims.say: do kentas advice so your pet keeps up with you

claims.text: Having more than one pet out at once requires finishing the pet prequests first.
claims.say: multi pet needs a quest first

claims.text: Pia and the Blue Mushroom is a level 20 quest that rewards a scroll.
claims.say: pia and the blue mushroom at 20 gives a scroll

claims.text: Jane and the Wild Boar is a level 30 quest that rewards a scroll.
claims.say: jane and the wild boar at 30 rewards a scroll

claims.text: Sakura and the Teddy Bear is a level 30 quest that hands out a scroll.
claims.say: sakura and the teddy bear at 30 gives a scroll

claims.text: Food Hunting For Moppie is a level 30 scroll-reward quest in an Orbis chain that begins with Moppie the Lone Dawg.
claims.say: moppie chain in orbis ends with a scroll at food hunting

claims.text: Eos Tower Threatened is a level 35 scroll-reward quest that opens after three earlier quests, the first being Cleaning Up Eos Tower.
claims.say: start with cleaning up eos tower to unlock eos tower threatened

claims.text: Sakura and the Seal is a level 35 quest that rewards a scroll.
claims.say: sakura and the seal at 35 gives a scroll

claims.text: Peace at Eos Tower is a level 40 scroll-reward quest you can only take after Eos Tower Threatened and its prerequisites are done.
claims.say: peace at eos tower at 40 opens after eos tower threatened

claims.text: Sakura the Kitty and the Orange Marble is a level 40 quest with a scroll reward.
claims.say: sakura the kitty and the orange marble at 40 gives a scroll

claims.text: Umi's Spiced Veggies is a level 75 quest that rewards a scroll.
claims.say: umi's spiced veggies at 75 gives a scroll

claims.text: Pam's Request is a level 78 quest with a scroll as the reward.
claims.say: pam's request at 78 rewards a scroll

claims.text: The Committee Challenges is a level 85 quest that rewards a scroll.
claims.say: the committee challenges at 85 gives a scroll

claims.text: Sabitrama's Life Work is a level 85 scroll-reward quest that can only be taken after The Committee Challenges is complete.
claims.say: sabitrama's life work opens after the committee challenges

claims.text: An Unknown Love is a level 85 quest that gives a scroll.
claims.say: an unknown love at 85 gives a scroll

claims.text: Eliminating Blue Mushmom is a level 85 scroll-reward quest at the end of a chain that starts with The Lantern at Mushroom Shrine.
claims.say: start at the lantern at mushroom shrine for the blue mushmom scroll

claims.text: Muse is Cooking is a level 95 scroll-reward quest that requires Nanuke's Ingredients first.
claims.say: do nanuke's ingredients first, then muse is cooking for a scroll

claims.text: From level 11 to 20, Henesys Hunting Ground is a simple place to train.
claims.say: 11 to 20 try henesys hunting ground

claims.text: Evil Eyes in the Ant Tunnel are another option in the 21 to 30 range.
claims.say: evil eyes in ant tunnel work in your 20s

claims.text: Ghost Ship 2 in Singapore can carry you from level 51 until around 73 to 75.
claims.say: ghost ship 2 in singapore carries you from 51 to about 75

claims.text: Guild Party Quest lineup: a character at level 30 or lower, a magician with Teleport at about level 17 or higher, a thief with Dark Sight, at least one ranged attacker and strong damage dealers for Ergoth.
claims.say: gpq needs a lv30 or lower, a teleport mage and a dark sight thief

claims.text: The party leader in the Guild Party Quest has to hold at least the Jr. Master guild rank.
claims.say: gpq leader has to be a jr master

claims.text: At the entry stage, hit the rocks to get a Protector Rock and keep it equipped for the whole run.
claims.say: hit the rocks for a protector rock and keep it on

claims.text: Stage 1: three players each watch the left, middle or right statues while they flash, then the party hits them in that order, for sequences of 4, 5 and 6. A mistake restarts it, so call out each flash with its number.
claims.say: stage 1: split left mid right and call out each statue flash

claims.text: Stage 2: kill the Muscle Stones for a key to the Room of Faith. The mage teleports over the rubble for a key, and the thief uses Dark Sight to slip past the rocks, open the door and take the first spear.
claims.say: room of faith: mage teleports for the key, thief dark sights in

claims.text: In the Room of Glory jump quests, the left ones need Haste and the rightmost one needs Teleport; the combination one uses the order 2 1 5 2 2 1 2.
claims.say: combination jq order is 2 1 5 2 2 1 2

claims.text: To grab a spear, press pick-up and jump together, then drop all four spears on the altars in the Room of Justice.
claims.say: pick up spears by jumping and looting at the same time

claims.text: Stage 3 is a Mastermind puzzle: collect the four item types from monsters and boxes and let only the leader pick them up. He gets 7 guesses, and the NPC says which items are right, misplaced or not in the answer.
claims.say: stage 3 is mastermind, let the leader hold all the items

claims.text: Stage 4: clear the two jump puzzles and send the level 30-or-lower character into its room to kill monsters for the item; kill the Gargoyles at the top with an Arch Mage or Haste and Teleport users.
claims.say: lowbie gets the item in stage 4, mages kill the top gargoyles

claims.text: Drop the stage 4 items on the skeleton in this order: shoes, bottom, top, then hat.
claims.say: skeleton order: shoes, bottom, top, hat

claims.text: Stage 5: one member, ideally the level 30-or-lower one, drops their earrings on the marked spot to be sacrificed. Fighters take the main entrance; weaker members use a broken mouse hole to reach a safe platform.
claims.say: the lowbie drops earrings in stage 5 to be sacrificed

claims.text: Hit the crystal to summon Ergoth, and kill the statues before him, especially the Knight Statues, which dispel buffs and cast 1/1 attacks.
claims.say: summon ergoth with the crystal, kill knight statues first

claims.text: Knight Statue B cannot be damaged until Ergoth is dead, Lion Statue B slows the party, and Lion Statue A heals and casts 1/1.
claims.say: knight statue b can't be hit until ergoth dies

claims.text: The Guild Party Quest bonus stage can give level 30 books for Advanced Combo Attack, Paralyze, Elquines, Chain Lightning, Ifrit, Taunt, Ninja Ambush, Ninja Storm, Assassinate, Sharp Eyes and Frostprey, Hurricane 20, and scrolls.
claims.say: gpq bonus stage can give 4th job mastery books

claims.text: Ludibrium Maze Party Quest is open to characters from level 51 to 70.
claims.say: lmpq is for levels 51 to 70

claims.text: In LMPQ you hit the boxes in each room to spawn monsters and collect the tickets they drop; rooms 12 through 16 have no monsters.
claims.say: hit the boxes in lmpq rooms and grab the mobs' tickets

claims.text: With a full party of six in LMPQ, each member usually takes two rooms that hold the same kind of monster.
claims.say: full lmpq: each person takes two rooms with the same mobs

claims.text: LMPQ rooms 1 and 11 hold Coolie Zombies and suit clerics or warriors who can hit many monsters at once.
claims.say: lmpq rooms 1 and 11 are coolie zombies, good for clerics

claims.text: LMPQ rooms 2 and 10 hold Stone Golems and Dark Stone Golems that any class can clear.
claims.say: rooms 2 and 10 are golems, anyone can do them

claims.text: LMPQ rooms 3, 4 and 9 hold Master Chronos and Dark Jr. Yetis, which any class can handle.
claims.say: rooms 3, 4 and 9 are chronos and dark yetis, anyone works

claims.text: LMPQ rooms 5 and 8 hold Zeta Grays and Ultra Grays; give them to someone who can hit flying monsters easily.
claims.say: give rooms 5 and 8 to someone good at flying mobs

claims.text: LMPQ rooms 6 and 7 hold Tauromacis and Flyeyes, so the party's strongest attacker should take them.
claims.say: rooms 6 and 7 are tauros and flyeyes, strongest hitter takes them

claims.text: Every LMPQ room except the exit room 16 has three portals; from room 6, for example, the left one goes to room 10, the middle to 13 and the right to 3.
claims.say: lmpq rooms have 3 portals, room 6 goes to 10, 13 or 3

claims.text: Max out Three Snails first; after Nimble Feet it is the best skill a Beginner gets. Stock up on snail shells before relying on it.
claims.say: max three snails and keep shells in your bag

claims.text: Nimble Feet is the most useful Beginner skill: a short speed boost with a short cooldown that helps even when leveling. Max it.
claims.say: nimble feet is the best beginner skill, max it

claims.text: Do not spend points on Recovery: the HP it gives is tiny and the cooldown is long, so it is only worth it for the animation.
claims.say: skip recovery, tiny heal and long cooldown

claims.text: The strongest Beginner build is pure STR, but low accuracy makes leveling and hitting mobs hard, so scroll armour with DEX or carry accuracy items.
claims.say: pure str beginner hits hard but misses, scroll your armor with dex

claims.text: A common Beginner compromise is keeping base DEX at 50, 60, 70 or 80 for accuracy depending on budget, putting the rest into STR and scrolling gear for STR or DEX as needed.
claims.say: keep base dex at 50 to 80 for accuracy, rest in str

claims.text: HP Beginners usually split AP as 2 STR, 2 HP, 1 DEX; full HP Beginners put everything into HP just to survive for a Zakum Helmet, but they cannot fight and depend on being leeched.
claims.say: hp beginner is weak, mostly done just to get a zakum helmet

claims.text: Frozen Tuna needs level 20 and 80 STR and is a Beginner's strongest weapon until level 36. It is slow, but the damage makes up for it.
claims.say: frozen tuna at 20 with 80 str is your best weapon till maroon mop

claims.text: Maroon Mop needs level 36 and 130 STR. It is the best Beginner weapon, so use it unless you can kill mobs in one or two hits with something faster. It is slow, but the damage makes up for it.
claims.say: maroon mop at 36 with 130 str is the beginner weapon to use

claims.text: One-handed Maple swords have no stat requirement, are fast, and give around 30 accuracy, which helps a STR Beginner who misses often, as long as they can one or two hit what they fight.
claims.say: 1h maple swords give accuracy, good if you one or two shot mobs

claims.text: Scrolled overall robes (level 20 and 30 versions) can be worn by any class including Beginners and have many slots, so look for one scrolled with STR or DEX.
claims.say: get a str or dex scrolled robe, anyone can wear it

claims.text: A Zakum Helmet is great for a Beginner but needs a Zakum run where you stand in the room while others fight him. Players disagree on whether low Beginner HP makes this hard or whether it is easy even without extra HP AP.
claims.say: zhelm is nice but beginner hp can make the zakum run hard

claims.text: Pain Reliever, sold in Omega Sector, gives a long-lasting weapon defence boost. It helps low-HP Beginners take less damage and use fewer potions. It is a hassle to reach down the Ludibrium tower, but worth it.
claims.say: pain reliever from omega sector cuts damage, lasts a long time

claims.text: Warrior Elixir from New Leaf City is a cheap weapon attack boost that is worth using constantly while leveling.
claims.say: warrior elixir from nlc is cheap attack, drink it while leveling

claims.text: Sniper Pill from Ludibrium gives a short accuracy boost; carry some if you have trouble hitting mobs.
claims.say: sniper pill from ludi boosts accuracy if youre missing

claims.text: From level 1 to 11, do all the quests on Maple Island.
claims.say: 1 to 11 just do the maple island quests

claims.text: For a Beginner from level 21 to 35, run Kerning City Party Quest or train in the Ant Tunnel.
claims.say: 21-35 do kpq or ant tunnel

claims.text: In that puzzle, a result of 2 different means one spot already has the right weight, while 3 different means every spot is wrong.
claims.say: 2 different = one spot is right, 3 different = all wrong

claims.text: The author starts with all five players on the first spot (5-0-0); if every spot comes back different, the next try is 0-4-1 rather than 3-1-1, ruling out each option before moving on.
claims.say: start with all 5 on one spot, if all wrong try 0-4-1 next

claims.text: Elemental weapons of the wrong element cut damage: fire or poison wands lower an Ice/Lightning mage's ice and lightning spells, and ice or lightning wands do the same to a Fire/Poison mage.
claims.say: dont use a fire or poison wand on an il mage, it lowers damage

claims.text: Bishops get no bonus or penalty from elemental wands and staves, because holy and non-elemental attacks ignore the weapon's element.
claims.say: bishops get nothing from elemental wands, holy isnt affected

claims.text: Element Amplification applies with any weapon, elemental or not, so it does not change which wand is better.
claims.say: element amplification works with any wand

claims.text: As an Archer, max Double Shot first, then Critical Shot, then The Eye of Amazon, and put everything left into The Blessing of Amazon. Double Shot gives more damage and consistency while leveling than an early maxed Critical Shot.
claims.say: archer sp: double shot, crit shot, eye of amazon, rest in blessing

claims.text: Skip Arrow Blow as an Archer. It is less consistent than Double Shot and, with Critical Shot, deals less overall damage; the extra knockback is not worth the mana cost, and Double Shot stays your main single-target attack until level 70.
claims.say: skip arrow blow, double shot is better for single targets

claims.text: Skip Focus at Archer level; its low-level bonus is too small to be worth rebuffing every few minutes. Accuracy and avoidability potions from New Leaf City or Ludibrium are stronger and last longer.
claims.say: skip focus early, accuracy and avoid potions are way better

claims.text: Crossbowman SP order: 1 Iron Arrow at 30, Crossbow Mastery 19, Booster 11, then max Iron Arrow and Power Knock-Back, finish Booster, then Focus, The Blessing of Amazon, last Crossbow Mastery, rest in Soul Arrow.
claims.say: xbowman sp: iron arrow 1, mastery 19, booster 11, max iron arrow

claims.text: Take Crossbow Mastery early: it raises your minimum damage and makes hits consistent, which helps timing and movement and gives more exp than any other second job skill.
claims.say: get crossbow mastery early, steadier damage = more exp

claims.text: Power Knock-Back is useful when you get cornered, and for pulling stacked monsters to one spot when Iron Arrow luring does not work because the group is too crowded.
claims.say: power knockback helps when cornered or to lure crowded mobs

claims.text: Do not take Final Attack: Crossbow if you mob with Iron Arrow; it lowers your overall damage. Its only plus is that it does not interfere with third job skills.
claims.say: skip final attack, it lowers your dps when mobbing with iron arrow

claims.text: Soul Arrow: Crossbow is a last-priority skill; put only a few points in it and rely on carrying plenty of arrows, so you never run out, just as you should never run out of potions.
claims.say: dont bother with soul arrow, just stock plenty of arrows

claims.text: Sniper SP order: max Arrow Eruption first (with 1 point in Strafe before 80), then max Strafe, max Puppet, Thrust 10, Golden Eagle 15, Blizzard 21, then max Mortal Blow; spend leftovers as you like.
claims.say: sniper sp: max arrow eruption, then strafe, puppet, thrust 10

claims.text: Stop Golden Eagle at 15: that is the requirement to get Frostprey, which replaces it entirely, so extra points are wasted.
claims.say: golden eagle only to 15, thats the req for frostprey

claims.text: Max Puppet: it is very useful for hunting area bosses, and later for soloing real bosses, which is how you find better crossbows.
claims.say: max puppet for area bosses, they drop better crossbows

claims.text: Mortal Blow is worth maxing as a Sniper because it can finish off a monster that has gotten too close, saving the time of knocking it back and repositioning.
claims.say: mortal blow is handy for mobs that got too close

claims.text: Grinding gets much easier at level 72 when you get Arrow Eruption: before that, second-job crossbowman is a slog best done with a party member, and after it you can hold the key down and let monsters line up.
claims.say: get arrow eruption at 72 and training gets way easier

claims.text: Bowmen and crossbowmen need near-max speed, since Iron Arrow and Double Shot do not work point-blank and positioning decides exp. Scroll your shoes and pet equipment for speed and raise Thrust once you have it.
claims.say: bowmen need max speed to position, scroll shoes for speed

claims.text: Get a pet and equip it with an auto HP pouch, then meso magnet and item pouch; the pet drinks potions and loots for you so you can just attack. Some actions interrupt auto HP, so keep watching your HP bar.
claims.say: get a pet with auto hp, it pots and loots while u grind

claims.text: At 51 to 57 the best spot for crossbowmen is Coolie Zombies at Forest of Dead Trees IV: good spawn, very slow movement, and they attack from range so they do not crowd you.
claims.say: 51-57 coolie zombies at forest of dead trees iv are the best

claims.text: At Forest of Dead Trees IV, train with a partner: you take the lower-left side and they take the top-right platform and the right side. This smooths the spawn and leaves you more flat ground for Iron Arrow.
claims.say: split dead trees iv with a partner, one low left one top right

claims.text: Voodoos are another strong 51-57 spot; once you do more damage the exp matches Coolie Zombies. They drop Heartstoppers, which are worth keeping for later.
claims.say: voodoos are a good 51-57 alt, they drop heartstoppers

claims.text: Forest of Golem only works for crossbowmen with a melee partner holding the top two lanes; exp then rivals Coolie Zombies, and the golems can drop Scroll for Gloves for ATT 60%. It stays awkward until about 60.
claims.say: forest of golem needs a melee partner on the top lanes

claims.text: Typhons hit softly and give very good exp for their HP; players report training there from level 76 with Arrow Eruption beats solo Wolf Spiders, but the map is hard to reach.
claims.say: typhons hit weak and give good exp even from 76 with arrow eruption

claims.text: At level 105 and up, Typhons gave less exp than solo Dreamy Ghosts or party Squids, and a slip on the way sends you back into a jump quest, so they are not recommended that late.
claims.say: typhons at 105+ are slower than himes or squids, skip them

claims.text: From 85 to 120, Gobies at Deep Sea Gorge II are the best solo exp. Against three or more monsters, such as a cluster of fish houses with Bone Fish around, Arrow Eruption does more damage than Strafe.
claims.say: 85-120 solo gobies at deep sea gorge ii give huge exp

claims.text: Fish houses at the Gobies map cast a weapon cancel buff; move to another house the moment it goes off. Strafing them from far away stops them casting it, and by about level 100 you break them before they can.
claims.say: when a fish house casts weapon cancel just move to the next house

claims.text: Squids and Risell Squids at Dangerous Sea Gorge II are great exp too, especially with a partner. Gobies give a little more exp, but Risell Squids drop Scroll for Gloves for ATT 60%, so swap between them.
claims.say: risell squids at dangerous sea gorge ii drop glove att scrolls

claims.text: Dreamy Ghosts at Encounter With The Buddha are probably the best exp of all the 85-120 spots, but also the deadliest: have at least around 3.5k HP so you survive two magic hits. When Black Crow spawns, the map is nearly unusable.
claims.say: dreamy ghosts at encounter with the buddha are best exp but need hp

claims.text: Beginners lose no exp when they die.
claims.say: beginners don't lose exp when they die

claims.text: Around level 35-36 the Maroon Mop gives a Beginner a huge damage jump, keeping them among the stronger characters until other jobs catch up in the late 60s; before it, Beginners hit weakly.
claims.say: get the maroon mop at 35, huge damage jump

claims.text: Islanders, Beginners who never leave Maple Island, can grind alone on Orange Mushrooms.
claims.say: islanders grind orange mushrooms solo

claims.text: Islanders gear up with the weapons and equipment that drop from Maple Island monsters.
claims.say: islanders wear whatever drops on the island

claims.text: On Maple Island, breaking boxes gives free potions that can be sold for mesos.
claims.say: break boxes on maple island for free pots

claims.text: The Stolen Fence shield is a worthwhile piece for an Islander to wear.
claims.say: islanders can rock the stolen fence shield

claims.text: Nimble Feet briefly raises a Beginner's movement speed.
claims.say: nimble feet makes you run faster for a bit

claims.text: Recovery boosts HP regeneration enough to save a lot of potions.
claims.say: recovery saves you a lot of pots

claims.text: The author's Beginner build puts everything into STR, claiming DEX and LUK aren't needed to hit monsters.
claims.say: beginner: all str, no dex or luk needed

claims.text: Beginners are fragile and can die from a single touch of a higher-level monster.
claims.say: beginners die in one hit to higher mobs, careful

claims.text: Getting to Windraiders takes a while, so once you have made the trip, use a Teleport Rock to get back there later.
claims.say: windraiders are far, use a teleport rock to come back

claims.text: Black Crow is a boss that can appear in Encounter with the Buddha, a map packed with hard-hitting Dreamy Ghosts.
claims.say: black crow can spawn in encounter with the buddha

claims.text: Black Crow takes a very long time to bring down alone and its loot is poor, with only small odds of mesos or equips, so hunting it is not worth the effort.
claims.say: black crow takes forever and drops junk, not worth it

claims.text: When merching, only buy items you can resell or scroll for a large profit; small margins on scrolls are not worth tying up your mesos.
claims.say: only buy stuff you can flip or scroll for a big margin

claims.text: Buying an already finished, fully scrolled item to resell rarely pays; most merchant profit comes from items you scroll or upgrade yourself.
claims.say: buying finished gear to resell rarely pays off

claims.text: Check Free Market shop prices often and sell near the going average; pricing above it means the item sells slowly or not at all.
claims.say: price at the market average or it wont sell

claims.text: Scarce items climb in price and plentiful ones drop, so hold on to an unusually scarce scroll and sell it when demand peaks.
claims.say: hold scarce scrolls and sell when demand is high

claims.text: Scroll success is pure chance; dummy scrolling and similar tricks do not change the odds.
claims.say: scrolling is pure luck, dummy scrolling does nothing

claims.text: Treat an item as dead and stop spending scrolls on it when the first slot fails, three slots fail in a row, you used the wrong scroll, or fewer than half the scrolls pass.
claims.say: first slot failed or 3 fails in a row? item's dead, stop

claims.text: Buying a market item that already passed a few good scrolls can cost less than chasing the same result by scrolling your own after bad luck.
claims.say: sometimes buying a decent scrolled item beats self scrolling

claims.text: For starting funds, farm Leprechauns at Creeping Evil: stand between the two spawns and kill them in turn for equipment drops and Lucky Charms to sell.
claims.say: stand between the two leprechauns in creeping evil and farm

claims.text: Some players hunt Platoon Chronos or Mixed Golems for Scroll for Gloves for ATT 60%, but the author finds that much slower and less reliable than farming Leprechauns.
claims.say: chronos and mixed golems drop gfa 60 but leprechauns are faster

claims.text: Protect your trading money: only buy gear for your own use when your savings are several times its price; the author uses five times and treats three times as the minimum.
claims.say: keep a reserve, only buy gear if you have 3-5x its price

claims.text: Black Versal Materia is a crafting material used to make Facestompers and Stormcaster Gloves.
claims.say: black versal materia is for facestompers and stormcaster gloves

claims.text: To let your pet drink potions for you, equip the auto HP or MP potion pouch on the pet and put the potion you want into the pet's potion slot.
claims.say: equip the hp/mp pouch on your pet and put pots in its slot

claims.text: The pet drinks a potion when your HP or MP drops below the alert percentage chosen in System Options, so change that setting to control when it triggers.
claims.say: set your hp/mp alert % in system options for pet pots

claims.text: If the pet's auto potion does nothing, relog or put the pet away and summon it again.
claims.say: pet not potting? resummon your pet or relog

claims.text: The pet's assigned potion is cleared when the game client is closed, but it survives a logout as long as the client stays open.
claims.say: closing the client clears your pet pot setting

claims.text: The Haunted House questline opens at level 15: talk to Old Man Tom outside the mansion for A Word to the Wise, then accept A Lost Girl. The monsters you must hunt are far stronger than a level 15 character.
claims.say: haunted house quests start at lv15 with old man tom

claims.text: Malady stands in New Leaf City, Amherst, Kerning City, Orbis, Ludibrium, Leafre, El Nath and Omega Sector; with the Omni Key you talk to her to get into the mansion vault.
claims.say: malady is in most big towns, talk to her with the omni key

claims.text: Sophilia is in her bedroom, reached from the left side of the Foyer's 2nd floor and then upstairs to the right. She wants her first doll, which you earn from Family Jewels.
claims.say: sophilia wants her first doll, get it from family jewels

claims.text: The Omni Key is not used up when you enter the vault, but its quest cannot be repeated on the same character.
claims.say: the omni key is permanent, the quest is one time only

claims.text: Ludmilla's Family Jewels asks for Tarrymore Earrings and Sepha Earrings; only the flying Sophilia Dolls drop them. The reward is Sophilia's First Doll for A Lost Girl.
claims.say: only the flying sophilia dolls drop the earrings

claims.text: Jonas Prendergast in the Toy Workshop (from the Hallway go top left into the Library, then the topmost door) gives The Infernal Toy Machine: 50 Firewood, 25 screws and 25 loaded springs.
claims.say: jonas wants 50 firewood, 25 screws and 25 loaded springs

claims.text: Bring the old doll Sophilia hands you back to Jonas, then take A Father's Love: kill 50 each of Psycho Jack, Nightmare and Sophilia Doll. The three hunts reward the Toymaker Cap, Cape and Hammer.
claims.say: kill 50 psycho jacks, nightmares and dolls for toymaker gear

claims.text: Bandit AP: LUK is the main stat. Base DEX is twice your level until level 40, then level plus 40, topping out near 150, which covers both the Dragon Khanjar and the level 110 weapon.
claims.say: dex = 2x lvl till 40 then lvl+40, rest into luk

claims.text: Do not add STR before about level 100; then put around 50 to 60 base STR in between levels 100 and 110 (with a Zakum Helmet) so the Dragon Khanjar can be worn.
claims.say: dont put ap in str till around lvl 100

claims.text: A STR-less Bandit (4 base STR) is stronger early on but falls behind once a scrolled Dragon Khanjar comes in, so add STR around 100 to 110; only stay STR-less if you already own a great Maple Shield.
claims.say: strless bandit is good early but add str for khanjar

claims.text: A full-LUK Bandit with no DEX or STR beyond requirements is noticeably weaker than the normal build; only worth it if you already have a DEX-less setup for cheap gear.
claims.say: full luk bandit is weaker, only if gear lets you

claims.text: A LUK-less Bandit relies on DEX and STR plus weapon attack from gear; its damage is very stable but lower than a normal Bandit, training is painful before level 70, and it needs heavy funding.
claims.say: luk-less bandit is stable dmg but weak and pricey

claims.text: A Blood Bandit gets 25 DEX for the advance then puts every AP into HP, since Meso Explosion damage ignores stats. It tanks anything but is useless without Meso Explosion, so it suits bossing mules.
claims.say: blood bandit: all ap into hp, only good for meso explosion

claims.text: Bandit first job: max Double Stab first, then Nimble Body for accuracy and avoid, then three points in Disorder to reach Dark Sight and the rest into Dark Sight. Skip Keen Eyes and Lucky Seven as you use no stars.
claims.say: double stab first, then nimble body, then dark sight

claims.text: A Sindit uses throwing stars with Lucky Seven and Keen Eyes until around level 40 and is stronger than a normal Bandit then; only worth it if you can afford a few sets of Ilbi Throwing-Stars.
claims.say: sindit is stronger early but needs ilbi stars
