claims.text: Bandit second job: one point in Dagger Mastery for a big damage jump, then max Savage Blow right away. Bandits have no area skill in this job, so training is rough but Savage Blow is fast.
claims.say: 1 dagger mastery then max savage blow

claims.text: After Savage Blow, raise Dagger Mastery to 5 to unlock Dagger Booster and max it, then finish Dagger Mastery, and max Haste after that.
claims.say: savage blow, then booster, then mastery, then haste

claims.text: Once the key second-job skills are maxed, finish Dark Sight (no speed loss when maxed) and dump the rest of the SP into Steal, which has little value.
claims.say: spare sp: finish dark sight then steal

claims.text: On third job, max Meso Explosion first because it is your core bossing skill, then put points into Meso Guard (one early point at level 72 is fine).
claims.say: 3rd job: max meso explosion first, then meso guard

claims.text: After Meso Explosion and Meso Guard, max Band of Thieves, your first area skill, then Assaulter. Band of Thieves hits mobs in front and behind with a very short delay between uses.
claims.say: band of thieves is your first aoe, max it after meso guard

claims.text: Assaulter is mostly for getting across the map faster through monsters; its damage and stun become irrelevant after fourth job.
claims.say: assaulter is just for travel, dmg gets outclassed at 4th job

claims.text: Spare third-job SP goes to Chakra (quick healing while bossing) and Pickpocket (small extra mesos and drops when hunting items on weak mobs, though its tiny mesos make weak Meso Explosions).
claims.say: leftover sp: chakra for healing, pickpocket for mesos

claims.text: Leave Shield Mastery empty as a Chief Bandit: a Dragon Khanjar has very little weapon defense, so the skill adds almost nothing.
claims.say: skip shield mastery as a chief bandit, tiny bonus

claims.text: Meso Explosion only detonates your own mesos: drops from monsters you killed, Pickpocket drops and mesos you dropped yourself. At full mastery its damage ignores LUK, DEX and STR.
claims.say: meso explosion only blows up your own mesos, stats dont matter

claims.text: Uninterrupted bombing makes Shadowers very strong at major bosses such as Zakum, Papulatus, Pianus and Horntail, which also makes them wanted bossing partners.
claims.say: shadowers are great boss partners with meso explosion

claims.text: Bombing a boss with Meso Explosion for a long time can make it stop moving and stop its magic attacks; it mostly shows up at Zakum, Papulatus, Pianus and Bigfoot.
claims.say: long meso explosion bombing can freeze bosses sometimes

claims.text: Dropped mesos disappear after about five minutes, so faster bombing lets you detonate more of a single drop phase before they vanish.
claims.say: mesos on the ground vanish after 5 min, bomb fast

claims.text: Thief fourth job at level 120: get the recommendation from your third job instructor in El Nath, then talk to Hellin in Leafre, who wants a Heroic Pentagon and a Heroic Star.
claims.say: 4th job: el nath letter, then hellin in leafre wants pentagon+star

claims.text: Meso Explosion damage does not scale with stats, so Bandits can boss early but other classes eventually out-damage them as their gear improves.
claims.say: bandits boss early but get outscaled later

claims.text: Bandits level very easily from 70 to 130, but the class is expensive, and training becomes slow and costly at very high levels.
claims.say: bandits level fast 70-130 but get pricey later

claims.text: HP washing means putting AP into HP, then using an AP Reset to pull a point back out of MP and re-spend it on your main stat. You end with more max HP and less max MP, and your damage stats are unchanged.
claims.say: hp washing swaps mp for hp with ap resets, your damage stays same

claims.text: You can park a single AP in HP and then just repeat AP Resets, each one moving a point from MP into HP, until you reach your minimum MP. The limit is the number of resets you own and the MP you have above the floor.
claims.say: park 1 ap in hp then reset mp into hp until you hit min mp

claims.text: Every class and level has a minimum MP you cannot wash below. If a reset cannot pull MP out, you have hit that floor and are temporarily weaker until more levels give you spare MP.
claims.say: you can only wash mp down to your min mp for your level

claims.text: Every 10 INT you are wearing when you level up gives 1 extra MP gained, which is spare MP you can wash. Put the INT gear on just before the level-up, ideally from the very first levels, to wash more.
claims.say: every 10 int you wear when you level gives +1 mp to wash with

claims.text: INT added by Maple Warrior, even one cast by another player, counts toward the bonus MP you get on level-up.
claims.say: maple warrior int counts toward the mp bonus on level up

claims.text: Warrior-type classes benefit most from HP washing: a wash gives them about 50 HP for only about 4 MP, by far the best trade of any class, so it is nearly essential for high-level bossing.
claims.say: warriors get like 50 hp per wash for 4 mp, best trade of any class

claims.text: Magicians get a poor deal from washing: each point costs them around 90 MP and returns only about 6 to 10 HP when the point comes from a level-up AP.
claims.say: mages lose lots of mp per wash for very little hp, poor value

claims.text: A wash gives thieves about 20 to 24 HP and bowmen about 16 to 20 HP, and each wash costs them around 12 MP.
claims.say: thief wash is about 20 hp for 12 mp, bowman about 16-20 hp

claims.text: Pirates get about 16 to 20 HP per wash for around 16 MP, and Brawlers get roughly double that HP because of their Improve MaxHP skill.
claims.say: brawlers get about double hp per wash compared to other pirates

claims.text: Thieves get about 4 less HP when a point goes into HP through an AP Reset than when it comes straight from a level-up, so a thief should wash level-up AP on the spot instead of cycling resets.
claims.say: thieves should put levelup ap into hp, cycling resets gets less hp

claims.text: Magicians and pirates (Brawlers especially) get more HP per point when it is added through an AP Reset than from level-up AP, so the park-one-AP cycle method suits them best.
claims.say: mages and pirates get more hp per point from the reset cycle method

claims.text: Wait until after second job advancement before washing, since advancing hands out free HP and MP that make each wash more efficient. Wearing INT gear earlier is still worthwhile.
claims.say: start washing after 2nd job, advancement gives free hp and mp

claims.text: You do not have to wash every level. You can save it for one session at a high level when you need HP for bossing, using the park-one-AP reset cycle to do it all at once.
claims.say: you can wash everything at once later when you need hp for bosses

claims.text: Do not try to AP-reset while Hyper Body is active; it does not work.
claims.say: dont reset ap with hyper body on, it wont work

claims.text: Max HP and max MP are capped at 30,000 for every job.
claims.say: max hp and mp cap at 30000 for every job

claims.text: Washing extra HP lets you survive one or two hits from heavy-hitting bosses such as Zakum, Horntail, Papulatus and Pink Bean, and it makes tough training spots safer too.
claims.say: wash hp before bossing, zakum and horntail hit really hard

claims.text: Dark Knights with a huge washed HP pool still get Berserk, because it triggers below a percentage of max HP and even that percentage of a large pool is enough to survive a hit.
claims.say: dks can still use berserk with washed hp, its a percent threshold

claims.text: Blood washing means putting AP into HP and never taking it back out, which permanently lowers your damage stats. Normal washing returns the point to your main stat, so damage is unaffected.
claims.say: blood washing keeps ap in hp and hurts dmg, normal wash doesnt

claims.text: Dark Knights are supportive and wanted in parties for Hyper Body, and their spammable big-range attack makes them strong farmers; late game they gain much from controlling HP for Berserk.
claims.say: dark knights are wanted in parties for hyper body

claims.text: Dark Knight downsides: no Power Guard so less damage reduction, lower base HP than Hero or Paladin, and it needs careful HP control to use Berserk.
claims.say: dk has no power guard and needs hp control for berserk

claims.text: Hero is the well-rounded warrior: very stable damage on single and multiple targets with Brandish's good range, but one attack does everything and there is no true area skill for mobbing.
claims.say: hero is the all-rounder, brandish range is great

claims.text: Paladins add Ice, Fire, Lightning or Holy to their attacks, which is great on bosses with weaknesses and costly otherwise; they knock back almost every boss, have short range and few party skills, so they train mostly solo.
claims.say: pally charges depend on the monsters weakness

claims.text: Sword Heroes are recommended over axe Heroes: swords have steadier minimum damage and the best end weapons like Stonetooth are faster than axes; axes have higher base attack but are unstable and rarer.
claims.say: swords over axes for heroes, steadier and faster

claims.text: A hybrid Spear and Pole Arm build loses nothing since both share the same max-damage multiplier for their own attack; start third job with the polearm since it is easier, and use mostly spears at endgame.
claims.say: dk hybrid spear + polearm works, polearm easier early

claims.text: A Paladin cannot really go hybrid since each elemental charge works with a particular weapon type, so decide between sword and blunt weapon before advancing.
claims.say: pick sword or blunt before you go pally

claims.text: Paladin swords are mostly faster, more stable and easier to find but pricier; blunt weapons hit harder at base and are cheap but slower and less stable. Either sword or blunt works.
claims.say: pally swords are steadier, blunt weapons are cheap but slower

claims.text: Warriors should aim for total accuracy of about 145 to 160 by roughly level 150 rather than chasing a set DEX number; DEX gives accuracy at a better rate than LUK, so that is where AP goes after gear.
claims.say: aim for around 145-160 acc by 150, not a dex number

claims.text: Accuracy comes from a Zakum Helmet, a maxed weapon mastery and a Horntail Necklace; then scroll DEX onto pants, overall, earring, shoes, glasses or cape before adding DEX as AP.
claims.say: zakum helm and horntail necklace give tons of acc

claims.text: A safe warrior start is DEX equal to twice your level up to level 30 (60 DEX), then adjust to taste.
claims.say: warrior dex 2x level till 30 then adjust

claims.text: Avoid going past 80 base DEX as a warrior; it costs a lot of damage for little benefit.
claims.say: dont go over 80 base dex as a warrior

claims.text: A DEXless warrior (4 DEX all game) is only for someone who already has scrolled gear and funding; a new player should start with some DEX and use AP resets later to remove it.
claims.say: dexless only if your gear already covers accuracy

claims.text: HP washing: put an AP into HP, use an AP Reset to take a point out of MP and put it into a stat, then repeat. Warriors can reach about 20k HP without adding any INT.
claims.say: hp wash = ap into hp, reset out of mp, repeat

claims.text: There is a minimum base MP you cannot wash below: for Spearmen it is 4 times level plus 156, and for Fighters and Pages it is 4 times level plus 56.
claims.say: base mp floor for washing: 4x lvl + 56 (spearman +156)

claims.text: HP washing is not essential for warriors but makes bossing more comfortable and makes Berserk much easier for Dark Knights.
claims.say: hp washing isnt required but makes bossing way easier

claims.text: Swordsman SP: a few points in Improving HP Recovery, then max Improving Max HP Increase, Slash Blast, and Power Strike; favor Slash Blast over Power Strike because mobbing levels you faster.
claims.say: max hp increase, slash blast, then power strike

claims.text: For a hybrid Spearman, pick the first weapon, max its Mastery and Booster early, take three points in Iron Will, then do the second weapon's Mastery and Booster after Hyper Body.
claims.say: spearman: first weapon mastery+booster, then hyper body, then 2nd

claims.text: Max Hyper Body right after the first weapon's early mastery and booster at levels 40 to 49; it helps you and makes you wanted in parties.
claims.say: max hyper body early, parties love it

claims.text: Dragon Knight third job: max your attack skill (start with the polearm one), then Dragon Roar, Elemental Resistance, then Sacrifice; Power Crash does not need to be maxed.
claims.say: dk 3rd job: attack skill, dragon roar, elem resistance, sacrifice

claims.text: Do not use Dragon Blood while bossing: it drains your HP, which can be deadly when a boss drops you to 1 HP, and it overrides attack potions or apples.
claims.say: dont use dragon blood while bossing, it drains hp

claims.text: Dark Knight fourth job gets no new attack, so order skills as Power Stance, Beholder, Berserk, Maple Warrior, then Achilles; Berserk and Beholder add stability and damage for early bossing.
claims.say: dk 4th job: stance, beholder, berserk, maple warrior, achilles

claims.text: Standard Fighter build: Mastery and Booster early, Power Guard as a lifesaver, and Rage too; fill the rest with anything except Final Attack.
claims.say: fighter: mastery, booster, power guard, rage, no final attack

claims.text: Crusader: max Combo Attack first as it hugely raises damage per minute; Coma is optional for mobbing, and Panic is skipped in both training and bossing since it resets your orbs.
claims.say: crusader: combo attack first, panic isnt used

claims.text: Hero fourth job: one point in Rush, max Brandish, then Advanced Combo, Power Stance, Maple Warrior, Achilles, Guardian, finish Rush and take Hero's Will for Horntail; Brandish's fixed range suits a one-handed weapon.
claims.say: hero 4th: brandish, adv combo, stance, mw, achilles, guardian

claims.text: Page second job needs only weapon Mastery, Booster and Power Guard plus three points in Threaten; the leftover SP can max the other weapon's Mastery and Booster, skipping Final Attack.
claims.say: page: mastery, booster, power guard, 3 threaten

claims.text: The boat between Ellinia and Orbis has a crate you can break open for the second Maple History book, and a Crimson Balrog can show up during the ride.
claims.say: orbis boat has a crate for the history book and a crimson balrog

claims.text: An Owl of Minerva searches every shop in the Free Market channel, including your own, so check your own shop for the item first or the search is wasted.
claims.say: check your own shop before using an owl, it searches yours too

claims.text: In New Leaf City the Glimmer Man forges iTCG gear such as Facestompers and Crystal Leaf Earrings if you bring the matching Forging Manual (found in NLC Gachapon) and the other required materials.
claims.say: glimmer man in nlc forges facestompers if you have the manual

claims.text: Mysterious Path 3 in Singapore is a solid solo map for a Dragon Knight at 60-80; it's big for one player, but fast kills let you clear it alone.
claims.say: mysterious path 3 is a good solo map at 60-80

claims.text: Wolf Spider Cavern gives good exp, drops and mesos from the 80s; follow the teleports and clear the top monsters, then sweep the bottom once it fills up.
claims.say: wolf spider cavern is good exp and mesos in your 80s

claims.text: Monsters in Wolf Spider Cavern hit hard, so try it in your 80s alongside a Priest or Bishop.
claims.say: go wolf spider cavern with a priest, the spiders hit hard

claims.text: Lower Ascent on Crimsonwood Mountain is a good map at 85-90 with easy kills, good exp, mesos and drops; use the teleports to clear both top and bottom quickly.
claims.say: lower ascent on crimsonwood is nice at 85-90

claims.text: You can train on Dreamy Ghosts alone, but a Priest or Bishop partner using Heal and Holy Symbol makes leveling much faster and keeps you alive.
claims.say: party a priest at dreamy ghosts for heal and holy symbol

claims.text: Power Elixirs are too expensive to burn while training; save them for bosses.
claims.say: save power elixirs for bosses, too pricey for training

claims.text: Ginger Ale from the New Leaf City shop heals well without costing as much as Power Elixirs, making it a good training potion.
claims.say: ginger ale from nlc is a good cheap training pot

claims.text: Warriors move slowly, so Speed Pills bought in Ludibrium help them get around training maps.
claims.say: warriors are slow, grab speed pills in ludi

claims.text: New Leaf City sells a Thief Elixir that helps when you keep missing and a Warrior Elixir that adds weapon attack for more damage.
claims.say: nlc thief elixir helps misses, warrior elixir adds attack

claims.text: Crimsonwood Keep badges can be exchanged 50 of one kind (or 25 of each kind) for a random reward, and the exchange can only be done once every 24 hours.
claims.say: you can turn in 50 cwk badges of one kind once a day for a prize

claims.text: The Windraider Badge exchange can also hand out 60% attack scrolls for claws, bows and knuckles.
claims.say: windraider badges can also give 60% claw, bow or knuckle scrolls

claims.text: Stormbreaker Badges can also give 60% attack scrolls for one-handed swords, one-handed blunt weapons, pole arms and spears.
claims.say: stormbreaker badges give 60% 1h sword/bw, polearm, spear scrolls

claims.text: 50 Firebrand Badges can give Raven Ninja Bandana, Kage, Thorns, a stack of 8 Heartstoppers, Tao of Sight, Tao of Shadows, or 60% wand and staff magic attack scrolls.
claims.say: firebrand badges can give heartstoppers or wand/staff scrolls

claims.text: Tao of Sight, Tao of Harmony and Tao of Shadows from the badge exchange are materials for item synthesis rather than gear in themselves.
claims.say: the tao items from badges are synthesis materials

claims.text: Marksman is a solid ranged class: Piercing Arrow handles groups, Snipe handles single targets, and Sharp Eyes makes parties want you around.
claims.say: mm pierces groups, snipes bosses and brings sharp eyes

claims.text: Bowmasters are still preferred over Marksmen for bossing, but both bring Sharp Eyes and Night Lords in the party will want that damage boost, so a Marksman still gets invited.
claims.say: bm is the usual boss pick but mm still gets invited for sharp eyes

claims.text: Marksman freezing is a big strength compared with Bowmaster fire attacks, but freeze does not work on certain monsters, so have another plan for those.
claims.say: mm freeze is great but some mobs just ignore it

claims.text: A full-STR Marksman keeps STR equal to level up to 110, so any crossbow can be wielded without gear help.
claims.say: full str mm matches str to level until 110

claims.text: A low-STR Marksman keeps STR just high enough to wield the best crossbow and covers the gap with gear; a Zakum Helmet, Silver Deputy Star and an STR-scrolled cape can easily give around 40 STR.
claims.say: keep str as low as your crossbow allows and cover it with gear

claims.text: A STR-less Marksman keeps STR at 4; it is simple in theory but costs a lot in practice because gear has to supply all the strength.
claims.say: str-less means 4 str but the gear gets expensive fast

claims.text: Every point of STR you can move into DEX is boosted further by Maple Warrior, so keep STR as low as your weapon allows even if you cannot go fully STR-less.
claims.say: less str means more dex and maple warrior boosts dex too

claims.text: At low levels STR matters less: a well-scrolled level 64 Maple Nishada carries you into the 80s and 90s, and later you work toward an end-game crossbow.
claims.say: a well scrolled maple nishada carries a crossbow user to the 80s-90s

claims.text: First-job archer build: 3 points in The Blessing of Amazon to unlock The Eye of Amazon (more range), 8 in The Eye of Amazon, 1 in Arrow Blow to unlock Double Shot, then max Double Shot and Critical Shot.
claims.say: 1st job sp: blessing 3, eye 8, then max double shot and crit shot

claims.text: In second job take Crossbow Mastery and Crossbow Booster first, since mastery steadies damage and booster speeds shots; after that Iron Arrow, Soul Arrow: Crossbow and Power Knock-Back.
claims.say: xbow mastery and booster first, then iron arrow and soul arrow

claims.text: Do not put points into Final Attack: Crossbow; the author argues it lowers overall damage and roots you in place while it fires, which gets dangerous at higher levels. Put spare points into first-job skills.
claims.say: skip final attack on a crossbow user, spare sp goes to 1st job skills

claims.text: Whether to max Strafe or Arrow Eruption first is a training-style choice: Strafe is a great single-target skill, while Arrow Eruption mobs, firing around targets and through floors.
claims.say: strafe first for single target, arrow eruption first for crowds

claims.text: Keep Golden Eagle at level 15 only, because Frostprey needs 15 Golden Eagle; extra points there only add a stun, and the author prefers putting them into Thrust for the speed boost.
claims.say: golden eagle only needs 15 for frostprey, extra goes to thrust

claims.text: Unlike Bowmasters, who get Hurricane, a Marksman has no skill that replaces Strafe, so max it; Strafe plus Snipe is your single-target attack for the rest of the game.
claims.say: mm has no hurricane so max strafe, it stays your single target skill

claims.text: First fourth-job points: one each into Dragon's Breath, Frostprey, Piercing Arrow and Snipe, then add more as you pass skill books.
claims.say: 4th job: 1 point each in dragons breath, frostprey, pierce, snipe

claims.text: After the first points, raise Sharp Eyes and Marksman Boost first: they give the biggest damage boosts, more and harder crits, and very stable damage through mastery. Maple Warrior can wait since someone in the party usually has it.
claims.say: 4th job priority: sharp eyes and marksman boost before the rest

claims.text: Piercing Arrow is a stronger Iron Arrow: its damage rises as it passes through more monsters, so groups of mobs make it better, though the bonus does not stack forever.
claims.say: pierce gets stronger the more mobs it goes through

claims.text: Snipe is far more useful than Blind, so do not save points for Blind; a low-level Snipe is poor but still better than leaving the points unused.
claims.say: put points in snipe over blind, blind is barely worth it

claims.text: Frostprey adds passive damage and more freezing, while Dragon's Breath pushes mobs off you; with a Marksman's range it is usually easier to pierce groups and keep moving, so the author favors Frostprey.
claims.say: frostprey for passive damage and freeze, dragons breath just pushes mobs

claims.text: For an archer around levels 15 to 25 the author recommends training at Caution Falling Down.
claims.say: try caution falling down for archers around 15-25

claims.text: From about 25 to 30, train in the Ant Tunnel and do the 99-kill quests on Horny Mushrooms and Zombie Mushrooms.
claims.say: 25-30 ant tunnel plus the horny and zombie mushroom kill quests

claims.text: For Strafe-first characters at 70 to 90, Windraiders work well; the author prefers the maps above the Headless Horseman maps and just sits and snipes them with Strafe.
claims.say: windraiders at 70-90 with strafe, just sit and snipe them

claims.text: At 90 to 100, Typhons are an option with maxed Arrow Eruption: you get huge mob groups to gun down, but it burns a lot of potions and the map is awkward to reach.
claims.say: typhons at 90-100 need maxed arrow eruption and burn lots of pots

claims.text: For bowmen each HP wash costs 12 MP and gains 16 to 20 HP, and the minimum MP you can wash down to is 14 times your level plus 148.
claims.say: bowmen lose 12 mp and gain 16-20 hp per wash

claims.text: Bowmen do not need fresh level-up AP to HP wash: resetting MP into HP gives about the same gain; only thieves use a different formula that gives slightly more for fresh AP.
claims.say: bowmen can wash with any ap, only thieves need fresh level up ap

claims.text: For a Marksman's gear, attack is worth more than DEX, and DEX is worth more than STR unless you need the STR to wear your crossbow.
claims.say: attack over dex over str unless you need str for your xbow

claims.text: The author always tries to get a Zakum Helmet at level 50: its defense, STR and DEX save potions at low levels and let you wield a STR-hungry crossbow earlier. A helmet DEX 60% scroll drops from Master Chronos if you want to improve it.
claims.say: get a zakum helm at 50 if you can, master chronos drops dex scrolls

claims.text: A glove with 8 to 10 attack boosts a Marksman's damage more than a Zakum Helmet does, unless the helmet's STR lets you wield a better crossbow; farm Platoon Chronos for glove scrolls and do not chase more than 8 of 10 until late game.
claims.say: an 8-10 attack glove beats a zakum helm for damage

claims.text: Pendant progression for a Marksman: Spiegelmann's Necklace early, a Silver Deputy Star as a mid option, and a Horntail Necklace for end game; all can be earned by questing or bossing.
claims.say: pendants go spiegelmanns necklace, silver deputy star, then ht necklace

claims.text: A non-mage explorer has 61 SP for 1st job skills: 1 from the advancement plus 3 per level from 10 to 30.
claims.say: 1st job gets 61 sp, 1 at advancement plus levels 10 to 30

claims.text: Magicians have 67 SP for 1st job skills because they advance at level 8 and earn two extra levels of SP before 30.
claims.say: mages get 67 sp in 1st job since they advance at 8

claims.text: 2nd job skills get 121 SP: 1 for the advancement and 120 from levels 30 to 70.
claims.say: 2nd job gets 121 sp total

claims.text: 3rd job skills get 151 SP: 1 for the advancement and 150 from levels 70 to 120.
claims.say: 3rd job gets 151 sp total

claims.text: After the 1st, 2nd and 3rd job shares are spent, every remaining SP goes into 4th job skills.
claims.say: everything left after 3rd job goes into 4th job

claims.text: The game blocks SP in a higher job's skills until the previous job has its full share, so trying to add one there tells you whether the lower tier is complete.
claims.say: cant add 2nd job sp till 1st job is full, use that to check

claims.text: When redistributing SP after a reset, subtract each tier's total from your pool to know when to stop, e.g. 500 minus 61 leaves 439 for 2nd job onward.
claims.say: subtract 61, 121 and 151 to track where each job ends

claims.text: 4th job characters can skip old attacks they've outgrown and spend the SP elsewhere; a Night Lord with Triple Throw doesn't need Lucky Seven.
claims.say: night lords with triple throw can skip lucky seven

claims.text: Future Spearmen can rush levels 1 to 10 on Maple Island without trouble.
claims.say: just rush maple island till 10

claims.text: Between levels 20 and 30 a warrior can spend time in Kerning City Party Quest.
claims.say: 20 to 30 you can just do kpq

claims.text: Wild Boars can drop the Maple Impaler, a spear worth picking up at this stage.
claims.say: wild boars drop maple impalers for spear users

claims.text: From the mid-30s you can join Monster Carnival, though the author would rather keep training on Wild Boars until 40.
claims.say: cpq opens up mid 30s but boars are fine too

claims.text: Monster Carnival is generally seen as the fastest way through levels 40 to 50, if you can find people to run it with.
claims.say: cpq is the fastest way from 40 to 50 if you find a group

claims.text: From 45 to 50 the author found nothing that beats Monster Carnival for a Spearman.
claims.say: 45 to 50 just do cpq honestly

claims.text: For levels 50 to 60, train on Cellions, Lioners and Grupins at Stairway to the Sky I.
claims.say: 50-60 try cellions, lioners and grupins at stairway to the sky

claims.text: Cellions drop the Maple Soul Spear, a good weapon for spear users in this range.
claims.say: cellions drop the maple soul spear

claims.text: With the Map of Phantom Forest and Marker of Heroism you can take the fastest way up Crimsonwood Mountain, skipping both the Phantom Forest maze and the jump quest.
claims.say: marker of heroism lets you skip the maze and jq up crimsonwood

claims.text: Finishing The Fallen Woods at Dead Man's Gorge opens Mo's shop there, which sells attack-boosting Ciders, All Cure Potions and return scrolls to New Leaf City.
claims.say: do the fallen woods so mo at dead man's gorge sells you ciders

claims.text: The Fallen Woods is required before the Crimsonwood exchange quests unlock, but you don't need it to lead CWKPQ.
claims.say: fallen woods is needed for cwk exchange, not to lead cwkpq

claims.text: With The Fallen Woods done, completing The Right Path unlocks Crimsonwood exchange and crafting, which is how you craft the Balanced Fury claw.
claims.say: the right path unlocks cwk crafting like balanced fury

claims.text: Mounts help most on classes that lack movement skills, mainly warriors, brawlers and bowmen, because they add a lot of speed and jump.
claims.say: no haste or flash jump? a mount fixes your speed

claims.text: The Hog questline needs level 70 and 3rd job. It opens with the quest Monster Riding from Kenta at the Aquarium zoo.
claims.say: hog quest needs lv70 and 3rd job, start at kenta in aquarium

claims.text: With the items in hand, talk to Kenta at the top of the room to leave, then turn in Monster Riding to receive a Saddle and the Monster Rider skill.
claims.say: finish monster riding for the saddle and monster rider skill

claims.text: Bring the bottle back to Kenta to finish Pheromone Perfume; he hands you a Pheromone Perfume, the item that tames the wild hog.
claims.say: kenta turns the bottle into the perfume that tames the hog

claims.text: The wild hog roams The Area of Wild Hog, a hidden map reached through a secret portal in Tiger Ridge in Korean Folk Town.
claims.say: wild hog is in a hidden map off tiger ridge in korean folk town

claims.text: Stand right next to the wild hog and use the Pheromone Perfume; the Hog lands in your equip inventory. If you are too far away you only get a message that no hog is nearby, and nothing is lost.
claims.say: stand right by the hog before using the perfume

claims.text: To ride, double-click the Hog and the Saddle to equip them, then use the Monster Rider skill.
claims.say: equip hog and saddle, then cast monster rider

claims.text: Silver Mane needs level 120 and a Hog that is at least level 3; once both are met the quest Silver Mane shows up at Kenta.
claims.say: silver mane needs lv120 and a level 3 hog

claims.text: Mounts level up by riding them until they get tired and then restoring them with a Revitalizer; the mount gains exp based on how much tiredness was restored. Doofus in Henesys Market sells Revitalizers.
claims.say: ride till tired then feed a revitalizer to level your hog

claims.text: Take off your Hog before turning in Silver Mane, or Kenta will not complete the quest.
claims.say: unequip your hog before turning in silver mane

claims.text: Red Draco needs level 200 and a Silver Mane. Take Dragon Rider from your 4th job instructor, unequip the mane and complete it to get the Red Draco.
claims.say: red draco: lv200, get dragon rider from your 4th job instructor

claims.text: Mount speeds: the Hog gives 150% speed and 120% jump, Silver Mane 170% speed and 120% jump, and Red Draco 190% speed and 123% jump.
claims.say: hog 150% speed, silver mane 170%, red draco 190%

claims.text: Cash Shop mounts are only cosmetic skins. They do nothing alone and must be equipped on top of a real Hog, Silver Mane or Red Draco.
claims.say: cash shop mounts are just skins, you still need a real mount

claims.text: The usual advice is Cleric to Bishop and selling leech, but the author finds Priests crawl from about 75 to 120 because, as a support class, they end up depending on others for help.
claims.say: priest from 75 to 120 is slow, they rely on others

claims.text: Poison training eats potions, so early on most mesos go to pots; the author's starter choice is Ginseng Root, which heals a share of both HP and MP, bought from Miki in New Leaf City.
claims.say: poison training eats pots, ginseng roots from nlc work well

claims.text: Keeping a Priest of your own in the party to recast Holy Symbol on your training F/P speeds up leveling a great deal.
claims.say: bring a priest for holy symbol while your f/p trains

claims.text: Holy Symbol is one of the most wanted buffs for training and bossing; a Priest who brings it often gets invited to parties or even leeched for free.
claims.say: priests with holy symbol get party invites everywhere

claims.text: The author levels the Priest until Holy Symbol is maxed, around level 82, before parking it to start the next character.
claims.say: level your priest till holy symbol is maxed, about 82

claims.text: You earn exp from a party kill if your level is no lower than the monster's level minus 5, or if you are within 5 levels of the party member who made the kill.
claims.say: you get party exp if within 5 levels of the killer or the mob

claims.text: Party exp is split among eligible members on the map, so a two-person party with Holy Symbol gets the most per kill; a third buffer can leave the map after buffing so it takes no share.
claims.say: buff holy symbol then leave the map so the two attackers get more

claims.text: Rolling a stack of tickets at the Mushroom Shrine Gachapon almost always lands a scroll worth real money, and can give a Chaos Scroll, but the scrolls clog your inventory and need a shop to sell.
claims.say: shrine gach nearly always pays, but scrolls fill your bags

claims.text: Kerning City Gachapon is the high-risk option: you are gambling on a Pink Gaia Cape or a Dragon sleeve, which is worth a fortune if it rolls above-average attack.
claims.say: kerning gach is a gamble for a pgc or dragon sleeve

claims.text: Before spending on cosmetics, buy a pet that picks up loot so you can keep attacking instead of stopping to collect drops.
claims.say: get a looting pet before buying outfits

claims.text: Monster-dropped equipment whose name shows in plain white or grey is almost always worthless and can go to a shop; ask someone you trust when unsure.
claims.say: white or grey named drops are junk, just npc them

claims.text: Scrolling your own gear is cheaper in theory, but worthwhile items need risky 10% and 30% scrolls, so new players are better off buying finished gear carefully.
claims.say: dont scroll your own gear early, 10s and 30s are too risky

claims.text: Mage INT gear is overpriced because so many players follow the Bishop route; the author would rather buy INT equipment that doubles as HP washing gear.
claims.say: skip pricey mage gear, buy int wash gear instead

claims.text: HP washing gear means INT equipment with a low level requirement that classes other than mages can wear; the more INT a piece has, the pricier it gets.
claims.say: wash gear is low level int gear any class can wear

claims.text: INT wash pieces worth buying at a fair price: Green Bandana, Raccoon Mask or White Raccoon Mask, Yellow Work Gloves or Red Marker, Silver Deputy Star and Yellow Snowshoes.
claims.say: good int wash pieces: green bandana, raccoon mask, work gloves

claims.text: INT wash gear resells more easily than mage-only equipment, and a mage can wear it now and pass it to a future attacker for HP washing later.
claims.say: int wash gear resells easy and helps your bosser later

claims.text: Voodoos in a bedroom map of the Haunted House drop Heartstoppers, attack potions that bossers buy; the author farms them semi-AFK for steady income.
claims.say: farm voodoos in the haunted house for heartstoppers

claims.text: A magician's MP gain on each level-up rises with the level of Improved MaxMP Increase and with total INT.
claims.say: more int and improved max mp means more mp per level

claims.text: The Crimsonwood Keep guards cast Seal often, so carry a large stock of Holy Water to cure it while training there.
claims.say: bring lots of holy water at cwk guards, they seal a lot

claims.text: Max spell damage works out to ((MATK squared / 1000 + MATK) / 30 + INT / 200) times the spell's basic attack, then times any Element Amplification and elemental staff bonus.
claims.say: mage dmg scales with matk squared, int barely adds

claims.text: Minimum spell damage uses the same formula, except the plain MATK term is multiplied by your mastery and by 0.9.
claims.say: min magic dmg depends on your mastery

claims.text: Because magic attack is squared in the damage formula, raising total MATK matters far more than raw INT; each INT point still adds one MATK.
claims.say: matk is king for mages, each int adds 1 matk

claims.text: Clerics, Priests and Bishops get neither Element Amplification nor elemental staves, so their damage relies on MATK alone.
claims.say: clerics dont get amp or elemental staves

claims.text: Common Chief Bandit spots in the 80s include Gobies with Meso Explosion and luring Windraiders together to hit them with Band of Thieves.
claims.say: cb 80s: me at gobies or bot on windraiders

claims.text: Iron Arrow out-damages Double Shot whenever two or more monsters are lined up, so save Double Shot for lone targets.
claims.say: iron arrow beats double shot on 2+ mobs

claims.text: Guardian only fires when you are hit or touch a monster; on a body touch it shoves the monster away and can stun it, but ranged or magic hits are not stunned.
claims.say: guardian only stuns mobs that touch you, not ranged hits

claims.text: At low levels Guardian rarely triggers and its stun lands far less often than the description suggests; players with it maxed report it stunning reliably.
claims.say: low lvl guardian barely stuns, maxed it stuns reliably

claims.text: An Ice/Lightning mage can stay at Mysterious Path 3 from about 55 to 70, though it turns into a slow grind toward the end.
claims.say: i/l can sit at mp3 from 55 to 70, gets slow late

claims.text: Windraiders and Firebrands are an alternative to Mysterious Path 3 for a 70-75 Ice/Lightning mage, but lightning attacks are too weak there until Ice Strike has more points.
claims.say: windraiders and firebrands work for i/l once ice strike has points

claims.text: Getting to the Windraider and Firebrand maps means passing Bigfoot, which is a real hazard on worlds where few high levels are around to kill it.
claims.say: watch for bigfoot on the way to windraiders and firebrands

claims.text: Death Teddies are the next step for an Ice/Lightning mage after the slow 70-75 stretch.
claims.say: after 75 an i/l can move on to death teddies

claims.text: A level 80 White Knight using Charged Blow does well on Dual Ghost Pirates; Blue Kentaurus also work but hit very hard.
claims.say: wk with charged blow? dual ghost pirates, blue kents hurt

claims.text: If you commit to Charged Blow as your main attack, max it as soon as possible rather than leaving it low.
claims.say: going charged blow? max it asap

claims.text: Build up accuracy before reaching your 90s, because monsters from around that level are much harder to hit reliably.
claims.say: stack accuracy before 90, mobs there get much harder to hit

claims.text: A common argument is that bishops rarely deal the main damage in boss runs and are brought mainly for Holy Symbol, Mystic Door and Resurrection.
claims.say: bishops at bosses are mostly there for hs, door and res

claims.text: Some players say pet auto-potion equipment and All Cure Potions make a bishop's healing and curing less necessary when bossing.
claims.say: some say pet pots and all cures replace a bishop

claims.text: Even critics of bishops accept that a mage is still needed for Guild Party Quest and Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest.
claims.say: gpq and cwkpq still need a mage

claims.text: Bishops are popular for leeching, killing mobs so lower-level party members gain exp without fighting.
claims.say: bishops get used a lot for leeching

claims.text: For Heal damage INT beats LUK: LUK's coefficient looks bigger, but INT also raises magic attack, which multiplies the whole result.
claims.say: int > luk for heal dmg since int also adds matk

claims.text: The HP Heal restores rises roughly in step with magic attack, like its damage does, though it follows a different formula.
claims.say: heal heals more the higher your matk

claims.text: Most attacks that cannot get through a monster's defense still deal 1 damage, because any result below 1 is raised to 1.
claims.say: if you cant beat a mobs def you still hit 1s

claims.text: Heal does not get that 1-damage floor: when defense would push its damage below zero, the hit shows up as a miss.
claims.say: heal misses instead of doing 1 when def is too high

claims.text: Clerics with low INT miss undead often with Heal, since magic accuracy rather than the level gap is the main limit.
claims.say: low int cleric heal misses a lot, magic acc is the issue

claims.text: The level-gap damage penalty only applies while you are below the monster's level; once you out-level it there is no reduction.
claims.say: level penalty only hits if youre under the mobs level

claims.text: Zombie Mushrooms are the weakest undead, which makes them the first practical target for attacking with Heal.
claims.say: zombie mushrooms are the easiest undead to heal

claims.text: Bowmen can get attack-boosting diamond arrows from a Crimsonwood Keep quest, or buy red arrows with the same attack in Showa; the Showa arrows are for bows only.
claims.say: get +att arrows from a cwk quest or red arrows in showa

claims.text: Pole arm Dark Knight solo at Papulatus: keep him pinned on the left until the top bombs are maxed with none near the top-right edge, then drag him right, pin him there and fight from the top right platform.
claims.say: pin pap left til top bombs max, then pin right and go up top

claims.text: Papulatus's stun and dispel only reach up to a certain height, so melee fighters attacking from the high platforms avoid them and save rebuffing time.
claims.say: stand up high at pap and his stun/dispel cant reach you

claims.text: From that top right ledge, pole arm Dragon Fury just barely reaches Papulatus; the author found no other warrior attack that does.
claims.say: pole arm fury barely reaches pap from the top right ledge

claims.text: Being knocked back by Papulatus on the high right ledge only pushes you back a little instead of off the platform.
claims.say: pap kb wont knock you off the ledge, just back a bit

claims.text: Stay in Berserk range for the whole Papulatus fight and only drink once HP is very low; that lets cheap potions carry most of the run.
claims.say: zerk the whole pap run, pot only when really low

claims.text: Once a Dark Knight has around 10k HP within Berserk range plus some Power Stance or Achilles, Papulatus can be pinned on the right from the very start.
claims.say: with ~10k zerk hp and stance, pin pap right from the start

claims.text: For Papulatus's second form, keep Berserk going and spam Dragon Fury; he goes down quickly without getting close.
claims.say: paps 2nd form: zerk + fury and he drops fast

claims.text: Papulatus's stun, dispel and slow carry no damage, so invincibility does not block them; debuffs that ride on damaging attacks, like Manon's and Griffey's, only apply if the hit lands.
claims.say: pap stun/dispel/slow ignore invincibility, only height helps

claims.text: Rush can dodge Papulatus's stun, dispel and 1/1 attacks, but the timing is hard, it costs attack time, and during some of his animations you plow straight through him.
claims.say: rush can dodge paps stun/dispel but timing is tough

claims.text: Attacks like Crusher only connect on Papulatus during his normal animation and a few others; while he heals they do not register.
claims.say: crusher wont connect on pap while hes healing

claims.text: Each Papulatus dispel strips a Dark Knight's Hyper Body, Dragon Blood, weapon booster and Maple Warrior, all of which must be recast.
claims.say: pap dispel = recast hb, dragon blood, booster, maple warrior

claims.text: Berserking Dark Knights should avoid very high jump at Papulatus; above roughly 110 jump it is easy to set off the top bombs early and spoil the full spawn.
claims.say: dont stack jump at pap, over ~110 you pop the top bombs

claims.text: Without a mount, the right side at Papulatus is easier to climb back onto than the left, which needs a long rope climb.
claims.say: no mount? right side at pap is easier to get back up

claims.text: Against Manon a Dark Knight can simply stand on him using Berserk and Dragon Fury, adding the occasional Sacrifice.
claims.say: manon: sit on him with zerk + fury, toss in sacrifice

claims.text: The Puppet trick for soloing Papulatus only works if your hits are strong enough to knock him back; if they are not, he leaves the Puppet and goes after you.
claims.say: puppet at pap only works if your hits can knock him back

claims.text: When setting two Puppets at Papulatus, place them at the far right of the room; set short of that, he can get hung up on the stairs.
claims.say: put your puppets all the way right at pap so he doesn't snag

claims.text: One Bowmaster 4th-job order: raise Hurricane and Bow Expert to about 21 first, then Sharp Eyes, and fill in the other skills later.
claims.say: bm: hurricane and bow expert first, then sharp eyes

claims.text: Many newer bosses and monsters, such as those in Temple of Time and at Pink Bean, resist elements, which makes Arch Mages and Paladins weaker there.
claims.say: tot and pink bean mobs resist elements, rough for ams

claims.text: Weapon-using classes boost their boss damage with Onyx Apples, and since their attacks carry no element, boss element resists do not hold them back.
claims.say: weapon classes eat onyx apples for boss dmg

claims.text: Many mage players hold that a lukless build out-damages a LUK build, and that LUK builds mostly pay off by letting you wear nicer looking gear.
claims.say: lukless mages hit harder, luk builds are mostly for looks

claims.text: Levels 1-10: Snails, Blue Snails and Red Snails on Maple Island, which also give decent mesos.
claims.say: 1-10 kill snails on maple island

claims.text: Levels 15-23: Pigs and Ribbon Pigs at Pig Beach, recommended and decent for mesos.
claims.say: 15-23 pigs at pig beach, ok mesos too

claims.text: Levels 42-52: Block Golems and King Block Golems in Eos Tower give good mesos.
claims.say: 42-52 block golems in eos tower, decent mesos

claims.text: Levels 71-90: Buffoons in Warped Path of Time <2>, then Ghost Pirates and Buffoons in Warped Path of Time <3>, the recommended pick from 75.
claims.say: 71-90 warped path of time, buffoons and ghost pirates

claims.text: Levels 77-90: Death Teddies in Forgotten Path of Time <3> are an option, suited to a fire-charge build.
claims.say: 77-90 death teddies in forgotten path of time 3

claims.text: Levels 82-100: Dual Ghost Pirates in Unbalanced Time are an option.
claims.say: 82-100 dual ghost pirates in unbalanced time

claims.text: Levels 94-120: Grim Phantom Watches in Forbidden Time are an option.
claims.say: 94-120 grim phantom watches in forbidden time

claims.text: Levels 95-110: Spirit Vikings in Warped Path of Time <4> are an option.
claims.say: 95-110 spirit vikings in warped path of time 4

claims.text: Levels 105-115: Gigantic Spirit Vikings in Twisted Time are an option.
claims.say: 105-115 gigantic spirit vikings in twisted time

claims.text: Levels 95-130: Red Wyverns in Red Wyvern's Nest near Leafre are a top recommendation.
claims.say: 95-130 red wyverns, one of the best spots

claims.text: Levels 101-140: Blue Wyverns in Blue Wyvern's Nest near Leafre are an option.
claims.say: 101-140 blue wyverns in their nest

claims.text: From level 100: Jr. Newties and Nest Golems in the Destroyed Dragon Nest in Leafre are recommended.
claims.say: 100+ newties and nest golems in destroyed dragon nest

claims.text: Many Leafre training spots burn through potions but give very fast exp.
claims.say: leafre spots burn pots but the exp is fast

claims.text: At Leviathan, Paralyze hits harder, but Chain Lightning can still reach the boss after its Wyverns spawn.
claims.say: at leviathan chain lightning still hits the boss past wyverns

claims.text: A Shadower with more base DEX than the dagger needs can reset the extra into LUK once gear and Maple Warrior cover the DEX requirement.
claims.say: once gear and mw cover dex, reset spare dex into luk

claims.text: Rangers train faster by raising Arrow Rain before Strafe.
claims.say: rangers: arrow rain before strafe trains faster

claims.text: A Ranger can train at Windraiders until Arrow Rain reaches about level 11, then move to a stronger spot.
claims.say: ranger: windraiders until arrow rain 11

claims.text: Maxing Snipe first is a bossing build for Marksmen; for training, most take Sharp Eyes, Marksman Boost and Piercing Arrow before Snipe.
claims.say: snipe first is for bossing, pierce first for training

claims.text: Firing Piercing Arrow through lines of Skelegons is a strong way for Marksmen to train.
claims.say: pierce the skelegons for great mm exp

claims.text: Snipe is worth firing on bosses like Zakum, Papulatus, Pianus, Bigfoot and Anego (Female Boss), which is where a Snipe-first build pays off.
claims.say: snipe every boss: zak, pap, pianus, bigfoot, anego

claims.text: Sharp Eyes helps classes with their own critical hits, like Night Lords, the most; for classes without crit skills the damage gain is small.
claims.say: sharp eyes helps nls the most, others get a small boost

claims.text: Marksmen can't keep a moving boss pinned in place the way Bowmasters can; dropping a Puppet usually fixes that on bosses like Headless Horseman.
claims.say: mm cant pin moving bosses, drop a puppet to hold them

claims.text: Shadowers at Skelegons usually combine Boomerang Step with Savage Blow, though some pair it with Band of Thieves instead.
claims.say: at gons shads usually do bstep then sb, some use bot

claims.text: Crimson Guardians can seal you, so a Shadower there wants a quick Boomerang Step and Band of Thieves rotation instead of lingering through repeated casts.
claims.say: crimson guardians seal you, keep your combo quick

claims.text: Mages gain more max MP per level the more INT they have, so leveling in INT gear with Maple Warrior active builds a far bigger MP pool.
claims.say: level up in int gear with mw on for way more mp

claims.text: For a Corsair in 4th job, Battleship, Wrath of the Octopi, Aerial Strike, Battleship Torpedo and Elemental Boost give much of their value at one point each, so grab those early.
claims.say: sair: 1 point in ship, octopi, aerial strike, torpedo, ele boost

claims.text: Battleship Cannon is the first skill a Corsair should max in 4th job.
claims.say: max battleship cannon first as a sair

claims.text: After Battleship Cannon, a Corsair raises Bullseye and Battleship for bossing and Battleship Torpedo and Aerial Strike for training.
claims.say: sair: bullseye + ship for bosses, torpedo + aerial strike to train

claims.text: A Corsair levels Rapid Fire after those, and leaves Maple Warrior, Wrath of the Octopi and Elemental Boost for last.
claims.say: rapid fire next, then mw, octopi and ele boost last

claims.text: Hypnotize is a situational Corsair skill that rarely affects training or bossing, so it is not worth many SP.
claims.say: hypnotize is situational, dont sink many sp into it

claims.text: When planning 4th-job SP, take the cheap one-point skills, then finish your top-priority skill before moving to lower tiers; a few points in second-tier skills first can help.
claims.say: 4th job sp: 1-pointers, finish ur main skill before lower tiers

claims.text: Spears are mostly one speed step faster than equivalent polearms and often carry accuracy, a big reason many Spearmen and Dragon Knights favor them.
claims.say: spears are usually a speed faster than polearms and have acc

claims.text: Swords are usually one or two speed steps faster than axes and blunt weapons and give steadier damage, so they are the popular pick over swing weapons.
claims.say: swords swing faster than axes and bws, steadier damage

claims.text: Glowing Whip stands out among swords, with built-in speed and attack well above average for its level.
claims.say: glowing whip is fast and strong for its level

claims.text: Put around 20 points into Dragon Roar so it covers a wide area; it is useful almost everywhere.
claims.say: around 20 in dragon roar covers a nice wide range

claims.text: Sacrifice helps you drop back into Berserk range after overpotting and works as a fallback attack when zerking isn't safe; keep its key away from your others, since its HP cost can kill you while zerked.
claims.say: sacrifice gets you into zerk range, keep it off nearby keys

claims.text: The Masteria quest Ancient Artifacts completes as soon as you show John Barricade any set 1 or set 2 ITCG etc item, such as a Taru Totem, Mystic Astrolabe or Naricain Jewel; nothing gets crafted.
claims.say: show john barricade an itcg etc item, quest done instantly

claims.text: Cool as Ice needs nearly every Masteria quest completed and a Mark of Naricain equipped, so despite its level 90 listing it can't be done before about 110.
claims.say: cool as ice needs a mark of naricain on, so 110+

claims.text: Dr. Kim's quest for a single Bloctopus keychain gives nothing by itself, but holding the rare Blocktopus Blueprint when you turn it in adds a scroll and exp.
claims.say: keep a blocktopus blueprint for dr kim's keychain quest

claims.text: Gathering up the Lacking Ingredients is a one-time turn-in for Mr. Ku: the reward improves as you bring more ginseng etc items, from 100 up to 1,000, then stays flat.
claims.say: save up ginseng for mr ku, rewards scale up to 1000

claims.text: Bring a Diferium Fuel Cell from deep in the jungle to T-1337 in New Leaf City to make very strong but short potions; parts dropped by NLC's mechanical monsters are also used.
claims.say: diferium fuel cell plus t-1337 makes strong short potions

claims.text: Ice Demon is mostly a debuff: it leaves monsters weak to fire so Ifrit can damage targets that resist ice and lightning, such as Nightshadows or Crimson Guardians.
claims.say: ice demon then ifrit for stuff that resists ice and lightning

claims.text: The mastery book that raises Blizzard to level 20 drops from Zakum.
claims.say: blizzard 20 book comes from zakum

claims.text: Some Rangers put a few points into Inferno just to lure and aggro monsters rather than using it as a main attack.
claims.say: some rangers take a bit of inferno just to pull mobs

claims.text: Ifrit's damage is not raised by Element Amplification or by an elemental wand.
claims.say: ifrit doesn't get boosted by amp or an e-wand

claims.text: A polearm Dark Knight plan for level 141: Berserk maxed, Maple Warrior at 19, Beholder at 10, one point each in Rush and Hex of the Beholder, and Aura of the Beholder at 5 before choosing a direction.
claims.say: 141 drk: max zerk, mw 19, beholder 10, then choose

claims.text: The author's chosen path stops Aura of the Beholder at 6 and puts every later point into Rush, the purely offensive option compared with maxing Achilles or Aura first.
claims.say: aura to 6 then dump all sp into rush for damage

claims.text: When mobbing, a polearm Dark Knight can Rush the nearest monsters into the ones behind them to pile the group against a wall, then clear the pile with area attacks.
claims.say: rush mobs into each other to stack them, then aoe

claims.text: Rush is a quick way to finish a single leftover monster, and it moves you away from it at the same time.
claims.say: rush works as a fast finisher on stragglers

claims.text: Rushing a monster that is still in its knockback animation either shoves it as normal or carries you through it, often without taking damage.
claims.say: rush a mob mid knockback and you usually slip through unhurt

claims.text: Early Rush points suit polearm Dark Knights better than spear users, because spears kill single monsters too quickly for repeated rushing to add much.
claims.say: early rush fits polearm drks, spears kill too fast for it

claims.text: Rush stacking pays off most on very tough monsters such as those in the Temple of Time, where each one gets rushed several times before it dies.
claims.say: rush adds up most on tanky mobs like at temple of time

claims.text: Players disagree on skipping Power Stance: some use monster knockback to travel faster and keep Stance for bossing, others say going without it hurts once you can 2-3 hit Skelegons.
claims.say: stance is argued, mainly bossing but some want it for skeles

claims.text: Achilles is a passive reduction of damage taken, while Power Stance is what prevents knockback; they solve different problems.
claims.say: achilles cuts damage taken, stance stops knockback

claims.text: Power Stance becomes worth getting if you plan to solo Papulatus, even for a Dark Knight who skips it for training.
claims.say: grab stance if you want to solo pap

claims.text: Hex of the Beholder adds handy buffs that a Dark Knight can live without, so it can be left for last.
claims.say: hex can wait, its buffs are nice but optional

claims.text: A Dark Knight training on Skelegons can face them so their blasts knock him forward, moving faster than walking, and jump into a pack to get pushed back into attack range.
claims.say: let skeles knock you forward, its faster than walking

claims.text: Leveling up while wearing INT gear gives bonus MP, about 1 extra MP per 10 INT, for every class except magicians.
claims.say: wear int gear when you level for extra mp

claims.text: Adding new AP into MP while still wearing INT gear also earns an INT bonus: a warrior with 144 INT got 12 to 14 MP per point instead of the usual 2 to 4.
claims.say: put new ap in mp while wearing int gear for way more mp

claims.text: Moving AP from STR to MP with an AP Reset does not get the INT gear bonus, so INT gear can't create an endless HP wash.
claims.say: resetting str into mp skips the int bonus

claims.text: When an AP Reset moves a point from MP to HP, Improved MaxHP Increase does not apply and you get only the minimum HP for that point.
claims.say: mp to hp resets give minimum hp, no skill bonus

claims.text: Double washing isn't worth it for a warrior who already has 80 or more INT from gear: plain washing twice a level gives about the same HP for less cost.
claims.say: double washing isnt worth it on a warrior with 80+ int gear

claims.text: HP washing only pays off if one AP in MP gives more MP than an AP Reset takes back out; warriors gain little MP per point, so they need INT gear to wash.
claims.say: you need more mp per ap than a reset takes to hp wash

claims.text: Placing AP right at level-up or later in the level makes no difference to the MP gained.
claims.say: no difference adding ap at level up or later

claims.text: For a spearman from about level 52 to 70, Truckers are a strong pick, with Tippos as a decent alternative.
claims.say: spearman 52-70? truckers are great

claims.text: Mysterious Path 3 drops a good amount of mesos, but a spearman with a weak weapon may struggle to kill there quickly.
claims.say: mp3 drops good mesos but you need decent damage

claims.text: By the 50s a spearman should move from a weak polearm to one with 85 or more attack; such weapons are not expensive and help a lot.
claims.say: get an 85+ att polearm in your 50s, its cheap and helps a ton

claims.text: To judge a training spot, note your exp percent and the clock, train nonstop for one full hour, then check again; also note whether you were solo or partied and any 2x exp card.
claims.say: note exp % and time, grind an hour straight, then compare

claims.text: Bowmen in their early-to-mid 20s did well on Pigs and on Horny Mushrooms and Green Mushrooms.
claims.say: low 20s archer? pigs or horny and green mushrooms work

claims.text: Around level 30 to 34, Ant Tunnel and Wild Boars both worked well for bowmen.
claims.say: around 30, ant tunnel or wild boars work for archers

claims.text: Jr. Wraiths gave hunters decent exp in the early-to-mid 40s, even with little STR.
claims.say: jr wraiths are fine for hunters in the 40s

claims.text: Crossbowmen in the 50s and 60s trained Stone Golems and Dark Stone Golems, and standing at the bottom of the golem map gave clearly better exp.
claims.say: golems work for xbows 52-66, bottom of the map is best

claims.text: Voodoo and Hoodoo were among the better bowman spots from the mid 60s to late 70s; players found them faster than the alternatives once into the late 60s, especially with 2x exp.
claims.say: voodoo and hoodoo are great for archers mid 60s to late 70s

claims.text: Target dummies (Straw Target Dummy and Wooden Target Dummy) gave bowmen steady exp from the late 40s through the 70s.
claims.say: target dummies are steady exp for archers late 40s to 70s

claims.text: Death Teddies gave slow exp for bowmen in the late 70s and 80s; Squids paid noticeably better at the same levels unless you shared Death Teddies in a party.
claims.say: death teddies are slow, squids are better for 80s archers

claims.text: Wolf Spiders around 76-80 split opinion: one sniper found them strong with heavy potion use, while another called them not worth it after burning hundreds of potions and dying several times an hour.
claims.say: wolf spiders: fast exp but they eat pots and can kill you

claims.text: In Red-Nose Pirate Den 2, bowmen in the late 70s and 80s gathered the pirates into one spot, placed Puppet somewhere safe, then spammed Iron Arrow or Arrow Rain.
claims.say: pirate den 2: gather them, drop puppet, spam iron arrow

claims.text: A Marksman at Jr. Newties can keep the line frozen with Frostprey so nothing reaches you, then fire Piercing Arrow down the frozen line, which hits very hard with an Onyx Apple.
claims.say: frostprey freezes the newtie line, then pierce it

claims.text: At Jr. Newties the left side is the popular place to stand, on the middle platform or at the bottom, where a Nest Golem mixes in.
claims.say: at newties stand on the left, middle platform or bottom

claims.text: Characters with high avoid often dodge Zakum's 1/1 attack and his stun and seal attacks, which makes that fight much easier on them.
claims.say: high avoid dodges a lot of zak's 1/1 and stuns

claims.text: Putting AP into LUK on a Bishop would dodge more of Zakum's status attacks, but Heal and damage scale with magic, so the extra LUK weakens both.
claims.say: luk bish dodges more but heals weaker, magic drives heal

claims.text: The extra attack from a cider can drop a monster from three hits to two, which raises exp per hour noticeably.
claims.say: a cider can turn a 3 hit kill into a 2 hit kill

claims.text: Ciders are sold in Showa Town, which is easier to reach than New Leaf City for Warrior Elixirs, especially for players training in Aqua Road or Ludibrium.
claims.say: grab ciders in showa, easier than going to nlc for elixirs

claims.text: Ciders lower accuracy by 5, which can cost hits for warriors, brawlers and perma-beginners sitting right at their accuracy threshold.
claims.say: ciders cut accuracy a bit, watch out if you barely hit

claims.text: Ciders take one use slot each instead of stacking like Warrior Elixirs, so classes that fill their use tab with ammo, like Night Lords and Gunslingers, may prefer elixirs.
claims.say: ciders dont stack, nls and gunslingers may want elixirs

claims.text: Damage from a monster's attack is applied when its damage number appears, not when the animation starts, so you can still drink a potion after seeing the attack begin.
claims.say: mob dmg lands when the number shows, you can pot after the anim

claims.text: The stat bonus from Maple Warrior counts toward equipment requirements, so you can wield a weapon whose stat needs you only meet while the buff is active.
claims.say: mw stats count toward weapon reqs while it's up

claims.text: When Maple Warrior gets dispelled and your weapon relied on its stats, the weapon stops working and you cannot attack again until you recast the buff.
claims.say: get dispelled and that weapon is dead til you recast mw

claims.text: Depending on Maple Warrior for weapon stats is risky against dispelling bosses such as Papulatus, Manon and Horntail; players disagree on whether a dispel during an attack still disconnects you.
claims.say: careful leaning on mw at pap, manon or ht, they dispel

claims.text: Meeting a bow's DEX requirement through Maple Warrior frees a Bowmaster to swap a stat necklace like the Horntail Necklace for a damage one like the Mark of Naricain.
claims.say: cover bow reqs with mw and swap ht pendant for a naricain mark

claims.text: For warriors DEX mostly supplies accuracy rather than equip requirements, so many keep it low and get accuracy from gear instead.
claims.say: warriors only need dex for acc, keep it low

claims.text: With equal weapon attack, a warrior with 500 STR and 4 DEX has a base damage range a few hundred higher than one with 440 STR and 64 DEX.
claims.say: dexless warrior gets a few hundred more base range

claims.text: High-level items made with Maker can carry plenty of accuracy, which lets warriors keep base DEX low.
claims.say: maker gear gives lots of acc, lets you keep dex low

claims.text: Low-stat builds depend on expensive gear; players on a small budget may do better keeping a normal amount of their secondary stat.
claims.say: no money for gear? a normal secondary stat is fine

claims.text: A Dragon Knight or Dark Knight aiming for about 12,500 base HP by level 120-130 should plan on washing roughly 75 to 80 AP from MP into HP; players' estimates differ.
claims.say: for ~12.5k base hp by 120-130 plan on washing about 75-80 ap

claims.text: Berserk only works while HP is under a share of max HP, so more max HP gives a bigger buffer: a high-HP Dark Knight can take a big hit and still stay in Berserk range.
claims.say: more max hp = bigger berserk window, tank hits and stay zerked

claims.text: Getting a Zakum Helmet early helps an HP washer, since its INT adds MP on each level-up that can later be washed into HP.
claims.say: zhelm early helps hp washing, the int means more mp to wash

claims.text: Blaze Wizard 1st job: max the max MP passive, one point in Flame, max Magic Claw, then max Flame and Magic Guard, ending with a point in Magic Armor.
claims.say: bw 1st: mp passive, magic claw, flame, magic guard

claims.text: Blaze Wizard 2nd job: 1 Teleport, max Fire Pillar, Spell Booster to 11, max Teleport, then finish Spell Booster, Meditation, Elemental Reset and Slow; Fire Arrow can be left out.
claims.say: bw 2nd: fire pillar first, then tele, booster, meditation

claims.text: Seal comes after Meteor Shower mostly because there is nothing else left to spend SP on.
claims.say: seal goes last, nothing else to put sp in

claims.text: Elemental Reset is so plainly useful for a Blaze Wizard that it simply gets maxed without much debate.
claims.say: max elemental reset, it's just plain good

claims.text: A DEX-less Brawler is fairly easy since pirates keep 20 base DEX; by level 60 you need about +40 DEX from gear and by 70 about +50.
claims.say: dexless brawler needs ~+40 dex gear at 60, +50 at 70

claims.text: Going DEX-less is cheaper on a Brawler than on a thief, because pirate gear can carry DEX in its clean stats.
claims.say: dexless is cheaper on a brawler, the gear has dex

claims.text: Brawlers stay fun and level fairly fast through first and second job.
claims.say: brawler levels pretty fast in 1st and 2nd job

claims.text: MP Eater can trigger only once per attack, however many monsters the spell hits.
claims.say: mp eater procs once per cast, not once per mob

claims.text: MP Eater doesn't work on bosses.
claims.say: mp eater does nothing on bosses

claims.text: A monster drained to 0 MP can't cast its MP-based skills; drained Stormbreakers stayed unable to cast for a couple of minutes.
claims.say: drain a mob's mp to 0 and it can't use skills

claims.text: Draining MP doesn't stop physical attacks; Yeti and Pepe kept using its ground stomp after being drained.
claims.say: 0 mp mobs still use physical attacks

claims.text: Stormbreakers are immune to lightning, so Thunder Bolt only deals 1 damage to them.
claims.say: stormbreakers are lightning immune, thunder bolt does 1

claims.text: MP Eater helps a little when sniping without taking hits, but it is close to useless if you get hit often or cast costly ultimates, so it can wait.
claims.say: mp eater can wait, it barely helps with ultimates

claims.text: Thunder Bolt makes 2nd job training for Ice/Lightning wizards quick and fun.
claims.say: thunder bolt makes 2nd job il fast

claims.text: Early 3rd job is a slog for Ice/Lightning mages until Ice Strike has some levels; once maxed it covers a wide area.
claims.say: early 3rd job il sucks till ice strike is leveled

claims.text: Switching to an Elemental Wand 3 noticeably raises an Ice/Lightning mage's damage.
claims.say: elemental wand 3 is a nice damage boost for il

claims.text: For sword warriors, about 6 STR does roughly the same damage as 1 weapon attack, a handy ratio when weighing stat buffs against attack buffs.
claims.say: with swords about 6 str is worth 1 weapon att

claims.text: Elemental Wands 1 through 4 can be equipped from level 70 and have no LUK requirement, so LUK-less mages can use them.
claims.say: e-wands 1-4 are lv70 and need no luk

claims.text: Elemental Staffs 1 through 4 need level 103 and, unlike the wands, do require LUK.
claims.say: elemental staffs 1-4 are lv103 and need luk

claims.text: Elemental Wands 5 through 8 are the level 130 versions and again need no LUK.
claims.say: e-wands 5-8 are lv130, still no luk

claims.text: The number on an elemental wand or staff tells its element: 1 is fire, 2 poison, 3 ice, 4 lightning, and wands 5 to 8 repeat that order.
claims.say: 1 fire, 2 poison, 3 ice, 4 lightning, 5-8 same order

claims.text: A fire/poison mage wants the fire elemental wand because it boosts fire spell damage, which means fewer casts per kill.
claims.say: f/p? grab the fire e-wand, it powers up your fire spells

claims.text: To learn Maker you need level 45 and any job other than Beginner or Noblesse; start with Meren in the far right building of Magatia.
claims.say: maker skill: lv45+, any job, talk to meren in magatia

claims.text: Refined gems and crystals are appraised inside the Maker window and come out as low, mid or high grade.
claims.say: appraise gems in the maker window, low mid or high grade

claims.text: In Maker, a Diamond adds weapon attack and a Sapphire adds magic attack to a weapon, worth 1, 2 or 3 depending on grade.
claims.say: maker: diamond = weapon att, sapphire = magic att

claims.text: Maker gems by stat: Garnet adds accuracy, Opal avoid, Aquamarine jump, Amethyst speed, Topaz HP and Emerald MP.
claims.say: garnet acc, opal avoid, aquamarine jump, amethyst speed

claims.text: Power, DEX, Wisdom and LUK Crystals add STR, DEX, INT and LUK to a made item, giving 2, 3 or 5 points by grade.
claims.say: power/dex/wisdom/luk crystal add 2/3/5 of that stat

claims.text: A Black Crystal rolls a random bonus among weapon attack, magic attack, jump, HP and MP, while a Dark Crystal rolls among accuracy, avoid, speed and the four main stats; use Dark for random stat points.
claims.say: black crystal = random att/jump/hp/mp, dark = random stats

claims.text: Every Maker recipe needs plates or powders: plates are refined by the synthesizing NPCs around the world, not in Maker, while powders are uncommon monster drops, and their colour matches the item made.
claims.say: maker recipes need plates or powders matching the item color

claims.text: Each recipe also needs a Monster Crystal, made in Maker from 100 ETC drops; ETCs from higher-level monsters give higher grades, from Low Grade C up to High Grade A.
claims.say: 100 etcs = 1 monster crystal, higher lvl mob etc = better

claims.text: Gems are optional in a Maker recipe, but after all the effort of gathering materials it is a waste not to add some.
claims.say: gems are optional but always add some

claims.text: Maker only covers equipment from about level 45 upward, and never more than 5 levels above your own character level.
claims.say: maker only does lv45+ gear, max your level + 5

claims.text: Only one gem of each type fits on a made item, so you cannot stack several Diamonds or mix grades of the same gem.
claims.say: one gem of each type per item, no stacking diamonds

claims.text: Maker only makes gear for your own job branch, with pirates able to make both guns and knuckles, and it cannot make all-class items.
claims.say: maker only makes your class gear, no common items

claims.text: Making items of level 75 and above needs Maker level 2, and items of level 105 and above need Maker level 3.
claims.say: maker lv2 for lv75+ gear, maker lv3 for lv105+

claims.text: Gem slots depend on item level: under 75 gets one slot, 75 to 104 gets two, and 105 to 134 gets three.
claims.say: gem slots: 1 under lv75, 2 under 105, 3 under 135

claims.text: Appraising Dark and Black Crystals needs Maker level 2 and upgrading them needs level 3; all other gems appraise at level 1 and upgrade at level 2.
claims.say: dark/black crystals: appraise at maker 2, upgrade at maker 3

claims.text: The Maker skill lets you craft equips and add stat crystals while making them, so a crafted item can come out with more clean stats than the usual version.
claims.say: maker lets you add stat crystals for better clean gear

claims.text: Adding a stimulator in Maker gives a random result that can be better or worse; some players craft several and keep the first good one, others avoid the risk.
claims.say: stimulators roll random stats, can be better or worse

claims.text: When you swap jump or speed shoes for a stat pair, make up the lost speed and jump with other equips.
claims.say: move speed and jump to other gear when swapping shoes

claims.text: Chaos Scrolls only nudge each stat by a small random amount, so getting several stats exactly where you want them takes a lot of scrolls.
claims.say: chaos scrolls shift stats a little, takes many tries

claims.text: A Fast 5 one-handed sword needs about 103% of a Normal 6 two-hander's weapon attack to match its damage per second, and a Fast 4 one needs about 97%.
claims.say: fast 5 1h sword needs about 103 percent of the 2h att to match

claims.text: Without an attack-scrolled shield, a one-handed sword falls behind a two-hander, so pick the 2H when forging or buying at the same level.
claims.say: no att shield? go 2h sword over 1h

claims.text: Chain Lightning is not a straight piercing attack: it can jump to monsters on another platform, but it does not reach monsters behind the caster.
claims.say: chain lightning hops to other platforms but won't hit behind you

claims.text: Cygnus Knights stop leveling at 120, so against Zakum and Horntail they keep the level-gap penalty to accuracy and damage that higher-level explorers grow out of, which makes them weaker bossers.
claims.say: cygnus cap at 120 so they keep struggling to hit zakum and ht

claims.text: Warriors receive an extra row of inventory space, which makes them the usual pick for a storage mule.
claims.say: make mules warriors, they get an extra inventory row

claims.text: Do every quest on Maple Island: Roger's apple quest hands out apples to refill MP, and Pio's recycling quest gives mesos you'll need for the taxi in Victoria.
claims.say: do all the maple island quests, roger and pio's pay off

claims.text: For Mia's training quests, stumps are in the two basins at the bottom middle of the map, red snails at the bottom right, slimes at the top left and pigs at the top right.
claims.say: mia's quests: stumps in the bottom basins, slimes top left

claims.text: Bari's Orange Mushroom quest on the road to Southperry: they spawn on the platform above him, so change channels until it has a good spawn.
claims.say: bari's shrooms spawn on the ledge above him, cc for spawn

claims.text: Dances with Balrog's final training asks for 20 Dark Stumps, found at Rocky Road I a few maps east, and pays out return scrolls and potions.
claims.say: balrog's last quest: 20 dark stumps at rocky road 1

claims.text: Levels 13 to 15 go quickly killing stumps at East Rocky Mountain I.
claims.say: 13 to 15 is quick on stumps at east rocky mountain 1

claims.text: Rush-through trick: hit a monster with a fast attack so it flinches, then Rush right away; done right you slide through it without pushing it and without taking touch damage.
claims.say: hit a mob so it flinches, then rush instantly to slide through

claims.text: Rush-through works best on narrow monsters like Skelegons and Skelosauruses; bulky ones such as Spirit Vikings can still hurt you.
claims.say: rush-through works on skeles, big stuff like vikings still hurts

claims.text: With low-level Rush you must stand right next to the monster for the slide-through to work; higher skill levels let you start farther away.
claims.say: low lvl rush needs you right next to the mob

claims.text: Warriors can avoid Zakum's stun by using Rush at the right moment.
claims.say: rush to dodge zakums stun

claims.text: In Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest, Rush through Rellik to his far side to dodge his front-only stun and 1/1 attacks; even a failed try shoves him out of range of your ranged allies.
claims.say: rush through rellik to dodge his front 1/1 and stun

claims.text: Rush is also an easy way to dodge Margana's magic attacks in Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest.
claims.say: rush dodges marganas magic in cwkpq

claims.text: Putting Rush in a skill macro lets you trigger it while airborne so it goes off as soon as you land.
claims.say: macro rush, cast it midair and it fires when you land

claims.text: After Crusher, Rush makes a fast finisher that also carries you to the next group, and at Temple of Time it stacks mobs while dealing big damage.
claims.say: crusher then rush to finish and move to the next mob

claims.text: Power Stance and Rush serve different needs: Stance keeps you planted in one spot, while Rush is for moving around.
claims.say: stance is for standing still, rush is for moving

claims.text: For solo mobbing a Dark Knight can sweep a map floor by floor, running one way, dropping down, running back, then returning to the top, stopping only for groups of four or more.
claims.say: sweep the map floor by floor, stop for groups of 4+

claims.text: Since Brandish has shorter reach and suits small groups, Heroes mostly use Rush for getting around rather than as an attack.
claims.say: heroes mostly use rush to get around

claims.text: Truckers are good exp in the late 40s but slow down by the early 50s.
claims.say: truckers are good late 40s, slow by early 50s

claims.text: Roids are a good Bandit target into the early 60s: about two Savage Blows each, and they cannot reach you.
claims.say: roids till early 60s, 2 savage blows each and they cant hit you

claims.text: Elemental Wand 5 needs level 130, past the Blaze Wizard cap of 120, which leaves Elemental Wand 1 as the strongest elemental wand a Blaze Wizard can equip.
claims.say: ele wand 5 needs lv130, bw caps at 120, so go ele wand 1

claims.text: Maxed Monster Magnet pulls monsters from a distance toward a Dark Knight, helping gather mobs to attack together.
claims.say: monster magnet pulls mobs to you so you can group them
