claims.text: A Dawn Warrior held at level 50 makes a handy mule for farming Monster Carnival coins and Ludibrium Party Quest rewards such as Broken Glasses.
claims.say: a lv50 dw mule farms cpq coins and lpq broken glasses

claims.text: One level 50 Dawn Warrior setup: 19 Sword Mastery, 6 Sword Booster, 1 Soul Rush, 30 Soul Blade and 5 Rage.
claims.say: lv50 dw: 19 mastery, 6 booster, 1 rush, max soul blade, 5 rage

claims.text: The other level 50 setup keeps 19 Sword Mastery, 6 Sword Booster and 1 Soul Rush but maxes Rage at 20 and splits 15 points between Final Attack and Soul Blade, trading Soul Blade levels for weapon attack.
claims.say: or max rage and split 15 into final attack and soul blade

claims.text: A low-DEX Monster Carnival mule can reach about 96 accuracy by level 50 with DEX gear such as a DEX overall, DEX shoes and a Zakum Helmet, which gives stats plus accuracy.
claims.say: zakum helm + dex overall and shoes gets a dexless dw ~96 acc

claims.text: An all-STR, DEX-less Soul Master tested as the strongest Monster Carnival damage dealer among Dawn Warrior builds.
claims.say: all str no dex soul master hits hardest in cpq

claims.text: A well-scrolled Glowing Whip with a STR shield is a favoured pick over a scrolled Lion's Fang for a level 50 Dawn Warrior Monster Carnival mule; DEX-less users of it can score around 1500 CP alone.
claims.say: glowing whip + str shield is the cpq pick over lion's fang

claims.text: During 2nd job a Dawn Warrior gets most of its damage from Final Attack procs, the same way explorer warriors do.
claims.say: in 2nd job final attack is most of your dmg as dawn warrior

claims.text: Players disagree on Final Attack once a Dawn Warrior has Brandish: one side says Brandish with combo outdamages it and does not trigger it, the author reads the skill text as Brandish working with Final Attack.
claims.say: people argue if final attack still matters once you get brandish

claims.text: Monster Carnival monsters resist lightning, so Thunder Bolt hits weakly there, though against a pack of six it can still outdamage Cold Beam.
claims.say: cpq mobs resist lightning, tbolt only wins on big packs

claims.text: An Ice/Lightning wizard can help a Monster Carnival team by luring and grouping monsters so the warriors can hit many at once.
claims.say: in cpq lure mobs into groups for your warriors

claims.text: Instead of waiting for a Monster Carnival invite, gather three players near your level and split into two parties of your own.
claims.say: no cpq invite? grab 3 people and make two parties

claims.text: Ice/Lightning wizards split on 2nd job: some max Thunder Bolt then Meditation and skip Cold Beam, others skip Meditation and keep Slow and Cold Beam.
claims.say: il 2nd job is argued: tbolt and medi, or cold beam and slow

claims.text: One experienced player regretted Cold Beam and wished the points had gone into Slow, which makes an Ice/Lightning more useful at bosses.
claims.say: some ils wish cold beam points went into slow

claims.text: Meditation also buffs the party, which helps in party play, but solo players may argue a potion gives the same boost better.
claims.say: medi buffs the party, solo players may prefer pots

claims.text: Magic attack potions such as the Wizard Potion can stand in for Meditation if you leave it out of your build.
claims.say: skip medi and use wizard potions for the magic boost

claims.text: If the monsters you train on have little MP, raise Teleport after Meditation to save MP potions; if they carry plenty of MP, MP Eater may be the better pick.
claims.say: low mp mobs? level teleport. mp-rich mobs? mp eater

claims.text: At 70 an Ice/Lightning mage gets Ice Strike, which can freeze a whole group that you then hit with lightning.
claims.say: at 70 ice strike freezes the whole mob for your lightning

claims.text: Avoid building an Ice/Lightning only around Monster Carnival, since you will outlevel it.
claims.say: dont build only for cpq, you outlevel it fast

claims.text: Jr. Cellions give good exp for a wizard around level 40.
claims.say: jr cellions are good exp around 40

claims.text: One mobbing-focused plan: max Thunder Bolt by 40, put 3 into MP Eater, then max Meditation and Cold Beam, then Teleport, finishing MP Eater by 70.
claims.say: one il plan: tbolt, medi, cold beam, teleport, mp eater

claims.text: This player puts a level's AP into LUK one level in five and all other AP into INT.
claims.say: il ap: int, with a level of luk every 5th level

claims.text: At level 10 a Cygnus Knight goes to Ereve and talks to Mihile to become a Dawn Warrior.
claims.say: lv10 cygnus: talk to mihile in ereve for dawn warrior

claims.text: At level 10 a Cygnus Knight talks to Oz in Ereve to become a Blaze Wizard.
claims.say: lv10 cygnus: oz in ereve makes you a blaze wizard

claims.text: At level 10 a Cygnus Knight talks to Irena in Ereve to become a Wind Archer.
claims.say: lv10 cygnus: irena in ereve makes you a wind archer

claims.text: At level 10 a Cygnus Knight talks to Eckhart in Ereve to become a Night Walker.
claims.say: lv10 cygnus: eckhart in ereve makes you a night walker

claims.text: At level 10 a Cygnus Knight talks to Hawkeye in Ereve to become a Thunder Breaker.
claims.say: lv10 cygnus: hawkeye in ereve makes you a thunder breaker

claims.text: The Chief Knight who gave you 1st job is the one who handles your later Cygnus job advancements.
claims.say: your 1st job knight handles your later advancements too

claims.text: At level 30 Neinheart contacts you through the lightbulb quest notice; see Neinheart in Ereve, then your Chief Knight, who sends you to the test field past the Training Forest maps.
claims.say: at 30 see neinheart in ereve, then your knight

claims.text: Dawn Warriors and Blaze Wizards find the fake Chief Knight behind one of the portals in Training Forest I.
claims.say: dw and bw: fake knight hides in a training forest 1 portal

claims.text: Wind Archers and Night Walkers find the fake Chief Knight behind one of the portals in Training Forest II.
claims.say: wa and nw: fake knight hides in a training forest 2 portal

claims.text: Thunder Breakers find the fake Chief Knight behind one of the portals in Training Forest III.
claims.say: tb: fake knight hides in a training forest 3 portal

claims.text: The fake Chief Knight only replies with dots; talk to it, let it turn into a monster, kill it for the stolen treasure, then return to your real Chief Knight for 3rd job.
claims.say: fake knight only says dots, talk to it then kill it

claims.text: Bandits debate STR versus LUK builds: STR gives steadier damage and can use STR shields like Khanjar and Dragon Khanjar, while LUK has a higher damage ceiling and meets armor stat requirements at their listed level.
claims.say: str bandit = steadier dmg and khanjars, luk = higher dmg ceiling

claims.text: Good STR daggers are even harder to find than well-scrolled LUK daggers, and LUK equivalents of the Khanjar shields are rare and expensive.
claims.say: good str daggers are rare, luk versions of khanjars are pricey

claims.text: A STR bandit usually cannot wear armor at its minimum level, because the combined STR, DEX and LUK requirements add up to more AP than the character has.
claims.say: str bandits cant wear armor at min level, not enough ap

claims.text: DEX is a bandit's secondary stat; around 80 base DEX is a common target, some players keep more, and some skip DEX entirely by using Maple weapons.
claims.say: aim for about 80 base dex on a bandit

claims.text: The less base DEX a bandit keeps, the more they depend on armor that gives DEX, armor scrolled for DEX, or Maker-crafted gear with DEX to equip higher-level weapons.
claims.say: low dex bandit? use dex gear to meet weapon reqs

claims.text: The standard LUK bandit adds 2 DEX and 3 LUK per level until 40, which reaches 80 DEX; then either stop DEX there or keep adding 1 DEX and 4 LUK per level until the chosen cap.
claims.say: luk bandit: 2 dex 3 luk til 40, then cap dex or 1 dex 4 luk

claims.text: The usual rogue build for a future bandit maxes Double Stab first, then Nimble Body, then puts 3 points into Disorder to unlock Dark Sight and spends the rest on Dark Sight.
claims.say: rogue: max double stab, then nimble body, 3 disorder, dark sight

claims.text: Dark Sight can only be learned after putting 3 points into Disorder.
claims.say: need 3 points in disorder before dark sight

claims.text: Nimble Body raises both accuracy and avoidability, which is why rogues max it right after their main attack.
claims.say: nimble body = accuracy and avoid, max it after your attack

claims.text: A rogue undecided between assassin and bandit can max Keen Eyes and Lucky Seven early with some Nimble Body, then take Disorder and Dark Sight, keeping both paths open.
claims.say: unsure sin or bandit? get lucky seven and keen eyes first

claims.text: One bandit build takes 1 Dagger Mastery, then raises Savage Blow and Dagger Mastery, finishes Savage Blow, then Dagger Booster and Haste, maxes Booster and Dark Sight around 60, then Endure, leaving Steal for last.
claims.say: bandit: mastery, savage blow, booster, haste, dark sight, endure

claims.text: Steal does almost nothing useful for a bandit, so Endure should be maxed before any points go into it.
claims.say: skip steal, max endure first

claims.text: When bombing Gobies, if Assaulter fails to stun a target, Disorder can stop it from attacking you; for this reason Disorder is rated above Steal.
claims.say: assaulter didnt stun? disorder it so it stops hitting you

claims.text: An alternative bandit build raises Dagger Mastery and some Dagger Booster before finishing Savage Blow, because a stable, faster Double Stab outperformed a half-leveled Savage Blow.
claims.say: mastery first, stable double stab beats a low savage blow

claims.text: One chief bandit build puts 1 point in Assaulter, 3 in Chakra and 1 in Meso Guard, maxes Band of Thieves first, then Assaulter, Meso Guard, Meso Explosion and Pickpocket, with Chakra last.
claims.say: cb: band of thieves first, then assaulter and meso guard

claims.text: Chief bandits should max Band of Thieves before Assaulter; leveling Assaulter first is considered a poor choice.
claims.say: max band of thieves before assaulter

claims.text: Players disagree on Pickpocket: one view calls it a show-off skill that does little for training and says Chakra pays off more, while others take it early for extra mesos while training.
claims.say: pickpocket is mostly for show, chakra helps more long term

claims.text: Some chief bandits max Meso Guard before Assaulter and leave Assaulter at 1 point, since there is little use for it later.
claims.say: max meso guard before assaulter, 1 assaulter is enough

claims.text: A bossing shadower can open 4th job with 1 point each in Shadow Shifter, Smokescreen and Boomerang Step, max Assassinate, then Boomerang Step and Shadow Shifter, then Maple Warrior, Smokescreen and Taunt.
claims.say: bossing shad: max assassinate, then boomerang step, then shifter

claims.text: Against Papulatus or Pianus, a shadower can use Smokescreen's invincibility to safely set up a Meso Explosion or charge up an Assassinate.
claims.say: smokescreen first, then meso explosion or assassinate safely

claims.text: Boomerang Step is handy at Papulatus and Pianus for destroying the bombs they spawn, dodging attacks, and hitting Papulatus from a distance.
claims.say: use boomerang step to clear papu bombs and dodge

claims.text: The dash at the end of Assassinate can be steered, so a shadower can use it to move toward or away from a boss after attacking.
claims.say: steer assassinate's last dash toward or away from the boss

claims.text: Once Assassinate is maxed, a shadower can start attempting Papulatus solo; Pianus is the harder of the two.
claims.say: maxed assassinate? you can start trying papu solo

claims.text: Shadow Shifter adds extra dodges, which helps survive if Smokescreen runs out early and lowers the potion cost of boss fights.
claims.say: shadow shifter extra dodges save pots at bosses

claims.text: A solo training shadower can max Boomerang Step first, then Shadow Shifter, then raise Maple Warrior and Assassinate, max Smokescreen and Venomous Stab, finish Assassinate and Maple Warrior, then take Hero's Will.
claims.say: solo shad: max boomerang step, then shifter, then maple warrior

claims.text: A common shadower start is 2 Boomerang Step plus 1 each in Venomous Stab, Smokescreen, Assassinate and Shadow Shifter; then max Boomerang Step fast, or level it alongside Venomous Stab and Shadow Shifter, whose passives make it stronger.
claims.say: start: 2 boom step, 1 each venom, smoke, assassinate, shifter

claims.text: Most shadowers put Venomous Stab and Shadow Shifter ahead of Assassinate for faster training, while those who max Assassinate early do it for bossing damage.
claims.say: training shad: venom and shifter before assassinate

claims.text: Blood building a shadower means putting about 50 AP into HP rather than LUK; it costs roughly 10 weapon attack's worth of damage but, with Meso Guard and a Hyper Body buff, lets the shadower take hits like a warrior.
claims.say: blood shad: ~50 ap into hp, small dmg loss, tanks like a warrior

claims.text: Crafting fresh gear with Maker can be a cheaper upgrade than buying pre-scrolled pieces.
claims.say: maker new gear instead of buying pricey scrolled stuff

claims.text: For a one-handed Crusader using a Red Katana, a higher-attack shield is a better upgrade than small STR gains on armor.
claims.say: 1h sader? a better att shield beats small str gains

claims.text: As a rough rule when comparing warrior upgrades, about 3 STR is worth 1 weapon attack.
claims.say: about 3 str is worth 1 att for warriors

claims.text: HP washing pays off most when you start from the earliest levels; starting around level 70 leaves you well behind someone who washed from the beginning.
claims.say: start hp washing early, starting at 70 puts you way behind

claims.text: Later HP-washing gear upgrades include a Zakum Helmet for its INT and a cape from the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest.
claims.say: later swap to a zak helm and a cwkpq cape for int

claims.text: At level 83, Squids were the best tested spot for this claw user: slow, but better than Death Teddies or Spirit Vikings.
claims.say: at 83 squids beat death teddies, slow but steady

claims.text: Partying on those maps is not advised unless someone brings Holy Symbol or a buff that speeds up kills, such as Speed Infusion, Sharp Eyes, or Hyper Body for low-HP players.
claims.say: dont party there unless someone has hs, se or hyper body

claims.text: Weapon defense clearly cuts touch damage: in collected samples a level 65 Page took less than half as much from a Croco with about 400 DEF as with about 300.
claims.say: more weapon def really does cut touch damage

claims.text: Since STR and weapon attack multiply together, at about level 100 with roughly 450 STR and 130 attack, one weapon attack is worth about 3.5 STR.
claims.say: around lvl 100, 1 attack is worth about 3.5 str

claims.text: Cygnus Knights stop at level 120, so plan their gear around that cap.
claims.say: cygnus knights cap at level 120

claims.text: When picking between two-handed swords, convert the weapon's STR into attack equivalents; a lower-level sword with much more STR can match a Stonetooth Sword with a few more attack and has easier requirements.
claims.say: a str-heavy sword can match one with a few more attack

claims.text: Players of the class report that the Dawn Warrior's Soul Charge is Holy element, which makes Soul Masters hit holy-weak monsters much harder.
claims.say: soul charge is holy, great vs holy weak mobs

claims.text: Thunder Breakers benefit from their lightning element, since many bosses are weak to lightning.
claims.say: strikers love all the lightning weak bosses

claims.text: For training, a faster polearm generally beats a slower one with more weapon attack; the author tested a fast, well-scrolled polearm and levelled much quicker than with a higher-attack slow one.
claims.say: take a fast polearm over a slow one with a bit more attack

claims.text: Spearman-line players either stay pure polearm all the way to Dark Knight or go hybrid, switching between spears and polearms; hybrid is the most common choice.
claims.say: most dks swap spear and polearm, a few stay pure polearm

claims.text: A typical Dawn Warrior 1st job build maxes the max HP skill first, then Slash Blast and Power Strike, and puts the remaining points into Soul.
claims.say: dw 1st job: max hp skill, then slash blast and power strike

claims.text: A first point in Soul makes the early Cygnus quests easier for a new Dawn Warrior, at the cost of a little max HP.
claims.say: a point in soul first makes early cygnus quests easier

claims.text: Dawn Warriors split on the 2nd job order: some max Soul Blade first since it replaces Power Strike and Slash Blast, others raise Sword Mastery first because Soul Blade only takes over around skill level 18.
claims.say: soul blade or mastery first in 2nd job, people are split

claims.text: In 2nd job, taking Sword Booster right after the first 5 points of Sword Mastery is a common, safe choice.
claims.say: grab sword booster right after 5 mastery

claims.text: Casting Soul Rush out of a jump carries a Dawn Warrior nearly as far as a Flash Jump, a handy way to cross maps; there is a short delay between uses.
claims.say: jump then soul rush, you go almost as far as flash jump

claims.text: Soul Blade does not trigger Final Attack, so Dawn Warriors usually take Final Attack last or skip it; it mainly matters for single-target fights.
claims.say: soul blade doesnt proc final attack, take fa last

claims.text: Taking Soul Blade before Rage is fine early on, since Warrior Elixirs can stand in for the attack bonus until Rage is maxed.
claims.say: soul blade before rage, use warrior elixirs till then

claims.text: Don't skip Rage on a Dawn Warrior to fund other skills; party members expect it and leaving it out mostly hurts you.
claims.say: dont skip rage, your party will want it

claims.text: One point in Soul Blade right at level 30 lets a fresh 2nd job Dawn Warrior lure monsters from a distance.
claims.say: 1 point in soul blade at 30 is handy for luring mobs

claims.text: Many Dawn Warriors play Monster Carnival around level 50, where Slash Blast backed by decent Sword Mastery works well on fields 3 and 4.
claims.say: cpq around 50: slash blast with mastery rocks on field 3/4

claims.text: Save SP through the late 90s to dump about 20 points into Brandish right at level 100, then save again to max Advanced Combo at 110; not saving is a common mistake.
claims.say: save sp in the 90s for brandish at 100 and adv combo at 110

claims.text: A Soul Master gets Brandish at 100 and Advanced Combo at 110 without needing any skill books.
claims.say: no books needed for brandish or adv combo on soul master

claims.text: Panic and Coma are rarely needed on a Soul Master; Combo's extra damage and Soul Driver do more for training, so both can wait until after 110.
claims.say: panic and coma can wait, combo and soul driver matter more

claims.text: Leftover 3rd job SP can go back into Sword Booster and the MP recovery skill, which helps in Mu Lung Dojo, rather than into Coma.
claims.say: spare sp into booster and mp recovery, it helps in dojo

claims.text: The Black Kentaurus map has a poor spawn, so Soul Masters do better at Gobies.
claims.say: black kents spawn badly, go gobies instead

claims.text: With Soul Charge leveled first, Dual Ghost Pirates or Black Kentauruses work until Gobies take over; at Gobies its holy bonus only helps on the Bone Fish.
claims.say: soul charge first works at duals or black kents before gobies

claims.text: Dawn Warrior 1st job: max the max HP passive by level 13, put one point in Soul, max Slash Blast by 20, then max Power Strike and put the leftovers into Soul.
claims.say: dw 1st job: hp passive, slash blast, power strike, then soul

claims.text: Soul together with Slash Blast makes Zombie Mushrooms an easy 1st-job spot for a Dawn Warrior.
claims.say: soul + slash blast on zombie mushrooms is easy exp

claims.text: Dawn Warrior 2nd job: a few points in Sword Mastery and Sword Booster, Mastery up to 19, then Soul Blade with Soul Rush maxed partway, finish Soul Blade, max Rage and Final Attack, and complete Booster and Mastery last.
claims.say: dw 2nd: mastery, soul blade, soul rush, rage, final attack

claims.text: That 2nd-job order front-loads damage so the Dawn Warrior is useful in Monster Carnival early on.
claims.say: this order gets you strong early for cpq

claims.text: Dawn Warrior 3rd job: max Soul Driver and Soul Charge first, then Combo Attack, then Brandish, Advanced Combo and Panic, with any spare points last.
claims.say: dw 3rd: soul driver, soul charge, combo, brandish, panic

claims.text: Physical accuracy from stats is about 0.8 per point of DEX and 0.5 per point of LUK, on top of any flat accuracy on gear.
claims.say: each dex is about 0.8 acc, each luk about 0.5

claims.text: A DEXless Dawn Warrior can make up accuracy with gear: an all-stat helmet like Zakum Helmet plus accuracy or DEX on the face accessory, earrings, bottom, cape, shoes, belt and medal.
claims.say: dexless soul master: stack acc on helm, mask, pants, cape, shoes

claims.text: If your gear cannot supply enough accuracy for your training mobs, fall back to a low-DEX build with roughly 15 to 20 base DEX.
claims.say: cant hit enough? go 15-20 base dex instead of dexless

claims.text: Night Walkers have no dagger mastery skill, so swapping a claw for a dagger leaves them with a poor damage range.
claims.say: nw has no dagger mastery, stick with a claw

claims.text: When comparing a dagger against a claw, count the throwing stars' attack along with the claw's: Ilbi Throwing-Stars on a low-level claw like Garnier add up quickly.
claims.say: claw att counts your stars too, ilbis on a garnier add up

claims.text: Blaze Wizards, Night Walkers and Dawn Warriors all level at roughly the same pace because each gets a mobbing attack early: Fire Pillar, Vampire and Soul Blade.
claims.say: bw, nw and dw level about equally fast, all mob early

claims.text: Night Walkers can race from 70 to 100 by training with their poison mobbing attack, Poison Bomb.
claims.say: nw goes 70 to 100 fast training with poison bomb

claims.text: A Blaze Wizard around level 70 can get very quick exp by mobbing Blue Kentaurus with Fire Strike.
claims.say: bw at 70 levels fast hitting blue kents with fire strike

claims.text: Dawn Warriors level very quickly once they can mob with Soul Driver.
claims.say: dw levels really fast mobbing with soul driver

claims.text: For a cheap Cygnus leveling alt, a Blaze Wizard costs less to fund than a Night Walker or Dawn Warrior while leveling about as fast.
claims.say: cheap cygnus alt? bw costs less to gear than nw or dw

claims.text: Sakura Cellions on the top platform of Purple Plains, the map to the right of Amoria, drop plenty of mesos for how quickly they die.
claims.say: sakura cellions up top in purple plains drop good mesos

claims.text: Leprechauns first show up as meso bags that hurt you if you walk into them; attack the bag and the Leprechaun appears, often with some mesos, then kill it for more.
claims.say: hit the meso bag, dont touch it, the leprechaun pops out

claims.text: From about level 80, Windraiders and Nightshadows in the mountains and caves around Crimsonwood Keep give good exp and drop badges for the keep's exchange quest, so you train and earn at once.
claims.say: 80+ hunt windraiders or nightshadows near cwk, exp and badges

claims.text: The Crimsonwood Keep badge exchange, which trades badges for mesos, scrolls and other rewards, only opens once you finish every quest in the keep and the forest around it.
claims.say: do all the cwk and forest quests to unlock the badge exchange

claims.text: Miner Zombies in the Dead Mine, between El Nath's dead-tree forest and the Zakum dungeon, sometimes drop gold teeth; players working toward a Zakum Helmet need many, so farming and selling them pays well.
claims.say: farm gold teeth off miner zombies, zakum helm hunters buy them

claims.text: Orbis has a repeatable exchange quest: hand in 100 of one etc item for exp and a small reward, as many times as you like, which is why players use it to level alts.
claims.say: orbis exchange quest repeats forever, 100 etc items per turn in

claims.text: Farming the etc drops used by the Orbis exchange quest and selling them in bulk to players levelling alts is steady money; Coolie Zombies, Sakura Cellions, Jr. Cellions and Jr. Yetis are good sources.
claims.say: sell orbis exchange etc drops in bulk, alt levelers buy them

claims.text: Once you reach 2nd job, quest exp no longer keeps up with grinding, but many quests still hand out item rewards that can be sold for good mesos.
claims.say: after 2nd job do quests for the rewards, not the exp

claims.text: The Outlaw in the Sea gives you a random reward rather than letting you pick one.
claims.say: outlaw in the sea reward is random, you dont get to pick

claims.text: Party quests rarely give as much exp as grinding, but their item and meso rewards often make the time worth it.
claims.say: pqs give less exp than grinding but the loot makes up for it

claims.text: Kerning City Party Quest (levels 21-30) mostly hands out junk, but it can reward a 10% overall DEX scroll, which sells for a good price.
claims.say: kpq loot is mostly junk but the 10% overall dex scroll sells

claims.text: In the Ariant party quest (levels 21-30) players compete in one room to capture spirit gems from scorpions: weaken them with attacks, then use the NPC's spirit rocks; bombs knock gems loose for anyone to grab.
claims.say: ariant pq: weaken scorpions then use spirit rocks to catch them

claims.text: Spirit gems turned in at the Ariant party quest add up to points, and enough points earn the Palm Tree Beach Chair, which sells for a lot.
claims.say: save ariant pq points for the beach chair, it sells well

claims.text: Monster Carnival (levels 30-50) is one of the few party quests that beats normal training for exp, especially when you win your matches.
claims.say: carnival pq beats grinding exp at 30-50 if you win

claims.text: Monsters in Monster Carnival sometimes drop Maple Coins, and 50 of them can be traded for a Spiegelmann's Necklace, which sells well.
claims.say: save 50 maple coins from cpq for a spiegelmann necklace

claims.text: To farm Maple Coins, both teams in Monster Carnival room 1 or 2 can agree to summon only Teddies; they cost few points and die fast, so more coins drop.
claims.say: for coin farming both teams just summon teddies

claims.text: Ludibrium Party Quest gives a wider and pricier spread of prizes than Kerning City Party Quest, including 10% and 60% scrolls and capes.
claims.say: lpq prizes beat kpq, you can get 10 and 60 scrolls

claims.text: Ludibrium Maze Party Quest (levels 51-70) is simple: follow a teammate through the maze and kill every Tauromacis you meet; runs are quick, so rewards add up.
claims.say: lmpq is easy, follow someone and kill every tauromacis

claims.text: Ludibrium Maze Party Quest rewards are mostly potions, and selling them to NPCs over many runs adds up to good mesos.
claims.say: npc the lmpq potion rewards, it adds up fast

claims.text: Mushmom spawns at Someone Else's House and drops a range of armor scrolls; she can also drop Ilbi Throwing-Stars, but very rarely.
claims.say: mushmom at someone elses house drops armor scrolls

claims.text: Zombie Mushmom, the undead version of Mushmom, spawns at The Grave of Mushmom and drops weapon scrolls; Ilbi or Hwabi stars from her are extremely rare.
claims.say: zombie mushmom at the grave drops weapon scrolls

claims.text: Jr. Balrog appears in the Cursed Sanctuary only rarely and hits hard with magic, so bring plenty of HP or a high Magic Guard; his scroll drops are mostly poor.
claims.say: jr balrog in cursed sanctuary hits hard, bring hp

claims.text: Crimson Balrog can appear on the ship between Ellinia and Orbis and drops Hwabi stars; if he has not shown up soon after the ship leaves, get off and try the next trip. His magic hits very hard.
claims.say: crimson balrog spawns on the ellinia orbis boat, drops hwabis

claims.text: Area bosses respawn on short, regular timers and mostly drop 10% and 60% armor scrolls plus a few weapon scrolls; fewer people hunt them than regular bosses.
claims.say: area bosses respawn fast and drop 10 and 60 armor scrolls

claims.text: When opening a shop in the Free Market, the best spots sit next to the portal of a low-numbered room, since buyers see those shops first and often buy without comparing.
claims.say: set up shop by the portal in a low numbered fm room

claims.text: Snowshoes from the El Nath armor shop have 7 upgrade slots instead of the usual 5 and stop you sliding on El Nath's ice, which makes them popular for bulk scrolling.
claims.say: el nath snowshoes have 7 slots and stop ice sliding

claims.text: A simple merchant trick is buying snowshoes in El Nath and reselling them in the Free Market to bulk scrollers who do not want to make the trip; margins are small but steady.
claims.say: buy snowshoes in el nath, resell them to scrollers in the fm

claims.text: One Night Walker 2nd job order: 1 Flash Jump, a few Claw Mastery, max Critical Throw while adding some Claw Booster, then Haste, Vampire, Flash Jump, the rest of Claw Booster, Claw Mastery 7 and 1 Vanish.
claims.say: nw: crit first, then haste, vampire, fj, booster

claims.text: Others insist on maxing Claw Mastery early because Vampire's damage depends on mastery, and on putting about 6 points in Claw Booster early to speed it up; players disagree on how much mastery matters.
claims.say: many max claw mastery early for vampire damage, it's debated

claims.text: Vampire is the Night Walker's 2nd job mob attack and drains HP, saving potions, which makes it strong in Monster Carnival.
claims.say: vampire mobs and drains hp, great in cpq

claims.text: A simpler option is the usual Assassin approach: 6 points in Claw Booster as soon as possible, then max Critical Throw.
claims.say: or go the sin way: 6 booster asap, max crit

claims.text: An early point in Flash Jump helps escape incoming monsters, for example in Monster Carnival.
claims.say: 1 fj early helps you dodge mobs in cpq

claims.text: When the game checks whether a monster misses you, both your avoidability and its accuracy are capped at 999.
claims.say: avoid and mob accuracy both cap at 999

claims.text: If a monster is your level or higher, your avoidability drops by half the level gap, rounded down, before the miss roll.
claims.say: higher level mobs cut your avoid by half the level gap

claims.text: A monster's chance to miss you equals your avoidability divided by 4.5 times the monster's accuracy.
claims.say: miss chance is your avoid over 4.5 times mob accuracy

claims.text: The miss chance is clamped: thieves end up between 5% and 95%, every other class between 2% and 80%.
claims.say: thieves can dodge up to 95%, everyone else caps at 80%

claims.text: Against low-level monsters such as Green Mushrooms, a character with a few hundred avoid already reaches the miss cap, so more avoid adds nothing there.
claims.say: a few hundred avoid already maxes dodge vs weak mobs

claims.text: A weapon's attack reach is set by its weapon type and swing animation, not by how large the weapon looks.
claims.say: reach depends on weapon type, not how big it looks

claims.text: Stab swings reach very little height while slash swings cover more vertical space; this also holds for spears and polearms.
claims.say: stabs hit low and narrow, slashes reach higher

claims.text: Sword stabs reach far forward, while blunt weapon and axe stabs are short.
claims.say: sword stabs reach farther than axe or bw stabs

claims.text: In one player's tests, one-handed axes had the long-reach swing while one-handed blunt weapons had the short one, so pages and white knights get less reach from a blunt weapon.
claims.say: 1h axes reach farther than 1h blunt weapons

claims.text: Of the basic swings, the sideways sweeping slash reaches farthest, then the upward slash and the two stabs, with the downward slash shortest.
claims.say: the sideways slash reaches farthest, downward slash least

claims.text: For mages each INT point counts toward magic attack much like weapon magic attack does, while LUK adds no damage, so AP in LUK beyond gear requirements makes a mage weaker.
claims.say: int adds to matk, luk doesnt, so lukless mages hit harder

claims.text: Elemental Wand 2 and Elemental Staff 2 also boost fire spells, only by less, and cost far less than the 1 versions.
claims.say: ew2/es2 give a smaller fire boost but are way cheaper

claims.text: Elemental staffs carry high LUK requirements, so a lukless mage usually takes the elemental wand rather than building LUK for the staff.
claims.say: ele staffs need lots of luk, lukless mages take the wand

claims.text: A lukless Blaze Wizard has no need for LUK equips; basic starter gear plus a maple weapon or elemental wand is enough.
claims.say: lukless bw dont need luk gear, maple weapon or ele wand is fine

claims.text: Monsters that resist an element take reduced damage from it, and a monster immune to poison simply won't get poisoned by Poison Mist.
claims.say: poison mist won't poison mobs that resist poison

claims.text: Blaze Wizards can use Elemental Reset so their fire damage-over-time field still burns monsters that resist fire, which widens what they can train on.
claims.say: bw: elemental reset lets your fire dot burn fire-resistant mobs

claims.text: Aran's Double Swing and Triple Swing come out by pressing the normal attack key again and again; each extra press continues the chain, and you can tap ahead of the animation.
claims.say: just keep tapping attack, double then triple swing chain out

claims.text: Double Swing and Triple Swing cannot be bound to their own keys; they only trigger as follow-ups to the basic attack.
claims.say: you cant hotkey double or triple swing, they chain off attack

claims.text: Aran command skills that list arrow keys plus attack are entered one key after another in the listed order, not held or pressed together; the tutorial drills this.
claims.say: aran commands are keys in order, not all pressed at once

claims.text: Combat Step is a quick dash: double-tap left or right to dash that way, or put it on a key to dash in the direction you are facing.
claims.say: double tap an arrow to combat step, or hotkey it to dash forward

claims.text: Training an Aran mostly means hammering the attack key nonstop and pausing only to drink potions.
claims.say: aran training is mostly spamming attack and potting

claims.text: Arans are warriors: they wear warrior equipment, build stats like warriors, and fight only with polearms, since most of their skills need one equipped.
claims.say: aran is a warrior, wears warrior gear, polearms only

claims.text: Combat Step helps at higher levels to dash into gaps between monsters and keep a combo going.
claims.say: combat step lets you dash between mobs to keep combo

claims.text: Even a level 1 Combat Step sends you flying off ledges and slopes, so maxing it is not essential.
claims.say: even 1 point in step flings you off ledges

claims.text: Combo Drain splits opinion: some call the 2nd job heal weak and skimp on it, while others say it cuts potion use a lot.
claims.say: combo drain is debated, some say it saves lots of pots

claims.text: Arans take hits constantly and burn through potions at low levels, so budget for potions.
claims.say: arans eat pots early, stock up

claims.text: Arans come from Rien, a town that was frozen in ice.
claims.say: arans start in rien, the frozen town

claims.text: Next to polearm Dragon Knights, Arans have lower HP, unlock their skills gradually, and can deal less single-target damage.
claims.say: arans have less hp and single target dmg than drks

claims.text: A DEX-less Aran is possible but takes heavy funding; a normal Aran is fairly cheap to build.
claims.say: dexless aran only if you can fund it

claims.text: Rush only works on the ground, but pressing it in mid-air through a skill macro makes it fire the moment you land.
claims.say: macro rush in the air and it fires as you land

claims.text: Standing about halfway off a platform edge, Rush can carry you across a small gap, even with no monsters nearby.
claims.say: rush from a ledge edge to cross small gaps

claims.text: Timeless and Reverse gear come in matching pieces with the same names; a Timeless piece can gain five item levels while its Reverse twin gains only three, and the Timeless version has slightly better base stats.
claims.say: timeless levels 5 times, reverse only 3

claims.text: An item's skill bonus stacks on top of your own SP; if the skill is already maxed the extra level does nothing, so take one SP back out of it if you want the item to fill that level.
claims.say: if the skill is maxed the item +1 is wasted, reset a point first

claims.text: Holding a skill one point short of max for an item bonus is only worth it when that one level is a breakpoint that clearly speeds up your training.
claims.say: only hold back a point for the item bonus at a real breakpoint

claims.text: The Locked Timeless Pendant is a level 30 pendant any class can wear, with modest weapon and magic defense and a little avoid; it can't be traded and you can only have one.
claims.say: locked timeless pendant is lv30, untradeable, one per char

claims.text: The Timeless Pendant needs level 140 and gives +9 to all four stats plus heavy defense and avoid; each of its five item levels adds a few more points, but it is untradeable and one per character.
claims.say: timeless pendant at 140 gives +9 all stats and grows as it levels

claims.text: Timeless Earrings are level 120 earrings for every class with high magic defense, some MP and accuracy and five slots, and they pick up small random stats as they level.
claims.say: timeless earrings are lv120 for all classes, 5 slots

claims.text: Timeless Moonlight is the level 120 cape for all classes, with good weapon and magic defense and five slots; its item levels can add small stat, speed and jump gains.
claims.say: timeless moonlight is the lv120 cape anyone can use

claims.text: On the warrior Timeless pieces, the Fennel hat can add Rush, the Bergamot gloves can add Advanced Charge, Advanced Combo Attack, Hex of the Beholder or Aura of the Beholder, and the Taragon overall can add Achilles.
claims.say: warrior timeless hat can add rush, overall adds achilles

claims.text: The warrior Timeless Kite Shield can add a level of Guardian and the Timeless Grabbe shoes can add Power Stance once they reach their last item level.
claims.say: timeless kite shield can add guardian, grabbe shoes power stance

claims.text: Magician Timeless pieces: the Coral hat can add Ice Demon, Fire Demon or Holy Shield, the Hermosa gloves add Elquines, Ifrit or Bahamut, and the Myst Blue overall, wearable from level 118, adds Infinity.
claims.say: mage timeless overall is lv118 and can add infinity

claims.text: The magician Timeless Prelude shield can add Mana Reflection and the Timeless Cabatina shoes can add Big Bang at their final item level.
claims.say: timeless prelude adds mana reflection, cabatina adds big bang

claims.text: Bowman Timeless pieces: the Rapido hat can add Sharp Eyes, the Presto gloves Bow Expert or Marksman Boost, the Evernew overall Hamstring or Blind, and the Rontano shoes Dragon's Breath.
claims.say: timeless rapido hat can give bowmen +1 sharp eyes

claims.text: Thief Timeless pieces: the Chive hat can add Taunt, the Lubav gloves Venomous Star or Venomous Stab, the Prinsid overall Shadow Shifter, the List shield Ninja Ambush, and the Moonsteed shoes Shadow Stars or Assassinate.
claims.say: thief timeless overall can give +1 shadow shifter

claims.text: Pirate Timeless gear: Conrad Henkel hat adds Bullseye or Speed Infusion, Charlston gloves Battleship Cannon or Snatch, Burgunt overall Super Transformation or Battleship, Faraon shoes Battleship Torpedo or Dragon Strike.
claims.say: pirate timeless gloves can add battleship cannon or snatch

claims.text: The Timeless Executioners one-handed sword and Timeless Nibleheim two-handed sword can each add Brandish or Blast, so they fit both Heroes and Paladins.
claims.say: timeless swords can roll +1 brandish or blast

claims.text: The Timeless Bardiche one-handed axe and Timeless Tabarzin two-handed axe can add Brandish, making them Hero weapons.
claims.say: timeless bardiche and tabarzin axes can add brandish

claims.text: The Timeless Allargando one-handed blunt weapon and Timeless Bellocce two-handed blunt weapon can add Blast, aimed at Paladins.
claims.say: timeless blunt weapons can add +1 blast for paladins

claims.text: The Timeless Alchupiz spear and Timeless Diesra polearm can add Beholder for Dark Knights; the polearm swings a step slower than the spear.
claims.say: timeless alchupiz and diesra can add beholder for dks

claims.text: Both Timeless daggers can add Boomerang Step: Timeless Killic is the LUK dagger for thieves, while Timeless Pescas asks for STR and DEX and is listed for warriors as well as thieves.
claims.say: timeless killic or pescas daggers can add boomerang step

claims.text: The Timeless Lampion claw can add Triple Throw and also carries +8 LUK and +8 avoid on top of its attack.
claims.say: timeless lampion can add triple throw, plus luk and avoid

claims.text: Magicians can use the Timeless Enreal Tear wand from level 118 and the Timeless Aeas Hand staff at 120; both can add Chain Lightning, Paralyze or Angel Ray, and the staff trades speed for a bit more magic attack.
claims.say: timeless wand is lv118, staff 120, both can add angel ray etc

claims.text: The Timeless Engaw bow can add Hurricane and the Timeless Black Beauty crossbow can add Piercing Arrow; both also give +12 speed.
claims.say: timeless engaw adds hurricane, black beauty adds piercing

claims.text: For pirates the Timeless Equinox knuckle can add Barrage and the Timeless Blindness gun can add Rapid Fire.
claims.say: timeless equinox can add barrage, blindness gun rapid fire

claims.text: Reverse weapons keep the same skill bonus as their Timeless versions but have about 2 less weapon attack, and the Reverse mage weapons a few points less magic attack.
claims.say: reverse weapons have about 2 less attack than timeless

claims.text: For a Night Lord, dexless versus low-DEX comes down to which setup gives more total weapon attack plus LUK for the same budget.
claims.say: nl build: whichever gives more att plus luk wins

claims.text: Low DEX opens up DEX-requiring claws and gear with more attack, and one Night Lord saw a higher damage range after switching from dexless.
claims.say: going low dex let me use better dex gear, range went up

claims.text: For a fast cleric start, stay on Maple Island until level 8, then train at Henesys Hunting Ground until level 10.
claims.say: maple island to 8, then hhg till 10

claims.text: From level 10 to about 21 a young magician can mix Henesys Party Quest runs with grinding Pigs and Horny Mushrooms.
claims.say: 10-21 do hpq or kill pigs and horny mushrooms

claims.text: From level 21 to 30 a magician heading for cleric can run Kerning City Party Quest or grind in Ant Tunnel.
claims.say: 21-30 kpq or grind ant tunnel

claims.text: A plain standard-LUK build is the low-effort choice for a cleric because it avoids spending heavily on stat equipment.
claims.say: regular luk build is easiest and cheap on gear

claims.text: At second job a cleric can put SP into Heal first and then Bless.
claims.say: at 2nd job max heal first, then bless

claims.text: From level 31 to 40 a cleric can Heal-train in Ant Tunnel, since Heal damages the undead monsters there.
claims.say: 31-40 heal the zombie shrooms in ant tunnel

claims.text: Monster Carnival is an option for a cleric from the early 30s up to about level 45 and is seen as one of the faster routes there.
claims.say: cpq is a solid way from 30 to 45

claims.text: From level 41 to 45 a cleric can Heal-train on Wraiths, which are undead and take damage from Heal.
claims.say: 41-45 heal train on wraiths

claims.text: From level 45 to 50 a cleric can level by running Ellin Forest Party Quest.
claims.say: 45-50 do epq

claims.text: The bonus MP from INT gear only counts for AP you spend right after leveling up, so adding AP to MP at that moment while wearing INT gear and resetting it later leaves spare MP to wash.
claims.say: int gear only boosts mp from ap at level up, so wear it then

claims.text: Warriors and Brawlers can double wash every other level: on one level-up, wear INT gear, put 5 AP into MP, then use AP Resets to move those 5 out of MP into STR.
claims.say: double wash: at level up put 5 ap in mp with int gear, reset to str

claims.text: On the following level-up, put that level's AP into HP and reset AP out of MP into STR, spending the MP banked on the level before.
claims.say: next level put ap in hp, then reset mp ap into str

claims.text: This alternating routine suits Warriors and Brawlers because their max HP passives make each AP put into HP worth more, so they gain more HP while losing less MP than with the thief or archer routine.
claims.say: warriors get more hp per ap, so alternate levels when washing

claims.text: Washing a warrior the way thieves, archers and Corsairs do, every level, burns a lot of MP for little HP.
claims.say: dont wash a warrior the thief way, it wastes mp

claims.text: Adding AP to MP and resetting it outside of a level-up only loses MP, because the reset removes more MP than the add gave you.
claims.say: adding mp ap then resetting it later just loses mp

claims.text: With this routine a Brawler can double wash on roughly 120 to 140 total INT from gear, noticeably less than the older method needed.
claims.say: brawlers can double wash with around 120-140 int gear

claims.text: Put your INT gear on before the level-up happens; forgetting it costs you that level's washable MP.
claims.say: equip int gear before you level or you lose the mp

claims.text: For a Paladin, Holy Charge (sword) or Divine Charge (blunt) mainly pays off on holy-weak monsters such as skeleton mobs; few worthwhile bosses are weak to holy.
claims.say: holy charge is great on skeles, few bosses are holy weak

claims.text: Rush is a training tool for gathering monsters into one group and gets used a lot while grinding.
claims.say: rush is handy for gathering mobs while training

claims.text: Blast is a bossing skill with little training use, and players usually pair it with Power Stance, so the two together cost many levels of SP.
claims.say: blast is for bossing, usually paired with power stance

claims.text: A one-handed blunt weapon like a Crushed Skull plus shield needs a high-attack shield to match a good two-handed sword, and it has shorter reach, so a hybrid Paladin may stick with the 2H sword.
claims.say: 1h bw + shield needs a big att shield to match a 2h sword

claims.text: A lukless mage can still use the level 130 elemental staff, since that tier comes in a version with no LUK requirement.
claims.say: lukless mages can still use the lv130 elemental staff

claims.text: Going back to normal LUK is the price of using the level 163 elemental weapons later, because those need LUK.
claims.say: 163 elemental weapons need luk, lukless can't wear them

claims.text: Maker training quests come every five levels from 45 to 105, forging items for the Alchemists; they are easy and give good exp.
claims.say: maker quests every 5 levels from 45, easy exp

claims.text: Most Maker quests need items from all over the world, so gather the materials beforehand to avoid repeated boat trips.
claims.say: gather maker mats early, saves boat trips

claims.text: The 75 and 105 Maker level quests stand apart from the training chain and need none of it, while inside the chain the 85 quest must come before the 90 one.
claims.say: maker level quests dont need the training chain

claims.text: Maker training quests also reward graded jewels, powders and stimulators, so they are worth doing even when you do not need the exp.
claims.say: maker quests give jewels and stimulators too

claims.text: Processed Wood can be made from five times as much Firewood.
claims.say: processed wood can be made from 5x firewood

claims.text: The Maker training quests do not expand what Maker can do; they only teach you how to use the skill.
claims.say: training quests dont boost maker, they just teach it

claims.text: Heaven's Hammer drops normal monsters to 1 HP no matter your attack, so the charge element hardly matters there; Ice Charge is a sensible pick because frozen mobs hit you less.
claims.say: hh leaves mobs at 1 hp, use ice charge to freeze them

claims.text: The author regrets maxing Heaven's Hammer early and would rather have maxed Holy Charge and Blast first for stronger bossing.
claims.say: id max blast and holy charge before hh for bossing

claims.text: Poison damage over time cannot kill a monster: it stops at 1 HP, so a Night Walker finishes poisoned mobs with Lucky Seven or Vampire.
claims.say: poison stops at 1 hp, clean up with lucky seven or vampire

claims.text: Monsters that stay inside the Poison Bomb cloud can be poisoned again, so it works best on mobs that stand still; its range is short, so moving mobs need several bombs.
claims.say: mobs sitting in the cloud get repoisoned, range is short though

claims.text: Poison-immune monsters ignore the poison from Poison Bomb, so pick targets that can actually be poisoned.
claims.say: poison immune mobs ignore poison bomb, pick other targets

claims.text: Vampire strikes as several separate hits with a drain chance on each, so monster defense cuts every hit; high-defense mobs such as Windraiders are a poor place to rely on it.
claims.say: vampire is weak on tanky mobs like windraiders

claims.text: Night Walker 2nd job SP mostly goes to Claw Mastery, Critical Throw, Haste, Flash Jump and Vampire, which leaves only around ten points for Claw Booster or a single point of Vanish.
claims.say: nw 2nd job: mastery crit haste fj vampire, leftovers to booster

claims.text: Alchemist makes timed items such as Warrior Elixirs and apples last longer but does nothing for potions that heal by percentage; it is still worth more than most alternatives, so don't drop it.
claims.say: alchemist makes elixirs and apples last longer, keep it

claims.text: Bowmasters widely rate Sharp Eyes, Bow Expert, Hurricane and Phoenix as the core 4th-job skills to level first.
claims.say: bm core skills: sharp eyes, bow expert, hurricane, phoenix

claims.text: Put a single point in Dragon's Breath early and max it near the end of a Bowmaster's build.
claims.say: 1 point in dragon's breath early, max it at the end

claims.text: Hamstring is a buff rather than an attack, so it costs no attacking time; it gives your shots a chance to slow the monsters they hit.
claims.say: hamstring is a buff that gives your shots a chance to slow

claims.text: Cygnus Knights such as the Dawn Warrior earn 6 AP per level until level 70, one more than Explorers get.
claims.say: cygnus knights get 6 ap per level until 70

claims.text: A Chaos Scroll can alter several of an item's stats at once rather than just one, though some players in the discussion disagreed.
claims.say: chaos scrolls can shift several stats at once

claims.text: An Onyx Apple raises a Night Lord's Lucky Seven damage dramatically thanks to its large weapon attack boost.
claims.say: onyx apple gives nls a huge l7 damage boost

claims.text: Blue Kentaurus are a usual stop for a Blaze Wizard in the 70s, but the spot gets dull and costs a lot in potions.
claims.say: blue kents are ok for bw in the 70s but burn lots of pots

claims.text: For a low-70s Blaze Wizard, Dual Ghost Pirates and Death Teddies return more exp for the HP you chew through than Blue Kentaurus; which one is faster comes down to map layout.
claims.say: duals or death teddys give more exp per hp than blue kents

claims.text: On a tight budget, a 70s Blaze Wizard can keep training at Mysterious Path 3 until their gear improves, then move on to Squids a few levels later.
claims.say: cheap route: stay at mp3 til better gear, then go squids

claims.text: The usual Blaze Wizard skill build maxes every 1st and 2nd job skill except Magic Armor and Fire Arrow.
claims.say: normal bw build maxes everything but magic armor and fire arrow

claims.text: Monster Carnival gives better exp than solo training in the 40s, though many players find it repetitive.
claims.say: mcpq is better exp in the 40s, just kinda boring

claims.text: Squids and Gobies are another spot suggested for a Blaze Wizard training with Fire Strike in the 70s, for those who find Blue Kentaurus dull over many levels.
claims.say: squids and gobies are a fun alt to kents in the 70s

claims.text: Many Shadowers say Venomous Stab speeds up training, and some who skipped it for bossing skills regretted the slower grind; others still prefer skills they actively press.
claims.say: skip venom and training gets slower, lots of shads regret it

claims.text: Assassinate is a strong pick for bossing such as Papulatus, especially if you will not train much past the 140s.
claims.say: assassinate is great for bossing like pap

claims.text: The Shadower dodge skill (Shadow Shifter, often called Fake) lets you avoid more hits, lowering what you spend on potions.
claims.say: the dodge skill saves you a lot on pots

claims.text: Maple Warrior can be a lower priority for a Shadower who usually gets it from party members.
claims.say: maple warrior can wait if your party has it

claims.text: Ludibrium Maze Party Quest is a weak exp option in the 50-70 range, though it pays reasonable mesos.
claims.say: lmpq at 50-70 is bad exp but ok mesos

claims.text: Ghost Ship 5 is a suggested spot for a Blaze Wizard in the 50s because its monsters are weak to fire.
claims.say: ghost ship 5 mobs are weak to fire, nice for bw

claims.text: Mysterious Path 3 has large monsters and only about half of them are weak to fire, so a small map with dense spawn tends to beat it unless your party splits the map.
claims.say: mp3 is only half fire weak, better if you split the map

claims.text: Bishops take a penalty on Holy skills when attacking with an Elemental Wand or Staff that is not Holy element, which removed the elemental wand advantage for them.
claims.say: bishop holy skills get a penalty with non-holy elemental wands

claims.text: A Priest or Bishop who mostly gives Holy Symbol leech does not need a strong wand, since the exp bonus does not depend on magic attack.
claims.say: for holy symbol leeching your wand barely matters

claims.text: A lukless Cleric-line mage should only switch to normal LUK if gear such as a Zakum Helmet and a Horntail Necklace can lift LUK close to what regular wands of their level require.
claims.say: only drop lukless if zhelm + ht pendant get your luk near wand reqs

claims.text: A mage converting from lukless to regular LUK should aim for Timeless weapons and gear.
claims.say: if you go normal luk, aim for timeless gear

claims.text: Stay lukless until you are sure about converting and can fund the new gear; switching on a thin budget leaves you weaker.
claims.say: stay lukless till you're sure and have the mesos to switch

claims.text: Leech from a Priest or Bishop is in high demand, so selling leech is a reliable way for them to earn mesos.
claims.say: bishops make good mesos selling leech, always in demand

claims.text: The usual Dawn Warrior 2nd job build maxes Rage and Sword Booster and leaves Final Attack around level 21.
claims.say: dw 2nd job: max rage and booster, leave final attack low

claims.text: For a Dawn Warrior, Final Attack seems to trigger almost at once after Brandish's second hit, though players argue over whether it raises damage overall.
claims.say: dw final attack procs right after brandish, debated if worth it

claims.text: Dawn Warriors have no Power Stance, so knockback at bosses can waste swings and erase small damage gains such as Final Attack's.
claims.say: no stance on dw, knockback at bosses wastes your swings

claims.text: Only AP from a level-up gets the INT bonus; moving points into MP with an AP Reset gives just the base amount.
claims.say: only level-up ap gets the int bonus, resets dont

claims.text: After adding the MP, use AP Resets to pull those points back out of MP and into your main stat.
claims.say: then reset the mp points back into your main stat

claims.text: HP and MP draw on the same AP pool, so with even one point in it you can reset from MP into HP over and over, trading the extra MP for HP.
claims.say: hp and mp share a pool, reset mp into hp to wash

claims.text: You can only wash MP down to your job's minimum; for a Night Lord that floor is 14 times level plus 148, and the last point above it goes back into your main stat.
claims.say: you cant wash mp below your job's minimum

claims.text: Double and triple washing are simply MP washing with more points shifted from MP to HP each level; the method is the same.
claims.say: double/triple washing is the same mp wash, just more points

claims.text: This INT-gear washing pays off most for Night Lords, Shadowers, Bowmasters, Marksmen and Corsairs.
claims.say: int-gear washing is best for nl, shad, bm, mm and sair

claims.text: For warriors and Buccaneers, AP reset into HP misses the max HP skill bonus that level-up AP gets, so alternate: MP wash one level with INT gear, then put the next level's AP into HP.
claims.say: warriors: mp wash one level, put the next level's ap in hp

claims.text: Magicians don't need this trick; their INT and MP skills already give them huge MP.
claims.say: mages dont need int washing, they get tons of mp anyway

claims.text: For a rich max-HP build, add INT with INT gear from level 10, MP wash every level from 40, then convert it all into HP with AP Resets; it works but costs a lot.
claims.say: rich route: base int from 10, mp wash from 40, reset into hp

claims.text: Soul Blade and Soul Driver hits build Combo Attack orbs, so a Dawn Warrior relying on them from 70 to 100 should put SP into Combo Attack before Soul Charge.
claims.say: soul blade and soul driver build combo orbs, so combo first

claims.text: A low-LUK mage can wear class armor that needs some LUK but carries more INT, ending slightly ahead in total magic of a LUKless mage using the same elemental wand.
claims.say: low luk lets mages wear higher int class gear

claims.text: Elemental staffs cost less than elemental wands, so they are easier to risk on 30% scrolls, but they need much more LUK to equip.
claims.say: ele staffs are cheaper but need way more luk

claims.text: Bowmasters are in demand at bosses because Sharp Eyes boosts the whole party's damage and Puppet draws the boss's attacks away.
claims.say: bowmasters get boss invites for sharp eyes and puppet

claims.text: Bowmasters have little crowd control besides their bird summon, which only stops one monster at a time, so they take more hits while training.
claims.say: bowmasters get hit a lot training, only the bird stuns stuff

claims.text: Corsairs control mobs well by freezing them with Ice Splitter and hitting them with Battleship Cannon and Battleship Torpedo, so they take fewer hits and spend less on potions while training.
claims.say: corsairs freeze and wreck mobs so they take few hits training

claims.text: Corsairs bring few party buffs, so they are less sought after for bossing than Bowmasters.
claims.say: corsairs have almost no party buffs so bosses want bms more

claims.text: For Dawn Warriors, Brandish goes up to 30 and Advanced Combo to 20, though players were split on the Brandish cap, so check the skill window before saving SP.
claims.say: dw brandish maxes at 30, advanced combo at 20

claims.text: On a Dawn Warrior, max Combo Attack before putting points into Soul Charge.
claims.say: max combo attack before soul charge on dw

claims.text: Spamming back and forth across a map only flows when monsters die in about three hits; at four hits you end up stopping too often.
claims.say: back and forth spam works once mobs die in 3 hits

claims.text: Sorcerer Elixirs are cheap and restore both HP and MP, so a mage can carry hundreds of them as the only potion while training.
claims.say: sorcerer elixirs are cheap and heal hp and mp, stock up

claims.text: The accuracy you need to always hit a monster goes down as your level rises, until your level matches or passes the monster's.
claims.say: more levels means less acc needed, until you pass the mob

claims.text: If you can kill Oblivion Monk Trainees in three hits they never get to shoot you, which makes training there much smoother; weaker players may have to drop back to Oblivion Monks.
claims.say: 3 hit kill monk trainees and they never get to shoot

claims.text: Swapping a damage pendant for the exp Pendant of the Spirit is not always a win: if it adds a hit per kill or drops you below the accuracy you need, you can lose more exp than the bonus gives.
claims.say: exp pendant isnt worth it if it costs a hit per kill

claims.text: Fewer hits to kill does not raise exp in proportion: monster spawn rate also limits you, so one-hit kills do not double exp over two-hit kills.
claims.say: one hit kills dont double exp, spawn caps it

claims.text: A Dawn Warrior can keep upgrading by getting a better scrolled Red Katana or a higher attack shield instead of switching weapons.
claims.say: just get a better scrolled red katana or a higher att shield

claims.text: Sparta, Black Crystal Blade and Dragon Carabella are one-handed swords with Fast (5) speed, good next steps after a Red Katana.
claims.say: after red katana look at sparta, black crystal blade or carabella

claims.text: For mages, a point of INT gives one magic attack plus magic defense and MP growth, and it also adds a little extra spell damage on top, so 1 INT is worth slightly more than 1 magic attack.
claims.say: 1 int is worth a bit more than 1 matk for mages

claims.text: Spell damage is commonly modeled as (3.3 x magic + 0.003365 x magic squared + INT/2) times the spell's percentage, so total INT matters a little beyond the magic it gives.
claims.say: spell dmg scales with matk plus half your int

claims.text: If two pieces of gear give the same total magic attack, take the one that gets more of it from INT; the gain is small but free.
claims.say: same matk total? pick the gear with more int

claims.text: A hybrid Dragon Knight rarely ends up using Dragon Fury, since swapping from spear to polearm during training is a hassle.
claims.say: hybrid dks rarely bother switching to polearm for fury

claims.text: INT raises how much MP you gain per level, and HP washing turns that MP into HP, so players who wash want as much INT as they can get while leveling.
claims.say: more int means more mp per level to wash into hp

claims.text: One view is to scroll a Zakum Helmet for INT while HP washing, then switch to a helm scrolled for your main stat once your HP is high enough.
claims.say: some scroll zhelm for int while washing, swap it later

claims.text: The counterpoint: a low-DEX warrior or hermit gives up DEX that can decide which weapons they can equip, so a DEX- or main-stat-scrolled Zakum Helmet may serve them better.
claims.say: low dex warriors want dex on the zhelm, not int

claims.text: Capes can be scrolled for any of the four main stats, for HP or MP, and for weapon or magic defense.
claims.say: capes take str, dex, int, luk, hp, mp or def scrolls

claims.text: Gloves are the accessory slot to scroll for weapon attack or magic attack, and glove scrolls for DEX exist as well.
claims.say: scroll gloves for att or matk, dex glove scrolls exist too

claims.text: Shields accept scrolls for weapon attack and magic attack as well as STR, INT, LUK, HP and defense.
claims.say: shields can be scrolled for att, matk, stats, hp or def

claims.text: Shoes can be scrolled for DEX, speed or jump.
claims.say: shoe scrolls give dex, speed or jump

claims.text: Helmet scrolls exist for HP, INT, DEX, accuracy and defense.
claims.say: helmets take hp, int, dex, acc or def scrolls

claims.text: Earrings can be scrolled for INT, DEX, LUK or HP.
claims.say: earrings can get int, dex, luk or hp scrolls

claims.text: Overalls can be scrolled for any of the four main stats as well as for defense.
claims.say: overalls can get str, dex, int or luk scrolls

claims.text: Bottoms can be scrolled for DEX, HP, defense and jump.
claims.say: bottoms take dex, hp, def or jump scrolls

claims.text: Tops can be scrolled for STR, LUK, HP and defense.
claims.say: tops take str, luk, hp or def scrolls

claims.text: A high-HP Dragon Knight can solo Wolf Spiders for excellent exp; one player stayed there until level 106.
claims.say: hp dk can solo wolf spiders for great exp

claims.text: A spear is fine for a Dragon Knight's whole career; many solo Dragon Knights train with a spear rather than a polearm.
claims.say: a spear works fine for a dk start to finish

claims.text: A low-LUK mage build gives only slightly more magic than a lukless one, so some players feel the extra effort is not worth it.
claims.say: low luk gives a bit more magic but lukless is less hassle

claims.text: On Roids, lure the monsters to one side of the map first and then hit the whole group with Storm Break.
claims.say: pull roids to one side then storm break the pack

claims.text: With Storm Break maxed, keep sweeping back and forth across the map without stopping, only looting every several passes and turning around only at the map edges.
claims.say: max storm break and keep moving, loot every few sweeps

claims.text: Put Storm Break and Wind Walk in one skill macro to keep damage and movement going together.
claims.say: macro storm break into wind walk for nonstop sweeps

claims.text: Stepping into the mini dungeon on the Roid map now and then gets you a speed buff from Agent O.
claims.say: hop in the roid mini dungeon for agent o speed buff

claims.text: One suggestion for a level 41 Wind Archer is Iron Mutae at Lab - Area B-3 until about 44, though the author found Roids gave better exp.
claims.say: iron mutae at b-3 until 44 is an option, roids may be better

claims.text: After about level 44, Roids at Lab - Area C-1 work until 50, then move on to Lab - Area C-2.
claims.say: roids at c-1 until 50, then go to c-2

claims.text: A Paladin has to raise Blast to level 15 before a Blast 30 mastery book can be used on it.
claims.say: get blast to 15 before trying the blast 30 book

claims.text: A Night Lord needs roughly 4.8k HP without Hyper Body to survive at Horntail.
claims.say: nl needs about 4.8k hp without hb for horntail

claims.text: Players disagree on when an unwashed Night Lord can do Horntail: some call about 160 typical, others say reaching enough HP without washing takes until around 190.
claims.say: unwashed nl usually waits till 160 or later for ht

claims.text: To reach Horntail HP, swap LUK gear for HP-scrolled pieces such as a face accessory, necklace, Zakum Helmet, top, bottom and cape; staying alive beats a little extra damage.
claims.say: swap luk gear for hp gear, living beats a bit more dmg

claims.text: Wearing INT gear while you level raises the MP gained per level, which lets you HP wash more often.
claims.say: wear int gear when you level up for more mp to wash

claims.text: Washing twice every level needs an unrealistic amount of worn INT; about three washes per two levels is the practical ceiling.
claims.say: 2 washes a level needs crazy int, 3 per 2 levels is max

claims.text: If you do Zakum often, scroll one Zakum Helmet for INT to wear while washing, then get a fresh one to scroll for HP once you are done.
claims.say: scroll a zhelm for int while washing, a new one for hp

claims.text: For bargains, note shops that are still being set up while you browse Free Market rooms and recheck them a few minutes later; whoever reaches a freshly opened cheap shop first gets the underpriced items.
claims.say: note unopened fm shops and check back, cheap ones go fast

claims.text: Keep tabs on many unopened shops across different rooms at the same time instead of waiting in one room on a single shop, since any one shop rarely turns out cheap.
claims.say: camp lots of unopened shops at once, not just one

claims.text: When a Super Megaphone hypes free or dirt-cheap items in a named Free Market room, go there: those rooms fill with sellers dumping items below normal prices to sell quickly.
claims.say: wild smega about an fm room? go, those rooms get cheap stuff

claims.text: A seller struggling to unload an item in a crowded megaphone room usually knows its worth but will often take a lower offer, so haggle before paying the listed price.
claims.say: in smega rooms, ask the seller to drop the price first

claims.text: Good shop spots are by the room's door, at platform edges, and the spot farthest from the portal that is still visible without moving; spots in the middle of a platform sell poorly.
claims.say: shop at platform edges or by the door, never mid platform

claims.text: Out-of-the-way spots, like the top-left platform in Free Market rooms 7-12, are worth taking because buyers who make the climb look through the shop more carefully.
claims.say: hard to reach fm spots get buyers who look closer

claims.text: To claim an edge spot, walk to the platform's edge, then jump repeatedly while tapping the arrow key once in mid-air; you end up on the outermost pixel, so a shop fits where it looked impossible.
claims.say: jump and tap arrow midair to reach the last pixel for a shop

claims.text: Never write off a gap between shops or beside a wall as too narrow; try opening a shop there before moving on, since many such spots do fit.
claims.say: always try a tight spot before giving up on it

claims.text: Keep your guild name and anything that reveals you as a merchant, such as a buying ad for scrolls, out of the shop title; a plain title hinting at cheap scrolls makes buyers browse more closely.
claims.say: keep shop titles plain, dont look like a merchant

claims.text: Use the shop title to mention a hard-to-find item you are buying or something you sell, but only advertise items actually in the shop so buyers are not left asking and waiting.
claims.say: only advertise stuff in your title that your shop has

claims.text: Group identical items and order the shop with costly scrolled equips first, scrolls in the middle where scroll merchants look, cheaper goods next, and valuable stackables like Chaos Scroll at the end.
claims.say: pricey stuff first and last, scrolls in the middle

claims.text: Listing several clean copies of the same equip, such as Work Gloves, draws players who scroll gear, because a single clean item is easily mistaken for a scrolled one.
claims.say: sell clean work gloves in bunches, scrollers buy them

claims.text: Price items ending in a run of 9s (1,299,999 instead of 1,300,000); round, repeating-digit or random-looking prices put buyers off and sell slower.
claims.say: price stuff ending in 9s, like 1,299,999

claims.text: Buy below market and sell at or slightly under the usual price; overpriced items sit for days, tie up your mesos and stop you from buying more stock.
claims.say: buy low, sell a bit under average so it moves

claims.text: If you do price above average, show no more than about three of the same scroll; a large stack signals that nobody is paying that price.
claims.say: dont show a big stack of one overpriced scroll

claims.text: Befriending trustworthy fellow merchants, even at the cost of one profit, pays back in tips and deals; the author advises against joining merchant guilds.
claims.say: make merchant buddies, skip merchant guilds

claims.text: If you trade face to face, such as at the Free Market Entrance or reselling Gachapon prizes, avoid a name for ripping people off, or repeat customers stop coming back.
claims.say: dont rip people off face to face, repeat buyers matter

claims.text: In the 30s, a Red Sauna Robe with 100% DEX scrolls (+10 DEX) and a Red Viper with 100% attack scrolls (+7 attack) give a big damage jump; losing the defense of a separate top and bottom hardly matters.
claims.say: dex-scrolled sauna robe and scrolled viper, huge damage boost

claims.text: Don't auto-assign AP on an archer: put points into DEX and add STR only when a piece of gear requires it.
claims.say: no auto assign, dex only, str just for gear reqs

claims.text: Blessing of the Fairy's level comes from your highest-level other character, about one skill level per 10 of their levels, so a strong main makes Cygnus Knights stronger.
claims.say: blessing of the fairy grows with your highest char's level

claims.text: Soul Arrow is still considered essential, because you stop using up arrows, even though it gives no attack of its own.
claims.say: soul arrow is a must even if it adds no attack

claims.text: Monsters themed on an element resist that element, so Holy Charge does poorly against holy-themed monsters.
claims.say: holy themed mobs resist holy, dont use holy charge

claims.text: Holy-weak Skelegons are a top Paladin training spot; some players say Paladins level faster there than Heroes.
claims.say: skelegons are great for paladins, theyre holy weak

claims.text: Blast with a blunt weapon still mixes slashes and stabs; the slashes reach higher, which helps hit Papulatus without jumping.
claims.say: blast slashes reach higher, nice vs papulatus

claims.text: A DEX-less Dawn Warrior is fairly cheap to fund while still dealing strong damage.
claims.say: dexless dw is pretty cheap to fund and still hits hard

claims.text: Soul Rush gives Dawn Warriors quick movement around maps, which makes them more fun to play than explorer warriors.
claims.say: soul rush makes dw way faster to get around than normal warriors

claims.text: A DEX-less Night Walker attacks and moves faster than a Dawn Warrior and gets fun skills like Vampire and Poison Bomb.
claims.say: nw attacks and moves faster, and vampire and poison bomb are fun

claims.text: For Dark Knights, a spear hits harder with stabbing skills like Spear Crusher and a polearm hits harder with swinging skills like Dragon Fury: Pole Arm; the mismatched pairing uses a much weaker range.
claims.say: spears stab harder, polearms swing harder

claims.text: The matching attack type multiplies STR by 5 in the damage formula and the mismatched type by 3, plus DEX either way; your displayed range spans both, so it overstates the weak skill.
claims.say: your shown range mixes swing and stab, it lies about the weak one

claims.text: There is no hidden bonus for swinging a polearm or penalty for stabbing with it; each animation simply has its own base damage range.
claims.say: no secret polearm swing bonus, just two damage ranges

claims.text: For a quick estimate, a mismatched skill like Pole Arm Crusher lands in roughly the bottom quarter of your displayed range, and a matched skill in the top quarter.
claims.say: pa crusher hits around the bottom quarter of your range

claims.text: Pole Arm Crusher still has uses with a polearm: a finisher when one Crusher kills where Fury would need two hits, and a steady attack that costs no HP, unlike Sacrifice.
claims.say: pa crusher is a decent finisher and costs no hp

claims.text: A character around level 120 is already strong enough to be a decent member of a Zakum run.
claims.say: you can do zakum decently around lv 120

claims.text: Most Horntail runners are roughly level 150, which is about where a character starts being useful in that fight.
claims.say: most ht runners are around lv 150

claims.text: Fire/poison and ice/lightning arch mages usually need to reach about level 160 to 170 before they pull their weight in a Horntail run.
claims.say: arch mages want like 160-170 for ht

claims.text: Pink Bean is the one fight that still challenges characters above level 180, but it needs a large group and has a short time limit.
claims.say: pink bean is the real test for 180+ chars

claims.text: Arch mages are excellent at clearing groups of monsters but fall behind most other classes at bosses, and soloing bosses is hard for them.
claims.say: arch mages are mobbers, bossing solo is rough

claims.text: Echo of Hero, gained at level 200, adds little for a magician who already kills training monsters in one hit.
claims.say: echo of hero doesnt help a mage much at 200

claims.text: An Outlaw who can't afford AP Resets can put AP straight into HP instead of DEX; a few hundred extra HP helps survival far more than 20-30 DEX helps damage.
claims.say: outlaw: some ap in hp beats a bit more dex

claims.text: Plan on roughly 4k HP before fighting Dodo at Temple of Time.
claims.say: want about 4k hp before dodo

claims.text: Cygnus Knights, Blaze Wizards included, are capped at level 120, while Explorers can keep levelling to 200.
claims.say: cygnus knights cap at level 120

claims.text: Players disagree on Blaze Wizards: critics say a capped Blaze Wizard does less than a Fire/Poison mage and is rarely wanted at bosses like Zakum or Horntail, while fans play it simply because it is fun.
claims.say: bw is fun but weaker than an fp mage at bosses, debated

claims.text: Dark Knights can't overpot while Berserking: any potion that restores a big share of HP lifts them above the Berserk threshold, so healing has to come in small amounts after each hit.
claims.say: drk cant overpot, big heals knock you out of berserk

claims.text: While Berserking at Skeles, don't Rush them into a big pile; if a large group aggroes anyway, heal back to full and kill them without Berserk.
claims.say: dont rush skeles while zerking, if a big mob aggros heal to full

claims.text: If a Dark Knight is just short of two-hitting Skeles, an attack potion such as a Warrior Elixir can bridge the gap until Berserk or gear improves.
claims.say: just short of a 2 hit ko? drink a warrior elixir

claims.text: Players disagree on HP washing as a Dark Knight: some say the extra HP pays off for training and bossing, others say pulling AP out of STR costs too much damage while you still struggle to two-hit.
claims.say: hp washing on drk is debated, more hp but less damage

claims.text: About 7k to 8k max HP is enough to Berserk most training spots; to Berserk Skeles comfortably, around 10k lets you take two hits and survive.
claims.say: 7-8k hp is enough to zerk, around 10k makes skeles comfy

claims.text: At Horntail a Dark Knight is mainly wanted for Hyper Body and can't Berserk safely; max Berserk and reach the 140s before asking to join, since lower ones die to a couple of magic attacks.
claims.say: at horntail drk is mostly the hb guy, be 14x+ first

claims.text: Achilles makes a Dark Knight sturdier while Berserking, but putting SP there early can slow training compared with damage skills.
claims.say: achilles helps survive zerk but can slow your training

claims.text: After Berserk, a Dark Knight who trains with players that already have Maple Warrior can put the next SP into Power Stance.
claims.say: after berserk go stance if your party has maple warrior

claims.text: Heroes and Dark Knights deal similar damage, but a Hero can overpot and stay at high HP, while a Dark Knight must stay low to keep Berserk on, making DK training harder on potions.
claims.say: hero and drk hit similar, but only hero can overpot
