claims.text: For a LUKless mage, INT gloves and shoes without a LUK requirement cost much more, while INT Purple Adventurer Capes are fairly cheap.
claims.say: lukless int gloves and shoes cost a lot, int capes are cheap

claims.text: The overall matters most for a LUKless mage: buy a scrolled bathrobe or sauna robe, or scroll a low-LUK overall that your Zakum Helmet's LUK lets you wear.
claims.say: lukless mage? focus the overall, zhelm luk helps you wear one

claims.text: First job plan: max Combo Ability (needed for Combo Critical later), max Double Swing, max Combat Step for getting around, and put the rest in Polearm Booster.
claims.say: 1st job: max combo ability, double swing, combat step, rest booster

claims.text: Combat Step is not a Flash Jump: it doesn't work in midair and you can't attack out of it, but used off a ledge it flings you a long way.
claims.say: combat step isnt a flash jump, but off a ledge it flies

claims.text: Second job plan: max Polearm Mastery, Triple Swing, Combo Smash, Combo Drain and Body Pressure, and stop Final Charge at 21.
claims.say: 2nd job: max mastery, triple swing, smash, drain, body pressure

claims.text: Combo Drain looks weak early but scales with your damage; by fourth job it may let you train while using almost no potions.
claims.say: combo drain gets great later, you barely need pots

claims.text: Combo Drain and Body Pressure are worth either maxing or skipping, not leaving half done.
claims.say: combo drain and body pressure: max them or skip them

claims.text: Third job plan: max Combo Critical, Full Swing, Smart Knockback and Snow Charge.
claims.say: 3rd job: max combo critical, full swing, smart kb, snow charge

claims.text: Players disagree on Combo Fenrir and Rolling Spin: one view maxes both, the other says Fenrir needs far more combo than Combo Smash for less damage and Rolling Spin only stuns without moving you.
claims.say: fenrir and rolling spin are debated, some skip them

claims.text: Full Swing is a single skill that boosts both Double Swing and Triple Swing, so 20 SP maxes it rather than 40.
claims.say: full swing is one skill for both swings, 20 sp maxes it

claims.text: Freeze Standing is the Aran counterpart of Power Stance.
claims.say: freeze standing is the aran power stance

claims.text: Arans end up with spare SP in fourth job: they can max every Aran skill plus Maple Warrior and still have points left over.
claims.say: arans end up with spare sp in 4th job

claims.text: Mana Bull refills MP only, so a Bishop chaining Genesis at Skelegons keeps having to pause and cast Heal, because Skelegons land hits often even when they die in two casts.
claims.say: mana bulls dont heal hp, at skeles you'll keep stopping to heal

claims.text: Ginger Ale is only efficient once MP is down near a quarter; waiting that long tends to leave a Bishop too low on HP to take a Skelegon hit, so the author used it only with Hyper Body up.
claims.say: ginger ales only with hyper body, low mp means low hp at skeles

claims.text: A potion that restores both HP and MP, set on the auto MP pot at around 60%, let the author spam Genesis at Skelegons without ever dying, unlike MP-only potions or combo potions triggered late.
claims.say: use an hp+mp pot on auto mp at 60% and just spam genesis

claims.text: A low-DEX assassin can meet a DEX-heavy claw like Casters by getting DEX from earrings, a cape, shoes and an overall, then adding base DEX only for what is left.
claims.say: low dex sin? get dex earrings, cape, shoes, overall for casters

claims.text: Mid-DEX shoes are cheap to buy, but Facestompers are the better long-term shoe investment.
claims.say: mid dex shoes are cheap, facestompers are the long term buy

claims.text: For Zakum's body phases, the soloing Dark Knight stood on the bottom left and kept using Dragon Fury.
claims.say: do zak bodies from the bottom left spamming fury

claims.text: Onyx Apple gives a large weapon attack boost and Gelt Chocolate a bit more; long boss solos plan a full stack of them.
claims.say: onyx apples or gelt chocs for long boss solos

claims.text: While Zakum's MP-draining arms are alive, a Berserk Dark Knight refills MP with pure MP potions like Sorcerer Elixir so HP stays low enough for Berserk.
claims.say: use pure mp pots on mp eater arms so zerk stays on

claims.text: Bring plenty of All Cure Potions to a long Zakum fight; a solo run went through about 350 of them.
claims.say: bring tons of all cures for zakum

claims.text: A Zakum solo used about 500 recovery potions an hour, half of what was planned; make room in your Use tab before a long run.
claims.say: solo zak used about 500 pots an hour

claims.text: Before a full Zakum solo, do an arms-only solo to estimate how long the whole fight will take.
claims.say: try an arms only solo first to time it

claims.text: With a polearm, swinging attacks use the higher end of the damage range compared to stabbing.
claims.say: polearm swings hit higher than stabs

claims.text: Combo Critical can only be learned once Combo Ability is at level 10 or higher.
claims.say: need combo ability lv 10 before combo critical

claims.text: Mages should switch to the percentage-recovery potions sold in New Leaf City once monsters hit them for over 1000 and their MP reaches about 4.5k, to stop constant repotting.
claims.say: go nlc % pots once mobs hit 1k+ or you have ~4.5k mp

claims.text: Low-DEX equipment suits both Hermits and Chief Bandits, so one set can be shared between low-DEX thieves of either branch.
claims.say: low dex gear works for both hermits and cbs

claims.text: Scissors of Karma let you pass an otherwise untradeable item such as a Zakum Helmet to another of your characters.
claims.say: scissors of karma let you pass a zhelm to an alt

claims.text: A Blaze Wizard can max Fire Strike first and mob with it, putting off a Flame Gear build for a long time without slowing leveling.
claims.say: bw can max fire strike first and skip gear for a long while

claims.text: When training with Fire Strike, keep teleporting backward between casts so the mob follows you and stays grouped for the next cast.
claims.say: teleport back and spam fire strike as the mob follows

claims.text: A Fire Strike Blaze Wizard can start on Blue Kentaurus and move on to harder mobbing spots as soon as accuracy allows, around level 80 once Fire Strike is maxed.
claims.say: start on blue kentaurus, move up once your accuracy allows

claims.text: The Fire Strike route leans on a fire-boosting Elemental Wand; without one, a Flame Gear build keeps pace better.
claims.say: fire strike build really wants a fire elemental wand

claims.text: Berserk only works while a Dark Knight stays at low HP, so you have to watch HP constantly and drink weaker potions to stay under the threshold.
claims.say: berserk means staying low hp, use small pots and watch ur hp

claims.text: A thief short on mesos can wear ordinary armor early and save up for a well-scrolled LUK top and DEX bottom to put on at level 50.
claims.say: wear plain armor, save for a good luk top and dex bottom at 50

claims.text: A Zakum Helmet ranks among the most helpful purchases for a thief once you can afford one.
claims.say: a zhelm is a huge help, grab one when you can

claims.text: Better throwing stars such as Steely Throwing-Knives or Ilbi Throwing-Stars give an assassin a big damage gain, and owning several sets is worthwhile.
claims.say: get a few sets of steelies or ilbis, big dmg boost

claims.text: If your gear still needs more DEX, finish scrolling your shoes or buy a better overall; once DEX is covered, spend on a stronger claw.
claims.say: need dex? fix shoes or overall. dex covered? upgrade the claw

claims.text: Some thieves stop raising DEX once they meet the level 50 armor requirement, since level 50 sets are the ones most often sold scrolled.
claims.say: stop adding dex once you can wear the lv50 set

claims.text: A warrior who puts AP into HP keeps low DEX, so accuracy has to come from gear and items: an accuracy Brown Bandana, accuracy gloves, a Pumpkin Spear, and accuracy pills or drinks.
claims.say: hp warriors get acc from gear like brown bandana and pumpkin spear

claims.text: Train levels 1 to 10 on Maple Island, then work through the job advancement quests up to about level 14.
claims.say: 1-10 on maple island, then job quests till around 14

claims.text: Henesys Party Quest is a good exp source from around level 14 to 24.
claims.say: hpq is good exp from about 14 to 24

claims.text: Between party quests, train on the slime tree from about level 14 to 18 and at Pig Beach from 18 to 24.
claims.say: slime tree 14-18 then pig beach 18-24

claims.text: From level 20, Kerning City Party Quest or Ariant Coliseum are good exp; winning Coliseum matches pays especially well.
claims.say: 20+ do kpq or ariant coliseum, wins there give great exp

claims.text: From about level 23 or 24, Octopuses are a good next training target.
claims.say: around 23-24 move on to octopuses

claims.text: Windraiders were a poor fit for a low-60s Blaze Wizard who had not learned Slow yet: kills came too slowly and the Stormbreakers around them made things worse.
claims.say: windraiders are rough without slow, and stormbreakers are there

claims.text: When open-field grinding stalls in the low 60s, Ludibrium Maze Party Quest is a workable way for a Blaze Wizard to push through a couple of levels.
claims.say: lmpq got me 2 levels when grinding stalled in the low 60s

claims.text: Arans fight with polearms, so polearm scrolls and well-scrolled polearms are what an Aran player should be shopping for.
claims.say: arans use polearms, grab good scrolled ones

claims.text: Brandish is the Hero's main multi-target attack, and one Hero player found its reach wider than a Dragon Knight's Spear Crusher.
claims.say: brandish is the hero mob skill, reaches wider than crusher imo

claims.text: Hero-line players rate Shout as close to worthless, so it deserves little SP.
claims.say: shout is pretty useless, dont rush sp into it

claims.text: Paladins can fight with one-handed or two-handed swords and one-handed or two-handed blunt weapons, giving four weapon types to pick from.
claims.say: paladin can use 1h or 2h swords and 1h or 2h blunts

claims.text: Hyper Body gets Spearmen and Dark Knights invited to nearly any boss party, since everyone wants the extra max HP.
claims.say: dk always gets into boss runs, everyone wants hb

claims.text: Dragon Roar is a wide area attack with respectable damage for clearing groups around a Dragon Knight or Dark Knight.
claims.say: dragon roar hits a big area with decent dmg

claims.text: Spearmen choose between pole arms and spears as two distinct weapon paths; pole arms are cheap while good spears cost much more.
claims.say: pole arms are cheap, spears cost way more

claims.text: Dark Knights are in high demand when a Pink Bean run is being put together.
claims.say: dks are wanted for pink bean runs

claims.text: The Sniper and Marksman line fights from long range and can freeze most monsters, keeping enemies away.
claims.say: xbow line keeps range and can freeze most mobs

claims.text: Marksmen end up with little HP unless they spend on HP washing.
claims.say: mm has low hp unless you hp wash

claims.text: The cleric line brings Heal and Dispel, which makes it valued support in parties and boss runs.
claims.say: clerics heal and dispel, great support

claims.text: Bishops are durable thanks to elemental resistance plus Magic Guard backed by a large MP pool, and Teleport lets them move quickly.
claims.say: bishops tank well with mg and big mp, tele to move fast

claims.text: Genesis is one of the best area attacks in the game, and with so many Bishops around the book that raises it to 30 is in heavy demand.
claims.say: genesis is a top aoe, the 30 book is in high demand

claims.text: Ice/Lightning mages can mob from 2nd job onward and are among the fastest classes to level.
claims.say: i/l mobs from 2nd job and levels super fast

claims.text: Magic Guard lets mages tank hits that their low HP otherwise could not survive.
claims.say: magic guard lets mages tank hits

claims.text: Smokescreen makes those standing in it practically untouchable for a while.
claims.say: smokescreen is basically godmode for a bit

claims.text: Shadowers have low HP, but Meso Guard softens incoming damage and HP washing helps further.
claims.say: shads are low hp but meso guard helps a ton

claims.text: Claw thieves attack at range with throwing stars and build LUK as the main stat with DEX as the secondary one.
claims.say: claw thief: luk main, dex secondary, throws stars

claims.text: Lucky Seven and later Triple Throw are not affected by Claw Mastery, which makes early training easier before mastery is raised.
claims.say: lucky seven ignores claw mastery so early levels are easy

claims.text: Assassins get Claw Booster and Haste at 2nd job, and Hermits add Flash Jump at 3rd job, giving the line fast attacks and great mobility.
claims.say: sin gets booster and haste at 2nd, flash jump at 3rd

claims.text: Nimble Body at 1st job raises a thief's accuracy and avoid.
claims.say: nimble body gives acc and avoid early

claims.text: Critical Throw at 2nd job gives claw users strong critical hits.
claims.say: critical throw at 2nd job gives big crits

claims.text: At 3rd job Hermits get Alchemist to make potions heal more and Meso Up to earn more mesos while hunting.
claims.say: hermits get alchemist for pots and meso up for mesos

claims.text: Assassins learn Drain at 2nd job, an attack that restores some HP as it deals damage.
claims.say: drain heals you while you attack

claims.text: Claw thieves mob poorly until Hermits learn Avenger at 3rd job.
claims.say: sins cant really mob until avenger at 3rd job

claims.text: Shadow Partner uses up a Summoning Rock on every cast, and the rocks are easiest to get around El Nath.
claims.say: shadow partner eats a summoning rock each cast, el nath has em

claims.text: Claw thieves are so popular that claws, claw scrolls and throwing stars sell for high prices, and stars rarely drop from monsters.
claims.say: claws, claw scrolls and stars are pricey, stars rarely drop

claims.text: Night Lords are a favoured pick for boss runs such as Zakum and Horntail.
claims.say: nls are great for zak and horntail

claims.text: Brawlers start with short-range punches but close gaps easily with Corkscrew Blow, and later get some of the longest reach of any melee class.
claims.say: brawler range is short early but corkscrew closes the gap

claims.text: The Brawler line is self-sufficient: MP Recovery gives back MP and Energy Drain restores HP while attacking.
claims.say: mp recovery gives mp back and energy drain heals hp

claims.text: Oak Barrel hides a Brawler in a similar way to Dark Sight and works better overall, but monsters can still occasionally land hits.
claims.say: oak barrel is like dark sight but not 100% safe

claims.text: Accuracy rarely troubles Brawlers thanks to free accuracy from Bullet Time and gear with low DEX requirements, so a DEXless Brawler is far more workable than a DEXless warrior.
claims.say: dexless brawler works fine, bullet time covers acc

claims.text: A mage who one-hits Skelegons generally earns more exp soloing the map than sharing it, and the map only has room for about two such killers.
claims.say: if you 1 hit skeles, solo beats partying

claims.text: A common Skelegon loop: clear the top, drop down and clear the bottom, climb the rope back up and repeat, leaving the right side alone until spawns slow down.
claims.say: clear top, drop, clear bottom, rope up, repeat

claims.text: The bottom of the Skelegon map spawns far less than the top, so a partner working the bottom gets clearly less exp.
claims.say: skele bottom spawns way less than top

claims.text: Holy Symbol from a Bishop in your party noticeably boosts exp at Skelegons, so mages often keep a Holy Symbol mule or partner around.
claims.say: bring a holy symbol bishop to skeles for the exp boost

claims.text: Extra jump and Haste-like speed make the Skelegon loop faster, since every cycle involves climbing back up to the top.
claims.say: speed and jump buffs make the skele loop much faster

claims.text: If you own both a one-hitting Arch Mage and a Bishop, killing with the Arch Mage while the Bishop sits in party for Holy Symbol levels both characters at once.
claims.say: kill with your am and let your own bishop leech with hs

claims.text: At level 120 an Ice/Lightning Arch Mage commonly puts one point each into Blizzard, Chain Lightning and Ice Demon to try them out.
claims.say: at 120 put 1 in blizz, cl and ice demon to test them

claims.text: One I/L build after 120: Chain Lightning to 25, Maple Warrior to 9, Blizzard to 10, then finish Chain Lightning, add a few Ice Demon points and max Elquines.
claims.say: il: cl first, then mw 9, blizz 10, max cl, then elquines

claims.text: Another I/L order: Maple Warrior 9 and Blizzard 10 first, then max Chain Lightning around levels 127-136, then Ice Demon to 5 and max Elquines by about 147.
claims.say: or mw 9 + blizz 10 first, max cl next, then elquines

claims.text: After Elquines, that build takes Blizzard to 20, maxes Ice Demon and Maple Warrior 10 by about 159, puts most of the next SP into Mana Reflection, then Blizzard 30 and Maple Warrior 20, and maxes Big Bang and Infinity last.
claims.say: late il: blizz 20, max ice demon, then mana reflect, big bang, inf

claims.text: I/L Arch Mages usually boss with Chain Lightning and Elquines and train with Blizzard; one player calls Ice Demon pointless while another maxes it.
claims.say: il bosses with cl + elquines, trains with blizzard

claims.text: Blizzard and Maple Warrior past level 10 need mastery books; if you cannot get them, holding SP is better than dumping it into Mana Reflection or Big Bang.
claims.say: no blizz/mw books? save ur sp instead of dumping it

claims.text: Mana Reflection is seen as a weak skill for I/L; once Elquines is done the main choice is whether Infinity or Big Bang comes next.
claims.say: mana reflection is meh, after elquines go infinity or big bang

claims.text: With every 4th job skill finished near 196-200, leftover SP can go into third-job skills such as Partial Resistance.
claims.say: spare sp late? dump it in 3rd job stuff like partial resistance

claims.text: Panic's skill text talks about weapon attack, but its percentage is really the damage of the hit.
claims.say: panic's % is damage, not weapon attack like the text says

claims.text: Double Shot can only be learned after putting one point into Arrow Blow.
claims.say: put 1 in arrow blow first to unlock double shot

claims.text: HP washing is expensive to keep up because it relies on stacking a lot of INT on equipment and using an AP Reset every level.
claims.say: washing is pricey, lots of int gear plus an ap reset each lvl

claims.text: Amoria Party Quest is for married characters, so players often marry their main to one of their own mule characters to get access.
claims.say: apq needs a married char, so ppl marry a mule for it

claims.text: At Bigfoot, warriors are among the best attackers, while mages, Bowmasters, Marksmen and Corsairs have serious trouble; Bishops are close to useless there.
claims.say: warriors are great at bigfoot, mages struggle

claims.text: Melee classes do best against Rellik; ranged attackers face real problems there no matter how well geared they are.
claims.say: rellik is a melee boss, ranged classes hate it

claims.text: Almost every class is useful at Zakum; Heroes, Bowmasters, Night Lords and Corsairs are the most wanted attackers.
claims.say: everyone helps at zakum, heroes nls bms sairs best

claims.text: Heroes and Dark Knights stand out against Dodo and Lilynouch, while mages contribute noticeably less.
claims.say: heroes and dks are best at dodo and lilynouch

claims.text: Corsairs are the top pick at Headless Horseman, though every class does solid damage there.
claims.say: headless horseman is easy for all, sairs best

claims.text: Bowmasters and Corsairs are the strongest at Papulatus; mages do okay but deal less.
claims.say: bms and sairs are best at pap

claims.text: Heroes and Dark Knights are the best at Red Nirg; ranged classes and mages do less there.
claims.say: red nirg: heroes and dks best

claims.text: Bowmasters, Night Lords and Corsairs are the standout attackers at Margana.
claims.say: bms nls and sairs do great at margana

claims.text: Margana resists every element, so a Paladin's charges give no edge there.
claims.say: margana resists all elements, no charge bonus

claims.text: At Manon, Griffey, Leviathan and Pianus most physical attackers are solid, while mages do okay but deal less.
claims.say: manon griffey levi and pianus suit physical attackers

claims.text: Mages are rated as doing okay at most single-target bosses but well below the top physical attackers.
claims.say: mages are ok at most bosses but not top dps

claims.text: Heroes are favored in Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest because Brandish can hit several of its bosses at once.
claims.say: heroes are great in cwkpq, brandish hits multiple bosses

claims.text: Holy Symbol makes a Priest easy to get invited into parties.
claims.say: priests get party invites easy thanks to holy symbol

claims.text: The drawback of Holy Symbol is its long cast delay.
claims.say: holy symbol has an annoying cast delay

claims.text: Snipers have good mobbing skills, and Blizzard adds the bonus of freezing the monsters it hits.
claims.say: sniper mobs fine and blizzard freezes stuff

claims.text: Bowmen get neither Haste nor Teleport, so they get around maps slowly.
claims.say: bowmen are slow, no haste or teleport

claims.text: The golem forest is mainly worth visiting for the Scroll for Gloves for ATT 60% drops, not for exp.
claims.say: golem forest is only good for the glove att 60 scrolls

claims.text: One player's suggestion for a Blaze Wizard from about level 52 to 70 is to train at Mysterious Path 3.
claims.say: bw 52-70? try mysterious path 3

claims.text: A Blaze Wizard may want to pick maps somewhat above the levels that general explorer training lists recommend.
claims.say: as a bw you may want maps a bit above the usual lists

claims.text: Almost every warrior attack, normal swings included, runs at the weapon's speed; Crusher, Dragon Roar and Final Attack are the exceptions.
claims.say: warrior skills follow weapon speed except a few

claims.text: A Final Attack follow-up takes about 60% of the time of a normal swing.
claims.say: final attack is quicker than a normal swing

claims.text: Sky Ski is only a little faster than Omega Spear, worth about four more Crushers a minute.
claims.say: sky ski is barely faster than omega spear

claims.text: Dragon Fury attacks faster than Crusher, running at normal attack speed.
claims.say: dragon fury swings faster than crusher

claims.text: Hermit plan: max everything except Shadow Web and Shadow Meso, keep Shadow Meso at 1 and Web partial, and use spare points to max Nimble Body.
claims.say: hermit: max all but web and shadow meso, then nimble body

claims.text: Shadow Web helps clear crowded platforms: lure monsters together, web them, then hit them with Avenger, for example on the bottom of the Wolf Spider maps.
claims.say: lure, web, then avenger to clear packed wolf spider floors

claims.text: Shadow Meso throws mesos instead of stars; if you have your throwing stars covered, one point is enough.
claims.say: shadow meso at 1 is fine if you have stars covered

claims.text: A polearm Spearman can max Pole Arm Mastery and Hyper Body during 2nd job before working on Pole Arm Booster.
claims.say: spearman: max pole arm mastery and hyper body, then booster

claims.text: A Spearman in the mid 40s who finds Truckers slow can move on to Mysterious Path 3.
claims.say: truckers slow at 44? try mysterious path 3

claims.text: At Zakum an Aran can keep combo up by hitting two or three arms at once, but getting stunned or seduced stops the attacks and costs the combo.
claims.say: aran at zak: hit 2-3 arms at once to keep combo, avoid stun/seduce

claims.text: Arans are among the strongest mobbers in the game, which makes them very good at solo training.
claims.say: arans mob really well, great for training

claims.text: An Aran does well with a fast or normal speed polearm, and Sharp Eyes from a party member raises its damage a great deal.
claims.say: aran + sharp eyes hits way harder, use a fast polearm

claims.text: Arans gain roughly 44 to 48 HP per level, a little under a Buccaneer but well above a Bandit.
claims.say: arans get like 44-48 hp a level, just under a bucc

claims.text: Arans get little MP per level and no extra HP at 2nd job, but their main attacks come off the normal attack key, so MP is rarely a problem.
claims.say: aran mp is low but they barely use it, combos are basic attack

claims.text: North Desert Road 2 is only two maps away from Ariant, so it is less remote than it seems.
claims.say: its only 2 maps out from ariant

claims.text: Kiyos and Sand Dwarves are poor for mesos, so that map is for exp rather than money.
claims.say: kiyos dont make much money, go there for exp

claims.text: The accuracy shown in the stat window is for physical attacks; spell accuracy is hidden, and accuracy bonuses on gear do not help spells.
claims.say: stat window acc is physical, spell acc is hidden

claims.text: A LUKless mage who starts missing higher-level mobs is short on hidden spell accuracy; adding LUK gear such as a LUK-scrolled shield is one suggested fix.
claims.say: missing as a lukless mage? add some luk gear

claims.text: Early on a mage's armor matters little; put mesos into the weapon first and upgrade other gear slowly when funds allow.
claims.say: early mage? weapon first, armor can wait

claims.text: Wand or staff speed does not change spell casting speed; Fire/Poison's Explosion is the only spell affected by weapon speed.
claims.say: weapon speed doesnt change cast speed, only explosion

claims.text: For a mage each INT point adds 1 to magic like a point of magic attack, and also gives a little MP and magic defense, so INT is slightly more valuable.
claims.say: 1 int = 1 matk plus a bit of mp and mdef

claims.text: Voodoo and Hoodoo maps are often empty and worked for a Marksman training from about level 71 to 77.
claims.say: voodoo and hoodoo maps are pretty empty for low 70s bowmen

claims.text: When Windraider maps are crowded, a mid-60s bowman can look at Mysterious Path 3 or the Singapore maps for quieter training.
claims.say: windraiders crowded? try mysterious path 3 or singapore maps

claims.text: Ludibrium Maze Party Quest and Pirate Party Quest are alternatives to fighting over crowded training maps in the 60s.
claims.say: tired of ks at windraiders? lmpq or ppq works too

claims.text: Charge Piercing Arrow fully: the first monster in the line takes the weakest part of the shot and each monster behind it takes more, so a full charge is needed to kill the front one.
claims.say: fully charge pierce, the front mob takes the weakest hit

claims.text: Bandit at 30: 1 point in Dagger Mastery, then Savage Blow up to 21.
claims.say: bandit 30: 1 mastery, then savage blow to 21

claims.text: Next raise Dagger Mastery to about 19, then finish maxing Savage Blow.
claims.say: then mastery to ~19 and finish savage blow

claims.text: After Savage Blow, put Dagger Booster to 12, max Haste, then finish Dagger Booster.
claims.say: booster to 12, max haste, then finish booster

claims.text: If Dark Sight was left low in 1st job, finish it next, then max Endure and put a single point in Steal by 70.
claims.say: finish dark sight, max endure, 1 steal at 70

claims.text: Endure improves MP recovery as well as HP recovery, which is a reason to max it.
claims.say: endure boosts mp recovery too, worth maxing

claims.text: If you already have about 18 Dark Sight, max Endure first and then put the remaining points into Steal.
claims.say: with 18 dark sight already, max endure then steal

claims.text: A low-DEX Fighter in the early 30s can train on Fire Boars, switching to Sakura Cellions when those maps are not busy.
claims.say: low dex fighter at 33? fire boars, or sakuras off peak

claims.text: A low-DEX warrior entering Monster Carnival at 32 without accuracy gear can barely hit anything, so sort out accuracy first.
claims.say: get some acc before cpq or you'll miss everything

claims.text: A low-DEX warrior covers accuracy with Sniper Pills plus accuracy and DEX gear such as a Brown Bandana and DEX-scrolled Work Gloves.
claims.say: low dex? sniper pills plus acc and dex gear fix your accuracy

claims.text: Upgrade order the author settled on: attack-scrolled Work Gloves first, then a DEX cape, then DEX shoes.
claims.say: att work gloves first, then a dex cape, then dex shoes

claims.text: Base stats cap at 999, which limits how much magic a mage can reach from INT alone.
claims.say: base stats cap at 999

claims.text: Aran's Smart Knockback only lowers the knockback threshold against normal monsters; bosses like Papulatus ignore it, so only very large hits push them back.
claims.say: smart knockback does nothing on bosses like pap

claims.text: Galloperas are weak to holy, and Dawn Warrior's Soul Driver and Soul Charge both carry holy, so the class does its best damage there.
claims.say: galloperas are holy weak, soul driver and soul charge wreck them

claims.text: The author rates Galloperas as the best Dawn Warrior training spot from around level 89 onward.
claims.say: dw 89 and up, galloperas are the best spot

claims.text: Stay on the side you enter, stand on one of the high ledges and keep casting Soul Driver; Galloperas spawning above and below drift into range without chasing them.
claims.say: stand on a ledge and spam soul driver, they walk into range

claims.text: Use Soul Blade to pull stray Galloperas toward you so Soul Driver can catch them.
claims.say: use soul blade to pull them into driver range

claims.text: From the left side, the small platform in the middle lets you hit the whole upper area; kill the Galloperas below first so they cannot knock you off.
claims.say: middle platform hits the top, kill the bottom ones first

claims.text: The right side of the Gallopera map mirrors the left, but mobs there tend to get stuck in the right corner.
claims.say: right side is a mirror, mobs get stuck in the right corner

claims.text: On the ledges you take no touch damage from Galloperas unless you jump into one from below, but their magic attack can still reach you from underneath.
claims.say: on the ledges no touch dmg, but their magic hits from below

claims.text: Bishops sell leech at the Gallopera map too, though it is less crowded than other leech spots.
claims.say: bishops leech at galloperas but it's not too packed

claims.text: A STRless gunslinger who puts all AP into DEX is not recommended, because even a very well-scrolled Maple Gun falls far behind an average Reverse Blindness.
claims.say: dont go strless slinger, maple gun cant keep up

claims.text: Low-STR gunslingers keep STR below their level and are the most popular type, but they need stat gear such as a Zakum Helmet and a Horntail Necklace to meet requirements.
claims.say: low str slinger needs gear like zak helm and ht pendant

claims.text: A normal-STR gunslinger keeps STR equal to their level up to about 120, which covers every gun requirement, and puts the rest into DEX while wearing DEX gear.
claims.say: keep str = level till 120, rest dex

claims.text: Gunslingers attack fast, can hover briefly with Wings, and their gear is cheap, but their damage stays low through 1st and 2nd job and only jumps at 3rd job.
claims.say: slingers are weak till 3rd job, then dmg jumps

claims.text: To become a Pirate at level 10 with at least 20 DEX, go to Nautilus Harbor, board the ship, take the portal under the up arrow, then the far-left portal, and talk to Kyrin.
claims.say: lv10 pirate: 20 dex, see kyrin on the nautilus

claims.text: A future gunslinger can put every AP into DEX until level 10 and worry about STR later.
claims.say: pre-pirate: dump dex, fix str later

claims.text: A pre-gunslinger pirate maxes Double Shot, then Dash, then Bullet Time, and puts the last 11 points into Somersault Kick.
claims.say: pirate 1st job: double shot, dash, bullet time, rest somersault

claims.text: Somersault Kick is the only multi-target attack a 1st job pirate gets, useful for clearing groups of monsters in party quests.
claims.say: somersault kick is your only 1st job mob skill

claims.text: Flash Fist is useless for a pirate who plans to become a gunslinger.
claims.say: skip flash fist if youre going gunslinger

claims.text: Dash gives a burst of speed that helps a gun user keep distance from monsters, and Bullet Time raises accuracy.
claims.say: dash to keep distance, bullet time for accuracy

claims.text: Pirates from 10 to 20 can train on Blue and Red Snails, Pigs, Ribbon Pigs, Green and Blue Mushrooms, Octopuses, Stumps and Slimes.
claims.say: lv10-20 pirate: snails, pigs, mushrooms, stumps, slimes

claims.text: From 20 to 30, pirates can train on Horny Mushrooms, Wild Boars, Evil Eyes, Curse Eyes and Scorpions.
claims.say: lv20-30: horny shrooms, boars, evil eyes, scorpions

claims.text: For the gunslinger 2nd job test, Kyrin sends you to a room of conveyor belts full of octopus monsters; kill them with Double Shot until you have the 15 items, then report back to Kyrin.
claims.say: 2nd job: kill octopuses on the belts for 15 items, back to kyrin

claims.text: Gunslinger 2nd job build: 1 Invisible Shot, max Gun Mastery, max Invisible Shot, 6 Gun Booster, 5 Wings, max Recoil Shot, finish Wings, max Blank Shot, finish Gun Booster, rest into Grenade.
claims.say: slinger: gun mastery, invis shot, booster, wings, recoil, blank

claims.text: Gun Mastery comes first to steady a gunslinger's damage, and platform sniping only works well once Invisible Shot itself is maxed.
claims.say: max gun mastery first, snipe once invis shot is maxed

claims.text: Recoil Shot requires 5 points in Wings before it can be learned.
claims.say: recoil shot needs 5 points in wings

claims.text: In Magatia's C-2 lab, Recoil Shot lets a gunslinger hop between platforms while sniping and rarely take damage, which saves a lot of potions.
claims.say: recoil shot between platforms at c-2 saves a ton of pots

claims.text: Blank Shot is useful while sniping with Invisible Shot, while Grenade is essentially useless beyond fun.
claims.say: blank shot helps sniping, grenade is just for fun

claims.text: Gunslingers from 30 to 50 can do Monster Carnival or train on Lupins and Scorpions, adding Straw Target Dummies, Sand Dwarves and Zombie Lupins in the 40s.
claims.say: lv30-50 slinger: monster carnival, lupins, scorpions, sand dwarves

claims.text: From 50 to 70, gunslingers can do the Ludibrium Maze Party Quest, train on Luster Pixies, or snipe Roids and Neo Huroids in Magatia and Stone and Mixed Golems in the golem dungeon.
claims.say: lv50-70: lmpq, or snipe roids, neo huroids, golems

claims.text: At 70 a gunslinger visits Pedro in El Nath for 3rd job, which works like other 3rd jobs: a fight with a clone of the 1st job instructor and a quiz, with the Door of Dimension in Cave of Evil Eye III.
claims.say: 3rd job: pedro in el nath, door in cave of evil eye iii

claims.text: As an Outlaw, Burst Fire becomes the main single-target attack and damage rises sharply.
claims.say: outlaw dmg finally jumps, burst fire is your main attack

claims.text: Ice Splitter freezes and Flamethrower burns; their damage is enhanced by carrying Glaze Capsules and Blaze Capsules respectively.
claims.say: bring glaze and blaze capsules for ice splitter and flamethrower

claims.text: A typical Outlaw build for Jr. Newtie sniping: max Burst Fire, 21 Octopus, 21 Ice Splitter, finish Octopus, max Gaviota, finish Ice Splitter, 11 Flamethrower, then max Homing Beacon.
claims.say: outlaw: burst fire, octopus, ice splitter, gaviota, then homing

claims.text: A goby-focused Outlaw maxes Ice Splitter and puts 26 into Flamethrower right after Burst Fire, stuns with Blank Shot, then alternates Ice Splitter and Flamethrower to hit several gobies.
claims.say: goby outlaw: max ice splitter, 26 flamethrower, blank shot stun

claims.text: From 90, Outlaws can add Gobies and Bone Fish, Nest Golems from 100, and Skelegons and Skelosauruses only with an HP wash or extra HP.
claims.say: 90+: gobies, bone fish; 100+: nest golems; skeles need hp

claims.text: A Dark Knight around level 140 who mostly solos can put points into Rush after Beholder and Berserk; the longer push lets you gather mobs and move across maps faster.
claims.say: solo dk can max rush, longer push gathers mobs faster

claims.text: Extra Maple Warrior levels only help training once they lower how many hits a kill takes; if your hits to kill stay the same, spend SP elsewhere first.
claims.say: mw only matters once it cuts your hits to kill

claims.text: A Dark Knight with lots of washed HP uses few potions at Skelegons and can take a hit while staying in Berserk, so Achilles can wait while you train.
claims.say: washed dk barely pots and stays zerked, achilles can wait

claims.text: When choosing what to level next, favor skills that raise exp gain over skills that only save potion money, since mesos buy potions but not exp.
claims.say: put sp into exp gain first, pots are just mesos

claims.text: If you make a Nisrock, the Dark Nisrock is recommended for its faster attack speed.
claims.say: make the dark nisrock, it attacks faster

claims.text: Reverse equipment such as Reverse Engaw, Evernew, Presto and Rontano needs level 120 or more, so leave it out of your plans if you won't pass 120 soon.
claims.say: reverse gear is 120+, don't plan on it before then

claims.text: Top Bowman overall choices are a Red Arzuna made with basic STR/DEX gems and then 30% scrolls, or a Reverse Evernew made with a stimulator, advanced STR/DEX gems and a dark crystal.
claims.say: best overalls: red arzuna or reverse evernew

claims.text: A Reverse Presto becomes untradeable once equipped, unlike gloves such as Stormcaster Gloves that you can sell when you upgrade.
claims.say: reverse presto locks once worn, other gloves you can resell

claims.text: With good Maker gems, level-ups and scrolling, a Reverse Presto can end up better than Stormcaster Gloves, but you will likely have to scroll it yourself.
claims.say: a well made reverse presto can beat scg

claims.text: Shoe jump scrolls add only 1 DEX, so favour shoes with strong clean stats; a well-made Reverse Rontano can equal a Facestompers with 4-5 attack.
claims.say: shoe scrolls give tiny dex, get shoes with good base stats

claims.text: A Bowman's cape should be a Pink Adventurer Cape; its attack is worth far more than the stats other capes give.
claims.say: pac is the cape, its att beats extra stats

claims.text: Leaving STR at base until you reach your gearing level makes a Bowman a bit stronger, and STR for gear requirements can be planned later.
claims.say: keep str at base for now, add it for gear later

claims.text: You can solo Papulatus once you have enough HP to survive its bomb and can land steady big hits; classes with lots of HP get there earlier.
claims.say: solo pap once you can survive a bomb and hit hard

claims.text: An unwashed Marksman had about 3.5k HP at 140; HP gear pushing that near 4k was enough to live through Papulatus's bombs.
claims.say: around 4k hp is enough to live through pap's bombs

claims.text: Blaze Wizards in their 70s can train on the Vikerolas in Malaysia's Fantasy Theme Park, but the spread-out spawn over platforms makes it awkward and the exp trails Blue Kentaurus.
claims.say: vikerolas are ok but blue kents give better exp at 7x

claims.text: The Fantasy Theme Park monsters use troublesome skills, so bring strong recovery potions such as Elixirs rather than cheap ones.
claims.say: bring elixirs for theme park, cheap pots wont cut it

claims.text: Using Fire Strike on Blue Kentaurus burns through a lot of potions; Fantasy Theme Park costs somewhat less but is still heavy on potions.
claims.say: striking kents eats pots, theme park a bit less

claims.text: Sacrifice ignores monster defense, but it does not get through a monster's weapon-attack cancel, so it is no answer to that buff.
claims.say: sacrifice ignores def but won't hit through weapon cancel

claims.text: Because Sacrifice drains your own HP, Dark Knights can use it to drop into Berserk range; at 1 HP it costs nothing more.
claims.say: sacrifice can drop your hp into berserk range

claims.text: Double Swing has no hotkey of its own; you perform it by pressing the attack key twice in quick succession.
claims.say: double swing is just tapping attack twice, no hotkey

claims.text: Combat Step dashes you a short distance when you tap a direction arrow twice; it needs Double Swing at level 5 and cannot be used while jumping.
claims.say: combat step = double tap an arrow, not usable midair

claims.text: Polearm Booster becomes available once Combat Step reaches level 5.
claims.say: polearm booster unlocks at combat step 5

claims.text: Combo Ability requires Double Swing level 10 and boosts your stats each time the combo counter climbs by another 10.
claims.say: combo ability needs double swing 10, buffs you per 10 combo

claims.text: Triple Swing needs Double Swing at level 20 and comes out when you press attack three times in a row.
claims.say: triple swing = attack three times, needs double swing 20

claims.text: Polearm Mastery needs Triple Swing level 3 and adds mastery and accuracy, but only while a polearm is equipped.
claims.say: polearm mastery needs triple swing 3, polearm only

claims.text: Final Charge pushes enemies forward; it needs Triple Swing level 20 and is used straight after Triple Swing by pressing forward plus attack.
claims.say: final charge: right after triple swing hit forward + attack

claims.text: Body Pressure is a short buff that makes monsters you run into take damage.
claims.say: body pressure lets you hurt mobs just by walking into them

claims.text: Combo Critical needs Combo Ability level 10 and adds critical rate and damage for every 10 combo you build.
claims.say: combo critical needs combo ability 10, more crits per 10 combo

claims.text: Full Swing is a hidden upgrade split into two parts that strengthens both Double Swing and Triple Swing.
claims.say: full swing upgrades both double and triple swing

claims.text: Snow Charge gives your polearm the ice element for a set time and slows the monsters you hit.
claims.say: snow charge makes your polearm ice and slows what you hit

claims.text: High Mastery requires Polearm Mastery level 20 and raises polearm mastery and attack further.
claims.say: high mastery needs polearm mastery 20

claims.text: High Defense is a passive that permanently lowers the damage you take from attacks.
claims.say: high defense is a passive that cuts damage taken

claims.text: Freeze Standing is the Aran fourth job stance that keeps you from being knocked back.
claims.say: freeze standing stops knockback, like power stance

claims.text: Arans also get Maple Warrior, which raises the whole party's stats, and Hero's Will in fourth job.
claims.say: arans get maple warrior and hero's will at 4th job

claims.text: One Aran end state for 1st job: Combo Ability 10, Combat Step 15, Double Swing 20 and Polearm Booster 16, with Booster finished later.
claims.say: 1st job: combo ability 10, double swing 20, step 15, booster 16

claims.text: Players disagree on Rolling Spin: some say it pushes monsters away to both sides, others say it stuns them.
claims.say: people argue if rolling spin pushes or stuns

claims.text: Boss parties often bring an Aran mainly for Combo Barrier, so keep it active the whole fight.
claims.say: boss parties want your combo barrier, keep it up

claims.text: Arans commonly train by using Final Charge to pull a large group of monsters together, then wiping the group and repeating.
claims.say: final charge to gather a big mob, kill it, repeat

claims.text: Final Charge plays somewhat like a warrior's Rush, which is why some Arans put extra points into it.
claims.say: final charge is like rush, worth extra points

claims.text: Smart Knockback, Combo Drain and Body Pressure are nice to keep up, but letting them drop does not lower your damage output.
claims.say: smart kb, drain and body pressure are nice but not dps

claims.text: Maker starts at skill level 1 and goes up through later quests at character level 75 and 105; level 1 forges gear for levels 50-70, level 2 up to 100, level 3 up to 120.
claims.say: maker lv1 makes 50-70 gear, lv2 up to 100, lv3 up to 120

claims.text: You can forge an item once you are within 5 levels of its level requirement, so a level 70 weapon can be made from level 65.
claims.say: you can make gear up to 5 levels above your level

claims.text: Maker can't make Maple weapons, all-class items such as earrings and capes, or gachapon-only gear; gear below level 50 is simply bought from shops.
claims.say: maker can't do maple weapons, capes, earrings or gach gear

claims.text: Maker forges your class's overalls, tops, bottoms, shoes, gloves and hats plus both weapon types your class uses, and higher level items need far more materials.
claims.say: maker makes your class's armor and both weapon types

claims.text: Most Maker armor recipes need Magic Powder in the item's colour; black is wanted by nearly every class and is scarcer, pirates use a lot of brown, and weapons rarely need any.
claims.say: black magic powder is in demand, pirates burn brown

claims.text: Putting 100 of one monster's etc drops through Maker makes a Monster Crystal; only etcs from monsters above level 30 count, and the crystal's grade follows the monster's level.
claims.say: 100 etcs from one mob make a monster crystal

claims.text: Etcs from level 31-50 monsters make Basic Monster Crystal 1, 51-60 Basic 2, 61-70 Basic 3; 71-80, 81-90 and 91-100 give Intermediate 1, 2 and 3; 101-110, 111-120 and 121 up give Advanced 1, 2 and 3.
claims.say: lv31-50 mob etcs give basic crystal 1, higher mobs better

claims.text: As an example, 100 Stone Golem Rubbles become a Basic Monster Crystal 2.
claims.say: 100 stone golem rubbles = one basic monster crystal 2

claims.text: Maker works anywhere, so when your etc tab fills while training you can stand somewhere safe and turn hundreds of etcs into a few crystals.
claims.say: etc tab full? use maker on the spot to make crystals

claims.text: Maker gem effects: Diamond adds weapon attack and Sapphire magic attack, both on weapons only; Garnet adds accuracy, Opal avoid, Aquamarine jump, Amethyst speed, Topaz HP and Emerald MP.
claims.say: diamond gives watk, sapphire matk, both weapon only

claims.text: Power Crystal adds STR, DEX Crystal DEX, Wisdom Crystal INT and LUK Crystal LUK, more at higher grades; Black Crystal and Dark Crystal add a random stat, Dark Crystal by a larger amount.
claims.say: stat crystals add str dex int luk, dark crystal is random

claims.text: Each Maker level allows one more gem, the second only on items level 75 and up, and you can't repeat a gem type, so a weapon tops out at +3 attack over average without a stimulator.
claims.say: one of each gem type only, so max +3 watk from a diamond

claims.text: Gems added in Maker don't use upgrade slots and can't make the forge fail, so you can give gear a stat it normally lacks, like LUK on shoes, and then Chaos Scroll it.
claims.say: add a stat with a maker gem, then chaos scroll it

claims.text: Skip stimulators when forging: the chance of losing the item outweighs the extra stats they might give.
claims.say: skip stimulators, not worth the fail risk

claims.text: Maker can't refine ores, so you still need a town refiner, and you can't add gems to an item you already own.
claims.say: maker can't refine ores or add gems to old gear

claims.text: Graded gems no longer count as the plain gem, so keep ungraded ones for quests that ask for gems.
claims.say: keep some ungraded gems, quests won't take graded ones

claims.text: Level 120 Maker recipes need a new ore that every Temple of Time monster drops.
claims.say: temple of time mobs drop the ore for lv120 maker gear

claims.text: The Leafre forging NPCs keep their old recipes with Dragon Scales and Dragon Spirit; their only edge over Maker is that they have no level requirement.
claims.say: leafre forgers have no level req but need dragon scales

claims.text: Weapons cost far more than armor in Maker: a level 50 knuckle took 20 Basic Monster Crystal 1, about 2,000 etc items, against 10 crystals for an overall, and recipes ask 5 of their powder colour.
claims.say: maker weapons cost way more crystals than armor

claims.text: Maker shines most on armor: putting high-grade main-stat and secondary-stat crystals on a top and bottom gives clean pieces well above average before any scrolling.
claims.say: maker armor with stat crystals beats average gear

claims.text: The best gem plan is one high-grade Diamond plus one high-grade main-stat crystal; the third slot adds little because the secondary stat mostly just meets equip requirements.
claims.say: best combo: one high diamond and one high main stat crystal

claims.text: Forged items can come out a point off average in defense even without a stimulator, so there is a small random factor.
claims.say: maker gear can roll a point off average, even no stim

claims.text: Truckers are one of the best places to train from level 50 to 60.
claims.say: 50-60? truckers are about the best spot

claims.text: On the Trucker map, run a figure-8 route through the floors: bottom, then middle, then top, then middle again, switching direction on each floor.
claims.say: at truckers do a figure 8: bottom, mid, top, mid and repeat

claims.text: Mysterious Path 3 gives very good exp around level 50 to 60.
claims.say: mp3 is great exp around 50-60

claims.text: Mu Lung Dojo is not a good exp source; it is only worth running for the belts.
claims.say: dojo isn't for exp, only do it for the belts

claims.text: Finishing a Pink Adventurer Cape with 60% scrolls is a worthwhile upgrade for a level 50s character with spare mesos.
claims.say: got mesos? finish scrolling your pac with 60%s

claims.text: Training the Maker skill lets you craft better equipment before you even start scrolling it.
claims.say: level maker, you can make better gear before scrolling

claims.text: For an Aran, the best training maps have big packs of mobs, a good exp return for the HP it takes to kill them, and a small or easy-to-cross layout so the combo counter stays up.
claims.say: aran maps: big mob packs, good exp per hp, small easy layout

claims.text: A first-job Aran can grind in Ant Tunnel I.
claims.say: 1st job aran? ant tunnel 1 works

claims.text: The Aran job quests give enough exp to cover the levels you would otherwise spend at Caution Falling Down, with Ant Tunnel I to fill any gap.
claims.say: aran quests carry 1st job, no need to sit at caution falling down

claims.text: Monster Carnival is a training option once an Aran has 2nd job.
claims.say: 2nd job aran can hit monster carnival

claims.text: Truckers are a 2nd job Aran training option.
claims.say: truckers work for a 2nd job aran

claims.text: The Roids on the Critical Error map are a 2nd job Aran option.
claims.say: roids at critical error are ok for 2nd job aran

claims.text: Forest of Evil I and Forest of Golem are further 2nd job Aran training spots.
claims.say: forest of evil 1 or forest of golem for 2nd job aran

claims.text: Mysterious Path 3 works for a 2nd job Aran, but it is a large map, which makes keeping the combo counter going harder.
claims.say: mp3 is ok for aran but it's big, combo keeps dropping

claims.text: Icy Cold Field is a 3rd job Aran spot, though it is also on the big side for holding a combo.
claims.say: icy cold field works at 3rd job, kinda big for combo

claims.text: Pillage of Treasure Island holds only Captains and is a 3rd job Aran option.
claims.say: pillage of treasure island is all captains, fine at 3rd job

claims.text: The monsters at Longest Ride on ByeBye Station give poor exp for the HP they have, but their drops are good.
claims.say: longest ride mobs: meh exp for their hp, nice drops though

claims.text: Encounter with the Buddha is another 3rd job Aran training map.
claims.say: encounter with the buddha is a 3rd job aran spot too

claims.text: Skelegons are a late 3rd job Aran target.
claims.say: skelegons work for a late 3rd job aran

claims.text: Tornado Corridor is a poor fit for an Aran: without Hyper Body it lacks the HP to survive the hard-hitting Guardians there.
claims.say: aran skip tornado corridor, no hyper body = not enough hp

claims.text: A permanent Beginner with a reliable group of friends can level through party quests, since PQ groups care more about knowing the quest than about damage.
claims.say: perma beginners can level via pqs if friends help

claims.text: Pirate Party Quest stays open to characters up to level 100, so it can carry you a long way.
claims.say: pirate pq goes up to level 100

claims.text: Clerics are valued members in Ludibrium Party Quest groups.
claims.say: clerics are welcome in ludi pq

claims.text: Repeating Ludibrium Party Quest can take a character up into the high 40s.
claims.say: you can ludi pq into the high 40s

claims.text: A tested Bandit 2nd job order: 1 point in Dagger Mastery at 30, then almost all SP into Savage Blow, finishing it around level 41 with a couple more Mastery points mixed in.
claims.say: bandit 2nd job: 1 mastery at 30 then pump savage blow to max

claims.text: Once Savage Blow is maxed, either finish Dagger Mastery or pick up some Dagger Booster along the way.
claims.say: after savage blow, max mastery or grab booster

claims.text: Dagger Booster only speeds up Savage Blow, not Double Stab, so there is no point taking it before Savage Blow has a decent level.
claims.say: booster only helps savage blow, get it after sb is decent

claims.text: Maxing the main attack first gets you one-hitting your training monsters sooner, which matters more at these levels than attacking slightly faster.
claims.say: max your main attack first so you one-hit mobs sooner

claims.text: As a Bishop at Horntail, keep healing and rebuffing through the preliminary heads, then stay near the wall in the main fight while spamming Heal and buffs.
claims.say: bishop at ht: heal and buff, hug the wall on the body

claims.text: After the tail and legs die, a Horntail Bishop moves under the right hand to heal and Dispel curses; a seduce healer keeps healing seduced players until it wears off.
claims.say: after tail and legs, bishop goes to the hand to heal and dispel

claims.text: Do not attack Horntail's hands until both the tail and legs are dead; the tail and legs also carry very heavy touch damage.
claims.say: dont hit ht hands until tail and legs are down

claims.text: Horntail's tail slams and poisons, and its legs stomp to stun.
claims.say: ht tail slams and poisons, legs stomp to stun

claims.text: Horntail's right hand casts darkness, weakness, curse and seal, drains MP and seduces; the left hand drains MP, seduces and dispels at low HP.
claims.say: ht hands seduce and drain mp, left hand dispels when low

claims.text: Horntail's heads summon wyverns, cast magic, can drop you to 1 HP and 1 MP and cancel weapon and magic attack buffs; the middle head also dispels at low HP.
claims.say: ht heads summon wyverns, can 1/1 you and cancel att buffs

claims.text: A future Bandit can stop Double Stab around 18 and max Dark Sight, since Savage Blow becomes the main attack after 2nd job.
claims.say: stop double stab at 18 and max dark sight, savage blow takes over

claims.text: Zakum's last body drops the level 10 mastery books for the Aran skills Final Blow, Combo Barrier, High Defense and Combo Tempest.
claims.say: zakum drops the aran 10 books: final blow, barrier, hi def, tempest

claims.text: The Final Blow 20 mastery book for Arans comes from Pianus and from Bone Fish.
claims.say: final blow 20 book drops from pianus or bone fish

claims.text: The Final Blow 30 mastery book for Arans comes from Horntail and from Chief Qualm Guardians in Temple of Time.
claims.say: final blow 30 book: horntail or chief qualm guardian

claims.text: The Combo Barrier 20 mastery book for Arans drops from Qualm Monk Trainees and from Lyka.
claims.say: combo barrier 20 book: qualm monk trainee or lyka

claims.text: The Combo Barrier 30 mastery book for Arans drops from Horntail and from Chief Oblivion Guardians.
claims.say: combo barrier 30 book: horntail or chief oblivion guardian

claims.text: The High Defense 20 mastery book for Arans drops from Chief Memory Guardians and from Dodo.
claims.say: high defense 20 book: chief memory guardian or dodo

claims.text: The High Defense 30 mastery book for Arans drops from Green Cornians and from Lyka.
claims.say: high defense 30 book: green cornians or lyka

claims.text: The High Mastery 20 mastery book for Arans drops from Dark Wyverns and from Griffey.
claims.say: high mastery 20 book: dark wyverns or griffey

claims.text: The High Mastery 30 mastery book for Arans drops from Papulatus and from Memory Monks.
claims.say: high mastery 30 book: papulatus or memory monks

claims.text: The Freeze Standing 20 mastery book for Arans drops from Manon and from Skelosaurus.
claims.say: freeze standing 20 book: manon or skelosaurus

claims.text: The Freeze Standing 30 mastery book for Arans drops from Memory Monk Trainees and from Lilynouch.
claims.say: freeze standing 30 book: memory monk trainees or lilynouch

claims.text: The Combo Tempest 20 mastery book for Arans drops from Qualm Guardians and from Lilynouch.
claims.say: combo tempest 20 book: qualm guardians or lilynouch

claims.text: The Combo Tempest 30 mastery book for Arans drops from Horntail and from Oblivion Guardians.
claims.say: combo tempest 30 book: horntail or oblivion guardians

claims.text: Horntail takes longer to learn than Zakum and eats a lot of supplies; any sensible player can lead a run, but every member has to know their part because one careless person can wreck it.
claims.say: ht is harder than zak, everyone has to know their job or it fails

claims.text: Double Swing and Triple Swing are the second and third presses of the Aran attack chain, which opens with a normal attack.
claims.say: double and triple swing are the 2nd and 3rd hits of the chain

claims.text: Full Swing does not add to Double Swing and Triple Swing; it swaps in its own damage values and makes the Double Swing step hit twice.
claims.say: full swing replaces swing dmg, not adds, and doubles the 2nd hit

claims.text: Rangers normally max Strafe, Arrow Rain and Puppet.
claims.say: rangers max strafe, arrow rain and puppet

claims.text: Common Ranger advice is to leave Inferno at 1 for luring since Arrow Bomb hits harder on everything except fire-weak monsters; raise Inferno to about 16 if 1 is not enough.
claims.say: leave inferno at 1 for luring unless you need more

claims.text: For a Ranger planning to train at Typhons: max Arrow Rain, then Strafe, then Silver Hawk, then Puppet, Mortal Blow and Thrust.
claims.say: ranger order: rain, strafe, hawk, puppet, mortal blow, thrust

claims.text: Putting Thrust ahead of Mortal Blow late in the Ranger build also works fine.
claims.say: thrust before mortal blow works too

claims.text: After Overswing, pour points into High Mastery for its extra mastery and weapon attack, finishing it off later.
claims.say: after overswing pump high mastery for mastery and att

claims.text: Players disagree on whether Freeze Standing or Final Blow comes next; most suggest Freeze Standing, while the author sees less need for it because Smart Knockback keeps mobs from shoving you around.
claims.say: freeze standing vs final blow next is debated, most say standing

claims.text: The author maxes Combo Barrier ahead of High Defense, with bossing and party training in mind.
claims.say: combo barrier before high defense for bossing

claims.text: One early point in Final Blow is enough to finish off weakened mobs from a distance; max it later for better mobbing damage.
claims.say: 1 in final blow early, max it later for mobbing

claims.text: Combo Tempest is left until late and maxed before Maple Warrior, which the build puts last.
claims.say: combo tempest late, then maple warrior last

claims.text: In 4th job, Smart Knockback stops most mobs from getting attacks off; kill quickly and you rarely get hit, and Combo Drain covers the hits that do land.
claims.say: smart knockback stops mobs hitting you, drain for the rest

claims.text: Arans can keep Skelegons knocked back so they never get to attack, sparing them the touch damage other warriors take there.
claims.say: arans can kb skelegons so they never get to attack

claims.text: Body Pressure damages monsters you touch and seals their physical attacks; damage from your polearm attacks can also put them into that sealed state.
claims.say: body pressure seals mobs so they can't hit you physically

claims.text: A level 20-30 Aran can try the mini dungeon full of Zombie Mushrooms and Horny Mushrooms; the mobs group up well enough to build combo quickly.
claims.say: aran 20-30: zombie/horny shroom mini dungeon builds combo

claims.text: Training on Zombie Mushrooms and Horny Mushrooms can pay for itself, since they can drop Chaos Scrolls that sell well.
claims.say: zombie and horny shrooms can drop chaos scrolls, nice money

claims.text: Auto-assign gives Arans warrior-style STR and DEX but not the best split; about 30-40 AP in DEX is enough, 60 at the very most, and pushing DEX to 80 is wasted.
claims.say: aran only needs 30-40 dex, maybe 60, never 80

claims.text: The Romeo and Juliet Party Quest needs a party of four, all between level 71 and 85.
claims.say: magatia pq is 4 people, lv 71 to 85

claims.text: Bring a thief with maxed Haste (or anyone with 120% jump) and a magician with maxed Teleport, since stage 4 has a room for each; Haste makes the thief room much easier.
claims.say: bring a max haste thief and a max teleport mage

claims.text: Someone who can freeze or stun monsters makes it much easier to keep Romeo or Juliet alive during the boss stage.
claims.say: bring a freezer or stunner to protect romeo

claims.text: Start from the hidden room of the Zenumist or Alcadno Society in Magatia: Zenumist's is the doorway at the top right, Alcadno's the doorway above Maed. Zenumist runs start with Romeo, Alcadno runs with Juliet.
claims.say: start from the hidden room in zenumist or alcadno

claims.text: Stage 1 has no monsters: search the piles of books by standing right on top of them and clicking. A spot may give mesos, exp, nothing, the letter, or the switch that opens the portal beside the NPC.
claims.say: stage 1: stand on the book piles and click them

claims.text: The partner's letter found in stage 1 is delivered in stage 4 by talking to Romeo or Juliet while holding it; delivering it is needed to face Angry Frankenroid.
claims.say: give the letter to romeo/juliet in stage 4

claims.text: Stage 2 is dark except right around your character: kill every Cyti and Homun, then take the portal on the right.
claims.say: stage 2: kill everything in the dark, go right

claims.text: In stage 3 Homunculus drop Suspicious Liquid, which you drop onto the three beakers. Each person can hold only one and the beakers leak, so pile liquids beside a beaker and pour them in together.
claims.say: stage 3: stockpile liquids, fill beakers together

claims.text: In stage 4 Neo Huroids sometimes drop key cards that open the left and right doors briefly. Cards don't work from inside, so a teammate has to drop one outside to let the runner back out.
claims.say: stage 4: keep a key card ready for each door

claims.text: The door rooms drain HP every few seconds, so move fast. The left room is a dark jump course of moving platforms for the thief, who breaks the boxes along the top row to find the experiment documents.
claims.say: thief room: break the top row boxes for the docs

claims.text: The right room is for the magician: Teleport up and to the right while breaking boxes for the documents, then Teleport back down to the door at the bottom left.
claims.say: mage room: teleport up right, break boxes, come back

claims.text: Once both sets of documents are given to Romeo or Juliet, the Neo Huroids vanish and the door to stage 5 opens.
claims.say: hand both docs to romeo/juliet to open stage 5

claims.text: In stage 5, kill the Reinforced Iron Mutae and Reinforced Mithril Mutae, then the party leader clicks the book switch on the platform.
claims.say: stage 5: kill the mutaes, leader hits the switch

claims.text: For Angry Frankenroid, in stage 5 have one member edge forward until Yulete just comes into view and click him; if he mumbles, Angry Frankenroid will appear. Going too far spawns the monsters and normal Frankenroid.
claims.say: creep in slowly and click yulete for angry frank

claims.text: Beating Angry Frankenroid lets the leader spare Yulete, which unlocks Yulete's Lab, where the quests toward the Horus' Eye pendant begin.
claims.say: beat angry frank to unlock yulete's lab

claims.text: Stage 6 gives each member a room of 10 rows with 4 platforms each; one per row takes you up, the rest drop you to the bottom. Your correct platform is wrong for the others, so share results; it reshuffles every run.
claims.say: stage 6: tell your party which platforms worked

claims.text: After stage 6 you gather at Entrance to Center Lab; wait for everyone before summoning the boss, and assign one member to guard Romeo or Juliet, since Neo Huroids keep spawning on their platform.
claims.say: assign someone to guard romeo/juliet at the boss

claims.text: When everyone is buffed, the party leader clicks Yulete in the middle of the lab to summon Frankenroid, who arrives with reinforced mutaes.
claims.say: leader clicks yulete to start the boss

claims.text: Frankenroid casts darkness, so carry Eyedrops; he can also send players back to Entrance to Center Lab, spreads a poison cloud, stomps, and has heavy touch damage.
claims.say: bring eyedrops for frankenroid's darkness

claims.text: A party of level 70s with plenty of potions can beat Frankenroid if they stay alert, and having a Priest along helps.
claims.say: a 7x party can kill frank with enough pots

claims.text: If Romeo or Juliet dies you still get the boss kill exp, but no bonus exp and no prize at the end.
claims.say: if romeo/juliet dies you get no prize

claims.text: To finish, talk to the NPC who started the run, walk to Yulete at the end of Traces of Yulete, then collect a Zenumist or Alcadno marble (by starting side) plus a random scroll or potion prize.
claims.say: finish by talking to yulete, then get your marble

claims.text: After Yulete's quests, 35 of each marble make the Horus' Eye pendant, which gives +3 to every stat and 60 HP and MP.
claims.say: 35 of each marble makes horus' eye, +3 all stats

claims.text: Yulete turns 10 marbles of either kind into a Rock of Wisdom, which is what you use to scroll the Horus' Eye.
claims.say: yulete makes rock of wisdom from 10 marbles

claims.text: End prizes are random: earrings, 10%, 60% or 70% scrolls such as wand magic attack or cape INT, or stacks of Blue Potions, White Potions, Elixirs or Power Elixirs.
claims.say: prizes are scrolls, earrings or pot stacks

claims.text: Horntail runs often give one bishop the job of rescuing players caught by seduce, which puts that bishop in reach of tail hits, so surviving one makes the role easier.
claims.say: ht runs need a seduce bishop who can tank a tail hit

claims.text: Higher weapon defense cuts the damage taken from Horntail's tail, and Bless plus defensive pendants are the ways a bishop raises it.
claims.say: stack weapon def and bless to live through ht tail hits

claims.text: Aran first job: bank SP from about level 18 to put 15 into Polearm Booster around 22, then end at 30 with Double Swing 20, Combat Step 15, Combo Ability 10 and Booster 16.
claims.say: aran 1st job: get 15 booster early, then double swing and step

claims.text: The order of Double Swing and Combat Step in first job is flexible; early Combat Step helps with getting around, and Combo Ability can wait because its bonus before second job is minor.
claims.say: 1st job order is flexible, combo ability can wait

claims.text: Aran second job: 1 in Triple Swing, raise Polearm Mastery, save SP to max Combo Smash in one go around 45, then Combo Drain, finish Triple Swing, and put Body Pressure and Final Charge last.
claims.say: 2nd job aran: mastery, save sp for combo smash, then drain

claims.text: Body Pressure together with Combo Drain cuts potion use a lot; on maps like Mysterious Path 3 only magic attacks really hurt you, so some players raise Body Pressure right after early Combo Drain.
claims.say: body pressure plus combo drain saves tons of pots

claims.text: With enough Smart Knockback, normal hits keep mobs like Windraiders knocked back, which together with Combo Drain saves a lot of potions.
claims.say: skb so windraiders stay knocked back, saves pots with drain

claims.text: Don't rush to Galloperas: around level 86-87 is a safe time unless your accuracy and attack gear are good, and bring at least 12 Smart Knockback.
claims.say: galloperas around 86-87 with 12+ skb unless your gear is good

claims.text: INT worn on gear increases the MP gained each time you put AP into MP, which is what MP washing depends on.
claims.say: wear int gear when adding ap to mp, you get more mp per point

claims.text: Thieves and bowmen need around 160 INT to gain enough MP from AP to do two AP resets per level instead of one.
claims.say: thieves and archers need about 160 int to double wash

claims.text: Pirates need far more INT than thieves or bowmen to double wash, around 340 INT.
claims.say: pirates need way more int to double wash, like 340

claims.text: A Chief Bandit can kill Bigfoot with Meso Explosion while a Marauder keeps knocking it back, though it is risky and deaths are likely.
claims.say: cb can bomb bigfoot if a marauder keeps it knocked back

claims.text: Bombing Bigfoot works best right after maxing Meso Explosion; below max it costs far more mesos and runs past 20 minutes, so it suits neither poor players nor Shadowers.
claims.say: bomb bigfoot with maxed me, else it eats mesos and time

claims.text: Chief Bandits commonly bomb Headless Horseman with Meso Explosion for exp.
claims.say: cbs bomb headless horseman with me for exp

claims.text: Final Attack adds little to a Page's mobbing and feels weak at low levels, so one plan is to max Power Guard first and then put points into Final Attack all at once.
claims.say: max power guard first, then fa in one go

claims.text: Charged Blow needs an elemental charge active, and keeping it going by recharging costs a lot of MP and time spent rebuffing.
claims.say: charged blow eats mp since you keep recharging

claims.text: Blunt weapons give a Paladin strong damage, but players who boss often see faster clear times from sword Paladins.
claims.say: bw pally hits hard but sword ones clear bosses faster

claims.text: Elemental weakness multipliers and elemental charge multipliers are applied to your damage before the monster's defense is subtracted.
claims.say: element and charge bonuses apply before mob defense

claims.text: Combo Attack's damage bonus is counted before the monster's defense is taken off, in the same step as elemental charges.
claims.say: combo attack bonus counts before mob defense

claims.text: Berserk's damage bonus appears to be applied after defense is subtracted, though some Dark Knights insist it comes before.
claims.say: berserk seems to apply after defense, not everyone agrees

claims.text: Panic and Coma multiply their own skill damage by an orb multiplier and by the Combo Attack bonus, so they hit hardest when used once you hold five or more orbs.
claims.say: use panic or coma once you have 5+ orbs

claims.text: When Final Attack triggers off Slash Blast on several monsters, its damage is split so each further target takes about a third of the previous one, leaving most of it on the first target.
claims.say: final attack off slash blast mostly hits the first mob

claims.text: To check whether a damage buff applies before or after defense, track your highest and lowest hits over many attacks with and without it; a gain bigger than the buff's multiplier means it applies before defense.
claims.say: test buffs by comparing max hits over lots of attacks

claims.text: In Pink Bean's final stage, warriors and buccaneers should keep it pinned in a corner so the middle beam of its Genesis falls on the small platform, giving ranged attackers a predictable pattern to dodge.
claims.say: keep pink bean pinned in the corner so genesis is easy to dodge

claims.text: Ranged classes can do Pink Bean's final stage without HP washing by attacking from near their maximum range, ducking under Genesis and moving away when Big Bang comes.
claims.say: at pink bean duck under genesis and run from big bang

claims.text: You can read Pink Bean's next move from its arms: arms swinging around in circles signal Big Bang, arms thrown upward signal Genesis or Seduce.
claims.say: pb arms spinning means big bang, arms up means genesis or seduce

claims.text: Pink Bean's damage reflect hits hard enough to kill ranged characters, so they should stop attacking while it is up; warriors with Hyper Body can absorb it and potion back.
claims.say: stop attacking pb during reflect unless you're a hb warrior

claims.text: A Corsair can duck while riding Battleship, and ducking lets Pink Bean's Genesis beam miss.
claims.say: corsairs can duck in battleship to dodge pb's genesis

claims.text: Buccaneers can chain the invincibility frames of Corkscrew Blow and Barrage to dodge Pink Bean's Big Bang, though other players point out this is not full invincibility.
claims.say: bucs can chain corkscrew and barrage i-frames vs big bang

claims.text: Lightning attacks like an Ice/Lightning Arch Mage's Chain Lightning do well on Pink Bean's final stage, and a Fire/Poison Arch Mage's Paralyze tested about as strong.
claims.say: chain lightning and paralyze both hit pink bean hard

claims.text: The Mini Beans that spawn during the Pink Bean fight are weak to both fire and ice.
claims.say: mini beans at pink bean are weak to fire and ice

claims.text: Wheel of Destiny revives you on the left side of Pink Bean's map, so keeping the boss on the right side lets revived players rejoin safely.
claims.say: keep pb on the right, wheel of destiny puts you on the left

claims.text: Standing on the platforms helps protect against Pink Bean's Seduce, which forces you to jump to the left.
claims.say: stand on the platforms at pb to stay safer from seduce

claims.text: A monster only turns to face the player knocking it back when it is not in the middle of an attack; mid-attack it just gets pushed and keeps facing the same way.
claims.say: mobs only turn toward a knockback if they aren't mid attack

claims.text: A monster that is hit and aggroed by a player who does not knock it back keeps facing that player for a while, even while someone else keeps knocking it back.
claims.say: a mob keeps facing whoever aggroed it, even if others knock it back

claims.text: Bowmasters reach slightly farther than Night Lords, which is why a Bowmaster can hit the top Gargoyle in Guild Party Quest without jumping off its platform.
claims.say: bms outrange nls, they hit the top gpq gargoyle without jumping

claims.text: Warriors at Pink Bean can avoid touch damage without HP washing by never standing on top of it and attacking from the far edge of a wide skill's reach.
claims.say: warriors, don't hug pb, hit it from the edge of your range

claims.text: Whether Pink Bean's final stage is practical without HP washing is disputed: critics say a full 30-person party rarely plays precisely enough for such a small margin of error.
claims.say: no-wash pink bean is possible but leaves almost no room for error

claims.text: To hold Pink Bean facing one way, one idea is a Buccaneer knocking it back with Barrage from one side, a warrior using Rush from the other, and an Arch Mage casting Slow.
claims.say: use barrage knockback, rush and slow to keep pb facing one way

claims.text: Heroes usually max Brandish, Advanced Combo Attack and Power Stance first in 4th job.
claims.say: hero: brandish, advanced combo, stance first

claims.text: After Power Stance, Heroes differ on Maple Warrior, Rush, Achilles or Guardian; one suggested order is Brandish, Advanced Combo, Stance, Achilles, then Guardian.
claims.say: after stance people pick mw, rush, achilles or guardian

claims.text: Achilles cuts damage on every hit while Guardian only blocks some of the time, so many max Achilles before Guardian, or put two points in Achilles per point in Guardian.
claims.say: achilles works every hit, guardian only sometimes

claims.text: Guardian needs a shield, so a Hero who wants it has to use a one-handed sword.
claims.say: guardian needs a shield, so go 1h sword

claims.text: Guardian's knockback can push a boss into your party's ranged attackers, and the only control you have is which way you face.
claims.say: guardian can kb a boss into your party, watch facing

claims.text: A Hero who bosses with parties can delay Maple Warrior, since someone else usually casts it there.
claims.say: mw can wait, someone buffs it at bosses anyway

claims.text: Enrage is mainly a bossing skill with little use for training, and it can be dispelled.
claims.say: enrage is for bosses, and it can be dispelled

claims.text: For an Ice/Lightning Arch Mage looking to upgrade, an elemental weapon that boosts ice or lightning is suggested as a bigger damage gain than just stacking more LUK gear.
claims.say: i/l: an elemental wand for your element is a big dmg boost

claims.text: Crafting new equipment with the Maker skill can be an affordable upgrade path when you already have a stock of ores saved up.
claims.say: got ores saved? maker can make you cheap new gear

claims.text: Arans are expected to HP wash before trying to solo Bigfoot, because getting hit by it is close to fatal.
claims.say: aran soloing bigfoot? hp wash first, its hits are brutal

claims.text: Smart Knockback and Snow Charge have no effect on Bigfoot, so they are not worth using there.
claims.say: smart knockback and snow charge do nothing on bigfoot

claims.text: With Freeze Standing an Aran is not knocked back by Bigfoot's magic hits, so it can stand and chain Triple Swing instead of slide-hitting with Double Swing.
claims.say: freeze standing on bigfoot lets you triple swing, no knockback

claims.text: For a Bigfoot attempt an Aran should buff Polearm Booster, Freeze Standing and Combo Barrier; Combo Drain matters little since the plan is to avoid being hit at all.
claims.say: bigfoot buffs: polearm booster, freeze standing, combo barrier

claims.text: A common view on Night Lords: low DEX suits modest funding, while going DEXless pays off once you own a high-attack claw plus attack-scrolled cape and shoes.
claims.say: low dex if poor, dexless once you have a big claw and att gear

claims.text: When your cape and shoes are scrolled for stats instead of attack, keeping some base DEX on a Night Lord makes more sense than going DEXless.
claims.say: stat-scrolled cape and shoes? then low dex makes sense

claims.text: For a low-DEX Night Lord the helmet is the cheapest place to scroll DEX, since helmets offer no LUK or attack scroll to give up.
