claims.say: helm is the place to scroll dex, no luk or att option there

claims.text: One low-DEX Night Lord upgrade order: a helmet such as Zakum Helmet, then overall, earrings, face accessory, shoes and eye accessory, all DEX-scrolled, with the new claw bought last.
claims.say: low dex nl: helm, overall, earrings, face, shoes, eye, claw last

claims.text: From level 1 to about 16, an Aran gets most of its exp from the tutorial and the Aran story quests.
claims.say: lv 1-16 aran: just do the tutorial and the aran quests

claims.text: From level 16 to 27, an Aran can train in the Zombie Mushroom mini dungeon.
claims.say: 16-27 aran: zombie mushroom mini dungeon

claims.text: Rotting Skeletons are an Aran training option from level 16 to 30.
claims.say: 16-30 aran: rotting skeletons

claims.text: From level 21 to 29, an Aran can train at Sahel 1, Sahel 2 or Sahel 3.
claims.say: 21-29 aran: sahel 1, 2 or 3

claims.text: Around level 29 to 30, an Aran should finish off the remaining Aran quests.
claims.say: lv 29-30 wrap up the last aran quests

claims.text: An Aran can keep training at Sahel 1 from level 30 to 35.
claims.say: 30-35 aran: sahel 1 still works

claims.text: Monster Carnival is an Aran training choice from level 35 to 50.
claims.say: 35-50 aran: monster carnival

claims.text: From level 35 to 38, an Aran can train on Cube Slimes and Rumos.
claims.say: 35-38 aran: cube slimes and rumos

claims.text: From level 38 to 42, an Aran can move to Rumos and Triple Rumos.
claims.say: 38-42 aran: rumos and triple rumos

claims.text: Truckers are an Aran option from level 40 to 55.
claims.say: 40-55 aran: truckers

claims.text: Straw Target Dummies are an Aran option from level 43 to 50.
claims.say: 43-50 aran: straw target dummies

claims.text: Forest of Golem is an Aran training map from level 43 to 60.
claims.say: 43-60 aran: forest of golem

claims.text: Mysterious Path 3 serves an Aran from level 50 up to about 80.
claims.say: 50-80 aran: mp3

claims.text: Windraiders are an Aran target from level 50 through the 80s.
claims.say: 50-89 aran: windraiders

claims.text: Twisted Jesters are an Aran spot from level 55 to 70.
claims.say: 55-70 aran: twisted jesters

claims.text: Stormbreakers at Tornado Corridor suit an Aran from about level 65 through the 80s.
claims.say: 65-89 aran: stormbreakers at tornado corridor

claims.text: Homunculus are an Aran option from level 65 to 70.
claims.say: 65-70 aran: homunculus

claims.text: Dual Ghost Pirates are an Aran spot from level 75 to 90.
claims.say: 75-90 aran: dual ghost pirates

claims.text: Wolf Spiders are an Aran target from level 80 to 89.
claims.say: 80-89 aran: wolf spiders

claims.text: Booper Scarlions and Yabber Doos are an Aran option from level 80 to 89.
claims.say: 80-89 aran: booper scarlions and yabber doos

claims.text: Body Pressure works like a buff that neutralizes monsters touching you, so an Aran can stand on mobs and take mainly their magic attacks.
claims.say: body pressure lets you stand on mobs, only magic hits you

claims.text: Arans in their 80s can train at Wolf Spiders with Body Pressure and take almost no damage.
claims.say: 8x aran: wolf spiders with body pressure, barely get hit

claims.text: Crimson Arcglaive is an endgame polearm goal, but it needs 80 DEX, which warriors usually reach through DEX on their equipment rather than by putting AP into DEX.
claims.say: crimson arcglaive wants 80 dex, get it from gear not ap

claims.text: A budget route to 80 DEX: 4 base DEX plus a scrolled Horntail Necklace (about 22), a Zakum Helmet (15), and DEX on earrings, top and bottom, shoes, cape and a ring, without trading away attack gear.
claims.say: ht necklace + zhelm + dex earrings and overall gets you to 80 dex

claims.text: An unscrolled Horntail Necklace can be moved from one of your characters to another with Scissors of Karma, which makes it an easier DEX source to obtain.
claims.say: karma an unscrolled ht necklace over from your other char

claims.text: Mortal Blow's automatic close-range hit can interrupt Hurricane when monsters get near, a nuisance at Zakum when its summons close in and nobody controls them.
claims.say: mortal blow can cut your hurricane when zak summons get close

claims.text: A low-DEX Aran in the mid-30s with only about 46 total DEX and a partly leveled Polearm Mastery misses Toy Trojans often in Monster Carnival; more DEX from gear fixes the hit rate.
claims.say: low dex aran at 35 misses toy trojans in cpq, grab some dex gear

claims.text: A bathrobe or warrior overall passed with ten 100% overall DEX scrolls gives about 10 DEX and is a cheap way for a warrior to stop missing.
claims.say: 10 dex overall from 100% scrolls is a cheap accuracy fix

claims.text: Until a warrior can wear a Zakum Helmet, a DEX hat such as a Brown Bandana or Blue Old Wisconsin is a good way to raise accuracy.
claims.say: wear a brown bandana or blue old wisconsin for acc till zhelm

claims.text: If you keep missing, Work Gloves with DEX or accuracy beat a higher-attack pair: always hitting with 10 less weapon attack does more than landing only 80% of hits.
claims.say: dex/acc work gloves > attack gloves if ur missing alot

claims.text: Arans have no DEX requirement for their advancements, so many players keep base DEX at 4; others still prefer raising some DEX.
claims.say: arans can stay at 4 base dex, no job needs dex

claims.text: For an Aran in the early 30s, 60 base DEX is more than needed; a DEX-scrolled overall with 10 or more DEX is the better way to get accuracy.
claims.say: 60 base dex is too much on an aran, get a dex overall instead

claims.text: Maker-made level 60 to 70 overalls, gloves and shoes come with a little LUK and have high stat potential; mages can add INT crystals when making them.
claims.say: maker 60-70 gear comes with some luk, add int crystals

claims.text: Ludibrium Maze Party Quest is an option for Bandits in the mid-50s instead of Orbis Party Quest.
claims.say: try lmpq around 56 instead of opq

claims.text: Voodoos and Hoodoos are a training option for Bandits in the mid-50s.
claims.say: voodoos and hoodoos are fine around 56

claims.text: For assassins, Straw Target Dummies are better exp than Gryphons, which fly around in large groups on an awkwardly laid out map.
claims.say: as a sin go straw target dummies, gryphons are a pain

claims.text: After Straw Target Dummies at 60, assassins can train on Voodoos up to level 70.
claims.say: after dummies at 60, voodoos till 70 works well

claims.text: Doing party quests until around level 50 before moving to Straw Target Dummies is a common assassin route.
claims.say: pq till 50 then hit the straw dummies

claims.text: Mysterious Path 3 needs more accuracy than Roids; with only 15 base DEX an Aran had enough around level 48.
claims.say: mp3 needs more acc, 15 base dex was enough around 48

claims.text: Combo Tempest freezes normal monsters solid; anyone who then hits one kills it outright and gets the full exp for it.
claims.say: tempest freezes mobs, any hit after that kills them

claims.text: If another player shatters your Tempest-frozen monsters, a partied Aran still gets the normal party share, but a solo Aran gets no exp from them.
claims.say: solo, you get no exp if someone else breaks your tempest ice

claims.text: Frozen monsters thaw after a few seconds, so hit them quickly after Combo Tempest.
claims.say: hit frozen mobs fast, they thaw in a few secs

claims.text: Reaching 200 combo on a boss is hard, since seduce and stun always break your combo.
claims.say: seduce and stun break combo, 200 on bosses is rough

claims.text: Dragon Knights come in three styles: pole arm only, spear only, or a hybrid that uses both; each has trade-offs and none is simply the best.
claims.say: dk can go pure polearm, pure spear or hybrid

claims.text: Pole arm Dragon Knights use Sacrifice as their single-target attack, so it is the skill they rely on at bosses.
claims.say: polearm dks boss with sacrifice

claims.text: Spear Dragon Knights max Spear Crusher as their main attack, sometimes after a few points in Dragon Fury: Spear to pull monsters together before finishing them with Crusher.
claims.say: spear dk: max spear crusher, fury just to lure

claims.text: Hybrid Dragon Knights carry both a spear and a pole arm and swap depending on the map, so they have to pay for two weapons at each upgrade instead of one.
claims.say: hybrid dk means buying a spear and a polearm

claims.text: Between 3rd job at level 70 and level 120 a Dragon Knight earns about 151 SP in total, counting the extra point at 120.
claims.say: you get about 151 sp between 70 and 120

claims.text: A standard pole arm build maxes Dragon Fury: Pole Arm, Sacrifice, Dragon Blood, Dragon Roar and Elemental Resistance, puts what is left into Pole Arm Crusher, and skips Power Crash.
claims.say: pa dk: max fury, sac, blood, roar, er, rest pa crusher

claims.text: Maxed Dragon Roar hits a whole crowd at once, which helps with kill-count quests and with clearing the bombs during the Papulatus fight.
claims.say: dragon roar is great for pap bombs

claims.text: Dragon Blood can be skipped if you drink the attack potions sold in New Leaf City instead, but they are expensive and fill up your Use inventory.
claims.say: skip dragon blood only if you can afford nlc pots

claims.text: Power Crash cannot be learned until Dragon Blood is at level 3.
claims.say: power crash needs 3 points in dragon blood

claims.text: A standard spear build maxes Spear Crusher, Dragon Blood, Dragon Roar, Elemental Resistance and Dragon Fury: Spear, then puts 20 into Sacrifice and 1 into Power Crash.
claims.say: spear dk: max crusher, blood, roar, er, spear fury

claims.text: Some spear Dragon Knights max Sacrifice and stop Dragon Fury: Spear at 20, because Sacrifice ignores the target's weapon defense and ends up used about as often.
claims.say: sacrifice ignores weapon def, worth maxing too

claims.text: A spear build that skips Dragon Blood can max both spear attacks, Sacrifice, Dragon Roar and Elemental Resistance with about 11 SP to spare, as long as you carry attack potions.
claims.say: no dragon blood lets a spear dk max every attack

claims.text: A common hybrid build maxes Dragon Fury: Pole Arm, Spear Crusher, Dragon Roar, Sacrifice and Elemental Resistance, skips Dragon Blood, and puts the remainder into Dragon Fury: Spear for luring.
claims.say: hybrid: max pa fury, spear crusher, roar, sac, er

claims.text: Hybrids get little out of Pole Arm Crusher since they swap to a spear for Spear Crusher, so their builds usually leave it empty.
claims.say: hybrids dont need pole arm crusher

claims.text: Crimson Arcglaive only comes from the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest and cannot be made with the Maker skill, which keeps it rare.
claims.say: crimson arcglaive only drops from cwkpq, can't make it

claims.text: A Maple Snowboard has the same attack as a Maple Karstan but no accuracy bonus, so it is no upgrade over the Karstan.
claims.say: maple snowboard is same att as karstan but no acc, skip it

claims.text: An Aran can keep using a clean Maple Karstan into the low 80s before needing another polearm.
claims.say: a clean maple karstan carries an aran into the 80s

claims.text: Most polearms past the Maple Karstan swing slower; the Purple Surfboard is the faster upgrade Arans look for.
claims.say: after karstan most polearms are slow, purple surfboard is faster

claims.text: For an Aran, Maple Karstan is the more popular mid-game polearm pick over Super Snowboard, trading some speed for STR and a large accuracy bonus.
claims.say: most arans take maple karstan at 64 over super snowboard

claims.text: Super Snowboard is one of the fastest polearms and adds speed, so it suits Arans who value attack speed over the Karstan's accuracy.
claims.say: super snowboard is a really fast polearm if you want speed

claims.text: Maple Karstan's accuracy bonus helps a low-DEX Aran keep landing hits on monsters.
claims.say: low dex aran? karstan accuracy helps you hit

claims.text: To land Final Charge, keep pressing attack after Triple Swing but add a direction arrow key; spamming attack alone often slips into a different move.
claims.say: after triple swing add an arrow key to the attack for final charge

claims.text: Arans do not need Final Charge maxed in 2nd job (around 21 by level 70 is typical); Combat Step and Combo Drain are more useful and are usually maxed by the mid-50s, with Body Pressure also worthwhile.
claims.say: no need to max final charge, max combat step and combo drain

claims.text: Pressing attack three times quickly chains the basic swing into Double Swing and then Triple Swing; lag or a slow computer makes these combos much harder to pull off.
claims.say: tap attack 3x fast to chain double and triple swing

claims.text: Combo Barrier's damage reduction stacks with Meso Guard and with Achilles instead of being replaced by them.
claims.say: combo barrier stacks with meso guard and achilles

claims.text: Some boosts overlap instead of stacking: Rage does not add to an Onyx Apple, and Haste does not add to a speed potion.
claims.say: rage wont stack w onyx apple, haste wont stack w speed pot

claims.text: Echo of Hero stacks with other attack-boosting items and skills.
claims.say: echo of hero stacks with your other att buffs

claims.text: Horntail's tail deals extreme touch damage, so damage reduction such as Meso Guard or Achilles matters a lot around it.
claims.say: ht tail touch dmg is brutal, use your dmg reduction

claims.text: Achilles and Power Guard damage reductions multiply together rather than add, so the combined cut is a little smaller than their sum.
claims.say: achilles and power guard multiply, they don't just add

claims.text: A blood build means putting AP straight into HP each level and keeping it there, instead of washing points out of MP with AP Resets; it is the cheap way to gain HP when washing is too costly.
claims.say: blood build = ap into hp, no resets, cheap way to get hp

claims.text: Many Bandits do not bother maxing Steal because it falls out of use later, preferring Endure, a passive that keeps helping for the whole game; others still want Steal builds.
claims.say: lots of bandits skip steal, endure keeps helping forever

claims.text: Final Attack: Crossbow is seen as a wasted skill; a Sniper who sank 23 points into it regretted the build.
claims.say: dont waste sp on final attack crossbow

claims.text: Early-Pierce Marksman plan: at 120 put 1 in Frostprey and start Piercing Arrow, add 1 Dragon's Breath, and max Piercing Arrow around 133.
claims.say: early pierce mm: 1 frostprey, 1 dragon's breath, rush pierce

claims.text: In that plan Marksman Boost and Sharp Eyes start around 128; max Marksman Boost, raise Sharp Eyes to 20, then max Snipe and finish Sharp Eyes last.
claims.say: then max boost, sharp eyes to 20, snipe, finish sharp eyes

claims.text: Piercing Arrow hits more monsters as its level rises, which is why some Marksmen level it first to train faster.
claims.say: pierce hits more mobs as you level it, good for training

claims.text: Buffs cast while hanging on a rope or ladder have a much shorter cast delay, about the same for every class, so long casts like Shadow Partner gain the most.
claims.say: cast buffs on a rope, the delay is way shorter

claims.text: Jumping while you attack or recast buffs keeps you moving instead of rooting you in place; just watch for what's overhead.
claims.say: jump while attacking or buffing to keep moving

claims.text: Hovering over your name and job in the lower-left corner of the UI shows your world and channel, handy in maps where you can't otherwise see it.
claims.say: hover your name bottom left to see your channel

claims.text: When surrounded by tall enough monsters, jump and fire Avenger as your feet reach their heads to hit the whole pack from above.
claims.say: jump avenger at head height to hit the whole mob

claims.text: Flash Jump right as you leave the ground for more distance, or at the top of the jump for more height, enough to clear the Headless Horseman; Haste improves both.
claims.say: flash jump early for distance, at the peak for height

claims.text: For a controlled high jump, jump facing away, turn in the air and Flash Jump at the peak; ropes can only be grabbed while falling, so this helps catch them. The Mu Lung Dojo entrance is a good practice spot.
claims.say: back-jump and flash jump at the peak to grab ropes

claims.text: Bind Combat Step to a key; dash, release the arrow key and jump to carry the momentum, then step again on landing to cross flat ground quickly.
claims.say: bind combat step to a key, step then jump to keep speed

claims.text: A Dragon Knight in the 80s still gets good exp training at spiders with a Priest in the party.
claims.say: 80s dk: spiders with a priest is still good exp

claims.text: Blue Kentaurus maps have three rows of mobs that suit a Dragon Knight, while the red and black ones wander around more.
claims.say: blue kentaurus 3 rows are great for dks, red and black roam

claims.text: Merchanting is a reliable way to make mesos; when selling quest leftovers on the MTS, search current prices first so you do not underprice.
claims.say: merchant for mesos, check mts prices before listing

claims.text: For a warrior in the high 70s, maps of Windraiders mixed with Stormbreakers, or Wolf Spiders, worked best of the usually suggested spots; Dual Ghost Pirates did worse by comparison.
claims.say: at 78 windraiders/stormbreakers or wolf spiders worked best for me

claims.text: The strongest setup is low DEX topped up by DEX on top and bottom equips with a high-attack claw, but it is expensive to reach; going dexless is the cheaper route.
claims.say: low dex with dex gear is best but pricey, dexless is cheaper

claims.text: Excavation Site is a good Assassin training spot for levels 20 to 30.
claims.say: 20-30 sins can grind excavation site

claims.text: Hoodoo and Voodoo are a decent training spot for levels 60 to 70.
claims.say: 60-70 try hoodoos and voodoos

claims.text: For a Hero, a one-handed sword plus attack shield only beats a two-handed sword if the one-handed sword has Fast attack speed; otherwise the 2H sword is the better value.
claims.say: 1h + shield only pays off if the 1h sword is fast speed

claims.text: If you plan to use attack items like Onyx Apples on big bosses such as Zakum or Horntail, the two-handed sword pulls further ahead.
claims.say: if you apple for zak or ht, the 2h sword wins

claims.text: Hermits should max Alchemist soon after Shadow Partner: longer-lasting apples and attack potions save a lot of money.
claims.say: max alchemist after shadow partner, saves pot money

claims.text: Avenger is mostly for gathering and mobbing, so it matters little if your main spot is Jr. Newties; raise it first only if you plan to mob.
claims.say: avenger is for mobbing, not needed at jr newties

claims.text: Jr. Newties earn little meso, so mix in an hour at Hoodoo and Voodoo or Windraiders to cover costs.
claims.say: newties pay little, farm hoodoo voodoo or windraiders for mesos

claims.text: Around level 82 a Hermit can kill Windraiders and Stormbreakers at Lower Ascent, though a free map is hard to find.
claims.say: low 80s: windraiders and stormbreakers at lower ascent

claims.text: Some Hermits prefer Lucky Seven with Shadow Partner over Avenger, since Avenger flies in a straight line and needs room; in tight spaces you end up bumping into mobs.
claims.say: avenger needs room, l7 plus shadow partner is safer in tight maps

claims.text: Chief Bandit opening: one point in Meso Explosion, Chakra to 3, then a single point each in Meso Guard, Assaulter and Band of Thieves before pouring SP into Band of Thieves.
claims.say: cb start: 1 me, 3 chakra, 1 each mg/assaulter/bot, then bot

claims.text: Max Band of Thieves first, finishing it around level 82, then max Assaulter by about level 92.
claims.say: max bot first, then assaulter

claims.text: After Assaulter, max Meso Guard, then Meso Explosion, then Pickpocket, finishing Chakra last and putting the final points into Dark Sight at 120.
claims.say: after that: mg, then me, then pickpocket, chakra last

claims.text: A Chief Bandit can leave Endure and Shield Mastery empty and the build still works fine.
claims.say: you can skip endure and shield mastery on a cb

claims.text: One early point in Assaulter is worth taking just for the mobility of its dash, long before leveling it.
claims.say: put 1 in assaulter early, the dash is handy

claims.text: Arans can take part in Horntail runs from the high 140s, and the fight plays much like it does for a Hero.
claims.say: aran ht plays a lot like hero ht, doable from high 140s

claims.text: At Horntail's preliminary heads, room lag can drop an Aran's combo, and the heads die fast enough that you only get one or two Combo Barrier casts in.
claims.say: prelim heads die fast, you get maybe 1-2 combo barriers off

claims.text: During Horntail's legs, stand on the legs with Body Pressure switched on so a stun does not reset your combo; this is the main place Body Pressure earns its keep.
claims.say: stand on ht legs with body pressure on so stuns dont drop combo

claims.text: Using Final Blow while standing on Horntail's left leg reaches the arms, wings, legs and tail together.
claims.say: final blow from the left leg hits arms wings legs and tail

claims.text: The legs and tail phase at Horntail lasts long enough for an Aran to fit in two Combo Barrier casts and a Combo Tempest.
claims.say: legs and tail give time for 2 barriers and a tempest

claims.text: For Horntail's tail, an Aran can simply stand close to the body's center line and keep attacking until it falls.
claims.say: for the tail just stand near ht's middle and keep hitting

claims.text: On Horntail's right side, use the platform that reaches the right head, right wing and right arm; when that head starts guarding, drop down and hit only the wing and arm.
claims.say: right platform hits head, wing and arm; drop down if head guards

claims.text: Horntail's left side is the easiest part for an Aran: the platforms are spaced so that if your stance fails you can still hit something and reposition before the combo runs out.
claims.say: left side is easy, platforms let you recover before combo drops

claims.text: If Horntail dispels you, recast buffs one at a time with an attack between each so the combo counter never times out.
claims.say: after a dispel, rebuff one at a time with hits in between

claims.text: Horntail's heads sink out of reach when they attack, so either land a quick Final Blow or wait for them to rise again before your combo expires.
claims.say: heads dip when they attack, quick final blow or wait for them

claims.text: Arans use Final Charge to dash in as close to Horntail's heads as possible.
claims.say: use final charge to dash up close to the heads

claims.text: Because an Aran's damage depends on keeping the combo alive, playing Horntail with almost no lag is close to a requirement.
claims.say: aran ht needs low lag or your combo keeps dropping

claims.text: A character short on funds can raise mesos by drop hunting Sakura Cellions and selling the loot.
claims.say: low on mesos? drop hunt sakura cellions

claims.text: A New Leaf City quest pays out a gloves attack scroll that can be sold for mesos.
claims.say: an nlc quest gives a glove att scroll you can sell

claims.text: A new mage can train on Slimes from about level 8 to 15.
claims.say: slimes are fine from 8 to 15 on a mage

claims.text: Ribbon Pigs at Pig Beach work for a mage from about level 15 to 17.
claims.say: ribbon pigs at pig beach for 15-17

claims.text: Octopuses are a decent mage target from about level 17 to 25.
claims.say: octopus maps from 17 to 25

claims.text: Jr. Cactus is a mage training option from about level 25 to 31.
claims.say: jr cactus from 25 to 31

claims.text: Full-size Cactus mobs suit a fresh Cleric from about level 31 to 37.
claims.say: regular cactus from 31 to 37

claims.text: A Cleric can train on Jr. Wraiths from about level 37 to 41 and then on Wraiths from 41 to 60.
claims.say: jr wraiths 37-41, then wraiths till 60

claims.text: Jr. Wraiths and Wraiths are undead, so a Cleric's Heal damages them, which is why LUK-less Clerics max Heal early and farm wraiths.
claims.say: wraiths are undead, heal hurts them

claims.text: Hoodoos are an option for a Cleric from about level 60 to 70.
claims.say: hoodoos from 60 to 70

claims.text: A LUK-less Cleric build for 30 to 70: 1 Teleport, max Heal, 1 MP Eater, max Teleport, max MP Eater, max Invincible, max Bless, then 11 Holy Arrow.
claims.say: cleric: 1 tele, max heal, tele, mp eater, invincible, bless

claims.text: If you plan to train at Wraiths, maxing Teleport early pays off through faster movement and exp; otherwise Bless often comes first.
claims.say: at wraiths max tele early, otherwise bless first

claims.text: Bowmasters gain nothing from another player's Sharp Eyes because they already have the buff themselves.
claims.say: bms already have sharp eyes, another se adds nothing

claims.text: Once learned, the Phoenix summon deals damage of its own alongside Hurricane, so a Bowmaster should keep it out.
claims.say: phoenix adds free damage on top of hurricane

claims.text: Summon damage, as with Phoenix or Octopus, is figured from your stats and the summon's own attack value, not from your weapon attack.
claims.say: summon damage comes from your stats, not weapon attack

claims.text: For end-game damage comparisons the author equips Bowmasters with a Reverse Engaw bow and Corsairs with a Reverse Blindness gun.
claims.say: reverse engaw for bms, reverse blindness for sairs

claims.text: Clerics don't get enough SP in 2nd job to max every skill, and Holy Arrow or MP Eater are the ones usually left short.
claims.say: cant max everything as cleric, holy arrow or mp eater gets cut

claims.text: Sniper start: 1 Blizzard, 1 Strafe, Mortal Blow to 5, then Arrow Eruption up to 21 by about level 79.
claims.say: sniper: 1 blizzard, 1 strafe, 5 mortal blow, then eruption

claims.text: This Sniper plan then puts a few points in Puppet and Golden Eagle, maxes Strafe by about 96 with Blizzard raised along the way, and finishes Arrow Eruption by 99.
claims.say: then a bit of puppet and eagle, max strafe, finish eruption

claims.text: Other players say early Golden Eagle points in the low 80s do little and that Blizzard should be raised sooner.
claims.say: skip early eagle points, get blizzard up sooner

claims.text: Sniper spread at 120 in this plan: Strafe and Arrow Eruption maxed, Mortal Blow, Puppet and Golden Eagle at 20, Blizzard 21, Thrust 10.
claims.say: by 120: strafe and eruption maxed, blizzard 21, thrust 10

claims.text: Crossbowman spread in this build: Crossbow Mastery and Iron Arrow maxed, Power Knock-Back 20, Crossbow Booster 15, and a few points in Soul Arrow.
claims.say: xbowman: max mastery and iron arrow, pkb 20, booster 15

claims.text: A Fire/Poison mage around level 71 can try training on Hoodoos.
claims.say: f/p around 71? try hoodoos

claims.text: Once Poison Mist has more points, a Fire/Poison mage can go to Squids and poison the entire map.
claims.say: with decent poison mist, go poison a whole map of squids

claims.text: The Ludibrium Maze Party Quest can carry a character all the way to about level 71.
claims.say: you can lmpq your way up to around 71

claims.text: A standard bandit 2nd job build makes Savage Blow the main attack and raises Dagger Mastery and Dagger Booster beside it, reaching about 30 Savage Blow, 19 Mastery and 6 Booster by level 48.
claims.say: bandit: savage blow main, plus mastery and booster by 48

claims.text: Once Savage Blow is maxed most bandits max Haste as soon as possible: it speeds moving between monsters and makes you more welcome in parties.
claims.say: max haste right after savage blow

claims.text: Leftover SP later goes into finishing Dagger Booster, so you are not recasting it every minute, and into Endure, which is always active.
claims.say: finish dagger booster so you recast it less

claims.text: In 3rd job Boomerang Step soon becomes the bandit's main attack and replaces the 2nd job attacks.
claims.say: boomerang step takes over in 3rd job

claims.text: Under Magic Guard, once MP runs out the rest of the damage lands fully on HP, so an empty MP bar means you take whole hits.
claims.say: if your mp hits zero magic guard stops saving you

claims.text: Every mage should max Magic Guard, since it is the core of a magician's survival.
claims.say: max magic guard on any mage, its your main survival skill

claims.text: Unwashed mages usually end up with far more MP than the 1 to 4 ratio can use, so a big hit kills through HP while MP is left over; HP washing moves points into HP to fix this.
claims.say: unwashed mages have too much mp for their hp, wash some

claims.text: Too much HP for your MP also hurts: if heavy HP gear, overwashing or a skipped Improved MaxMP Increase leaves MP short, MP drains first and HP takes the rest of the hit.
claims.say: dont overwash, too little mp means hits go straight to hp

claims.text: Chasing the MP cap is unnecessary; apart from a big ultimate like Meteor Shower, mage spells use little MP thanks to MP Eater, so the MP lost to washing barely matters.
claims.say: you dont need max mp, the mp you wash away barely matters

claims.text: A washed mage copes far better with being dispelled: stun plus dispel at Manon and Griffey, hits from Papulatus, or Pianus become survivable without Magic Guard.
claims.say: hp washed mages survive dispel at pap and pianus way better

claims.text: Start HP washing a mage early; the MP lost per washed point grows as you level and add INT, and deciding at level 200 is too late.
claims.say: start washing early on a mage, mp loss per point keeps growing

claims.text: A mage gains 6 to 10 HP per AP put into HP, about 8 on average; because gains are random, recheck your washing plan after each reset.
claims.say: mages get 6 to 10 hp per ap into hp, about 8 average

claims.text: Backwashing, moving points from HP back into MP, returns very little MP for the HP lost, so treat HP washing on a mage as permanent.
claims.say: dont backwash a mage, you get almost no mp back

claims.text: Count the HP gear you plan to wear before washing all the way; once washed to the ratio, your MP caps how much that extra gear HP adds to survival.
claims.say: count your hp gear before you wash, mp caps the benefit

claims.text: Keep INT as high as possible at every level up, using Maple Warrior and INT gear; MP gained per level rises by about 1 for every 10 INT, leaving more MP to wash later.
claims.say: level up with int gear and maple warrior on for more mp

claims.text: Plan HP washing from projected level 200 HP and MP rather than current stats; a mage gains about 12 HP per level on average.
claims.say: plan your wash from your projected lv200 hp and mp

claims.text: For classes other than mages, washing is simple: keep washing until MP sits at the minimum you need to cast your skills.
claims.say: non mages just wash till mp is the minimum for skills

claims.text: Snow Charge turns an Aran's attacks ice element and slows monsters, so ice-weak monsters take extra damage.
claims.say: snow charge makes your hits ice and slows mobs

claims.text: Against monsters that resist ice, Snow Charge lowers your damage, so turn it off for ice-resistant mobs or bosses.
claims.say: turn off snow charge on ice resistant mobs

claims.text: Elderwraiths resist ice, so an Aran with Snow Charge on struggles to kill them.
claims.say: elderwraiths shrug off snow charge, turn it off

claims.text: Combat Step is easier to use from its own hotkey than by double-tapping a direction, especially with slow input such as a game controller.
claims.say: put combat step on a hotkey instead of double tapping

claims.text: Night Walkers are advised to max Vampire early rather than Flash Jump: it hits a group and heals you at once, cutting potion use while mobbing.
claims.say: max vampire early on nw, it beats flash jump

claims.text: Vampire is very strong in Monster Carnival: monsters right on top of you die quickly and the life drain means you hardly need HP potions.
claims.say: vampire is great in cpq, you barely need hp pots

claims.text: Vampire needs Claw Mastery behind it to deal steady damage, so raise the two together.
claims.say: vampire wants claw mastery for steady damage

claims.text: Night Walkers never get Shadow Stars, so how many stars you carry matters; Steely Throwing-Knives give a lot of stars per slot without the cost of top-end stars.
claims.say: nw has no shadow stars, steelies give lots of stars cheap

claims.text: One mobility-first Night Walker plan stops Flash Jump at 13, takes Critical Throw to 15 and Claw Booster to 6, then fills Vampire and Claw Mastery.
claims.say: fj 13, crit throw 15, booster 6, then vampire and mastery

claims.text: Take Haste yourself (around level 52 in one plan) instead of relying on party members to buff it; parties do not like carrying a slow thief.
claims.say: get haste yourself, dont lean on the party for it

claims.text: Leprechauns in Crimsonwood are good for mesos but poor for exp, and getting to them means crossing a map full of Elderwraiths.
claims.say: leprechauns are for mesos, not exp, past elderwraiths

claims.text: Most Crimsonwood mountain maps mix several monster types and are often crowded with Windraiders, which are bad to train on.
claims.say: cwk maps full of windraiders are bad exp

claims.text: Firebrand's second form flies around, but unlike other flying monsters it doesn't sink when frozen.
claims.say: frozen firebrands don't drop like other flyers

claims.text: Path of Strength looks like the most party-friendly Crimsonwood map: no Windraiders and monsters that pay off well for the effort, though flying Firebrands and Elderwraiths can be a nuisance.
claims.say: path of strength is the best party map in cwk

claims.text: Crimson Guardians hit very hard, but there is a spot where you can hit them with Arrow Rain or Arrow Eruption without being touched, if you can survive their physical hit; looting is awkward.
claims.say: crimson guardians: use the safe spot and arrow rain them

claims.text: Venomous Stab helps most on monsters a Shadower cannot kill in one or two hits, such as in Temple of Time, and matters less as you outlevel your maps.
claims.say: venom helps where you cant 1-2 hit stuff, like tot

claims.text: Boomerang Step's frequent stun pairs well with Venomous Stab for training.
claims.say: bstep stun plus venom is a nice training combo

claims.text: Assassinate is a slow single-target hit that needs Dark Sight active, so it does little for training and is mainly a bossing skill.
claims.say: assassinate is a boss skill, too slow for training

claims.text: Shadow Shifter's extra dodging mostly saves potions and cuts down on knockback in boss fights; it does not make training faster.
claims.say: shifter saves pots and knockback, wont speed training

claims.text: Dawn Raven's Claw needs some DEX on top of LUK but gives more attack, while Night Raven's Claw needs only LUK and attacks one speed step faster.
claims.say: dawn raven has more att, night raven is faster and luk only

claims.text: If you already meet Dawn Raven's Claw's DEX requirement, its extra attack makes it the better pick over Night Raven's Claw.
claims.say: if you have the dex, take dawn raven for the extra att

claims.text: Many Phantom Forest portals are one-way, so stepping back into the portal you arrived from can send you somewhere else.
claims.say: lots of phantom forest portals are one way, dont backtrack

claims.text: The signposts in Haunted Hill, Phantom Road, Bent Tree and Forgotten Path lead to dead-end maps (Creeping Evil, Evil Rising, Hidden Evil, The Evil Dead) whose only exit goes back.
claims.say: signpost maps are dead ends, they only lead back

claims.text: Dead Man's Gorge has two gates: the bottom one drops you at its own top-left area and the top one goes to Haunted Hill, whose gate leads back to Dead Man's Gorge.
claims.say: dead man's gorge top gate goes to haunted hill

claims.text: From the low 60s, Fire/Poison mages train on Death Teddies and often stay until Poison Mist is close to maxed.
claims.say: f/p low 60s: death teddies till poison mist is near max

claims.text: After 3rd job, Fire/Poison mages often level to 4th job by laying Poison Mist on Skelegons and other high-HP mobs.
claims.say: 3rd job f/p: poison mist skelegons all the way to 120

claims.text: Power Guard cuts the damage you take from monster touches, by a smaller share against bosses, and it also lessens the knockback.
claims.say: power guard cuts touch dmg, less so on bosses

claims.text: Horntail's Wings buff the attack of the other parts, so running into the Tail can kill even a 30k HP warrior with Power Guard on; cross it carefully.
claims.say: ht wings buff atk, tail touch can kill you even with pg

claims.text: Before adding Genesis levels, check whether they change how many casts a mob takes; levels that keep the same hit count only raise the MP cost.
claims.say: only level genesis if it drops your hits to kill

claims.text: While Genesis cannot reach a better hit count, put SP into Maple Warrior and Bahamut, then save 8 or more points to raise Genesis in one go.
claims.say: put sp in mw and bahamut, then save 8+ for genesis

claims.text: One-hitting Skelegons with Genesis cuts potion cost because you avoid their magic attacks and only take touch damage from fresh spawns.
claims.say: 1 hit kos at skeles save pots, no magic attacks to eat

claims.text: Reverse Nibleheim, formerly called Reverse Claymore, is the top end-game two-handed sword for those willing to hunt Pieces of Time or pay more.
claims.say: best 2h endgame is reverse nibleheim, needs pieces of time

claims.text: A suggested I/L 4th-job order: 1 point in Blizzard, max Chain Lightning (or get it to at least 20), then 9 in Maple Warrior, then work on Ifrit and Blizzard.
claims.say: i/l: 1 blizz, max chain lightning, 9 mw, then ifrit and blizz

claims.text: Many Ice/Lightning mages skip Thunder Spear in 3rd job, and some skip Chain Lightning in 4th as well, leaning on Blizzard to level.
claims.say: lots of i/l skip thunder spear, some skip chain lightning too

claims.text: A Shadower soloing Bigfoot can keep it pinned by using Assassinate, cancelling its last hit, then following up with Boomerang Step; Boomerang Step on its own won't hold it in place.
claims.say: assassinate, cancel last hit, then bstep keeps bigfoot pinned

claims.text: Killing Bigfoot with Meso Explosion works but is slow, leaving plenty of time for someone else to take the kill.
claims.say: meso exploding bigfoot works but takes forever

claims.text: Elemental Wand 6 is the poison-element level-130 wand; Ice/Lightning mages look for the ice-element version instead.
claims.say: elemental wand 6 is the poison one, i/l want the ice wand

claims.text: Elemental weapons are meant to strengthen spells of their own element and weaken spells of other elements, so pick the one that matches your main element.
claims.say: use the elemental wand that matches your element

claims.text: From level 1 to 10 a beginner can level on Snails, Blue Snails, Shrooms and Red Snails.
claims.say: lv 1-10 just kill snails, blue snails, shrooms and red snails

claims.text: Between 11 and 20, Slimes, Stumps and Orange Mushrooms are good targets for a beginner.
claims.say: 11-20 slimes, stumps and orange mushrooms are good

claims.text: Pigs and Ribbon Pigs on The Pig Beach are a solid spot in the 11 to 20 range.
claims.say: pigs and ribbon pigs at pig beach are nice for 11-20

claims.text: From 21 to 30, Kerning City Party Quest is an alternative to grinding mobs.
claims.say: 21-30 you can just do kpq instead of grinding

claims.text: Octopuses are a 21 to 30 option, with the map Caution! Falling Down suggested for them.
claims.say: octopus are fine for 21-30

claims.text: Blue Mushrooms and Ghost Stumps work from the 20s into the 30s, with Ghost Stumps found at the Excavation Site.
claims.say: ghost stumps at excavation site are good in your 20s

claims.text: Horned Mushrooms and Zombie Mushrooms in Ant Tunnel I to IV are a classic spot for the 30s; Horned Mushrooms already work from the mid 20s.
claims.say: 30s: horny and zombie mushrooms in ant tunnel

claims.text: Ludibrium Party Quest is an alternative to grinding in the 31 to 40 range.
claims.say: 31-40 lpq is a good alternative to grinding

claims.text: Jr. Sentinels on Orbis Tower <20th Floor> are a suggested spot for 31 to 40.
claims.say: jr sentinels in orbis tower 20th floor for 31-40

claims.text: Wooden Masks and Rocky Masks at the Excavation Site are another option in the 30s.
claims.say: wooden and rocky masks at excavation site in the 30s

claims.text: Trixters and Wild Boars are also fine targets from 31 to 40.
claims.say: trixters and wild boars work for 31-40 too

claims.text: Brown Teddies and Pink Teddies in Ludibrium, on the Cloud Terrace and Sky Terrace maps, round out the late 30s.
claims.say: late 30s teddies on cloud terrace in ludi are good

claims.text: Teddies move fast, so a slow weapon like the Frozen Tuna is not the best choice against them.
claims.say: teddies are fast, a slow frozen tuna isnt great there

claims.text: Fire Boars are a decent target in the 41 to 50 range.
claims.say: fire boars are decent around 41-50

claims.text: Ratz around Eos Tower 100th Floor are a suggested spot from the 40s, and stay usable into the 60s.
claims.say: ratz up in eos tower 100th floor in your 40s

claims.text: Scuba Pepes are another option for the 41 to 50 range.
claims.say: scuba pepes work in the 40s

claims.text: Tick-Tocks in the Whirlpool of Time move slowly, which makes them a good spot from 41 to 60 if you swing a Frozen Tuna.
claims.say: tick-tocks are slow, nice spot if you use a frozen tuna

claims.text: Toy Trojans and Jr. Wraiths are other monsters worth hunting in the 40s.
claims.say: toy trojans or jr wraiths are ok in the 40s

claims.text: Orbis Party Quest is a good alternative to grinding from 50 to 70.
claims.say: 50-70 opq is a good alternative

claims.text: Block Golems and King Block Golems on Eos Tower 4th Floor and 5th Floor are a suggested spot for 50 to 60.
claims.say: block golems at eos tower 4th and 5th floor in the 50s

claims.text: Ludibrium Maze Party Quest is a good option in the 61 to 70 range.
claims.say: 61-70 try lmpq

claims.text: Arch Mage training on Crimson Guardians is disputed: one plan tags the crowd with Ice Demon or Fire Demon and finishes with Blizzard, but critics say the small packed map and heavy hits make it slow and costly.
claims.say: crimson guardians for archmages is debated, they hit hard

claims.text: Ice Demon and Fire Demon leave a lingering damage-over-time effect on the monsters they hit, which adds to the damage of a follow-up attack.
claims.say: ice demon and fire demon keep ticking damage after the hit

claims.text: When training in Crimsonwood Mountain, the nearest place to restock potions is New Leaf City, and the author finds the round trip takes only a few minutes.
claims.say: need pots in crimsonwood? nlc is close, quick trip

claims.text: When HP washing, put the level-up AP into HP first; the AP Reset cannot take a point out of MP until you have done so.
claims.say: hp washing: put the ap into hp first, then reset mp

claims.text: Spell damage grows with the square of magic attack: the top hit is about ((MATK^2/1000 + MATK)/30 + INT/200) times the spell's power, and the low end also scales with skill mastery.
claims.say: mage dmg scales with matk squared, int adds very little

claims.text: Because magic attack is squared in the damage formula and INT only adds a small term, mages gain far more from extra magic attack on gear than from extra INT.
claims.say: go for matk on gear, extra int barely moves your damage

claims.text: For one-target bossing, Fire/Poison Arch Mages keep Ifrit out and cast Paralyze nonstop, while Ice/Lightning Arch Mages keep Elquines out and cast Chain Lightning nonstop.
claims.say: fp: ifrit out + spam paralyze. il: elquines out + spam cl

claims.text: An Arch Mage's summon attacks on its own timer and adds a real share of boss damage on top of the main spell, so it should stay summoned for the whole fight.
claims.say: keep your summon up the whole boss fight, it's free damage

claims.text: LUKless mages often use the level 64 Maple Shine Wand or Maple Wisdom Staff; because they are common they tend to be scrolled heavily and can keep up with pricier endgame wands.
claims.say: lukless mages: a well scrolled maple shine wand holds up fine

claims.text: The chance that exactly n of t scrolls succeed follows the binomial formula: t choose n, times the success rate to the power n, times the fail rate to the power t minus n.
claims.say: chance n of t scrolls pass follows the binomial formula

claims.text: To get the chance of n or more successes, add the binomial chances for every count from n up to t.
claims.say: for at least n passes add up chances from n to t

claims.text: Most Crimsonwood Mountain quests reward new privileges such as warps or shortcuts instead of items, exp or mesos; Lita Lawless's quests are the exception.
claims.say: cwk quests mostly unlock stuff, not exp or items

claims.text: Completing Jack's quests in Crimsonwood earns you the forest map, which opens special warps around the area.
claims.say: do jack's quests in cwk for the map, it unlocks warps

claims.text: One of John Barricade's quests rewards an item that lets you skip the Crimsonwood jump quest and the areas past it.
claims.say: john barricade's quest gives an item to skip the cwk jq

claims.text: Joko's badge exchange opens after you finish The Fallen Woods, which asks for 50 Phantom Seeds, and the next quest where you show Taggrin the Map of the Phantom Forest.
claims.say: finish the fallen woods and taggrin's map quest to unlock joko

claims.text: Joko, a Raven Ninja, runs a once-a-day exchange: turn in 50 badges of one kind, or 25 of each of the four kinds, for a random prize.
claims.say: joko trades 50 badges of one kind once a day for a prize

claims.text: Joko's exchange needs at least one empty slot in every inventory tab, Set-up included, before it will go through.
claims.say: free a slot in every tab, even setup, before joko

claims.text: Joko's prize pool includes high-level Crimsonwood weapons such as Crushed Skull, Raven's Claw, Onyx Blade, Infinity's Wrath and Silver Crow.
claims.say: joko can hand out cwk weapons like raven's claw

claims.text: Other Joko prizes are 60% attack scrolls for many weapon types (claw, bow, knuckle, spear, pole arm, gun, dagger, wand, staff and more) or a pile of mesos.
claims.say: joko also gives 60% weapon att scrolls or mesos

claims.text: The Raven Ninja Bandana is one of Joko's prizes and was reported from both Windraider and Stormbreaker badge turn-ins.
claims.say: raven ninja bandana can come out of joko's trade

claims.text: Hold on to Elder Ashes; they are needed for Taggrin's final quest.
claims.say: keep elder ashes, taggrin's last quest uses them

claims.text: Defeating Lilynouch at Temple of Time is the step that opens access to the Oblivion-area monsters.
claims.say: beat lilynouch to open the oblivion mobs at tot

claims.text: Lilynouch's damage reflect ignores Magic Guard and can kill a mage in one hit, so stop attacking as soon as it goes up.
claims.say: lilynouch reflect ignores magic guard, stop hitting

claims.text: You can hear Lilynouch start its damage reflect before the animation shows, so fight it with sound on.
claims.say: play with sound on, you hear lilynouch's reflect first

claims.text: Lilynouch's ground stomp can be dodged by jumping, and its ice attack has a fixed range you can leave with Teleport.
claims.say: jump its stomp, teleport out of its ice range

claims.text: Lilynouch's reflect damage goes straight to HP, so keeping HP full helps sturdier characters live through it; a party makes the fight much easier.
claims.say: keep hp full at lilynouch, reflect hits hp

claims.text: As a mage, teleport out of Lilynouch's falling-rock range instead of walking into it, and teleport down to safety while its reflect is up.
claims.say: teleport away from lilynouch while reflect is up

claims.text: Parties often invite Dragon Knights mainly for Hyper Body.
claims.say: parties mostly want dks for hyper body

claims.text: Fighters and Pages play almost the same way from level 1 to 70.
claims.say: fighter and page play about the same til 70

claims.text: Venomous Star's poison damage reportedly does not scale with INT or magic attack gear, going by one Night Lord's testing.
claims.say: int gear doesnt seem to boost venom damage

claims.text: Always charge Big Bang fully; the only good reason to release it early is needing to drink potions during a boss fight.
claims.say: only let big bang go early if you need to pot at a boss

claims.text: Mastery controls how steady your damage is: higher mastery raises your minimum hit closer to your maximum.
claims.say: mastery tightens your range, more mastery higher min

claims.text: With swords, STR raises your minimum damage in proportion to mastery while DEX adds a smaller flat amount to both ends, which is why DEX-less players care so much about mastery.
claims.say: dexless? mastery matters since str lifts min through it

claims.text: With bows and guns, the roles of STR and DEX in the damage formula are swapped compared with swords.
claims.say: on bows and guns dex and str swap roles

claims.text: For mages, INT adds MP regen per tick, more MP per level and a small flat damage bonus, and each INT also counts as 1 magic attack.
claims.say: int gives mp regen, mp per level and 1 matk each

claims.text: Magic attack scales damage faster than linearly, each point worth a little more than the one before, and it also raises mastery slightly.
claims.say: each matk point is worth more than the last

claims.text: LUK has no effect on magic damage, so a LUK-less magician loses nothing in damage.
claims.say: luk does nothing for magic damage

claims.text: Typhons knock you back hard enough to throw you all the way back to the jump quest section of the map.
claims.say: typhon kb can fling you back to the jump quest

claims.text: Sharing the Typhon map with another player helps keep a steady swarm flying toward you.
claims.say: sharing the typhon map keeps a steady swarm coming

claims.text: It is safer to walk into the nearby cave before logging out than to log out on the open Typhon map.
claims.say: log out in the cave, not out on the typhon map

claims.text: One Night Lord path: 1 point each in Triple Throw, Venomous Star and Shadow Stars at 120, Triple Throw to 10, Venomous Star to 13, then Triple Throw to 20.
claims.say: nl: tt 10, venom 13, then tt 20

claims.text: Maple Warrior can come last for a Night Lord when guildmates or party members already cast it.
claims.say: skip mw early if your party already has it

claims.text: Players disagree on Venomous Star versus Triple Throw 20: training-focused Night Lords favor Venom (better at Jr. Newties), bossers want Triple Throw 20 first.
claims.say: venom first for training, tt 20 first for bossing

claims.text: Moving from Lucky Seven to Triple Throw is the biggest damage jump a Night Lord notices.
claims.say: going from l7 to triple throw is a huge damage jump

claims.text: Cold Eyes at Sleepy Dungeon III have a strong spawn for training from about 38 to 45, though the map is often crowded.
claims.say: cold eyes in sleepy dungeon 3 have great spawn for 38-45

claims.text: Among endgame claws, the Reverse Lampion was the usual top pick for Night Lords thanks to its very high weapon attack, though it asks for more DEX than lower claws.
claims.say: reverse lampion is the go-to endgame claw for nl

claims.text: Night Lords get much of their damage from criticals: Critical Throw supplies the base crit chance, and a Bowman's Sharp Eyes stacks extra crit chance and crit damage on top.
claims.say: sharp eyes stacks with critical throw, nls love it

claims.text: A Night Lord only needs enough DEX to equip the claw; any DEX above that requirement is better moved into LUK with AP Resets, since LUK drives claw damage.
claims.say: keep dex at your claw req, reset the rest into luk

claims.text: Night Lords care most about damage output at bosses, so they drink Onyx Apples for boss fights rather than for training.
claims.say: save the onyx apples for bossing on your nl

claims.text: For a well-geared Night Lord, about four to five points of LUK are worth roughly one weapon attack, so a claw with much more attack usually beats one that only adds a few stats.
claims.say: on a geared nl about 5 luk is worth 1 attack

claims.text: Each class has a level-based standard weapon defense the game expects you to have; you use the value for the highest listed level not above yours, and reaching it changes how much damage you take.
claims.say: game expects a set wdef per class and level, it changes dmg taken

claims.text: Warriors are expected to carry far more weapon defense than other classes: roughly 494 at level 100, versus about 266 for magicians, 298 for bowmen, 309 for pirates and 331 for thieves.
claims.say: warriors are expected to have way more wdef than other classes

claims.text: The standard weapon defense effect is odd (reaching it can even raise damage taken) and makes little practical difference, so it is not worth building around.
claims.say: the expected wdef thing barely matters, dont build around it

claims.text: Gear INT worn while you level raises the MP you gain per level, about 1 extra MP per 10 INT, and that spare MP is what you later convert into HP by washing.
claims.say: wear int gear while leveling, +1 mp per lvl for every 10 int

claims.text: Max HP is hard-capped at 30,000.
claims.say: hp can't go past 30k

claims.text: A warrior only needs about 50 INT from gear across levels 10 to 140 to bank enough MP to wash up to max HP with Hyper Body.
claims.say: warriors need just ~50 int gear to wash to max hp

claims.text: An Aran needs roughly 380 washes to reach max HP with Hyper Body by level 140, so about 90 INT from gear while leveling is enough.
claims.say: arans need ~90 int gear while leveling to wash to max hp

claims.text: A Dark Knight or Paladin needs about 180 washes for max HP by level 140, while a Hero needs a few less because Heroes get more base HP.
claims.say: dk/pally need ~180 washes by 140, heroes a bit fewer

claims.text: Buccaneers need more washes than warriors because their max HP skill only arrives in 2nd job and is weaker than the warriors' 1st-job version.
claims.say: buccs need more washes, their hp skill is weaker and later

claims.text: Low-HP classes like thieves, bowmen and Corsairs need far more INT gear to wash; one calculation puts thieves and bowmen near 360 INT and Corsairs near 400.
claims.say: thieves, archers and sairs need hundreds of int gear to wash

claims.text: Estimates for how much gear INT a Buccaneer needs to wash to max HP by level 140 range from about 160 to 240.
claims.say: buccs need roughly 160-240 int gear to wash by 140

claims.text: Raising a Hero's Enrage past level 20 needs a mastery book that mainly comes from Horntail, so it can be hard to get.
claims.say: enrage past 20 needs a book, mostly from horntail

claims.text: Achilles is especially worth maxing for a Hero who never HP washed and has a low HP pool.
claims.say: unwashed hero? max achilles, it helps a lot

claims.text: Holy Shield protects the party from status ailments; even at level 10 it is a big help at Zakum.
claims.say: holy shield blocks status effects, great at zakum

claims.text: Of Holy Shield, Infinity and Mana Reflection, Bishops usually raise Holy Shield first as the most useful of the three.
claims.say: raise holy shield before infinity or mana reflection

claims.text: Mana Reflection does not lower the magic damage you take, even from Skelegon lasers, despite rumors that it does.
claims.say: mana reflection doesn't cut magic damage you take

claims.text: The skills a Bishop really needs are Maple Warrior, Genesis and Bahamut, and they are also the hardest to raise because they need mastery books.
claims.say: bishops need mw, genesis and bahamut most

claims.text: Keep spare SP saved so you can raise Genesis and Maple Warrior right away once you find their mastery books.
claims.say: save sp for genesis and mw books

claims.text: Maxed Bahamut plus a decent Angel Ray is enough for a Bishop to solo Capt. Latanica.
claims.say: max bahamut plus angel ray can solo capt latanica

claims.text: One point in Resurrection can be enough when you play with a Buccaneer, whose Time Leap resets skill cooldowns.
claims.say: 1 resurrection is fine if a bucc can time leap it

claims.text: Arans can train at Mysterious Path 3 from about level 50 to 60.
claims.say: aran 50 to 60? mysterious path 3 works

claims.text: From level 60 to 70 an Aran gets very fast exp on Windraiders.
claims.say: aran 60 to 70, go windraiders, exp is fast

claims.text: A gun user's maximum damage is roughly (DEX x 3.6 + STR) / 100 x weapon attack, so DEX and weapon attack both scale it directly.
claims.say: gun max dmg is about (dex x 3.6 + str)/100 x attack

claims.text: INT adds a small amount to attack-spell damage by itself, on top of the magic attack it provides.
claims.say: int adds a little spell dmg beyond the matk it gives

claims.text: Multi-target attack spells deal the same damage to every monster they hit, whether they hit one or fifteen.
claims.say: mob spells hit every target for the same dmg

claims.text: Heal's damage against undead follows a different formula from attack spells.
claims.say: heal dmg has its own formula

claims.text: Critical bonus damage is applied after monster defense is subtracted.
claims.say: crits are applied after defense

claims.text: Poison Breath on Master Death Teddys gives a Fire/Poison mage excellent exp from about level 55 until Poison Mist is maxed around 80.
claims.say: fp: poison breath at mdts is great exp from 55 to 80

claims.text: Putting 28 or more points into Poison Breath during 2nd job pays off for Fire/Poison training, though some players say it barely saves time.
claims.say: 28+ in poison breath in 2nd job pays off for fp

claims.text: A Fire/Poison mage who skips Element Composition can put those points into maxing Partial Resistance, which helps when fighting Papulatus.
claims.say: skipping element compo? max partial resist for pap

claims.text: Shadow Shifter adds a separate chance to dodge attacks on top of normal avoidability, which makes it very strong for a low-DEX, high-avoid Shadower in both bossing and training.
claims.say: shifter stacks on your avoid, huge for low dex shads

claims.text: One Shadower order: max Boomerang Step, then max Shadow Shifter while leaving Maple Warrior low, which finishes Shadow Shifter around level 144.
claims.say: max bstep, then shifter, keep mw low till later

claims.text: Another Shadower route is Shadow Shifter to 11, a single point in Taunt, and then building Assassinate.
claims.say: or go shifter 11, 1 taunt, then assassinate

claims.text: Mastery books for Assassinate 30 are very rare and costly, a big reason many Shadowers level Shadow Shifter before Assassinate.
claims.say: assassinate 30 books are rare, most take shifter first

claims.text: Assassinate at level 21 is already usable while training, not just on bosses, and breaks up the routine.
claims.say: assassinate 21 is fine to use while training too

claims.text: Final Attack is a worthwhile warrior pick: it adds free follow-up hits without MP and speeds up kills, even though you cannot control when it triggers.
claims.say: fa is worth it on warriors, free extra hits

claims.text: For Crusaders, Final Attack also helps build combo orbs faster.
claims.say: fa helps saders stack combo orbs faster

claims.text: Final Attack can trap you at bosses: it may fire just when you need to move, and one player died at Zakum after being knocked toward a body while it went off.
claims.say: careful, fa can lock you in place at zakum

claims.text: Final Attack is considered good for warriors but weak for bowmen.
claims.say: fa is good on warriors, weak on bowmen

claims.text: The SP Final Attack takes would otherwise go into weaker skills like Iron Body or Endure, so most warriors keep it unless they go hybrid.
claims.say: skip fa and your sp ends up in iron body, not worth it

claims.text: To become a bowman you need level 10 and at least 25 DEX; go to Henesys and talk to Athena Pierce in the bowman building on the far right side.
claims.say: lv10 with 25 dex, go see athena pierce in henesys

claims.text: DEX is the bowman's core stat and drives damage; STR comes second, mainly raising minimum damage so hits are steadier.
claims.say: dex is your main stat, str just steadies your min damage

claims.text: Rule of thumb for STR: bow users keep STR about 5 above their level, crossbow users keep STR equal to their level.
claims.say: bow: str = level + 5, xbow: str = level

claims.text: Low-STR build: cap base STR around 75 and meet weapon STR needs with gear such as a Zakum Helmet, a STR cape and STR clothes.
claims.say: low str: cap str around 75, use str gear and a zhelm

claims.text: Super low-STR build: bowman overalls only need DEX and some carry STR, so a STR-scrolled overall, Zakum Helmet and STR cape let you equip high bows with almost no base STR; it costs more.
claims.say: super low str: str overall, zhelm and str cape, pricier

claims.text: STR-less build: put every AP into DEX and use weapons with no stat requirement, such as Maple weapons or the Bow of Magical Destruction.
claims.say: strless = all dex, use maple bows or a bomd

claims.text: Crossbows carry slightly more clean attack than bows of the same level and use a stronger damage formula, so a crossbow can hit harder with less listed attack.
claims.say: xbows have more att and a better damage formula

claims.text: Whether bows shoot faster than crossbows is disputed: the author's unbuffed timing had bows slightly ahead, while others found all normal-speed weapons fire at the same rate, especially with a booster.
claims.say: bow vs xbow speed is debated, most say same with booster

claims.text: Max The Eye of Amazon: the extra range lets you fight from farther away and take fewer hits.
claims.say: max eye of amazon, more range means fewer hits taken

claims.text: The Blessing of Amazon need not be maxed; many archers put points in Focus for its avoid instead, while others prefer Blessing's permanent accuracy, which stacks with Bless.
claims.say: blessing of amazon is optional, lots go focus instead

claims.text: Second job at 30: talk to Athena Pierce, follow Henesys's top platform right through the portal to the job instructor, collect 30 Dark Marbles, and bring the reward back to Athena.
claims.say: 2nd job: see athena, then the instructor, get 30 dark marbles

claims.text: Choosing Hunter or Crossbowman locks your weapon for good: Hunter skills only work with bows, which are faster, and Crossbowman skills only with crossbows, which are stronger.
claims.say: hunter = bows and speed, xbowman = crossbows and power

claims.text: Bow Mastery adds a little accuracy and raises your minimum damage, making hits more consistent.
claims.say: bow mastery raises your min damage and acc

claims.text: Final Attack : Bow only triggers off early attacks like Arrow Blow or Double Shot, never 3rd or 4th job skills; if you take it, max it, since a few points are wasted.
claims.say: final attack: max it or skip it, its dead after 3rd job

claims.text: Soul Arrow : Bow lets you shoot without using arrows, freeing use slots, but attack-boosting arrows stop adding damage while it is active.
claims.say: soul arrow saves arrows, but special arrows add no att

claims.text: Power Knock-Back damages and shoves back several monsters right in front of you, useful when something spawns on top of you and you cannot shoot.
claims.say: pkb shoves mobs off you when theyre too close to shoot

claims.text: Henesys Hunting Ground I can be worked floor by floor: snails and mushrooms at the bottom for about 10-15, the slime floor for 13-18, and Orange Mushrooms with Stumps for 15-20. It is usually very busy.
claims.say: hhg1: bottom floor at 10, slimes mid teens, orange shrooms till 20

claims.text: Henesys Party Quest opens at level 10 and beats grinding for low levels, but the exp stops being worth it at around level 20.
claims.say: hpq is good from 10, stops being worth it near 20

claims.text: Pig Beach gives strong exp from about 16 to 23 on a mostly flat map. If potions are tight, stay on the upper right platform where the spawn is softer, and watch for the Iron Hog that turns up there.
claims.say: pig beach 16-23, low on pots? stay on the top right ledge

claims.text: Caution Falling Down has a dense spawn of Octopus and Blue Mushroom, which are scarce elsewhere, so it is good exp at 21-30 and a handy stop for their quest items. Its two small platforms are easy to share.
claims.say: caution falling down = octopus and blue shroom farm for quests

claims.text: Dungeon, Southern Forest IV is a narrow, quiet map of Horny and Green Mushrooms; once they die in one hit, it beats Kerning City Party Quest for exp at 23-30 unless you need mesos.
claims.say: one-shot horny shrooms? southern forest dungeon iv beats kpq

claims.text: Kerning City Party Quest takes levels 21-30. It is often crowded, so if a few tries to get in fail, go train instead of waiting.
claims.say: kpq is 21-30, if you can't get in after a few tries go grind

claims.text: Kerning City Party Quest rewards make it a strong meso source, and its exp is decent when the leader solves the stages quickly.
claims.say: kpq rewards are great mesos, exp needs a quick leader

claims.text: Ant Tunnel I with Horny and Zombie Mushrooms gives more exp for their HP than Wild Boars for 26-35. The bottom floor is best but crowded, so start on the upper floors and work your way down.
claims.say: ant tunnel 1 at 26-35, start on the high floors and work down

claims.text: Orbis Tower <20th Floor> is narrow, so Jr. Sentinels pile up; they give a bit less exp for their HP than boars but drop more mesos and hit softer, a good spot at 28-38 when short on cash.
claims.say: jr sentinels in orbis tower 20f, more mesos than boars

claims.text: Land of Wild Boar II beats the first boar map: no Jr. Boogies, fewer players and a smaller layout. Once Wild Boars die in one hit, loop it clockwise to keep spawn flowing. Good from 28 to 40.
claims.say: boar map ii over i, no jr boogies and less crowded

claims.text: Monster Carnival is for levels 30-50 and pits two parties against each other; with several rooms per channel it is much easier to join than Ludibrium Party Quest.
claims.say: cpq is 30-50 and way easier to get into than lpq

claims.text: Coins dropped in Monster Carnival trade at Spiegelmann for level 30-50 weapons, so poorer players can gear up there, and they also buy the valuable Spiegelmann's Necklace.
claims.say: cpq coins get you free 30-50 weapons or the spiegelmann necklace

claims.text: Ludibrium Party Quest takes levels 35-50, but its exp gets weak past 40, so it is best run in your late 30s.
claims.say: lpq is 35-50 but do it before 40, exp drops after

claims.text: The Burnt Land I and II hold fast Fire Boars that are fair exp in the late 30s if they die in one hit, and they drop Arwen's Glass Shoe.
claims.say: fire boars at burnt land, late 30s, they drop arwen's glass shoe

claims.text: On Eos Tower 100th Floor, Ratz gather on the thin platforms; just climb up and down killing everything. Good for 37-42, and Ludibrium Party Quest is nearby for a change of pace.
claims.say: ratz at eos tower 100f for 37-42, climb and kill

claims.text: Ludibrium Maze Party Quest takes levels 51-70, is simple to learn and a run takes only a few minutes; empty your Use slots first because the prizes pile up fast.
claims.say: lmpq is 51-70, clear your use tab, prizes stack up quick

claims.text: Orbis Party Quest takes levels 51-70 and gives steadier exp than the maze quest, and any class can contribute equally.
claims.say: opq gives steady exp for any class from 51

claims.text: Practice Field: Easy Level is only a fallback when the beginner field is full, since its two platforms make the dummies spawn about half as fast.
claims.say: easy level field only if the beginner field is full

claims.text: The Forest of Golem with Mixed and Dark Stone Golems is steady training from the 50s once Mixed Golems die in two hits; bring one or two partners to keep its four platforms clear and pack plenty of HP potions.
claims.say: golems at forest of golem, party up and bring hp pots

claims.text: Cloud Park VI still gives fair exp at 63-70 if Luster Pixies die in one hit, and their exchange-quest items sell from a shop; use a route that keeps both the upper ledges and the big bottom platform spawning.
claims.say: luster pixies at cloud park vi, 63-70, their etc sells

claims.text: Nightmares in a study room of the haunted house give great exp for their HP in a small flat room but burn many potions; aim for a reliable two-hit kill. Good for about 40-57.
claims.say: nightmares in the haunted house study, bring tons of pots

claims.text: Monsters above your level give you accuracy and damage penalties, so moving to a higher-level spot too early means missing often and hitting weakly.
claims.say: mobs above your level cut your accuracy and damage

claims.text: Jr. Newtie parties give decent exp and usually have a Priest casting Holy Symbol.
claims.say: jr newtie parties are decent exp and usually have hs

claims.text: Many Priests in Jr. Newtie parties just sit and cast Holy Symbol instead of healing the attackers, so bring plenty of your own potions.
claims.say: priests at newties often just hs, bring your own pots

claims.text: Ellin Forest, where the Ellin Forest Party Quest starts, is reached by going to Helios Tower in Ludibrium and passing through it.
claims.say: ellin pq is reached through helios tower in ludibrium

claims.text: For a sword-using Page the maple weapon options are the Maple Soul Singer and the Maple Sword, and they feel weak unless paired with an attack shield.
claims.say: maple soul singer and maple sword are meh without an att shield

claims.text: For mages, INT and Magic Attack both raise total magic, but INT also adds a little extra damage, more MP gain and magic defense, so a point of INT is worth slightly more.
claims.say: for mages 1 int is a bit better than 1 magic attack

claims.text: For physical attackers one weapon attack outweighs one point of main stat, so a cape that gained attack from a Chaos Scroll beats one scrolled for stats.
claims.say: for physical classes 1 att beats 1 main stat on gear

claims.text: Ice/Lightning Arch Mages are great at clearing big groups thanks to Blizzard, their ultimate, but add little in boss fights.
claims.say: i/l are amazing mobbers with blizzard but meh at bosses

claims.text: Buccaneers are wanted in boss parties for Time Leap, which resets the party's skill cooldowns, and Speed Infusion, which raises the party's attack speed.
claims.say: bossing parties want a bucc for time leap and speed infusion

claims.text: Big Bang is a charge skill: a full charge hits much harder than a quick release, and you can't chain full-charge shots back to back.
claims.say: big bang only hits hard fully charged, can't spam it

claims.text: You can't Teleport while charging or firing Big Bang, which makes repositioning awkward when training with it.
claims.say: no teleporting while you charge big bang

claims.text: Big Bang fizzles if you release it in the air or get knocked back at the moment of release, so stand on the ground when you let go; jump casting it is very hard.
claims.say: let big bang go on the ground or it fizzles

claims.text: Since knockback cancels the release, Big Bang is unreliable at bosses with constant map-wide hits such as Horntail and Pink Bean.
claims.say: big bang flops at ht and pb, knockback cancels it

claims.text: Big Bang's hit area is fairly small, so it isn't the map-clearing skill many players expect.
claims.say: big bang's range is small, not a map clearer

claims.text: A Dawn Warrior's Final Attack extra hit lands with a short delay, roughly half a second, after the attack that triggers it, such as Brandish, instead of hitting instantly.
claims.say: dw final attack procs a moment after the brandish, not instantly

claims.text: Chief Bandits around 81 can train on Wolf Spiders; once Band of Thieves reaches the mid-20s, exp picks up noticeably and potion use drops a lot.
claims.say: wolf spiders get way better once bot is mid 20s

claims.text: INT is the only stat that changes HP or MP growth: each level adds about a tenth of your total INT as extra MP. STR and DEX do nothing for HP.
claims.say: only int affects mp gain, str doesnt add hp

claims.text: AP Reset is lossy for HP and MP: pulling a point out removes the most a point can give, while putting one in gives the least.
claims.say: ap resets on hp/mp always give the worst roll

claims.text: So it is better to add HP with level-up AP along the way than to swap MP into HP with resets later, especially for warriors, magicians and pirates, whose max HP/MP increase skills don't apply to reset points.
claims.say: add hp as you level, washing late is worse

claims.text: Warriors gain 24-28 HP per level and 20-24 per AP put in HP, plus the Improving Max HP Increase bonus; their MP grows only 4-6 per level.
claims.say: warriors get 24-28 hp a level plus the hp skill

claims.text: Magicians gain only 10-14 HP per level and 6-10 per AP put in HP.
claims.say: mages only get 10-14 hp per level

claims.text: Bowmen and thieves gain 20-24 HP per level and 16-20 per AP put in HP; an AP put in MP gives 10-12.
claims.say: archers and thieves get 20-24 hp per level

claims.text: Beginners gain 12-16 HP per level, and an AP put in HP gives 8-12.
claims.say: beginners get 12-16 hp per level

claims.text: Warriors get 200-250 HP at 1st job; Fighters get another 300-350 HP at 2nd job, while Pages and Spearmen get 100-150 MP instead.
claims.say: fighters get the big hp bonus at 2nd job

claims.text: Magicians get 100-150 MP at 1st job and 450-500 MP at 2nd job, but no HP from either.
claims.say: mages get a big mp bump at 2nd job, no hp

claims.text: Bowmen and thieves get 100-150 HP at 1st job, then 300-350 HP and 150-200 MP at 2nd job.
claims.say: archers and thieves get 300ish hp at 2nd job

claims.text: A warrior's HP floor is about level x 24 + 172, or level x 24 + 472 for a Fighter after 2nd job; HP can't be washed below it.
claims.say: warrior hp floor is about level x 24 + 172

claims.text: A magician's HP floor is about level x 10 + 64, and a 2nd-job bowman's or thief's is about level x 20 + 378.
claims.say: mage hp floor is about level x 10 + 64

claims.text: The MP floor that limits HP washing is about level x 22 + 488 for 2nd-job magicians, level x 14 + 148 for 2nd-job bowmen and thieves, and level x 4 + 59 for Fighters (100 more for Pages and Spearmen).
claims.say: you can't wash mp below your class's mp floor

claims.text: Apart from damage, DEX raises accuracy and avoidability, and LUK raises avoidability and accuracy.
claims.say: dex and luk both add accuracy and avoid

claims.text: Steal can take any kind of item a monster drops, including Monster Book cards, skill books, Pieces of Time, potions, ores and throwing stars.
claims.say: steal can grab any drop, even cards and skill books

claims.text: Some quest items can be stolen and some can't; it is inconsistent, so test each one.
claims.say: some quest items can be stolen, not all

claims.text: Steal no longer gives duplicate items; that was patched out long ago.
claims.say: steal doesn't dupe items anymore

claims.text: Fire/Poison mages can keep misting Twisted Jesters for a very long stretch, from the 50s into the high 70s, though it gets tedious.
claims.say: you can mist twisted jesters from 5x to late 7x as fp

claims.text: Galloperas heal themselves, so a Fire/Poison mage with little Explosion can't finish them fast enough to train there well.
claims.say: gallos heal up, bad for fp with low explosion

claims.text: Wolf Spiders gave a high-70s Fire/Poison mage poor exp.
claims.say: wolf spiders werent good exp for fp at 78

claims.text: Sharp Eyes stays one of the best party damage buffs, which keeps Bowmasters and Marksmen welcome in boss runs.
claims.say: sharp eyes is one of the best party dmg buffs around

claims.text: Bring some ranged attackers to Targa and Scarlion; parties made only of melee classes get chaotic there.
claims.say: bring ranged to targa and scarlion, all melee is chaos

claims.text: Expect your first few solo attempts at Papulatus to fail; soloing it takes practice.
claims.say: most people fail their first pap solo, keep at it

claims.text: Fire/Poison wizards can level quickly in 2nd job by mixing Monster Carnival with Poison Breath training on Twisted Jesters.
claims.say: f/p 2nd job: cpq plus poison breath on twisted jesters

claims.text: For Fire/Poison mages, levels 70 to 80 are a slow, painful grind after a fast 2nd job.
claims.say: f/p 70 to 80 is a rough grind, push through

claims.text: You can level on exchange quests all the way to 30, but they slow down from about 23, cost a lot and need plenty of storage, so mix in normal training near the end of first job.
claims.say: exchange quests work till 30 but get slow and pricey after 23

claims.text: If nobody invites you to Monster Carnival at 30, train on Teddies for a while and try again; the Carnival entry is in Ludibrium, and smart play counts as much as damage there.
claims.say: nobody takes you to cpq at 30? train on teddies and retry

claims.text: Straw Target Dummies spawn in big numbers and suit mobbing skills, while Voodoos and Hoodoos come four at a time and die one by one; dummies have less HP and exp, so you overkill them as you level.
claims.say: dummies are for mobbing, voodoos are one at a time

claims.text: A Sniper with one point in Blizzard and good gear can start on Squids as early as level 71.
claims.say: snipers with 1 blizzard can hit squids around 71

claims.text: Archers who raise Arrow Rain or Arrow Eruption first should train where mobs bunch up, like Gryphons, pirates or Gobies, while Strafe-first archers do better on strong monsters killed one at a time.
claims.say: rain first = mobbing maps, strafe first = single target maps

claims.text: The bottom of Ant Tunnel I has a mostly safe ledge from which an archer can hit both the lowest floor and the ledge above; only the odd Zombie Mushroom dropping down reaches you.
claims.say: ant tunnel 1 has a safe snipe ledge at the bottom for archers

claims.text: On an Ant Tunnel map with no climbing, sweep it from top to bottom and change channel to land back at the top; never let the bottom fill up, since there is no safe spot to shoot from down there.
claims.say: sweep ant tunnel top to bottom, cc to get back up top

claims.text: Ariant Party Quest is a competition rather than a team effort, so it is easy to join, and the exp you get depends on how well you compete.
claims.say: ariant pq is free for all, exp depends on how you do

claims.text: At second job, Hunters' Arrow Bomb splashes and stuns around where it lands, reaching ledges above and below, while Crossbowmen's Iron Arrow pierces in a straight line; Hunters suit stacked maps, Crossbowmen flat ones.
