claims.say: arrow bomb hits up and down, iron arrow goes straight through

claims.text: In Monster Carnival you heal with the match's own items and cannot pick up mesos, but the coins it drops trade for necklaces that add 1 to all stats.
claims.say: no pots or mesos in cpq, but coins buy +1 all stat necklaces

claims.text: Zombie Lupins in Monkey Forest II suit Hunters only, since Arrow Bomb splash reaches the stacked rows; go in the late 30s with maxed Bow Mastery and a decent Arrow Bomb, and their dolls sell to quest-doers.
claims.say: hunters: zombie lupins late 30s with maxed mastery and bomb

claims.text: Scuba Pepes at the bottom of Orbis Tower are a quiet late-30s spot where you shoot while swimming, so HP potion use is low; they do not bunch up, so stick to Double Shot or Arrow Blow.
claims.say: scuba pepes at the bottom of orbis tower, swim and shoot

claims.text: Jr. Yetis are worth hunting only for their 60% glove attack scroll drop; one long climb makes their map poor for training.
claims.say: hunt jr yetis only for the 60% glove att scroll

claims.text: In the 50s a Hunter can stay on Zombie Lupins instead of Straw Target Dummies: the exp is about the same and the map is far emptier.
claims.say: hunters in their 50s: zombie lupins, same exp, less crowded

claims.text: Mysterious Path 3 has a high spawn, a jeep you can shoot from and a chance at Steely Throwing-Knives, but it needs lots of climbing and moving around.
claims.say: mp3 has a jeep snipe spot and steelies can drop

claims.text: From 70 to 80, Strafe-first archers do best at Lower Ascent while Arrow Rain-first archers suit Twisted Jesters.
claims.say: 70s: strafe first at lower ascent, rain first at twisted jesters

claims.text: From 80 to 110, Jr. Newties and Galloperas are the fastest solo exp, while partying at Gobies is the more economical choice.
claims.say: 80-110: newties or galloperas fast, gobies cheaper

claims.text: Past 110, Jr. Newtie parties work well with a Bishop on the upper ledge and the archer shooting from below.
claims.say: 110+: newtie party, bishop up top, archer below

claims.text: From 120 up, Skelegon parties backed by Holy Symbol give the fastest exp for archers.
claims.say: 120+: skelegon parties with holy symbol are fastest

claims.text: Wolf Spiders are the archer's main drop-hunting spot from level 80 up, where you may lose mesos until a valuable drop pays it all back.
claims.say: 80+ archers drop hunt at wolf spiders

claims.text: From 100 up, the pirates by Herb Town are a strong meso spot if you can afford to spend on potions.
claims.say: 100+: herb town pirates for mesos if you can pay for pots

claims.text: Pirate Party Quest is a fun break from grinding for archers in their 70s through 90s.
claims.say: ppq is a fun break from grinding in your 70s-90s

claims.text: Henesys Party Quest needs a party of three, and its bonus stage is full of Pigs and Ribbon Pigs.
claims.say: hpq needs 3 people, bonus stage is full of pigs

claims.text: A new 4th-job Dark Knight usually spends the first levels raising Berserk to 20, since it boosts damage for both training and bossing.
claims.say: new drk? berserk to 20 first, helps training and bossing

claims.text: Alongside Berserk, a Dark Knight can take Beholder to 10 early because its mastery boost makes damage more consistent.
claims.say: beholder to 10 early on drk, steadier damage

claims.text: Dark Knights should keep at least one point in Rush from the start of 4th job.
claims.say: drk: put 1 point in rush right away

claims.text: After Berserk and Beholder, the next Dark Knight priority is Power Stance to 20 or 30, so attacks are not interrupted by knockback.
claims.say: drk after zerk and beholder, get power stance up

claims.text: Past Power Stance, a common Dark Knight order is Maple Warrior, then Hex of the Beholder, then maxing Rush.
claims.say: drk after stance: maple warrior, then hex, then max rush

claims.text: Hex of the Beholder is mainly worth raising for its weapon attack and accuracy buff.
claims.say: hex of the beholder is for the attack and accuracy buff

claims.text: Berserk stops at 20 unless the Dark Knight finds and successfully uses its mastery book to unlock level 30.
claims.say: zerk past 20 needs the mastery book, and it can fail

claims.text: Beholder is the base Dark Knight summon skill; Aura of the Beholder and Hex of the Beholder are separate skills that add effects to the summoned Beholder.
claims.say: beholder is the base skill, aura and hex are add-ons

claims.text: Only Explorer classes can enter the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest; Cygnus Knights and other newer classes are kept out.
claims.say: cwkpq is explorers only

claims.text: The Sigils inside Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest are each activated by a particular Explorer class, so the party needs a mix of classes.
claims.say: cwkpq sigils need the right explorer class, bring a mix

claims.text: At a boss, a Crusader does more damage by building combo orbs with a few attacks and then using Panic than by spamming Power Strike at full orbs.
claims.say: charge orbs then panic, beats spamming power strike

claims.text: Each combo orb raises the damage of following attacks, and finishers such as Panic spend the orbs on one big hit.
claims.say: orbs boost each hit, panic spends them on a big one

claims.text: A Beginner loses no exp on death, one of the perks of never taking a job.
claims.say: beginners dont lose exp when they die

claims.text: A permanent Beginner has weak damage, a narrow gear choice and no real attack skill besides Three Snails, so levelling is slow and kills are easy to steal.
claims.say: perma beginners hit weak and only have three snails

claims.text: When rolling stats for a permanent Beginner, put as much as you can into STR, about 10 to 13, and keep DEX, INT and LUK at 4 or 5.
claims.say: roll 10-13 str with the rest at 4 or 5 for a perma beginner

claims.text: Each DEX point gives a Beginner 0.8 accuracy; add only enough DEX to hit your training monsters every time, and none early on since Maple Island mobs are easy to hit.
claims.say: add just enough dex to always hit what you train on

claims.text: INT is useless to a permanent Beginner and LUK adds only a little accuracy and avoid, so leave both alone unless you want a LUK novelty build.
claims.say: dont add int or luk on a perma beginner

claims.text: Do every quest on Maple Island before leaving; together they give a good share of the exp to level 10 and their rewards help even funded players.
claims.say: do all the maple island quests before you leave

claims.text: A regular-DEX Beginner adds just enough DEX to hit their targets and the rest to STR; it is cheap and avoids accuracy problems, at the cost of somewhat lower damage.
claims.say: regular dex beginner: enough dex to hit, rest into str

claims.text: A low-DEX Beginner stops DEX at about 30 to 50, puts the rest in STR and wears DEX and accuracy gear; damage is higher but gear costs more and fewer spots work.
claims.say: low dex beginner: 30-50 dex, rest str, wear dex gear

claims.text: A dexless Beginner puts every AP into STR and relies on lots of DEX and accuracy gear; it hits hardest, close to a warrior until around 40, but gear is costly and only low-avoid mobs are viable.
claims.say: dexless beginner hits hardest but needs pricey acc gear

claims.text: Scroll a Beginner's weapon and gloves for attack, shoes for speed, hat and eye accessory for accuracy, and top or cape for STR.
claims.say: scroll weapon and gloves for att, hat for acc, shoes for speed

claims.text: A Frozen Tuna is the best weapon a Beginner can use; if you own one, pick it over everything else.
claims.say: if you got a frozen tuna use it, best beginner weapon

claims.text: From level 15 a Gold Surfboard is the Beginner weapon to get: fast, strong and cheap; a Hard Briefcase will do if you are broke.
claims.say: lv15 get a gold surfboard, fast and cheap

claims.text: At 60 a good Blood Snowboard is very cheap and lasts a Beginner ten levels; a White Mop at 65 or a Maple Glory Sword at 64, with its big accuracy bonus, are the alternatives.
claims.say: lv60 blood snowboard is cheap and lasts till 70

claims.text: At 70 a Maple Snowboard carries a Beginner for a long time; at 95 the Red Surfboard is next, or a Sky Ski if you need accuracy.
claims.say: lv70 maple snowboard, lv95 red surfboard

claims.text: Facestompers are the best shoes thanks to their weapon attack bonus but cost a fortune; Yellow Snowshoes with extra DEX are a cheaper choice from level 60.
claims.say: facestompers are best, yellow snowshoes are the budget pick

claims.text: A common cape path: Old Raggedy Cape at 25, Icarus Cape at 42, a Pink or Yellow Adventurer Cape at 50 (Yellow if you will scroll it), then a pricey Pink Gaia Cape at 60.
claims.say: cape: raggedy at 25, icarus at 42, adventurer cape at 50

claims.text: For a pendant, Spiegelmann's Necklace is fine; from level 50, a Silver Deputy Star from Crimsonwood Keep is a great upgrade if you can afford it.
claims.say: spiegelmann necklace is fine, silver deputy star at 50 is better

claims.text: At level 42 get a Bone Helm; clean, it beats every other hat at its level.
claims.say: lv42 get a bone helm, best clean hat for the level

claims.text: The Zakum Helmet is the best hat around, with 15 to every stat, 20 accuracy and avoid and high defense; for a Beginner it adds roughly 40 accuracy in total, solving accuracy trouble.
claims.say: zakum helm is the best hat, huge accuracy for beginners

claims.text: The Zakum Helmet drops from Zakum and cannot be traded; you need level 50 and the Zakum prequests done to enter, so many players pay a Zakum group for a looting spot.
claims.say: zakum helm needs lv50 and the zakum prequests, cant trade it

claims.text: From 10 to about 13 (15 if unfunded) a Beginner trains like a warrior at Henesys Hunting Ground I, then moves to the Slime Tree map, Southern Forest I.
claims.say: train hhg1 till 13, then go to the slime tree

claims.text: Once a Beginner can one-shot Pigs, Pig Beach is a long-term spot through the 20s.
claims.say: once you one shot pigs, camp pig beach in your 20s

claims.text: A permanent Beginner who wants Kerning City Party Quest will usually have to lead the party, since few parties invite Beginners who struggle to hit anything there.
claims.say: as a perma beginner you gotta lead your own kpq party

claims.text: In the 30s a Beginner can handle Wild Boars: Land of Wild Boar has more boars on a big map, Land of Wild Boar II fewer on a small one; Ant Tunnel I is also good but crowded.
claims.say: 30s: wild boars or ant tunnel 1, watch for kill stealers

claims.text: Monster Carnival is the best exp for a Beginner in the 30s and 40s, though you will usually need a higher-level friend's party to get in.
claims.say: cpq is the best exp for beginners in their 30s and 40s

claims.text: In the early 40s, Psycho Jacks are great training for a Beginner who can two-shot them, as the spawn is calm and the exp is good for their toughness.
claims.say: early 40s psycho jacks are great if you two shot them

claims.text: Once a Beginner hits hard enough, many 40s spots open up: Jr. Cellions, Brown Teddies, Fire Boars, Sakura Cellions, Ticks, Tick-Tocks, Jr. Wraiths, Kiyos and Sand Dwarfs.
claims.say: hit hard enough and jr cellions, teddies, fire boars open up

claims.text: From the 50s into the 60s, Ludibrium Maze Party Quest is a Beginner's best option, giving good mesos and decent exp.
claims.say: 50s and 60s beginners should run lmpq

claims.text: Rushing only the first two stages of Orbis Party Quest gives exp similar to Ludibrium Maze Party Quest but no rewards, and Beginners get invited to it more easily.
claims.say: rush opq gives about lmpq exp, no rewards, easier invites

claims.text: Past level 70 a Beginner can barely train, so most leech in a party instead, often off a Bishop because Genesis covers a huge area.
claims.say: past 70 most beginners leech, usually off a bishop

claims.text: For a warrior, accuracy comes from DEX and LUK only; STR adds none, so a DEX-less warrior has to find accuracy in gear, scrolls and skills.
claims.say: str gives no accuracy, only dex and luk do

claims.text: Cheap accuracy for a DEX-less fighter: pass 100% accuracy or DEX scrolls on gloves and overall, and wear a hat that gives accuracy.
claims.say: dexless? 100% scroll your gloves and overall, wear an acc hat

claims.text: A DEX-less fighter should aim to get a Zakum Helmet in the 50s, since its accuracy covers much of what the build lacks.
claims.say: dexless warrior? grab a zhelm in your 50s for the acc

claims.text: Trading a STR-scrolled Pink Adventurer Cape for a DEX-scrolled one costs a DEX-less fighter little damage and buys extra accuracy.
claims.say: swap your str pac for a dex pac if you need more acc

claims.text: Maxing Sword Mastery adds a big chunk of accuracy, which is a major help to a DEX-less fighter in its twenties and thirties.
claims.say: max sword mastery, the acc saves a dexless fighter

claims.text: A suggested leveling path for a low-accuracy fighter: Kerning City Party Quest until 30, Sakura Cellions until 35, then Monster Carnival up to 50.
claims.say: kpq till 30, sakura cellions till 35, then cpq to 50

claims.text: Caution: Falling Down is decent training for a DEX-less fighter in the mid twenties but becomes slow by about level 30.
claims.say: caution falling down is fine mid 20s, slow by 30

claims.text: Many Heroes choose a Red Katana despite lower attack than other high-level one-handed swords, because it reportedly swings slightly faster and so does more damage over time at bosses.
claims.say: red katana swings a bit faster, better boss dps

claims.text: When an item will take both 10% and 30% scrolls, use the risky 30% ones first so a boom doesn't destroy scrolls that already passed.
claims.say: put the 30%s on first, then the 10%s, so a boom hurts less

claims.text: Night Raven's Claw is a level 90 claw that needs only LUK and no DEX, ideal for DEXless thieves; it has slightly less attack than the level 90 claw that also needs DEX.
claims.say: night ravens claw is the lv90 claw for dexless thieves

claims.text: Night Raven's Claw is earned through Joko's exchange quests and is hard to get.
claims.say: night ravens claw comes from joko's exchange quests

claims.text: Balanced Fury stars are very hard to make: they need all three Tao pieces, including the rare Tao of Harmony, plus a lot of Black Crystals.
claims.say: balanced fury needs all 3 taos and lots of black crystals

claims.text: The Crimson Arcglaive polearm has a DEX requirement, so DEX still matters for warriors who want to use it.
claims.say: crimson arcglaive needs dex to equip

claims.text: For claw users one point of weapon attack is worth more than several points of LUK, so a higher-attack claw beats stacking a bit more LUK.
claims.say: 1 claw attack beats a few luk points

claims.text: The level 130 elemental staff needs no LUK and carries more magic attack than the level 163 LUK staff once the LUK requirement is counted, so a LUKless Arch Mage should not switch to LUK for the cheaper weapon.
claims.say: lukless mage: dont go luk for the lv163 staff, lv130 is better

claims.text: Apart from LUKless weapons and Doomsday, wands and staves that require LUK gain about as much magic attack as they add in LUK requirement, so the extra attack is cancelled out.
claims.say: luk staves: extra matk just cancels the extra luk req

claims.text: The level 103 and level 163 LUK elemental staves come out equal in practice, and the 103 is the better buy thanks to its lower level and LUK requirements.
claims.say: lv103 and lv163 luk staves are equal, 103 is easier to wear

claims.text: A strong Bishop or Arch Mage goes after a high-INT scrolled Zakum Helmet, an INT overall, gloves with INT and magic attack, INT and magic attack earrings, a magic attack shield and a good cape.
claims.say: mage endgame: int zak helm, int overall, matk gloves, earrings

claims.text: Bishops favour a Doomsday Staff as their weapon, while Arch Mages look for elemental wands instead.
claims.say: bishops want a doomsday staff, archmages want e-wands

claims.text: Mage gear gives the least power per meso spent: weapon-attack classes can buy attack on gloves and shoes, while each extra INT for a mage is costly.
claims.say: mages get the least power per meso spent on gear

claims.text: With equally scrolled gear, a LUK-less mage always has more total magic attack than a mage who adds LUK normally.
claims.say: same gear, lukless mage always has more magic than luk mage

claims.text: An islander, a Beginner who never leaves Maple Island, can do most of their leveling on Orange Mushrooms.
claims.say: islander? orange mushrooms are your main grind

claims.text: For islanders, a STR-based build and a DEX-based build train at nearly the same speed, so the stat choice barely changes leveling.
claims.say: str or dex islander, leveling speed is about the same

claims.text: Brawlers build like warriors with STR as the main stat and DEX second, but unlike warriors they need DEX to meet the stat requirement on their knuckles.
claims.say: brawler is str main, dex second, knuckles need dex

claims.text: When rolling a future brawler, aim for INT and LUK at 4 each, and make sure you have 20 DEX by level 10 for the first pirate advancement.
claims.say: roll 4 int 4 luk, have 20 dex for 1st job pirate

claims.text: Unfunded first-job build for a future brawler: max Somersault Kick, then max Flash Fist, put 1 point in Dash, and finish by maxing Bullet Time by level 30.
claims.say: max somersault kick, then flash fist, 1 dash, rest bullet time

claims.text: Players disagree on maxing Flash Fist or Somersault Kick first; the case for the kick is that hitting several mobs at once levels faster, the case for the fist is that it has almost no delay.
claims.say: some max flash fist first, i go kick first since mobbing is faster

claims.text: If you can afford DEX or accuracy gear you do not need to max Bullet Time; stop around 11 and put the remaining first-job points into Dash for more speed.
claims.say: funded? skip maxing bullet time, dump the rest into dash

claims.text: Somersault Kick can be used with any weapon equipped or even bare-handed, which makes it a flexible early attack.
claims.say: somersault kick works with any weapon or none at all

claims.text: Dash is not a timed buff like Haste: you trigger it by double-tapping a direction key, and it stops once you halt or turn around, so you recast it often.
claims.say: dash is double tap arrow, it drops when you stop or turn

claims.text: Bullet Time raises accuracy and avoidability, which matters most for pirates without accuracy gear.
claims.say: bullet time gives acc and avoid, good if you lack acc gear

claims.text: At second job, max Improve MaxHP before anything else.
claims.say: max improve maxhp first after 2nd job

claims.text: Raise Knuckle Mastery to 5 early so you can learn Knuckle Booster, get the booster to about 5 for a usable buff, then keep adding to mastery.
claims.say: get knuckle mastery 5 asap to unlock knuckle booster

claims.text: Level Corkscrew Blow early in second job because it gives the best damage in Monster Carnival, where most players train from 30 to 50.
claims.say: push corkscrew blow early, it's your best skill for cpq

claims.text: After Corkscrew Blow is maxed, max Double Uppercut for single targets, then Backspin Blow, then MP Recovery, and finish Knuckle Booster and Knuckle Mastery; one point in Oak Barrel is enough.
claims.say: then double uppercut, backspin blow, mp recovery, finish booster

claims.text: A common high-level tactic is to knock a group of monsters into a corner with Backspin Blow and then finish them with the big attacks.
claims.say: backspin blow mobs into a corner then finish them off

claims.text: To become a pirate, travel to Nautilus Harbor and talk to Kyrin once you reach level 10.
claims.say: pirate job advance is kyrin at nautilus harbor, lv 10

claims.text: Around level 15 to 18, Pig Beach is a good place for a pirate to hunt.
claims.say: at 15-18 try pig beach

claims.text: If you cannot get into a Kerning party or get bored of it, hunt Wild Boars in your 20s.
claims.say: no kpq party? go kill wild boars

claims.text: In Monster Carnival you can farm coins and arrange with the other party to take turns winning.
claims.say: in cpq you can farm coins and trade wins with the other team

claims.text: If you can kill Selkie Jr. in two hits, they are one of the best spots in the 50s; they are found in Singapore.
claims.say: if you 2-hit selkie jrs in singapore, best spot in the 50s

claims.text: Pandas in Territory of Wandering Bear are good from the 50s into the 60s; the maps are flat, which suits Corkscrew Blow.
claims.say: pandas at territory of wandering bear, flat maps suit corkscrew

claims.text: Well-funded brawlers (gear like a Pink Adventurer Cape, Zakum Helmet and Stormcaster Gloves) can train on Voodoos and Hoodoos from the late 50s through the 60s.
claims.say: late 50s with good gear? try voodoos and hoodoos

claims.text: Very well-funded brawlers in their 60s can train on Captains and Krus, which spawn densely and close together.
claims.say: rich? captains and krus have tight spawns for 60s

claims.text: Comparing builds with equal gear, a low-DEX brawler (just enough base DEX for the current knuckle plus a STR-scrolled overall) hits hardest; dexless is close behind and a regular-DEX build trails.
claims.say: low dex with str gear hits hardest, regular dex falls behind

claims.text: Third-job core: max Stun Mastery, Energy Charge, Transformation and Shockwave; one route takes Stun Mastery and Energy Charge with Energy Blast first, the other rushes Transformation and Shockwave first.
claims.say: 3rd job: max stun mastery, energy charge, transform, shockwave

claims.text: In fourth job your skill build depends largely on which mastery books you find or pass, so plan around the books you get.
claims.say: 4th job build depends on which mastery books you get

claims.text: Max Time Leap for bossing, since resetting your cooldowns lets you use Super Transformation more often.
claims.say: max time leap for bossing, more super transform uptime

claims.text: A Booster raises weapon speed by two steps, turning a Normal(6) bow or crossbow into Fast(4).
claims.say: booster bumps weapon speed 2 steps, normal 6 to fast 4

claims.text: To convert an attack delay to attacks per minute, divide 60000 by the delay in milliseconds; a 720 ms attack is about 83 per minute.
claims.say: attacks per min = 60000 / delay in ms, 720ms is ~83

claims.text: For a normal LUK magician, reroll the starting stats until STR and DEX are both 4; a LUKless mage wants 4 in every stat except INT.
claims.say: roll mage with 4 str 4 dex

claims.text: A normal magician adds 4 INT and 1 LUK every level, while a LUKless magician puts all 5 points into INT.
claims.say: mage ap: 4 int 1 luk per level

claims.text: On Maple Island a weak future magician gets the safest exp from snails, and can skip the quests that send you after other monsters.
claims.say: on maple island just kill snails

claims.text: On Maple Island, Pio's recycling quest rewards a chair that helps an unfunded player, and Rain's Maple quiz is cheap extra exp.
claims.say: do pio's quest for a chair and rain's quiz for exp

claims.text: To become a Magician at level 8, climb to the top of Ellinia, take the portal into the job chamber and talk to Grendel the Really Old.
claims.say: lv8 mage job: top of ellinia, talk to grendel

claims.text: A cleric-bound magician can take 1 Energy Bolt, max Improving Max MP Increase early with a few points of Improving MP Recovery, then split MP Recovery and Magic Claw, max Magic Claw, and max Magic Guard last.
claims.say: 1 energy bolt, max mp increase, then magic claw, magic guard last

claims.text: Never put more than 1 point in Energy Bolt and skip Magic Armor entirely; Magic Claw and Magic Guard are worth far more.
claims.say: only 1 energy bolt and skip magic armor

claims.text: A magician with spare mesos for potions can put Magic Claw ahead of Improving MP Recovery for faster kills.
claims.say: if youre rich, put claw before mp recovery

claims.text: Improving MP Recovery scales with character level and keeps working while you attack, unlike the warrior HP recovery skill.
claims.say: mp recovery skill scales with level, works while attacking

claims.text: Magic Armor only helps briefly, since it only lowers physical damage and later buffs cover it, so the points belong in Magic Guard.
claims.say: magic armor falls off fast, take magic guard instead

claims.text: Energy Bolt stops at walls and steep edges, while Magic Claw passes through walls, hits harder, and stays a magician's main attack until the late 30s.
claims.say: magic claw goes through walls, energy bolt doesnt

claims.text: Magic Guard matters little early on but becomes a lifesaver later against monsters that would otherwise kill you in one hit.
claims.say: magic guard saves you from one-hit deaths later on

claims.text: Around 19 to 23, Pigs and Ribbon Pigs at Pig Beach are good for a magician; leave or steer clear if an Iron Hog is there, and go back to Slimes if potions get too costly.
claims.say: lv19-23: pigs at pig beach, watch out for iron hog

claims.text: From 24 into the 30s, Horny Mushrooms at Ant Tunnel I suit a magician; weaker players should stay in the top section, and Zombie Mushrooms are good just before 40.
claims.say: lv24-35: horny mushrooms at ant tunnel i, top part if weak

claims.text: If Ant Tunnel I is taken, Southern Forest IV with Green and Horny Mushrooms is nearly as good, though slower because of the climbing; avoid its bottom area.
claims.say: ant tunnel full? try southern forest iv

claims.text: For 2nd job, talk to Grendel, head north out of Ellinia to the forest map, climb to the NPC at the top to enter the test, gather the Dark Marbles, then take the proof back to Grendel.
claims.say: 2nd job mage: grendel, then the test north of ellinia, get marbles

claims.text: Bring around 100 Mana Elixirs and 100 White Potions into the magician 2nd job test.
claims.say: bring ~100 mana elixirs and 100 white pots to the 2nd job test

claims.text: A new cleric puts 1 point in Teleport at 30, then maxes Heal by level 40.
claims.say: cleric: 1 teleport then max heal by 40

claims.text: A solo cleric, after Heal, maxes MP Eater, then Teleport, then splits Invincible and Bless and maxes both, putting the leftovers into Holy Arrow.
claims.say: solo cleric: heal, mp eater, teleport, then bless and invincible

claims.text: A party cleric, after Heal, puts 5 in Invincible, maxes Bless, then Invincible, MP Eater and Teleport, with the leftovers in Holy Arrow.
claims.say: party cleric: heal, bless, invincible, then mp eater, teleport

claims.text: Heal damages undead monsters, so clerics gather groups of Jr. Wraiths, Zombie Lupins, Coolie Zombies, Voodoos or Hoodoos together and heal them all at once.
claims.say: heal hurts undead, gather a group then spam heal

claims.text: Heal is still a weak attack from 30 to 35, so keep using Magic Claw on Horny Mushrooms.
claims.say: lv30-35 cleric: still claw horny mushrooms

claims.text: Zombie Lupins in Monkey Forest I and II suit clerics around 45 to 55: heal whenever two or more are in range, and sell the Cursed Dolls they drop for good mesos.
claims.say: lv45-55: heal zombie lupins, sell the cursed dolls

claims.text: Around 50 to 55 the Ludibrium Maze Party Quest is an option for a cleric, although groups tend to prefer attackers.
claims.say: lmpq works around 50, parties prefer attackers though

claims.text: Wraiths at Line 1 <Area 4> in the Kerning Subway give good exp for a cleric who has Teleport; a pet with Meso Magnet and Item Pouch helps because there is little time to loot.
claims.say: wraiths at line 1 area 4, bring teleport and a looting pet

claims.text: From around 75, clerics can leech at Dreamy Ghosts by gathering them toward a strong attacker who does the killing; Heal works well for that mobbing.
claims.say: 75+: mob dreamy ghosts to an attacker for leech

claims.text: Heal replaces HP potions until 3rd job; when healing yourself keep a margin of two or three hits, and top up party members whenever they are below full.
claims.say: heal before youre 2-3 hits from death, keep party topped

claims.text: Bless gives the party accuracy, which helps low-DEX warriors hit, and parties expect a cleric to provide it.
claims.say: parties expect bless for the accuracy

claims.text: Teleport makes a cleric the fastest 2nd job, quicker than Haste even at level 1, and makes party quest areas such as the Orbis Party Quest lobby much easier.
claims.say: teleport is faster than haste, great in opq lobby

claims.text: A maxed MP Eater saves a lot on mana potions; the author trained several levels at Voodoos without drinking any.
claims.say: max mp eater, you barely need mana pots

claims.text: Thieves get most of their damage from LUK; DEX is the secondary stat and is needed mainly to meet the DEX requirements on claws, daggers and thief clothing.
claims.say: luk is your damage stat, dex is only for gear requirements

claims.text: Any AP put into DEX beyond what your current weapon and clothes require is AP taken from LUK, so hold DEX at the requirement and put everything else in LUK.
claims.say: dont add dex past what your gear needs, rest goes in luk

claims.text: For a normal-DEX thief the base DEX targets are about 25 at level 10, 40 at 20, 60 at 30, 80 at 40, 90 at 50 and 100 at 60, set by the claws and clothes used at those levels.
claims.say: normal dex thief: 40 at 20, 60 at 30, 80 at 40, 100 at 60

claims.text: Past level 60 a normal-DEX thief adds about 10 DEX every 10 levels: 110 at 70, 120 at 80, 130 at 90, 140 at 100, 150 at 110 and 160 at 120.
claims.say: after 60 its +10 dex per 10 levels, 140 dex at 100

claims.text: Early claw steps and their DEX needs: Steel Titans at level 15 (30 DEX), Bronze Igor at 20 (40), Meba at 25 (50), Steel Guards at 30 (60) and Bronze Guardian at 35 (70).
claims.say: steel titans needs 30 dex, igor 40, meba 50, guards 60

claims.text: Black Mamba (level 80) needs 120 DEX, Casters (90) needs 130 and Red Craven (100) needs 140; the Craven is a favourite claw to scroll thanks to solid attack and easy availability.
claims.say: red craven at 100 needs 140 dex, popular claw to scroll

claims.text: A low-DEX build pulls DEX from equipment such as tops, bottoms, capes, helmets, shoes, gloves and eye or ear accessories, keeping base DEX lower so the spare AP can go into LUK.
claims.say: low dex: let your gear cover dex so more ap goes into luk

claims.text: When worn gear gives DEX you do not need, drop your base DEX by that much and move to a claw with a higher requirement, so the gear's DEX actually does something.
claims.say: lower base dex by what your gear gives, then use a better claw

claims.text: The Zakum Helmet gives both DEX and LUK (15 each), so a low-DEX thief wearing it can shift 15 base DEX into LUK, roughly three levels' worth of AP.
claims.say: zakum helm lets you move 15 dex into luk, like 3 levels of ap

claims.text: DEX gear generally sells for much less than LUK gear because fewer players want it, which makes low DEX the cheaper route to extra damage.
claims.say: dex gear is cheap cuz nobody wants it, low dex saves mesos

claims.text: A dexless thief leaves base DEX at 25, the amount needed to become a thief, at every level.
claims.say: dexless means base dex stays at 25 the whole way

claims.text: Dexless claw users stick to claws with no DEX requirement, such as Garnier (level 10), Maple Claw (35), Maple Kandayo (43) and Maple Skanda (64), and look for LUK on gear instead of DEX.
claims.say: no-dex claws: garnier, maple claw, maple kandayo, maple skanda

claims.text: Dexless claws have low attack for their level, so dexless users fall behind DEX-claw users unless their LUK gear makes up for the missing weapon attack.
claims.say: dexless claws are weak, you need lots of luk gear to keep up

claims.text: An extreme low-DEX thief keeps 25 base DEX yet wields DEX-requirement claws like Black Mamba or Casters, getting all the needed DEX from heavily DEX-scrolled equipment.
claims.say: 25 base dex with a mamba works if your gear is dex scrolled

claims.text: Lucky Seven and Triple Throw ignore the stat window damage range; their max damage is 5.0 x LUK / 100 x weapon attack and their min is 2.5 x LUK / 100 x weapon attack.
claims.say: l7 and triple throw max = 5 x luk / 100 x watk

claims.text: For a claw user, total weapon attack is the claw plus the stars being thrown plus attack on capes, shoes and gloves; total LUK is base LUK plus every LUK bonus on gear.
claims.say: your watk is claw + stars + att on your gear

claims.text: Dividing total LUK by total weapon attack shows how many LUK points one attack is worth right now; use that ratio to judge whether a LUK or an attack upgrade adds more damage.
claims.say: luk divided by watk = how much luk one att is worth

claims.text: One weapon attack is worth several LUK points, so thieves should put attack scrolls on their weapon and gloves first and treat LUK and DEX scrolls as secondary.
claims.say: scroll for att first, luk and dex come after

claims.text: Shoe jump scrolls also add DEX: the 10% and 30% kinds give +3 DEX, +5 jump and +1 speed, and the 60% and 70% kinds give +1 DEX and +2 jump, handy for low-DEX builds.
claims.say: shoe jump scrolls give dex too, good for low dex

claims.text: Helmet accuracy scrolls and face accessory avoidability scrolls both add DEX too (+2 on the 10% and 30% kinds, +1 on 60% and 70%), another way for low-DEX thieves to gain DEX.
claims.say: helm acc and face avoid scrolls add dex too

claims.text: Overall DEX scrolls give +5 DEX, +3 accuracy and +1 speed at 10% or 30%, and +2 DEX with +1 accuracy at 60% or 70%.
claims.say: overall dex 60% gives +2 dex, the 10% gives +5

claims.text: More scroll types add DEX than LUK, and LUK scrolls are harder to find, so getting DEX from gear is easier than getting LUK, which favours low-DEX builds.
claims.say: way more dex scrolls than luk ones, low dex is easier

claims.text: LUK can be scrolled onto earrings, overalls, tops and capes; top and cape LUK scrolls give +2 LUK at 60% and +3 at 10%.
claims.say: scroll your top and cape for luk, +2 each at 60%

claims.text: Weapon attack scrolls give +2 attack at 60% and +5 at 10%; glove attack scrolls give +2 at 60% and +3 at 10%.
claims.say: claw att 60% gives +2, glove att 60% gives +2 too

claims.text: Your total INT decides roughly how much MP you gain per level, so INT gear or INT scrolls help a thief who plans to HP wash.
claims.say: int gear means more mp per level, nice if you plan to hp wash

claims.text: HP washing: on level up put one AP into HP, then use an AP Reset to take a point out of MP and put it in LUK or DEX; for a thief each wash trades 12 MP for 16 to 20 HP.
claims.say: hp wash: ap into hp, then ap reset one from mp into luk

claims.text: You can only keep washing while MP stays above a floor that grows with level; for a thief that floor is about 14 x level + 148 MP.
claims.say: thief mp cant go below about 14 x level + 148 when washing

claims.text: Stormcaster Gloves (level 50) carry +5 attack and are worth scrolling further with glove attack scrolls.
claims.say: stormcaster gloves have +5 att, scroll them for more

claims.text: A top and bottom give 14 upgrade slots (7 each) against 10 on an overall, so a well-scrolled two-piece set eventually beats an overall on stats.
claims.say: top + bottom gives 14 slots, an overall only 10

claims.text: Thief overalls are scarce (one for males, two for females), so many thieves scroll common overalls like the Blue Sauna Robe or Bathrobe for Men, which need no DEX and can be worn early.
claims.say: lots of thieves scroll a sauna robe, no dex req and 10 slots

claims.text: A Red Katina needs 140 DEX, the same as a Red Craven, so its own DEX bonus is wasted unless your claw needs more; scroll Katinas for LUK rather than DEX.
claims.say: katinas need 140 dex like a craven, scroll em for luk

claims.text: Weaker bosses like Pianus and Papulatus can be done with a few friends or even solo to keep all the loot, but their drops are worth much less than Zakum or Horntail drops.
claims.say: pap and pianus can be soloed but the drops arent great

claims.text: Self-scrolling means buying cheap scrolls, scrolling gear yourself and selling the good results; well-scrolled gear sells for far more than the scrolls cost, but failed scrolls lose money.
claims.say: buy cheap scrolls, scroll gear and sell the good ones

claims.text: The Amoria Party Quest requires married characters, and its bonus stage can give Onyx Apples, which Zakum and Horntail groups always want, making it a steady source of income.
claims.say: apq needs you married, bonus stage can give onyx apples

claims.text: Onyx Apples give a +100 weapon attack boost, so boss runners are always buying them and they sell well.
claims.say: onyx apple is +100 att, boss runners always buy them

claims.text: The Gachapon at Zipangu's Mushroom Shrine is the most popular one because it hands out rare items more often than the others.
claims.say: mushroom shrine gacha is the popular one for rares

claims.text: When soloing Papulatus with Puppet, wait for the current puppet to die before casting a new one; recasting too early can leave the second form not targeting the puppet and pinning you.
claims.say: at pap dont recast puppet till the old one dies or it loses aggro

claims.text: Papulatus' second form hits far harder than the first, so a ranged soloer should keep it focused on the Puppet rather than try to tank it.
claims.say: pap 2nd form hits way harder, keep it on your puppet

claims.text: Assassinate's final hit can be cancelled, which lets a Shadower use it more safely when bossing.
claims.say: you can cancel assassinates last hit, safer on bosses

claims.text: Holding down an attack key fires just as fast as mashing it; only charge skills can be used quicker by tapping.
claims.say: just hold the attack key, mashing isn't any faster

claims.text: Brawler skills such as Corkscrew Blow, Backspin Blow and Double Uppercut take clearly longer to reuse when they connect with monsters than when used on empty air.
claims.say: corkscrew and backspin are slower to spam when they hit mobs

claims.text: Spell Booster speeds up cast time for most mage spells, and Explosion is the one spell whose speed also depends on how fast your wand or staff is.
claims.say: explosion is the only spell that cares about wand speed

claims.text: Spell Booster also makes plain wand and staff swings faster, so a fast wand like Evil Wings together with Spell Booster suits the Amoria Party Quest.
claims.say: evil wings plus spell booster is great for apq

claims.text: A booster does not shorten how long Piercing Arrow takes to charge up.
claims.say: booster won't make piercing arrow charge any faster

claims.text: A 4th job I/L Arch Mage can train on Crimson Guardians by running laps: Seal them from the lower safe platform, jump to the spawn platform to cast Ice Demon, and let Ifrit do much of the killing.
claims.say: il can lap crimson guardians with seal, ice demon and ifrit

claims.text: Monsters hit by Ice Demon take noticeably more damage from Ifrit's fire attacks than neutral targets, so an I/L should cast Ice Demon on a group before Ifrit works on it.
claims.say: cast ice demon first, ifrit hits way harder after

claims.text: Bring a big stack of Holy Water for Crimson Guardians; All Cure Potions run out fast there, and having a priest along cuts how many cures you burn.
claims.say: bring lots of holy water for crimson guardians

claims.text: Standard first-job build for a future cleric: 1 Energy Bolt, Improved MP Recovery to 5, max Improved MaxMP Increase, then max Magic Claw, finish Improved MP Recovery, then max Magic Guard.
claims.say: 1 energy bolt, mp recovery 5, max maxmp increase, claw, then guard

claims.text: First-job magician prerequisites: Magic Claw needs Energy Bolt at 1, Improved MaxMP Increase needs Improved MP Recovery at 5, and Magic Armor needs Magic Guard at 3.
claims.say: claw needs 1 bolt, maxmp increase needs mp recovery 5

claims.text: Improved MaxMP Increase grants extra max MP on every level-up and on every AP point put into MP, so it pays to take it early.
claims.say: maxmp increase gives extra mp per level and per ap, get it early

claims.text: Heal restores HP for you and nearby party members and also damages undead monsters, reaching up to six targets at once.
claims.say: heal hits undead mobs too, up to 6 at once

claims.text: Cleric prerequisites: Invincible needs Heal at 5, and Bless needs Invincible at 5.
claims.say: invincible needs heal 5, bless needs invincible 5

claims.text: Bless raises the whole party's accuracy, avoidability, weapon defense and magic defense for a while.
claims.say: bless buffs party acc, avoid and both defenses

claims.text: MP Eater gives each attack a chance to absorb part of the monster's max MP, helping a cleric keep MP up.
claims.say: mp eater steals mp from mobs when you hit them

claims.text: Teleport moves you a short distance; higher skill levels cost less MP and reach slightly farther.
claims.say: teleport costs less mp and goes a bit farther as you level it

claims.text: Dispel cures party members of certain status ailments and can also strip buffs off monsters.
claims.say: dispel cures your party and strips mob buffs

claims.text: Holy Symbol raises the exp you and your party get from monsters; it needs Dispel at 3 and only gives its full bonus when more than two party members are nearby.
claims.say: holy symbol boosts party exp, best with 3+ people around

claims.text: Elemental Resistance lowers the damage you take from elemental magic attacks.
claims.say: elemental resistance cuts elemental magic damage

claims.text: Shining Ray is the priest's holy mobbing spell, hitting up to six monsters.
claims.say: shining ray is your holy mob attack, hits up to 6

claims.text: Mystic Door opens a portal to the nearest town for the whole party; it needs Dispel at 3 and uses one Magic Rock per cast.
claims.say: mystic door to town for the party, costs a magic rock

claims.text: Summon Dragon calls a dragon that attacks one monster at a time, and each summon uses a Summoning Rock.
claims.say: summon dragon hits one mob at a time, uses a summoning rock

claims.text: Doom turns up to six monsters into snails for a short time, using one Magic Rock per cast.
claims.say: doom turns up to 6 mobs into snails, costs a magic rock

claims.text: Amoria Party Quest requires you to be married and carrying your wedding ring, and to be at least level 40; there is no upper level limit.
claims.say: apq: lv 40+, married, wedding ring on you, no max level

claims.text: Go in with a full party of six that has at least one male and one female character; a single-gender party cannot clear the first stage.
claims.say: apq party needs 6 with at least one guy and one girl

claims.text: Your spouse does not have to come along, but the couples bonus stage only opens for a party holding three married couples.
claims.say: spouse is optional, couple bonus needs 3 couples

claims.text: Useful buffs for the Amoria run are Haste, Hyper Body, Heal, Holy Symbol, Sharp Eyes and Slow; fourth jobbers with Maple Warrior and Rush speed up the boss.
claims.say: bring haste, hb, heal, hs, se or slow for apq

claims.text: To enter, collect 10 Lip Lock Keys from Indigo Eyes and Crystal Boars on the maps leading to Amos' Training Ground, then trade them to Amos for an entry ticket.
claims.say: get 10 lip lock keys from indigo eyes and crystal boars

claims.text: If you lead, enter the final waiting room last so you can still recruit a replacement if someone disconnects; once inside, the party cannot change.
claims.say: leader goes in last in case someone dcs

claims.text: The run has a 75-minute limit, but a normal run takes only about 10 to 15 minutes.
claims.say: apq usually takes 10-15 min, plenty of time

claims.text: Stage 1: after the leader talks to Amos, three green portals appear but only one works, so try each until you drop down the map.
claims.say: stage 1: three green portals, only one is real, try them

claims.text: Stage 1: males take the hidden rock portal on the right, females the left one; clear both areas fully, and kill the fairies fast because they stun you and buff nearby monsters' attack.
claims.say: guys take the right rock, girls the left, kill fairies first

claims.text: Stage 2 works like the Orbis Party Quest sealed room: five members hang on three ropes and Amos says same or different after each wrong guess; seven misses summon monsters but the answer does not reset.
claims.say: stage 2: like opq ropes, use amos's same/different hints

claims.text: Stage 3 has nine platforms; five people must stand on the right ones, one per platform. Each wrong try summons monsters, and the number of slimes equals how many people stand on correct platforms, so count before killing.
claims.say: stage 3: count the slimes, that's how many spots are right

claims.text: Stage 3 method: four people on the top row and one on the bottom-left; count slimes, then shift the bottom person right each try. Bottom spots that raise the slime count are correct; move top people down onto them.
claims.say: test the bottom row one spot at a time, then move people down

claims.text: Stage 4 needs 50 Cupid Code Pieces from the monsters; the five non-leaders gather 10 each and give them to the leader, who hands them to Amos.
claims.say: stage 4: 10 cupid code pieces each, give them to the leader

claims.text: Before turning in the stage 4 pieces, make sure nobody is AFK or lagging, since the next stage can wipe the run; laggy players should drop to the lowest graphics and mute sound, and everyone should equip a fast weapon.
claims.say: before stage 5 make sure nobody is afk or lagging

claims.text: Stage 5 is a race to the right ahead of invincible Bloctopuses, Block Golems, King Block Golems and Rombots that kill on touch; break the gates with normal attacks and push through the lava jets.
claims.say: stage 5: run right, break the gates, dont touch the block mobs

claims.text: All six members must survive stage 5 and reach the door together; if anyone dies or disconnects before the boss, the run cannot continue.
claims.say: if anyone dies in stage 5 the run fails

claims.text: Smokescreen works in stage 5 and keeps anyone standing inside it from being hit by the chasing monsters.
claims.say: smokescreen keeps you safe from the stage 5 mobs

claims.text: The final stage boss has three forms: a regular Balrog, then Crimson Balrog, then Geist Balrog itself, which teleports away, raises its defenses and casts Dispel.
claims.say: apq boss goes balrog, crimson balrog, then geist

claims.text: Stand on the thorns whenever you can to dodge Geist Balrog's claw attack; priests should cast Holy Symbol from the thorns because the map has no ropes.
claims.say: stand on the thorns to dodge geist's claw

claims.text: When Geist Balrog casts Dispel, rebuff right away, especially Magic Guard for magicians.
claims.say: rebuff right after geist dispels, mages recast magic guard

claims.text: When Geist Balrog flies off, stand on the floating platforms and press up, since they are hidden portals around the map; try to keep him low, pin him in a corner with Rush, and Slow him if you can.
claims.say: chase geist with the hidden portals on the floating platforms

claims.text: The first two boss forms are weak to holy, but the final Geist Balrog form resists everything, so clerics, priests and bishops should switch to Magic Claw.
claims.say: holy does nothing to geist, clerics use magic claw

claims.text: Players who lag badly or cannot survive big hits should wait out the boss fight in a corner on the thorns.
claims.say: if you're weak or laggy, sit on the thorns in a corner

claims.text: Geist Balrog drops the Geist Fang; give it to the leader, who turns it in to Amos. During that talk never press End Chat or Escape, or the party loses the bonus stage.
claims.say: leader: don't hit end chat when giving amos the fang

claims.text: Geist Balrog can also drop a Balrog Claw, an untradeable material used to forge Bosshunter equipment.
claims.say: geist sometimes drops a balrog claw for bosshunter gear

claims.text: Before the leader hands in the fang, everyone should equip their fastest weapon and rebuff Haste so the bonus stage is not wasted.
claims.say: fast weapon and haste on before the bonus stage

claims.text: A party of three guys and three girls lands in the couples bonus even without married couples; just talk to Amos there to move on to the normal bonus.
claims.say: 3 guys 3 girls and no couples? talk to amos to skip ahead

claims.text: The bonus stage gives one minute to break boxes; most drops are mesos, Gold Plates, Diamonds and ores, but the real prizes are Onyx Apples, Amorian Relaxers and scrolls.
claims.say: bonus is 1 min of boxes, hope for an onyx apple

claims.text: Onyx Apple heals most of your HP and MP and gives a large weapon and magic attack boost for several minutes, which makes it prized for Zakum and Horntail.
claims.say: onyx apples give huge att for zakum or horntail

claims.text: For the bonus stage, use a fast-swinging weapon such as a Pumpkin Spear or Red Whip and a pet equipped to loot over a wide range.
claims.say: use a fast weapon like a pumpkin spear and a looting pet

claims.text: In the bonus stage grab the Amorian use items, which make good buffs for grinding, and the earrings, which sell to shops for decent mesos.
claims.say: loot the earrings in bonus, they npc for good mesos

claims.text: Once in the boss map, all six members must stay in the map, alive or dead, for the party to reach the bonus; with three guys and three girls, everyone must stay alive.
claims.say: at the boss, all 6 must be in the map to get bonus

claims.text: After a run, collect your next 10 Lip Lock Keys right away so you are ready when the next ticket becomes available.
claims.say: farm your next 10 keys right after a run

claims.text: Max damage by weapon: two-handed swords use (STR x 4.6 + DEX), one-handed swords (STR x 4.0 + DEX) and spears (STR x 5.0 + DEX), each multiplied by weapon attack / 100.
claims.say: 2h sword is str x 4.6, 1h sword x 4.0, spear x 5.0

claims.text: Daggers use (LUK x 3.6 + STR + DEX) x weapon attack / 100, while the claw skills Lucky Seven and Triple Throw use LUK x 5.0 x weapon attack / 100.
claims.say: dagger is luk x 3.6, l7 and tt use luk x 5.0

claims.text: Bows use (DEX x 3.4 + STR) and crossbows (DEX x 3.6 + STR), multiplied by weapon attack / 100.
claims.say: bow is dex x 3.4, crossbow is dex x 3.6

claims.text: Knuckles use (STR x 4.8 + DEX) and guns (DEX x 3.6 + STR), multiplied by weapon attack / 100.
claims.say: knuckle is str x 4.8, gun is dex x 3.6

claims.text: One-handed weapon users can wear a shield scrolled for attack, extra weapon attack two-handed users never get; around +14 is a realistic figure for a 7-slot shield.
claims.say: 1h users get extra att from a shield scrolled for att

claims.text: The author saw Night Lords and Bowmasters as likely to be one-shot at Horntail, so parties of only those classes were not workable there; lineups with Heroes, Vipers or a Bishop were safer.
claims.say: nl and bm get one-shot at ht, bring tankier classes too

claims.text: An Onyx Apple adds +100 weapon attack, dwarfing ordinary attack potions like the Warrior Elixir (+12), so it greatly raises boss damage for physical attackers.
claims.say: onyx apple is +100 att, way more than any elixir

claims.text: The endgame attack gear the author assumed for every class: Stormcaster Gloves scrolled to about +15 attack, a 4-attack Pink Adventurer Cape and 2-attack Facestompers.
claims.say: stormcaster gloves, pink adv cape and facestompers for att

claims.text: A DEXless Hermit gains little from converting to low-DEX before level 100, when the DEX-hungry level 100 claws become wearable.
claims.say: dexless hermit? no need to convert before 100

claims.text: Some advise holding off on converting from DEXless until you own a well-scrolled Horntail Necklace.
claims.say: dont convert from dexless till you have a scrolled ht necklace

claims.text: Explosion hits above, below and behind you, while Fire Demon is a flat pillar in front of you that reaches only a little above your head.
claims.say: explosion hits all around you, fire demon only in front

claims.text: Range percentages in skill tables count 100% for your own character, so subtract 100% to get the reach on each side; a low-level Explosion listed at 110% barely reaches past you.
claims.say: skill range % counts 100 for you, subtract it for real reach

claims.text: For a mist-and-finish combo, Poison Mist followed by Fire Demon is preferred over Explosion because Fire Demon casts much faster.
claims.say: mist then fire demon to finish, its faster than explosion

claims.text: You can Teleport almost right after casting Fire Demon, but Explosion holds you for about two thirds of its animation, so telecast Fire Demon and jump-cast Explosion instead.
claims.say: telecast fire demon, jumpcast explosion

claims.text: Explosion stays useful on slope-heavy maps thanks to its strong downward reach; otherwise most Fire/Poison Arch Mages drop it in 4th job since Meteor Shower covers the wide-area role.
claims.say: keep explosion for slopes, meteor covers the rest

claims.text: Fire Demon keeps burning the monsters it hits and leaves them weak to ice attacks.
claims.say: fire demon burns mobs and makes them weak to ice

claims.text: In this axe hybrid build the Fighter opens at level 30 by putting every point into Axe Mastery until it sits at 19, then adds a few points to Axe Booster.
claims.say: at 30 dump sp into axe mastery first, then some booster

claims.text: Rage gets maxed right after the early Axe Mastery and Booster points, finishing around level 45.
claims.say: after mastery and a bit of booster, max rage

claims.text: Final Attack: Axe is maxed next, roughly from 45 to 55; you can also hold those SP and spend them on Final Attack in one go later.
claims.say: max axe final attack next, or save sp for it

claims.text: Power Guard is maxed from about 55 to 65, then the rest of Axe Booster, with the last Axe Mastery point and one Sword Mastery point spent at 70.
claims.say: then max power guard and finish booster by 70

claims.text: The author leaves Shout at only 2 points because he considers it nearly useless.
claims.say: shout isnt worth much, 2 points is enough

claims.text: As a Crusader the first priority is maxing Combo Attack, done by around level 80.
claims.say: as a crusader max combo attack first

claims.text: Improving MP Recovery is maxed after Coma and Panic, followed by two points in Shout.
claims.say: after coma and panic, max improving mp recovery

claims.text: The remaining Crusader SP goes into Sword Mastery and then Sword Booster, so the hybrid's second weapon is fully supported by 120.
claims.say: hybrid: finish sword mastery and sword booster by 120

claims.text: A dexless Shadower can max Boomerang Step first in 4th job as the main training skill, then spread points into Maple Warrior and Assassinate.
claims.say: shadower: max boomerang step first, then mw and assassinate

claims.text: Training alongside a Bowmaster with maxed Sharp Eyes boosts a Shadower's damage a lot.
claims.say: train with a bowmaster, maxed sharp eyes boosts your dmg a ton

claims.text: Assassinate is a disputed training skill for Shadowers; the author holds that it works well even at a low level if used properly.
claims.say: assassinate is fine for training if you use it right

claims.text: Bigfoot counts as a boss, so it can't be stunned, and it doesn't stay reliably knocked back, so standing still and shooting won't work.
claims.say: bigfoot cant be stunned and wont stay knocked back

claims.text: At Forgotten Path, cast Puppet near the middle of the high platform, which Bigfoot can't jump straight onto; when he heads toward the side platforms, hit him so he turns back, and recast Puppet the moment it dies.
claims.say: puppet mid top platform at forgotten path, recast it right away

claims.text: Puppet appears on the platform you are standing on, so to place it on a higher platform you have to stand up there when casting.
claims.say: puppet lands where you stand, so cast it from the top platform

claims.text: Bigfoot's hitbox is smaller than his sprite: the pole and hair don't hurt, and you can even jump over him on a mount, though roaming Elderwraiths make that risky.
claims.say: bigfoot's pole and hair cant hit you, his hitbox is small

claims.text: If you lose control of Bigfoot, put the Puppet beneath him so he stays on the top platform, or on the small left platform to hold him near the portal while you set up again.
claims.say: lost bigfoot? drop puppet under him or on the small left ledge

claims.text: Fight Bigfoot when nobody else is on the map; other players stir up Elderwraiths that knock down your Puppet and Leprechauns that can stun you.
claims.say: do bigfoot on an empty map, others pull elderwraiths on you

claims.text: On flat maps Bigfoot stomps on the Puppet with long invincible frames, leaving little window to hurt him; maps with an unreachable high platform work far better.
claims.say: flat maps are bad for bigfoot, hes invincible while stomping

claims.text: If Bigfoot corners you, use a return scroll instead of changing channel, which could drop you beside another Bigfoot.
claims.say: cornered by bigfoot? use a return scroll, not cc

claims.text: When adds pile up, stand in the middle of the top platform and clear them with Arrow Rain or Arrow Eruption, then go back to the Puppet method; mages could fight from there too, just very slowly.
claims.say: too many adds? clear them from the top platform, then puppet again

claims.text: Save a White Scroll for the last upgrade slot of a valuable item such as a Dragon Khanjar so a failed scroll does not use up the slot.
claims.say: use a white scroll on the last slot of a good khanjar

claims.text: An Islander is a Beginner who never leaves Maple Island, staying around Amherst and Southperry and never sailing to Lith Harbor.
claims.say: islanders never leave maple island or reach lith harbor

claims.text: Islanders level slowly past level 20, since only a handful of monster types live on the island and usable equipment is hard to come by.
claims.say: islanding gets slow after 20, few mobs and little gear

claims.text: For a starting weapon on Maple Island, pick the Hand Axe or Wooden Club over the Sword, since they have a better damage range.
claims.say: pick the hand axe or wooden club over the sword

claims.text: On Maple Island only STR really matters at first: 10 or more STR is plenty, and base DEX is enough to hit every monster on the island.
claims.say: islander: str is what matters, base dex hits everything

claims.text: Pure STR is the usual Islander build: every AP goes into STR while DEX, INT and LUK stay at 4, giving about 58 STR at level 10 and 133 at level 25.
claims.say: pure str islander: all ap in str, rest stay at 4

claims.text: A pure DEX Islander keeps 10 STR and puts everything else into DEX so its minimum damage eventually one-shots Orange Mushrooms and Pigs on every hit; a STR plus DEX build chases the same goal.
claims.say: pure dex islander aims to one shot orange mushrooms and pigs

claims.text: A mage-style Islander raises 20 LUK and 55 INT to equip the level 18 Metal Wand: STR until level 3, then LUK, then INT, and back to STR once both are met.
claims.say: mage-lander: 20 luk and 55 int to use the metal wand

claims.text: Beginners get only 6 SP for Three Snails, Recovery and Nimble Feet, so just two can be maxed; Three Snails throws a Snail Shell, Blue Snail Shell or Red Snail Shell depending on its level.
claims.say: beginners get 6 sp, enough to max two skills

claims.text: Maple Island's monsters are Snails, Blue Snails, Shrooms, Red Snails, Stumps, Slimes, Pigs and Orange Mushrooms.
claims.say: maple island mobs: snails, shrooms, stumps, slimes, pigs

claims.text: Orange Mushrooms on Maple Island can drop the level 10 Double Axe, the level 15 Leather Purse blunt weapon and White Gomushin shoes, all wearable by Beginners.
claims.say: orange mushrooms drop double axe, leather purse, gomushin

claims.text: Red Snails drop the level 18 Metal Wand and the stat-less Amethyst Earrings.
claims.say: red snails drop the metal wand

claims.text: Island armor drops: Blue Snails give the Blue One-lined T-Shirt and Grey Thick Sweat Pants, Shrooms give Ice Jeans, and Slimes give the White Bandana.
claims.say: blue snails drop shirts and pants, slimes drop bandanas

claims.text: Island scroll drops: Snails give helmet DEF 10%, Slimes bottomwear DEF 10%, Stumps topwear DEF 10%, Pigs shoes DEX 10%, and Orange Mushrooms shoes Jump 10%.
claims.say: pigs drop shoe dex 10%, orange shrooms drop shoe jump 10%

claims.text: Mai's training quests in the field east of Amherst hand you an untradable Razor dagger, a usable early weapon for an Islander.
claims.say: mai's first training gives you a razor dagger

claims.text: Maple Island quests an Islander can do include Roger's Apple, Rain's Maple Quiz series and Pio's recycling quests in Amherst, Mai's trainings, Yoona's shopping quiz, and Bari's Test west of Southperry.
claims.say: maple island has tons of quests, roger rain pio mai yoona

claims.text: Meso Guard costs nothing to cast; mesos are only taken when it absorbs damage from a hit.
claims.say: meso guard only spends mesos when you get hit

claims.text: The level 64 Maple Dark Mate dagger swings faster than most non-STR daggers, but its clean attack is only around a Kandine's.
claims.say: maple dark mate is fast but clean att is about kandine level

claims.text: A LUKless support Cleric can level mostly through party content such as Kerning City Party Quest, Ariant Coliseum, Monster Carnival and Ludibrium Maze Party Quest until 3rd job.
claims.say: support cleric can pq to 70: kpq, carnival, lmpq

claims.text: At 30 this Cleric build puts one point in Teleport and then pours SP into Heal until it is maxed around level 41.
claims.say: cleric: 1 in teleport at 30, then max heal

claims.text: This build maxes Invincible right after Heal, because Monster Carnival and Ludibrium Maze Party Quest involve a lot of contact damage.
claims.say: max invincible early if you do carnival or lmpq

claims.text: Bless can wait in a party Cleric build aimed at Monster Carnival, since the Assassins common there rarely need the extra accuracy.
claims.say: bless can wait, sins in carnival dont need the acc

claims.text: After Invincible, this build maxes Bless, then Teleport, then MP Eater, and puts the last 2nd-job points into Holy Arrow.
claims.say: then bless, teleport, mp eater, leftovers in holy arrow

claims.text: As a Priest, this build takes 1 Elemental Resistance, 3 Dispel and 1 Mystic Door, then maxes Holy Symbol first.
claims.say: priest: a point in door and dispel, then max holy symbol

claims.text: After Holy Symbol, Mystic Door gets a few more points so the door lasts longer, and Elemental Resistance is maxed.
claims.say: after holy symbol, max elemental resistance

claims.text: Shining Ray is maxed by about 102; the author delays it because in his 80s and 90s he plans to party at Gobies buffing with Bless and Holy Symbol, using Shining Ray only to lure.
claims.say: party priest can max shining ray late, by about 102

claims.text: Summon Dragon has to reach level 15 to unlock Bahamut at 4th job, so this build stops it at 15.
claims.say: get summon dragon to 15, bahamut needs it

claims.text: Dispel is finished last and Doom is left only partly leveled, since it has few real uses.
claims.say: finish dispel, doom isnt worth maxing

claims.text: The 3rd job advancement at 70 grants one bonus SP, so you have an extra point to spend at that level.
claims.say: 3rd job gives you a bonus sp at 70, dont forget it

claims.text: For a future Bishop without strong stat gear, a well-scrolled Maple Wisdom Staff or Maple Shine Wand gives more magic attack than higher-level LUK-heavy staves.
claims.say: bishop without godly gear? maple wisdom staff or shine wand

claims.text: For a future Archmage, the level 130 elemental staves give the highest magic attack and also amplify spells of their element.
claims.say: future archmage? go for the lvl 130 elemental staff

claims.text: Marksmen usually take Marksman Boost, Sharp Eyes and Maple Warrior first; after those it comes down to which mastery books you can get.
claims.say: mm: boost, sharp eyes, mw first, then whatever books you get

claims.text: Frostprey at level 11 or 21 is a decent investment, adding extra damage plus a short freeze.
claims.say: frostprey 11 or 21 is decent, extra damage and a freeze

claims.text: Blind is worth points if you spam Arrow Eruption across big mobs, such as on the top of the Skelegon map.
claims.say: blind is worth it if you spam arrow eruption a lot

claims.text: Piercing Arrow is slow for training on most maps; Arrow Eruption clears Skelegons faster, and Piercing Arrow also wants Dragon's Breath at 11 to 21 for mobbing, making it the most SP-hungry choice.
claims.say: pierce is slow to train with, eruption clears gons faster

claims.text: A mobbing Ranger build can max Inferno early, for example finishing it at 93 while Arrow Rain sits at 1.
claims.say: mobbing rangers can max inferno early, rain at 1

claims.text: A common archer build keeps STR at level plus 5 for Hunters and equal to level for Crossbowmen, then puts 4 DEX and 1 STR in each level.
claims.say: hunters keep str at level+5, xbows at level, rest dex

claims.text: Save STR points until just before your next weapon: put AP into DEX for most levels, then add STR in the last level or two to meet the bow's requirement, such as 55 STR for an Olympus at 50.
claims.say: dump dex, add str right before your next bow

claims.text: A low-STR archer meets weapon requirements with STR from gear; a gear point of STR is worth as much as one of DEX, so buy whichever piece is cheaper, and with equal funds this build hits harder.
claims.say: low str? get str from gear, buy whichever piece is cheaper

claims.text: Stop adding STR once you reach what your final bow or crossbow needs, such as a Metus or Casa Crow, counting total STR with gear, and plan ahead if a gear swap would lower your STR.
claims.say: cap str at your endgame bow's requirement, gear str counts

claims.text: STR has no effect on the HP you gain per level, but INT does add MP: roughly one extra MP per level for every 10 points of total INT.
claims.say: str doesn't give hp, every 10 int adds a bit of mp per level

claims.text: Power Knock-Back scales with DEX, not STR, so a pure STR archer built around it just does weak damage.
claims.say: power knock-back runs off dex, pure str archers don't work

claims.text: While Soul Arrow is active, the attack bonus of equipped arrows such as Diamond Arrows is not applied to damage, even though the stat window still shows it.
claims.say: soul arrow ignores your fancy arrows' attack bonus

claims.text: A Marksman cannot keep Golden Eagle and Frostprey out together; casting one replaces the other.
claims.say: golden eagle and frostprey replace each other, one at a time

claims.text: Archers can jumpshoot by pressing jump and attack at the same moment: the arrow fires from where you stood and you keep moving, which helps dodge attacks and saves a little time and potions.
claims.say: jumpshoot: hit jump and attack together to fire and move

claims.text: A Hunter can stop Final Attack from firing its extra arrow by jumpshooting, since it never triggers while airborne.
claims.say: jumpshoot if you don't want final attack to fire

claims.text: Bows and crossbows cannot use attack skills in midair, unlike claws and guns, which are meant to shoot while jumping.
claims.say: bows can't shoot midair, claws and guns can

claims.text: Jump scrolls for shoes also add DEX, unlike the shoe DEX scrolls that add only avoid and accuracy, so archers scroll shoes for jump to gain DEX.
claims.say: jump scrolls on shoes give dex, dex shoe scrolls don't

claims.text: Consider two pairs of shoes: speed-scrolled ones for big maps where every mob dies in the same number of hits, and DEX ones for maps where kills take a varying number of hits.
claims.say: keep speed shoes for 1-hit maps, dex shoes for tough mobs

claims.text: Weapon attack raises archer damage more than DEX does, since the damage range is roughly (3.4 x DEX + STR) / 100 x attack for bows, with 3.6 in place of 3.4 for crossbows.
claims.say: for archers attack beats dex, att multiplies everything

claims.text: Between a faster bow and a stronger one at the same level, such as Red Viper versus Vaulter 2000, the higher-attack bow usually deals more over time unless the attack gap is small; fast bows also lose more to monster defense.
claims.say: vaulter 2000 usually beats red viper, attack wins over speed

claims.text: A STR-less Hunter uses a War Bow until 35, then a Maple Bow, a Maple Soul Searcher at 43, a Maple Kandiva Bow at 64 and a Bow of Magical Destruction at 65; the Kandiva matches its average attack but fires faster.
claims.say: strless hunter: war bow, maple bow, soul searcher, kandiva

claims.text: A STR-less Ranger keeps pace with a normal one until about level 100, after which the normal build's higher attack pulls ahead; the build is also costly since it relies on scrolled rare gear.
claims.say: strless rangers keep up till about 100, then fall behind

claims.text: A STR-less Crossbowman can use the fast Maple Nishada, so the build now carries on past 60 much like the STR-less Hunter.
claims.say: strless xbow? the maple nishada keeps it going past 60

claims.text: Final Attack never triggers off third-job skills such as Strafe, only off earlier attacks like Double Shot.
claims.say: final attack doesn't proc off strafe or other 3rd job skills

claims.text: Fire/Poison mages can downcast Explosion: hold the down key, then press jump and the attack key together while a monster is below you.
claims.say: hold down, then jump + attack to cast explosion downward

claims.text: Downcasting stretches Explosion's reach below you to roughly double, so a monster under you can be hit even when it sits outside the normal blast range.
claims.say: downcast explosion reaches about twice as far below you

claims.text: Only Explosion can be downcast; other spells, Ice Strike included, just make you swing your weapon when used in mid-jump.
claims.say: only explosion downcasts, other spells just swing your weapon

claims.text: Downcasting Explosion is handy while training with Poison Mist, letting you hit the mobs on the platform below.
claims.say: downcasting explosion is great while misting

claims.text: A beginner needs 25 base DEX to become a thief; DEX from equipment such as gloves does not count toward it.
claims.say: thief needs 25 base dex, gear dex doesnt count

claims.text: The dexless assassin build keeps DEX at the 25 needed to advance and puts every other AP into LUK, all the way through Night Lord.
claims.say: dexless sin: stop at 25 dex, rest all luk

claims.text: Lucky Seven and Triple Throw scale from LUK and weapon attack, so the extra LUK from skipping DEX usually beats wearing a slightly stronger claw.
claims.say: lucky seven scales off luk and att, not dex

claims.text: Each DEX point gives 0.8 accuracy and each LUK point gives 0.5, so a LUK-heavy thief with only 25 DEX still has plenty of accuracy.
claims.say: luk gives thieves acc too, 25 dex is enough

claims.text: On Maple Island, kill Snails until around level 6 or 7, then Blue Snails and Shrooms until 10, doing every island quest along the way.
claims.say: snails till 6ish, then blue snails and shrooms till 10

claims.text: The thief instructor, the Dark Lord, waits at the bottom of the hideout under the bar sign in Kerning City; press up beneath the sign to go in.
claims.say: dark lord is under the bar sign in kerning, press up

claims.text: First job order for a future assassin: 1 Lucky Seven, 3 Nimble Body to open Keen Eyes, max Keen Eyes for range, max Lucky Seven, 3 Disorder, max Dark Sight, then Nimble Body.
claims.say: 1 l7, 3 nimble, max keen eyes, max l7, 3 disorder, max ds

claims.text: If you can pay for MP potions, max Lucky Seven before Keen Eyes for earlier damage; either way a future assassin leaves Double Stab at zero.
claims.say: got pot money? max lucky seven first, skip double stab

claims.text: To get in, go to the map west of Kerning City, climb the big steel construction tower using its hanging cords, step onto the sign at the top and press up in the middle.
claims.say: climb the steel tower west of kerning, press up on top

claims.text: From Perion take the portal by the dead tree to Perion Street Corner, keep taking right-hand portals through the rocky maps, climb the rope to Excavation Site I, then use top-right portals to II and III.
claims.say: perion to street corner, keep going right, then dig site

claims.text: Second job: the Dark Lord hands you a letter (keep an Etc slot open) for the instructor standing on top of the construction structure east of Kerning City.
claims.say: dark lord letter, then instructor on the tower east of kerning

claims.text: In the test map, kill monsters until you hold 30 Dark Marbles, turn them in for the instructor's proof, then give it to the Dark Lord and choose Assassin.
claims.say: collect 30 dark marbles in the test map

claims.text: Usual assassin order: 3 Claw Mastery, max Critical Throw, 2 more Claw Mastery, Claw Booster to 6, max Haste, 3 Endure, max Drain, then max Claw Mastery and put leftovers in Endure.
claims.say: 3 mastery, max crit throw, booster 6, haste, drain

claims.text: Third job: speak to Arec in El Nath, then the Dark Lord in Kerning City sends you through the Door of Dimension in Monkey Swamp II to fight his clone.
claims.say: 3rd job: arec in el nath, then dark lord, then his clone

claims.text: Kill the clone before the Tauromacis it summons; it drops the Black Charm, which the Dark Lord swaps for the Necklace of Strength to show Arec.
claims.say: kill the clone first, ignore the tauros

claims.text: Next, bring a Dark Crystal, not a Black Crystal, to the Holy Stone at Holy Ground at the Snowfield and answer its five questions; a wrong answer uses up the crystal. Its Necklace of Wisdom goes to Arec.
claims.say: bring a dark crystal to the holy stone, not a black one

claims.text: To reach the Holy Stone, head east from El Nath through the Cold Field maps, climb to Ice Valley II, take the passage up to Sharp Cliff II and enter the wooden door on the right.
claims.say: el nath east, up to ice valley 2, then sharp cliff 2

claims.text: Usual hermit order: max Shadow Partner, 5 Avenger, max Flash Jump, max Avenger, then Alchemist, Meso Up and Shadow Web, with leftovers in Shadow Meso; some put 1 in Avenger before Shadow Partner.
claims.say: max shadow partner, flash jump, avenger, then the rest

claims.text: Good 90-120 spots include Black and Red Kentaurus, Bains in Showa, Gobies in the Squid map, and past 100 Dual Birks, Bone Fish and Grim Phantom Watches.
claims.say: 90-120 kentaurus, gobies, dual birks, grim phantom watches

claims.text: Fourth job: get a recommendation from Arec, see Hellin in Leafre, and bring a Heroic Star and a Heroic Pentagon, which drop from Manon and Griffey.
claims.say: 4th job: hellin in leafre wants heroic star and pentagon

claims.text: Triple Throw and Ninja Storm depend on storybook quests linked to Zakum; a Night Lord without them should put SP into Maple Warrior and Venomous Star first.
claims.say: no zakum books? put sp in maple warrior and venom

claims.text: With Triple Throw available, start with 1 each in Triple Throw, Shadow Stars and Maple Warrior, raise Triple Throw to 20 once you have its mastery book, then Maple Warrior to 9, then Venomous Star and Ninja Storm.
claims.say: nl: triple throw first, then maple warrior 9, then venom

claims.text: A strong Night Lord can solo the Female Boss in Showa by sniping from behind the sofa and keeping her pinned against the wall with nonstop attacks.
claims.say: snipe the female boss from behind the sofa

claims.text: Most new magicians put their first point into Energy Bolt and then start raising Improved Max MP Increase.
claims.say: 1 in energy bolt then start on max mp increase early

claims.text: Warriors take their first job from Dances with Balrog in Perion at level 10.
claims.say: warrior 1st job is dances with balrog in perion

claims.text: Job tiers run 10-30 for first job, 30-70 for second, 70-120 for third and 120 onward for fourth.
claims.say: job advances at 10, 30, 70 and 120

claims.text: Pages should commit to either swords or blunt weapons, because their skills are tied to one weapon type and a hybrid loses damage.
claims.say: page: pick swords or blunts, dont mix

claims.text: Swords hit more consistently, while blunt weapons have a higher top end but a much lower minimum; by the math swords come out ahead.
claims.say: swords are steadier, blunts swing wild

claims.text: A one-handed weapon needs about 17 more weapon attack, from weapon and shield scrolls, to keep pace with a two-handed weapon's damage over time.
claims.say: 1h needs about 17 more att to match a 2h

claims.text: Two-handed weapons swing slower but hit harder and usually reach further, which helps keep monsters off you.
claims.say: 2h hits harder and reaches further

claims.text: Every scroll attempt uses up an equipment slot whether it passes or fails, and many scrolls can also destroy the item when they fail.
claims.say: every scroll eats a slot, pass or fail

claims.text: Warrior armor mostly comes as top and bottom pairs, with overalls at levels 30 and 80; tops and bottoms carry more defense and 7 slots each.
claims.say: warrior armor is top+bottom except lv30 and 80 overalls

claims.text: Warrior tops take STR scrolls and bottoms take DEX or jump scrolls, while overalls have 10 slots and give a bigger STR or DEX gain per successful scroll.
claims.say: overalls get 10 slots, scroll them str or dex

claims.text: Warrior gear only requires STR; DEX matters mostly for accuracy, so add DEX until you hit your targets reliably and put everything else into STR.
claims.say: warriors: dex only for acc, rest into str

claims.text: For accuracy, one DEX gives 0.8 and one LUK gives 0.5, so warriors gain little from scrolling for LUK.
claims.say: dex gives more acc than luk, dont scroll luk

claims.text: Normal DEX, adding DEX as your accuracy needs grow, suits new or unfunded warriors: less damage than no-DEX, but no need for pricey DEX gear.
claims.say: new and broke? go normal dex warrior

claims.text: High-DEX warriors can use the Stonetooth Sword, a fast level 100 two-handed sword needing 120 DEX, or the Night Raven's Wing, a fast level 90 one needing 95 DEX.
claims.say: high dex? stonetooth sword or night ravens wing

claims.text: STR scrolls only exist for capes, tops, overalls and shields, while DEX scrolls cover capes, bottoms, overalls, gloves, shoes, earrings and hats.
claims.say: str scrolls only for cape, top, overall and shield

claims.text: Low-DEX warriors rely on well scrolled accuracy gear and can move DEX into STR with AP Resets as their equipment improves; going all the way to 4 DEX needs heavy funding.
claims.say: low dex needs good acc gear, ap reset dex later
