claims.text: The Zakum Helmet gives all four stats plus accuracy, avoid and defense and cannot be traded, so you must be in the Zakum fight yourself; it is a top accuracy source.
claims.say: zhelm is huge acc, you have to kill zakum yourself

claims.text: Around 147 accuracy lets a warrior hit almost every late training mob and most bosses, Papulatus included, at their level; build toward it gradually.
claims.say: aim for about 147 acc over time as a warrior

claims.text: Sniper Pills from the Ludibrium potion shop are a cheap way to add accuracy.
claims.say: sniper pills from the ludi potion shop = cheap acc

claims.text: The accuracy from Bless does not stack with accuracy buffs from items such as the Sniper Pill; whichever is used later replaces the other.
claims.say: bless and sniper pills dont stack

claims.text: Good accuracy gear for warriors includes Maple weapons, DEX-scrolled gloves (cheap since most are scrolled for attack), Spiegelmann's Necklace, Mark of Naricain and the Horntail Necklace.
claims.say: acc gear: maple weapons, dex gloves, spiegelmann necklace

claims.text: Maple Warrior adds a share of your base stats only, so a stat that comes almost entirely from equipment, like 4 base DEX, gains nothing.
claims.say: maple warrior only boosts your base stats

claims.text: HP washing: level up wearing INT gear for extra MP, put AP into HP, then use AP Resets to take AP back out of MP and place it into STR or DEX.
claims.say: hp wash: int gear on level, ap in hp, reset mp

claims.text: MP cannot be reset below a minimum for your level, so the more surplus MP you build up, the more AP Resets you can turn into HP.
claims.say: more spare mp means more resets you can wash

claims.text: Warriors have the highest max HP of any class and use little MP, which makes HP washing easiest for them.
claims.say: warriors have the most hp and wash easiest

claims.text: Warriors have the lowest avoid and no movement skills, and fighting in melee range means they take more touch damage than ranged classes.
claims.say: warriors dodge the least and eat touch damage

claims.text: White Knights and Paladins lean on elemental charges: freezing and stunning lets them solo well, but their damage is weak against monsters with no elemental weakness.
claims.say: wk and pally live on charges, pick the right element

claims.text: Paladins are tough but not prized for bossing, since they depend on elements and bring only one party buff.
claims.say: pallys are tanky but not great bossers

claims.text: Recommended ranger order for levels 70-90: 1 Strafe, 5 Mortal Blow, Arrow Rain to 21, then Strafe to 20, Puppet to 6 and Silver Hawk to 9.
claims.say: 70-90: 1 strafe, 5 mb, 21 rain, 20 strafe, 6 puppet, then hawk

claims.text: Early Arrow Rain is often said to fall apart in the 80s without max Strafe, but the author's timed solo data on a Rain-first ranger showed no slow levels from 70 to 90.
claims.say: rain first works fine, no hell levels from 70 to 90

claims.text: One point in Inferno is optional, mainly to lure distant mobs such as hovering Griffeys or pirates outside Arrow Rain's range.
claims.say: 1 inferno is optional, just for luring

claims.text: Pirate method: jump-shoot Arrow Rain back and forth across the middle deck, firing once about six pirates are lined up, and climb the center sail now and then to clear the top-left ledge.
claims.say: jump shoot rain across the middle deck, hit top left from the sail

claims.text: At the pirates Strafe barely gets used because you mob constantly; save it for a lone straggler or a last surviving Captain.
claims.say: strafe is only for stragglers at the pirates

claims.text: When spawn runs thin, fire one Inferno to each side to lure pirates in, especially the top-left group toward the sail; Arrow Bomb : Bow also works, but its stun makes it a weaker lure.
claims.say: low spawn? one inferno each side pulls the pirates in

claims.text: The pirates hit hard, so potions are the main cost; some players snipe from the safe left sail to save pots, but the author stays on the main deck since bigger mobs mean much better exp.
claims.say: stay on the main deck, the safe spot costs you too much exp

claims.text: The Herb Town pirates drop lots of mesos and some valuable equips, so training there can turn a profit despite the potion bill.
claims.say: pirates drop tons of mesos, you can profit there

claims.text: A pet is strongly advised at the pirates: drops cover the ship quickly, and looting by hand wrecks your exp rate or makes you miss the valuable drops.
claims.say: bring a pet at pirates, way too much loot to grab by hand

claims.text: At Griffeys a pet is not needed since most drops fall off cliffs, but the speed from scrolled pet gear helps with the long walks between teleporters.
claims.say: no pet needed at griffeys, but extra speed helps

claims.text: At the black squids in Aqua Road a pet is unnecessary: you kill strong single targets and the map is vertical, so looting and speed matter less.
claims.say: no pet needed at black squids

claims.text: Partying at the pirates with an Ice/Lightning mage or another Rain or Eruption bowman was faster than soloing there.
claims.say: party the pirates with an i/l or another rain bowman

claims.text: A sniper can run the same early-area-skill plan with Arrow Eruption, taking 1 Blizzard instead of Inferno, probably just before leaving the pirates.
claims.say: snipers: same build with eruption, blizzard instead of inferno

claims.text: Pets pick up loot for you and, once given the matching pet items, can drink HP and MP potions for you; some pet equips also add speed or jump.
claims.say: pets loot for you and can auto pot with the right pouch

claims.text: Pet level follows closeness: pet level 10 needs 287, level 15 needs 1642, level 20 needs 5542, and the max pet level 30 needs 30000 closeness.
claims.say: pet lv 30 is 30000 closeness, lv 15 is about 1642

claims.text: Most pets learn extra commands at pet levels 10 and 20, some at 11 and 21 (Golden Pig, Rudolph, Jr. Balrog, Robot, Mini Yeti, Baby Dragon); Turkey and Porcupine also get level 30 commands.
claims.say: pets learn new commands around pet lv 10 and 20

claims.text: A pet that ignores a command is almost always below the pet level that command needs.
claims.say: pet ignoring a command? its level is too low for it

claims.text: Giving your pet commands while you wait for a ship or the subway to New Leaf City is a free way to build pet closeness.
claims.say: spam pet commands while waiting for the boat to raise closeness

claims.text: For Kenta's Advice, talk to Kenta in Aquarium, break the treasure chests outside town to collect papers A to E, and hand them to Kenta for pet closeness.
claims.say: kenta in aquarium gives pet closeness for papers a to e

claims.text: Ludibrium pet park: from Ludibrium town head left to Patricia, climb the floating steps into the portal, get the letter from the NPC there and run the jump course.
claims.say: ludi pet park is left of town past patricia, up the steps

claims.text: On the Ludibrium pet course, at the top-left blue structure simply walk off and fall instead of jumping down; you land safely on the platform below.
claims.say: top left of ludi pet course: just drop off, dont jump

claims.text: Henesys pet park: in Henesys Park press up twice at the left cat statue, walk to the far left, take the letter from Trainer Bartos and clear the jump course, which is mostly jump timing.
claims.say: henesys pet park: press up at the left cat statue in the park

claims.text: Pet equips that every pet can wear are cheaper and have 5 upgrade slots; equips made for one pet type cost more but have 7 slots.
claims.say: pet-specific equips have more slots than all-pet ones

claims.text: Meso Magnet lets your pet collect mesos and Item Pouch lets it collect items.
claims.say: get meso magnet and item pouch so your pet loots it all

claims.text: Auto HP Potion Pouch and Auto MP Potion Pouch let your pet drink HP and MP potions on your behalf.
claims.say: auto hp and mp pouches make your pet pot for you

claims.text: Wing Boots let your pet grab items from farther away, and Binoculars let it travel farther to loot.
claims.say: wing boots and binoculars widen your pet's loot range

claims.text: Magic Scales let your pet pick up drops belonging to other players once they have lain on the ground for 30 seconds or more.
claims.say: magic scales let your pet grab others' drops after 30 sec

claims.text: Item Ignore Pendant makes your pet skip any item you put on its ignore list.
claims.say: item ignore pendant stops your pet looting junk

claims.text: Dragon and Robot pets can evolve: raise one to pet level 15, buy a Rock of Evolution and take it to Garnox in New Leaf City with drops from Cold Eyes and Lupins; the new color is random.
claims.say: evolve dragon or robot pets at lv 15 with garnox in nlc

claims.text: If the evolved pet's color is not the one you wanted, you can evolve again, but that takes another Rock of Evolution and a fresh set of materials.
claims.say: dont like the evolved color? you need a new rock and mats

claims.text: From pet level 15 you can type /pet followed by text to make your pet say it, with no cooldown between lines; censored words are blocked. It gives no closeness.
claims.say: lv 15 pets can talk, type /pet then your text

claims.text: Dragon and Robot pets doing random motions on their own is normal behaviour, not a bug.
claims.say: dragon and robot pets move around on their own, its normal

claims.text: The standard sword Fighter build maxes Sword Mastery, Final Attack: Sword, Power Guard, Sword Booster and Rage.
claims.say: fighter: max sword mastery, fa, pg, booster and rage

claims.text: A hybrid sword-and-axe Hero is widely seen as pointless: swords outperform axes in practice, and once you have Brandish you only ever train with one weapon.
claims.say: hybrid sword axe hero isnt worth it, you use one weapon

claims.text: Crusaders rarely use Shout except to stun crowds or for quests; at the popular training maps it slows you down.
claims.say: shout is mostly for stuns, it slows normal training

claims.text: Some I/L wizards keep Cold Beam at the minimum and max Slow, since extra Cold Beam levels add damage but not freeze time and Slow works on bosses that move; others say a strong Cold Beam is needed to train.
claims.say: some il skip extra cold beam for slow, its debated

claims.text: Papulatus is easy to keep pinned with knockback once you are in 4th job.
claims.say: papu is easy to pin with knockback in 4th job

claims.text: Top-end Shadower gear goals include a Chaos-scrolled Pink Adventurer Cape with 7-11 attack, shoes with 7+ attack, a shield with 24+ attack and a level 120 dagger.
claims.say: endgame shad: 7+ att cape and shoes, 24+ att shield

claims.text: On the Birk map, circle the top two platforms two or three times, then sweep the bottom floor.
claims.say: at birks loop the top two floors a few times, then clear the bottom

claims.text: Death Teddies can be frozen but are not weak to ice and give less exp than Birks, so an Ice/Lightning mage finds them slow by comparison.
claims.say: death teddies felt slow for il, birks give more

claims.text: Harps can inflict Weakness, which is milder than Seal; carry All Cure Potions when training on them.
claims.say: harps cast weakness, bring all cures

claims.text: A Priest wearing a Zakum Helmet can train at Skelegons and Skelosauruses from about 105 to 120 by spamming Heal, with MP Eater keeping MP up; take care on the top ledge.
claims.say: priest 105-120: heal the skeles with a zhelm, careful up top

claims.text: A fresh Bishop's SP usually goes into Genesis and Maple Warrior, with a single point in Resurrection.
claims.say: new bishop: genesis and mw first, 1 in resurrection

claims.text: After the 4th job advancement a Bishop still has quests to finish before Genesis and Bahamut can be learned.
claims.say: after 4th job do the quests for genesis and bahamut

claims.text: Monster Carnival is open to levels 30 to 50, and you cannot drink potions inside the battlefield.
claims.say: cpq is lv 30-50 and you cant use pots inside

claims.text: Enter Monster Carnival by talking to Spiegelmann in Kerning City, Orbis or Ludibrium, who sends you to his waiting room.
claims.say: talk to spiegelmann in kerning, orbis or ludi for cpq

claims.text: In the waiting room only the party leader should talk to Spiegelmann to choose a battle room; the other members just wait.
claims.say: only the leader talks to spiegelmann

claims.text: Carnival rooms 1 to 4 take parties of 2 to 4, rooms 5 and 6 take parties of 3 to 6, and a party can wait in a room up to 3 minutes for a challenger.
claims.say: rooms 1-4 for 2-4 people, 5-6 for 3-6

claims.text: To challenge a waiting party, yours must have the same number of members and an average level within 10 of theirs.
claims.say: need same party size and avg level within 10

claims.text: When challenge pop-ups arrive, press Y to accept or N to decline instead of clicking, which keeps up with players who spam challenges.
claims.say: use y and n to answer cpq challenges fast

claims.text: A Carnival match lasts ten minutes, and the side with the higher total CP at the end wins.
claims.say: 10 minute match, most total cp wins

claims.text: Dying in the Carnival costs 10 spendable CP but no exp and you rejoin from a side room; your total CP, which decides the winner, never goes down.
claims.say: dying only costs spendable cp, not exp

claims.text: Carnival monsters drop potions, CP orbs and curse items that take effect the moment you loot them, so leave healing drops on the floor until you need them.
claims.say: cpq pots work on pickup, leave them till needed

claims.text: Faded monsters that look like they are in Dark Sight belong to the other team; you cannot hit them, so ignore them.
claims.say: faded mobs belong to the other team, ignore them

claims.text: Never summon monsters just to spend leftover CP; the other team simply earns CP by killing them.
claims.say: dont dump spare cp on summons, they just feed them

claims.text: An All Cure removes every lasting Carnival curse except Slow.
claims.say: all cure clears cpq curses except slow

claims.text: Protectors are jewel pillars that buff your own team's summoned monsters; attack the pillars of the other team's color to strip their buffs.
claims.say: break the other teams pillars to drop their buffs

claims.text: The Cancel Weapon Attack and Cancel Magic Attack protectors make that type of damage deal only 1 to the guarded monsters, so break that pillar first.
claims.say: cancel attack pillar up? break it before hitting mobs

claims.text: Rooms 1 and 2 are a flat floor with Brown Teddies and King Block Golems below and protector platforms above; mages do well there because Teleport covers the map fast.
claims.say: rooms 1-2 are flat, mages teleport around easy

claims.text: Rooms 3 and 4 hold Robos and Toy Trojans; room 3 spawns fewer due to a spawn bug while room 4 fills quickly, which suits warriors with Slash Blast and ice mages.
claims.say: rooms 3-4 are robos and trojans, great for slash blast

claims.text: In rooms 5 and 6, Robos spawn on the upper levels and Rombots on the bottom; Rombots give the most CP, so send your sturdiest attackers after them.
claims.say: rooms 5-6: strongest people farm the rombots

claims.text: Carnival monsters resist lightning, so Ice/Lightning mages deal less there; when swarmed, stand on a small platform and use Thunder Bolt, which still reaches the floor below.
claims.say: il mage swarmed? hop on a platform and thunder bolt

claims.text: Fire/Poison mages do best in rooms 5 and 6 by focusing Rombots, which do not resist fire, while the Robos there do.
claims.say: fp mages: rooms 5-6, shoot the rombots

claims.text: Clerics keep a Carnival party alive with Heal, give warriors needed accuracy with Bless, and Heal also damages the undead Master Chronos summons.
claims.say: clerics heal, bless for acc, heal hurts master chronos

claims.text: Low-level warriors miss too much for the Carnival; train until weapon mastery is maxed around 37, then start in rooms 3 and 4.
claims.say: warriors: max mastery around 37 before cpq

claims.text: Slow warriors struggle to reach protector pillars, so pair them with a mage or an assassin with Haste to break pillars.
claims.say: let a mage or haste sin break the pillars

claims.text: Spearmen help a Carnival party with Hyper Body, which keeps members alive so fewer CP are lost to deaths.
claims.say: spearman hyper body keeps the cpq team alive

claims.text: Assassins do well in rooms 1, 2, 5 and 6 but tend to get overrun by fast Toy Trojans in rooms 3 and 4 unless they have maxed Haste.
claims.say: sins avoid rooms 3-4 unless haste is maxed

claims.text: Bowmen should pick rooms 1, 2, 5 or 6; in 5 and 6 stand still and snipe Robos across platforms, while rooms 3 and 4 swarm them.
claims.say: bowmen: rooms 5-6, snipe robos across platforms

claims.text: Once Sharp Eyes, Bow Expert and Hurricane are maxed, a Bowmaster chooses among Phoenix, Concentrate, Hamstring and Maple Warrior; for boss-focused play the author leans to Phoenix for damage.
claims.say: bm after se, bow expert and hurricane? phoenix for bossing

claims.text: Phoenix adds real damage per second, but you need to stay close to your target so it stays in Phoenix's range.
claims.say: phoenix adds dps but you have to stay near the target

claims.text: Hamstring slows monsters, which helps in training when mobs get close, but it adds little in boss fights.
claims.say: hamstring helps training when mobs get close, meh for bosses

claims.text: If you usually train or boss with someone who already casts Maple Warrior, your own can wait.
claims.say: if your party has maple warrior, yours can wait

claims.text: Holy Arrow is a single-target cleric attack with strong knockback that is reliable against dark-type monsters and reaches farther than Magic Claw, though unlike Magic Claw it does not pass through walls.
claims.say: holy arrow knocks back hard and outranges magic claw

claims.text: Shining Ray is an area attack with very short reach, so a priest can keep Holy Arrow for monsters that come at you from outside Shining Ray's range; the two skills do different jobs.
claims.say: shining ray is short range, holy arrow covers the gap

claims.text: Heal only damages undead monsters and does nothing to demon-type monsters, so it is not a dependable attack outside undead maps.
claims.say: heal only hurts undead, not demons

claims.text: A typical cleric maxes Heal, Bless and Teleport first; MP Eater and Holy Arrow are the weakest picks, and which one you take depends on how well funded you are.
claims.say: max heal, bless and tele, then choose ha or mp eater

claims.text: Invincible cuts incoming damage by a percentage, so unlike a flat defence buff such as Bless it never falls off; players call it essential once you are a priest because it saves so many potions.
claims.say: get invincible, it saves a ton of pots as a priest

claims.text: MP Eater rarely pays for itself: each monster only has so much MP to drain, so well-funded clerics usually skip it.
claims.say: mp eater barely refunds mp, skip it if you have mesos

claims.text: Even a support-minded cleric should keep one real attack; Holy Arrow's knockback can push off a hard-hitting monster when you are cornered, something Magic Claw does less well.
claims.say: keep an attack even as support, ha knocks mobs off you

claims.text: Angel Ray replaces Holy Arrow in 4th job, but before 120 a cleric or priest has no other ranged single-target attack, which is the main case for leveling Holy Arrow.
claims.say: angel ray replaces ha at 4th, ha fills in until then

claims.text: Capping a warrior's base DEX at 80 gives up STR the author later regretted; with 40 fewer DEX he would still have the accuracy for what he trains on.
claims.say: 80 base dex is too much for a warrior, you lose str dmg

claims.text: Each level gives 5 AP, so 40 misplaced stat points add up to eight levels of AP.
claims.say: 5 ap a level, so 40 points is 8 levels worth

claims.text: Iron Body isn't worth SP: the defense it gives cuts only a little damage per hit, which stops mattering once monsters hit for thousands.
claims.say: skip iron body, the defense barely matters

claims.text: In first job, warriors should spend SP on Improved MaxHP Increase, Power Strike and Slash Blast before anything like Iron Body.
claims.say: 1st job: max hp increase, power strike, slash blast first

claims.text: Improved MaxHP Increase only unlocks after 5 points in Improved HP Recovery.
claims.say: put 5 in hp recovery to unlock max hp increase

claims.text: Slash Blast requires 1 point in Power Strike first.
claims.say: slash blast needs 1 point in power strike first

claims.text: A Fighter needs Final Attack to train efficiently; if SP has to come from somewhere, take it from the booster.
claims.say: fighters need final attack, cut booster first

claims.text: For Heroes, Brandish makes Power Strike and Slash Blast obsolete at 4th job, but those two carry you from 30 to 120.
claims.say: brandish replaces ps and sb at 4th, need them till then

claims.text: Paladins swap Power Strike for Blast at 4th job; until then White Knights depend entirely on Power Strike and Slash Blast, while Crusaders can also use Panic and Coma.
claims.say: white knights live on ps and sb, crusaders get panic and coma

claims.text: An I/L mage can skip Thunder Spear entirely and keep Ice Strike as the main attack all through 3rd job.
claims.say: i/l can skip thunder spear, ice strike carries 3rd job

claims.text: If Ice Strike stays your main attack, Element Composition is not worth maxing; put the points into Seal instead.
claims.say: not using composition? max seal instead

claims.text: Final Attack swinging at empty air wastes time you could spend moving, and covering the map faster is part of training faster.
claims.say: fa swings at air waste time you could spend moving

claims.text: Final Attack's follow-up lands so fast that the monster is not knocked back again, so you can take touch damage, which shows at Ghost Pirates and Dual Ghost Pirates.
claims.say: fa doesnt re-knockback, you get bumped at ghost pirates

claims.text: Crusaders still want Final Attack because it builds combo orbs faster for their big finishing attack.
claims.say: crusaders want fa to stack combo orbs faster

claims.text: Most warriors max Slash Blast before Power Strike, because hitting several monsters at once trains faster.
claims.say: max slash blast before power strike, mobbing is faster

claims.text: Points saved by skipping Final Attack can go into Endure, Improving HP Recovery, Iron Body, or a second weapon's mastery and booster.
claims.say: skipping fa? put points in endure, iron body, hp recovery

claims.text: Going lukless (AP into INT instead of LUK) is favoured: LUK only serves to meet the requirement of higher magic attack weapons like the Dragon Staff, while the Maple Wisdom Staff or Maple Shine Wand need none.
claims.say: go lukless, luk is only for weapon requirements

claims.text: Top-tier lukless magician gear costs far more than top-tier LUK gear, but by the time it matters you should have ways to earn mesos.
claims.say: godly lukless gear costs more than godly luk gear

claims.text: Improving Max MP Increase is the most valuable first-job magician skill: it adds extra MP on every level up and on AP put into MP, so max it as early as you can.
claims.say: max improving max mp increase early, it adds up

claims.text: First-job magician prerequisites: Improving Max MP Increase needs 5 points in Improving MP Recovery, Magic Claw needs 1 in Energy Bolt, and Magic Armor needs 3 in Magic Guard.
claims.say: max mp increase needs 5 in mp recovery, claw needs 1 bolt

claims.text: Magic Armor is a poor use of SP, since the weapon defense it adds does very little.
claims.say: skip magic armor, weapon def barely matters

claims.text: Standard first-job build: 1 in Energy Bolt at 8, Improving MP Recovery to 5, max Improving Max MP Increase, max Magic Claw, finish Improving MP Recovery, then max Magic Guard by level 30.
claims.say: 1 bolt, 5 mp rec, max max mp, max claw, mp rec, then guard

claims.text: Putting the very first SP into Energy Bolt lets a new magician attack with magic right away instead of hitting snails with the staff for several more levels.
claims.say: take energy bolt first so you arent bonking snails

claims.text: Delaying Energy Bolt to rush Improving Max MP Increase gains only a little extra MP, and most players consider the slower early levels not worth it.
claims.say: rushing max mp before bolt isnt worth the slow start

claims.text: Finishing Improving MP Recovery before Magic Claw saves a few MP potions, but delaying Claw for that is not worth it.
claims.say: dont delay magic claw just to save a few pots

claims.text: Improving MP Recovery restores extra MP over time; it will not replace MP potions but noticeably slows how fast you go through them.
claims.say: mp recovery wont replace pots but slows your use

claims.text: With the standard build Magic Guard comes last, so expect to use a fair number of HP potions until you have it.
claims.say: expect to chug hp pots until you get magic guard

claims.text: Second job choices: Fire/Poison has strong single-target damage plus poison, Ice/Lightning freezes enemies and excels at mobbing, and Cleric focuses on healing and buffs with lower damage.
claims.say: f/p single target, i/l mobbing, cleric heals and buffs

claims.text: Bishops are regarded as excellent bossing characters.
claims.say: bishops are great at bossing

claims.text: Teleport gives magicians strong mobility for getting around maps.
claims.say: mages get teleport, great for getting around

claims.text: From level 16 to 22 a magician can train at Pig Beach.
claims.say: 16-22 head to pig beach

claims.text: From level 26 to 29 a magician can train in the Ant Tunnel or keep doing the Kerning City Party Quest.
claims.say: 26-29 ant tunnel or kpq

claims.text: A magician who skipped Energy Bolt to rush MP still has to melee early, so levels 8-12 are spent on Snails and Blue Snails at Henesys Hunting Ground I.
claims.say: no bolt yet? hit snails at henesys hunting ground

claims.text: Ariant Coliseum gives good exp for a magician up to level 29 once you can hit the Scorpions reliably, and can also earn a Palm Tree Beach Chair.
claims.say: ariant coliseum is good exp till 29 if you hit scorpions

claims.text: Skelegons are a main training target for high-level I/L Arch Mages, and one-shotting them makes the later levels much faster.
claims.say: 1hitting skelegons makes higher levels way easier

claims.text: A Fighter's party Rage can replace a party member's stronger attack potion buff such as an Onyx Apple, so ask the party before casting it.
claims.say: ask before casting rage, it can override someone's apple

claims.text: Using an Onyx Apple for a Monster Carnival round is a waste; save it for bosses.
claims.say: dont waste onyx apples in monster carnival

claims.text: Beginners who stay on Maple Island for good, known as Islanders, commonly use a pure DEX build.
claims.say: islanders usually go pure dex

claims.text: A pure DEX beginner trades the huge but unreliable hits of a STR beginner for tight, predictable damage, so you always know how many hits a monster will take.
claims.say: pure dex beginner hits lower but super steady

claims.text: Beginners have almost no weapon mastery, so a STR-heavy beginner's hits swing from tiny to huge; piling on DEX lifts the low end until the damage range is narrow.
claims.say: beginner str builds swing wild, dex lifts your min hit

claims.text: The high accuracy of a DEX beginner lets it reliably tag higher-level monsters and leave the kill to friends.
claims.say: lots of dex lets you tag big mobs and let friends finish

claims.text: A DEX beginner that one-hits Horned Mushrooms can farm them steadily, and those maps often have Green Mushrooms to mix in.
claims.say: dex beginner can 1 hit horny mushrooms, steady exp

claims.text: Strong beginner weapons for higher levels include the Green Ski at 55, the fast Emergency Rescue Tube at 60 and the Maple Snowboard at 70, which has the highest attack of the three.
claims.say: beginner weapons: green ski 55, rescue tube 60, snowboard 70

claims.text: When choosing where to train, compare each monster's exp against its HP and pick the best ratio you can kill comfortably.
claims.say: pick mobs with the best exp for their hp

claims.text: When soloing, train on monsters you can kill in one or two hits every time, the way mages do; steady kills give steadier exp than lucky one-shots.
claims.say: solo on mobs you kill in 1-2 hits every time

claims.text: Party quests are the easy way to carry a beginner up into the 70s.
claims.say: pqing is the easy way to level a beginner

claims.text: Party quests generally use fewer potions than grinding because several stages are puzzles or jumping rather than fighting, and their prizes usually cover what you spend.
claims.say: pqs burn way fewer pots than grinding

claims.text: Henesys Party Quest, open from level 10, costs next to nothing in potions, so it is a safe pick over grinding at low levels.
claims.say: hpq at lv10+ barely costs any pots

claims.text: Kerning City Party Quest is for characters level 21 to 30.
claims.say: kpq is lv 21 to 30

claims.text: Kerning City Party Quest is the first decent meso source for low levels: prizes can include valuable scrolls, and potion use is moderate, heaviest in the first stage.
claims.say: kpq prizes can be good scrolls, stage 1 eats the most pots

claims.text: Monster Carnival is for characters level 30 to 50.
claims.say: monster carnival is lv 30 to 50

claims.text: Inside Monster Carnival only the potions the carnival hands out can be used, so a run costs you nothing in your own potions.
claims.say: carnival costs no pots, only its own potions work inside

claims.text: Monster Carnival gives very strong exp for its level range; the author ranks it above every other party quest.
claims.say: carnival exp is amazing for its levels

claims.text: Maple Coins earned in Monster Carnival can be traded to Spiegelmann; 50 coins buy a Spiegelmann's Necklace.
claims.say: save 50 maple coins from carnival for spiegelmann's necklace

claims.text: Ludibrium Party Quest is for characters level 35 to 50.
claims.say: lpq is lv 35 to 50

claims.text: Ludibrium Party Quest stays cheap on potions as long as the party kills Alishar quickly; prizes range from weapon attack scrolls down to mana potions.
claims.say: lpq is cheap if your party kills alishar fast

claims.text: Amoria Party Quest needs characters level 40 or higher who are married.
claims.say: apq is lv 40+ and you gotta be married

claims.text: Orbis Party Quest is for characters level 51 to 70.
claims.say: opq is lv 51 to 70

claims.text: Only a full Orbis Party Quest run gives a prize; rush runs give nothing. Papa Pixie at the end can drain potions if the party is unprepared.
claims.say: do full opq runs, rushing gives no prize

claims.text: Ludibrium Maze Party Quest is for characters level 51 to 70.
claims.say: ludi maze pq is lv 51 to 70

claims.text: Ludibrium Maze Party Quest can be cleared in a couple of minutes with almost no potion use, and its potion and scroll prizes sell to NPCs, so repeated runs turn a profit.
claims.say: ludi maze is fast, no pots, npc the prizes for profit

claims.text: Pirate Party Quest in Herb Town is for characters level 55 to 100.
claims.say: ppq is lv 55 to 100

claims.text: The author rates Pirate Party Quest poorly for both exp and mesos: no sellable prize, and Lord Pirate and his minions drain a lot of potions.
claims.say: ppq is rough on pots, lord pirate hits hard

claims.text: Warriors can earn a Goblin Cape with STR and 5 slots from a Black Mountain quest; scrolled with 100% STR scrolls it rivals a far pricier attack-scrolled Pink Adventurer Cape.
claims.say: goblin cape + 100% str scrolls is a cheap pac swap

claims.text: STR bandits can use a Khanjar or Dragon Khanjar in the shield slot instead of paying for an attack-scrolled shield.
claims.say: str bandit? khanjar is a cheap shield swap

claims.text: A dexless assassin can use a Maple Skanda claw instead of an expensive Shinobi Bracer and get close to the same results.
claims.say: dexless sin? maple skanda instead of shinobi bracer

claims.text: Warriors save MP by using Slash Blast only when three or more mobs are in range, and a single-target attack otherwise.
claims.say: only slash blast when 3+ mobs are in range

claims.text: Fighters and pages should keep Power Guard running at all times; it cuts HP lost to monster touches and so saves potions.
claims.say: keep power guard up always, saves pots

claims.text: Assassins on a budget should max Drain before putting points in Claw Booster; training is a bit slower but HP potion spending drops a lot.
claims.say: max drain before claw booster to save hp pots

claims.text: Max Claw Mastery before Claw Booster; the larger throwing star sets it gives save a lot of mesos over time.
claims.say: claw mastery before booster, bigger star stacks

claims.text: Chief bandits can pair Pickpocket with Meso Explosion so the mesos Pickpocket drops pay for Meso Explosion instead of their own purse.
claims.say: pickpocket + meso explosion so me doesn't drain you

claims.text: In first job, magicians can put leftover SP into Improving MP Recovery to cut down on mana potion spending.
claims.say: 1st job mage? spare sp into improving mp recovery

claims.text: Clerics short on mesos can max MP Eater instead of Holy Arrow, saving a good amount on expensive mana potions.
claims.say: cleric? mp eater over holy arrow saves mana pots

claims.text: Fire/poison mages should only clear misted mobs with Explosion once it kills them in one cast; Explosion is slow, and needing a second cast gives the mobs time to hit back.
claims.say: only explode misted mobs once you 1hit them, it's slow

claims.text: Lucky Seven and Triple Throw damage scales only with LUK and weapon attack (about 5 x LUK x attack / 100), so STR and DEX add nothing to it.
claims.say: triple throw only scales off luk and attack

claims.text: A dagger thief's max damage is about (3.6 x LUK + STR + DEX) x weapon attack / 100, so LUK matters most while STR and DEX still help.
claims.say: dagger thieves: luk counts most, str and dex help too

claims.text: A Dragon Knight around level 85 can train on Blue Kentaurus as a change from Wolf Spiders; a polearm works better there than a spear.
claims.say: dk at 85 can do blue kentaurus, polearm beats spear there

claims.text: Expect heavy potion use and constant knockback at Blue Kentaurus, though the exp makes up for it.
claims.say: blue kentaurus eats pots and knocks you around but exp is good

claims.text: Blue Kentaurus is the place to hunt if you want a Fairfrozen drop.
claims.say: want a fairfrozen? hunt blue kentaurus

claims.text: At Blue Kentaurus, sweep each platform from left to right and alternate going up and down between platforms.
claims.say: mob left to right and switch platforms up and down

claims.text: Magician summons such as Summon Dragon, Ifrit and Elquines work out damage with the same magic formula as spells, so they grow with your Magic Attack.
claims.say: mage summons scale off your magic attack just like spells

claims.text: Heal's power scales with INT and Magic, so a STR-built Cleric restores very little HP with it.
claims.say: heal scales with int, str clerics barely heal

claims.text: Most Magic comes from base INT, so a STR magician who keeps INT low tops out around 100 Magic from weapons and gear, leaving spells and summons weak.
claims.say: str mages top out near 100 magic, summons stay weak

claims.text: Summon Dragon is strong enough that some Priests choose to max it before Shining Ray.
claims.say: some priests max summon dragon before shining ray

claims.text: When rolling a future magician, aim for 4 STR and 4 DEX; 5 in either is fine, so don't spend hours chasing a perfect roll.
claims.say: roll 4 str 4 dex for a mage, 5 is fine too

claims.text: The author keeps LUK at character level plus 3, puts every other point into INT, and eventually stops raising LUK altogether (she stopped at 60).
claims.say: keep luk at level plus 3, rest int, then cap luk

claims.text: To become a Magician you need level 8 and at least 20 INT; go to the Magic Library at the top of Ellinia and talk to Grendel the Really Old.
claims.say: mage job at lv 8 with 20 int, see grendel in the ellinia library

claims.text: Magician 1st job plan: 1 point in Energy Bolt, start Improving MP Recovery, max Improving Max MP Increase, finish Improving MP Recovery, then max Magic Claw and finally Magic Guard.
claims.say: mage 1st job: 1 bolt, mp skills, max claw, then magic guard

claims.text: Levels 1 to 8: hunt Snails, Blue Snails and Shrooms on Maple Island.
claims.say: lv 1-8 just kill snails and shrooms on maple island

claims.text: Magicians at 8-20 can hunt the snails, Stumps, Slimes and mushrooms of Henesys Hunting Ground I, or Slimes at The Tree That Grew I.
claims.say: 8-20: henesys hunting ground i, or slimes at the tree that grew

claims.text: Henesys Party Quest is a good alternative to grinding for low-level magicians.
claims.say: do hpq between 10 and 20

claims.text: Levels 20-30: Pigs and Ribbon Pigs at Rain-Forest East of Henesys or at Pig Beach.
claims.say: 20-30 pigs east of henesys or at pig beach

claims.text: Levels 20-30: Rocky Masks and Wooden Masks at Excavation Site III.
claims.say: 20-30 masks at excavation site iii work well

claims.text: Levels 20-30: Stirges at the Transfer Area, or Trixters on the 73rd floor of Eos Tower.
claims.say: 20-30 stirges at transfer area or trixters in eos tower

claims.text: Kerning City Party Quest is a solid option for magicians in their 20s.
claims.say: kpq is solid from 21 to 30

claims.text: For 2nd job, Grendel the Really Old sends you to the job instructor north of Ellinia; inside, collect 30 Dark Marbles from monsters that give no exp, then bring the Proof of a Hero back to Grendel.
claims.say: 2nd job: get 30 dark marbles for the instructor, bring pots

claims.text: Heal restores HP to you and nearby party members and damages undead monsters around you; its power scales with INT.
claims.say: heal patches up your party and burns nearby undead

claims.text: MP Eater drains monster MP into yours with each magic attack until the monster runs dry, which cuts down on MP potions.
claims.say: mp eater steals mob mp with each spell, saves pots

claims.text: Invincible lowers the physical damage you take but does nothing against magic attacks.
claims.say: invincible cuts physical damage, not magic

claims.text: Bless raises defense, magic defense, accuracy and avoid for nearby party members, which makes clerics popular party picks.
claims.say: bless buffs party def, acc and avoid, parties love it

claims.text: Teleport is needed for some party quests, Guild Party Quest included, and lets you reach spots others cannot.
claims.say: max teleport, gpq and some other pqs need it

claims.text: Party Cleric plan: 1 Teleport at 30, max Heal first, then max Teleport, MP Eater, Invincible and Bless, with the last points in Holy Arrow.
claims.say: party cleric: heal, teleport, mp eater, invincible, bless

claims.text: Solo Cleric plan: 1 Teleport at 30, max Heal, then max MP Eater, Holy Arrow, Invincible and Bless, leaving Teleport at 1.
claims.say: solo cleric: heal, mp eater, holy arrow, invincible, bless

claims.text: Always max Heal and Invincible; a single point of MP Eater is enough for a party cleric, while a solo cleric benefits from maxing it.
claims.say: max heal and invincible, 1 mp eater is ok in parties

claims.text: Holy Arrow can be skipped because Shining Ray in 3rd job hits up to 6 monsters and outclasses it.
claims.say: skip holy arrow, shining ray at 3rd job replaces it

claims.text: Clerics at 30-40 can train on Horny Mushrooms and Zombie Mushrooms throughout the Ant Tunnel maps.
claims.say: 30-40 cleric: horny and zombie shrooms in ant tunnel

claims.text: Wild Boars at The Land of Wild Boar I are another option for clerics at 30-40.
claims.say: wild boars are fine for 30-40 clerics

claims.text: Clerics from 30 to 50 can run Monster Carnival or Ludibrium Party Quest, though LPQ parties can be hard to get into below 40.
claims.say: cpq or lpq at 30-50, lpq is easier to join after 40

claims.text: Clerics from 40 to 60 can train on Zombie Lupins in Monkey Forest II or Monkey Swamp III.
claims.say: 40-60 cleric: zombie lupins around the monkey forest

claims.text: Clerics from the 50s to 70 can run Ludibrium Maze Party Quest and Orbis Party Quest.
claims.say: lmpq and opq are good for clerics 50-70

claims.text: Clerics at 60-70 can team up with a Dragon Knight on Forgotten Path of Time <1> for Soul Teddies and Master Soul Teddies, or on <3> for Death Teddies.
claims.say: party with a dk for soul teddies on forgotten path of time

claims.text: Pirate Party Quest in Herb Town is another option for clerics at 60-70.
claims.say: ppq in herb town works at 60-70

claims.text: Clerics heal themselves with MP and use very few HP potions, which makes them a cheap class to level.
claims.say: clerics heal themselves and barely use hp pots

claims.text: STR is the one main stat a warrior builds.
claims.say: warriors put their ap into str

claims.text: Accuracy decides whether a warrior reliably lands hits on the monsters they train on, so it needs attention when picking a spot.
claims.say: warriors need enough acc to hit their mobs

claims.text: For a warrior, each DEX point counts as 0.8 accuracy and each LUK point as 0.5 accuracy.
claims.say: 1 dex is 0.8 acc and 1 luk is 0.5 acc for warriors

claims.text: A Bishop in the 140s can farm mesos by sweeping maps with Genesis; Harps are often suggested over Wolf Spiders, mostly because of the map layout.
claims.say: bishops can farm with genesis, harps beat wolf spiders for layout

claims.text: Harps drop Steely Throwing-Knives and Wolf Spiders drop Ilbi Throwing-Stars, which makes both worth farming to sell the stars.
claims.say: harps drop steelies and wolf spiders drop ilbis

claims.text: Selling leech to lower-level players is a very lucrative use of a high-level Bishop.
claims.say: leeching with a bishop makes a ton of mesos

claims.text: The Magician first job advancement becomes available at level 8 and requires 20 INT.
claims.say: mage 1st job is at lvl 8 and needs 20 int

claims.text: The standard magician rule for gear is to keep LUK at your level plus 3 (41 LUK at level 38, for example) so mage equipment stays wearable, with the remaining AP in INT.
claims.say: keep luk at your level +3 for gear, rest in int

claims.text: An unfunded warrior can keep roughly 40 to 60 DEX to avoid accuracy trouble and skip costly accuracy items; dexless hits harder but needs expensive accuracy gear.
claims.say: unfunded warrior? keep like 40-60 dex, saves a ton on acc gear

claims.text: Around level 25, DEX only slightly above your level can still miss Dark Axe Stumps and Ghost Stumps fairly often.
claims.say: dex barely above level still misses axe stumps a lot

claims.text: Have 25 DEX before taking the 1st job advancement to become a Bowman.
claims.say: get 25 dex before your bowman 1st job

claims.text: Bowmen use DEX as the main stat and STR as the secondary one.
claims.say: bowman: dex main stat, str secondary

claims.text: Rule of thumb for weapon requirements: crossbow users keep STR about equal to their level, bow users about their level plus 5.
claims.say: xbow str about your level, bow str about level+5

claims.text: Most bowmen skip Final Attack because it never triggers with Strafe, the main 3rd job attack, though it stays a personal choice.
claims.say: most skip final attack, it doesn't proc with strafe

claims.text: Hurricane, the rapid machine-gun style attack, is exclusive to Bowmasters.
claims.say: hurricane is bowmaster only

claims.text: The crossbow line generally hits harder but attacks slower; the bow line is weaker but attacks faster.
claims.say: xbows hit harder, bows attack faster

claims.text: Crossbow line signature skills: Iron Arrow in 2nd job, Blizzard and Arrow Eruption in 3rd, and Piercing Arrow, Blind, Snipe and Frostprey in 4th.
claims.say: xbow line gets iron arrow, blizzard, pierce, snipe, frostprey

claims.text: Bow line signature skills: Arrow Bomb in 2nd job, Inferno and Arrow Rain in 3rd, and Hurricane, Concentrate, Hamstring and Phoenix in 4th.
claims.say: bow line gets arrow bomb, inferno, arrow rain, hurricane

claims.text: Snipers are usually considered to have the better 3rd job because Blizzard freezes; once both have Strafe the bow's speed edge mostly disappears, and Bowmasters and Marksmen end up fairly even.
claims.say: sniper 3rd job is better thanks to freeze, 4th job is even

claims.text: Archers' hardest stretches are roughly the mid 40s to 50 and the 60s to mid 70s, when weapons fall behind or 3rd job skills are still undeveloped.
claims.say: archer hell levels: mid 40s-50 and 60s-mid 70s

claims.text: Most archers keep a Red Viper bow or Heckler crossbow from the 30s up to 50 because of their fast attack speed.
claims.say: keep a red viper or heckler till 50, they attack fast

claims.text: Soul Arrow does not add your arrows' attack bonus: the stat window may show the higher range, but real damage never includes it.
claims.say: soul arrow ignores arrow attack, stat window lies

claims.text: You need at least 25 DEX to take the first job advancement into Thief.
claims.say: need 25 dex to become a thief

claims.text: Bandits are the melee thief branch, fighting up close with daggers and often a shield.
claims.say: bandits go melee with daggers and a shield

claims.text: Assassins are the ranged thief branch, attacking from a distance with claws and throwing stars.
claims.say: sins are ranged, claw plus throwing stars

claims.text: Warrior equipment never requires DEX, so DEX on a warrior is only worth the accuracy it brings.
claims.say: warriors only need dex for accuracy, gear doesnt need it

claims.text: Accuracy needed to always hit a monster is (55 + 2 x level gap) x its avoid / 15, where the gap is the monster's level minus yours and counts as 0 once you outlevel it.
claims.say: acc needed grows with mob avoid and how much it outlevels you

claims.text: Every level you gain lowers the accuracy a monster requires until you reach its level; after that the requirement no longer drops.
claims.say: the higher you level the less acc you need, until you pass the mob

claims.text: The author's preferred accuracy goal is 129, because a Sniper Pill on top reaches the roughly 139 needed to always hit Bone Fish, the hardest to hit of the good-exp mobs.
claims.say: aim for 129 acc, a sniper pill covers bone fish

claims.text: Many warriors stop at 119 accuracy instead, which covers the usual solo targets and still lets them hit Grim Phantom Watch and Bone Fish every time when partied with a Bless.
claims.say: 119 acc works too if you party with a priest's bless

claims.text: Papulatus's second body takes around 147 accuracy to hit fully, but that figure only applies once you are about level 125, so building DEX for it early is wasted.
claims.say: pap 2nd body needs ~147 acc, only reachable near lvl 125

claims.text: Plan DEX ahead: work out the accuracy a target monster needs at the level you will start training on it, a few levels early, so there is time to get gear or stats.
claims.say: check acc needs a few levels before moving to a new spot

claims.text: For warriors who don't want to plan, a simple rule is to have 50 to 60 DEX by level 30 and stop adding DEX after that.
claims.say: easy route: 50-60 dex by lvl 30 then stop

claims.text: Overall DEX scrolls add accuracy as well as DEX, so an overall beats a top and bottom for a warrior short on accuracy; once accuracy is plentiful a well scrolled top and bottom gives more total stats.
claims.say: dex scrolls on an overall give acc too, better than top/bottom

claims.text: On shoes, jump scrolls add a little DEX while DEX scrolls add accuracy; the 100% versions of either add neither.
claims.say: shoe jump scrolls give dex, shoe dex scrolls give acc

claims.text: The author scrolls warrior shoes for accuracy rather than DEX: it is cheaper and yields more accuracy, and lots of jump with no speed can actually slow you down.
claims.say: scroll your shoes for acc, cheaper and more acc

claims.text: From level 70 on, pick up a pair of scrolled warrior shoes unless you can afford something better.
claims.say: grab scrolled warrior shoes once you hit 70

claims.text: Before weapon mastery matters any weapon type works, so a low-level warrior of any branch can carry a Pumpkin Spear or Fish Spear just for their accuracy.
claims.say: low lvl? a pumpkin spear or fish spear gives free acc

claims.text: A Zakum Helmet is worth close to 40 accuracy for a warrior once you count both its own accuracy and the accuracy its LUK provides.
claims.say: zhelm is like 40 acc once you count its luk

claims.text: Fourth job Arch Mages and Bishops can sell leech: they clear maps of Wolf Spiders, Jr. Newties, Skelegons or Harps while a paying partied player idles and collects exp.
claims.say: 4th job mages sell leech at skeles, newties or harps

claims.text: Selling leech gives a mage steady mesos to pay for potions, although some players frown on it.
claims.say: selling leech pays for pots, some ppl hate it though

claims.text: A Ranger can pull mobs into a corner with Arrow Rain so a Bishop's Genesis wipes them; some count this luring as a form of leeching.
claims.say: arrow rain mobs into a corner and let a bishop gen them

claims.text: Unless you can count on lots of boss runs, max Piercing Arrow before Snipe, since it trains very well at Skelegons.
claims.say: max pierce before snipe unless you boss a lot

claims.text: At Skelegons, a Bishop on the top platform with a Marksman using Piercing Arrow on the bottom makes a very strong training pair.
claims.say: bishop up top, mm piercing below at gons is a great duo

claims.text: Strong attack potions like Onyx Apples speed up a sniping Marksman's boss kills even more.
claims.say: onyx apples make snipe boss runs even quicker

claims.text: Final Attack is a Fighter passive that sometimes follows your attack with an extra hit, adding damage without any MP cost.
claims.say: final attack gives free extra hits, no mp needed

claims.text: The downside of Final Attack is less predictable output: damage per button press, attack timing and knockback all vary more, and the passive cannot be switched off once SP is in it.
claims.say: fa makes dmg and knockback less predictable, can't turn it off

claims.text: Nearly every Fighter takes Final Attack in 2nd job and most players recommend it; the usual alternatives weighed against it are the weapon mastery and Iron Body.
claims.say: most fighters still put their 2nd job sp into final attack

claims.text: Hunting Headless Horseman can be a training alternative for Bowmasters; on crowded servers it is easiest to find during off-peak hours such as school time.
claims.say: hunt headless horseman off-peak, its decent exp

claims.text: On Maple Island, doing the island's quests while fighting snails and shrooms is the easy way to level 10.
claims.say: do every quest on maple island, easy way to 10

claims.text: In the 20s a rogue can farm Green Mushrooms and Horny Mushrooms at Forest Up North II in the Tree Dungeon.
claims.say: 20s: green and horny mushrooms in forest up north

claims.text: Pigs and Ribbon Pigs at Pig Beach or the rain forest east of Henesys make easy 20s training for a rogue.
claims.say: pigs at pig beach are easy exp in your 20s

claims.text: Kerning City Party Quest and the Ariant Coliseum are both suggested in place of grinding during the 20s.
claims.say: 20s: try kpq or the ariant coliseum instead of grinding

claims.text: Players can enter Ludibrium Party Quest at 35, but anyone under 40 is a weak contributor and tends to be passed over by higher members.
claims.say: you can lpq at 35 but people prefer 40 and up

claims.text: Ludibrium Party Quest exp is fast early in the 40s and tapers off by the late 40s.
claims.say: lpq exp is best early 40s, falls off late 40s

claims.text: Kiyos on North Desert Road 2 are good training from roughly 35 to 45, and the Meerkats on the road before come just ahead of that.
claims.say: kiyos are a good pick from 35 to 45

claims.text: Brown and Pink Teddies at Terrace Hall in Ludibrium are a standard spot for thieves in their 30s.
claims.say: teddies at terrace hall are good in your 30s

claims.text: Luster Pixies at Cloud Park V are not worth it for meso drops, but their sun etc items trade for a chance at a cape INT 60% scroll, so keep them.
claims.say: keep luster pixie sun pieces, they trade for cape int 60 tries

claims.text: Jr. Yetis on Watch Out for Icy Path I make money mostly through rare gloves attack 60% scroll drops, with skins and leather as extra income.
claims.say: jr yetis: sell the skins, hope for glove att 60

claims.text: From 50 to 70, Orbis Party Quest and Ludibrium Maze Party Quest sit alongside the grinding spots as good thief options.
claims.say: opq and lmpq are good from 50 to 70

claims.text: Death Teddies on Forgotten Path of Time <3> are meant for the upper 70s, best handled by a Hermit with Shadow Partner at 21 or more.
claims.say: death teddies are for late 70s hermits with 21+ shadow partner

claims.text: An assassin can safely hit Jr. Newties by standing on the left platform of the middle section and sniping the first one or two that come.
claims.say: stand on the left mid platform at newties and snipe

claims.text: In the 80s and up, grinding with a Holy Symbol Priest and a Hyper Body Dragon Knight is faster than soloing; only solo when no party can be found.
claims.say: find a hs priest and hb dk, way faster than solo

claims.text: Kentaurus at Griffey Forest give fair exp, but the boss Griffey can appear at any moment, so treat the map as dangerous.
claims.say: careful at griffey forest, griffey can pop any second

claims.text: Spirit Vikings on Warped Path of Time <4> give little in mesos, and the occasional Ilbi Throwing-Stars drop is mostly a tease.
claims.say: vikings are bad money, the ilbi chance just teases you

claims.text: Grim Phantom Watches at Forbidden Time in Ludibrium are a thief spot from 100 to 120.
claims.say: grim phantom watches are good from 100 to 120

claims.text: A bold Night Lord in the 120s can try clearing the bottom of Destroyed Dragon's Nest rather than sniping from the platform.
claims.say: brave nls can clear the bottom of the newtie map

claims.text: Before a 70s Chief Bandit trains on Gobies he needs at least level 1 Meso Guard and level 1 Meso Explosion, because Meso Explosion is the training attack there.
claims.say: gobies need 1 meso guard and 1 meso explosion minimum

claims.text: On a busy channel, players over 100 will kill-steal a Chief Bandit hogging a Goby map; joining a party with a Priest and sharing the map is smarter and faster.
claims.say: dont hog a goby map solo, party with the 100+ guys

claims.text: For Bandits in the 60s, the listed spots are only worth it if the monsters die in two hits or fewer.
claims.say: 60s bandit: if you cant 2 hit it, move on

claims.text: For a Bandit in the 40s, Curse Eyes are only worthwhile if they die in a single hit.
claims.say: curse eyes are only good if you 1 hit them

claims.text: Wolf Spiders give a Chief Bandit fast exp in the 80s at the price of heavy potion use, with a slim shot at Ilbi Throwing-Stars.
claims.say: wolf spiders are fast exp but you burn a lot of pots

claims.text: For Dreamy Ghosts a Shadower needs deep pockets for potions and a maxed Band of Thieves, and having a Priest friend helps.
claims.say: himes need lots of pot money and max band of thieves

claims.text: Dragon Forest III in Leafre, with Brextons and Dark Cornians, is a Shadower spot for the 110s and 120s.
claims.say: dragon forest 3 is solid for shads 110 to 130

claims.text: For a Chief Bandit, Kentaurus are the best bet until Dreamy Ghosts, with Gobies as the main alternative and the Zipangu Armory only if you can handle its boss.
claims.say: kents are your best bet until himes, or gobies

claims.text: From 80 to 110, Chief Bandits grind the Leafre Kentaurus maps: the red, black and blue Kentaurus areas and the Battlefield of Fire and Darkness.
claims.say: 80-110 cb: grind the kentaurus maps in leafre

claims.text: Leeching a low-level character off a very high-level mage without Holy Symbol is slow, because the high-level partner takes much of the exp; just training the character can be faster.
claims.say: leeching off a high level without hs is slow, just train it

claims.text: Each scroll's success is rolled independently: a run of failures does not make the next scroll more likely to pass.
claims.say: each scroll roll is independent, fails dont raise odds

claims.text: Bait scrolling, failing cheap scrolls before using a valuable one, is not worth the money spent.
claims.say: bait scrolling wastes mesos

claims.text: Bowmasters are the stronger single-target branch thanks to Hurricane, while Marksmen are better at mobbing; choose by which playstyle you prefer.
claims.say: bm for single target, mm for mobbing, pick your style

claims.text: At Horntail, especially before the tail is down, heavy knockback keeps breaking Hurricane, so Bowmasters often switch to Strafe there.
claims.say: at horntail bms use strafe till the tail dies, kb breaks hurricane

claims.text: At endgame spots like Skelegons and Skelosaurus both branches level at about the same pace; Bowmasters usually kill them before getting hit, so they don't miss freezing.
claims.say: at skeles bm and mm level about the same

claims.text: For Snipers, freezing monsters with Blizzard is a big help throughout 3rd job.
claims.say: blizzard freeze carries snipers through 3rd job

claims.text: Bowmasters stay safe in 4th job without freezing because Hurricane's knockback keeps mobs at range, with Dragon's Breath for monsters that spawn too close.
claims.say: hurricane kb keeps mobs away, dragon's breath for close ones

claims.text: A Marksman tactic: hang on a rope mid-platform, Blizzard one side, charge Piercing Arrow while Frostprey hits mobs coming from the other side, then release it and repeat on the other side.
claims.say: mm: rope in the middle, blizzard one side, frostprey the other

claims.text: Marksmen use a wider mix of skills and need more strategy, while Bowmaster training is mostly walking back and forth firing Hurricane.
claims.say: mm juggles skills, bm mostly holds hurricane

claims.text: In boss parties most of the damage comes from Night Lords, so a bowman's survivability (HP) matters more than small damage differences between the two branches.
claims.say: in boss parties your hp matters more than a bit of damage

claims.text: Arrow Bomb's stun and Power Knock-Back's knockback do not land at the listed rates; they seem to depend on the target monster's knockback resistance and level.
claims.say: arrow bomb stun and pkb rates vary by mob

claims.text: Against Zakum while his weapon defense buff is up, Arrow Bomb's explosion shows misses: damage is capped at 1 and the explosion's reduced share rounds down to 0.
claims.say: arrow bomb misses on zak while his wdef buff is up

claims.text: For an Arch Mage, any elemental wand, even a poorly scrolled one, is better than every non-elemental weapon.
claims.say: even a bad ele wand beats any other weapon for archmages

claims.text: Buying underpriced elemental wands in the Free Market and reselling them can bring in large profits.
claims.say: flip cheap ele wands in the fm for good profit

claims.text: An I/L Arch Mage may sell gear to buy the books for Maple Warrior 20 and Blizzard 30, valuing those skill levels over a few points of magic attack.
claims.say: sell spare gear for mw20 and blizz30 books if you must

claims.text: Giving up a couple of INT on a necklace for extra HP can be worth it for a mage, since surviving hits matters more than tiny INT gains.
claims.say: trade a bit of int for hp on your pendant, survival matters

claims.text: Max damage with a one-handed sword is (STR x 4.0 + DEX) / 100 x weapon attack.
claims.say: 1h sword max dmg = (str*4 + dex)/100 * watk

claims.text: One-handed axes and one-handed blunt weapons use a STR multiplier of 4.4: (STR x 4.4 + DEX) / 100 x weapon attack.
claims.say: 1h axe or bw uses str*4.4 + dex

claims.text: Two-handed swords use STR x 4.6 + DEX, and two-handed axes and blunt weapons use STR x 4.8 + DEX, each divided by 100 and multiplied by weapon attack.
claims.say: 2h sword str*4.6, 2h axe or bw str*4.8, plus dex

claims.text: Spears and polearms share the highest warrior multiplier: (STR x 5.0 + DEX) / 100 x weapon attack.
claims.say: spear and polearm use str*5 + dex, best warrior multiplier

claims.text: Bow max damage is (DEX x 3.4 + STR) / 100 x weapon attack, while crossbows use DEX x 3.6 + STR.
claims.say: bow uses dex*3.4 + str, crossbow dex*3.6 + str

claims.text: Claw and dagger thieves calculate max damage as (LUK x 3.6 + STR + DEX) / 100 x weapon attack.
claims.say: thief range is (luk*3.6 + str + dex)/100 * watk

claims.text: Knuckles use STR x 4.8 + DEX and guns use DEX x 3.6 + STR, each divided by 100 and multiplied by weapon attack.
claims.say: knuckle str*4.8 + dex, gun dex*3.6 + str

claims.text: Scrolling a batch of cheap weapons and keeping the best result is an inexpensive way to raise your weapon attack a few points.
claims.say: mass scroll cheap weapons and keep the best one

claims.text: Jack, the explorer twin of John Barricade, is the NPC who handles the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest; he stands at the Cavern of Pain in the first area of Crimsonwood Keep.
claims.say: jack at the cavern of pain is the crimsonwood pq npc

claims.text: During the first two stages of the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest, a party member who dies is brought back to life and keeps playing instead of being removed from the quest.
claims.say: dying in cwkpq stage 1 or 2 just revives you, you stay in

claims.text: In Crimsonwood Keep, defeating Red Nirg, the warrior Twisted Master, makes two ninja-style bosses, Azure Ocelot and Scarlet Phoenix, spawn, so be ready for a second fight.
claims.say: after red nirg dies azure ocelot and scarlet phoenix pop out

claims.text: Crimsonwood Keep lies in the Phantom Forest part of Masteria and is reached from New Leaf City.
claims.say: crimsonwood keep is out past the phantom forest from nlc

claims.text: The Headless Horseman is a boss that wanders the Phantom Forest.
claims.say: headless horseman roams the phantom forest

claims.text: Facestompers are shoes that carry an attack bonus, a pick for players who put offense ahead of defense.
claims.say: facestompers are shoes that give you attack

claims.text: Crimsonwood Keep is occupied by the Twisted Masters' corrupted army of Windraiders, Nightshadows, Firebrands and Stormbreakers, trained in the fighting styles of the Keep's old guilds.
claims.say: cwk is full of windraiders, nightshadows, firebrands, stormbreakers

claims.text: A bossing-focused Night Lord build: Triple Throw 20, Venomous Star 13, Shadow Shifter 15, Shadow Stars 15, then max Shadow Shifter and Triple Throw, leaving Maple Warrior for last.
claims.say: bossing nl: tt 20, venom 13, shifter, stars 15, mw last

claims.text: Maxing Shadow Shifter early means fewer potions used, which suits bossing, but training is slower without a higher Venomous Star.
claims.say: maxed shifter saves pots, but you train slower without venom

claims.text: The common view is that raising Triple Throw first improves damage for both bossing and training.
claims.say: max triple throw first, it helps training and bossing

claims.text: After Triple Throw 20, a suggested next step is Maple Warrior to 9, then Venomous Star for faster training or Shadow Shifter to save potions.
claims.say: after tt 20: mw 9, then venom or shifter

claims.text: Elemental wands and staffs are not monster drops; they come only from Gachapon machines.
claims.say: ele wands and staves only come from gachapon

claims.text: The level 70 Elemental Wand 2 (poison), Elemental Wand 3 (ice) and Elemental Wand 4 (lightning) come from the New Leaf City Gachapon.
claims.say: lv70 ele wands 2, 3 and 4 come from nlc gacha

claims.text: The level 130 Elemental Wand 5 (fire) and Elemental Wand 7 (ice) have been won from the New Leaf City Gachapon.
claims.say: lv130 fire and ice ele wands come from nlc gacha

claims.text: The level 130 lightning Elemental Wand 8 has been reported from the Mushroom Shrine Gachapon.
claims.say: lv130 lightning wand reported from mushroom shrine gacha

claims.text: Putting AP straight into MaxHP without resets (blood washing) gives a thief only about 18 HP per point, roughly 90 HP per level, and costs LUK and damage.
claims.say: ap into hp gives a thief about 18 hp each, costs luk

claims.text: Blood washing suits a Shadower better than a Night Lord: Night Lords are brought to Horntail for damage, while Shadowers are valued for staying alive.
claims.say: nl is wanted for damage, dont trade too much luk for hp

claims.text: Instead of blood washing, keep a swap set of HP gear (top, bottom, gloves, pendant, cape) for Horntail only; it adds a few hundred HP while you still train in your attack gear.
claims.say: keep an hp gear set just for horntail runs

claims.text: Thieves gain about 22 HP per level up on average, so natural HP growth alone is slow.
claims.say: thieves only get about 22 hp per level

claims.text: Minimum to solo Crimson Guardians as a ranger or sniper: roughly 3400+ HP (more without a Zakum Helmet), maxed Arrow Rain or Arrow Eruption, and Puppet at 12 or higher.
claims.say: for guardians: 3400+ hp, max rain or eruption, 12+ puppet

claims.text: Sharp Eyes and a higher level make Crimson Guardian kills much faster, though they are not strictly required.
claims.say: sharp eyes helps a lot at guardians

claims.text: The guardians on the Crimsonwood Keep map outside the keep are the author's pick for the best solo exp for high-level rangers and snipers, with low potion use since you hit from safety.
claims.say: crimson guardians outside the keep are great solo exp

claims.text: Crimson Guardians have a very short sideways reach, so from the stairs a little off to the side of them you can hit them with area skills while they cannot hit you back.
claims.say: guardians barely hit sideways, snipe them from the stairs

claims.text: Guardians cast a long-range seal that does no damage but blocks your skills; bring plenty of Holy Water.
claims.say: bring lots of holy water, they seal a lot

claims.text: On that map the top guardians roam freely, but invisible walls split the bottom floor into left, middle and right pens, so whichever pen you cannot reach slowly fills up.
claims.say: the bottom floor is split in 3 by invisible walls

claims.text: Main spot: the right-side staircase, one step above the middle; from there Arrow Rain or Arrow Eruption reaches both rows while neither row can reach you.
claims.say: stand 1 step above the middle on the right stairs and rain

claims.text: When the right side thins out, stand under the bottom-left guardians and clear them, then return right; luring them across fails because of an invisible wall near the door arch.
claims.say: when the right side thins, clear bottom left then go back

claims.text: Do not AFK on the staircases: if another player attacks the bottom guardians, a mace swing can touch you and drop you down among them.
claims.say: dont afk on the stairs, a mace swing can knock you down

claims.text: Skip any looting that pulls you out of position at the guardians; it slows your kills and costs more in potions than it earns.
claims.say: dont go out of your way to loot at guardians

claims.text: Cast Puppet twice to shed aggro before you loot or leave a safe spot.
claims.say: double puppet to drop aggro before you move or loot

claims.text: If you get knocked to the floor with guardians aggroed, drop down quickly; bumping a guardian on purpose gives a moment of invincibility to get away.
claims.say: knocked down? jump down fast, bump a guardian for i-frames

claims.text: Cross between the two sides along the topmost stairway, where the top guardians cannot touch you.
claims.say: cross over on the top stairway, its safe there

claims.text: A point in Inferno or Blizzard is handy for luring guardians toward you, which works on the right side of the map.
claims.say: 1 inferno or blizzard to lure them on the right side

claims.text: Two players can split the map, one per side, which is faster; a priest in the party adds Holy Symbol and Dispel, which saves Holy Water.
claims.say: split the map with a friend, a priest's dispel saves holy water

claims.text: Summons there are debated: the author skips them because guardians resist ice so Frostprey won't freeze them and Golden Eagle's stun can miss, while another player finds Silver Hawk great since it stuns them as they spawn.
claims.say: summons are iffy there, hawk can stun them as they spawn

claims.text: Mysterious Path 3 in Singapore works for a White Knight in the 70s but starts to feel slow by around level 79.
claims.say: mysterious path 3 is ok for a wk in the 70s, slows by 79

claims.text: Around level 79-80, a White Knight with average equips can move on to the regular Ghost Pirates rather than the harder spots.
claims.say: wk near 80 with avg gear: try the regular ghost pirates

claims.text: The Zakum Helmet is close to a final hat for archers: it adds both DEX and STR, so you can wear higher bows without putting more AP into base STR.
claims.say: get a zhelm, the str on it lets you use better bows

claims.text: Besides its stats, the Zakum Helmet gives a lot of weapon and magic defense, which cuts damage taken while training and saves potion money.
claims.say: zhelm defense saves you a ton on pots

claims.text: A near end-game archer setup: Zakum Helmet, Horntail Necklace, high-DEX earrings, a well-scrolled bow, 15+ attack gloves, a DEX/attack Pink Adventurer Cape, a 30+ DEX overall and Facestompers.
claims.say: endgame is zhelm, ht necklace, a good pac and facestompers

claims.text: The cheapest decent bowman overall: buy a clean one and pass 100% DEX scrolls on every slot, which lands around mid-teens DEX for very little.
claims.say: 100% dex scroll a clean overall, cheap and solid

claims.text: For a few more DEX, keep trying a low-chance overall DEX scroll until one passes, then fill the remaining slots with 100% scrolls; expect it to take a few tries.
claims.say: hit one 30% dex on the overall then 100% the rest

claims.text: Clean shoes are fine until about level 70-80; at 80 the bowman Dark Wing Boots are widely scrolled and good value.
claims.say: clean shoes till 80, then grab dex dark wing boots

claims.text: Wait until level 90 to buy a 20+ DEX overall; level 90 overalls get scrolled far more often, so good ones are easier to find than level 70 ones.
claims.say: wait till 90 for a 20+ dex overall, way more around

claims.text: Weapon upgrades usually beat armor for archers: one point of weapon attack is worth several DEX, so an 8-9 attack bow upgrade outweighs any shoe upgrade.
claims.say: upgrade your bow first, 1 att is worth a few dex

claims.text: A Pink Adventurer Cape scrolled for DEX and attack is the main archer cape upgrade; at lower levels a plain DEX-scrolled cape is a fine stopgap.
claims.say: save for a dex/att pac, a dex cape is fine till then

claims.text: Attack-scrolled Work Gloves are the standard archer gloves; end game is 15+ attack Stormcaster Gloves or Brown Work Gloves. Gloves can wait until other upgrades are done.
claims.say: att work gloves are the go-to, upgrade them after the rest

claims.text: Choose upgrades by DEX gained per meso spent; splitting a budget across two mid upgrades, such as shoes and earrings, can beat one top-end piece.
claims.say: compare dex per meso, two mid upgrades can beat one big one

claims.text: For a 90s crossbowman who already has a Zakum Helmet, good next steps are a DEX/STR Pink Adventurer Cape and 8-9 DEX earrings, then a better Dark Raven or Casa Crow.
claims.say: after zhelm get a pac and 8 dex earrings, then a better raven

claims.text: A Marksman who mostly bosses can pull points out of Piercing Arrow and Blind to max Snipe sooner.
claims.say: bossing mm? take points from piercing and blind into snipe

claims.text: Players disagree whether a Marksman should max Marksman Boost before Snipe.
claims.say: some max marksman boost before snipe, people argue it

claims.text: After Bahamut, a Bishop's remaining picks are situational: Big Bang for looks and a non-elemental attack, Infinity for places you cannot use potions, Mana Reflection for bossing.
claims.say: after bahamut: mana reflect for bossing, infinity for no-pot maps

claims.text: Genesis, Angel Ray, Bahamut and Maple Warrior come first for a Bishop; save points for Genesis and Maple Warrior so you can add them right after passing the mastery book.
claims.say: bishop priority: genesis, angel ray, bahamut, mw

claims.text: Holy Shield is very useful at Zakum, which often uses its sealing skill, and at Horntail when party members get weakened.
claims.say: holy shield is great vs zak seals and ht weaken

claims.text: Mana Reflection's damage is small; critics say at best it saved a few potions during a Papulatus solo, while fans take it as a long-lasting fun buff.
claims.say: mana reflect dmg is tiny, people take it for fun

claims.text: Big Bang gives a Bishop a stronger non-elemental attack for holy-immune monsters like Crimson Guardians, but getting hit while charging it cancels the cast.
claims.say: big bang hits holy-immune mobs but cancels if you get bumped

claims.text: Mana Reflection triggers on many boss attacks, including all of Pianus's.
claims.say: mana reflect works on all of pianus's attacks

claims.text: Elemental wands give no bonus to holy spells, but a Bishop still benefits from their high magic attack.
claims.say: ele wands dont boost holy but bishops still get the matk

claims.text: Players disagree on whether a training Bishop needs Genesis at 30: some call level 20 plenty, others find it too weak to one-shot Skelegons and Jr. Newties.
claims.say: gen 20 trains fine for some, others want gen 30 for skeles

claims.text: A LUKless lightning Ice/Lightning mage can train on Teddies with Magic Claw around levels 30-35.
claims.say: il at 30-35? teddies with magic claw

claims.text: From about level 35 until Truckers, Paper Lantern Ghosts gave this Ice/Lightning mage better exp than Retz.
claims.say: 35 till truckers, lanterns beat retz for il

claims.text: Truckers spawn in big packs with spots where you can stand still and pick them off, good Thunder Bolt exp from the mid 40s into the 60s.
claims.say: truckers come in big packs, great for thunder bolt

claims.text: Slimys are an Ice/Lightning option from the 60s into the 70s.
claims.say: slimys work for il in the 60s and 70s

claims.text: Monster Carnival is solid exp around levels 30-37 on a busy channel, but grinding beats it afterward.
claims.say: cpq is good at 30-37, grind after that

claims.text: Night Lords use little MP since Triple Throw is cheap, so some move points from MP into HP with AP Resets without wearing INT gear and just carry more mana potions.
claims.say: nls dont need much mp, reset some into hp and carry mana pots

claims.text: HP washing means adding AP to HP and then using an AP Reset to pull AP back out of MP; you can only remove MP above your level's minimum, so your spare MP is the washing budget.
claims.say: hp washing: ap into hp, then ap reset it out of mp

claims.text: A warrior's minimum MP is roughly level times 4 plus 155, and resetting one AP out of MP takes away up to about 4 MP.
claims.say: warrior mp floor is about level times 4 plus 155

claims.text: Each 10 INT you have when you level up adds about 1 MP, and that extra MP is what pays for HP washing; round INT targets up to the next 10 to be safe.
claims.say: each 10 int at level up gives about 1 extra mp

claims.text: Magicians around level 8 to 20 can train at Henesys Hunting Ground I on snails, slimes and mushrooms, using Energy Bolt and then Magic Claw.
claims.say: lv 8-20 mage? henesys hunting ground 1 with magic claw

claims.text: From level 20 to 30, magicians can Magic Claw Pigs and Ribbon Pigs at Pig Beach.
claims.say: 20-30 mage, pigs at pig beach w magic claw

claims.text: The Horny Mushrooms and Zombie Mushrooms in Ant Tunnel I are a solid Magic Claw spot for magicians from level 20 to 40.
claims.say: ant tunnel 1 shrooms are good magic claw exp 20-40

claims.text: Trixters on the Eos Tower floors in Ludibrium are a Magic Claw option for magicians from level 20 to 40.
claims.say: trixters in eos tower for magic claw 20-40

claims.text: Jr. Wraiths at Hollowed Ground suit fire/poison wizards with Fire Arrow and clerics with Heal from level 30 to 50.
claims.say: jr wraiths at hollowed ground, fire arrow or heal em

claims.text: The Jr. Wraiths in Line 1 <Area 2> of the Kerning subway work for fire/poison wizards with Fire Arrow and clerics with Heal at level 40 to 50.
claims.say: jr wraiths in subway line 1 area 2, good at 40-50

claims.text: Poison Breath on Death Teddies at Forgotten Path of Time <3> or Ghost Pirates at Warped Path of Time <3> only works well in the late 50s; earlier you miss a lot and get outkilled by others.
claims.say: poison breath on teddies or ghost pirates only from ~57

claims.text: Fire/poison wizards from 60 to 70 can Fire Arrow Coolie Zombies in the Forest of Dead Trees maps, though it is slow since that area was weakened.
claims.say: fp 60s can fire arrow coolie zombies, slow tho

claims.text: Dual Ghost Pirates at Unbalanced Time are a main fire/poison spot from 70 into the 100s: Poison Mist the groups and finish them with Explosion, later in a full attacker party.
claims.say: dual ghost pirates at unbalanced time, mist + explosion

claims.text: Grim Phantom Watches at Forbidden Time suit fire/poison mages from about 80 with Poison Mist; past 100 they can split the map with a strong priest who solos the lower platforms while the mage mists the top.
claims.say: grims at forbidden time, split the map w a priest

claims.text: Misting Sharks and Cold Sharks at The Grave of a Wrecked Ship pays very well in exp and mesos but is dangerous; expect to die a lot while learning, and some mages never get comfortable there.
claims.say: sharks pay great but you'll die a lot learning em

claims.text: From about 90, fire/poison mages can Poison Mist Skelegons, Skelosaurus and Nest Golems at Peak of the Big Nest, Nest of a Dead Dragon or The Dragon Nest Left Behind in Leafre.
claims.say: 90+ fp, mist the skeles at peak of the big nest in leafre

claims.text: Dreamy Ghosts at Encounter with the Buddha in Showa work for fire/poison mages from about 110 with Explosion, and later for arch mages with Fire Demon and Elquines.
claims.say: dreamy ghosts in showa for fp 110+, fire demon later

claims.text: Ice/lightning wizards from 30 to 50 can Cold Beam Jr. Cellions at Garden of Red I and Jr. Lioners at Garden of Yellow I in Orbis.
claims.say: il 30-50, cold beam jr cellions or lioners in orbis

claims.text: Ice/lightning wizards in their 30s can Thunder Bolt the Crows at Crow Forest in Showa.
claims.say: il 30s, thunder bolt the crows in showa's crow forest
