claims.text: Ice/lightning mages from 70 to 90 can Cold Beam and Ice Strike Wolf Spiders at Wolf Spider Cavern, which are known for a tiny chance at Ilbi Throwing-Stars.
claims.say: wolf spiders at 70-90, tiny ilbi chance

claims.text: Birks and Dual Birks at Forest Crossroad in Leafre are an Ice Strike spot for ice/lightning mages in their 70s and 80s.
claims.say: birks at leafre forest crossroad, ice strike 70-90

claims.text: Spirit Vikings at Warped Path of Time <4> are a party spot for ice/lightning mages from 90 to 120, using Thunder Spear and Ice Strike alongside other attackers.
claims.say: spirit vikings, thunder spear + ice strike in a party

claims.text: Red Wyverns at Red Wyvern's Nest suit ice/lightning mages from 90 with Ice Strike and later Blizzard, and go faster in a party with other attackers.
claims.say: red wyverns for il, ice strike then blizzard

claims.text: Ice/lightning mages from 100 to 150 can Ice Strike or Blizzard Jr. Newties and Nest Golems at Destroyed Dragon Nest; it can be soloed but goes much faster with a priest or bishop.
claims.say: newties at destroyed dragon nest, party w a priest

claims.text: Clerics from 40 to 80 can Heal the undead Wraiths in Line 1 <Area 4> and Line 2 <Area 3> of the Kerning subway.
claims.say: cleric 40-80, heal the wraiths in the subway

claims.text: Clerics can solo Death Teddies at Forgotten Path of Time <3> with Heal if they keep Magic Guard on, or party with a Dragon Knight there and for Master Death Teddies at Lost Time.
claims.say: death teddies: heal w magic guard on, or duo a dk

claims.text: Dreamy Ghosts at Encounter with the Buddha are risky for priests in their 80s and 90s, because the Black Crow there can kill them even through Magic Guard.
claims.say: careful at dreamy ghosts, black crow can kill you

claims.text: Sacrifice is a poor way to drop into Berserk range while training: its self-damage varies and it angers the monster first, so just letting a mob hit you works as well.
claims.say: dont sacrifice to trigger zerk while training, just take a hit

claims.text: Against a boss that can kill you in one hit, such as Pianus, Sacrifice makes a good Berserk trigger: heal to just above the Berserk threshold, then use Sacrifice once.
claims.say: vs pianus heal just over zerk hp, then sacrifice once

claims.text: Sacrifice can knock a boss back, but Rush moves bosses more reliably.
claims.say: rush pushes bosses better than sacrifice

claims.text: Iron Body and Iron Will add little useful defense while training; Rage or Bless overwrite them and Hex of the Beholder gives more, so they are low-priority skills.
claims.say: iron body and iron will can wait, hex of beholder covers it

claims.text: Dark Knights rarely find a use for Power Crash, and a Bishop's Dispel covers the same job, so one point is plenty.
claims.say: 1 point in power crash is plenty

claims.text: Dragon Fury: Spear is not wasted SP: it nearly matches an extra Spear Crusher hit but is faster with wider reach, good for luring quick mobs like Dreamy Ghosts and clearing weak quest monsters.
claims.say: spear fury is great for luring and killing weak quest mobs

claims.text: Dark Knight 4th job: max Beholder, Berserk, Power Stance and Maple Warrior first with one point in Rush; the other skills can wait.
claims.say: dk 4th job: beholder, zerk, stance, mw first, 1 in rush

claims.text: Leftover SP on a spear Dark Knight can go into one point each of Pole Arm Crusher and Dragon Fury: Pole Arm to make a polearm usable, or into Iron Will as a party buff.
claims.say: spare sp? 1 in each polearm skill or max iron will

claims.text: Max Improved MaxHP Increase early in 1st job; leaving it until around level 30 leaves a warrior noticeably short on HP through the 30s and 40s.
claims.say: max hp increase early on a warrior or your hp lags

claims.text: A Shadower who mostly solos with Boomerang Step as the main attack should max it before investing in Maple Warrior.
claims.say: solo shad? max bstep before mw

claims.text: Venom adds real damage for Shadowers who kill slowly, but once a Boomerang Step, Taunt, Boomerang Step chain kills mobs the poison has no time to matter.
claims.say: venom helps slow killers, useless once bstep kills fast

claims.text: After maxing Boomerang Step, a Shadower can put points into Maple Warrior and Assassinate to prepare for bossing.
claims.say: after bstep, put some in mw and assassinate for bosses

claims.text: Combo orb bonuses multiply with a skill's damage percent rather than adding to it: estimate a full-orb Brandish hit as your damage range times the orb multiplier times Brandish's percent.
claims.say: combo orbs multiply skill dmg, they don't add to it

claims.text: Monster defense is subtracted from every hit, so skills made of many small hits like Savage Blow lose far more damage on tough monsters such as Skelegons than skills with a few big hits.
claims.say: many-hit skills like savage blow lose more to mob defense

claims.text: Heroes have a higher base damage range than Bandits, so skills with similar damage percents hit harder on a Hero.
claims.say: heroes have a bigger dmg range than bandits

claims.text: The quest Jane and the Wild Boar, open from level 25, rewards a random 60% weapon scroll you can sell.
claims.say: jane and the wild boar at 25 gives a random 60% weapon scroll

claims.text: Sabitrama's Life Work, from level 85, rewards a random 30% scroll: either gloves for DEX or overall for INT.
claims.say: sabitramas life work at 85 gives a 30% glove dex or overall int

claims.text: The Committee Challenges, from level 85, gives one random reward: a 30% scroll for gloves attack, gloves DEX or overall INT, or a Power Elixir.
claims.say: committee challenges at 85 gives a 30% scroll or a power elixir

claims.text: Soul in the Dark, from level 70, rewards a random 30% scroll; the pool includes shoes speed, jump and DEX, gloves DEX and attack, earring INT and DEX, and overall DEX and INT.
claims.say: soul in the dark at 70 gives a random 30% scroll

claims.text: The Ludibrium quest EOS Tower Threatened!, from level 35, rewards a random 60% weapon scroll.
claims.say: eos tower threatened at 35 gives a random 60% weapon scroll

claims.text: Peace at EOS Tower in Ludibrium, from level 40, rewards a 10% or 60% gloves attack scroll.
claims.say: peace at eos tower at 40 gives a 10% or 60% glove att scroll

claims.text: Captain Lord Pirate, for levels 55 to 100 around Herb Town, rewards a 10% or 60% gloves attack scroll at random.
claims.say: captain lord pirate 55-100 gives a 10% or 60% glove att scroll

claims.text: When you are short on mesos, do quests that reward weapon and gloves attack scrolls and sell the scrolls instead of using them.
claims.say: broke? do quests that give glove att scrolls and sell them

claims.text: Instead of HP washing, a low-HP archer can keep a set of HP-scrolled gear to swap in for dangerous maps or bosses, but HP gear only goes so far and cuts damage while worn; players disagree on its worth.
claims.say: some archers swap hp gear for deadly maps instead of washing

claims.text: A cheaper alternative to washing is a mini blood build: put 10 to 15 AP into HP spread over a few levels.
claims.say: or toss 10-15 ap into hp over a few levels

claims.text: Overalls can't take HP scrolls, so wearing a separate top and bottom is the way to add HP through scrolling.
claims.say: overalls can't take hp scrolls, use a top and bottom

claims.text: Gloves, and capes to a lesser extent, are where most extra attack comes from, so keep them attack-scrolled rather than swapping them for HP pieces.
claims.say: keep your glove for attack, don't swap it for hp

claims.text: Elderwraiths on the way to Windraiders easily kill low-HP archers, so carry enough HP before passing through.
claims.say: watch out for elderwraiths on the way to windraiders

claims.text: Chief Bandit start: 1 Assaulter at 70, then 1 Meso Explosion and Chakra to 3, plus a point each in Meso Guard and Band of Thieves by 72.
claims.say: 70: 1 assaulter, then 1 me, 3 chakra, 1 mg, 1 bot

claims.text: Raise Band of Thieves to 18 early, then max Assaulter around level 88, and finish Band of Thieves around 93.
claims.say: bot to 18, max assaulter, then finish bot

claims.text: After Band of Thieves, max Meso Guard, then Meso Explosion, then Chakra, and put what is left into Pickpocket.
claims.say: then max mg, me, chakra, and the rest into pickpocket

claims.text: Players argue over Chakra versus Pickpocket: Chakra is slow to cast and only works below half HP, while Pickpocket gives a strong opening hit and stays useful into 4th job.
claims.say: chakra vs pickpocket is debated, chakra only works under half hp

claims.text: Speed Infusion does not raise the attack speed cap, so a weapon already at the fastest allowed speed gains nothing.
claims.say: speed infusion wont push past the speed cap

claims.text: Speed Infusion helps slow weapons the most, letting a slow two-handed sword attack at near-capped speed at bosses.
claims.say: speed infusion makes slow 2h swords feel fast

claims.text: A one-handed sword with an attack shield beats a two-handed sword mostly through speed; with Speed Infusion evening speed and an Onyx Apple or Gelt Chocolate adding attack, the two-handed sword pulls ahead.
claims.say: with speed infusion and apples, 2h beats 1h + shield

claims.text: A decently scrolled level 70 elemental wand gives the same element boost as a level 130 one and trails it by only about 20 to 30 magic attack, making it a cheap option for Mages and Arch Mages.
claims.say: a good lv70 element wand boosts as much as the lv130 one

claims.text: Daily Horntail and Zakum runs, plus some merchanting, are how the author raised the mesos for an expensive elemental wand.
claims.say: daily ht and zak runs fund the pricey gear

claims.text: Players split on Dragon Blood: skip it if you will max Hex of the Beholder later since Hex replaces the attack buff, or max it as a backup attack buff that saves on attack potions.
claims.say: dragon blood is optional if you plan to max hex later

claims.text: Some advise never maxing Hex of the Beholder, because its constant rebuffing overwrites apple attack buffs; they cap it before it starts adding weapon attack.
claims.say: dont max hex, it keeps overwriting your apple buff

claims.text: Sacrifice divides opinion: some rate it poorly next to Endure, while the author sees it as the best single-target option for polearm users.
claims.say: sacrifice is good single target for polearm, some prefer endure

claims.text: Dragon Roar requires 3 points in Sacrifice first, so even builds that skip Sacrifice put 3 points there.
claims.say: dragon roar needs 3 points in sacrifice first

claims.text: Another suggested 3rd-job split is 1 Power Crash, 3 Sacrifice to open Dragon Roar, maxed Dragon Blood as a backup attack buff, and the rest wherever you like.
claims.say: alt: 1 power crash, 3 sacrifice, max dragon blood

claims.text: Keep your distance from Papulatus during the fight; its bombs mostly catch players who stay close to the clock.
claims.say: keep away from pap, the bombs get you when youre close

claims.text: If Papulatus corners you against a wall, Flash Jump through it to the open side of the map.
claims.say: cornered by pap? flash jump right through him

claims.text: Watch for the bomb animation in the Papulatus fight and run the other way as soon as it starts.
claims.say: see the bomb animation, run the other way

claims.text: After Papulatus's first form dies, clear the leftover bombs before you start attacking the second form.
claims.say: clear the bombs before you start on pap's second form

claims.text: Dark Sight together with Flash Jump makes dodging Papulatus's second form easy for thieves.
claims.say: dark sight and flash jump make pap form 2 easy

claims.text: Once your hits are strong enough to knock Papulatus back, soloing it becomes much easier.
claims.say: once you can knock pap back the solo gets easier

claims.text: The author maxed Magic Claw first and then put points into Improved MaxMP Increase from about level 15 or 16.
claims.say: max magic claw first, then improved max mp from around 15

claims.text: Maxing Improved MaxMP Increase early matters more for Fire/Poison and Ice/Lightning mages, since Element Amplification drives their MP use up.
claims.say: f/p and i/l want max mp early, element amp burns mp

claims.text: Sand Rats spawn very densely and move fast, which suits warriors and brawlers with mob skills from about 20 to 27; expect constant light touch damage. Sahel 3 is the best map.
claims.say: sand rats 20-27 for warriors and brawlers, sahel 3 is best

claims.text: Sand Rats are a poor fit for archers, gunslingers and assassins because the spawn is too dense to handle at range.
claims.say: archers and sins should skip sand rats, too mobby

claims.text: Scorpions spawn more thinly on the same flat desert maps, so they suit ranged classes and anyone still lacking a mob skill; Sahel 1 is the best map.
claims.say: scorpions in sahel 1 if you're ranged or lack a mob skill

claims.text: Cube Slimes in Lab - Unit 101 suit roughly levels 28-32; they share the map with Rumos and can jump, but a book cart gives you a spot to snipe from.
claims.say: cube slimes in lab 101 for 28-32, snipe off the book cart

claims.text: Rumos are good for the low-to-mid 30s; Lab - Unit 102 is mostly Rumos, which can't jump and are easy to hit from the cart, while Unit 103 adds the more dangerous Triple Rumo.
claims.say: rumos in lab 102 for low-mid 30s, 103 has triple rumos

claims.text: Iron Mutae in Lab - Area B-3 on the Alcadno side are a great spot from the late 30s to 45 and can be used up to 50.
claims.say: iron mutae in b-3 are great from late 30s to 45

claims.text: At Iron Mutae, run the floor hitting everything, then hop onto the platform and mob them; brawlers can reach them from the lower platform with Somersault Kick and gunslingers with Invisible Shot.
claims.say: run the floor, then jump up and somersault kick them

claims.text: Archers struggle at Iron Mutae because Iron Arrow flies straight and can't reach the floor from the safe platform.
claims.say: archers skip iron mutae, iron arrow can't angle down

claims.text: If Iron Mutae is taken, Mithril Mutae in Lab - Area B-1 across the hall are a weaker backup.
claims.say: iron mutae full? mithril mutae in b-1 is a backup

claims.text: Roids are Magatia's best training spot, good from 50 to 70, and they drop useful equipment, especially pirate gear.
claims.say: roids are magatia's best spot from 50 to 70

claims.text: Start Roids in Lab - Area C-1, a pure Roid map; Lab - Area C-2 is longer with a faster spawn but mixes in Neo Huroids, whose magic attacks hurt lower levels.
claims.say: start roids in c-1, c-2 is faster but has neo huroids

claims.text: For levels 50-70 Roids likely beat Mysterious Path 3, at least early on, since the map is smaller and needs less movement.
claims.say: roids probably beat mp3 early on, less walking

claims.text: At level 35 you can join both Magatia factions at once by starting both entry quests with Han the Broker in the middle of town.
claims.say: at 35 you can join both alcadno and zenumist via han

claims.text: The Zenumist entry asks you to drop an item on the alchemy circle so it becomes a branch you hand in; for the Alcadno entry, Han the Broker tells you the answers to the chairman's quiz.
claims.say: zenumist test: drop item on the circle; alcadno: quiz

claims.text: Joining gives the Zenumist Cape or Alcadno Cape, with no slots, +5 speed and +2 jump, and tradeable; some faction quests only start while you wear it.
claims.say: faction capes give speed and jump, wear one for their quests

claims.text: The Magatia story picks up in the 70s and ends with a choice: give the secret to the Zenumists or the Alcadno for an untradeable level 80 version of your cape, or tell the neutral family for a lot of fame.
claims.say: end of magatia story: pick a side for a lv80 cape, or fame

claims.text: The Romeo and Juliet Party Quest takes a party of 4 to 6 and starts from Romeo on the Zenumist side or Juliet on the Alcadno side.
claims.say: magatia pq needs 4-6 people, start at romeo or juliet

claims.text: Bring a thief with maxed Haste and a magician with maxed Teleport to the Romeo and Juliet Party Quest.
claims.say: magatia pq wants a thief with max haste and a mage with teleport

claims.text: The Romeo and Juliet Party Quest pendant, Horus' Eye, needs items you only get by keeping Romeo or Juliet alive during the run; it beats the Monster Carnival pendant.
claims.say: keep romeo or juliet alive to earn items for horus' eye

claims.text: Horus' Eye gives 60 weapon and magic defense plus 14 avoid, and players usually Chaos Scroll it.
claims.say: horus' eye: 60 def, 14 avoid, people chaos it

claims.text: Magatia has no Spiegelmann, so you can't enter Monster Carnival from there; Maple Administrator and Duey are about the only NPCs not unique to the town.
claims.say: no spiegelmann in magatia, go elsewhere for carnival

claims.text: A Hero typically maxes Brandish first in 4th job and then fills Advanced Combo Attack.
claims.say: hero 4th job: max brandish, then advanced combo

claims.text: Heroes need Power Stance maxed to pull their weight at Horntail; starting Stance around 145 gets it done near 155, so mid-to-late 150s is a realistic first Horntail.
claims.say: hero needs max stance for ht, think mid 150s

claims.text: Raising Power Stance past its starting cap needs the Power Stance 20 mastery book, which can fail, so plan the Stance build around getting one.
claims.say: you need the stance 20 book to go past the base cap

claims.text: A Hero who spends a lot of time grinding the Crimsonwood Keep guards does well splitting spare 4th job SP between Rush and Maple Warrior.
claims.say: grinding cwk guards as hero? put sp into rush and mw

claims.text: Elemental mage weapons come in level 103, 130 and 163 tiers; only the 130 tier has a version with no LUK requirement, while the 163 ones all need LUK.
claims.say: elemental weapons at 103, 130, 163; only the 130 has a lukless one

claims.text: Because of the lukless level 130 wand, the author holds that lukless mages stay ahead of LUK mages, who lose over 100 magic attack by comparison; another player argued the 163 weapons' LUK need balances it.
claims.say: lukless mages still beat luk mages thanks to the 130 lukless wand

claims.text: Paladin suits players who want a sturdy close-range warrior without combo juggling or low-HP risk, and who do not mind not being a top bossing pick.
claims.say: paladin is the safe warrior pick if bossing isnt your thing

claims.text: Hero is the choice for a close-range warrior who still wants to boss without having to fight at low HP.
claims.say: hero if you want to boss as a warrior without low hp

claims.text: Dark Knight means fighting at low HP to get Berserk's extra damage, and Dark Knights are in heavy demand for boss parties because of Hyper Body.
claims.say: dk lives on low hp for berserk and gets begged for bosses

claims.text: Shadower is a skill-heavy close-range class that fills your keyboard but gives steady, consistent damage.
claims.say: shadower has lots of skills but steady damage

claims.text: Night Lord fits ranged players who want to spam one attack and move around fast.
claims.say: nl if you want to spam one attack and be fast

claims.text: Corsair suits ranged players who enjoy strategy and juggling several skills more than raw speed.
claims.say: sair is for people who like strategy over speed

claims.text: Bowmaster lets you spam a single skill, while Marksman play mixes several different skills.
claims.say: bm spams one skill, mm switches skills more

claims.text: Between the two Arch Mage branches, Fire/Poison is the one that paralyzes monsters and Ice/Lightning is the one that freezes them.
claims.say: f/p paralyzes, i/l freezes

claims.text: Staying a permanent Beginner is a novelty choice with weak damage and short range.
claims.say: perma beginner is just for fun, damage is weak

claims.text: Papulatus starts healing and summoning bombs soon after his HP drops below full.
claims.say: pap starts healing and bombing early in the fight

claims.text: He summons a few bombs at a time up to a cap of 50 on screen; once that cap is reached the rest of the first form gets much easier.
claims.say: once pap has 50 bombs out the first form gets easy

claims.text: Papulatus's bombs appear either on the top or the bottom of the room, never on both at once.
claims.say: pap bombs spawn top or bottom, never both

claims.text: Bomb blasts count as weapon attacks, so a Pain Reliever from Omega Sector lowers the damage if your HP is close to surviving one.
claims.say: pap bombs are weapon attack, pain relievers help

claims.text: Right after he heals, Papulatus is invincible for about a second, so do not waste a strong attack at that moment.
claims.say: dont waste big hits right after pap heals, hes immune

claims.text: Papulatus can cast two skills back to back, such as lightning followed straight away by bombs, so stay alert.
claims.say: pap can double cast, stay sharp

claims.text: Keep game sound on during the fight so you can hear bomb summons even when Papulatus is off screen.
claims.say: keep sound on, you can hear the bombs being summoned

claims.text: Pin Papulatus against the wall from a spot just far enough away that his stun and dispel cannot reach you.
claims.say: keep pap kbd on the wall from out of stun range

claims.text: At the bomb summon animation, run away at once rather than jumping: a jump can set off a bomb as you land, while bumping one on the run gives brief invincibility.
claims.say: when he summons bombs just run, dont jump

claims.text: Some players clear bomb explosions entirely by jumping with plenty of Jump from gear; it works but is risky.
claims.say: high jump gear can clear a blast, but its risky

claims.text: If you can knock him back reliably and bombs are maxed, drop Puppet on the far side when he hides; he fixates on it, hides and casts less, and you get more shooting time.
claims.say: bombs maxed? puppet the far side so pap stops hiding

claims.text: Avoid the far-side Puppet trick before bombs are maxed: after healing he can walk in, stun you and use fresh bombs as shields.
claims.say: dont do the puppet trick before bombs are maxed

claims.text: If you cannot pin him, keep your distance so he never gets close enough to stun you; run through him if cornered, and Puppet behind him when he hides in his clock so bombs land farther from you.
claims.say: cant pin pap? keep distance, puppet behind him when he hides

claims.text: Second form: Strafe it, turn and Puppet behind you; when the Puppet dies, Strafe once more, re-Puppet behind you and duck so it floats over you. Never try to outrun it.
claims.say: 2nd form: strafe, puppet behind you, duck, repeat

claims.text: If the second form pins you, stay calm and wait for it to drift away, then jump-cast Puppet and duck.
claims.say: pinned by pap? wait, then jump cast puppet and duck

claims.text: Bring around 400 mid-level potions plus Elixirs and Power Elixirs for when he drops you to 1 HP/MP, and reuse the Elixirs he drops on your next run.
claims.say: bring about 400 pots plus elixirs for the 1/1

claims.text: An archer's Papulatus solo takes roughly 25 minutes, about 3-4 Warrior Elixirs' worth.
claims.say: a pap solo takes about 25 min, 3-4 warrior elixirs

claims.text: Scrolling HP gear to survive Papulatus's bombs is a poor trade: you give up defense and damage, and the bombs are weapon attacks anyway.
claims.say: dont scroll hp gear for pap, you lose too much

claims.text: Angel Ray at about level 20 is already enough for a Bishop to solo Papulatus.
claims.say: angel ray around 20 is enough to solo pap

claims.text: Bahamut can attack monsters you did not mean to pull, causing unwanted aggro.
claims.say: bahamut can pull mobs you didnt want

claims.text: Genesis can only go past 20 with its costly mastery book, so many Bishops leave it partway and save points to bring it to 20 later.
claims.say: genesis past 20 needs the book, plan for 20 first

claims.text: Put the first point into Magic Claw at level 10 so you can fight, then pour the next points into Increasing Max MP until it is maxed.
claims.say: 1 magic claw first, then max increasing max mp

claims.text: Once Increasing Max MP is maxed, add one point to Flame for its extra damage and defense, then max Magic Claw.
claims.say: then 1 point in flame and max magic claw

claims.text: After Magic Claw, max Flame next and finish first job with Magic Guard; Magic Armor gets no points in this plan.
claims.say: max flame next, magic guard last, skip magic armor

claims.text: At second job put a single point in Teleport, then max Fire Pillar before anything else.
claims.say: 2nd job: 1 teleport then max fire pillar first

claims.text: After Fire Pillar, put about 11 points into Spell Booster for speed and then max Meditation; swap the two if you want damage before speed.
claims.say: after pillar, about 11 booster then max meditation

claims.text: Late in second job max Teleport and then Slow, leaving a few spare points for Magic Armor, Fire Arrow or more Spell Booster.
claims.say: later max teleport and slow, spares wherever

claims.text: At third job max Flame Gear first and use it as the main training skill, much like a Fire/Poison mage uses Poison Mist.
claims.say: 3rd job max flame gear first, it's your poison mist

claims.text: A single point in Seal is worth having for when monsters that cast magic attacks give you trouble.
claims.say: 1 point in seal helps vs mobs that cast magic

claims.text: To play like an Explosion-first Fire/Poison mage, swap the order and max Fire Strike before Flame Gear.
claims.say: want explosion-style play? max fire strike before flame gear

claims.text: Dragon's Breath shoves monsters back only as far as the edge of bowman range, so they stay in reach for your next attacks.
claims.say: dragons breath pushes mobs to the edge of your range, not past it

claims.text: Cygnus Knights are started by talking to Nineheart in Ereve, and each world allows only one Cygnus character.
claims.say: talk to nineheart in ereve to make a cygnus, one per world

claims.text: At level 10 a Noblesse reports to Nineheart, then takes the job quest from the instructor of the chosen class, such as Irina for Wind Archer.
claims.say: at 10 see nineheart, then your class instructor in ereve

claims.text: Cygnus job advancements are quests, so a Noblesse can put one off and take the job later.
claims.say: cygnus job advances are quests, you can do them later

claims.text: A Wind Archer's first-job summon, Storm, hits several monsters at once and gives a mob attack from level 10, so it's worth a point right away.
claims.say: put your first sp in storm, it hits a few mobs at once

claims.text: Wind Archer first-job SP order: one point in Storm, max The Eye of Amazon for range, then max Critical Shot, then max Double Shot, and spend the rest on Storm.
claims.say: wa 1st job: 1 storm, max eye, max crit, max double shot, rest storm

claims.text: Wind Archers can skip Focus, since Cygnus get extra DEX from their bonus AP and have plenty of accuracy; Double Shot stays the main attack until 3rd job.
claims.say: skip focus on wind archer, dex from ap gives you enough acc

claims.text: Cygnus Knights get an extra AP each level up to level 70, which makes them noticeably stronger than explorers of the same level.
claims.say: cygnus get bonus ap till 70 so they level easier

claims.text: Cygnus have their own quest trainers in Henesys, Kerning City, Ellinia and Perion whose quests carry you from the low teens into the 20s with little grinding.
claims.say: cygnus trainers in the vic towns give quests through your 20s

claims.text: Around level 28 Nineheart sends Cygnus to a hidden door deep in the Ant Tunnel where a puppeteer NPC turns into a boss; he can seal or seduce you, so carry All Cure Potions.
claims.say: bring all cures for the puppeteer fight in the ant tunnel

claims.text: The Cygnus 2nd job test is a training room in Ereve where you hunt small birds for crests; the crests drop often, so it goes quickly.
claims.say: cygnus 2nd job test is quick, the birds drop crests a lot

claims.text: Ereve has boats from Ellinia and Orbis that leave as soon as you board; going Orbis to Ereve to Ellinia can stand in for the regular Orbis to Ellinia boat if you just missed it.
claims.say: missed the orbis boat? ride to ereve and on to ellinia

claims.text: At level 50 Nineheart starts the Cygnus mount quest: get an egg from the bird raiser in Ereve's hunting grounds, hatch it, buy the item Kenta sells, and bring it back for the mount and Monster Rider.
claims.say: cygnus mount quest starts at 50 from nineheart

claims.text: Cygnus 3rd job at level 70 needs a Dark Crystal: refine one in El Nath, give it to Nineheart for a pass into the hunting grounds, and beat the impostor instructor in a side room.
claims.say: bring a dark crystal to nineheart for cygnus 3rd job

claims.text: The impostor in the Cygnus 3rd job test hits hard with knockback slams, seals and zombifies you and heals itself, so bring strong potions and expect a tough fight on weak gear.
claims.say: the fake instructor at 3rd job hits hard, bring good pots

claims.text: Cygnus Knights cap at level 120, so they can't take the level 121 Temple of Time quests and can never reach Pink Bean.
claims.say: cygnus cap at 120, so no pink bean for them

claims.text: The Black Witch fight is solo and she uses seduce, zombify and darkness, so carry All Cure Potions; beating her earns a Cygnus medal with HP, MP and stat bonuses.
claims.say: bring all cures for the black witch, she seduces and zombifies

claims.text: Wind Archers only get Hurricane and Bow Expert at level 100; take Hurricane first and leave Bow Expert for last.
claims.say: wind archer at 100: hurricane first, bow expert last

claims.text: Classes that are weaker at hitting one target usually make up for it by being better at clearing groups of monsters.
claims.say: weaker single target classes usually mob better

claims.text: Ranged 4th jobs have little HP and survive bosses by staying out of attack range, relying on avoid, other party members drawing aggro, and Hyper Body.
claims.say: ranged classes are squishy, stay out of range and get hb

claims.text: Heroes, Paladins and Dark Knights have very high HP, shrug off knockback with Power Stance, have Rush, and are strongest against small groups of monsters.
claims.say: warriors are tanky, stance stops knockback, great on small mobs

claims.text: Shadowers and Buccaneers hit less hard than Heroes or Dark Knights but survive through avoid and defensive skills, letting them kill tough bosses like Bigfoot without burning many potions.
claims.say: shads and bucs dodge a lot, cheap on pots vs bosses like bigfoot

claims.text: Magicians deal little single-target damage: Bishops are mainly support at bosses, and Arch Mages need a boss weak to their element, while many bosses are neutral or resist poison and lightning.
claims.say: mages aren't boss dps, bishops are support at bosses

claims.text: Mages are excellent mobbers and are useful for quickly wiping out the minions a boss summons.
claims.say: mages clear boss summons fast, that's their job there

claims.text: Onyx Apples give physical attackers a big weapon attack boost for boss fights, but they do nothing for magicians.
claims.say: onyx apples are huge for physical classes, useless for mages

claims.text: Night Lords are modest single-target hitters on their own, but Venomous Star adds damage while training and a Sharp Eyes buff raises their damage a lot.
claims.say: nl solo dmg is meh, sharp eyes makes them hit way harder

claims.text: Corsairs post very high damage while on the Battleship, but the ship has its own HP and breaks if it takes too much, which limits how long it can be used.
claims.say: sair battleship hits hard but it has hp and can break

claims.text: Monster defense lowers your damage range before skill multipliers: take half the monster's defense off your max and 60% of it off your min.
claims.say: mob defense eats into your range, more off the min than the max

claims.text: Guns have a base attack speed of Fast (5) before any booster.
claims.say: guns are fast 5 speed before boosters

claims.text: A Paladin's elemental charge adds nothing against a boss that resists that element, so pick the charge the boss is weak to or at least neutral against.
claims.say: paladins: don't use a charge the boss resists, it does nothing

claims.text: Casting Octopus takes a noticeable chunk of time unlike most summons, so how much it adds to a Corsair's damage depends on the fight.
claims.say: octopus is slow to cast, so it's not always worth it

claims.text: The Zakum Helmet and Horntail Necklace are standard endgame pieces for any class thanks to their all-stat bonuses.
claims.say: zhelm and ht necklace are endgame staples for any class

claims.text: A class's boss damage ranking says nothing about its overall value or how well it trains.
claims.say: boss dps charts don't tell you how good a class is to train

claims.text: On a Band of Thieves build, Savage Blow stays the main attack until about level 80, by which time Band of Thieves should be around 18.
claims.say: on a bot build, savage blow carries you till about 80

claims.text: Balanced Fury throwing stars can only be recharged at the New Leaf City weapon shop.
claims.say: balanced fury only recharges at the nlc weapon shop

claims.text: Leaving New Leaf City means riding the subway back out, so bundle your Balanced Fury recharges into fewer trips.
claims.say: leaving nlc means the subway ride, recharge a lot at once

claims.text: A typical F/P Arch Mage order: max Meteor Shower first, then raise Paralyze and Elquines to 20, which is their cap until you use the mastery books.
claims.say: fp: max meteor first, then paralyze and elquines to 20

claims.text: Paralyze and Elquines stop at level 20 until you use a level-30 mastery book for each; the books can fail and can be hard to find.
claims.say: paralyze and elquines need a 30 book to go past 20

claims.text: While hunting for the Paralyze and Elquines books, an F/P Arch Mage can put spare SP into Maple Warrior instead of letting it sit.
claims.say: waiting on books? put spare sp into maple warrior

claims.text: Rather than sinking SP into the weak leftover F/P 4th-job skills such as Mana Reflection, save the points until your late 160s.
claims.say: save sp, skip the weak 4th job extras till late 160s

claims.text: For a Dark Knight who mostly grinds, Aura of the Beholder is the stronger pick: its steady healing keeps HP near the Berserk line so you can stick to one potion type instead of juggling several.
claims.say: aura of the beholder first if you grind, makes zerk way easier

claims.text: Achilles pays off most at bosses such as Zakum and Horntail, where it shrinks big hits before they land; Aura of the Beholder heals too slowly to matter next to potting against boss damage.
claims.say: achilles is the bossing pick, aura heals too slow at bosses

claims.text: Dark Knights disagree on whether to max Achilles or Aura of the Beholder first; the usual answer is Aura if you spend more time training and Achilles if you spend more time bossing.
claims.say: achilles or aura first? depends if you boss or train more

claims.text: Achilles is an always-on passive that lowers both physical and magical damage taken, whereas Power Guard only reduces physical hits.
claims.say: achilles cuts magic and physical dmg, power guard only physical

claims.text: The spear line never learns Power Guard; that skill belongs to Fighters and Pages, so a Dark Knight has to rely on its own defensive skills instead.
claims.say: dks dont get power guard, only fighters and pages do

claims.text: Because Achilles reduces each hit before it lands, it can raise how many Skelegon hits a Dark Knight survives at Berserk HP; Aura of the Beholder only heals afterwards and cannot prevent a one-shot.
claims.say: achilles can save you from a one shot, aura only heals after

claims.text: At bosses a Bishop usually covers the party's healing, so the damage prevention from Achilles is worth more there than the extra healing from Aura of the Beholder.
claims.say: with a bishop healing, achilles beats aura at bosses

claims.text: Aura of the Beholder copes well with many small hits but falls behind whenever incoming damage outpaces its healing.
claims.say: aura is great vs small hits, weak when damage comes fast

claims.text: Hex of the Beholder is usually one of the last Dark Knight skills to raise, since its buff clashes with apple attack buffs and adds little else.
claims.say: leave hex of the beholder for last, it clashes with apples

claims.text: A Hero using a two-handed axe deals less Brandish damage than a sword Hero, and the gap widens against fast swords.
claims.say: axe heroes brandish for less than sword heroes, esp fast swords

claims.text: Two-handed axe Fighters are easy to train and cheap to scroll gear for.
claims.say: 2h axe fighters are easy to train and cheap to scroll

claims.text: An axe Fighter levels only slightly slower than a Cleric does.
claims.say: axe fighters level about as fast as clerics

claims.text: A dexless Assassin keeps base DEX minimal and leans on gear for its DEX, so it needs heavy funding; plan and fund it before the first job advancement.
claims.say: dexless sin needs gear for dex, get funded before you job

claims.text: For a dexless Assassin, line up glove attack scrolls and overall DEX scrolls ahead of time so the equipment carries the stats the build skips.
claims.say: stock glove att and overall dex scrolls for a dexless sin

claims.text: Party exp from a kill goes mainly to the member who dealt the damage, with smaller shares to the other members on the map.
claims.say: whoever does the damage gets the big share of party exp

claims.text: An I/L Arch Mage paired with an attacking Bishop is a very fast exp duo, ahead of setups that add a leecher or swap the Bishop for a Holy Symbol mule.
claims.say: i/l + bishop both attacking is the fastest exp duo

claims.text: Blue Elemental Gloves and Blue Elemental Shoes are level 110 magician equips crafted through the Maker skill.
claims.say: blue elemental gloves and shoes are lv110 maker mage gear

claims.text: A mage who keeps around 80 base LUK can, with LUK equips and Maple Warrior, meet the requirements of nearly all mage gear, including level 110 and Timeless items.
claims.say: 80 base luk plus mw lets a mage wear almost any gear

claims.text: Magicians take their first job advancement at level 8 by speaking with Grendel the Really Old at the top of Ellinia.
claims.say: mage 1st job at lv 8, talk to grendel at the top of ellinia

claims.text: For more total MP, put the job-advance point into Improving MP Recovery and max Improving Max MP Increase first; the trade-off is fighting with basic attacks until about level 13.
claims.say: want more mp? do the mp skills first, basic attack till 13

claims.text: For an attack skill right away, spend the level 8 point on Energy Bolt; a single point is all Energy Bolt ever gets in this build.
claims.say: 1 point energy bolt at 8 so you can attack

claims.text: After Magic Claw, finish Improving MP Recovery and then max Magic Guard by level 30, leaving Magic Armor at zero.
claims.say: max magic guard by 30, magic armor can stay at 0

claims.text: Max Heal first as a Cleric; it is both your recovery and your attack against undead until third job.
claims.say: max heal first as a cleric

claims.text: In this Cleric build Invincible is maxed right after Heal.
claims.say: invincible goes right after heal

claims.text: Max MP Eater before Bless: with so many quick low-level training maps it trims your MP potion use, although maxing Bless first is also a reasonable order.
claims.say: max mp eater early, saves a lot of mana pots

claims.text: Bless overrides Magic Armor, so points spent in Magic Armor are wasted once you have Bless.
claims.say: bless overrides magic armor, dont put sp in it

claims.text: Max Bless around levels 55 to 60, then finish Teleport, and dump the last second-job points into Holy Arrow.
claims.say: bless then teleport, leftovers into holy arrow

claims.text: Holy Symbol is the first Priest skill to max; training parties want a Priest who has it, and the earliest it can be maxed is level 81.
claims.say: rush holy symbol, max it by 81, parties love it

claims.text: Spend the level 70 point on Shining Ray so you have an attack besides Heal; it does not delay maxing Holy Symbol at 81.
claims.say: 1 point shining ray at 70 so you have an attack

claims.text: Doom is mostly a fun skill rather than a useful one, so a single point is plenty.
claims.say: doom is a joke skill, 1 point is enough

claims.text: Summon Dragon only needs level 15 to unlock Bahamut at fourth job, so the rest of its points can wait.
claims.say: summon dragon 15 is enough to unlock bahamut

claims.text: After Holy Symbol, this build maxes Elemental Resistance, then Shining Ray, then works through Summon Dragon, Dispel and Mystic Door by 120.
claims.say: after holy symbol: elemental resist, then shining ray

claims.text: Put one point in Resurrection at 120 alongside Genesis, and start Maple Warrior early in fourth job.
claims.say: 1 in resurrection at 120, start maple warrior early

claims.text: Bishops differ on Bahamut versus Angel Ray first; some see Angel Ray mainly as a bossing skill, others put it ahead of Bahamut.
claims.say: bahamut or angel ray first, people split on it

claims.text: Late fourth-job points go to Holy Shield, then Mana Reflection and Infinity, with Big Bang saved for last.
claims.say: big bang last, holy shield and infinity first

claims.text: Fourth-job skill order depends on when you get the skill books for Maple Warrior 20 and Genesis 30, which drop from Horntail, so plan around them.
claims.say: mw20 and gen30 books drop from horntail

claims.text: LUKless Bishops, putting no AP into LUK, became especially common once Genesis arrived.
claims.say: lots of bishops go lukless these days

claims.text: Iron Hogs are hard to find in numbers; besides Pig Park, they spawn mixed in with Iron Boars at Burnt Land III and IV, a bearable spawn for hunting them.
claims.say: iron hogs mix with iron boars at burnt land 3 and 4

claims.text: Green Snails are hard to find once you leave Maple Island; search the beaches around Lith Harbor. Cygnus Knights never visit Maple Island, so they have it worse.
claims.say: need snails? check the beaches around lith harbor

claims.text: Shrooms are easiest to find at Henesys Hunting Ground and on a platform in the map just east of Henesys.
claims.say: shrooms are at henesys hunting ground and right of henesys

claims.text: Ticks spawn on a single Ludibrium map, outnumbered by Tick-Tocks; the two drop the same etc items, so quests are easy but the Tick card is slow.
claims.say: ticks and tick-tocks drop the same quest etc items

claims.text: Dark Stumps usually spawn mixed with other stumps; the best map for them is on the border between Perion and Kerning City.
claims.say: dark stumps are best on the perion-kerning border map

claims.text: Dark Sand Dwarves appear on only a few Ariant maps, mixed with plenty of Sand Rats and Scorpions.
claims.say: dark sand dwarves are rare, only a few ariant maps

claims.text: Roloducks only spawn on a few Cloud Terrace maps in Ludibrium, and just one of them has a decent spawn.
claims.say: roloducks only live in a few cloud terrace maps

claims.text: Regular, non-transforming Dark Jr. Yetis are among the rarest monsters, found on only two maps in the El Nath area; plan ahead for quests that need them.
claims.say: dark jr yetis only spawn on two maps around el nath

claims.text: Jr. Lucida only appears when Eliza summons them, so its card takes a lot of effort.
claims.say: jr lucida only shows up when eliza summons them

claims.text: Every boss drops a monster card, party quest bosses like King Slime and Lord Pirate included.
claims.say: all bosses drop cards, even pq bosses

claims.text: Bubblings appear on lots of maps, but none match the density of the Kerning Subway, which stays the best place for them.
claims.say: bubblings are still best in the kerning subway

claims.text: The map right outside Sleepywood is great for quests that need Evil Eyes.
claims.say: evil eye quests? use the map right outside sleepywood

claims.text: Steely Throwing-Knives stack more per slot and cost far less than Ilbi Throwing-Stars while giving up only 2 attack, so they last longer in long fights.
claims.say: steelies stack more and cost less than ilbis, only 2 less atk

claims.text: You cannot recharge stars in the middle of a boss fight such as Zakum, so a Night Lord with low-level Shadow Stars should bring plenty of sets; running out matters more than a little attack.
claims.say: no recharging at zakum, bring lots of star sets

claims.text: Early 4th job Night Lords put SP into Triple Throw first (at least 20), then usually Shadow Shifter or Venomous Star, so Shadow Stars stays at a low level for many levels.
claims.say: nl: triple throw to 20 first, shadow stars stays low a while

claims.text: A practical Night Lord mix is a few Crystal Ilbi sets for damage plus many cheaper sets for training and bossing, moving to all high-attack stars once Shadow Stars reaches 10 or more.
claims.say: use cheap stars until shadow stars is 10+, then upgrade

claims.text: Crystal Ilbi Throwing-Stars are the step up from Ilbis in attack and cost several times as much.
claims.say: crystal ilbis are the step above ilbis, pricey though

claims.text: Carry about 12 to 16 sets of stars for a long training session or a boss run.
claims.say: carry 12 to 16 star sets for training or bossing

claims.text: A Dark Knight should put one point in Rush at 120, or keep one ready for it, and that single level is enough for a long time.
claims.say: 1 point in rush at 120 is enough for ages

claims.text: Early Maple Warrior only pays off if you solo a lot; in parties someone usually casts it already, so putting Power Stance first can be the better choice.
claims.say: skip early mw if you party, someone has it

claims.text: Berserk is handy on weaker bosses such as Mushmom, and on Geist Balrog in the Amoria Party Quest when the party has no healer.
claims.say: berserk works on weak bosses like mushmom

claims.text: Power Stance to 10 is worth getting fairly early since Dark Knights boss often, and it speeds training too because hits stop knocking you off your target.
claims.say: get stance early, helps bossing and training

claims.text: Aura of the Beholder heals on a timer, holds the heal until you take damage, and only heals while you are under the Berserk threshold, so it never knocks you out of Berserk.
claims.say: aura heal wont pull you out of berserk

claims.text: Maxing Aura of the Beholder in the late 130s and early 140s cuts potion use a lot while training.
claims.say: max aura of the beholder, you'll pot way less

claims.text: One point in Hero's Will is worth it if you are often the one getting seduced at Horntail.
claims.say: 1 in heros will if you get seduced at ht

claims.text: The Berserk 20 mastery book drops from Zakum and the Berserk 30 book from Horntail.
claims.say: berserk 20 book is from zakum, 30 from ht

claims.text: The Power Stance 20 book drops from Papulatus and the Power Stance 30 book from Zakum.
claims.say: stance 20 from pap, stance 30 from zakum

claims.text: Both Rush books come from Pianus: the 20 book from the left-side Pianus and the 30 book from the right-side one.
claims.say: rush books drop from pianus

claims.text: The Achilles 30 book drops from Manon and the Maple Warrior 20 book from Horntail.
claims.say: achilles 30 from manon, mw 20 from ht

claims.text: Some Dark Knights put one point in Beholder and then rush Berserk to its cap, so they can solo with it in the 120s instead of slowly grinding or getting leeched.
claims.say: some dks go berserk first so they can solo

claims.text: Other Dark Knights max Rush before Hex of the Beholder for training, and take Power Stance to 30 before Achilles because Stance matters so much at Horntail.
claims.say: some max rush before hex, stance before achilles

claims.text: When Papulatus or Pianus drops you to 1 HP you are in Berserk range, so one strong attack before you drink a potion acts as a cheap finisher.
claims.say: after a 1/1 at pap, hit once in berserk then pot

claims.text: Meso Explosion hits much harder with many separate meso drops than with one large drop, because each drop explodes for its own damage.
claims.say: drop lots of small meso stacks for meso explosion, not one big one

claims.text: Training by spamming Blizzard eats a lot of mana potions, so it is costly for an Arch Mage short on mesos.
claims.say: blizz training eats a ton of mana pots

claims.text: Most sword Paladins stick to two-handed swords because one-handed swords reach less, and short reach makes Blast whiff often.
claims.say: pallys mostly use 2h swords, 1h reach makes blast miss

claims.text: Heroes mind short weapons less because Brandish has a fixed reach; a short sword only makes finishers like Panic and Coma harder to land, and you get used to it.
claims.say: brandish has fixed reach, short swords only hurt finishers

claims.text: Black Crystal Blade is a level 100 fast one-handed sword with 99 attack, 3 STR, 50 accuracy and 7 slots; the accuracy alone saves a lot on accuracy gear.
claims.say: black crystal blade: lvl 100 1h sword with 50 acc

claims.text: To make a Black Crystal Blade, bring a Crystal Blade, a Zakum Diamond, 50 Black Crystals, a One-Handed Sword Forging Manual and a One-Handed Sword Forging Stimulator to Adonis in El Nath; a failed forge loses everything.
claims.say: forge it at adonis in el nath, failing eats the materials

claims.text: Whether the Crystal Blade really reaches far is disputed: its data uses the short one-handed sword after-image like a Red Katana, though the author felt it hit farther in play.
claims.say: crystal blade reach is debated, it may be short like a katana

claims.text: A cheaper one-handed Paladin setup is a well scrolled Black Crystal Blade paired with a shield of around 10 attack.
claims.say: budget 1h pally: black crystal blade plus a 10 att shield

claims.text: Sacrifice ignores the monster's weapon defense, which makes it strong against high-defense bosses for Dragon Knights.
claims.say: sacrifice ignores weapon def, nice vs tanky bosses

claims.text: Polearm Dragon Knights generally max Sacrifice, while spear users often skip it or leave it low, and hybrids lean on Spear Crusher for bossing instead.
claims.say: polearm drks max sacrifice, spear drks often skip it

claims.text: Besides Sacrifice, attacks said to bypass weapon defense include Assaulter, Boomerang Step, Shadow Meso, Phoenix, Frostprey, Snipe and Heaven's Hammer.
claims.say: assaulter, bstep, shadow meso, snipe and hh skip weapon def

claims.text: Summons appear to ignore weapon defense, doing the same damage to high-defense and low-defense monsters, unlike normal attacks.
claims.say: summons seem to ignore weapon def

claims.text: Sacrifice spends your own HP, so combining it with Berserk's low-HP playstyle can leave a Dark Knight at almost no HP.
claims.say: careful, sacrifice plus berserk can drop you near 1 hp

claims.text: Common first-job opening: 1 point in Arrow Blow at level 10, 3 into The Blessing of Amazon, then max The Eye of Amazon for range.
claims.say: lv10: 1 arrow blow, 3 blessing, then max eye of amazon

claims.text: After The Eye of Amazon, max Critical Shot first if you want crits right away, or Double Shot first for the most raw damage, then max the other one.
claims.say: max crit shot or double shot next, then the other

claims.text: The last first-job points, around levels 28-30, go into Focus.
claims.say: dump the last 1st job sp into focus

claims.text: If restocking arrows bothers you more than weak hits, put 2 points into Soul Arrow : Bow early; otherwise finish Bow Mastery first.
claims.say: hate buying arrows? put 2 in soul arrow early

claims.text: From level 40, raise Arrow Bomb : Bow; take Power Knock-Back before finishing Arrow Bomb only if monsters getting too close is a real problem for you.
claims.say: after 40 pump arrow bomb, pkb only if close mobs bug you

claims.text: Late second job: max Bow Booster and Soul Arrow : Bow, then spend the leftover points in Focus by level 70.
claims.say: finish booster and soul arrow, rest into focus by 70

claims.text: These hunter builds leave out Final Attack : Bow entirely, since few players still consider it worth taking.
claims.say: most hunters skip final attack these days

claims.text: Rushing Power Knock-Back before putting a second point into Arrow Bomb : Bow is no longer worth it with the training spots now available.
claims.say: dont rush pkb before arrow bomb, not worth it

claims.text: Single-target ranger path: 1 Strafe at 70 and max Strafe first, then Puppet to 6, then start on Silver Hawk.
claims.say: single target ranger: max strafe, 6 puppet, then hawk

claims.text: Mobbing ranger path: 1 Strafe at 70, 5 Mortal Blow to open Arrow Rain, Arrow Rain to 21, then 1 point in Inferno.
claims.say: mob ranger: 1 strafe, 5 mortal blow, rain to 21, 1 inferno

claims.text: Almost every ranger path puts about 6 points into Puppet early in third job and raises it further later on.
claims.say: get puppet to 6 early in 3rd job

claims.text: Late third job: max Silver Hawk and Arrow Rain, then finish Puppet and either Inferno or Mortal Blow; Thrust gets its points last.
claims.say: late 3rd: max hawk and rain, then puppet, thrust last

claims.text: If you will mob with Hurricane at 4th job anyway, skip maxing Inferno late in third job and put those points into Mortal Blow and Thrust instead.
claims.say: going hurricane later? skip inferno, take mortal blow and thrust

claims.text: Snipers can mirror these ranger builds with their own skills, except Blizzard does not fill the same role as Inferno and Golden Eagle is less useful in the long run.
claims.say: snipers can copy it, but blizzard isnt inferno and eagle matters less

claims.text: Standard 1st job warrior SP: max Power Strike, Slash Blast and Improved MaxHP Increase, then put Improved HP Recovery at 5, Endure at 3 and Iron Body at 2.
claims.say: 1st job war: max power strike, slash blast, max hp skill

claims.text: The Zakum prequests need level 50; first ask your class's 3rd job instructor in El Nath's Chief's Residence for permission to start them.
claims.say: zak prequests need lv 50, ask your 3rd job instructor in el nath

claims.text: In El Nath, Tylus gives Zakum quest permission to warriors, Robeira to magicians, Rene to bowmen, Arec to thieves and Pedro to pirates.
claims.say: tylus, robeira, rene, arec or pedro start the zakum quests

claims.text: Adobis, who runs the Zakum prequests, waits at The Door to Zakum, which you reach by walking down through El Nath's Dead Mine maps.
claims.say: adobis is at the door to zakum, past the dead mine

claims.text: Bring a big stack of HP potions, around 300 if you are inexperienced, before heading out for the Zakum prequests.
claims.say: bring around 300 hp pots for the zakum prequests

claims.text: You need an Eye of Fire to enter Zakum's Altar, and you must have finished the prequests at least once yourself; a bought Eye of Fire alone will not get you in.
claims.say: you need an eye of fire and must do the prequests once yourself

claims.text: An Eye of Fire is refined from one Piece of Fire Ore, one Breath of Lava and 30 Zombie's Lost Gold Tooth.
claims.say: eye of fire needs fire ore, breath of lava and 30 gold teeth

claims.text: Stage 1: form a party and choose to explore the Dead Mine at Adobis; you get 30 minutes to collect 7 Keys and trade them for the Fire Ore.
claims.say: zak stage 1: party up and find 7 keys within 30 minutes

claims.text: Exiting the far end of room 7-2 or 10-2 takes you into inner chamber 16, which holds the last three keys.
claims.say: go through 7-2 or 10-2 to reach the room 16 chamber

claims.text: Rooms 8-2 and 16-1 hold neither keys nor documents, so skip them and leave their chests alone.
claims.say: skip rooms 8-2 and 16-1, they're empty

claims.text: Breaking chests inside chamber 16 can throw you back to the main chamber; go back in through room 7 or 10.
claims.say: chests in room 16 can kick you out, re-enter via 7 or 10

claims.text: With all 7 Keys gathered, one player drops them in front of the big chest in room 16-5, and a Fire Ore pops out a few seconds later.
claims.say: drop all 7 keys at the big chest in 16-5 for the fire ore

claims.text: The party leader collects the Fire Ore and all documents before talking to Aura in the main chamber, and must leave last or members who leave after get no reward.
claims.say: leader hands in to aura and leaves last or others get nothing

claims.text: The Dead Mine return scrolls drop you at the first Dead Mine map, so later Zakum trips skip most of the dungeon walk.
claims.say: dead mine return scrolls skip the long walk to zakum

claims.text: A party of two or fewer that is short on time should ignore the documents and only gather the 7 Keys, which takes roughly 8 to 12 minutes.
claims.say: small party? skip documents and just get the 7 keys

claims.text: Stage 2 at Adobis is a two-room jump quest and the toughest part for most players; talk to Lira at the end to receive the Breath of Lava.
claims.say: zak stage 2 is a jump quest, lira gives the breath of lava

claims.text: Stage 3 needs 30 Zombie's Lost Gold Tooth, hunted from Miner Zombies in Dead Mine I through IV or bought from other players.
claims.say: farm 30 gold teeth from miner zombies in the dead mine

claims.text: Once you hold the ore, the Breath of Lava and the teeth, ask Adobis to refine them and he hands over 5 Eyes of Fire.
claims.say: adobis refines the three items into 5 eyes of fire

claims.text: The Zakum Helmet is an untradeable one-of-a-kind level 50 hat that adds all four main stats, high defenses, accuracy and avoid; it is the main prize players chase at Zakum.
claims.say: zakum helm: lv 50 hat with all stats, def, acc and avoid

claims.text: With little mastery, your minimum hit can drop below zero after a monster's weapon defense; those hits become 1 damage, so a low-mastery Savage Blow lands many 1s on sturdy mobs.
claims.say: low mastery = lots of 1 dmg hits on high def mobs

claims.text: When a monster is a higher level than you, your damage drops by about 1% per level of difference, on top of the weapon defense reduction.
claims.say: mobs above your level cut your dmg about 1% per level

claims.text: For dagger thieves, max damage comes from LUK times 3.6 plus STR and DEX, scaled by weapon attack; mastery only lifts the low end of the range.
claims.say: dagger dmg is mostly luk x3.6 + str + dex, mastery lifts min

claims.text: A typical bandit around 37 to 43 leaves STR and INT at base, keeps DEX around 70 to 80 and puts the remaining AP into LUK.
claims.say: bandit: base str/int, dex 70-80, rest luk

claims.text: A monster can be poisoned by Venom up to three times at once, stacking the damage.
claims.say: venom stacks up to 3 times on one mob

claims.text: Venom damage seems to be unaffected by elemental weakness.
claims.say: venom ignores elemental weakness i think

claims.text: Weapon speed does not change how fast most magician spells cast; Explosion is the exception and casts noticeably faster with a faster staff or wand.
claims.say: weapon speed only matters for explosion, not other spells

claims.text: Spell Booster only works with a wand or staff; keeping it active on a one-handed sword is a glitch, not normal play.
claims.say: spell booster only works with wands and staffs

claims.text: After casting Infinity there is a short delay before you can start casting, and that delay already counts against its active time.
claims.say: infinity has a cast delay that eats into its duration

claims.text: Balanced Fury throwing stars can only be recharged in New Leaf City, and that limit is intended rather than a bug.
claims.say: balanced furies only recharge in nlc

claims.text: Wolf Spider Cavern is among the best spots for fire/poison mages from about 70 to 100 who cannot yet hit Skelegons reliably, using Poison Mist and Explosion on its dense spawn.
claims.say: fp 70-100 that can't hit skeles yet? mist wolf spiders

claims.text: Wolf Spiders have no magic attacks or dispel, are small enough to jump over on slopes, and are easy to teleport through, so deaths are rare when misting them.
claims.say: wolf spiders got no magic attacks, pretty safe to mist

claims.text: Wolf Spiders can also drop Blue Scarab claws and the rare Dark Scroll for Pole Arm for ATT and Dark Scroll for Spear for ATT; those dark scrolls are the rarest drops there.
claims.say: wolf spiders can drop scarabs and rare dark scrolls

claims.text: Stock plenty of potions such as Ginger Ale, Sorcerer Elixir, Mana Bull or Unagi before going to Wolf Spider Cavern; the map is crowded and you may not get it back after leaving.
claims.say: stock up before wolf spiders, you might lose the map

claims.text: For misting, use a Fast (4) wand or staff so a jumpcast Explosion goes off before you land; it has to be a wand or staff so Spell Booster still works.
claims.say: use a fast 4 wand or staff so jumpcast explosion lands

claims.text: The Fast (4) mage weapons are Hinomaru Fan, Evil Wings, Poison Mushroom and Zhu-Ge-Liang Wand; Hinomaru Fan and Poison Mushroom only come from Gachapon.
claims.say: fast 4 mage weps: hinomaru fan, evil wings, poison mushroom

claims.text: Poison Mushroom has a very low LUK requirement, which makes it the one Fast (4) staff a LUKless mage can wear.
claims.say: luckless mage? poison mushroom is your fast staff

claims.text: Celestial Staff is listed as fast on some item sites but actually casts at Normal (6) speed, the same as ordinary staves.
claims.say: celestial staff is really normal speed, not fast

claims.text: A LUKless mage without a Poison Mushroom should use a Maple wand or staff such as Maple Staff or Maple Wisdom Staff; speed-boosting one-handed swords cannot be used with Spell Booster.
claims.say: no poison mushroom? use a maple staff so booster works

claims.text: For misting, a Zakum Helmet beats movement helmets like a Bone Helm, because cutting touch damage matters more than a little extra speed and jump.
claims.say: zhelm beats a bone helm here, less touch dmg

claims.text: Poison from Poison Mist leaves mobs at 1 HP instead of killing them, so magic attack matters less while misting; wear HP gear if you have it and let Explosion finish the job.
claims.say: mist leaves em at 1 hp, wear hp gear and explode

claims.text: Speed or jump scrolled shoes help while misting; jump shoes make jumpcasting easier and with enough jump let you skip a few teleports.
claims.say: jump or speed shoes help, jump makes jumpcasting easier

claims.text: On single targets use Magic Claw rather than Fire Arrow; Magic Claw passes through walls and is a little faster.
claims.say: single target? magic claw, it goes through walls

claims.text: Always keep Magic Guard up while misting, and recast Spell Booster before it runs out.
claims.say: never forget magic guard, keep booster up

claims.text: Jumpcasting Explosion down slopes saves a lot of time; put Explosion right next to your jump key, and avoid wireless keyboards that drop combined key presses.
claims.say: jumpcast explosion down slopes, bind it next to jump

claims.text: Holding down while jumpcasting Explosion drops you through the platform while you attack, clearing what is below you so you land safely.
claims.say: hold down + jump + explosion to drop thru while attacking

claims.text: Telecast, attacking while teleporting, anywhere you are not jumpcasting, and do it the moment you land to avoid getting touched.
claims.say: telecast wherever you can, right as you land

claims.text: If a priest buffs you with Holy Symbol or a thief with Haste, have them sit up top instead of attacking the bottom spawn, or they may loot rare drops like Ilbis that you mostly damaged.
claims.say: bring a priest for hs but keep em up top, not looting

claims.text: On the three maps leading to Wolf Spider Cavern, changing channel puts you mid-map or right by the next portal, so a restock trip can take only about a minute and a half.
claims.say: cc on the maps before spiders to reach the portal faster

claims.text: Cast buffs like Spell Booster in midair while dropping off the middle platforms so the animation ends before you land, rather than on the busy bottom ladder; Slow is another good midair cast there.
claims.say: cast booster midair while dropping, not on the ladder

claims.text: No need to mist the bottom-right corner of Wolf Spider Cavern; its few spiders soon walk toward the middle and get caught in the mist there.
claims.say: don't bother misting bottom right, they walk to the middle

claims.text: The bottom of Wolf Spider Cavern has a safe crevice where misted spiders bunch up, so one Explosion there clears a big group.
claims.say: bottom crevice is a safe spot, misted spiders pile up

claims.text: A low-level Cleric can level by partying with a Dragon Knight who keeps using Dragon Roar, which burns his own HP, and healing him back up with Heal.
claims.say: cleric tip: party a dk spamming roar and keep healing him

claims.text: Heal costs the Cleric little MP in this setup; the Cleric can hand Mana Elixirs to the Dragon Knight so he can keep casting Dragon Roar.
claims.say: toss the dk some mana elixirs so he can keep roaring

claims.text: Healing a partner who hurts himself needs no monsters, so a Cleric can level this way anywhere, even in the Free Market.
claims.say: you can literally level a cleric in the fm this way

claims.text: A Dragon Khanjar can come out of Gachapon, and a clean one with above-average attack is rare and highly valued by dagger users.
claims.say: dragon khanjars come from gach, high att clean ones are rare

claims.text: On a rare high-attack clean dagger, scroll with 10% scrolls backed by White Scrolls so failed scrolls don't eat the upgrade slots.
claims.say: on a godly clean dagger, use 10%s with white scrolls

claims.text: Meso Explosion only shows a limited number of damage lines per monster; when many bags explode, the extra hits are added into the shown numbers, so piles look stronger per bag than they are.
claims.say: with lots of bags the hits merge into fewer numbers on screen

claims.text: A new rogue can reach level 10 on Maple Island by killing snails and shrooms and finishing the island quests.
claims.say: maple island quests plus snails and shrooms get you to 10

claims.text: The Land of Wild Boar, with Wild Boars, Dark Axe Stumps and Jr. Boogies, stays a usable thief spot from the 20s into the 30s.
claims.say: wild boars are fine from your 20s into your 30s

claims.text: In the 20s a rogue can hunt Leatty on the upper Orbis Tower floors or Snowy Hill, moving to Dark Leatty on the lower floors once past level 25.
claims.say: leattys in orbis tower, switch to dark leattys after 25

claims.text: Kerning City Party Quest is a listed alternative to grinding for a rogue in the 20s.
claims.say: in your 20s kpq is a nice break from grinding

claims.text: Ludibrium Party Quest admits players from level 35, but those under 40 contribute little, so higher level members often avoid taking them.
claims.say: lpq lets you in at 35 but most parties want 40+

claims.text: Ludibrium Party Quest gives quick exp in the low to mid 40s, and the pace falls off by the late 40s.
claims.say: lpq is great early 40s, it slows down late 40s

claims.text: Fresh second job thieves can train on Brown and Pink Teddies at Terrace Hall in Ludibrium, or on Horny and Zombie Mushrooms in Ant Tunnel I.
claims.say: 30s thief: teddies at terrace hall or ant tunnel shrooms

claims.text: The Orbis colour gardens with Jr. Cellion, Jr. Grupin and Jr. Lioner work through the 30s and 40s, though they are decent rather than the best choice.
claims.say: jr cellions in the orbis gardens are ok in your 30s and 40s

claims.text: Luster Pixies drop poor mesos, but their sun etc items can be exchanged for a chance at a cape INT 60% scroll, so exchange them or sell them to players.
claims.say: luster pixie sun pieces trade for a shot at cape int 60

claims.text: Truckers at Suburban Area 2 in Singapore remain a workable thief spot over a wide span, from the 40s up to about 80.
claims.say: truckers in singapore are good from 40 all the way to 80

claims.text: Jr. Yetis are good mesos: their skins and leather sell, but most of the value comes from the chance of a gloves attack 60% scroll.
claims.say: jr yetis are good money, glove att 60 drops are the prize

claims.text: Orbis Party Quest and Ludibrium Maze Party Quest are good alternatives to grinding for thieves in their 50s and 60s.
claims.say: 50s and 60s, mix in opq or lmpq

claims.text: Windraiders at the Phantom Forest crossroads maps, and later at Lower Ascent in Crimsonwood Mountain, are a thief option from the 50s through the 80s.
claims.say: windraiders in phantom forest work from the 50s to the 80s

claims.text: For assassins in the 60s and 70s, Singapore's Mysterious Path and Ghost Ship maps hold Pac Pinkies, Selkie Jr. and Slimies to train on.
claims.say: 60s-70s sin: ghost ship and mysterious path in singapore

claims.text: The Forest of Golem, with Mixed Golems and Dark Stone Golems, is a thief spot from the 60s up to about 100.
claims.say: forest of golem is a solid thief spot from 60s to 90s

claims.text: Death Teddies at Forgotten Path of Time <3> suit the late 70s and 80s, ideally for a Hermit whose Shadow Partner is level 21 or higher.
claims.say: death teddies late 70s, best with 21+ shadow partner

claims.text: At Destroyed Dragon's Nest, Hermits and Night Lords snipe Jr. Newties from the popular platform on the middle left of the map, which keeps lower levels safe.
claims.say: newties: stand on the mid left platform and snipe them

claims.text: From the 80s on, partying with a Priest for Holy Symbol and a Dragon Knight for Hyper Body is faster than soloing; solo only when no party is available.
claims.say: get a priest for hs and a dk for hb, beats soloing

claims.text: Red and Black Kentaurus at Griffey Forest in Leafre give decent exp from 80 to 100, but Griffey can spawn there at any moment, so stay alert.
claims.say: kents in griffey forest are good but watch for griffey

claims.text: Squids and Risell Squids in the Dangerous Sea Gorge maps on Aqua Road are a thief option from 80 up to 120.
claims.say: squids in aqua road work from 80 to 120

claims.text: Spirit Vikings at Warped Path of Time <4> are not good mesos; their main lure is the rare Ilbi Throwing-Stars drop.
claims.say: spirit vikings arent good money, you just hope for ilbis

claims.text: Crimson Guardians in Crimsonwood Keep are an endgame thief spot from 120 onward.
claims.say: crimson guardians are good once you hit 120

claims.text: A Chief Bandit can train on Gobies at Deep Sea Gorge II from the 70s, but needs at least one point each in Meso Guard and Meso Explosion, since Meso Explosion does the killing.
claims.say: gobies as a cb need at least 1 meso guard and 1 meso explosion

claims.text: Soloing a Goby map makes higher level players resent and kill-steal you; partying with them, ideally with a Priest, and sharing the map gets everyone faster exp.
claims.say: party up at gobies, soloing the map just gets you ksed

claims.text: Elderwraiths at The Evil Dead suit Chief Bandits with Meso Explosion, Meso Guard and level 20 Dark Sight: lure them while in Dark Sight, drop meso bags and explode them.
claims.say: elderwraiths: lure in dark sight then drop mesos and explode

claims.text: For a Bandit in the 60s, a training spot is only worth it if you can kill its monsters in two hits or fewer.
claims.say: only train where you can 2 hit the mobs

claims.text: A Shadower training on Dreamy Ghosts needs plenty of mesos for potions and a maxed Band of Thieves, and a Priest friend helps a lot.
claims.say: himes as a shad: max band of thieves, bring cash and a priest

claims.text: Typhons on The Path of Peril in Crimsonwood Mountain are a Chief Bandit and Shadower option from 90 to 120.
claims.say: typhons in crimsonwood work for cbs from 90 to 120

claims.text: Brextons and Dark Cornians at Dragon Forest III in Leafre are a Shadower spot from 110 to 130.
claims.say: 110-130 shad: brextons and dark cornians in dragon forest

claims.text: Wolf Spiders at Wolf Spider Cavern cost a lot in potions but pay back well in mesos, with a chance at Ilbi Throwing-Stars.
claims.say: wolf spiders eat pots but the money is good

claims.text: For a cheap bossing character, a Bowmaster costs less to fund than a Night Lord because it does not need expensive throwing stars.
claims.say: bm is cheaper to fund than nl, no pricey stars to buy

claims.text: Heroes can start bossing early once their accuracy is high enough, but they deal less damage at bosses than Bowmasters.
claims.say: heroes can boss early with enough acc but bm hits harder

claims.text: A Bowmaster can only boss early with enough HP, so expect to do some HP washing if you want to boss on one.
claims.say: bm needs decent hp to boss early, expect to wash a bit

claims.text: High-level Night Lords use very few potions at bosses because of their high avoid, often fewer than a Bishop even in a long Zakum run.
claims.say: nls barely use pots at zak, their avoid does the work

claims.text: At Zakum a Bowmaster goes through roughly three times as many potions as a Night Lord.
claims.say: bm burns way more pots at zak than an nl does

claims.text: Soloing Papulatus goes much faster on a Bowmaster or a Hero than on a Night Lord.
claims.say: bm or hero solos pap way faster than an nl

claims.text: Heroes can solo most bosses without much funding, though a few bosses stay out of reach for them until very high levels.
claims.say: heroes solo most bosses cheap, a few need really high lvl

claims.text: A Bishop's job at most bosses is healing and support, so a cheap shop wand from Ellinia is enough for that role.
claims.say: bish at bosses can get by with a cheap ellinia wand

claims.text: Corsairs lose damage at bosses while they wait to get Battleship back, so the author ranks them below Night Lords for bossing.
claims.say: corsairs lose dps while waiting on their battleship

claims.text: Soloing Bigfoot is slow and risky because its knockback behaves oddly and it keeps closing in; expect a long fight, around 25 minutes for the author.
claims.say: solo bigfoot is slow and risky, its knockback is weird

claims.text: Archers and Night Lords solo Bigfoot by keeping it knocked back, then dropping a Puppet or Flash Jumping away when they need to recast buffs.
claims.say: archers/nls: kb bigfoot, puppet or flash jump away to rebuff

claims.text: Bigfoot hands out a big exp reward, which is why many players leech it rather than solo it.
claims.say: bigfoot gives big exp, lots of people leech it

claims.text: A Beginner gains roughly 10 max HP for each AP placed into HP.
claims.say: beginners get about 10 hp per ap in hp

claims.text: A Zakum Helmet adds defense and accuracy, which helps a low-DEX Beginner hit monsters more reliably.
claims.say: zak helm gives def and acc, nice for low dex beginners

claims.text: If a Beginner still trains well without it, it is better to wait for natural HP to grow than to sink saved AP into HP early just to join a Zakum Helmet run.
claims.say: no rush on zak helm, dont dump ap in hp if you train fine

claims.text: Bigfoot is boss-flagged, so Mortal Blow cannot instantly kill it and poison or web effects do not work either; you simply have to out-damage it.
claims.say: mortal blow cant instakill bigfoot, its boss flagged

claims.text: A Bowmaster can let Bigfoot pin them against a wall and keep Hurricane going, but should be ready to jump clear of its stomp attack.
claims.say: vs bigfoot, let it pin you to a wall and hold hurricane

claims.text: Mortal Blow still triggers on Bigfoot without killing it, and the proc knocks it back, giving you room to keep attacking.
claims.say: mortal blow still procs on bigfoot and knocks it back

claims.text: Under the newer stat system, Beginners can't put AP into HP or MP until level 11.
claims.say: beginners can't add ap to hp or mp before level 11

claims.text: At the first job advancement your stats reset to that class's base, e.g. a Magician gets 20 INT and 4 in the rest, and all AP goes back into your pool.
claims.say: 1st job advance resets your stats and refunds the ap

claims.text: HP pumped into a Beginner before the first job advancement disappears when stats reset at promotion, so it is not a way to get extra HP.
claims.say: don't pump hp as a beginner, job advance wipes it

claims.text: Taking first job late still gives the SP for every level you skipped; a Magician who advances at 11 gets all the missed SP.
claims.say: late 1st job still gives you all the sp you missed

claims.text: HP and MP share a single count of invested AP, so AP Reset can only take points back out of HP or MP up to the number of AP you put into them; plan washes around what you have invested.
claims.say: you can only reset as many ap out of hp/mp as you put in

claims.text: Every DEX point adds 0.8 accuracy and every LUK point adds 0.5 accuracy.
claims.say: each dex is 0.8 acc, each luk is 0.5 acc

claims.text: Monsters above your level take extra accuracy to hit; the requirement eases as you level up toward the monster's level.
claims.say: mobs over your level need more acc, it eases as you level

claims.text: A common hit-rate rule: accuracy of about 3.67 times a monster's avoid means you never miss it, while about 1.83 times its avoid is where you start landing hits at all.
claims.say: about 3.7x a mob's avoid in acc and you never miss

claims.text: Keeping DEX low gives a warrior more damage, but it costs hit rate and narrows which mobs they can train on at lower levels.
claims.say: low dex warrior hits harder but misses lots early

claims.text: An unfunded low-DEX Fighter near level 50 can trade an attack glove for a cheap accuracy glove to hit mobs a few levels sooner, with Rage covering part of the lost attack.
claims.say: low dex fighter? an acc glove lets you hit stuff sooner

claims.text: Players generally rate a scrolled Lionheart above a scrolled Lion's Fang for a Fighter around level 50.
claims.say: most say a scrolled lionheart beats a lion's fang

claims.text: Hermits do not strictly need to HP wash for bosses like Papulatus, Zakum or Capt. Latanica.
claims.say: hermits dont need to hp wash for pap, zak or latanica

claims.text: Horntail is where a thief's low HP becomes a real barrier.
claims.say: horntail is where low thief hp really hurts

claims.text: A Hyper Body buff from a party member makes HP targets for bosses much easier for a thief to reach.
claims.say: hyper body makes boss hp targets way easier

claims.text: To compare attacks, estimate damage per second as average damage times skill percentage times modifiers such as combo or element, divided by the attack's animation time; between skills of one job you can skip damage range and defense.
claims.say: compare skills by avg dmg x skill % / attack time
