claims.text: Average damage comes from primary stat times the weapon multiplier plus secondary stat, scaled by mastery and weapon attack; a two-handed sword uses a multiplier of 4.6.
claims.say: 2h swords use a 4.6 weapon multiplier in the dmg formula

claims.text: For a Brawler skill combo, damage per second is simply the combo's total damage percent divided by its total time.
claims.say: brawler combo dps = total % dmg over total time

claims.text: A new warrior needs 35 STR to make the 1st job advancement, so early AP goes into STR until it reaches 35.
claims.say: get str to 35 first, that's what warrior 1st job needs

claims.text: For an HP-washing warrior, the plan is to stop spending AP once STR hits 35 and bank every point through the early levels until Improved MaxHP Increase is maxed.
claims.say: hp washer? bank ap after 35 str till improved max hp is maxed

claims.text: With Improved MaxHP Increase maxed around level 15, the banked AP all goes into MaxHP, because each point added then gives extra HP on top of the normal gain.
claims.say: once improved max hp is maxed, dump the saved ap into hp

claims.text: At the Red Wyvern nest, one snipe spot covers three lanes, but you must drop to a square below for the last lane, taking hits from wyverns on your platform meanwhile.
claims.say: red wyverns: nuke 3 lanes up top, drop down for the last

claims.text: The Blue Wyvern nest has three lanes; a middle platform that spawns nothing lets you hit the third lane without being touched, though the spawn is a bit weaker than at the Reds.
claims.say: blue wyverns: hit lane 3 from the empty middle platform

claims.text: The Blue Wyvern nest's split-up spawn makes it poor training; once you can one-hit them, Newties give better exp.
claims.say: blue wyvern nest is meh, newties are better if you 1-hit

claims.text: Red Wyverns give an I/L Archmage more exp per hour than Blue Wyverns give an F/P Archmage, so Bishops selling leech also do better at the Reds.
claims.say: reds beat blues for exp, bishops should sell leech there

claims.text: At the wyvern nests, standing in the middle of a platform covers more wyverns around you than a snipe spot near the edge, though you will still get hit.
claims.say: stand mid-platform at wyverns for the most coverage

claims.text: For an unfunded claw user in the 50s and 60s, a Zakum Helmet is the best single upgrade to save up for.
claims.say: low funds at 5x? save for a zakum helmet first

claims.text: Maple claws are scarce and expensive, so a low-funded assassin can aim for a level 60 claw instead, which scrolls can push to around 45 attack.
claims.say: skip maple claw, a scrolled lv 60 claw can hit about 45 att

claims.text: When a Priest lures for a partner, run out one way and come back, then Teleport ahead of the mob so you can cast Holy Symbol on the partner before the monsters reach you.
claims.say: tele ahead of your lure and cast hs before the mob catches up

claims.text: Press Heal right after taking a hit instead of holding the key down, so you waste less time and MP.
claims.say: tap heal right after you get hit, dont hold it

claims.text: You can drink HP potions during Holy Symbol's casting delay, so keep potions that restore what you lose while casting.
claims.say: you can pot during the hs cast delay

claims.text: A Priest who trains without Magic Guard can turn it on just to cover the Holy Symbol cast and then right-click the buff icon to cancel it.
claims.say: mg for the hs cast then right click it off

claims.text: With a Triple Throw 30 mastery book, a new Night Lord can put 4th job points straight into Triple Throw from 120, which helps a lot in bossing, especially Zakum.
claims.say: get the tt30 book and pour points into triple throw at 120

claims.text: Since someone in a party, often the Bishop, usually casts Maple Warrior, a Night Lord can delay it; players who solo get more from maxing it.
claims.say: party has mw anyway, solo players should max it though

claims.text: Using Heal on party members is not blocked by the anti-AFK check that stops attacks after about 100 uses without moving.
claims.say: heal on party members dodges the 100 attack afk limit

claims.text: A Cleric earns more exp the more HP a party member is missing, so a high-HP warrior makes a far better heal target.
claims.say: heal a high hp warrior, more missing hp = more exp for you

claims.text: Shadowers survive well through high avoid and Meso Guard, while Meso Explosion, their strongest tool for soloing bosses, spends mesos every use.
claims.say: shadower tanks with meso guard, meso explosion costs mesos

claims.text: Marksmen are often taken to high-level bosses mainly for Sharp Eyes, and their low HP means they need Hyper Body or HP washing to survive Horntail and Pink Bean.
claims.say: mm at big bosses is mostly there for sharp eyes, needs hb

claims.text: Snipe and Piercing Arrow hit far harder than most training monsters can absorb, so much of the damage is overkill that brings no extra exp.
claims.say: snipe and pierce overkill most training mobs

claims.text: Marksmen need not be slow: most put around 9 points into Thrust and make up the rest of their speed with gear, pets or a mount.
claims.say: put some points in thrust, gear and mounts cover speed

claims.text: Crossbow users avoid hits by freezing monsters with Blizzard, luring them with Puppet and pushing them away with Power Knock-Back.
claims.say: mm stays safe with blizzard, puppet and knockback

claims.text: A fighter gains little from going one-handed unless they own a well-scrolled Red Katana plus an attack shield; otherwise two-handed swords are the better pick.
claims.say: only go 1h with a good red katana and an att shield

claims.text: A budget fighter path: keep a 100% scrolled early sword until about level 60, move to a Sparta, then a Doombringer or Red Katana at level 70.
claims.say: lv60 sparta, then doombringer or red katana at 70

claims.text: A character must be at least level 15 to give fame or defame, so a fame alt only needs to reach 15.
claims.say: you need lv 15 to fame someone

claims.text: On Maple Island almost all fast early exp comes from the starter quests rather than from kills, so run through them in order to level quickly.
claims.say: on maple island do the quests, thats where the exp is

claims.text: The Mushroom Town starter quests go Heena, Sera, Roger (eat the apple he gives you), Nina and Sen, Todd, then Peter, taking a new character to about level 3-4.
claims.say: start with heena, sera, roger's apple, then nina and sen

claims.text: At level 4 put 3 SP into Nimble Feet and keep it on a hotkey to run between quest NPCs faster on Maple Island.
claims.say: lv4: 3 sp in nimble feet, use it to run between npcs

claims.text: Mai's four training quests east of Amherst have you kill Stumps (and gather branches), then Red Snails, then Slimes, then Pigs; change channels whenever a map's spawn runs dry.
claims.say: on mai's quests, change channel when the mobs run out

claims.text: Pio's recycling quest in Amherst needs items from the breakable boxes around Amherst and its fields, so smash boxes as you pass them.
claims.say: break the boxes around amherst for pio's quest

claims.text: Yoona's quest needs drops from Shrooms and Blue Snails; kill both while heading back west toward Southperry.
claims.say: kill shrooms and blue snails for yoona's quest

claims.text: Bari's Test west of Southperry asks for an Orange Mushroom Cap from Orange Mushrooms and gives a big exp reward for that level.
claims.say: bari's test: grab an orange mushroom cap, nice exp

claims.text: Shanks in Southperry is the way off Maple Island; talking to him ends your time on the island and takes you to Lith Harbor.
claims.say: talk to shanks in southperry to leave maple island

claims.text: Olaf at Lith Harbor has quick quests on arrival, including the Path of Pirate and Path of Warrior introductions, that can push you to level 10.
claims.say: do olaf's quests in lith harbor right when you land

claims.text: Around level 10 the Nautilus has several quick exp quests, starting with Kyrin, and the Mysterious Presence chain that sends you to Bart at the harbor pays out over several steps.
claims.say: lv10: the nautilus has quick quests, start with kyrin

claims.text: Thomas Swift in Henesys takes you to Amoria, where Claudia's quest in the hair salon gives good exp around level 11-12.
claims.say: thomas swift in henesys sends you to amoria for claudia

claims.text: From about level 10 to 15 the Henesys Party Quest gives faster exp than questing; you can run it as a Beginner and keep going after first job.
claims.say: hpq is faster exp than questing at 10-15

claims.text: A weak low-level character in the Henesys Party Quest can equip a low-attack weapon and act as the party's lurer, pulling monsters instead of fighting them.
claims.say: in hpq a weak char can lure mobs for the party

claims.text: Warriors take their first job from Dances with Balrog in the Warriors' Sanctuary in Perion.
claims.say: warrior 1st job: dances with balrog in perion

claims.text: A new warrior can put 5 SP into Improved HP Recovery and 2 into Improved MaxHP Increase, then keep adding to Improved MaxHP Increase while leveling to 15.
claims.say: new warrior: 5 in hp recovery, rest into max hp increase

claims.text: Park a finished fame alt where you will need it most, which for most players is the Henesys Free Market.
claims.say: park your fame alt in the henesys free market

claims.text: Do not name fame alts after your main character, so people you defame cannot trace them back to you.
claims.say: dont name fame alts after your main

claims.text: Training on Birks and Dual Birks as a Crusader without Power Guard burns through hundreds of potions an hour, which makes soloing there costly.
claims.say: birks without power guard eat hundreds of pots an hour

claims.text: Honsters sold in New Leaf City heal far more for the price than ordinary potions, and their healing grows with your max HP; park a mule in New Leaf City to buy them.
claims.say: buy honsters in nlc, cheap and heal a ton

claims.text: Satay, a Singapore food item, restores a large fixed amount of HP and works as a main potion for high-HP characters.
claims.say: satay from singapore is a solid hp pot

claims.text: Ciders from Showa Town give more weapon attack than Rage at a small accuracy cost, but the buff does not stack.
claims.say: showa ciders beat rage for atk but dont stack

claims.text: A Crusader can solo at Mysterious Path 3 until about level 76; after that potion costs push you toward training with priests.
claims.say: mysterious path 3 works for saders till about 76

claims.text: Power Guard and Improving MP Recovery save a Crusader a lot on potions; skipping them makes solo training expensive.
claims.say: dont skip power guard, it saves pots

claims.text: A Cygnus Knight can only be created once the account already has a character above level 20.
claims.say: you need a char over lv 20 on the account to make a cygnus

claims.text: Cygnus Knights receive 6 AP per level up until level 70, and their level cap is 120.
claims.say: cygnus get 6 ap a level until 70, max level is 120

claims.text: Blaze Wizards have no Energy Bolt or Improving MP Recovery in 1st job, and their Magic Claw is fire element, so it hits fire-weak monsters harder and fire-resistant ones softer.
claims.say: blaze wizard magic claw is fire, so watch for fire resistant mobs

claims.text: Flame, the Blaze Wizard's sprite summon, raises your weapon and magic defense and attacks up to 3 nearby monsters with fire damage.
claims.say: the flame sprite boosts def and hits 3 mobs with fire

claims.text: Blaze Wizard 1st job plan: 1 point in Magic Claw at 10, max Increasing Max MP, then max Magic Claw, then max Flame, then Magic Guard, ending with a point in Magic Armor at 30.
claims.say: bw 1st job: claw 1, max mp skill, claw, flame, then magic guard

claims.text: Max Increasing Max MP early, because it only boosts the MP gained from level ups and MP AP spent after you learn it.
claims.say: max increasing max mp early, it only helps future level ups

claims.text: Blaze Wizards learn Spell Booster in 2nd job, a casting-speed buff that explorer magicians only get in 3rd job.
claims.say: blaze wizards already get spell booster at 2nd job

claims.text: Blaze Wizard 2nd job: put 1 point in Teleport, then max Fire Pillar first, since it is the only 2nd job spell that hits several monsters (up to 6).
claims.say: bw 2nd job: 1 teleport then max fire pillar for mobbing

claims.text: After Fire Pillar the plan maxes Spell Booster, then Teleport, Meditation and Elemental Reset, with Slow filled last.
claims.say: after pillar: booster, teleport, meditation, reset, then slow

claims.text: Leave Fire Arrow at 1 point: 3rd job attacks replace it, and a maxed Magic Claw handles single targets through 2nd job.
claims.say: keep fire arrow at 1, magic claw does single target fine

claims.text: Elemental Reset makes your spells element-neutral for a while, which helps against monsters that resist fire.
claims.say: use elemental reset on mobs that resist fire

claims.text: Meditation is a party buff that raises the magic attack of members nearby.
claims.say: meditation gives your party extra magic attack

claims.text: Slow lowers the movement speed of up to 6 monsters at once.
claims.say: slow hits up to 6 mobs and makes them crawl

claims.text: Blaze Wizard 3rd job: max Flame Gear first; it leaves a fire zone that keeps damaging and burning monsters inside, much like Poison Mist does for Fire/Poison.
claims.say: bw 3rd job: max flame gear first, it works like poison mist

claims.text: After Flame Gear, max Fire Strike, a fireball that hits up to 6 monsters, to finish off the burning mobs, then max Element Amplification.
claims.say: then max fire strike, then element amplification

claims.text: Element Amplification raises spell damage in exchange for a higher MP cost on every cast.
claims.say: element amp means more spell damage but more mp per cast

claims.text: Seal stops nearby monsters from using their skills for a short time, but it does not work on bosses.
claims.say: seal stops mobs using skills, but not bosses

claims.text: The Blaze Wizard's Elemental Resistance reduces damage from fire, ice, lightning and poison magic alike, broader than the explorer Fire/Poison's Partial Resistance.
claims.say: bw elemental resistance covers all four magic elements

claims.text: Ifrit summons a fire spirit that attacks up to 3 monsters for you.
claims.say: ifrit is a fire summon that hits 3 mobs

claims.text: Spare points at the end of 3rd job go into Seal and Elemental Resistance once the attack skills are done.
claims.say: dump leftover sp into seal and elemental resistance

claims.text: Dawn Warriors get no Improving HP Recovery or Endure in 1st job, and their Max HP Enhancement needs no prerequisite.
claims.say: dawn warriors skip endure, max hp skill has no prereq

claims.text: Dawn Warrior 1st job plan: max Max HP Enhancement at 10-13, put 1 point each into Soul, Power Strike and Slash Blast, then max Slash Blast, then Power Strike, with the rest in Soul.
claims.say: dw 1st job: max hp skill, slash blast, power strike, then soul

claims.text: Soul, the Dawn Warrior's sprite, raises your defense and hits up to 3 monsters with holy damage; it is the only holy-element skill the class gets.
claims.say: the soul sprite is the only holy skill a dawn warrior has

claims.text: Soul Rush works like Flash Jump, giving Dawn Warriors thief-style mobility from 2nd job on.
claims.say: soul rush is basically flash jump for dawn warriors

claims.text: Soul Blade throws a ranged soul projectile that hits several monsters, the Dawn Warrior's 2nd job mobbing attack.
claims.say: soul blade is the dw ranged mob attack in 2nd job

claims.text: Dawn Warrior Final Attack is an active buff: its follow-up strikes can only trigger while the buff is on.
claims.say: dw final attack is a buff, it only procs while active

claims.text: Rage raises weapon attack for party members nearby but lowers their weapon defense.
claims.say: rage gives party attack but lowers weapon def

claims.text: Sword Booster needs Sword Mastery at level 5 and Final Attack needs it at level 3; Sword Mastery also adds accuracy.
claims.say: sword booster needs mastery 5, final attack needs mastery 3

claims.text: Dawn Warrior 2nd job plan: 1 Soul Blade, max Soul Rush, then Sword Mastery with part of Sword Booster, max Soul Blade, then Rage, leaving Booster unmaxed and Final Attack last.
claims.say: dw 2nd: soul rush, mastery, soul blade, rage, fa last

claims.text: Dawn Warrior 3rd job: max Combo Attack first, then Soul Driver, then Soul Charge.
claims.say: dw 3rd: combo first, then soul driver, then soul charge

claims.text: Soul Driver strikes up to 8 monsters four times over a wide area, similar to Shout or Dragon Roar.
claims.say: soul driver hits lots of mobs 4 times, great for mobbing

claims.text: Soul Charge adds damage to your sword attacks but is neutral, not holy.
claims.say: soul charge is neutral, not holy

claims.text: Coma uses a fully charged combo and hits up to 6 monsters with a chance to stun them.
claims.say: coma uses full combo, hits 6 mobs and can stun

claims.text: Panic is rated poorly for Dawn Warriors; after the main skills put points into Coma and then MP recovery, leaving Panic for last.
claims.say: panic is weak on dw, leave it for last

claims.text: Brandish hits several monsters in front of you twice and can trigger Final Attack.
claims.say: brandish hits several mobs twice and triggers final attack

claims.text: Advanced Combo requires Combo Attack at max; it raises the orb cap to 10 and sometimes charges two orbs at once.
claims.say: adv combo needs max combo and lets you stack 10 orbs

claims.text: Risell Squids resist fire and lightning, so F/P mages lean on Poison Mist there rather than fire spells.
claims.say: squids resist fire, so f/p rely on poison mist there

claims.text: Mist from the top of the squid map to the bottom (or the reverse), change channel where you end up, then work back the other way killing poisoned squids with Magic Claw and Explosion.
claims.say: mist down the map, cc, then kill your way back up

claims.text: A point in Explosion lets you clear clumps of three or more squids quickly, though some players would rather hold off on Explosion until their accuracy on squids improves.
claims.say: a point in explosion helps clear squid clumps

claims.text: Magic Claw stays useful at squids: its two hits rarely both miss and its fast cast lets you hit and move away.
claims.say: magic claw is still great for finishing poisoned squids

claims.text: Speed potions from the Ludibrium potion shop make getting around the squid map much quicker.
claims.say: speed pills from the ludi pot shop help a lot at squids

claims.text: At squids a Zakum Helmet beats a Bone Helm: its avoid and defense cut damage taken and potion use.
claims.say: wear your zhelm at squids, saves pots

claims.text: Speed shoes matter at squids; Violet Snowshoes already have speed and jump, and cheap Scroll for Shoes for Speed 60% can push them past 14 speed.
claims.say: violet snowshoes plus speed scrolls are great for squidding

claims.text: Jump still affects movement while swimming in Aqua Road, but speed is the more important stat for getting around underwater.
claims.say: jump helps underwater too, but speed matters more

claims.text: Skip level 70 elemental wands for squid training; their slow attack speed hurts the mist-and-kill cycle.
claims.say: skip the lv70 element wands at squids, too slow

claims.text: Only use a speed weapon like a Red Whip or an umbrella at squids before you have Spell Booster; afterwards switch to a real mage weapon.
claims.say: ditch the red whip once you have booster

claims.text: Capes with speed or jump such as an Icarus Cape help at squids, and the Alcadno Cape or Zenumist Cape from the Magatia quests are even better.
claims.say: wear a speed cape at squids, magatia capes are best

claims.text: Use the jump-down move at squids to escape squids you've provoked and to drop into spots you can't teleport to.
claims.say: use jump down to escape aggro squids

claims.text: Mounts at squids are debated: some find mounting too slow and risky since you can't pot or attack while mounted, while others tap the mount on and off for fast downward moves in the water.
claims.say: careful mounting at squids, you cant pot while riding

claims.text: Other squids spawn among the Risell Squids and can clog the map; clear them with Magic Claw or move to another channel.
claims.say: if the other squids clog the map, claw them or cc

claims.text: If you can't afford speed gear for squids, HP gear makes potions go further and lowers the risk of dying.
claims.say: no speed gear? wear hp gear at squids so pots go further

claims.text: Save potions at squids by not bumping into squids, using Aqua Road's low gravity and Teleport to get clear, and only potting when you need to.
claims.say: dont bump squids and tele away, your pots last way longer

claims.text: Risell Squids drop Scroll for Gloves for ATT 60% and Scroll for Gloves for DEX 60%, along with Mana Elixirs and Power Elixirs.
claims.say: risell squids drop glove att and dex 60% scrolls

claims.text: Squids are easier for F/P mages than sharks, which strip your buffs with Dispel.
claims.say: squids are easier than sharks, no dispel to deal with

claims.text: Early in 4th job a Marksman picks up one point each in Frostprey, Dragon's Breath, Snipe and Marksman Boost before investing heavily in the main skills.
claims.say: early 4th: 1 point each in frostprey, db, snipe and boost

claims.text: Marksman Boost raises mastery and weapon attack, which matters most for Piercing Arrow because that skill depends on steady base damage rather than critical hits.
claims.say: boost is big for pierce, pierce wants min damage not crits

claims.text: Marksman Boost adds flat attack, so it is relatively stronger for a character with low weapon attack, whereas the value of Sharp Eyes does not depend on base stats.
claims.say: low att? boost helps you more than it helps geared people

claims.text: Since the gains from Sharp Eyes and Marksman Boost multiply, a split between the two can beat putting everything into one of them.
claims.say: se and boost multiply, a split can beat maxing one

claims.text: A higher Sharp Eyes makes a Marksman more wanted in training parties and boss runs, since the buff boosts the whole party's damage.
claims.say: high sharp eyes gets you into parties and boss runs easier

claims.text: If you regularly party with another archer who already has maxed Sharp Eyes, putting points into Marksman Boost is the better choice.
claims.say: if your party has a max se archer, go boost instead

claims.text: Dragon's Breath pairs well with an Ice/Lightning mage's Blizzard, which makes an early point in it worthwhile.
claims.say: dragons breath combos nicely with a blizzard

claims.text: One Marksman's priority order is Sharp Eyes, then Marksman Boost, then Piercing Arrow, then Dragon's Breath and Snipe, then Frostprey, with Blind last.
claims.say: se, boost, pierce, then db and snipe, frostprey, blind last

claims.text: Choose between Dragon's Breath and Snipe by your training map: big mob maps favour Dragon's Breath, while maps of fewer tough monsters such as Jr. Newties favour Snipe.
claims.say: mobby map? db first. newtie style map? snipe first

claims.text: Snipe is useful for instantly removing stray monsters left between Piercing Arrow mobs, and it adds more at bosses than extra Sharp Eyes levels would.
claims.say: snipe is great for picking off strays between pierces

claims.text: Soloing Jr. Newties is poor for a 4th job archer; one player found Crimson Guardians at about 128 beat a three-attacker Newtie party for exp.
claims.say: by 128 crimson guardians beat newtie parties for an mm

claims.text: Crimson Guardians cannot be frozen and their mace attack is too strong to tank, so expect some deaths while learning them and try them early in a level when little exp is at stake.
claims.say: guardians: avoid the mace hit, learn them early in a level

claims.text: At Crimson Guardians a Marksman deals most damage with Arrow Eruption and fires Snipe while moving from one side of the map to the other.
claims.say: at guardians spam arrow eruption, snipe while crossing

claims.text: Archers farm Pianus for the Sharp Eyes mastery book, and it can take several books before one succeeds.
claims.say: pianus is where people farm the sharp eyes book

claims.text: If you want to boss early, take Marksman Boost to about 6, then Sharp Eyes to 15 before adding more Boost, since bossing parties value Sharp Eyes.
claims.say: wanna boss early? boost to 6, then se to 15 first

claims.text: HP washing means putting AP into MP and then using an AP Reset to move that point into HP.
claims.say: hp wash: ap into mp, then ap reset it into hp

claims.text: AP put into HP on level up gives more HP than moving a point into HP with an AP Reset, though players disagree on the exact amounts.
claims.say: level up ap in hp gives more than resetting into hp

claims.text: Higher INT, including INT from gear, raises the MP gained per point put into MP, so leveling in INT gear lets you wash more HP later.
claims.say: wear int gear when adding mp, you get more mp per point

claims.text: When using an AP Reset you can see how much HP the move would add and cancel without consuming the reset.
claims.say: you can check what an ap reset gives and cancel it

claims.text: The Balrog quest line in Sleepywood opens at level 50 and has no upper level cap.
claims.say: balrog quests start at 50, no level cap

claims.text: You must finish Manji's old Gladius quest before you can pass the new doorway into the deep area of the dungeon.
claims.say: finish manjis gladius quest first or you cant get in

claims.text: The first quest sends you down the long path to find Muyoung, who waits in the room at its bottom.
claims.say: first quest: walk down the path and find muyoung

claims.text: Chrishrama asks you to seal six tombstone NPCs spread through the Ant Tunnel, so expect to walk all the way down.
claims.say: chrishrama wants 6 tombstones sealed down the ant tunnel

claims.text: A note near the start of the Ant Tunnel goes to Muyoung; handing it over warps you into a fight with Jr. Balrog, after which Tristan's soul tells his story.
claims.say: bring the note to muyoung and you fight jr balrog

claims.text: Muyoung only lets a party of at least three into the Balrog boss map.
claims.say: need 3+ in your party to enter balrog

claims.text: Later quests in the chain have you defeat the Balrog, carry reports between Muyoung and Manji, and visit a suspicious man Muyoung spotted.
claims.say: later quests: kill balrog, run reports to manji

claims.text: A Wheel of Destiny revives you in the same map but does not stop exp loss the way a Safety Charm does.
claims.say: wheel of destiny revives you but doesnt save exp

claims.text: HP washing means putting level-up AP into HP, then using AP Resets to take points out of MP and move them into your main stat.
claims.say: hp washing: hp on level up, reset mp into your main stat

claims.text: Blood washing is adding AP to HP for several levels and resetting it later; you give up damage until you reset.
claims.say: blood washing is pumping hp now and resetting later

claims.text: Warriors gain the most from HP washing thanks to Improving Max HP Increase; bowmen and thieves gain less, and mages get no benefit.
claims.say: warriors gain the most from hp washing

claims.text: Each AP washed into HP gives warriors about 50-55 HP for 4 MP lost, thieves and bowmen about 16-20 HP for 12 MP, and mages only 10-20 HP for 90 MP.
claims.say: warriors get about 50 hp per ap washed, others way less

claims.text: Mages should not HP wash; Magic Guard makes MP their real protection, so trading MP for HP is a loss.
claims.say: mages shouldnt hp wash, magic guard uses mp

claims.text: Wearing INT gear when you level raises the MP you gain, roughly 1 extra MP per 10 INT, which lets you reset more MP into HP later.
claims.say: wear int gear when you level for more mp to wash

claims.text: Every class has a minimum MP for its level; you cannot reset MP below it, and that floor limits how much you can wash.
claims.say: you cant reset mp below your level's minimum

claims.text: Double resetting, or resetting MP straight into HP, does not work as another way to wash.
claims.say: double resetting doesnt work, just reset mp

claims.text: Wash after you have Improving Max HP Increase for the full benefit; you can add AP to HP now and reset it out later as long as you stay above the minimum MP.
claims.say: wash after you get improving max hp increase

claims.text: Higher max HP also makes percent-based potions heal you for more.
claims.say: more hp means percent pots heal you more

claims.text: Night Raven's Wing and Stonetooth Sword attack at the same speed; Night Raven's Wing asks for less DEX but has lower attack.
claims.say: night raven's wing: same speed as stonetooth, less dex, less att

claims.text: A Hero with 4 base DEX can wear Night Raven's Wing full time by getting the DEX from equipment while keeping a STR pendant.
claims.say: 4 base dex hero can still wear night raven's wing with dex gear

claims.text: With gear and a Sniper Pill, the author's low-DEX Hero hits everything he fights, Blue Mushmom included, so more DEX gear would only trade away attack.
claims.say: low dex hero + gear + sniper pill hits even blue mushmom

claims.text: Once the main Chief Bandit skills are maxed, the usual place for leftover SP is Chakra rather than Shield Mastery, which few bandits bother leveling.
claims.say: after your main cb skills, chakra usually beats shield mastery

claims.text: Chakra only restores HP after a short wait, so many Chief Bandits hardly use it while training even once it has points in it.
claims.say: chakra heals slow cuz you gotta wait, lots of cbs barely use it

claims.text: A Hero bossing Bigfoot can use a two-handed sword to stand in one spot and keep attacking; the slower attack speed fits better with how Bigfoot reacts to knockback.
claims.say: 2h sword is comfy on bigfoot, stand and spam

claims.text: Around levels 150-157, repeatedly hunting Bigfoot can provide most of a warrior's exp.
claims.say: bigfoot hunting is solid exp in the 150s

claims.text: On Bigfoot, Power Strike can deal damage faster than Brandish once Final Attack procs are counted.
claims.say: on bigfoot power strike can beat brandish with final attack

claims.text: Pink Bean's first stages hit moderately, but the later stages bring large area attacks that can kill low-HP ranged characters outright.
claims.say: pink bean gets way nastier in the later stages, watch hp

claims.text: When Ariel comes out in Pink Bean's fifth stage, ranged attackers gather on a ledge spot to stay clear of the big attack in the middle of the map.
claims.say: pb stage 5: ranged stand on the ledge, away from the middle

claims.text: Pink Bean's final form hits harder than most archers' HP, so a ranged player's survival there depends on the rest of the party.
claims.say: last pb form can one-shot archers, lean on your party

claims.text: Bringing Buccaneers with Time Leap and several Shadowers to Pink Bean saves a lot of lives.
claims.say: bring bucs with time leap and a few shads to pb

claims.text: Archers short on HP for bosses can HP wash; MP washing lets you wash even more HP but costs a lot of AP Resets.
claims.say: hp wash for bosses, mp washing lets you go further but costs

claims.text: Higher total LUK lowers the percentage of exp you lose when you die.
claims.say: more luk means you lose less exp when you die

claims.text: Chief Bandits around 100 can train on Bains: lure them with Band of Thieves, then Savage Blow them from a small edge platform where they can't hit you.
claims.say: cb 10x: lure bains with bot, savage blow from a ledge

claims.text: Bains shoot fire; do two Savage Blows, then a jumping Savage Blow to hop over the flame ball and take no damage.
claims.say: vs bains: 2 savage blows, then jump sb over the fireball

claims.text: If Bains keep shooting instead of walking to the platform edge, crouch or step back a little until they come closer.
claims.say: if bains keep shooting, crouch or back off a bit

claims.text: Use Assaulter to cross between platforms and to finish off lone Bains.
claims.say: assaulter to hop platforms and kill lone bains

claims.text: The Slime Tree, Southern Forest I, works for warriors from 10 to 18: a tall tree full of bouncing Slimes to climb around and clear.
claims.say: slime tree is good 10-18, climb around and kill everything

claims.text: Henesys Hunting Ground I has four tiers: Snails and Shrooms at the bottom, then Slimes, Orange Mushrooms, and Green Mushrooms on top; hunt Slimes to 18, Orange Mushrooms to 20, then Green Mushrooms to 25.
claims.say: hhg1: slimes till 18, orange shrooms till 20, greens till 25

claims.text: Pig Beach suits warriors from 15 to 25: Pigs and Ribbon Pigs fill the bottom and an Iron Hog sometimes shows up; to leave, go far right, climb, and jump across the platforms.
claims.say: pig beach is good 15-25, watch out for the iron hog

claims.text: Warriors from 22 can Power Strike the mushrooms in the upper part of Ant Tunnel; stay away from the lower areas until about 25.
claims.say: ant tunnel top part from 22, skip the deep part till 25

claims.text: The Land of Wild Boar is a 25-35 warrior spot with Wild Boars, Dark Axe Stumps and Jr. Boogies, which are hard to hit and can curse you; run back and forth killing everything.
claims.say: wild boar land is good 25-35, jr boogies can curse you

claims.text: Changing channel or stepping into the Cash Shop and back drops you at the map's entry point, a quick way to get back to the top after clearing down a map.
claims.say: cc or pop into cash shop to get back to the top of a map

claims.text: Eos Tower's 8th floor of Block Golems is one of the best warrior spots from 40 to 50: clear from top to bottom, killing the big groups that gather at each end, and repeat.
claims.say: eos tower block golems are great for warriors at 40-50

claims.text: Practice Field: Easy Level is flat, so warriors 50-69 can mob its Straw Target Dummies side to side or Power Strike them one at a time; slightly more efficient than Jr. Yetis, but crowded.
claims.say: practice field easy is flat and good 50-69, but crowded

claims.text: Watch out for Icy Path I has Jr. Yetis on two platforms plus some Hectors; at 50-58, mob the bottom, clear the top, then drop down to a bigger spawn and repeat.
claims.say: icy path 1 is good 50-58, bottom then top then repeat

claims.text: At Cold Field I, poke each Hector on the way across without killing it, then Slash Blast the pack as it charges you; sell the Hector Tails for mesos.
claims.say: cold field: tag every hector then slash blast the pack

claims.text: Drake's Meal Table suits warriors 55-62: Slash Blast the Cold Eyes and Wild Kargos at the bottom, climb up killing everything, and use the Cash Shop to return to the bottom; the Kargos burn a lot of potions.
claims.say: drake's meal table 55-62, kargos make it a big pot burn

claims.text: Ghost Pirates and Dual Ghost Pirates can't hit you with their magic while you stay on the ground close to them; jump after attacking and they fire a shot you can't avoid.
claims.say: never jump near ghost pirates, their magic only hits you airborne

claims.text: Death Teddies in Forgotten Path of Time 3 suit Dragon Knights and Crusaders, ideally with a Priest following you counter-clockwise; without one you burn huge amounts of potions.
claims.say: death teddies at forgotten path 3, bring a priest along

claims.text: Master Death Teddies in Lost Time are one of the fastest Dragon Knight spots when a Priest gathers them for you; start at the bottom and work up together.
claims.say: master death teddies at lost time, fast for drk with a priest

claims.text: Dual Ghost Pirates in Unbalanced Time are top White Knight exp from about 80 with Fire Charge near max: clear each platform from the top down, then change channel or use the Cash Shop to restart at the top.
claims.say: dual ghost pirates are wk heaven from 80, clear top to bottom

claims.text: At Dual Ghost Pirates, Power Strike them one or two at a time and save Slash Blast for groups of three or more.
claims.say: ps 1-2 duals, only slash blast groups of 3+

claims.text: Blue Kentauruses burn potions; a Priest helps, but needs to be about 83+ to leech since they are not undead; mob the bottom, middle and top platforms in turn.
claims.say: blue kents burn pots, bring a priest if you can

claims.text: White Knights on a budget with Ice Charge 13 or higher can hunt Red Kentauruses instead: slower than Blue ones, but easier to move around and much cheaper on potions.
claims.say: wk with ice charge can do red kents, slower but cheap on pots

claims.text: Wolf Spiders suit warriors from about 88 to 120, with White Knights starting once Ice Charge reaches 16; they burn lots of potions but can drop Ilbi Throwing-Stars.
claims.say: wolf spiders 88-120, big pot burn but ilbis can drop

claims.text: A Dragon Knight Wolf Spider rotation: clear upper left, then upper right, then the bottom mob, then herd each leg's spiders to its edge; pull them with a mobbing skill rather than walking in, and skip legs with four or fewer.
claims.say: at spiders herd them to the edge, skip legs with 4 or less

claims.text: Grim Phantom Watches in Forbidden Time suit Dragon Knights and Crusaders from 90 with a Priest: circle the top section, then mob the middle and bottom; a 100+ Hermit can take the bottom.
claims.say: grims at forbidden time from 90, bring a priest

claims.text: At Deep Sea Gorge II, swim around breaking Goby houses and killing the Gobies that pour out; White Knights want Ice Charge 16 first, and Crusaders lean on Coma.
claims.say: gobies: break the houses, then kill the gobies that come out

claims.text: At Gobies, killing the Bone Fish makes more Goby houses spawn, so clear stray fish as you go; bring houses and fish low and finish them fast before they cast their defense boosts.
claims.say: kill the bone fish at gobies, it makes more houses spawn

claims.text: Before 90, Crusaders at Gobies do better with a Chief Bandit partner taking the top platform; Haste helps, and Priests, Hermits or Ice/Lightning mages also pair well, since Coma plus Ice Strike wipes a Goby mob.
claims.say: under 90 do gobies with a cb, coma plus ice strike is great

claims.text: Black Crow sometimes spawns at Encounter with the Buddha; leave or avoid it unless you want to spend a pile of potions and time.
claims.say: if black crow shows up at the buddha map just run

claims.text: The Armory is a long, flat map full of Bains for Dragon Knights and White Knights from 100; mob them across the map, which gets easier once 4th job Rush arrives.
claims.say: bains at the armory from 100, rush makes it easier

claims.text: Pinning a boss such as Bigfoot against a wall and timing throws well raises a Night Lord's real damage output.
claims.say: pin the boss on a wall and time your throws

claims.text: A common Zakum rule of thumb is at least 2000 HP with your gear on, counted before Hyper Body.
claims.say: have 2k hp with gear, before hb, for zakum

claims.text: One of Zakum's attacks drops your HP and MP to 1, so be ready to pot right away.
claims.say: zak can drop you to 1/1, pot right away

claims.text: Players disagree on where to stand at Zakum: some hug the left wall, others warn the fire attack's marker lands right on the wall and suggest standing between the wall and the platform edge above.
claims.say: stand between the wall and the plat edge at zak

claims.text: Bring a big stack of Power Elixirs for Zakum, around 500 for a run of about 15 minutes, since they refill MP fully for Magic Guard users.
claims.say: bring like 500 power elixirs for a zak run

claims.text: Pack plenty of All Cure Potions for Zakum to clear its curses and seals; around 400 was suggested.
claims.say: bring a few hundred all cures to zak

claims.text: For a player short on mesos, the cheapest mage branch to raise is Cleric, then Ice/Lightning, with Fire/Poison the most expensive.
claims.say: cheapest mage to play: cleric, then i/l, then f/p

claims.text: A mage without funds is best off leveling mostly through party quests until about level 71.
claims.say: broke mage? just pq your way up to 71

claims.text: From 71 to 4th job, Fire/Poison levels fastest thanks to Poison Mist, while Ice/Lightning is slower but saves potions because its attacks freeze monsters.
claims.say: f/p levels fastest with poison mist, i/l is slower but cheap

claims.text: Clerics get invited to parties easily, while Fire/Poison and Ice/Lightning mages have a much harder time finding one.
claims.say: clerics get party invites easily, other mages less so

claims.text: A LUKless mage needs almost no funding: base INT does most of the work, and a broke LUKless mage ends up only a little behind a heavily funded LUK mage in total INT at the same level.
claims.say: go lukless if you're broke, base int carries you

claims.text: A cheap mage weapon path: Wooden Wand, then Maple Staff, then Maple Lama Staff, then Maple Wisdom Staff.
claims.say: wooden wand, maple staff, maple lama staff, then maple wisdom

claims.text: Spiegelmann's Necklace from Monster Carnival is a cheap pendant that gives mages a little INT.
claims.say: get the spiegelmann necklace from cpq for a bit of int

claims.text: Broke mages can fill their slots with cheap HP gear, 100%-scrolled earrings and capes, and cheap Work Gloves, then upgrade slowly as mesos come in.
claims.say: use cheap hp gear and 100% scrolled stuff, upgrade later

claims.text: Choose between 30% and 70% scrolls by weighing price against how much stat you actually lose: on a cape the 70% gives only 1 less INT, but on gloves the 30% gives far more and is worth it.
claims.say: pick 30% or 70% by how much stat you actually give up

claims.text: Don't sink mesos into scrolling a hat before you get a Zakum Helmet, since a pre-Zakum hat will never match a scrolled Zakum Helmet.
claims.say: don't godly scroll a hat before you get a zakum helm

claims.text: From 10 to 21, Henesys Party Quest gives good exp at almost no cost.
claims.say: hpq from 10 to 21 is cheap good exp

claims.text: From 21 to 30, Kerning City Party Quest is a good way for a broke mage to level.
claims.say: kpq from 21 to 30 is fine for a broke mage

claims.text: From 30 to 50, do Monster Carnival until you own a Spiegelmann's Necklace, or Ludibrium Party Quest, which costs potions but can give valuable scrolls.
claims.say: 30-50 do cpq for the necklace or lpq for scrolls

claims.text: From 51 to 71, Ludibrium Maze Party Quest pays out potions to sell and handy scrolls such as cape INT and HP scrolls.
claims.say: lmpq from 51 to 71 gives pots and handy scrolls

claims.text: The author advises mages against leveling in Pirate Party Quest, though its hat reward is nice.
claims.say: ppq is poor for leveling but the hat is cool

claims.text: With an MP Eater and Heal build, a cleric can reach 4th job while barely buying any potions or relying on Magic Guard.
claims.say: clerics can level to 4th job with almost no pots

claims.text: Clerics past level 80 are wanted in boss parties while other mages are often passed over, so clerics can earn shares of boss drops.
claims.say: 80+ clerics get boss invites and loot splits easily

claims.text: INT and magic attack gear pays off more for attack mages than for clerics, since their attack spells scale harder than Heal; clerics can get by on cheaper HP gear.
claims.say: attack mages gain more from int gear than heal clerics do

claims.text: Players disagree on which mage makes the most mesos: some argue Fire/Poison farms best, then Ice/Lightning, with priests last because their income depends on party splits.
claims.say: some say f/p makes the most mesos, then i/l, priests last

claims.text: New mages should scroll their early gear for HP first and slowly move to INT and magic attack gear once they can afford it.
claims.say: scroll for hp first, switch to int gear when you can

claims.text: Some players put a few AP into HP as a Beginner, where each point gives more HP, for a cheap HP boost; the author warns it is risky on a first character since gear is easier to change than AP.
claims.say: some put beginner ap into hp, risky on a first char

claims.text: A new priest can spend the first levels of 3rd job hunting Voodoos.
claims.say: new priests can start 3rd job at voodoos

claims.text: One Fire/Poison 2nd job plan: 1 point in Teleport, then max Fire Arrow, Teleport, Poison Breath and Slow, leaving the last points for Meditation or MP Eater.
claims.say: fp 2nd job: max fire arrow, tele, poison breath, slow first

claims.text: The Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest bonus stage can drop the Crimsonheart Cloak, a tradeable level 90 cape with +4 to all stats and 8 upgrade slots.
claims.say: cwkpq bonus can drop crimsonheart cloak, +4 all stats and 8 slots

claims.text: The same bonus stage can drop the Blackfist Cloak, a tradeable level 100 cape giving +120 HP and +4 weapon attack with 5 slots.
claims.say: blackfist cloak from cwkpq bonus: lvl 100 cape with hp and 4 att

claims.text: The Goldensoul Cape, a tradeable level 120 cape with +3 INT and +100 MP and 5 slots, also comes from the CWKPQ bonus stage.
claims.say: goldensoul cape from cwkpq bonus is a lvl 120 int and mp cape

claims.text: Players report the CWKPQ bonus stage dropping high-level weapons such as Crushed Skull, Khanjar, Stormshear, Concerto, Berzerker, Crossheider and Elemental Wand 5.
claims.say: cwkpq bonus can drop weapons like crushed skull and khanjar

claims.text: Reported mastery book drops from the CWKPQ bonus include level 30 books for Big Bang, Blizzard, Brandish, Heaven's Hammer, Hurricane, Rapid Fire and Sharp Eyes.
claims.say: cwkpq bonus drops 4th job books like hurricane 30 and brandish 30

claims.text: Tao of Harmony, Tao of Shadows and Tao of Sight also drop in the CWKPQ bonus; Tao of Harmony is a material for crafting Balanced Fury throwing stars.
claims.say: taos drop in cwkpq bonus, tao of harmony goes into balanced fury

claims.text: A Buccaneer's Speed Infusion lifts a Marksman's attack speed close to a Bowmaster's, which helps a lot at bosses such as Zakum.
claims.say: grab a bucc's speed infusion, your mm attacks way faster

claims.text: Drop hunting is a decent income for a poor character; hunting the Snowman area boss about once a week while channel hopping can turn up several scrolls.
claims.say: channel hop snowman weekly for scroll drops

claims.text: Running Amoria Party Quest regularly is a way to keep a steady meso income.
claims.say: run apq regularly for steady mesos

claims.text: Snipe becomes a strong Marksman skill once it has a good skill level.
claims.say: snipe gets really good once it has some levels

claims.text: Skelegons are a standard grinding target for high-level Night Lords, and getting a reliable two-hit kill on them is a common damage goal.
claims.say: skelegons are great nl exp once you can 2-hit them

claims.text: Training next to a Marksman or Bowmaster for their Sharp Eyes buff makes two-hitting Skelegons far more consistent than spending on gear upgrades.
claims.say: get a sharp eyes buff, 2-hitting gons gets way more reliable

claims.text: A weapon attack potion can lift a Night Lord over the damage needed to two-hit Skelegons part of the time when gear alone is not enough.
claims.say: attack pots can get you over the 2-hit line at gons

claims.text: A Night Lord that never adds extra DEX can still reach steady two-hit kills on Skelegons once the equipment is upgraded enough.
claims.say: dexless nl can still 2-hit gons with good gear

claims.text: A Khanjar requires 60 STR, so a LUK-based Shadower usually gathers STR from gear such as a STR top or cape, or adds a few AP to base STR.
claims.say: khanjar needs 60 str, use str gear or put a few ap in str

claims.text: When trading DEX pieces for STR or LUK gear, make sure you still meet your dagger's DEX requirement (for example a Blood Dagger); a DEX face accessory can cover a small gap.
claims.say: swapping dex gear? make sure you still meet your dagger's dex req

claims.text: The Horntail Necklace's all-stat bonus can cover both STR and DEX requirements at once, letting a Shadower move the cape and earring slots from DEX gear to LUK gear.
claims.say: ht necklace stats let you swap dex pieces for luk ones

claims.text: Build your gear so you meet equip requirements without Maple Warrior active; leaning on the buff to wear items is unreliable.
claims.say: dont rely on maple warrior to meet equip reqs

claims.text: A common Shadower attack loop is Boomerang Step followed by two Savage Blows, repeated.
claims.say: shadower combo: boomerang step then savage blow twice

claims.text: Hamstring does not slow bosses at all; testing on Anego (Female Boss) showed no effect.
claims.say: hamstring does nothing to bosses

claims.text: Bowmasters can leave Hamstring at one point and spend SP on Phoenix, Concentrate and Maple Warrior first.
claims.say: bm: 1 in hamstring, max phoenix, concentrate and mw first

claims.text: Hamstring only pays off if you first push mobs away with Dragon's Breath; otherwise just killing them with Strafe or Hurricane is quicker.
claims.say: hamstring only helps after you knock mobs back

claims.text: Bow and claw attacks reach about 400 pixels, measured from a spot slightly in front of your character's center.
claims.say: archer and sin range is about 400 px in front of you

claims.text: Puppet is rarely worth casting while training; when surrounded, firing Hurricane one way and then the other clears things faster.
claims.say: skip puppet when training, hurricane both ways

claims.text: Training a cleric on monsters Heal cannot hurt, like Dark Stone Golems, Yetis or Malady, is slow exp; some still hunt them for drops.
claims.say: dsg and yetis are slow for clerics, only farm them for drops

claims.text: Cleric players argue over Holy Arrow versus Teleport: critics say Holy Arrow barely beats Magic Claw and want Teleport maxed instead, others keep Holy Arrow for holy-weak targets.
claims.say: holy arrow vs teleport is debated, most max teleport

claims.text: Holy Arrow is useful against holy-weak monsters that Heal does not damage, such as Dark Stone Golems.
claims.say: holy arrow helps on holy-weak mobs heal cant hit, like dsg

claims.text: Use Magic Claw sparingly: to tag a boss for leech exp or to finish off a lone monster that Heal can hurt.
claims.say: only claw to tag bosses or finish a lone undead

claims.text: A Priest around level 86 with little HP gear can solo Grim Phantom Watches without Magic Guard, which saves mesos.
claims.say: priest at 86 can solo grims without magic guard

claims.text: Shining Ray is not worth maxing first; it only sees occasional use at higher levels.
claims.say: dont max shining ray first, its rarely used

claims.text: One point in Doom is all you need if you only want it for fun.
claims.say: doom at level 1 is plenty

claims.text: Angel Ray takes over from Holy Arrow once a cleric reaches 4th job.
claims.say: angel ray replaces holy arrow at 4th job

claims.text: A level 170 Fire/Poison Arch Mage can solo Zakum; one solo took a little over four hours and needed steady attention through the third body.
claims.say: fp can solo zakum but plan on 4+ hours

claims.text: Bring a huge potion stock for a mage Zakum solo: thousands of Ginger Ales for MP and a few hundred All Cure Potions for his status attacks.
claims.say: mage zak solo: thousands of ginger ales, hundreds of all cures

claims.text: The Zakum solo was done with Paralyze, Meteor Shower, Fire Demon, Elquines and Maple Warrior all maxed.
claims.say: solo zak with max paralyze, meteor, fire demon, elquines, mw

claims.text: New Fire/Poison Arch Mages should max Meteor Shower first for training; putting early points into Fire Demon and Elquines instead slowed training noticeably.
claims.say: fp 4th job: max meteor shower first, trains way faster

claims.text: A workable order after Meteor Shower: max Paralyze, put 10 into Maple Warrior, then max Elquines and Fire Demon.
claims.say: after meteor: paralyze, mw 10, then elquines and fire demon

claims.text: For the last levels: max Big Bang, then Mana Reflection, keep 10 points for the Maple Warrior 30 book, then raise Infinity and Spell Booster.
claims.say: late fp: big bang, mana reflect, mw30, infinity, booster

claims.text: Maple Warrior 20 mastery books were scarce Horntail drops, while Big Bang 30 books drop in the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest.
claims.say: mw20 books from horntail, big bang 30 from cwkpq

claims.text: The Crushed Skull, a strong one-handed blunt weapon for White Knights, can be obtained from the Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest.
claims.say: crushed skull comes from cwkpq, solid 1h blunt

claims.text: On a weapon you cannot afford to lose, fill the remaining slots with 60% scrolls rather than gambling on 30% scrolls that can destroy it.
claims.say: use 60%s on a weapon you cant afford to boom

claims.text: Fire Tusks are immune to fire and resist poison but are weak to ice, so ice attacks work best on them.
claims.say: fire tusks are ice weak, fire does nothing

claims.text: Electrophants are immune to ice and resist lightning but take extra damage from fire.
claims.say: electrophants are fire weak, ice won't touch them

claims.text: Boomers resist fire, are weak to ice, and blow themselves up once their HP gets low.
claims.say: boomers are ice weak and self destruct when low

claims.text: Mighty Maple Eaters are weak to holy and attack on their own.
claims.say: mighty maple eaters are holy weak and aggressive

claims.text: Headless Horseman is a boss that is weak to lightning.
claims.say: headless horseman is lightning weak

claims.text: Targa resists fire, is weak to ice and is immune to poison.
claims.say: targa is ice weak, poison won't work

claims.text: Scarlion resists ice and lightning but is weak to fire.
claims.say: scarlion is fire weak, resists ice and lightning

claims.text: Targa has a stun attack that can lock down a whole squad, while Scarlion has no stun, which makes Scarlion the easier of the two to fight.
claims.say: scarlion is easier than targa, no stun

claims.text: New Leaf City is reached by subway from Kerning City: get a ticket, wait in the waiting room, and ride the train across.
claims.say: take the subway from kerning to get to nlc

claims.text: A LUKless Ice/Lightning mage can grind Retz with Thunder Bolt around levels 37-40.
claims.say: il at 37-40? retz with thunder bolt does fine

claims.text: Truckers carry an Ice/Lightning mage from about level 40 into the mid 50s, but they get slow by the 60s.
claims.say: truckers from 40 to mid 50s, they get slow after

claims.text: Around level 55 an Ice/Lightning mage can move to Mysterious Path 3 and keep training there into the 60s.
claims.say: try mysterious path 3 from about 55 on your il

claims.text: At level 63 Windraiders are a poor pick for an Ice/Lightning mage: they take too long to kill and their touch damage eats through potions.
claims.say: skip windraiders at 63, too tanky and they drain pots

claims.text: Around level 110, a pendant giving 10 weapon attack beats the Horntail Necklace's stats for a bowman; in 2nd and early 3rd job the two are closer in value.
claims.say: at 110ish a 10 att pendant beats ht pendant stats for bowmen

claims.text: Most STR-less bows are Fast, so a bowman can stay STR-less and add STR only when a particular bow needs it.
claims.say: strless bows are mostly fast, add str only when a bow needs it

claims.text: Bowmasters put points into Maple Warrior later than Bishops or Arch Mages, since they have more useful skills to level first.
claims.say: bms put mw off since they have better skills to max first

claims.text: Typhons are great exp for Rangers from the 80s to past 100.
claims.say: typhons are great ranger exp from 80s to 100+

claims.text: A Ranger can rush Arrow Rain to 30 first to mob Gryphons, pirates and Typhons faster, then go back to the usual build.
claims.say: rush arrow rain to 30 for faster mobbing, then normal build

claims.text: Non-sword warrior weapons (axes, blunt weapons, spears and polearms) randomly swing or stab, and over many attacks this averages out to about three swings for every two stabs.
claims.say: axes bws spears and polearms swing 3 times per 2 stabs on average

claims.text: Swords do the same damage whether they swing or stab, so a sword user's average damage is simply halfway between the min and max of the range.
claims.say: swords swing and stab the same, avg dmg is just min+max over 2

claims.text: Spears hit harder with the stab than the swing, while axes, blunt weapons and polearms hit harder with the swing.
claims.say: spears stab harder, axes bws and polearms swing harder

claims.text: Because swing and stab ranges differ, the shown damage range has a gap no hit lands in; estimate average damage by weighting average swing damage 0.6 and average stab damage 0.4, not by blending the overall min and max.
claims.say: for avg dmg weight avg swing 60% and avg stab 40%

claims.text: The swing and stab mix also shapes average damage for warrior attack skills such as Power Strike, Slash Blast, Charged Blow, Blast, Panic and Coma.
claims.say: skills like power strike still roll swing or stab dmg

claims.text: Deo's cane slam sends a quake along the ground that you avoid by jumping; it is weak and not a real threat.
claims.say: jump to dodge deo's cane quake

claims.text: The Deo quest opens at level 38: you answer a series of questions from the refining NPC in Ariant and need a Lidium; a wrong answer costs you the Lidium.
claims.say: deo quest at 38, bring a lidium, answer carefully

claims.text: Seruf spawns on a platform of Seaweed Tower in Aqua Road, starts hidden in its shell, and never moves; it spits pearls you can dodge and slaps with its shell if you stand close.
claims.say: seruf is on seaweed tower, it never moves

claims.text: Seruf can blind you, but since it cannot chase, just step out of its range and wait it out; it buffs weapon defense but not magic defense, so magicians hit it normally.
claims.say: step out of seruf's range when blinded

claims.text: Faust spawns on The Forest of Evil I, the first Malady map, which has a corrupted portal in the top right; he calls in Zombie Lupins and throws handfuls of bananas.
claims.say: faust is on forest of evil 1, the first malady map

claims.text: Timer spawns at Whirlpool of Time in Ludibrium; its main danger is a heavy knockback, and when its head turns to the gray side you should get clear or be thrown across the map.
claims.say: move when timer's head flips gray, big knockback

claims.text: Timer is often hard to find because players on their way to Papulatus kill it, and it has no drops worth chasing.
claims.say: timer usually gets killed by pap runners

claims.text: Dyle spawns at Dangerous Croko I in the Kerning swamp; it heals itself and buffs its attack and defense, but has no magic attack.
claims.say: dyle is at dangerous croko 1, it heals itself

claims.text: With the note, ask Nella, Jake, Mr. Pickall and Shumi in Kerning for clues, report to JM, speak to Lakelis, go back to JM, then kill Dyle and finish with JM.
claims.say: dyle quest: ask around kerning, then lakelis, then jm

claims.text: Zeno lives on a hidden map reached by pressing up on a rock on the upper level of Kulan Field 4 in Omega Sector; its only move is a strong knockback hit that you can jump over.
claims.say: jump zeno's knockback, it's his only move

claims.text: Chimera spawns in Lab - Secret Basement Path in Magatia, which only opens after a long stretch of the Magatia quest line ending with a quest from Parwen; it has no quest of its own but good drops.
claims.say: chimera needs the magatia quests to reach its map

claims.text: Leviathan hits about as hard as Griffey and Manon, so it is deadly for bowmen, Night Lords and Gunslingers below the 130s.
claims.say: leviathan hurts, low hp classes under 130 beware

claims.text: Leviathan's map is reached by pressing up at Dragon Canyon in Leafre; it summons Wyverns two at a time and can inflict Weakness and reversed controls.
claims.say: leviathan summons wyverns and reverses your keys

claims.text: Leviathan resists both fire and ice, so fire/poison and ice/lightning mages lose damage on those spells there.
claims.say: leviathan resists fire and ice

claims.text: Leviathan is known for dropping skill books, but few people hunt it because it is dangerous and out of the way.
claims.say: leviathan drops skill books

claims.text: When many bags explode at once the hits are merged into about five damage numbers on screen, but no damage is lost.
claims.say: lots of bags show as ~5 numbers, no damage lost

claims.text: Monster Carnival is entered through Spiegelmann, who stands in Kerning City, Orbis and Ludibrium; from his map parties are matched up to fight each other.
claims.say: talk to spiegelmann in kerning, orbis or ludi to do carnival

claims.text: In Monster Carnival both parties kill Ludibrium monsters; every kill earns Carnival Points that you spend to summon monsters on the other team, debuff them, or place protector towers.
claims.say: kill mobs for cp, spend it summoning and debuffing the other team

claims.text: Dying in Monster Carnival costs no exp, only some of your unspent Carnival Points, so it pays to spend CP instead of saving it.
claims.say: dying in cpq eats unspent cp, not exp, so spend your points

claims.text: Warriors do well in Monster Carnival thanks to Slash Blast and high HP, but suffer from low accuracy, no ranged attack, and enemy Avoid Up or Weapon Cancel towers.
claims.say: warriors slash blast well in cpq but watch accuracy and avoid towers

claims.text: A Spearman's Hyper Body raises the party's max HP and MP, a big help to thieves and mages in Monster Carnival; spearmen also reach further than other melee but take more damage with no Power Guard.
claims.say: spearman hyper body really helps squishy mages and thieves in cpq

claims.text: In Monster Carnival a Fighter's Rage raises party attack, and a Page's Threaten lowers enemy monsters' attack and defense.
claims.say: fighters bring rage, pages bring threaten for the cpq party

claims.text: Assassins are among the best Rombot killers in Monster Carnival thanks to fast ranged attacks, but must carry enough stars; a few points in Double Stab give a fallback if stars run out.
claims.say: sins melt rombots in cpq, just bring plenty of stars

claims.text: Bandits move quickly between scattered monsters in Monster Carnival and become strong once Savage Blow is maxed, but have no ranged attack and are weaker before that.
claims.say: bandits get good in cpq once savage blow is maxed

claims.text: Thieves are fast and hard to hit in Monster Carnival and can hide in Dark Sight when low on HP, but low HP, the Weakness debuff and Weapon Cancel towers hurt them.
claims.say: thieves can dark sight to rest in cpq, but weakness hurts

claims.text: Archers in Monster Carnival should invest in Power Knock-Back to keep monsters away and fight from the map edges; without Soul Arrow, carry plenty of arrows since running out makes you useless.
claims.say: archers: pkb keeps mobs off you in cpq, bring lots of arrows

claims.text: Hunters can stun groups of monsters with Arrow Bomb in Monster Carnival, while Crossbowmen hit harder but slower and have no stun.
claims.say: hunters arrow bomb stuns mobs in cpq, xbows hit harder

claims.text: Mages in Monster Carnival fear Seal, stun and Magic Cancel towers rather than Weapon Cancel, and die fast without Magic Guard; Teleport helps them dodge.
claims.say: mages in cpq keep magic guard up and watch for seal

claims.text: Clerics are valuable in Monster Carnival when potion drops are scarce: Heal keeps the party alive and shreds Chronos and Master Chronos, and Bless helps warrior allies.
claims.say: bring a cleric to cpq, heal wrecks chronos and keeps you alive

claims.text: Ice/Lightning mages should be wary of Robos in Monster Carnival, which resist ice and cannot be frozen; Rombots are boss monsters and cannot be frozen either.
claims.say: i/l: robos resist ice and rombots cant be frozen

claims.text: Fire/Poison mages are strong against Rombots and Block Golems in Monster Carnival because their fire attacks hit them hard.
claims.say: f/p fire attacks are great on rombots and block golems in cpq

claims.text: Gunslingers have a hard time in Monster Carnival until Gun Mastery and Invisible Shot are decent around the late 30s; attack potions, scrolled gear and a high Somersault Kick help in crowded rooms.
claims.say: gunslingers struggle in cpq until late 30s, level somersault kick

claims.text: Brawlers are strong in Monster Carnival with stuns, heavy knockback and time to charge between spawns, but should aim Corkscrew Blow so it doesn't push mobs onto ranged teammates or away from melee allies.
claims.say: brawlers rock cpq, just aim corkscrew so you dont scatter mobs

claims.text: Don't summon anything weaker than a Toy Trojan in Monster Carnival unless you are coin farming; weak summons just give the other team easy kills, CP and potions.
claims.say: dont summon weak stuff in cpq, it just feeds the other team

claims.text: Massed Toy Trojans with Speed Up and Power Up towers corner archers and weak mages in rooms 1 to 4; they do little against warriors, brawlers or I/L mages who mob them, or thieves in Dark Sight.
claims.say: spam trojans vs archers and weak mages in cpq rooms 1-4

claims.text: Only summon Robos in Monster Carnival when one of the strongest opponents is an Ice/Lightning mage, since Robos resist ice and can't be frozen.
claims.say: summon robos only when the other side has a strong i/l

claims.text: Master Chronos has a ranged magic attack that goes through Dark Sight and knocks climbers off ladders; with Weapon or Magic Cancel and Speed Up towers, it keeps foes from reaching the towers to break them.
claims.say: master chronos plus cancel towers keeps people off the ladders

claims.text: Avoid summoning Master Chronos in Monster Carnival rooms 3 and 4 when the other team has a Cleric or a strong warrior or brawler; they kill them fast and gain CP.
claims.say: dont send master chronos at a team with a cleric in rooms 3-4

claims.text: Rombots are tanks with strong touch damage and a slam that hits grounded players, so pair them with Weakness; don't summon them where foes can kill them easily, since they hand over lots of CP.
claims.say: rombot plus weakness is nasty, but dont feed them to strong teams

claims.text: Every Monster Carnival debuff except stun can be removed by looting an All Cure Potion dropped in the map.
claims.say: grab an all cure drop to clear cpq debuffs, stun just wears off

claims.text: The Poison debuff works best early in a Monster Carnival match, before potions pile up and while foes have low HP; it pairs well with stun but falls off late or against a Cleric.
claims.say: use poison early in cpq before potions drop

claims.text: The Weakness debuff stops opponents from jumping, keeping them off your protectors and in the path of Rombot slams; it's especially strong against thieves.
claims.say: weakness stops jumping, great vs thieves and with rombots

claims.text: Darkness cuts accuracy and wrecks melee teams, warriors most of all; paired with an Avoid Up tower early in a match, when All Cures are scarce, it can lock them down cheaply.
claims.say: darkness plus avoid up shuts warriors down early in cpq

claims.text: Curse is a waste of CP in Monster Carnival; it only halves exp gain and does nothing to the fight itself.
claims.say: dont waste cp on curse, it only halves exp

claims.text: In Monster Carnival, Seal blocks all skills, which cripples mages, low-DEX assassins relying on Lucky Seven, archers using Power Knock-Back, and pirates' stuns, Wings, Recoil Shot and Corkscrew Blow.
claims.say: seal shuts down mages and pirates in cpq

claims.text: A stunned player can't move, attack or loot until it wears off; in Monster Carnival rest on a platform rather than a ladder, because a stun on a ladder drops you into the mob below.
claims.say: never rest on a ladder in cpq, a stun drops you to the bottom

claims.text: The Cancel Buff ability strips skill buffs such as Hyper Body, Magic Guard, Dark Sight and Haste but not item buffs, and hits only one opponent, who can simply recast.
claims.say: cancel buff removes skill buffs but they can just recast

claims.text: Weapon Cancel and Magic Cancel towers make that damage type deal 1 per hit; break enemy ones at once, and make sure you summon the right one, since Magic Cancel does nothing to a team of warriors.
claims.say: break cancel towers asap, and dont summon the wrong cancel

claims.text: An Avoid Up tower makes your monsters hard to hit and works on its own, best against warriors; Accuracy Up helps against evasive thieves and works best with an attack-boosting tower.
claims.say: avoid up works alone, acc up needs a power up with it

claims.text: Monster Carnival rooms 1 and 2 suit low-to-mid 30s and newer players: teddies and Block Golems spread across the bottom, with ladder platforms to retreat to; ranged players should avoid getting cornered.
claims.say: new to cpq? rooms 1 and 2 are the easy balanced ones

claims.text: Monster Carnival rooms 3 and 4 are small and best for warriors and brawlers; don't summon monsters there against them, but against an all-ranged team mass Block Golems, Rombots or Master Chronos.
claims.say: cpq rooms 3 and 4 are warrior and brawler heaven

claims.text: Monster Carnival rooms 5 and 6 favour ranged players: Rombots spawn at the bottom and Robos on upper platforms, with small ledges to snipe from; have a warrior or strong ranged player handle the Rombots.
claims.say: ranged do best in cpq rooms 5 and 6, snipe from the ledges

claims.text: A stun wave, with each player using Stun every few seconds, can stall the other team completely; it needs a steady CP income and makes a strong finisher or comeback play.
claims.say: chain stuns as a team to stall the other side late in cpq

claims.text: Coins sometimes drop in Monster Carnival and can be traded to Spiegelmann for weapons, with more coins buying higher-level ones, or for Spiegelmann's Necklace, a small all-stat pendant.
claims.say: save cpq coins for spiegelmann's weapons or his necklace

claims.text: For coin farming, both teams agree to summon easy monsters for each other, such as Brown Teddies, Chronos or Rombots, often with Speed Up; it is also good exp for mobbing classes.
claims.say: coin farming cpq: both teams summon easy mobs for each other

claims.text: In Crimsonwood Keep Party Quest stage 4 the mage is sent into one of three randomly chosen Teleport mazes and has to reach a statue to take its staff.
claims.say: cwkpq stage 4 mage room is a random teleport maze to a statue

claims.text: One of the stage 4 mage mazes is worked from left to right and lets you reach the statue, but you cannot teleport back left to the entrance, which can cost the whole run.
claims.say: one cwkpq mage maze wont let u teleport back left to the door

claims.text: To get out of that maze, drop down at the marked spot as close to the right edge as you can while holding right; you fall to the bottom and reappear at the door so the stage can be finished.
claims.say: stuck? drop at the right edge holding right, u land at the door

claims.text: The level 30 Marksman Boost mastery book drops from Zakum; it is rare and sells high even though few Marksmen need it.
claims.say: marksman boost 30 book drops from zak, its rare

claims.text: Zakum run leaders often keep rare mastery books for the run's profit, so ask about loot rules before joining if you are after a specific book.
claims.say: ask the zak leader about book loot before you join

claims.text: A standard first-job Magician skill order is one point in Energy Bolt, five in Improved MP Recovery, then maxing Improved MaxMP Increase.
claims.say: 1 energy bolt, 5 mp recovery, then max the max mp skill

claims.text: A mage whose MP looks a little low in the 40s does not need to restart; MP totals tend to even out at later levels.
claims.say: slightly low mp at 40 is fine, it evens out later
